Mistfall Hollow.name: Mistfall Hollow

Forest Edge.description: The eastern boundary of the Hollow where the gentle clearing meets the true Verdania Wilds. The footpath to Lanternmoss Village begins here, marked by the faded wooden signpost and a natural archway of intertwined branches. The transition is sharp: behind you, warmth and wildflowers; ahead, deeper shadow, denser undergrowth, and the distant sounds of a living forest that does not necessarily want company. The path is always clear. The forest on either side of it is not.

Stream Bend.description: Where the clear stream curves around a formation of moss-covered stones, creating a shallow pool deep enough to wash in and cold enough to shock the sleep from your bones. Smooth flat rocks along the bank serve as natural seats. The water is safe to drink and faintly sweet, filtered through the Elder Tree's root network far below. Small silver fish dart through the shallows. Travelers sometimes find perfectly round stones in the streambed that glow faintly at night.

Clearing Heart.description: The central depression of the Hollow where wildflowers grow thickest and the mist lingers longest. A natural bowl of soft grass ringed by the oldest trees, their roots forming comfortable seats along the perimeter. The bioluminescent spores are densest here, drifting upward in lazy spirals that catch the light. This is where Reborn souls most often wake: face-up in the flowers, staring at a canopy that seems impossibly far away. The air tastes clean in a way that feels deliberate, as if the forest prepared the room.

Mossdraped Ring.description: A circle of ancient trees whose branches have grown together into a natural canopy, their trunks draped in hanging moss that sways without wind. The light here is green and gold, filtered through layers of living curtain. The ground is carpeted in soft moss rather than grass, and the acoustics are strange: whispers carry farther than shouts. Beastkin hunters consider this ring sacred and will not hunt within it. Something about the arrangement of the trees feels intentional, as if someone planted them in a perfect circle millennia ago.

Mistfall Hollow.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 1-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected] A quiet sun-dappled clearing on the western edge of the Verdania Wilds, where soft grass, wildflowers, and a slow clear stream ring a circle of ancient moss-draped trees. Bioluminescent spores drift lazily in the shafts of light that fall through the canopy, and the air smells of rain and green growing things. A worn footpath leads east toward Lanternmoss Village, close enough that woodsmoke and the faint sound of a village bell reach the clearing on a still morning. Travelers call it a gentle place to wake, and more than one lost soul has found their feet here before walking on. Nothing hunts in the Hollow itself, though the deeper Wilds beyond the treeline are another matter.

The clearing breathes with the forest. Morning mist pools knee-deep between the ancient trees, burning off by midmorning into shafts of gold that make the wildflower carpet glow. Bioluminescent spores drift lazily upward in the stillness, tracing slow spirals toward the canopy like lanterns released at a festival. The stream bends around moss-covered stones worn smooth by centuries of water, and the sound of it fills the silence without breaking it. Small forest creatures (iridescent beetles, cotton-tailed rabbits, a fox that watches from the treeline with golden eyes) treat visitors as furniture. A carved wooden signpost near the eastern footpath reads "Lanternmoss Village" in three languages, the paint faded but the letters still legible. Travelers who rest here often remark that they slept better than they have in years, and woke knowing exactly which direction to walk.
Mistfall Hollow.hiddenInfo:
Mistfall Hollow is the Verdania Wilds' most common arrival point for Reborn souls, and the village elders of Lanternmoss have developed a welcoming protocol refined across generations. When the bioluminescent spores in the hollow begin drifting upward instead of down, a watcher is dispatched within the hour. The watcher carries a blanket, water, and a basket of food, because arrivals are consistently disoriented, cold, and hungry. The protocol's gentle efficiency has saved lives, and the elders consider it the community's most important civic duty.

The hollow's clearing is maintained by the forest itself. Paths leading away from Lanternmoss are always slightly overgrown; the path toward the village is always clear. The elders attribute this to the Elder Tree's benevolence, and the practical effect is that confused new arrivals naturally drift toward help rather than deeper into dangerous wilderness. Whether the forest's path maintenance is intentional guidance or ecological coincidence is a question the elders consider irrelevant; it works either way.

Four Reborn individuals currently live in Lanternmoss under assumed identities, having chosen quiet lives over adventure. The village elder knows about each of them and protects their privacy with the same fierce discretion she applies to all community matters. One runs the bakery, one teaches the children, one works as a carpenter, and one sits on the elder council itself. Their integration is so complete that newer residents have no idea their neighbors came from another world.

The hollow's reputation as a peaceful arrival point has attracted a Veilwalker operative who poses as an herbalist in Lanternmoss. The operative documents every arrival: timing, condition, apparent abilities, and the direction the spores were drifting. The reports suggest arrival frequency is increasing, and the operative's superiors have not told them why this matters.

Lastlight Bridge.name: Lastlight Bridge

Lastlight Bridge: Span.description:
Lastlight Bridge: Span is an area within Lastlight Bridge; entry requires reaching that parent location.

Weathered granite wide enough for two wagons abreast, worn to a shine by centuries of feet and lately by boots that march in step. Signal flags snap from the parapet, the river runs fast and cold beneath, and the wind carries whichever side's cook-smoke is losing that day. Halfway across, a painted line nobody will admit is a border.

North Gatehouse.description: The Crown-held northern head of the bridge, standing on Ecclesia ground under the Lastlight Accord: portcullis, murder-holes, a bored-looking sergeant who has learned that most trouble wears a friendly face, and a Church road-keeper at the sergeant's elbow who has learned the same. This is the last hard point on the road to the Crownlands, and everyone who works it knows that if it ever falls the next stops are the Lantern Road checkpoint, Greyhaven, the fort, then home.

South Gatehouse.description: The scarred southern head, which has changed hands twice this season and shows it: fresh mortar over old scorch, a Crown banner hung over a patch where a different banner used to be. The stone here remembers more than the garrison does, and the garrison is careful never to relax with the Frontier at their backs.

The Toll House.description: A cramped office of books, stamps, and quiet transactions where papers are checked, refugees are processed, and bribes are called handling fees. The clerk sees everyone who crosses in either direction and remembers the ones who cross too often, which makes this the best-informed and most-watched room on the whole front.

Lastlight Bridge: Underbridge.description:
Lastlight Bridge: Underbridge is an area within Lastlight Bridge; entry requires reaching that parent location.

The dank timber-and-stone world beneath the span: smuggler caches, refugee squats, and the demolition charges nobody talks about. Sound carries strangely down here, boots overhead, water below, and the people who shelter under a bridge everyone is fighting over have learned to hear an argument three piers away.

Lastlight Bridge.basicInfo:
[Border Crossing · Recommended Level: 15-40 · Danger: High · contested crossing]

The ancient stone crossing that carries the Ashenmere Frontier's only good road north, and the single most important span on the continent right now. Its north end comes down on Ecclesia ground at the Pilgrim's Lantern Road checkpoint; from the Crossroads beyond it, the Crown's war road runs east into the Crownlands, past Greyhaven and Fort Dawnsward to Aureliath. Long before the war it was just the last dependable road north; now every commander on three sides knows the same arithmetic. If the Twilight Dominion ever holds Lastlight, they have a road to march a real army through Church land and into the Crownlands. Crown banners fly over it today under the Lastlight Accord, the Church's grudging leave for a royal garrison on its border; the checkpoint never closes, and the traffic across it is refugees, requisition wagons, couriers, pilgrims, and the occasional corpse the river gives back. It is guarded like a throne and crossed like a wound.
Lastlight Bridge.hiddenInfo: Nobody blows the bridge because nobody can afford to be the one who did. Destroying Lastlight would strand the Twilight raiders already north of it, forfeit the Crown's own supply road, and hand the Church a heresy to hang on whoever gave the order. So it stands, deliberately, a knife everyone keeps sharp and no one will throw. There is a set of pre-placed Crownveil demolition charges under the third pier that three separate parties have quietly disarmed for three separate reasons.

Bannerfall Field.name: Bannerfall Field

The Churned Ground.description: Mud, ruts, and the debris of engagements nobody won: shattered pavise, spent arrows, a wagon wheel standing upright in the muck like a monument to bad planning. The footing is treacherous and the smell is worse, and veterans read the ground here like a page, this rut is cavalry, that scorch is a mage, that quiet patch is where something is buried that should not be dug up.

The Banner Line.description: The rough no-man's-land where the front actually sits on any given week, marked by the leaning, faded, half-burned banners the place is named for. To stand at the banner line is to be visible to three armies at once. People cross it quickly, or they cross it under a flag of truce, or they do not finish crossing it.

The Scavenger Camp.description: A shifting cluster of tents and lean-tos where war-dogs, deserters, and honest looters trade what the dead no longer need. There is a brisk market in salvaged gear, forged papers, and information, and an unwritten law that you do not bring the war into camp, broken often enough that the enforcers are the scariest people present.

The Carrion Crater.description: A collapsed sinkhole where a Riftmaw once opened and never fully closed, ringed by bones the scavengers won't touch. Things come up out of it after the fighting, drawn to the field's reliable harvest, and the Moonwatch scouts mark it on maps in a red that means do not approach without a reason worth dying for.

The Field-Medic Post.description: A canvas awning and a hard-eyed cutter who patches whoever reaches them and asks which side they're on only for the paperwork. This is the closest thing Bannerfall has to neutral ground, protected less by any law than by the fact that everyone might need it next, and even that protection is thinner than the medic pretends.

Bannerfall Field.basicInfo:
[Battlefield · Recommended Level: 20-45 · Danger: Very High · active battlefield]

The wide churned plain just south of Lastlight where the skirmishes happen most and the banners of three armies have fallen enough times to name the place. It is nobody's ground and everybody's graveyard: Crown patrols, Twilight raiders, and Church corruption-hunters all cross it, rarely at the same time and never in peace. Worse, the carnage draws things up out of the Frontier's Riftmaws, monsters that have learned a battlefield is a reliable table. Adventurers take Guild contracts here for the pay and the loot; most learn fast why the pay is that high.
Bannerfall Field.hiddenInfo: Something in the Riftmaw beneath Bannerfall is learning. After every clash the field's monsters come back a little more coordinated, a little more patient, hitting supply lines instead of soldiers, and the Moonwatch scouts who have noticed are being told by everyone above them that a hungry Riftmaw is not their department. It is feeding on the war, and the war keeps setting the table.

Gloamspire Camp.name: Gloamspire Camp

The Muster Yard.description: Where raiders and scouts form up before crossing north: gear inspected, routes assigned, the night's targets read out flat. The discipline is real but the material is rough, opportunists, exiles, and true believers in roughly equal measure, and the sergeants spend as much effort pointing that violence north as aiming it.

The War-Tent.description: The command pavilion: maps weighted with obsidian, a slate wall of troop dispositions kept in a demon-script shorthand, and a commander who runs a war the way a good clerk runs an office. Nothing here is frenzied. That is the frightening part. Decisions are made here in calm sentences that end villages.

The Trophy Line.description: A grim gallery of captured Crown and Church banners, sigils, and gear, displayed less as boast than as intelligence, a running catalogue of exactly who they are facing and what those enemies can do. A careful visitor learns more here about the state of the war than in any war-tent.

The Binding Pens.description: The part of camp the disciplined parts pretend not to see: warded cages and quiet specialists doing careful, patient, monstrous work on what corruption does to a living host. It is not cruelty for its own sake; it is research, which is worse. The things that come out of the pens are why Bannerfall's monsters have started thinking.

The Envoy's Tent.description: A deliberately comfortable pavilion of low lamps and good wine where the Dominion does the work it truly prefers: talking. Deserters are welcomed, grievances are heard, and the envoy makes the Twilight offer sound less like treason and more like the only honest deal on the whole front. It is the most dangerous room in the camp precisely because it never raises its voice.

Gloamspire Camp.basicInfo:
[War Camp · Recommended Level: 22-45 · Danger: Very High · hostile military]

The largest forward position the Demon Lord's army holds in this part of Ashenmere, the southern anchor of the whole front and the fist aimed at Lastlight. Do not mistake it for a horde. Gloamspire is disciplined, patient, and unnervingly well-run: ordered tent-rows under a black spire of raised obsidian, sentries who do not slouch, and a command that would rather take the bridge intact through one opened gate than lose a thousand raiders storming it. The Twilight Court plays a long war, and Gloamspire is where the long war is administered.
Gloamspire Camp.hiddenInfo: Gloamspire's commander has explicit orders to take Lastlight without breaking it, and a standing offer, carried quietly by envoys, for any Crown-side soul willing to open the north gate one night: land, title, and a place in the Dominion that treats its useful traitors better than the Crown treats its loyal poor. Beneath the discipline, in the pens, the camp is also doing the other work the war is good for: finding out exactly how much corruption a living body can carry before it stops being a person and starts being a weapon.

Fort Dawnsward.name: Fort Dawnsward

The Curtain Wall & Gatehouse.description: Grey stone, iron-shod gates, and sentries watching a southern horizon that has learned to worry them. This is the face the fort shows the road, and the road knows it: the wall is real, the garrison is stretched, and the gap between how strong Dawnsward looks and how strong it is keeps the commander awake.

Fort Dawnsward: War Room.description:
Fort Dawnsward: War Room is an area within Fort Dawnsward; entry requires reaching that parent location.

Maps, casualty lists, and the constant grinding math of holding a line with never quite enough. Officers argue here in the shorthand of people who have had the same argument for a year: where the reserves go, which village gets the escort, what the fort can afford to lose to keep from losing everything.

The Requisition Yard.description: Where the villages' grain, wagons, and livestock end up, logged by clerks who have stopped meeting anyone's eyes. Officially it is the beating heart of a fort that must not fall. Unofficially it is where the numbers stop matching, where a wagon of Greyhaven's grain becomes a smaller wagon of fort supply and the difference walks away in Thorne's book.

The Barracks.description: Cramped bunks, frayed nerves, and off-duty soldiers with too much fear and too little pay, which is a recipe the local taverns know well. The garrison is not cruel by nature, just tired and frightened and armed, and the friction that produces, the requisitions, the brawls, the escort a family didn't get, is the war's quiet second front against the people it claims to defend.

Fort Dawnsward: Commander's Tower.description:
Fort Dawnsward: Commander's Tower is an area within Fort Dawnsward; entry requires reaching that parent location.

The highest room in Dawnsward, where the commander keeps a clear view of the southern road and a set of books they have deliberately never reconciled. Everything about the tower says a soldier doing an impossible job with honor. The unopened book in the locked drawer is the one thing that might say otherwise.

Fort Dawnsward.basicInfo:
[Fortress · Recommended Level: 15-38 · Danger: Moderate inside · High on sortie]

The primary Crownveil military position guarding the southern approach into Aureliath, and the wall the whole Crownlands is leaning on. Its commanders live by one grim syllogism: if Dawnsward falls, Twilight gains a road into the Crownlands; therefore anything that keeps Dawnsward standing is justified. In practice that means the fort takes what it needs. If Briarwick has grain and the garrison needs grain, the army takes the grain. If civilians need an escort while the scouts are needed elsewhere, the civilians wait. The soldiers are brave, overworked, underpaid, and increasingly rough on the war-torn villages they are supposedly protecting.
Fort Dawnsward.hiddenInfo: Dawnsward's supply and requisition contracts route through a merchant house that is a shell backed by Baron Thorne. Military necessity has become the perfect laundry: confiscated civilian grain, livestock, and lumber are logged as fort supply and quietly resold, the requisition quotas inflated to cover the skim, and every objection buried under the unanswerable phrase the fort must not fall. The commander is either loyal and blind or complicit and careful; nobody at the fort can afford to find out which, because the alternative to Thorne's crooked supply line is no supply line at all.

The Vigil of Saint Aurel.name: The Vigil of Saint Aurel

paths: Vigil of Saint Aurel: Paladin Barracks
The Reliquary Chapel.description: Cold stone, warm light, and the relics of Saint Aurel kept behind warded glass: a scorched sword, a sealed reliquary, a prayer worn smooth by a thousand frightened lips. The chapel is beautiful and it is not comforting, because the people who pray here pray before doing something they have decided is necessary.

The Quarantine Cells.description: Clean, warded, and quiet cells where the investigated are held while the hunters decide what they are. Some walk out cleared. Some do not walk out. The cells are where the Vigil's whole moral weight sits: every door is either a life saved from an outbreak or an innocent one wrong ruling away from the pyre, and the hunters have stopped being able to tell the difference from the outside.

The Pyre Yard.description: A walled court of ash and consecrated fire where contaminated remains, and worse, are burned under prayer. The Vigil insists it is mercy and containment, not punishment, and the smoke that hangs over the yard does not care what anyone insists. Villagers can smell it on the wind from the road, and they have learned to read the days by it.

paths: Vigil of Saint Aurel: Warded Vault
Vigil of Saint Aurel: Paladin Barracks.description:
Vigil of Saint Aurel: Paladin Barracks is an area within The Vigil of Saint Aurel; entry requires reaching that parent location.

Spare, ordered quarters for holy warriors who train like their lives and souls both depend on it, which here they do. The paladins are the best of the Vigil, disciplined, brave, kind to the frightened when they are allowed to be, and the tragedy of the place is how often they are not allowed to be.

paths: Vigil of Saint Aurel: Paladin Barracks
Vigil of Saint Aurel: Warded Vault.description:
Vigil of Saint Aurel: Warded Vault is an area within The Vigil of Saint Aurel; entry requires reaching that parent location.

A sealed strongroom of recovered artifacts too dangerous to destroy and too dangerous to keep, each in its own warded niche, each logged and prayed over. The vault is the Vigil at its most defensible and its most exposed: everything in it is a weapon, a temptation, and a heresy waiting for the wrong hand, and everyone on the front knows the Vigil has it.

The Vigil of Saint Aurel.basicInfo:
[Holy Bastion · Recommended Level: 18-42 · Danger: High · militant holy order]

A fortified Ecclesian chapter-house at the front, named for the saint who died sealing a corruption breach with her own body, from which paladins, priests, healers, and specialized corruption-hunters wage their own version of this war. To the Vigil, the Twilight incursion is not a territorial dispute; it is contamination, and contamination is answered, not negotiated. Their patrols investigate corrupted creatures, recover dangerous artifacts, burn contaminated remains, and question, and sometimes purge, civilians who may have had prolonged contact with Twilight forces. They are genuinely holy, genuinely skilled, and genuinely not here to comfort you.
The Vigil of Saint Aurel.hiddenInfo: The Vigil's terrible secret is that they are usually right. Some of the refugees coming up out of Ashenmere really are carrying something, a seed, a mark, a slow rewriting, and the corruption-hunters can prove it more often than the villages want to believe, which is exactly what makes their purges impossible to cleanly condemn. The line between a zealot burning an innocent and a saint stopping an outbreak runs straight through the Vigil's quarantine cells, and nobody there, least of all the hunters, is certain which side of it they stand on this week.

Greyhaven.name: Greyhaven

The Stripped Market.description: A market square that used to provision everyone heading into Ashenmere and now mostly displays what the requisitions left behind. Prices are predatory, stalls stand empty, and the few merchants still working the war charge a war's prices, while everyone pretends not to notice how much of the good stock leaves east in fort wagons and never comes back.

The Lastlight Inn.description: The village's stubborn heart: a low, warm common room that has hosted merchants, hunters, soldiers, and now refugees, and refuses to close no matter who is winning. The ale is watered, the stew is thin, the rumors are the realest currency in town, and the innkeeper has learned to feed the frightened first and ask about coin never, which is slowly ruining them.

The Broken Row.description: A street of houses damaged in raids and never repaired, because the timber and the labor both went to the fort. Families live in half-homes under patched roofs, and the row is a daily argument the village is having with the Crown that claims to protect it: this is what protection looks like, and it is not enough.

The Refugee Quarter.description: A crowded improvised sprawl of tents and shared rooms where people who fled the fighting farther south wait for a safety that is not coming. Tempers are short, supplies are shorter, and the Church patrols walk through slowly, watching for the wounds and symptoms and simply-been-south-too-long that can get a person taken to the Vigil for questions.

The Militia Post.description: A single hard-pressed building where a handful of locals do the job the Crown's soldiers pass through without doing, standing watch, walking the farms at night, burying the ones the raiders reach. They are underarmed, unpaid, and the only people in Greyhaven the villagers actually trust, which is a weight the militia captain feels every single dawn.

The Outlying Farms.description: The ring of farmsteads beyond the village edge, half of them burned or abandoned, all of them dangerous after dark. Twilight raiders and scouts reach this far north, people have vanished on the isolated roads, and the families still working the outer fields do so in daylight, in groups, with one eye always on the treeline and the bridge-road southwest.

Greyhaven.basicInfo:
[Frontier Village · Recommended Level: 8-30 · Danger: Moderate · abandoned frontier village]

A small Crownlands settlement on the war road beyond Lastlight Bridge, the first Crown village a traveler reaches after crossing the span and leaving the Ecclesia's Lantern Road at the Crossroads. Once the last dependable stop before Ashenmere, it is inns, stables, smithies, and small farms grown up around honest through-traffic. The war made Lastlight strategic and made Greyhaven an afterthought. Crown forces poured into the region and deployed to the fortifications, not to the village; soldiers pass through Greyhaven constantly and protect it never. The Crown requisitions its livestock, food, wagons, and lumber; damaged homes stay damaged because the labor went to the fort; refugees from the south strain what little is left; and merchants brave enough to come this close charge whatever they please. It is officially protected Crown territory. Its people have stopped believing that means anything.
Greyhaven.hiddenInfo: Greyhaven is being bled twice. Once by the war, and once by Baron Thorne, whose shell company logs more requisitioned from the village than the Crown ever receives, the same skim that runs through Fort Dawnsward, with Greyhaven's books the cleaner half of the crooked books. Caught between a Crown that takes and does not guard, a Church whose patrols treat every refugee as a possible carrier, and Twilight raiders who reach the outlying farms at night, the village is one hard winter from deciding that being Crown territory in name is not worth what it costs, and there are quiet people, some of them Thorne's, and some of them Gloamspire's, ready to help them decide.

Riftwatch Rifts.name: Riftwatch Rifts

Rift Switchback.description: A rope-railed switchback cut into the overlook's rock, leading down from Riftwatch Camp's Watch Platform to the three rift mouths. Guild trail markers, a signal bell at the bottom, and a last flat ledge where delvers check their gear and decide which rift to take.

The Shallow Rift.description: The stable rift and the Guild's training ground. Rope lines and painted floor numbers lead down three shallow floors of glowing moss and dripping stone. Cave rats, rift-moths and slow green slimes are the usual company, with the occasional horned hare-beast for the unlucky. Most adventurers fight their first real battle here.

The Echoing Rift.description: The active rift. Its passages shift between visits, so maps go stale within a week. Goblin scouts, rift hounds and crystal crawlers den in its galleries, and its deepest floor holds an E-rank nest the Guild posts bounties on. The Riftlight loot is richer here, and so are the bruises.

The Sealed Rift.description: The restricted rift, wider every month. Guild ward-posts, a chalk line and a two-person monitoring team stand between the camp's rookies and its mouth, and rhythmic tones rise from below on quiet nights. The monitors turn delvers back; anyone who forces past them is on their own, in danger far beyond rookie depth.

The Glowmoss Rest.description: A dry chamber between the Shallow and Echoing rifts where the moss glows bright enough to read by. Monsters avoid the light, so delvers rest, bandage, and trade rumors here. Old Guild chalk on the walls records the names of everyone who made it this far.

Riftwatch Rifts.basicInfo:
[Recommended Level: 1-12 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Three young Riftmaw entrances in the rock below Riftwatch Camp, a short switchback climb down from the camp's Watch Platform. They are not The Riftmaw itself, which lies a journey away at the Maw. These are shallow rifts where the Guild sends new adventurers for their first delves: F and E rank work, with real teeth.

The Shallow Rift is stable and Guild-roped: a few floors of glowing moss, cave rats, rift-moths and slow slimes, the place most adventurers fight their first real battle. The Echoing Rift is active: its passages shift between visits, goblin scouts and rift hounds den in its galleries, and it pays better for the risk. The Sealed Rift is restricted: Guild ward-posts and a monitoring team turn delvers back, and nobody who knows anything wants to go past them.

The monsters are rookie-scale, but they are monsters: the camp's wards end at the rift mouths. Riftlight loot drops as it does in any Riftmaw, the camp's mess board posts which rifts are stable each morning, and the climb back up to Riftwatch Camp is always an option, usually a wise one.
Riftwatch Rifts.hiddenInfo: The Sealed Rift is the entrance Riftwatch Camp's quiet reports describe: it has widened every month faster than any natural process, and on still nights rhythmic tones rise from it. Past the Guild seals its floors are far deadlier than the other two rifts, closer to The Riftmaw's middle depths than to rookie ground. The Echoing Rift's shifting passages are a symptom of the same pressure. Much of Dr. Yua Sakima's data on Riftmaw exposure comes from delvers who use these three rifts. The Faceless Ones have a hand in the Sealed Rift's widening; the Guild does not know it.

The Saltglass Rift.name: The Saltglass Rift

Saltglass Rift: Rift Mouth.description: The tear itself: a ragged opening in the ground with edges that look torn, not dug. The air moves inward. Whatever the land was here, pieces of it hang just inside, and the Guild's first chalk marks, if anyone has come, stop a few paces down.

Saltglass Rift: Outer Hollows.description: The first chambers under the mouth, where the rift is still mostly the country it swallowed, bent the wrong way. Daylight reaches a little way in. Things already live here, and none of them were here last week.

Saltglass Rift: The Branching.description: The rift divides: passages that were not dug by anything, some closing behind the party, some ending in pockets the rift has filled with what it took. Nothing here stays put long enough to map.

Saltglass Rift: Deep Hollow.description: Past the branching the rift stops imitating the surface. The walls are its own material now, faintly lit from inside, and the largest things it has made keep to these chambers.

Saltglass Rift: The Core.description: The heart of the rift: one chamber, one bright knot of Riftlight hanging at its center, and whatever the rift made to keep it. The core can be read, or taken. Taking it starts the rift closing.

Hollowvein Rift: The Core.description: The heart of the rift: one chamber, one bright knot of Riftlight hanging at its center, and whatever the rift made to keep it. The core can be read, or taken. Taking it starts the rift closing.

The Hollowvein Rift.basicInfo:
[Recommended Level: 1-88 · Danger: Rising (Moderate), unstable]

A wild rift: a fresh tear in the world that opens without warning in Kurogane Deephollow. From outside: crystal growing fast enough to hear. Wild rifts are young Riftmaws that have not taken root. One holds for a few days and then seals, and no two openings are alike: the same scar can be flooded one season and burning the next, shallow or dangerously deep, and its strength is set by whoever stands nearest when it opens.

Inside are five stretches, from the mouth to the core. The Guild pays for a core reading and far more for the core itself, and taking the core starts the rift closing. Riftlight loot drops here as in any Riftmaw.

Nobody maps a wild rift. There is no time.

A wild rift takes its shape from what it swallowed and its strength from whoever is near when it opens. The Guild's rift-watchers know this and do not say it. Each opening is a new dungeon: never reuse the layout, creatures or keeper of an earlier one.

Driftshell Cove.name: Driftshell Cove
Driftshell Cove.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Driftshell Cove is a small horseshoe of pale sand tucked between two arms of low grey rock on the Cerulean Coast. The water inside the cove is calm and glass-clear, shading from pale green over the sand to deep blue where the rocks drop away. Gulls drift overhead, terns dive for silver fish, and each tide leaves a fresh line of spiral shells, sea glass and dried kelp. Above the beach a bluff of wind-bent pines gives shade and a soft carpet of needles. Fresh water trickles down a cleft in the rock into a mossy basin. The air smells of salt and pine resin. On clear days the far-off sails of the open sea are only white specks on the horizon, and nothing comes ashore here but crabs, seabirds and slow green waves. It is a safe place to sleep, gather shellfish and work out what comes next, so long as the tide and the afternoon sun are respected.
Driftshell Cove.hiddenInfo: Behind a curtain of ivy at the back of the pine bluff, a dry hollow in the rock holds an old sea chest, its lid rusted shut, packed with waxed sailcloth and a corroded brass spyglass.

Shell Strand.description: A curved beach of fine pale sand, littered with spiral shells, sea glass in green and amber, and ropes of dried kelp. Small waves fold onto the shore with a soft hush. Sand crabs skitter sideways into their holes at any movement, and terns stand in a neat row at the waterline, facing the wind. The sun warms the sand by midmorning and bakes it by noon.

Tidepool Shelf.description: A flat ledge of grey rock at the cove's eastern arm, pocked with clear pools left by the tide. Each pool holds its own small world: purple urchins, red anemones that close at a touch, darting blennies and mussels clustered in black ranks. At high tide the sea washes over the shelf, and the rock grows slick with green weed. Spray hangs in the air on windy days.

Pine Bluff.description: A grassy rise above the beach crowned with wind-bent pines, their trunks leaning inland and their roots gripping the sandy soil. Fallen needles make a soft, dry floor, and pinecones lie everywhere. A thin stream of fresh water runs down a mossy cleft in the rock into a cold basin. From here the whole cove is visible, bright and still below.

Gullbreak Headland.name: Gullbreak Headland
Gullbreak Headland.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Gullbreak Headland is a great blunt fist of dark rock thrust out into the open sea at the wild end of the Cerulean Coast. The wind never stops here. Waves the height of houses smash into the base of the cliffs and throw white spray a hundred feet into the air, and the whole headland booms with the impact. Thousands of seabirds nest on its ledges and sea stacks, filling the air with screaming and the rock with white streaks. The cliff top is bare turf and pink thrift, cut by sudden blowholes that roar and spit when the tide rises. The danger is real: razorclaw crabs the size of carts hunt the lower ledges, storm gulls with hooked beaks dive at anything near their nests, and the sea caves below hold something long and eel-like that hunts in the dark water. Storms roll in fast and turn the cliff paths into slick, deadly stairs.
Gullbreak Headland.hiddenInfo: Deep in the largest sea cave, above the high-water mark, a dry shelf hides a pool of fresh rainwater fed by a crack in the rock, and beside it lies a fallen bronze bell crusted with barnacles.

Spray Ledge.description: A narrow shelf of black rock halfway down the cliff, soaked by constant spray. Every big wave hits below with a deep boom that shakes the stone, and a curtain of white water rises and falls back as cold rain. Green weed makes the footing treacherous. Razorclaw crabs, broad as carts and armored in mottled red shell, wedge themselves into the cracks here and wait.

Gannet Stacks.description: Three tall pillars of rock stand just off the cliff, joined to it by a crumbling neck of stone. Every ledge is crowded with nesting seabirds, and their shrieking rises over the roar of the sea. Storm gulls, grey-backed and big as eagles, wheel overhead and dive in screaming pairs at anything that comes near their eggs. The rock is white with droppings and smells sharp.

Undertow Caves.description: At the base of the cliffs, the sea has carved a row of dark caves that fill and empty with every wave. The water inside churns green and black, sucking at the rocks, and the air is wet, cold and loud with echoes. Long shapes move under the surface. At low tide a pebble floor appears for a short while, strewn with bones and broken shell.

Bellflower Dell.name: Bellflower Dell
Bellflower Dell.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Bellflower Dell is a sunlit opening in the deep forests of the Verdania Wilds, a shallow bowl of grass where the great trees step back and let the sky in. In spring and summer the ground is blue with bellflowers, and the air hums with bees. A clear brook runs along the bottom of the dell over smooth stones, and deer come down at dawn and dusk to drink, unbothered and slow. Around the edges, oaks and beeches older than any kingdom stand in a ring, their trunks furred with moss and their roots rising from the soil like the backs of sleeping animals. Squirrels chatter in the branches, woodpeckers knock, and at night fireflies drift above the grass. There are hazelnuts, wild strawberries and clean water. The main dangers are cold nights, wandering too far into the trees, and the forest's habit of making every direction look the same.
Bellflower Dell.hiddenInfo: Inside the hollow oak, under a layer of dry leaves, a flat stone carved with a spiral rune stays warm to the touch all year, and small animals sleep curled against it in winter.

Bluebell Clearing.description: The open heart of the dell, a gentle slope of soft grass and nodding blue bellflowers that reach knee height in summer. Bees and white butterflies work the flowers all day. Sunlight pours in through the gap in the canopy and makes the whole clearing glow. Wild strawberries hide low among the stems, and rabbits sit up at the edges, watching.

Mossy Ford.description: Where the brook crosses the bottom of the dell it spreads wide and shallow over a bed of round stones. The water is cold, clean and cheerfully loud. Moss coats every rock above the waterline in thick green cushions, and ferns crowd both banks. Small trout hang in the current, and deer prints mark the soft mud at the edge.

Hollow Oak.description: An enormous oak at the dell's edge, its trunk split open at the base into a dry chamber big enough to sit in. The inside smells of old wood and leaf litter. Hazel bushes grow thick around it, heavy with nuts in autumn. Beyond the oak the true forest begins: columns of trunks fading into green shade, every direction alike.

Mossback Gorge.name: Mossback Gorge
Mossback Gorge.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Mossback Gorge is a deep green wound in the Verdania Wilds, where a cold river has cut straight down through the forest floor and into the stone beneath. The walls rise sheer on both sides, dripping with ferns, moss and hanging roots, and the canopy almost closes overhead, so the light at the bottom is dim and green. The river roars through the narrows in white rapids, and the air is full of cold mist and noise. Mossback bears, huge and shaggy with green moss growing in their fur, fish the pools and defend them with fury. Higher up, the cliff faces are draped with grey webs where hound-sized forest spiders wait for anything that climbs. Footing is slick everywhere, flash floods come with every heavy rain upstream, and a fall from the wrong ledge means the rapids. No trail leads through. The only way along is over boulders, roots and wet stone.
Mossback Gorge.hiddenInfo: Behind the largest waterfall a dry cave runs back into the gorge wall, and on its floor lies the long skeleton of a spirit stag, its antlers still faintly silver.

Rapids Run.description: The bottom of the gorge, where the river crashes through a chute of black boulders in white, thundering water. Spray soaks everything. Between rapids lie deep, dark green pools where big fish turn slowly. Driftwood is jammed high in the rocks, marking where the floods reach. The roar is so loud that nothing else can be heard down here.

Webbed Cliffs.description: A stretch of the gorge wall where roots and ledges make a rough climbing route toward the forest above. Grey sheets of web stretch between the roots, heavy with dew and the dried husks of birds. Forest spiders, brown and banded and the size of hounds, rest motionless in the shadows of the overhangs until something touches a line.

Bear Shelf.description: A wide ledge of flat rock above the river, carpeted with moss and scattered with fish bones and bark torn from fallen logs. Deep claw marks score the nearby trees. This is where the mossback bears come to eat and to sleep in the sun that reaches down at midday. The smell of bear is strong and musky.

Lilypad Reach.name: Lilypad Reach
Lilypad Reach.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Lilypad Reach is a wide sheet of shallow, still water on the quiet edge of the Meikyo Spiritfen, broken by reed beds and small islands of willow. Lily pads and pink lotus cover much of the surface, so it looks less like a lake than a floating garden. The water is warm, waist-deep at most, and so clear that small orange fish can be seen moving between the stems. Dragonflies hover everywhere. At dusk the frogs begin a steady chorus, and pale blue wisps rise from the lotus like slow sparks, drifting a little way and fading. They are harmless and seem curious, sometimes circling a raised hand before floating off. The mist is thin and soft here, the sky shows twice, once above and once in the water, and the nights are mild. Food is easy: lotus roots, water chestnuts, duck eggs in the reeds. The real risks are wet feet, insect bites and losing the way when the evening mist thickens.
Lilypad Reach.hiddenInfo: Under the roots of the oldest willow on the isle, a small stone lantern lies tipped on its side in the mud, and whenever the moon is full a faint light still glows inside it.

Reed Margin.description: The firm edge of the Reach, where dry ground gives way to tall golden reeds that rustle in every breeze. Narrow animal paths wind between them to the open water. Ducks and moorhens nest deep in the reed beds, and the mud is printed with the long toes of herons. Cattails stand like brown candles above the reeds.

Lotus Shallows.description: Open water covered with flat green lily pads and tall pink lotus flowers, some as wide as dinner plates. The water is warm and clear to the sandy bottom, and orange fish nose between the stems. Dragonflies in blue and red hover and dart. At dusk, pale blue wisps rise from the flowers and drift slowly above the water.

Willow Isle.description: A small, low island near the middle of the Reach, covered in soft grass and shaded by three old willows whose long branches trail in the water. The island is dry, sheltered and quiet. Frogs plop into the water at any movement. From under the willows the whole Reach spreads out, flat and shining, with the reeds a golden line in the distance.

Blackwater Sinks.name: Blackwater Sinks
Blackwater Sinks.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Blackwater Sinks is the deep heart of a peat bog in the Meikyo Spiritfen, where the water turns black as ink and the ground itself cannot be trusted. Thick grey mist hangs at waist height almost all day. Dead alders stand in the water like grey bones, and the moss underfoot looks solid until it swallows a leg to the hip. Pale green lights drift through the mist at night, and unlike the friendly wisps elsewhere in the fen, these lead toward the deepest sinkholes. Bog hounds, long-legged and grey, hunt in near silence. Drowned shades, cold shapes of mist with hollow eyes, rise from the black pools after dark and drain the warmth from anything they touch. The only sounds are dripping, the croak of unseen frogs and the slow gulp of gas rising from the mud. A pair of half-sunken gate posts suggests that a path once crossed here, long ago.
Blackwater Sinks.hiddenInfo: Beneath the leaning gate, the peat has preserved a sealed clay jar full of pale blue spirit salt, which keeps the drowned shades at bay when scattered in a circle.

Sunken Gate.description: Two great wooden posts, once lacquered red and now black and split, lean toward each other above a pool of dark water. Their crossbeam has fallen and lies half buried in the peat. Green lights gather here at night, drifting slowly in circles, and the frogs fall silent all at once when they come.

Quaking Peat.description: A broad stretch of brown moss and sedge that trembles underfoot like a mattress. Hidden beneath it are pockets of black water, and a wrong step drops a leg in to the thigh with a cold suck that does not want to let go. Grey mist lies low and thick. Bubbles break the surface with a slow gulp, and the air smells of rot and iron.

Drowned Alders.description: A flooded stand of dead alder trees, their bark peeled to grey and their branches bare. Black water fills the spaces between the trunks, deep and still, reflecting nothing. Bog hounds pad along the fallen logs in near silence, long-legged and grey as the mist. After dark, pale shapes rise from the water here and drift between the trees.

Palmshade Pool.name: Palmshade Pool
Palmshade Pool.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Palmshade Pool is a small, perfect oasis in a hollow between golden dunes in the Renka Mirage Sea. A spring rises from the sand into a round pool of clear blue water, ringed with date palms, fig bushes and soft green grass that ends sharply where the desert begins. The palms rattle in the dry wind, and their shade is cool even at noon. Bright finches and sandgrouse come to drink in the mornings, and a family of long-eared desert foxes visits at dusk. Ripe dates hang in heavy clusters, and the figs are sweet. By day the sun is fierce and the dunes shimmer, sometimes showing false lakes and towers on the horizon that fade on approach. By night the stars are so bright they cast shadows, and the cold comes fast. The dangers are heat, thirst away from the pool, and the mirages that make the open sand look closer and kinder than it is.
Palmshade Pool.hiddenInfo: A flat stone at the bottom of the pool covers a second, deeper spring; when it is lifted, the water runs faintly sweet and leaves a taste of honey.

Date Palm Grove.description: A ring of tall date palms around the pool, their trunks rough and scaled, their fronds clattering softly high above. Heavy clusters of amber dates hang within reach of a short climb. Fallen fronds and husks lie thick on the ground, dry enough to burn or weave. Finches flit between the fig bushes, and the shade is deep and cool.

Clear Pool.description: A round pool of startlingly clear blue water, fed from below by a gentle spring that dimples the surface. The sandy bottom is visible even at the center. Green grass and reeds grow thick around the edge, and dragonflies skim the water. The pool is cold enough to be a shock on a hot afternoon, and the water tastes clean.

Dune Crest.description: The top of the tallest dune beside the oasis, a sharp ridge of fine golden sand that hisses as it slips underfoot. From here the desert rolls away in every direction, wave after wave of gold. Heat shimmer bends the horizon, and on some afternoons a false lake and a ghostly line of towers appear in the distance. At night the stars blaze overhead.

Scaldrock Barrens.name: Scaldrock Barrens
Scaldrock Barrens.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Scaldrock Barrens is a broken wasteland at the hard edge of the Renka Mirage Sea, where the soft dunes give way to cracked red hardpan and tall pillars of wind-carved sandstone. Nothing here is gentle. The ground radiates heat until it burns through boot soles, the air shakes with mirage, and there is no shade except the shadows of the rock pillars. Dust devils spin across the flats, and full sandstorms can blot out the sun for half a day. Giant scorpions, glossy black and as long as a horse, hunt from the cracks in the hardpan. Sandwyrms, eyeless and wide-mouthed, cruise beneath the softer sand of the southern troughs and rise toward any vibration. Vultures circle all day. At night it turns bitterly cold, and the pillars moan in the wind. Sun-bleached bones mark where animals have died of thirst. There is no water anywhere on the surface.
Scaldrock Barrens.hiddenInfo: At the base of the tallest pillar, under a slab of wind-polished stone, a narrow crack drips water into a tiny basin that the scorpions avoid because of the salt crust on its rim.

Cracked Hardpan.description: A flat plain of red clay baked into six-sided plates, each edged by a crack wide enough to swallow a hand. Heat rises off it in waves that bend the horizon. Nothing grows. Black scorpions, long as horses, lie hidden in the deeper cracks with only their tail tips showing, and the dry tick of their claws is the only warning.

Wind-Cut Pillars.description: A forest of tall sandstone pillars, banded red, orange and cream, carved by the wind into mushroom caps, arches and narrow fins. Their shadows offer the only shade in the Barrens. When the wind blows, the holes in the rock moan and hoot. Vultures roost on the tops, and sand piles in drifts against the windward sides.

Sandwyrm Trough.description: A long valley of soft, deep sand between low ridges of rock. The surface looks smooth and harmless, but faint ripples run across it with no wind to cause them. Sandwyrms swim below, pale and eyeless, and burst up through the sand toward any footstep. Bleached ribs of large animals stick up from the sand at odd angles.

Chalkhill Downs.name: Chalkhill Downs
Chalkhill Downs.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Chalkhill Downs is a sweep of rolling green hills in the quiet countryside of Sanctum Ecclesia, where thin turf lies over white chalk and the air is so clean it seems to sparkle. The hills are covered in short, springy grass, wild thyme and tiny flowers in purple, yellow and white, and skylarks rise singing from them all day. Where the turf has worn away, the chalk shows through bright white. In the folds between hills, beech copses offer shade, and a cold spring bubbles up from the chalk into a clear stream lined with watercress. Sheep that went wild long ago graze in loose flocks and scatter at any sudden noise. A fallen waystone, its carving worn smooth, lies half sunk in the grass of one slope. The light is soft and golden. Nights are cool and dewy, and the only real hardships are rain, cold and the long distances between anything.
Chalkhill Downs.hiddenInfo: The fallen waystone hides a hollow cut into its underside, and in that hollow rests a small sun disc of white gold that warms in the hand and gives off a faint glow at night.

Larksong Slope.description: A long, gentle hillside of short green turf scattered with thyme, harebells and yellow vetch. Skylarks spring up from the grass and climb, singing, until they are dots against the blue. Half sunk in the grass lies a fallen waystone, its carving worn smooth by weather. Wild sheep graze in loose groups and watch with mild suspicion.

Chalk Spring.description: In a fold between two hills, cold water bubbles up from a white chalk basin into a stream so clear it is almost invisible. Watercress grows thick along its edges, and small brown trout dart away from passing shadows. The chalk around the spring is bright white, and the grass is greener here than anywhere else on the downs.

Beech Copse.description: A small wood of tall grey beeches on the shoulder of a hill, their smooth trunks rising like pillars and their leaves turning the light green and gold. The ground beneath is a deep, dry bed of copper leaves and beechnuts. Wood pigeons coo in the branches, and the copse stays still and sheltered when the wind blows across the hills.

Kestrel Fells.name: Kestrel Fells
Kestrel Fells.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Kestrel Fells is a high, bare upland on the edge of Sanctum Ecclesia, far above the gentle valleys, where grey rock breaks through thin brown grass and the weather changes in minutes. The fells roll on and on under a huge sky, cut by gullies and dotted with dark peat tarns. Kestrels hover overhead, tails fanned, and ravens call from the crags. The holy calm of the lowlands does not reach here. Storms sweep in from the north with sudden hail and lightning that strikes the high points, and thick cloud can drop to the ground and erase every landmark. Cave bears den in the gullies and are short-tempered after waking. Wild griffons, smaller and fiercer than tamed ones, nest on the crags and hunt anything that crosses open ground. A tall cairn of stacked stones marks the highest summit, the only sign that anything ever passed this way.
Kestrel Fells.hiddenInfo: Inside the summit cairn, among the stacked stones, a slab of pale marble is carved with a single sun ward that keeps lightning from striking within a few paces of it.

Fell Top Cairn.description: The highest point of the fells, a bald dome of grey rock and wiry grass topped by a tall cairn of stacked stones. The wind is fierce and constant. The whole upland spreads below, brown and grey, cut by dark gullies and shining tarns. Storms show long before they arrive, black curtains moving across the land, and lightning favors this summit.

Peat Tarns.description: A wide, soggy plateau dotted with small dark pools, their water brown as tea and cold as ice. Cotton grass nods white over the bog. Curlews call with long, rising notes. The ground between the tarns is spongy and treacherous, and wild griffons glide low over it, watching for hares and anything else that moves in the open.

Bear Gully.description: A deep, narrow cleft in the fellside, choked with boulders and stunted rowan trees. A stream trickles at the bottom, and the walls give shelter from the wind. Several dark cave mouths open in the rock. Scratched bark, tufts of brown fur and a heavy, musky smell mark them as bear dens, and the bears inside are rarely asleep for long.

Lilac Cascade.name: Lilac Cascade
Lilac Cascade.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Lilac Cascade is a hidden waterfall in the hills of the Twilight Dominion, where the sky never fully brightens and never fully darkens but stays a soft violet shading to amber at the edges. A thin, bright waterfall drops in silver threads down a wall of black basalt columns into a round pool. Lilac and pale purple flowers grow thickly around it, and at the edges of the clearing ferns and glowing blue mushrooms make soft points of light in the dusk. Large white moths drift between the blossoms. Small, sleek black deer with faintly glowing eyes come to drink and pay little attention to anything else. The water is cold and sweet. The air smells of wet stone and lilac. Twilight here is calm rather than menacing, and the deep shadows hold nothing worse than owls and foxes. The hardest part is the light: without sunrise or sunset, it is easy to lose track of time.
Lilac Cascade.hiddenInfo: One of the basalt columns behind the falling water is hollow, and inside it a seam of violet crystal hums softly and keeps the pool from ever freezing.

Cascade Pool.description: A round pool at the foot of the falls, deep blue in the middle and pale over the pebbles at its edge. The waterfall drops in silver threads from the black rock above, and its steady rush fills the clearing. Fine spray drifts across the water and catches the violet sky. Small black deer with softly glowing eyes come here to drink.

Moth Glade.description: A soft clearing of grass and lilac bushes beside the pool, heavy with purple blossom and sweet scent. Large white moths drift between the flowers on slow, powdery wings. Around the edges, ferns and clusters of glowing blue mushrooms light the ground in gentle points. The grass is dry and thick enough to sleep on.

Basalt Steps.description: A natural stair of black six-sided basalt columns climbing beside the falls, each top flat and slick with spray. Moss and tiny violet flowers grow in the cracks between them. From the highest step, the view opens over rolling dark hills under a violet and amber sky, with no lights anywhere in sight.

Hexbriar Heath.name: Hexbriar Heath
Hexbriar Heath.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: Rising (Moderate)]

Hexbriar Heath is a dark, rolling moorland in the Twilight Dominion, covered in black heather and twisted thorn bushes under the endless violet dusk. The heather grows waist-high and smells bitter, and the briars that give the heath its name are black-barked and sharp, their thorns faintly glowing purple at the tips. A scratch from them burns for hours and leaves a strange numbness. Shade hounds hunt here in packs: lean, smoky beasts whose outlines blur at the edges and that make no sound until they attack. Nightmare ravens, too large and with too many eyes, watch from the crooked standing stones that dot the high ground. Sinkholes open in the heath without warning, hidden by heather. A cold wind blows steadily across the moor, carrying the hounds' scent away from whatever they stalk. There is no shelter and no clear path, only heather, stone and violet sky.
Hexbriar Heath.hiddenInfo: Beneath the largest crooked menhir lies a small chamber lined with flat stones, and the shade hounds will not cross the circle of white lichen that grows around its entrance.

Black Heather Rise.description: A long, swelling slope of black heather, waist-high and stiff, broken by patches of briar whose thorns glow faintly purple. Walking through it is slow and noisy, and the bitter smell rises with every step. The wind runs over the heather in dark waves, and low, smoky shapes move with it, never quite in clear view.

Crooked Menhirs.description: A loose ring of tall standing stones on the highest ground of the heath, every one leaning at a different angle. Their surfaces are crusted with white lichen and old carvings worn too smooth to read. Nightmare ravens, big as dogs and with rows of small black eyes, perch on top and turn their heads together to watch.

Hound Sinkhole.description: A wide pit in the heath where the ground has fallen in, its edges ragged with overhanging heather roots. The bottom is a tangle of fallen stone and black thorn, and the walls are riddled with burrows. The smell of wet fur and old bones drifts up from below. This is where the shade hounds den between hunts.

Thistledown Vale.name: Thistledown Vale
Thistledown Vale.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Thistledown Vale is a quiet, grassy valley tucked into the hills of the Ashenmere Frontier, out of sight of the roads and far from any town. A slow creek winds along the bottom under a line of willows, and the slopes are thick with tall grass, purple thistles and white thistledown that floats in the air all summer. A small herd of wild shaggy ponies grazes the valley and moves off at a trot when approached. Rabbits are everywhere, and blackberries ripen along an old tumbled stone wall that once marked a field, now half buried in brambles. The Frontier's monsters keep to the darker country beyond the ridges, and the vale is sheltered enough that the wind rarely reaches the bottom. The nights are clear and loud with crickets. The main dangers are bramble scratches, cold dew, and walking out over the ridge into the wild land beyond.
Thistledown Vale.hiddenInfo: Inside the tumbled wall, a hollow stone holds a rusted iron key and a small tin box of dry flint and tinder, still usable.

Creekside Willows.description: The bottom of the vale, where a slow, brown creek bends lazily between banks of soft grass. Old willows lean over the water, their roots forming small dry nooks along the bank. Minnows flick in the shallows, and a kingfisher darts past in a flash of blue. The water is cool and good to drink once it settles.

Thistle Slope.description: The sunny side of the vale, covered in tall grass and purple thistles that stand above the grass. Thistledown drifts off the seed heads in white puffs and floats on the breeze. Goldfinches cling to the stems. A herd of shaggy wild ponies grazes here, brown and grey, and they lift their heads to watch anything that moves.

Tumbled Wall.description: A long line of old stone wall, fallen in places and almost buried by brambles and nettles. Moss and yellow lichen cover the stones. In late summer the brambles hang heavy with fat blackberries. Wrens and robins nest in the gaps, and the wall still breaks the wind, leaving a sheltered spot to sleep on its leeward side.

Cracktooth Hills.name: Cracktooth Hills
Cracktooth Hills.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: Rising (Moderate)]

Cracktooth Hills is a jumble of broken, rocky hills deep in the Ashenmere Frontier, where layers of grey shale have been tilted on end and weathered into rows of sharp, leaning slabs like a mouth of bad teeth. Thin scrub and dry grass grow between them, and the ground is loose and noisy underfoot. The hills are full of monsters. Dire wolves run the valleys in packs of six or more, grey and shoulder-high. Shalebacks, armored lizards the size of oxen, bask on warm rock and charge without warning. Carrion wyverns circle above the basins and drop on anything weak or alone. Old weapons, rusted and broken, lie in the gullies, left from some long-forgotten fight. The wind howls through the stone teeth at night with a sound like wolves, and sometimes it is wolves. Water is scarce, found only in muddy seeps that every beast in the hills also uses.
Cracktooth Hills.hiddenInfo: In a crack between two leaning slabs on the highest hill, a buried iron strongbox holds a dented steel helm and a pouch of tarnished silver coins.

Wolf Run.description: A long, winding valley floor between the hills, worn into a bare trail by the passage of many paws. Tufts of grey fur catch on the thornbushes, and gnawed bones lie in the dust. The valley walls are steep and loose. At dusk, dire wolves come through here at a lope, and their howls bounce from hill to hill.

Shale Teeth.description: A ridge of grey shale slabs tilted upright and leaning in jagged rows, some taller than a house. The gaps between them are narrow and cold. Loose flakes of stone slide and clatter with every step. Shalebacks, armored lizards as big as oxen, lie on the sun-warmed tops and are almost impossible to tell from the rock until they move.

Carrion Basin.description: A round, dry hollow among the hills with a muddy seep at its center, trampled by hooves and claws. Bones and rusted, broken blades lie scattered in the cracked mud. Carrion wyverns, leathery and grey, circle high above or perch on the rim, waiting. Every animal in the hills comes here to drink sooner or later.

Swansdown Lake.name: Swansdown Lake
Swansdown Lake.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Swansdown Lake is a long, still lake in the rolling hills of Rosethorn Nocturne, where the sky glows rose-gold at dusk and the night never turns fully dark. The water is smooth as glass and reflects every color of the sky. A flock of white swans lives here all year, gliding in pairs across the shallows, and their shed feathers drift along the shore. Silver birches line the eastern bank, their white bark bright in the dim light. Wild pink and red flowers climb over everything near the water. On a small point stands an old garden folly, a little round pavilion of pale stone with a cracked dome, swallowed by ivy and long abandoned. The lake is calm and safe. Fish are plentiful, the water is clean, and the swans are the only creatures that might object to company, hissing at any approach to their nests.
Swansdown Lake.hiddenInfo: Under the floor of the folly, a loose flagstone covers a small dry cellar holding a dozen dusty bottles of dark red wine, still sealed.

Swan Shallows.description: The western end of the lake, where the water is shallow and edged with reeds and floating flowers. White swans glide in pairs over the glassy surface, their reflections perfect beneath them. Feathers drift against the shore. At dusk the water turns rose and gold, and the swans settle to sleep with their heads tucked under their wings.

Silver Birch Bank.description: A stretch of shore lined with slender silver birches, their white bark glowing pale in the long dusk. The ground beneath is soft with grass and fallen leaves. Small waves lap at a pebble beach. Owls call from the trees at night, and the lake beyond is a sheet of dark silver under the rose-tinted sky.

Lakeview Folly.description: A small, round stone pavilion on a grassy point jutting into the lake, its pale columns wrapped in ivy and climbing red flowers. The dome is cracked, and moss grows on the marble floor. The stone benches inside are still whole. It is long abandoned and perfectly quiet, with the whole lake visible through its open arches.

Batwing Crags.name: Batwing Crags
Batwing Crags.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: Rising (Moderate)]

Batwing Crags is a line of tall, broken limestone cliffs in the wild borderlands of Rosethorn Nocturne, honeycombed with caves and fringed with dark red ivy. At dusk, when the sky turns rose-gold, the caves pour out clouds of bats so thick they darken the light, and the air fills with the dry rustle of thousands of wings. Most are small and harmless. Some are not: blood bats with wingspans wider than outstretched arms hunt in groups and drain their prey slowly. Stone drakes, grey and lean, sleep on the ledges looking like part of the rock and wake hungry. The cliff paths are narrow, crumbling and slick with guano, and the caves run deep into the dark. Below the crags lies a scree slope of white boulders and thorn bushes. The view from the top over the red fields is stunning, and the climb there is deadly.
Batwing Crags.hiddenInfo: Deep in the roost caverns, a side passage ends in a chamber of white flowstone where a pool of clear water reflects a crack of sky, and no bat ever enters it.

Crag Path.description: A narrow ledge trail winding up the face of the limestone cliffs, crumbling at the edges and streaked with guano. Dark red ivy hangs in curtains from above. The drop to the white scree below grows with every step. Wind gusts along the cliff, and loose stones rattle away down the slope at a touch.

Roost Caverns.description: A series of caves cut deep into the cliff, their ceilings crowded with hanging bats. The floor is thick with guano, and the air is warm, damp and sharp-smelling. The rustling never stops. Among the small bats hang larger shapes, blood bats with wings like dark leather cloaks, waiting for dusk.

Drake Ledge.description: A wide shelf near the top of the crags, open to the sky and scattered with cracked bones. Grey stone drakes lie curled along it, lean and scaled, looking like boulders until an eye opens. From here the view stretches across the red fields of the Nocturne under a glowing gold horizon.

Turtleback Islet.name: Turtleback Islet
Turtleback Islet.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Turtleback Islet is a tiny, round island in the turquoise shallows of Tsukihana Tidelace, so low and smooth that from a distance it looks like a sea turtle's shell rising from the water. A ring of white sand beach surrounds a small rise of grass and coconut palms. The sea around it is warm, waist-deep for a long way out, and so clear that every ripple of the sand below can be seen. Green sea turtles haul themselves up the beach to nest on moonlit nights and leave wide tracks in the sand. A shallow lagoon on the sheltered side holds bright fish and drifting jellies too small to sting. At night the water glows faintly blue where the waves break, and the moon lays a silver path toward the horizon. The islet is safe and peaceful. Its dangers are sunburn, a sudden squall, and the long swim to anywhere else.
Turtleback Islet.hiddenInfo: At the top of the palm knoll, buried under the roots of the oldest palm, a small shell-shaped charm of pearl lies in the sand, and while it stays there the tide never rises high enough to reach the knoll.

Nesting Beach.description: A wide crescent of soft white sand on the islet's seaward side, crisscrossed with the broad flipper tracks of nesting turtles. Small mounds mark buried eggs. The waves are small and gentle, and each one leaves a line of foam that glows faintly blue after dark. Hermit crabs trundle along the tide line in borrowed shells.

Clear Lagoon.description: A warm, shallow lagoon on the sheltered side of the islet, protected by a low sandbar. The water is a bright, glowing turquoise over white sand. Striped fish in yellow and blue dart in small schools, and tiny clear jellies drift by, harmless. Starfish lie scattered on the bottom like dropped orange stars.

Palm Knoll.description: The grassy center of the islet, a low rise shaded by a dozen leaning coconut palms. Fallen coconuts lie in the grass, and the fronds rattle overhead in the steady sea breeze. From the top, the sea spreads out on every side in bands of turquoise and deep blue, and other islands float like green smudges far away.

Kelpwrack Atoll.name: Kelpwrack Atoll
Kelpwrack Atoll.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Kelpwrack Atoll is a broken ring of reef and sandbars on the outer edge of Tsukihana Tidelace, where the gentle shallows give way to open ocean. At low tide, the reef flat stands exposed in a wide maze of sharp rock and tide pools. At high tide, nearly everything disappears beneath churning water. Strong currents race through the gaps in the ring, and the riptides can drag even a strong swimmer out to sea. A deep channel choked with giant kelp runs through the middle, home to reef sharks, long chains of stinging jellies and lashing eels as long as boats. On the sand spit at the north end lies the shattered hull of an old ship, its ribs open to the sky and its timbers grey and barnacled. Seabirds scream overhead. Storms build quickly out here, and there is no high ground at all. The tide decides what can be walked and what drowns.
Kelpwrack Atoll.hiddenInfo: Wedged under the wreck's keel, beneath the sand, a brass-bound sea chest holds a moon-tide compass whose needle always points to the nearest dry land.

Wreck Spit.description: A narrow bar of coarse sand at the north end of the atoll, the only part that stays above most tides. The broken hull of an old ship lies on its side here, grey ribs open to the sky and crusted with barnacles. Seabirds nest in its timbers and scream at any intruder. Waves break on both sides of the spit.

Reef Flat.description: A wide plain of sharp, dead reef rock exposed at low tide, riddled with pools and cracks. Every surface cuts. The pools hold spiny urchins, octopus and small trapped fish. The sea roars at the outer edge where the waves break white. When the tide turns, water floods back across the flat faster than a run.

Kelp Channel.description: A deep, fast channel through the middle of the atoll, filled with towering kelp that sways in the current like a drowned forest. The water is dark green and cold. Reef sharks circle in the shadows. Lashing eels, mottled and as long as boats, coil among the stalks, and stinging jellies drift through in long pale chains.

Birchsteam Basin.name: Birchsteam Basin
Birchsteam Basin.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Birchsteam Basin is a sheltered hollow in the snowy foothills of Yukishiro Veilpeak, ringed by silver birch trees and filled with drifting steam from a natural hot spring. The water rises from cracks in the rock into a chain of pools, the upper ones too hot to touch and the lowest perfectly warm, with mineral crusts in white and orange along their rims. Snow covers everything else in soft, deep drifts, so the steaming pools stand out like breath on a cold morning. A troop of white-furred snow monkeys comes to soak in the lowest pool and ignores anything that keeps a respectful distance. Red-capped cranes pick through the shallows of a half-frozen brook below. The air is still and quiet except for dripping water and the occasional crack of ice. The warmth makes it a safe place to survive, though the cold beyond the steam is fierce and the snow hides the way out.
Birchsteam Basin.hiddenInfo: A flat stone at the bottom of the hottest pool bears a carved frost ward, and lifting it releases water that heals small cuts and frostbite almost at once.

Birch Stand.description: A thick ring of silver birches around the basin, their white trunks marked with black and their branches heavy with snow. Underfoot the snow lies deep and soft, blue in the shadows. Tracks of hares and foxes wander between the trunks. Dead birch bark peels off in papery strips that catch fire easily.

Steaming Pool.description: A chain of natural rock pools, rimmed with white and orange mineral crust, stepping down the hillside. Steam rises thickly into the cold air and drifts away through the birches. The lowest pool is deep and perfectly warm. White snow monkeys sit soaking in it, eyes half closed, with snow settling on their heads.

Frozen Brook.description: Below the pools, the warm runoff meets a mountain brook and keeps a channel of open water flowing between shelves of ice. Red-capped cranes stand in the shallows, picking at small fish. Icicles hang from the banks and ring faintly when they fall. The air is very cold away from the steam.

Rimeback Glacier.name: Rimeback Glacier
Rimeback Glacier.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Rimeback Glacier is a vast tongue of blue-white ice crawling down from the high peaks of Yukishiro Veilpeak, cracked and ridged like the back of some enormous frozen beast. Its surface is a field of crevasses, some hidden under thin snow bridges, some open and blue to unseen depths. The wind comes off the summits sharp enough to burn skin, and blizzards can erase the world within minutes. Frost wolves hunt the glacier in packs, white on white, almost invisible until they are close. In the ice caves at the glacier's snout dwell rime trolls, hulking and slow, whose touch freezes flesh. Avalanches rumble down the side valleys after every fresh snowfall. The light is blinding by day and the cold is lethal by night. A long ridge of piled rock and boulders along the glacier's flank is the only ground that does not move.
Rimeback Glacier.hiddenInfo: Frozen inside the wall of the deepest ice cave, clearly visible through the blue ice, is a long silver spear with a wolf's-head socket, and a thin crack runs toward it as if the glacier is slowly letting it go.

Moraine Ridge.description: A long, high ridge of jumbled rocks and boulders piled along the glacier's edge, the only solid ground for miles. Lichen grows in orange patches on the stones. Frost wolves use the ridge as a lookout, and their tracks run along its crest. Avalanche debris lies in broad fans below the side valleys.

Crevasse Field.description: A broad stretch of the glacier split by countless cracks, some narrow as a hand, others wide enough to swallow a cart. Their walls glow deep blue and drop into darkness. Snow bridges span many of them, smooth and white, and some are only a few fingers thick. The wind howls across the ice, driving loose snow in stinging sheets.

Ice Cave Mouth.description: At the glacier's snout, a huge arch of blue ice opens into a cave lit by pale, cold light filtering through the ice. Meltwater drips constantly. Inside, tunnels branch away into the dark. Deep scrapes in the floor, gnawed bones and the smell of old meat mark the lair of the rime trolls.

Skypool Tarn.name: Skypool Tarn
Skypool Tarn.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Skypool Tarn is a small mountain lake high in the Aetherglass Reaches, so still and clear that it holds a perfect copy of the sky. Clouds drift across its surface as they drift overhead, and the floating stone fragments that hang above the highlands appear twice, once in the air and once in the water. Soft green pasture surrounds the tarn, full of white clover and tiny blue gentians, and the floating stones cast slow-moving pools of shade across it. Wild goats with curling horns graze the slopes. A line of small stones hovers low beside the water, close enough to the ground to climb from one to the next. The wind is cool and steady, the light is brilliant, and the silence is broken only by birdsong and the wind in the grass. It is a calm, lovely place to begin, with clean water and wide views, though the edges of the highland drop away more suddenly than they appear.
Skypool Tarn.hiddenInfo: The lowest floating stone hides a shallow basin on its upper side, filled with rainwater and a few smooth pebbles that glow faintly and slowly lift into the air when warmed in the hand.

Tarn Shore.description: The edge of a small, perfectly still lake, its water clear enough to show every pebble and calm enough to mirror the whole sky. Clouds move across the surface, and the floating stones above appear again below. Soft grass and white clover run right to the waterline. Small trout rise and leave circles that slowly fade.

Shadow Pasture.description: A broad, gently sloping meadow of green grass and blue gentians around the tarn. High above, floating stone fragments drift slowly, and their shadows slide across the grass like passing clouds. Wild goats with curling horns graze here and watch with yellow eyes, then go back to eating.

Drift Stone Steps.description: A line of flat stones hovering beside the tarn, the lowest barely a step above the grass and each one a little higher than the last. They bob very slightly underfoot. Moss and small flowers grow on their tops. From the highest stone, the Reaches spread out in shimmering plains and distant floating islands.

Sundered Mesas.name: Sundered Mesas
Sundered Mesas.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Sundered Mesas is a canyon country in the Aetherglass Reaches where the land has shattered into towering flat-topped mesas of pale, glassy rock, some still rooted to the ground and some torn loose and drifting slowly in the air. Between them, the canyons drop hundreds of feet to dry riverbeds.
