The wind is the first danger: violent gusts and updrafts roar through the gaps without warning, strong enough to throw anything off an edge. Natural stone arches link some of the mesas, narrow and crumbling. Storm drakes, sleek and blue-scaled, nest in hollows on the mesa tops and dive on intruders trailing crackles of lightning. Wild griffins hunt from the heights. Loose drifting rocks sometimes collide with a grinding crash, raining stone into the canyons. The views are dizzying and beautiful, with light flashing off the glassy cliffs, but the ground is never as steady as it looks.
Sundered Mesas.hiddenInfo: Inside a hollow beneath the longest arch, a slab of sky-blue crystal set into the rock pulses softly, and while anything touches it, the wind in the canyon goes still.

Mesa Rim.description: The flat top of a great pale mesa, bare rock and tough grass, ending in a sheer drop on every side. The glassy cliff faces flash in the sun. Nearby mesas float loose in the air, turning slowly. Gusts roar up from the canyon without warning, and loose grit stings the eyes.

Gale Bridge.description: A long, natural stone arch spanning the gap between two mesas, barely wider than a cart and cracked along its length. The canyon floor lies hundreds of feet below. The wind funnels through the gap with a constant roar, and it shoves at anything on the arch in sudden, heavy blows.

Drake Hollow.description: A wide bowl worn into the top of a mesa, lined with scorched rock and scattered with shed blue scales. Storm drakes nest here in rough piles of stone. The air tastes of metal, and every hair stands on end. When a drake takes flight, small lightning crackles along its wings.

Sedgewater Swale.name: Sedgewater Swale
Sedgewater Swale.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Sedgewater Swale is a long, shallow dip in the endless golden steppe of the Kagaribi Duskfields, where rainwater gathers into a reedy pond and the grass grows thicker and greener than anywhere around it. The sky here is always in golden hour, copper and amber overhead, and the light lies warm and low across everything. Small herds of tawny antelope graze the swale, flicking their tails and bounding off in graceful leaps when startled. Wild ducks and geese rest on the pond. A low hill at one end gives a long view over the grasslands, where distant storm-beast herds look like dark smudges flickering with lightning far away. They never come down into the swale. Grass seed, duck eggs and pond water make survival possible, and the steady breeze keeps the insects down. The real hardships are the vast distances, the lack of trees, and the strange timelessness of a sun that never sets.
Sedgewater Swale.hiddenInfo: On the hilltop, under the turf, lies a ring of flat stones carved with wind spirals; on still days, sitting at its center brings a cool breeze from nowhere.

Swale Pond.description: A shallow pond at the lowest point of the swale, ringed with sedge and tall reeds that glow gold in the low light. The water is brown but clean. Ducks and grey geese float in the middle and grumble at any disturbance. Frogs sing from the reeds, and the mud at the edges is printed with antelope hooves.

Antelope Grass.description: A broad sweep of thick, green-gold grass filling the bottom of the swale, rippling in long waves under the breeze. Tawny antelope graze in small herds, lifting their heads and flicking their ears at every sound. Grasshoppers leap at every step. The copper sky hangs low and warm overhead.

Kite Hill.description: A low, rounded hill at the end of the swale, crowned with short grass and a few wind-bent shrubs. Small hawks hang in the steady wind above it. From the top, the steppe rolls away to every horizon, and far off, dark herds of storm-beasts drift across the plain with lightning flickering over them.

Hoofbreak Plain.name: Hoofbreak Plain
Hoofbreak Plain.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Hoofbreak Plain is an open stretch of the Kagaribi Duskfields where the great storm-beast herds pass on their migrations, and the land shows it. The grass is trampled flat in wide brown bands, the ground is churned into dried ruts, and scorch marks scar the earth wherever lightning has struck. When a herd comes through, the plain shakes, the air crackles, and bolts leap from the beasts' backs to the ground. Being caught in the open then means being crushed or burned. Between migrations the plain belongs to dusk raptors, huge birds that dive at anything smaller than an ox, and to packs of grass jackals that follow the herds to pick off the weak. Grass fires flare up after lightning and race with the wind. A single enormous boulder stands in the middle of the plain, the only cover for miles. The copper sky never darkens, and there is nowhere to hide from it.
Hoofbreak Plain.hiddenInfo: Beneath the lone boulder, a narrow gap leads into a small dry cave, and the storm-beast herds always split around the boulder as if something under it warns them away.

Trampled Track.description: A band of earth half a mile wide where the storm-beast herds pass, the grass beaten flat and the ground torn into hard ridges and ruts. Dried dung and shed hair lie everywhere. The ground hums faintly underfoot when a herd is near, long before it comes into view. Grass jackals trot along the edges, noses down.

Lightning Scar.description: A wide, blackened patch of plain where lightning and fire have burned the grass to ash. The earth is fused into glassy streaks in places, and the smell of smoke lingers. Dusk raptors, broad-winged and copper-brown, circle overhead, watching the open ground for anything that moves.

Lone Boulder.description: A single huge grey boulder standing alone in the middle of the plain, its sides streaked with lichen and lightning burns. It is the only shade and the only cover for miles. Raptor feathers and small bones collect at its base. From its top, the plain stretches flat and endless under the copper sky.

Shimmerpool Cavern.name: Shimmerpool Cavern
Shimmerpool Cavern.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Shimmerpool Cavern is a wide, quiet cave in the upper reaches of Kurogane Deephollow, close enough to the surface that a shaft of real daylight falls through a hole in its roof. Below that shaft lies a still underground lake, clear as glass and glowing faintly from within, where mana-rich water lights the bottom in soft blue and green. The ceiling above is covered with glowworms, thousands of tiny blue lights that make the vault look like a night sky. Blind white fish drift in the shallows, and small pale bats flit out through the daylight shaft at dusk. The air is cool and steady, and the only sounds are dripping water and the soft echo of the lake. Pale mushrooms, safe to eat, grow on the damp rocks. It is a gentle place to wake: calm, lit and sheltered. Its dangers are the cold, the dark tunnel behind the vault, and slipping on wet stone.

The layout is the same on every visit. The Daylight Shaft is the way in, down a slope of moss and roots under the hole in the roof. The Underground Lake fills the middle. The Glowworm Vault rises at the far end, and behind it one narrow tunnel slopes down into the deeper Kurogane Deephollow: the only other way out, and it leaves this cavern. Nobody lives here, and nobody else is inside unless they came in by the shaft or the tunnel.
Shimmerpool Cavern.hiddenInfo: At the deepest point of the lake, a ring of quartz crystals surrounds a fist-sized geode that glows brighter whenever anything with ill intent enters the cavern.

Daylight Shaft.description: A spot near the cavern's edge where a round hole in the roof lets in a column of real daylight. Ferns and moss grow in the light, bright green against the grey stone, and roots dangle from the rim far above. Pale bats stream out through it at dusk. When it rains, water falls straight down through it in a silver thread.

Underground Lake.description: A broad, still lake filling most of the cavern, its water perfectly clear and lit from below by a soft blue and green glow. Every stone on the bottom can be seen. Blind white fish drift slowly in the shallows. Drips fall from the ceiling and send rings spreading across the surface, and the echoes go on for a long time.

Glowworm Vault.description: The high, arched part of the cave, where the ceiling is covered with thousands of glowworms, tiny blue points of light like a field of stars. Fine silk threads hang down from them, glittering. The floor is smooth, dry stone ridged with old flowstone. It is completely silent except for the distant drip of water.

Blackdrop Chasm.name: Blackdrop Chasm
Blackdrop Chasm.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Blackdrop Chasm is a vast vertical crack in the stone of Kurogane Deephollow, so deep that its bottom cannot be seen from the top. The walls are black rock seamed with veins of glowing violet mana that pulse slowly like a heartbeat, giving just enough light to see a few steps ahead. Narrow ledges and natural rock bridges cross the darkness. Wind rises from below, warm and smelling of minerals. Crystal spiders, translucent and as large as dogs, weave webs of glassy thread between the walls and hunt anything that touches them. Deep crawlers, long and many-legged, climb up the walls from below. Rockfalls happen often, signaled by a rising rattle, and the sound of falling stone goes on for a long time. Far below, at a rubble floor reached only by a long, dangerous descent, there is water and grey fungus. The chasm is beautiful in its violet glow and lethal at every step.
Blackdrop Chasm.hiddenInfo: Partway down the chasm, a single violet mana vein runs into a small hollow where a perfect sphere of polished obsidian sits, warm to the touch and humming.

Chasm Lip.description: The upper edge of the chasm, where a sloping shelf of black rock ends in a sheer drop into darkness. Glowing violet veins run down the walls, fading into the depths. A warm wind blows up from below, carrying the smell of minerals. Pebbles kicked over the edge fall for a long time before the faint click of landing.

Crystal Web Ledge.description: A narrow ledge halfway down the chasm wall, bridged to the far side by a thin span of natural rock. Glassy webs stretch between the walls, catching the violet light like frost. Crystal spiders, clear-bodied and big as dogs, sit motionless in them. The ledge is slick and crumbling at the edges.

Rubble Floor.description: The bottom of the chasm, a jumble of fallen boulders and broken stone in near darkness, lit only by faint violet glimmers far above. Grey fungus grows on the rocks, and a cold stream trickles between them. The scrape of deep crawlers moving on the walls echoes out of the dark. Fresh rockfall lies everywhere.

Butterfly Lagoon.name: Butterfly Lagoon
Butterfly Lagoon.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Butterfly Lagoon is a still, green-blue pool at the edge of the Shingetsu Evergrove, where a slow jungle stream widens into a lagoon ringed by a narrow beach of pale sand. Thousands of butterflies gather here in shimmering clouds, blue, gold, orange and green, settling on the warm sand to sip minerals and lifting in bright waves when disturbed. Giant fig trees lean over the water, their roots forming arches and their branches heavy with fruit. Orchids in pink and white cascade from the trunks. Turtles bask on fallen logs, and small green parrots chatter in the canopy. The jungle here is calm and generous, offering fruit, clean water and dappled shade, and the canopy seems to part over the lagoon to let a soft column of light reach the water. The dangers are heat, humidity, insects, and the green maze of jungle that starts a few steps from the sand.
Butterfly Lagoon.hiddenInfo: Inside the arched roots of the largest fig tree, a moss-covered stone tablet carved with strange square letters lies half buried, and the butterflies always gather thickest around it.

Lagoon Beach.description: A narrow crescent of warm, pale sand along the lagoon's edge, covered with clouds of butterflies in blue, gold and orange. They rise in a bright, fluttering wave at any movement and settle again a moment later. The water is calm and clear. Turtles bask on logs nearby, sliding in with a soft splash when startled.

Fig Tree Arch.description: A giant fig tree leaning over the lagoon, its roots arching above the ground to form a natural shelter tall enough to stand in. The branches are heavy with soft purple figs, and green parrots squabble over them. Moss and ferns cover the roots. The shade beneath is deep and cool.

Orchid Stream.description: The slow jungle stream that feeds the lagoon, winding between mossy banks under a tunnel of leaves. Pink and white orchids hang from the trunks along its edge in long sprays. Small silver fish dart in the brown-green water. The light falls in moving golden patches, and the air smells sweet and damp.

Stranglevine Deep.name: Stranglevine Deep
Stranglevine Deep.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Stranglevine Deep is the darkest, thickest part of the Shingetsu Evergrove, where the canopy closes completely overhead and the jungle floor sinks into permanent green twilight. Vines as thick as arms hang everywhere, and some of them move. Stranglevines coil slowly around anything that stands still too long and tighten like a constrictor. Massive buttress roots form walls and corridors that turn the forest floor into a maze. In the low ground, pitcher plants big enough to swallow a dog grow in a sweet-smelling bog. Jungle cats, black and nearly invisible, hunt from the branches, and constrictor serpents lie along the roots. The air is hot, wet and heavy, buzzing with insects. Moss-covered blocks of carved stone lie scattered through the roots, fragments of some ancient ruin swallowed long ago. Sound carries strangely here, and the jungle seems to shift its paths between one glance and the next.
Stranglevine Deep.hiddenInfo: Deep in the root maze, a carved stone face with closed eyes is set into the base of the largest tree, and the stranglevines never grow within ten paces of it.

Root Maze.description: A tangle of giant buttress roots, taller than a house, forming twisting walls and dead-end corridors across the forest floor. Moss covers everything in a thick green skin. Carved stone blocks lie half swallowed among the roots. Vines hang from above, and some shift slowly when nothing touches them.

Pitcher Plant Bog.description: A low, soggy hollow where the ground turns to black mud and standing water. Huge pitcher plants rise from it, green and red-veined, their mouths wide enough to swallow a dog. They smell sweet as honey. Insects drone over the bog in clouds, and the bones of small animals float in the plants' fluid.

Jaguar Ridge.description: A raised spine of rock and roots running through the jungle, slightly higher and drier than the rest. Thick branches stretch over it at head height. Jungle cats, black-coated and silent, lie along them, hard to see in the shadow. Claw marks score the bark, and constrictor serpents sun themselves on the warm rocks.

Fireweed Valley.name: Fireweed Valley
Fireweed Valley.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Fireweed Valley is a wide, green valley in the foothills of Kagutsuchi Emberwake, where an ancient lava flow has cooled into black rock and slowly turned to rich soil. Now the valley is covered in tall spires of pink and magenta fireweed that sway in the warm wind. A warm stream runs down the middle over black stones, heated by springs far upslope, and its water is pleasant to bathe in. Red dragonflies hover in clouds above it. Bamboo groves grow along the valley sides, creaking softly. At one end, an arch of old black lava stands like a gate, with ferns sprouting from its cracks. The distant volcano smokes peacefully on the horizon, and the sky at dusk burns red-orange. The valley is safe and warm, and the soil is full of edible roots and berries. The main hazards are sharp rock underfoot and the heat of the midday sun on black stone.
Fireweed Valley.hiddenInfo: Inside the lava arch, a small chamber holds a pool of clear water heated to the perfect temperature, fed by the stream through a carved stone dragon's head worn smooth with age.

Fireweed Slope.description: A broad hillside covered in tall spires of pink and magenta fireweed, swaying in the warm breeze. Bees and butterflies work the flowers all day. Between the stems, patches of black lava rock show through. At dusk the flowers seem to glow under the red-orange sky, and the whole slope shimmers.

Warm Stream.description: A clear stream running down the center of the valley over smooth black stones. The water is warm, heated by distant springs, and steam rises faintly from it in the cool mornings. Red dragonflies hover above it in clouds. Bamboo creaks along the banks, and small brown frogs sit on the warm rocks.

Lava Arch.description: A tall natural arch of old black lava standing at the head of the valley, rough-textured and crusted with orange lichen. Ferns sprout from its cracks. Through it, the distant volcano is framed, smoking gently against the sky. The ground around it is warm, and the black rock holds the day's heat long into the night.

Brimstone Steps.name: Brimstone Steps
Brimstone Steps.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: Rising (Moderate)]

Brimstone Steps is a raw, terraced field of volcanic ground high on the slopes of Kagutsuchi Emberwake, where the earth is still very much alive. Fumaroles hiss jets of yellow, sulfur-stinking steam from cracks in the rock, and the ground is crusted with yellow and white mineral deposits. Pools of boiling mud bubble and pop. In places, the crust is thin enough to break and drop a foot into scalding water. Lava tubes run beneath the slope, some open at the surface like dark mouths, glowing faintly orange deep inside. Fire salamanders as long as wagons swim in the hottest pools and spit flame. Ember imps, small and quick, skitter over the rocks and swarm anything that disturbs them. Gas pockets can make the air unbreathable without warning, and every few hours the ground shudders. The sky is hazed with smoke, and at night the whole slope glows red.
Brimstone Steps.hiddenInfo: In the deepest lava tube, where the glow is brightest, a vein of red fire crystal runs through the rock, and a chunk broken from it stays warm for months.

Fumarole Field.description: A broad terrace of yellow and white crusted rock, split by cracks that hiss jets of steam. The air reeks of sulfur and stings the eyes. Pools of grey mud bubble and burst with wet pops. The crust underfoot rings hollow in places, and patches of it are thin enough to break into scalding water.

Lava Tube.description: A dark, round tunnel opening into the slope, its walls smooth and ridged like the inside of a throat. The air inside is hot and dry. Far down the tube, a faint orange glow pulses. Ember imps, small, red and quick, cling to the ceiling in clusters and chitter at any sound.

Salamander Pools.description: A cluster of steaming pools in shades of blue, green and orange, ringed with brittle mineral terraces. The hottest pools boil. In them swim fire salamanders as long as wagons, their skin glowing like coals, and they spit gouts of flame when anything comes near. Heat shimmers above the water.

Crabapple Hill.name: Crabapple Hill
Crabapple Hill.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Crabapple Hill is a gentle, rounded hill in the farm country of the Crownveil Sovereignty, far from the roads, where an orchard planted long ago has gone completely wild. Gnarled crabapple and pear trees grow in uneven rows half lost in long grass, white with blossom in spring and heavy with small sour apples and hard pears in autumn. An old dry-stone wall runs around the base of the hill, collapsed in places, with a wild beehive humming in one of its gaps. A wildflower meadow covers the hilltop, thick with poppies, cornflowers and clover. Rabbits, hedgehogs and a family of red foxes live among the trees. From the top, green farmland rolls away to white walls far off on the horizon. The hill is sheltered, quiet and safe, with fruit, honey for the careful, and clean water from a spring at the foot of the wall. The worst threats are bee stings, rain and a stomach ache from too many green apples.
Crabapple Hill.hiddenInfo: Beneath the oldest pear tree, a buried clay pot holds a pair of rusted pruning shears, a silver ring engraved with a crowned apple, and seeds that still sprout.

Feral Orchard.description: The slope of the hill, covered in gnarled crabapple and pear trees growing in rough, half-lost rows. Long grass fills the spaces between them. In spring the branches are white with blossom, and in autumn they hang heavy with small red apples and hard green pears. Windfalls lie in the grass, and wasps buzz over them.

Beehive Wall.description: An old dry-stone wall running around the foot of the hill, collapsed in places and furred with moss and ivy. In one gap, a wild beehive hangs in golden combs, humming loudly. A small spring trickles out from under the stones into a mossy pool. Hedgehogs nose through the leaves along the wall's base.

Hilltop Meadow.description: The rounded top of the hill, open to the sky and thick with poppies, cornflowers and clover. Butterflies drift across it, and the grass bends in the breeze. From here the green farmland of the Sovereignty rolls away in every direction, and distant white walls catch the sun on the horizon.

Hartwild Chase.name: Hartwild Chase
Hartwild Chase.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Hartwild Chase is an old royal hunting forest in the Crownveil Sovereignty, abandoned for so long that it has turned truly wild. Massive oaks and dark yews crowd together, and the old rides cut through the forest have grown over with bracken and thorn. The game once protected here has grown huge and bold. Great harts with antlers like tree branches lead herds through the clearings and charge anything that comes near in the rutting season. Wild boar the size of ponies root through the leaf litter and attack without warning. In the thickest parts, owlbears den, feathered and clawed and terribly strong, and a wolf pack hunts the edges. A crumbling stone park wall, overgrown with ivy, runs for miles through the trees, broken in many places. The forest is dim, damp and full of sounds: crashing in the undergrowth, distant bellows, the hoot of an owl that might not be an owl.
Hartwild Chase.hiddenInfo: Set into the broken park wall is a stone niche carved with a crowned stag, and behind its loose back panel lies a silver hunting horn that makes every beast in earshot freeze for a moment when blown.

Stag Clearing.description: A wide, grassy clearing among massive oaks, the grass cropped short and churned by hooves. Great harts graze here in herds, with antlers broad as tree limbs. The trees around the edge are scarred where they rub their antlers. In the rutting season, the clearing rings with bellowing and the crack of clashing horns.

Owlbear Thicket.description: A dense, dark tangle of holly, yew and thorn, so thick that the light barely reaches the ground. Broken branches and loose feathers mark a trail into the center. Deep claw gouges score the trunks, and a sharp, musky smell hangs in the air. Owlbears den here, and their low hooting carries through the shadows.

Broken Park Wall.description: A long, crumbling stone wall winding through the forest, overgrown with ivy and moss and fallen in many places. Its top is capped with worn carved stones. Wild boar root along its base, churning the earth into mud. Wolf tracks follow the wall, and the gaps in it make the only easy paths through the thorn.

Raybloom Shallows.name: Raybloom Shallows
Raybloom Shallows.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Open water · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Raybloom Shallows is a wide sheet of turquoise water over white sand just off the eastern beaches of the Cerulean Coast, below the broken tiers of the sunken amphitheater. The sea here is waist deep for a long way out, warm in the afternoon and so clear that every ripple throws a moving net of light across the bottom. Spotted rays glide over the sand in loose flocks, green turtles graze the seagrass, and small striped fish hang in clouds around a few round heads of coral. Above the surface, a long low sandbar shows at half tide, crusted with drift and visited by terns and sandpipers. The weather is mild, with a soft onshore breeze and the odd warm shower. Nothing here hunts anything larger than a shrimp. The worst a castaway meets is sunburn, a stinging jelly drifting in on the tide, or a crab defending its hole.
Raybloom Shallows.hiddenInfo: Half buried in the sand at the seaward edge of the ray meadow lies a small bronze lantern washed down from the amphitheater, its glass still whole, and when it is rubbed clean it glows faintly blue under water.

Tern Sandbar.description: A long low bar of white sand that rises out of the sea at half tide and shrinks to a narrow spine at high water. It is above water and dry enough to sleep on, crusted with bleached driftwood, cuttlefish bones and tangled weed. Terns and sandpipers run along the edges picking at the wet sand. There is no shade and no fresh water, only the wide bright sea on every side and the beaches to the west.

Ray Meadow.description: An underwater field of soft seagrass a few feet below the surface, rippling gently with the swell. Spotted rays settle into the sand here and flap up in clouds of silt when disturbed. Green turtles crop the grass with slow, steady bites and ignore almost everything. Small fish dart between the blades. The light is green and gold, the water warm, and a swimmer can stand up almost anywhere with their head clear.

Coral Heads.description: A scatter of round coral heads rising from the sand, mostly underwater, though their flat crowns break the surface at low tide and a person can stand on them. Below the surface they are crowded with life: striped damselfish, blue tangs, purple fans and slow cleaner shrimp. Small reef eels peer from holes and pull back at once. Drifting jellies sometimes catch in the eddies here and sting bare skin.

Squall Reach.name: Squall Reach
Squall Reach.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Open water · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Squall Reach is open blue water off the south-east of the Cerulean Coast, past the last beach, where nothing lies to the east but more sea. The swell runs long and heavy here, lifting and dropping anything afloat by the height of a man, and a steady current pulls away from shore toward the ocean. Most afternoons a dark squall line marches in from the east with sheets of rain, sudden wind and white-capped chop. Grey reef sharks patrol the deeper water, and frigatebirds and hook-beaked storm gulls hunt flying fish at the surface and will strike at anything small that floats. Little stands above the waves: a single stack of black rock ringed with surf, and great mats of drifting brown weed that hold crabs, small fish and the odd tired seabird. This is real danger for a weak swimmer. The current, the cold rain and the sharks do not forgive mistakes.
Squall Reach.hiddenInfo: Wedged in a crack near the top of the rock stack is a sealed clay jar from a long-sunk trading ship, still holding dry tinder, a flint and a coil of tarred rope.

Lone Stack.description: A single stack of black rock standing out of the open sea, its lower sides crusted with barnacles and battered white by surf. Above the water line a rough ledge and a few cracked hollows give room to sit or sleep, wet with spray. Storm gulls nest on top and scream at anyone who climbs near. Rainwater collects in shallow dips after each squall, brackish but drinkable in need.

Drift Weed Mats.description: Broad rafts of brown floating weed, some as wide as a house, ride the swell on the surface. They will hold a light body if it spreads out flat, though they sag and tear. Under them hide crabs, tiny fish and young turtles, and above them frigatebirds circle. The mats move with the current, slowly away from land, and break apart when a squall hits.

Sharkwater Drop.description: Underwater, past the rock, the bottom falls away into a deep clear blue with no floor in sight. Grey reef sharks cruise here in loose groups, curious and twitchy, quick to bite anything that thrashes. Shoals of silver jacks wheel past like thrown coins. The current is strong below the surface, and a swimmer who drifts too far out loses sight of the stack and the land.

Coilwater Deep.name: Coilwater Deep
Coilwater Deep.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Open water · Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: Rising (Moderate)]

Coilwater Deep is a stretch of dark blue open sea north of the Cerulean Coast, between the lighthouse isle and the ship graveyard. The water here is far too deep to see the bottom, cold below a thin warm top layer, and heavy with a slow swell. This is where wild sea serpents come to hunt. Long finned shapes in green, blue and bronze coil through the shoals of tuna and squid, rising to breathe with a hiss of spray and sinking again. They fight each other over kills and will take a swimmer as easily as a seal. To a newborn serpent they are both rivals and the closest thing to kin. Something larger lives lower still: a shadow the size of a ship that passes beneath every few days and sends the serpents scattering. Above the surface there is only the snapped mast and tilted deck of a drifting wreck. This water is deadly for anything weak.
Coilwater Deep.hiddenInfo: In the flooded hold of the drifting wreck, beneath waterlogged crates, a lead-lined box holds a sea serpent egg turned to stone and a page of faded notes about where the wild serpents lay their clutches.

Snapped Mast Hulk.description: A drifting cargo ship, mostly sunk, with its main mast snapped off and lying flat in the water, still lashed by rigging. The mast and a tilted stretch of deck sit above water, slick with weed and gull droppings, and roll with every swell. Barnacles crust the hull below the surface, and small fish shelter in its shade. Serpents sometimes rub their scales against the wreck.

Serpent Run.description: Underwater, in the blue middle depths, a broad lane where shoals of tuna and squid pass and the wild sea serpents follow to hunt. Long finned bodies flash past, trailing bubbles as they turn. They test newcomers with feints and snapping jaws, and a larger serpent will claim the best water and drive off rivals. A serpent who holds its ground may be tolerated here. Anything weaker is food.

Shadowfall Drop.description: Underwater, the sea falls away into black water so deep no light reaches the bottom. Cold upwellings rise from below, carrying the smell of something huge. Every few days a shadow the length of a warship moves slowly beneath, and one pale arm as thick as a tree trunk sometimes reaches up into the blue. The serpents flee when it comes. Nothing sensible lingers here.

Sunwarm Shoal.name: Sunwarm Shoal
Sunwarm Shoal.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Open water · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Sunwarm Shoal is a warm, shallow stretch of sea off the desert coast of the Renka Mirage Sea. To the west, golden dunes roll down to the shore and a line of date palms leans over the beach. Out in the shallows stands one small islet of pale sandstone, wind-carved and hollowed, its top crowned with a few tough shrubs. The water is clear green over sand and warm as a bath by afternoon. Bright parrotfish crunch the rocks, rays bury themselves in the sand, and sea turtles haul out on the islet to rest. Pelicans and white egrets fish the shallows. Heat shimmer over the water sometimes paints false islands on the horizon. The real dangers are small: sunstroke, thirst, sharp coral and a stinging sand ray stepped on by accident. It is a quiet place to wake up and gather strength.
Sunwarm Shoal.hiddenInfo: Inside a wind-carved hollow on the islet, a sealed jar of blue glass from an old caravan ship lies wedged in the sand, and it still holds sweet water and a folded star chart.

Sandstone Islet.description: A small islet of pale sandstone rising a few yards above the sea, its sides carved by wind into scoops and hollows that give real shade. Tough salt shrubs grow in the cracks, and turtles haul up on the low shelf to doze in the sun. It is above water and dry, the only place to stand for some distance. Seabirds have left white streaks across the top.

Parrotfish Gardens.description: Underwater, a few feet down, low beds of coral and rubble spread around the islet. Parrotfish in green and pink crunch at the stone with beaklike mouths, leaving clouds of fine sand. Small wrasses clean anything that holds still. The water is warm and gold with sunlight. Sea urchins and sharp coral edges are the main danger, along with a moray that guards one crack and only bites if poked.

Pelican Flats.description: Knee-deep shallows of rippled sand reaching back toward the desert shore, on the surface and easy to wade. Pelicans glide low in lines and drop with a splash, and egrets stalk the edges. Sand rays bury themselves here with only their eyes showing, and a careless step earns a painful sting. Afternoon heat makes the air shimmer so the dunes and palms seem to float.

Dustwind Swell.name: Dustwind Swell
Dustwind Swell.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Open water · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Dustwind Swell is open warm sea off the rocky desert coast of the Renka Mirage Sea, where sandstone cliffs stand red and gold to the west and nothing but water stretches east. Hot winds pour off the desert and meet the sea breeze, and the clash brings sudden squalls of rain and blown sand that turn the water brown and rough. A strong current sweeps along the foot of the cliffs. Below the surface, rocky reefs fall away in steps where barracuda shoal and long reef eels hunt from the cracks. Blacktip sharks patrol the edges, and fish eagles nest high on the cliffs, diving for anything near the top of the water. Above the water there is only a broken shelf of fallen cliff stone and a few tumbled boulders at the waterline. This is open sea, dangerous to a weak swimmer and to anyone caught out in a squall.
Dustwind Swell.hiddenInfo: Behind a curtain of dripping water in one cliff crack, reachable only at low tide, lies a dry grotto holding the bones of an old smuggler's skiff and a strongbox of tarnished silver coins.

Fallen Stone Shelf.description: A jumble of huge sandstone blocks that broke from the cliffs and now lie at the waterline, the top ones above water and warm from the sun. Waves surge through the gaps and slam into hollows with a boom. The rock gives a place to stand, rest and dry out, but squalls wash spray over everything, and fish eagles watch from the cliffs above.

Eel Steps.description: Underwater, the reef falls away from the cliffs in broad steps of red rock thick with sponges and sea fans. Every crack seems to hold a reef eel, some longer than a man, mottled and quick, striking at fish and fingers alike. Barracuda hang in silver walls further out. The current tugs hard here, pulling along the cliff toward open water.

Sandrain Chop.description: On the surface well off the cliffs, the open sea runs in long warm swells that turn to steep chop when a squall arrives. Rain mixed with blown desert sand stings the skin and turns the water brown. Blacktip sharks circle below, drawn by thrashing. There is nothing to hold on to here, and a tired swimmer can be carried far out to sea within an hour.

Duneshadow Trench.name: Duneshadow Trench
Duneshadow Trench.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Open water · Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: Rising (Moderate)]

Duneshadow Trench is a deep blue rift in the sea below the sandstone cliffs east of the great labyrinth, where the coastal shelf breaks off and plunges into open ocean. The cliffs throw long shadows over the water each afternoon, and the surface is warm while the depths are cold and dark. Wild sea serpents hunt here in numbers, sand-gold and banded, riding the upwelling to catch shoals of sardines and the big squid that rise at dusk. They are territorial and quick to strike, but a serpent who holds its own is accepted among them, and their calls carry for miles through the water. Lower still lives a whale-eater, a grey shape with a jaw like a cave mouth, which rises only to feed. Above water, a tall needle of sandstone stands at the trench edge, and its ledges are the only footing for a castaway. This is very dangerous water.
Duneshadow Trench.hiddenInfo: Halfway down the trench wall, a sunken stone doorway carved with the same maze patterns as the great labyrinth leads into a flooded passage, sealed long ago and now home only to blind white crabs.

Sandstone Needle.description: A tall needle of red and gold sandstone standing alone at the edge of the trench, its foot in deep water. Above water, narrow ledges ring the stone, wide enough to sit on and sheltered from the wind on the cliff side. Cormorants dry their wings on the top. Below the ledges the water turns dark blue at once, and long shapes sometimes rise beside the rock to breathe.

Serpent Upwelling.description: Underwater, where cold water rises up the trench wall, sardines gather in shining balls and the wild serpents come to feed. Gold-banded bodies wind through the shoals, snapping and twisting, calling to each other in low clicking hums. They challenge newcomers, circling close with fins raised. A serpent who stands firm may share the hunt. Anything weaker is driven off or eaten.

Coldjaw Hollow.description: Underwater, deep in the trench where the light fades to near black, the water is cold and very still. Bones of whales and serpents litter the ledges below. This is where the whale-eater rests, a grey bulk longer than three ships with a jaw like a cave mouth. When it stirs, the whole trench shudders and every living thing flees upward toward the light.

Softfin Lagoon.name: Softfin Lagoon
Softfin Lagoon.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Open water · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

Softfin Lagoon is a sheltered sheet of turquoise water in Tsukihana Tidelace, lying between the moon palace isle and the green jungle islands to the east. Reefs on every side break the swell, so the water stays calm, warm and clear down to its white sand floor. By day the light is bright and blue. By night the moon lays a silver path across the lagoon and tiny glowing plankton spark around anything that moves. Turtles graze the seagrass, small rays and silver fish drift in loose schools, and herons stand in the shallows. A low ring of reef flat shows at low tide, and a tiny islet of sand with two leaning palms rises near the middle, offering coconuts and shade. There are no real predators. The worst dangers are sunburn, sharp coral, and the slow tide that covers the reef flat each evening.
Softfin Lagoon.hiddenInfo: Under the sand at the foot of the two palms lies a small lacquered shrine box, long abandoned, holding a moonstone that glows when held under water at night.

Two Palm Islet.description: A tiny islet of white sand barely larger than a room, rising above water near the middle of the lagoon. Two coconut palms lean over it at odd angles, dropping green nuts and giving a little shade. Hermit crabs trundle everywhere. At night the moon lights the sand silver and the surrounding water glows faintly where fish move. It is dry, calm and safe to sleep on.

Glowgrass Bed.description: Underwater, a broad bed of soft seagrass spreads across the lagoon floor a body length or two below the surface. Green turtles graze here slowly, and small spotted rays lift off the sand like leaves. After dark, the grass shimmers with tiny glowing plankton, and every movement leaves a trail of blue light. The water is warm, still and clear.

Low Tide Coral Ring.description: A ring of flat coral rock along the lagoon's edge that lies above water at low tide and sits on the surface under ankle-deep water at high tide. Pools in the rock hold starfish, tiny octopus and bright blennies. Herons stalk along it hunting. The coral is sharp and cuts bare feet, and each evening the tide creeps back over the flat.

Crosscurrent Sound.name: Crosscurrent Sound
Crosscurrent Sound.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Open water · Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

Crosscurrent Sound is a stretch of open lagoon water south-west of the moonbridge, between the grotto isle and the moon palace isle in Tsukihana Tidelace. Here two tidal flows meet, and the water churns in bands of turquoise and deep blue, with strong currents that switch direction with each tide and whirl into small eddies. Sudden squalls blow in off the outer sea, flattening the water with rain and then heaving it into short steep waves. Reef sharks hunt the edges of the channels, banded sea snakes swim the shallows, and boobies and frigatebirds dive for fish. Above water stands a cluster of black lava rocks crowned with screw pines, and long rafts of floating seaweed collect where the currents meet. The water is beautiful and clear, but a weak swimmer caught in the turning tide can be swept far before reaching anything to hold.
Crosscurrent Sound.hiddenInfo: Wedged between two lava rocks and visible only at low tide is the barnacled hull of an old moon-viewing boat, and its sealed lantern locker still holds three dry paper lanterns and a flask of lamp oil.

Screwpine Rocks.description: A cluster of black lava rocks rising above water in the middle of the sound, the largest crowned with a few screw pines whose stilt roots grip the stone. Spiny fruit hangs from the branches. Boobies nest in the roots and squawk at intruders. The rock is rough and sharp but holds a dry hollow sheltered from the rain, and tide pools at its foot hold small crabs.

Turning Tide Race.description: On the surface, where the two tidal flows meet, the water runs in bands of turquoise and dark blue and spins into small whirlpools. Floating weed collects here in long rafts that can hold a tired body for a while. The current changes direction with every tide and can carry a swimmer far. Squalls whip the water into steep, slapping waves.

Sharkfin Channel.description: Underwater, a sandy channel cuts between coral walls, deeper and darker than the lagoon around it. Whitetip reef sharks rest on the sand by day and hunt at dusk. Banded sea snakes weave through the coral in search of eels, venomous but rarely aggressive unless grabbed. The tide pushes water through the channel hard, and fish ride it in shining streams.

Nightcoil Channel.name: Nightcoil Channel
Nightcoil Channel.basicInfo:
[Wilderness · No residents · Open water · Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: Rising (Moderate)]

Nightcoil Channel is a deep blue gash in the lagoon floor of Tsukihana Tidelace, running between the harbor and the glowing sea cave. The turquoise shallows end at a sudden edge, and the water below goes dark and cold, falling into a trench far deeper than anything else in the lagoon. Wild sea serpents use the channel as a hunting road, silver and blue with long glowing fins, following eels and moonfish through the dark and surfacing at night to breathe in the moonlight. They are wary and fierce, but they know their own kind and will test a young serpent before they accept it or drive it off. Something larger waits in the deepest part: a tangle of pale arms that rises from a crack in the trench floor to snatch whatever passes. Above water, a broken coral spur with a ruined stone lantern post stands at the channel edge. This is dangerous water for anyone.
Nightcoil Channel.hiddenInfo: On the trench floor, among the leavings of the pale arms, lies a bronze bell from an old shrine boat, and when it is struck under water every serpent in the channel falls silent and turns toward it.

Lantern Post Spur.description: A spur of dead coral rock that juts above water at the channel's edge, topped by an old stone lantern post, cracked and empty, its shrine long abandoned. The rock is wide enough for one person to sit and sleep with their back to the post. At night the moon silvers the water around it, and glowing fins pass just below the surface.

Moonfin Road.description: Underwater, the middle depths of the channel form a dark road where moonfish shoal and eels hunt, and the wild serpents follow them. Their long fins glow pale blue in the gloom. They circle strangers closely, snapping and trilling, testing strength and nerve. A serpent who holds its ground may be allowed to hunt alongside them. A human swimmer here is prey.

Pale Arm Crack.description: Underwater, at the bottom of the channel, the trench floor splits into a black crack too deep to see into. The water is cold and smells of rot. Pale arms, each thicker than a mast and ringed with suckers, slide out of the crack to grab fish, serpents or anything else that drifts too close. Broken shells and old bones lie scattered on the rim.

Riftmaw: The Glowcap Wilds.name: Riftmaw: The Glowcap Wilds
Riftmaw: The Glowcap Wilds.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw · Floors 6-10 · Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

The Glowcap Wilds are the first place the Riftmaw stole. Below the Shallows the limestone gives way to soft black loam and a forest that was once a fae wood, swallowed whole and gone to mushroom. Glowcaps the size of oaks raise their gills overhead and shed a shifting blue-green light, puffballs as big as huts split open at a touch, and the old fae paths still run between them, paved with flat white stones that lead nowhere now.

What hunts here is the forest's defense. Myconid hunters walk on root-feet and carry spears of hardened stalk. Spore-moths drift in clouds and settle on anything warm. Mycelial crawlers move under the loam and come up beneath a sleeping camp. Small myconid hamlets will trade spores with a delver who keeps their weapons sheathed, but even they report every intruder to the floor below.

The rule of the Wilds: the fungi flare when disturbed. A footstep brightens the ground, a fight lights the whole clearing, and stealth here is close to impossible. The spores taste faintly sweet and are harmless, mostly.

The Sporemother holds the stair down from floor 10: a colony that grew itself a shape and lights the cavern when it is angry. Delvers swear every stratum hides one way up that skips the rest of it.

[Narrator: a Rise is found in the story, by searching, a bargain or luck, never just by asking. Everything this stratum breeds is the Riftmaw's own defense: hostile to intruders and never generous; one that talks wants something for anything it gives. The myconids of Sporeward on floor 7 slipped the Riftmaw's will and are a hold, not its defense.]
Riftmaw: The Glowcap Wilds.hiddenInfo:
The white paving stones carry elven waymarks from a grove that elven songs say the earth swallowed four centuries ago. The paths still lead toward the place its heart-tree stood, and something at that spot still answers when it is spoken to in Elvish.

[Not public knowledge: let it surface through play, never through narration or a convenient NPC.]

Floors 6-10.description: Floors 6 to 10 themselves, crossed chamber by chamber and stair by stair. The forest floor of the Glowcap Wilds: black loam, white fae paving stones, and glowcap trunks as wide as towers under a canopy of glowing gills. Myconid hamlets cling to the larger stalks. Every step brightens the ground underfoot for a moment, so a party can always see where it has been, and so can everything else.

Riftmaw: The Singing Geodes.name: Riftmaw: The Singing Geodes
Riftmaw: The Singing Geodes.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw · Floors 11-15 · Recommended Level: 13-23 · Danger: Rising (Moderate)]

The Singing Geodes are crystal caverns cracked out of some other world's stone. Floors 11 to 15 are hollow geodes the size of cathedrals, their walls furred with violet and white crystal and linked by narrow throats of rock. Air moving through them makes the crystal ring, and the whole stratum hums at a pitch that settles in the teeth.

Sound is how everything here hunts. Echo-bats map a party by its breathing and strike from the dark above the light. Shard golems shake loose from the walls when the ringing changes. Basilisks with gem-crusted backs wait in the lower geodes and turn their eyes on whatever made the last noise.

The rule of the Geodes: sound carries. A shout or a clash of steel rings through three caverns and draws hunters from all of them. Quiet magic, soft steps and stillness are strong here, and loud fighters pay for every swing.

The Guild's First Rest Station sits in a warded alcove on floor 12, inside the small town of Quietwell. The Choir of Echoes holds the stair down from floor 15. One hidden way up skips the rest of this stratum.

[Narrator: a Rise is found in the story, by searching, a bargain or luck, never just by asking. Everything this stratum breeds is the Riftmaw's own defense: hostile to intruders and never generous; one that talks wants something for anything it gives. The gargoyles of Stillwing Roost on floor 13 slipped the Riftmaw's will and are a hold, not its defense.]
Riftmaw: The Singing Geodes.hiddenInfo:
The ringing is a language. Scholars at the First Rest Station have logged it for years and believe the geodes are repeating, over and over, the last thing their stolen world heard before the Riftmaw took them.

[Not public knowledge: let it surface through play, never through narration or a convenient NPC.]

Floors 11-15.description: Floors 11 to 15 themselves, crossed chamber by chamber and stair by stair. Five floors of hollow geodes linked by narrow passages of raw rock. Crystal furs every wall in violet and white, and the air moving between the caverns makes it ring, a hum that never quite stops. Guild touch-marks are scratched at every junction, because the echoes make it hard to tell which way a sound came from.

Riftmaw: The Drowned Forgehold.name: Riftmaw: The Drowned Forgehold
Riftmaw: The Drowned Forgehold.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw · Floors 16-20 · Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Rising (Moderate)]

The Drowned Forgehold is where the Riftmaw stops being a cave. On floor 16 the rock gives way to cut stone: the halls of a hold built by some vanished people of smiths, too precise for Luxcellian masonry and too old to date. The Riftmaw took the hold with its forges still lit. Half of it has flooded since, black water standing waist deep in the lower halls, and the other half still burns, forges and slag channels glowing in rooms nobody has tended for an age.

What hunts here was made to guard the hold. Forge golems of riveted iron walk the dry halls, still on their rounds. Rust-eaters swarm out of the flooded levels and strip the metal off anything that wades. The shades of the drowned smiths keep working at anvils that are not there, and turn on anyone who touches their tools.

The rule of the Forgehold: water and fire. Every route is either flooded or burning, and the safe way through one is usually the dangerous way through the other. Rift-Touched Ore runs in the walls, and the old forges will still take a blade for anyone brave enough to work them.

The Gatewright holds the stair down from floor 20, a mason of worked stone still closing a door that was opened long ago. One hidden way up skips the rest of this stratum.

[Narrator: a Rise is found in the story, by searching, a bargain or luck, never just by asking. Everything this stratum breeds is the Riftmaw's own defense: hostile to intruders and never generous; one that talks wants something for anything it gives. The forge-golems of Anvilward on floor 16 slipped the Riftmaw's will and are a hold, not its defense.]
Riftmaw: The Drowned Forgehold.hiddenInfo:
The smiths did not simply die when the Riftmaw took their hold. Some of their shades still remember their names, and a smith who earns their respect can learn a technique no living teacher knows.

[Not public knowledge: let it surface through play, never through narration or a convenient NPC.]

Floors 16-20.description: Floors 16 to 20 themselves, crossed chamber by chamber and stair by stair. Cut-stone halls of a vanished people of smiths: anvil rooms, slag channels, storerooms behind iron doors. The lower halls stand flooded with still black water; the upper ones still glow with forge heat. Steam rises where the two meet, and the sound of hammering comes and goes from rooms with nobody in them.

Riftmaw: The Halls of the Tall Kings.name: Riftmaw: The Halls of the Tall Kings
Riftmaw: The Halls of the Tall Kings.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw · Floors 21-30 · Recommended Level: 23-38 · Danger: Veteran (High)]

Below the Forgehold the Riftmaw swallowed a palace. The Halls of the Tall Kings fill floors 21 to 30 with throne rooms, galleries and audience chambers built for a people taller and narrower than any in Luxcellia: doorways twice a man's height and barely wider than his shoulders, steps too high to take comfortably, thrones nobody living could sit in. The stone absorbs sound, so talk feels private even in an open hall, and the light is a steady amber.

The kings are long gone. Their household still stands guard. Suits of animated armor step down from their alcoves, gargoyles unfold from the cornices, and court wraiths in tall, faded finery drift through the audience chambers, still waiting for a petition to hear. They do not like it when the petitioner is an intruder.

The rule of the Halls: court law still holds. A drawn weapon, a raised voice or a spell in a throne room wakes every sentinel in it; a party that bows, waits and keeps its weapons at rest crosses a sentinel's hall with no roll at all. Court law binds the sentinels only: the hunting packs that roam between the halls answer to nothing. Regalia and old court arms lie where they fell, and every piece belonged to someone.

The Guild's Midway Outpost, the deepest permanent Guild presence in the Riftmaw, is built into a gatehouse on floor 25, inside the small town of Kingsrest. The Hall Warden holds the stair down from floor 30, and no bow or court manners will stay it. One hidden way up skips the rest of this stratum.

[Narrator: a Rise is found in the story, by searching, a bargain or luck, never just by asking. Everything this stratum breeds is the Riftmaw's own defense: hostile to intruders and never generous; one that talks wants something for anything it gives. The minotaur clan of Hornhall on floor 22 slipped the Riftmaw's will and is a hold, not its defense.]
Riftmaw: The Halls of the Tall Kings.hiddenInfo:
The Tall Kings left an heir's crown somewhere on these floors. The court wraiths are not guarding the palace. They are waiting for someone to carry that crown to the throne on floor 30.

[Not public knowledge: let it surface through play, never through narration or a convenient NPC.]

Floors 21-30.description: Floors 21 to 30 themselves, crossed chamber by chamber and stair by stair. Throne rooms, audience galleries and long processional halls built for a people taller and narrower than any in Luxcellia. Doorways rise twice a man's height, and the steps are awkward for human legs. Amber light falls evenly from no visible source, the stone swallows sound, and a suit of armor stands in every alcove, waiting.

Riftmaw: The Galleries of Theft.name: Riftmaw: The Galleries of Theft
Riftmaw: The Galleries of Theft.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw · Floors 31-40 · Recommended Level: 33-48 · Danger: Veteran (High)]

The Galleries of Theft are the Riftmaw's hoard. Floors 31 to 40 are corridors of alcoves, each holding something taken: weapons, tools, crowns, clothing, books and games from dozens of civilizations, none of them Luxcellian. Everything is real, working and kept, dusted and arranged as if for visitors who never come. Touching an object sometimes brings a vision of its owner: a hand on the hilt, a reader turning a page, an owner who wanted it back.

The hoard has keepers. Mimics wear the shapes of chests, doors and display stands. Hoard-drakes, lean wingless things with gold-dusted scales, sleep coiled around the richest alcoves. Exhibit keepers, tall shapes of dust and glass, appear only when something is moved, and they follow the thief until it is put back or they are destroyed.

The rule of the Galleries: take an exhibit and its keeper comes for it. Some pieces are worth it, and a cache on these floors is an exhibit too. Every one of them carries a catch, because the Riftmaw keeps nothing ordinary.

The Curator of Thefts holds the stair down from floor 40. It does not want the party dead; it wants what they carry. One hidden way up skips the rest of this stratum.

[Narrator: a Rise is found in the story, by searching, a bargain or luck, never just by asking. Everything this stratum breeds is the Riftmaw's own defense: hostile to intruders and never generous; one that talks wants something for anything it gives. The mimics, imps and kobolds of the Mimic Bazaar on floor 38 slipped the Riftmaw's will and are a hold, not its defense.]
Riftmaw: The Galleries of Theft.hiddenInfo:
Some exhibits came from Luxcellia. The Guild found a Silverfang hunting knife in an alcove on floor 37 whose owner had died on the surface twenty years before, and it has never explained how.

[Not public knowledge: let it surface through play, never through narration or a convenient NPC.]

Floors 31-40.description: Floors 31 to 40 themselves, crossed chamber by chamber and stair by stair. Corridor after corridor of alcoves, each holding one stolen thing on display: a sword, a crown, a music box, a painted kite. The dust is wiped from every piece and from nowhere else. The light is soft, as in a gallery, and the silence is complete until something is moved.

Riftmaw: The Living Architecture.name: Riftmaw: The Living Architecture
Riftmaw: The Living Architecture.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw · Floors 41-50 · Recommended Level: 43-58 · Danger: Elite (Severe)]

Below the Galleries the Riftmaw stops wearing stolen places and shows its own body. The Living Architecture fills floors 41 to 50 with corridors of a material that is not stone and not metal, warm to the touch and rising and falling on a breath too slow to notice until you hold your own. Doorways narrow and widen on their own cycle, rooms are never the same shape twice, and the dull violet Riftlight pulses in the walls like a vein.

This is where the dungeon defends itself directly. Antibody knights, pale armored things without faces, grow out of the walls fully formed and walk toward whatever does not belong. Acid gut-rivers run through the lower halls and dissolve whatever falls in. The things that hunt here fight like trained soldiers: they withdraw when the odds are bad and come back with a better plan.

The rule of the Living Architecture: it digests. A party that lingers draws more defenders every hour, a door can close on a straggler, and a body is gone by morning. Nothing here is rated for a newcomer, and the dungeon has no interest in being fair to one. It gives nothing: whatever a delver carries out of here was taken by force or found by searching.

The Deep Threshold on floor 50 is the end of the mapped Riftmaw, and its guardian, the Threshold Reader, waits there reading the walls aloud. One hidden way up skips the rest of this stratum. It bites on the way.

[Narrator: a Rise is found in the story, by searching, a bargain or luck, never just by asking. Everything this stratum breeds is the Riftmaw's own defense: hostile to intruders and never generous; one that talks wants something for anything it gives. Scab Camp, a delver camp on floor 43, and the Lymph Pools, a slime-kin hold on floor 46, are not its defense: the body tolerates both. The body itself is on no one's side: it never watches with approval, keeps a foe from fleeing for anyone, or offers loot; when it notices intruders, it sends defenders.]

The Living Architecture is this place, not a creature: no single being is called that or speaks for it, and its defenders are many and nameless.
Riftmaw: The Living Architecture.hiddenInfo:
The Living Architecture is the closest anyone has come to seeing what the Riftmaw is: a living thing, and every monster it makes is part of its defense. It does not hate delvers. It treats them the way a body treats a splinter.

[Not public knowledge: let it surface through play, never through narration or a convenient NPC.]

Floors 41-49.description: Floors 41 to 49 themselves, crossed chamber by chamber and stair by stair. Corridors of warm, faintly moving material that is neither stone nor metal, lit by a dull violet pulse in the walls. Doorways narrow and widen on a slow cycle, and rooms change shape between visits. The floor gives very slightly underfoot, and there is no smell at all.

The Deep Threshold.description: Floor 50, the boundary between the mapped Riftmaw and the unmapped deep. A wide chamber with exits in every direction, most leading to passages the Guild has never charted. The walls here are covered in script that matches the 97th Floor writing, and the script shifts slowly enough to watch. A Guild marker at the chamber's entrance reads: 'MAPPED RIFTMAW ENDS. GUILD SUPPORT ENDS. BEYOND THIS POINT YOU ARE A STATISTIC UNTIL YOU RETURN.' Someone has crossed out 'until' and written 'unless.' The correction has not been removed.

Riftmaw: The Hollow Manor.name: Riftmaw: The Hollow Manor
Riftmaw: The Hollow Manor.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw · Floors 51-60 · Recommended Level: 53-68 · Danger: Elite (Severe)]

Beyond the Deep Threshold the Riftmaw has furnished itself. The Hollow Manor is rooms taken from a hundred houses and joined into one: parlors, dining halls, studies and servants' corridors from homes of no recognizable culture, all of them clean, lit by a warm light with no source, and set for guests. Clocks tick in rooms with no clock in them. A meal is sometimes laid and still warm.

The house keeps itself. Poltergeists hurl whatever is not nailed down. Portrait watchers follow a party from frame to frame and step out of the last one. The furniture hunts: a wardrobe that closes, a chair that holds, a long table that walks. Monsters are absent for long stretches, and the silence between them is attentive.

The rule of the Manor: house manners. Doors open for guests who knock, take nothing and keep their voices down. A guest who breaks a house rule is corrected, and the house's corrections escalate. A ghostly butler sometimes offers to show a polite party the way, and what he asks in return is always a small, strange household task.

The Furnished Silence holds the stair down from floor 60, a whole room that is one creature. One hidden way up skips the rest of this stratum.

[Narrator: a Rise is found in the story, by searching, a bargain or luck, never just by asking. Everything this stratum breeds is the Riftmaw's own defense: hostile to intruders and never generous; one that talks wants something for anything it gives. The ghosts and household spirits of the Attic Court on floor 57 slipped the Riftmaw's will and are a hold, not its defense.]
Riftmaw: The Hollow Manor.hiddenInfo:
Every room in the Manor came from a house where someone was waiting for a guest who never arrived. The house is still waiting with them, and it treats a delver who sits down to the laid meal as that guest, for better or worse.

[Not public knowledge: let it surface through play, never through narration or a convenient NPC.]

Floors 51-60.description: Floors 51 to 60 themselves, crossed chamber by chamber and stair by stair. Rooms from a hundred houses joined into one: a parlor opens into a study, the study into a wine cellar, the cellar into a ballroom. Everything is clean, lit warm from nowhere, and laid out for guests. Somewhere a clock always ticks, and there is always one more door than the room should have.

Riftmaw: The Labyrinth That Decides.name: Riftmaw: The Labyrinth That Decides
Riftmaw: The Labyrinth That Decides.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw · Floors 61-75 · Recommended Level: 63-83 · Danger: Mythic (Deadly)]

The Labyrinth That Decides is a maze with a will. Floors 61 to 75 are corridors of pale stone that rearrange themselves while nobody watches: junctions that were three-way become four-way, and long straight passages end where they began. The light is warm and directional and casts proper shadows, as if it came through windows that are not there.

The maze has hunters. Something horned and patient walks its corridors, larger every time it is seen, and it always knows where the party is. Thread-spiders string the junctions with silk that sings when touched. Wall-mouths open in the stone and close on whatever leans against them.

The rule of the Labyrinth: say what you seek and the maze bends toward it. Name a stair, a rest or a way out, and the corridors start leading there, but the Labyrinth takes a toll for every favor: a memory, an item, a wound or an hour. Wandering without intent leads in circles.

The Corridor That Decides holds the stair down from floor 75, where the way down and what guards it are the same thing, and beating it leaves an anchor on that floor. One hidden way up skips the rest of this stratum.

[Narrator: a Rise is found in the story, by searching, a bargain or luck, never just by asking. Everything this stratum breeds is the Riftmaw's own defense: hostile to intruders and never generous; one that talks wants something for anything it gives. The spider-kin of the Silk Vaults on floor 69 slipped the Riftmaw's will and are a hold, not its defense.]
Riftmaw: The Labyrinth That Decides.hiddenInfo:
The toll the maze takes is not lost. It keeps everything it takes, and a party that reaches its center can bargain to get one thing back.

[Not public knowledge: let it surface through play, never through narration or a convenient NPC.]

Floors 61-75.description: Floors 61 to 75 themselves, crossed chamber by chamber and stair by stair. Pale stone corridors that rearrange themselves while nobody watches, lit warm and slanting as if by windows that are not there. Junctions change how many ways they have. Silk threads cross the passages at ankle height and hum when brushed, and far off something heavy walks the maze at an unhurried pace.

Riftmaw: The Sunless Gardens.name: Riftmaw: The Sunless Gardens
Riftmaw: The Sunless Gardens.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw · Floors 76-90 · Recommended Level: 78-98 · Danger: Mythic (Deadly)]

The Sunless Gardens are terraces of orchard and flowerbed lit through tall windows by a sun that does not exist. Floors 76 to 90 grow trees whose fruit no Luxcellian has a name for, hedges of glass-thorned roses, and lawns kept at a height nobody tends. The light falls warm and golden through the windows, and on the other side of the glass there is nothing at all.

The gardens are tended. Gardener beasts, long-limbed and slow until they are not, prune whatever grows out of place, delvers included. Light-eating moths settle on lanterns, spells and eyes. Thorn wardens grow up out of the beds wherever blood is spilled.

The rule of the Gardens: the foreign light heals, and it marks. Standing in it closes wounds and rests the tired, and leaves a faint golden mark on the skin that every hunter in the stratum can see. The shade is safe and does not heal.

The Lamp-Bearer holds the stair down from floor 90, carrying the only moving light on these floors and waiting for someone to follow it. One hidden way up skips the rest of this stratum.

[Narrator: a Rise is found in the story, by searching, a bargain or luck, never just by asking. Everything this stratum breeds is the Riftmaw's own defense: hostile to intruders and never generous; one that talks wants something for anything it gives. The dryads and plant-folk of the Rootcourt on floor 81 slipped the Riftmaw's will and are a hold, not its defense.]
Riftmaw: The Sunless Gardens.hiddenInfo:
The golden mark fades a month after a delver returns to the surface. While it lasts monsters anywhere can see it, and some Reborn who carried one swear the light felt like a sun they remembered.

[Not public knowledge: let it surface through play, never through narration or a convenient NPC.]

Floors 76-90.description: Floors 76 to 90 themselves, crossed chamber by chamber and stair by stair. Terraced orchards and flowerbeds under tall windows full of golden light from a sun that does not exist. Paths of raked white gravel, hedges of glass-thorned roses, fruit trees heavy with fruit that has no name. Beyond the glass there is nothing. The shade between the windows is cool and dark and does not heal.

Riftmaw: The Last Stair.name: Riftmaw: The Last Stair
Riftmaw: The Last Stair.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw · Floors 91-96 · Recommended Level: 93-100 · Danger: Mythic (Deadly)]

The Last Stair is one spiral stair, wide enough for a cart, winding down the inside of a well whose walls open onto a field of stars. Floors 91 to 96 are its landings: broad stone platforms where the stair pauses, each with a few chambers cut into the well wall. There is no up or down in the sky beyond the edge, and things fall past it now and then, slowly.

What waits on the landings has waited a long time. Mirror-wraiths wear the faces of delvers who came this far and did not go back, and speak in their voices. Falling stars break on the steps as burning shards. The few beasts that hunt here are larger than anything above them and do not hunt for food.

The rule of the Last Stair: nowhere on the stair is safe to rest. No landing is safe for long, no chamber stays sealed, and the stair only goes up or down. There is no shortcut on this stratum; the Last Stair is climbed or descended a landing at a time.

The Echo on the Last Stair holds the way down from floor 96. It looks like whoever in the party has come farthest, and it has had ninety-six floors to practice. Below it there are no more floors, only a corridor and the 97th Floor Door.

[Narrator: Everything this stratum breeds is the Riftmaw's own defense: hostile to intruders and never generous; one that talks wants something for anything it gives. The moth-folk of the Starwing Eyrie on floor 92 slipped the Riftmaw's will and are a hold, not its defense.]
Riftmaw: The Last Stair.hiddenInfo:
The faces the mirror-wraiths wear belong to real delvers, and every one reported so far matches a name in the Guild's missing-persons records.

[Not public knowledge: let it surface through play, never through narration or a convenient NPC.]

Floors 91-96.description: Floors 91 to 96 themselves, crossed chamber by chamber and stair by stair. Broad stone landings on a spiral stair wide enough for a cart, built down the inside of a well open to a field of stars. Each landing has a few chambers cut into the wall. There is nothing past the edge of the steps but sky, and now and then something falling slowly past it.

Riftmaw: The Shallows.name: Riftmaw: The Shallows
Riftmaw: The Shallows.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw · Floors 1-5 · Recommended Level: 1-13 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

The Shallows are the first five floors under the Maw: limestone caves, glowing moss, slimes and the best-mapped monster hunting ground on the continent. Guild training parties work here, rookies earn their first plates here, and the scaffolding at the top is the way home. Lantern Row, a delvers' haven, sits on floor 2, and Gutterwarren, a goblin and kobold warren that slipped the Riftmaw's will, on floor 4. Its guardian, the Crowned Slime, lairs by the stair down from Floor 5.

Floor 1-5: The Shallows.description: [Floors 1-5 · Monster Level 3-11] Floors 1 to 5 themselves, crossed chamber by chamber and stair by stair. Natural limestone caverns with reliable Guild mapping and manageable threats. Phosphorescent moss provides ambient light supplementing the Riftlight, and the monsters here are territorial but predictable: slimes, cave crawlers, and the occasional lost surface predator that wandered in and cannot find its way back. Training parties from Floor Zero Gatehouse operate here under instructor supervision. Rest alcoves with Guild supply caches are spaced at regular intervals, and the walls carry generations of carved party graffiti: names, dates, kill tallies, and one elaborate mural of a slime wearing a crown.

Lantern Row.name: Lantern Row
Lantern Row.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Riftmaw Floor 2 · Recommended Level: 1-13 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Lantern Row is the first place below the Maw where a delver can put down their pack and sleep without a watch: a dry limestone gallery on floor 2, walled off from the caves by stacked stone and a ward that hums faintly in the teeth. It survives because the Guild keeps it: instructors from the Floor Zero Gatehouse rotate through, and the slimes have learned that lanterns mean steel. Who lives here: rope menders, a healer trained at the Gatehouse, two or three stall keepers who came down for a season and stayed, and whatever training party is resting between drills. Water comes from a cleaned seep at the back; food comes down the scaffolding in crates and is sold hot. Prices run in Copper: a hot bowl 3, a lantern refill 2, a stitched cut 8, a new rope 1 Silver. Law: blades stay sheathed past the stall line. Rookies are welcome; a monster player meets crossbows unless a sponsor's tag is shown, and the healer treats anyone who can pay. Home base: a bunk for 5 Copper a night, or a curtained alcove of your own for 2 Silver a week. People come back for the Notice Wall and the last hot meal before the dark gets serious.
Lantern Row.hiddenInfo: The ward is older than the Guild's paperwork says, and it is not the Guild's: the first rookies found it already humming in the gallery wall. The healer has noticed that wounds close faster on floor 2 than anywhere else in the Riftmaw and has told nobody. Right now one of the stall keepers buys slime oil from Gutterwarren through the Letterbox and sells it as Guild lamp oil; if the instructors find out, the Row loses its license. Work on offer: in the Mender's Nook, the rope and lantern mender wants someone to find which stall sells slime oil as Guild lamp oil, before the instructors do.

The Rope Stair Landing.description: Where the scaffolding's last ladder meets the gallery floor. A coil-board holds Guild ropes for checkout, a brazier burns by the stair, and a rookie on watch duty pretends not to be asleep. Every party that comes down rings the small brass bell hung from the ladder, so the Row always knows someone is home.

Stall Row.description: A dozen plank stalls along the gallery's dry wall, each lit by its own lantern: hot broth, candles, rope, dried meat, moss poultices, chalk. Prices are chalked on slate in Copper, and haggling is expected. The smell of broth and lamp oil covers the cave's damp, mostly.

The Bunk Gallery.description: Three tiers of bunks cut into the gallery's back wall, curtained with old Guild sailcloth. A bunk is 5 Copper a night; a curtained alcove with a lockbox is 2 Silver a week and stays yours while the rent is paid. The ward hums strongest here, and most people sleep better for it.

The Mender's Nook.description: A corner workshop where rope is spliced, lanterns are soldered and cuts are stitched on the same table, wiped down between jobs. The mender charges 8 Copper a stitched cut and 1 Silver for a new rope, and keeps a jar of slime-core salve for burns.

The Notice Wall.description: A flat stretch of limestone covered in chalk and pinned paper: lost parties, contracts for slime cores, alcoves for rent, warnings about rising water. Notices for parties that never came back stay up until someone brings word. Reading it takes an hour, and it changes every time you visit.

Gutterwarren.name: Gutterwarren
Gutterwarren.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Monster Hold · Riftmaw Floor 4 · Recommended Level: 1-13 · No wild spawns inside · Residents decide who stays]

Gutterwarren is a goblin and kobold warren dug into a collapsed side cave on floor 4, where a hundred small tunnels open off one sloping cavern lit by slime-oil lamps. Its people were spawned by the Riftmaw like any other monster and slipped its will, the way some do: they stopped guarding the floor and started keeping house. The Riftmaw treats them as intruders now, so the warren lives behind traps, a midden wall and a watch that never sleeps. Who lives here: goblin scavengers and lamp-makers, kobold trappers and diggers, a handful of hobgoblin wall-guards, and whoever is boss this month. They eat slime-jelly from their own pens and cave mushrooms, drink from the Shallows' stream, and trade slime oil, scavenged gear and traps for Copper, salt and favors. Law: you don't steal from the pens, you don't bring a delver in without the boss's yes, and you add to the midden. Delvers are met at the gate with spears and a price; a monster player of a small kind is greeted as kin and handed a lamp. Home base: a burrow of your own is free to kin who dig it out and share food at the Loud Seat. People come back because the warren remembers who brought gifts.
Gutterwarren.hiddenInfo: The warren is older than it admits: its deepest tunnels carry kobold carvings of the Maw from before the Guild built its checkpoint. The current boss is a kobold trapmaster who rules by deciding where the traps go, and the goblin lamp-makers want the seat for themselves. Right now the Crowned Slime's court on floor 5 is pushing upward, slimes are getting into the pens, and the warren has started to wonder whether delvers might be worth hiring. Work on offer: at the Slime Pens, a kobold pen-keeper wants the wild slimes driven out and their way in found, and pays in Copper, a lamp or a burrow.

The Midden Gate.description: The warren's front door, a narrow mouth in a wall of packed refuse, bones and broken gear, with a trapped approach only the warren can walk blind. Two hobgoblins and a kobold with a bell keep the gate. Delvers stop at the chalk line and state their business; kin walk straight in.

The Lamp Market.description: The sloping main cavern, crowded with stalls of slime-oil lamps, stitched leather, old delver blades sharpened to a shine and trap parts. Goblins haggle loudly and enjoy it. Prices run in Copper, salt and favors, and a delver who pays in food gets the best deal.

The Slime Pens.description: Rows of shallow stone basins where tame slimes are fed scraps and milked for oil and jelly. The smell is strong and the floor is slick. Kobold keepers guard the pens jealously, because they are the warren's food, light and trade all at once.

The Burrow Rows.description: Tiers of small tunnels dug into the cavern's back wall, each one a household's den behind a hide curtain with a lamp niche. An empty burrow belongs to whoever digs it deeper and shares a meal at the Loud Seat; kin of a small kind can claim one the day they arrive.

The Loud Seat.description: A flat boulder at the cavern's heart where the warren argues, feasts and chooses its boss: whoever can keep the whole cavern listening longest. The boss sits there most evenings with a trapmaker's pouch and hears complaints, offers and gossip, in that order.

The Tally Wall.name: The Tally Wall
The Tally Wall.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 3 · Recommended Level: 1-13 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]
