The Tally Wall is a long, smooth face of limestone on floor 3 where delvers carve a mark on the way down and a second mark beside it on the way up. Thousands of paired marks cover it from the floor to the height of a raised hand, in every style the Guild has ever taught, and some marks have no partner. Rookies come here to carve their first and read the old ones; instructors bring training parties here to make a point about coming home. Above the Guild marks, out of easy reach, runs a band of older marks nobody can read: thin clawed lines in sets of three. The cavern in front of the wall is wide and quiet, which is why cave crawlers like it too: they nest in the cracks and come out when the lanterns burn low.
The Tally Wall.hiddenInfo: The oldest band is a tally kept by Gutterwarren's founders before the Guild came, counting delvers who went down and came back. It stops on the day the Guild built its checkpoint. A kobold elder can read it, and it records a party the Guild lists as lost on floor 3 that came back up, walked out into the Ashenmere, and never reported in.

The Carved Face.description: The main sweep of the wall, covered in paired marks: initials, Company sigils, little drawings of swords and slimes. Chalk and carving knives wait in a niche for anyone without their own. Tradition says you carve before you go down, never after.

The Unpaired Marks.description: A stretch near the cavern's mouth where the instructors have scratched a ring around every mark that never got its partner. Some rings have moss flowers tucked into the cracks beside them. It is the quietest place in the Shallows, and even the crawlers seem to leave it alone.

The Oldest Marks.description: A band of thin clawed triple lines high on the wall, reachable only from a ledge at the cavern's far end. The ledge is crumbling, and crawlers nest in the cracks behind it. Up close, the marks were cut by small hands, carefully.

The Slime Wells.name: The Slime Wells
The Slime Wells.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 1 · Recommended Level: 1-13 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

The Slime Wells are a cluster of round sinkholes on floor 1 where the stream pools and the Riftmaw breeds its slimes: blue, green, and the odd clear one that is hard to see until it is on your boot. It is the first hunting ground most rookies ever see, a short walk from the scaffolding, and the Guild pays a steady bounty on Blue Slime Cores. The rims are slick, the pools are deeper than they look, and a slime dropping on you from the ceiling is a rite of passage. Gutterwarren's keepers come here at quiet hours to catch small slimes for their pens, which the instructors pretend not to see.
The Slime Wells.hiddenInfo: The wells drain through an overflow crawl back toward floor 2, and when the stream rises the crawl floods in minutes; twice this season a rookie has been caught in it. Something has been taking the clear slimes before anyone else can, and the bite marks it leaves are not a goblin's.

The Well Rim.description: A ring of slick limestone around the largest well, scuffed by a thousand boots and marked with Guild chalk where the footing holds. Rookies line up here to practise on the slimes that crawl up the sides while instructors shout from the dry side.

The Breeding Basins.description: Shallow side pools where slimes divide and drift, glowing faintly, and Blue Slime Cores sit in the oldest ones. A careful harvester can lift a core without waking the pool; a careless one wakes all of them at once.

The Overflow Crawl.description: A low tunnel half full of cold water that carries the wells' overflow back toward floor 2. It is the short way to Lantern Row when the water is low and a death trap when it rises. A rope strung along its roof gives handholds.

Lampblack Camp.name: Lampblack Camp
Lampblack Camp.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Riftmaw Floor 6 · Recommended Level: 8-18 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Lampblack Camp is a delver camp inside a fallen glowcap stalk on floor 6: a hollow tube of dead mushroom flesh as wide as a barn, blackened inside with lamp soot to stop it glowing. Because it is dead it does not flare when someone walks in it, which makes it the one place in the Wilds where a party can sleep unseen. It survives because the hunters cannot smell anything through the soot, and because two Guild Companies take turns holding the door. Who lives here: a camp boss from one of those Companies, a mask-maker who sews spore masks from moth-silk, a cartographer who redraws the paths every week, a cook, and delvers on their way down. Water is filtered from a root-pool; food is mushroom stew and whatever came down from the Shallows. Prices: stew 4 Copper, a cot 8 Copper a night, a spore mask 6 Silver, a map copy 2 Silver. Law: no open flame outside the stalk, no fighting within sight of the door, and nobody brings a live myconid in. A monster player is let in only if a Company member vouches. Home base: a soot-black cot bay of your own for 4 Silver a week. People come back for the masks, and for the maps, which are wrong a week after they are drawn.
Lampblack Camp.hiddenInfo: The two Companies holding the camp do not trust each other, and each keeps a quiet count of what the other takes from the supply crates. The cartographer has noticed the white paths shifting a few paces every week, always toward the Heart-Tree Ruin. Right now the soot is wearing thin on the east wall, and on quiet nights the stalk glows faintly through it. Work on offer: at the Stalk Door, the camp boss from the Company on watch pays for help blacking over the east wall, where the soot has worn thin and the stalk glows.

The Stalk Door.description: A round opening cut into the fallen stalk, hung with a heavy soot-black curtain and watched by two delvers with crossbows. Outside, the loam glows at every step; inside, it does not. The guards check masks before anyone goes out.

The Hollow Bunks.description: Cots in rows down the stalk's dark length, each bay divided by hanging cloth. A cot is 8 Copper a night, and a bay of your own with a lockbox is 4 Silver a week. The air smells of soot, stew and old mushroom.

The Mask Bench.description: A worktable under a single shuttered lamp where the mask-maker stitches spore masks from moth-silk, cloth and resin. A good mask is 6 Silver and lasts a delve; repairs are 1 Silver. Finished masks hang from the ceiling like rows of sleeping faces.

The Mapping Table.description: A long plank table under layers of dated charcoal maps of the Wilds. The cartographer sells copies for 2 Silver and buys corrections for food. The paths drawn here are right this week and probably wrong the next.

The Spore Screen.description: A small chamber by the door where everyone coming in is brushed down and sprayed with vinegar water so no live spores ride inside. It is cold, wet and mandatory, and it is where the camp's best gossip happens.

Sporeward.name: Sporeward
Sporeward.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Monster Hold · Riftmaw Floor 7 · Recommended Level: 8-18 · No wild spawns inside · Residents decide who stays]

Sporeward is a myconid hold under the largest glowcap on floor 7: a ring of low mushroom dwellings grown around its trunk and joined by root bridges. Its people were one of the forest's hamlets, sworn like the rest to report every intruder to the floor below, until they stopped. Now the Riftmaw's hunters raid them, and Sporeward lives behind a ring of spore-bloom that blinds anything crossing it uninvited. Who lives here: myconids of every size, from knee-high diggers to stalk-elders taller than a door, who talk among themselves in drifting spores and to outsiders in slow, careful words; a few moth-tenders; and delvers who have learned the manners. They eat what they grow and trade it: healing caps, lamp mushrooms that burn a week, dried spore-cakes that feed a delver for a day. Prices: a spore-cake 2 Copper, a healing cap 1 Silver. Law: weapons are bound at the Sheathing Post, or the visitor leaves blind. Monster players of fungal or plant kinds are kin, and any monster player who arrives peaceful is heard. Home base: a hammock in the gills for a week's work in the beds; a dwelling of your own takes a season and the Spore Circle's yes. People come back for the food, the cures and the quiet.
Sporeward.hiddenInfo: Sporeward broke from the Riftmaw because its eldest stalk heard something else in the loam: the old heart-tree at the elven ruin, still singing under the ground. The Spore Circle believes waking the heart-tree would free every hamlet in the Wilds, and the Sporemother knows it. Right now a loyal hamlet on floor 8 is carrying Sporeward's spores to the hunters, and the Circle is quietly deciding whether to burn it. Work on offer: at the Sheathing Post, a myconid guard on the bloom ring wants help catching whoever gathers Sporeward's spores at the ring's edge by night.

The Sheathing Post.description: A ring of living stalks at the hold's edge where visitors bind their weapons with moth-silk cord before crossing the spore-bloom. A small myconid guard watches and puffs sour spores at anyone who refuses. Past it, the air tastes sweet.

The Trading Ring.description: A clearing of flat caps around the great trunk where myconids lay out what they grew: healing caps, lamp mushrooms, spore-cakes, moth-silk. They trade for salt, metal and stories of the surface, and they never haggle; a price is set once and kept.

The Gill Hammocks.description: Hammocks slung high in the great glowcap's gills, rocking in the warm air that rises off the trunk. A visitor earns one with a week of work in the beds; kin may take one on arrival. The light here is soft, blue and steady, and sleep comes easily.

The Spore Circle.description: A hollow at the trunk's base where the stalk-elders stand in a ring and speak in slow drifting spores. Decisions take days. Outsiders may listen, and a careful listener in a mask can feel the shape of what is being said.

The Cultivation Beds.description: Terraces of tended loam where myconids grow everything the hold eats and sells, watered from root-pools and lit by the trunk. Visitors who want a hammock work here, weeding, carrying and turning compost. The myconids are patient teachers.

The Heart-Tree Ruin.name: The Heart-Tree Ruin
The Heart-Tree Ruin.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 8 · Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

The Heart-Tree Ruin is where the white elven paths of the Glowcap Wilds all lead: a wide court of white paving on floor 8 around the stump of a tree so large its broken trunk could hold a village. The fae wood grew around it before the Riftmaw swallowed the grove. Now mushrooms crowd the court's edges but never cross the paving, and the stump is the one thing in the Wilds that does not glow. Myconid hunters patrol the court and will not step onto the stone. Delvers come for the quiet and for the carvings on the paving, which are elven verse. Spoken Elvish carries strangely here, as if the stump were listening.
The Heart-Tree Ruin.hiddenInfo: The heart-tree is not dead. Its roots run under the whole stratum and still sing, too low to hear, and Sporeward's spores carry that song. A verse spoken in Elvish at the stump's centre makes the roots answer with light. Under the stump is a root vault where the grove's keepers left something before the Riftmaw took them, sealed with a verse only an elf or a careful scholar could finish.

The White Paving.description: A broad court of white stone slabs, each carved with a line of elven verse worn smooth by feet that are no longer here. Mushrooms crowd the edges but never cross onto the stone. The court is cool, dark and very quiet.

The Stump Court.description: The heart of the ruin: a stump wider than a house, its broken trunk rising like a wall of grey wood. It is the only thing in the Wilds that does not glow. Words spoken here hang in the air a moment longer than they should.

The Root Vault.description: A sealed hollow beneath the stump, reached through a crack between two great roots and closed by a door of living wood carved with an unfinished verse. The roots around the door are warm, and something waits behind it.

The Puffball Reach.name: The Puffball Reach
The Puffball Reach.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 9 · Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Frontier (Low)]

The Puffball Reach is a wide open field on floor 9 where the glowcaps thin out and giant puffballs crowd the loam: pale domes as big as huts that split at a touch and fill the air with choking spores. Crossing it masked is slow and possible; crossing it unmasked is a mistake people make once. Dreamspore Clusters grow on the oldest puffballs, and alchemists above pay well for them. Spore-moths gather here in clouds, and the Riftmaw's hunters use the spore fog to stalk anyone who comes to harvest.
The Puffball Reach.hiddenInfo: A Sporeward hunter band went into the Reach two weeks ago and has not come back. Their bodies are not here; their spears are, stuck point-down in a ring around the largest puffball, which has not burst in living memory and is warm to the touch.

The Masked Path.description: A line of flagged stakes marking the safest route across the field, set by Lampblack's cartographer and moved every few days. Even on the path the air is hazy. A mask keeps a delver breathing; nothing keeps them from being seen.

The Burst Fields.description: The open heart of the Reach, where puffballs stand shoulder to shoulder and the ground is ankle deep in spent spore dust. One misstep sets off a chain of bursts, sight drops to an arm's length, and the moths come.

The Dreamspore Hollow.description: A dip where the oldest puffballs grow and Dreamspore Clusters hang from their sides like pale grapes. Harvesting them is quiet, careful work. The largest puffball stands at the centre, unburst and warm, ringed with stuck spears.

Quietwell.name: Quietwell
Quietwell.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Riftmaw Floor 12 · Recommended Level: 13-23 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Quietwell is the small town that grew around the Guild's First Rest Station on floor 12: a warded terrace of stone shelters, felt-hung doors and crystal-glass lamps built out from the station's alcove, around a clear pool that never stops filling. The ward and the Guild lift made it possible; the traders who followed the lift made it a town. Everyone here whispers, because a shout in the Geodes brings the hunters, and the rules are written on slates, not spoken. Who lives here: the station keeper and two wardens, crystal tuners who repair and sell resonance gear, a cook, scholars studying the ringing, and delvers resting between floors. Water comes from the pool; food comes down the lift and is not cheap. Prices: stew 6 Copper, a cot 1 Silver a night, a tuning 3 Silver, a resonance shard 8 Silver. Law: no raised voices, no bare steel on the terrace, and every party signs the logbook. A monster player needs a sponsor's tag to stay. Home base: a felt-walled room on the Warded Terrace for 5 Silver a week, or a share of a bunk room for 2. People come back for the lift, the quiet and the news on the slates.
Quietwell.hiddenInfo: The station keeper has kept the logbook for eleven years and knows which open entries are dead and which are only hiding; one of the hiding ones lives in Stillwing Roost. The pool is fed by the cold river from the Wilds and carries a faint hum of its own. Right now the tuners have heard a new note in the ringing, and they think the Geodes are trying to say a word. Work on offer: in the Tuning Market, a crystal tuner of the market pays for a silent trip into the geode to find and tune the new note in the ringing.

The First Rest Station.description: The Guild's original waypoint on floor 12: a fortified alcove with reinforced walls, a ward perimeter, supply caches restocked weekly, a water source and sleeping space for eight. The lift gantry stands at its back, iron and chain, running up into the dark. The logbook lies open by the door, and entries with no return date are left open.

The Tuning Market.description: A quiet terrace of crystal-glass stalls where tuners repair, sell and tune resonance gear by ear, holding each piece to a fork until it stops singing. Bargains are whispered and written on slates. A resonance shard is 8 Silver; tuning a blade or lantern is 3.

The Warded Terrace.description: Rows of small stone shelters along the ward's inner edge, each with a felt-hung door that muffles every sound. A room of your own is 5 Silver a week and stays yours while the rent is paid; a share of a bunk room is 2. Inside, the hum fades almost to nothing.

The Quiet Kitchen.description: A low cookhouse beside the pool where meals are made without clatter: felt on the pots, wooden ladles, bowls passed hand to hand. Stew is 6 Copper, and the bread came down on the last lift and gets harder by the day. Meals are eaten in silence, and nobody minds.

The Station Office.description: A crystal-lit room where the station keeper sorts lift passes, posts notices on slates and keeps the logbook's older volumes. Parties sign in and out here. Contracts for the Geodes are chalked on the wall, and payment waits in a locked chest for whoever comes back.

Stillwing Roost.name: Stillwing Roost
Stillwing Roost.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Monster Hold · Riftmaw Floor 13 · Recommended Level: 13-23 · No wild spawns inside · Residents decide who stays]

Stillwing Roost is a gargoyle hold on a terrace of crystal spires high in a geode on floor 13. Its gargoyles were carved for the cornices of the Halls of the Tall Kings far below and woke there under the court's law; some broke from it and climbed up into the Geodes, where stone that sleeps is never noticed. The Riftmaw hunts them now, so they keep to the Roost and sleep as statues among the crystal, and the Choir passes over them. Who lives here: gargoyles of grey and violet stone, a few greater gargoyles who serve as elders, and carvers among them who shape crystal into charms. They need no food, drink from the dripping crystal and take their strength from stillness; they trade charms, shards and what they have seen from the heights. A charm costs 2 to 5 Silver. Law: silence; nobody speaks above a whisper on the spires, and anyone who rings the crystal is thrown down. Delvers who climb up quietly with something to trade are tolerated; monster players of stone or winged kinds are welcomed as kin. Home base: a perch for kin who keep a watch shift; others may rent a ledge for a week of watch duty. People come back for the charms and for what the gargoyles saw.
Stillwing Roost.hiddenInfo: The Roost watches the lift shaft for Quietwell in return for a basket left on a ledge, though gargoyles do not eat; they pass it to the delver who has lived among them for years and is listed in the station's logbook as lost. The elders know the Hall Warden of floor 30 still calls them home. Right now one of the newest gargoyles has started answering the ringing in the crystal, and the elders fear the Choir will hear it. Work on offer: at the Elder Spire, a greater gargoyle of the elders asks, in a whisper, that someone find and silence the crystal the newest gargoyle sings back to.

The Spire Steps.description: A narrow stair cut into the crystal, winding up from the geode floor to the Roost's terrace, every step padded with felt the gargoyles took from delvers. A gargoyle sentry sits motionless at the top and moves only to stop someone.

The Sleeping Perches.description: Ledges and niches on the highest spires where gargoyles sleep as statues, wings folded, for days at a time. Kin who keep a watch shift are given a perch of their own; others may rent a ledge for a week of watch duty. It is cold, still and silent.

The Carving Floor.description: A broad shelf where gargoyle carvers shape crystal into charms that hum against a sleeper's skin and keep nightmares quiet. Charms cost 2 to 5 Silver. The carvers work in silence and point at what they want in trade.

The Hush Ward.description: A ring of carved stones around the terrace's edge that deadens sound, so a whisper inside does not carry. The first gargoyles to arrive carved it. Anyone who rings the crystal inside the ring is thrown off the terrace by the watch.

The Elder Spire.description: The tallest spire, where the greater gargoyles sit motionless and settle the Roost's business by long silence and a few words. Visitors bring questions here, and answers come slowly, sometimes days later, scratched into the crystal.

The Cartographer's Hollow.name: The Cartographer's Hollow
The Cartographer's Hollow.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 11 · Recommended Level: 13-23 · Danger: Rising (Moderate)]

The Cartographer's Hollow is a small geode on floor 11 where an old delver who went deaf in the ringing years ago lives and maps the Geodes by touch. Its walls are carved floor to ceiling with routes, scratched by hand: every passage, every throat, every place the crystal changes. The cartographer does not leave, trades maps for food and news, and answers only questions written down. The hollow lies outside every ward, and the echo-bats leave it alone for reasons nobody understands.
The Cartographer's Hollow.hiddenInfo: The cartographer is not entirely deaf: they hear the ringing as words and have been writing them down for years, in a column of tiny marks along the hollow's floor. The routes on the walls include one that does not match any floor the Guild knows. The echo-bats leave the hollow alone because the cartographer feeds them.

The Carved Map Wall.description: Every wall of the hollow carved floor to ceiling with routes: passages, throats, pools and warnings, scratched by hand with a knife. It is the most complete map of the Geodes anywhere, and it can only be read by touch and patience.

The Workroom.description: A cluttered corner of crystal shelves, knives, slates and food tins where the cartographer sits and copies routes onto slate for anyone who pays in food, news or 3 Silver. Questions are written on a slate and answered the same way.

The Touch Library.description: A narrow passage at the hollow's back lined with carved slates stacked like books, each one a single route the cartographer walked. Some are wrapped in cloth and not for sale. A long column of tiny marks runs along the floor here.

The Choirless Geode.name: The Choirless Geode
The Choirless Geode.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 14 · Recommended Level: 13-23 · Danger: Rising (Moderate)]

The Choirless Geode is a cavern on floor 14 where sound dies. The crystal is dull and grey, the ringing stops at its mouth, and a shout inside makes no noise at all. Delvers come here to rest from the hum, and some never leave, because the things that hunt by sound wait at the edge of the silence for someone to speak on the way out. Basilisks bask in the dead crystal, and the dull grey shards are prized by Quietwell's tuners for silence charms.
The Choirless Geode.hiddenInfo: The silence is not natural. The Choir of Echoes took this geode's voice and keeps it on floor 15, and the dull crystal remembers. A careful tuner could give it back, which would make the whole Geodes louder and the Choir weaker. Right now the edge of the silence is creeping outward a hand's width a day.

The Silent Throat.description: The narrow passage into the geode, where the hum fades step by step until it is gone. Delvers pause here to let their ears adjust. The rock is scratched with warnings in hand-sign, because spoken ones do not work.

The Bowl.description: The geode's wide, dull heart: grey crystal on every side and a silence so complete a dropped blade makes no sound. Basilisks sleep in its warm hollows. It is the only place in the Geodes where a delver can hear their own heartbeat.

The Listener's Ledge.description: A shelf on the geode's far side where the silence ends abruptly, so anything waiting outside hears the first word spoken. Dull grey shards worth good Silver to the tuners lie scattered along it.

Emberhold.name: Emberhold
Emberhold.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Riftmaw Floor 17 · Recommended Level: 18-28 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Emberhold is a salvagers' town in the dry upper forge halls on floor 17, built around the one great furnace the Riftmaw's patrols never come near. Its people are independent delvers, smiths and pump-keepers who came down for Rift-Touched Ore and decided to stay where it is mined. It survives because the halls are high and dry, the pumps keep the water out, and the forge golems on patrol walk past the old furnace doors as if they were sealed. Who lives here: salvage crews, a forge-master who runs the furnace, pump-keepers, an ore assayer, and a cook who trades in hot food and gossip. Food comes down from Quietwell or across from Anvilward for metalwork; water comes from the cascade, filtered. Prices: a hot meal 8 Copper, a bunk 1 Silver a night, an ore assay 2 Silver, a blade repaired 4 Silver. Law: everyone takes a pump shift, and nobody touches a shade's tools. Delvers are welcome if they work; Anvilward's golems trade here openly, and other monster players are judged by what they bring. Home base: a stone room with a door for 6 Silver a week and a pump shift. People come back because the furnace takes Rift-Touched Ore better than any forge on the surface.
Emberhold.hiddenInfo: The patrols are not fooled by the furnace doors. The forge-master made a bargain with the smiths' shades years ago, a share of every blade forged here, and the shades turn the patrols away. Nobody else knows. Right now the pumps are failing as the water rises, and the town is quietly arguing about moving up into Anvilward's halls. Work on offer: in the Pump House, a pump-keeper on the night shift needs a sound valve hauled up from the flooded halls before the water passes the gauge.

The Pump House.description: A hall of iron pumps and leather bellows that keep the black water out of Emberhold's lower rooms, worked in shifts day and night. Everyone who lives here takes a shift. The pumps are the town's heartbeat, and silence from the pump house means trouble.

The Furnace Terrace.description: A stepped stone terrace around the great furnace, still lit, where the forge-master and the smiths work Rift-Touched Ore into blades and plate. A repaired blade is 4 Silver; new work is priced by the ore. The heat is fierce and the light is red.

The Salvage Yard.description: A walled yard piled with what the crews dragged out of the flooded halls: iron, gears, golem plates, ore. The assayer weighs and prices it, 2 Silver an assay, and buys what the furnace can use. Trade here is loud, fair and quick.

The Dry Bunks.description: Stone sleeping rooms on the town's highest floor, dry and warm from the furnace below. A bunk is 1 Silver a night; a room with a door is 6 Silver a week and a pump shift, and stays yours while both are paid. The walls sweat in the heat.

The Floodwatch.description: A balcony over the flooded halls where a watch is kept on the water's level and on what moves in it. A painted gauge on the wall shows how high the water has come this season, and the latest mark is the highest yet.

Anvilward.name: Anvilward
Anvilward.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Monster Hold · Riftmaw Floor 16 · Recommended Level: 18-28 · No wild spawns inside · Residents decide who stays]

Anvilward is a hold of awakened forge-golems in a sealed smithy wing on floor 16. They were built to walk the hold's rounds, like the golems that still patrol, until one day they stopped walking and started working. The Riftmaw counts them as broken now and sends its patrols against them, so Anvilward keeps its iron doors barred and its one forge lit. Who lives here: forge-golems of riveted iron, smaller construct-kin built from salvage, a few living armors that wandered in and stayed, and a golem elder who keeps time for all of them. They do not eat; they need oil, coal and parts, and trade repairs and metalwork for them. A repair of plate or limbs costs 3 to 10 Silver, or the same in coal and oil. Law: they never strike first, and the forge never goes out. Delvers are let in to trade if they bring oil, coal or parts; monster players of construct kinds are greeted as kin and repaired for free. Home base: an alcove in the Core Vault for construct kin who take a forge shift; others may rent a workspace by the week. People come back because Anvilward repairs what the surface cannot.
Anvilward.hiddenInfo: The golems did not stop their rounds by accident. Before the Riftmaw took the hold, its last smith gave the golem elder a core with a will of its own, and the elder has been waking the others one at a time ever since. The patrols want that core. Right now a patrol is camped outside the Hammer Gate, and the golems have refused to strike first for nine days. Work on offer: at the Quiet Forge, a forge-golem at the bellows asks for coal brought in past the patrol at the gate before the forge goes cold.

The Hammer Gate.description: A pair of iron doors twice a man's height, barred from inside and hung with a great hammer that visitors strike to ask entry. A golem sentry opens a hatch and looks. Those who bring oil, coal or parts are let in; others are asked to leave politely, and only once.

The Maintenance Bays.description: Long racks and benches where golems and construct-kin are taken apart, oiled, mended and put back together. Construct kin are repaired free; others pay 3 to 10 Silver or the same in coal and oil. The smell of oil and hot metal never fades.

The Quiet Forge.description: The hold's one forge, kept lit by golems who take turns at the bellows in perfect rhythm. They make tools, plate and parts here and sell what they do not need. Nobody speaks over the hammering, and nobody needs to.

The Core Vault.description: A round chamber of alcoves where golems stand still to rest, their cores dimmed, with spare cores in a locked case at the centre. Construct kin who take a forge shift are given an alcove of their own; others may rent a workspace here by the week.

The Clock of Work.description: A great iron clock on the wall, built by the golems, that marks the shifts at the forge and the bays; every golem in the hold moves by it. The golem elder stands beneath it, keeps time, and hears visitors when the hammers rest.

The Slagfall Crossing.name: The Slagfall Crossing
The Slagfall Crossing.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 18 · Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Rising (Moderate)]

The Slagfall Crossing is the only way over the molten slag channel that cuts floor 18 in two: an old iron bridge, black and sagging, above a river of glowing slag that has run for an age. A toll-keeper's camp sits on the near bank behind a wall of salvaged plate, charging for passage and for the use of the bridge's one safe rail. The heat on the bridge blisters skin, and the forge golems' patrol route crosses it twice a day.
The Slagfall Crossing.hiddenInfo: The toll-keeper was set here by Emberhold's forge-master and reports every party that crosses back to the town. The bridge's middle span rests on a single golem that has stood still beneath it for longer than anyone remembers, and it has started to move.

The Toll Camp.description: A cluttered camp on the near bank, walled with salvaged golem plate and roofed against the heat. The toll-keeper charges 3 Silver a head for the bridge and sells water at a price the heat makes fair. A board lists who crossed and when.

The Iron Bridge.description: A long iron span over the slag, black, sagging and hot enough to blister bare hands. One rail is safe; the other is not. The air shimmers with heat, and the crossing takes a long, careful minute.

The Molten Channel.description: The river of glowing slag below the bridge, slow, bright and roaring softly, its banks crusted with cooled slag full of trapped ore. Harvesting at the edge is possible for anyone who can stand the heat, between the golem patrols.

The Sunken Foundry.name: The Sunken Foundry
The Sunken Foundry.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 19 · Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Rising (Moderate)]

The Sunken Foundry is the drowned heart of the Forgehold: a great foundry hall on floor 19 flooded to its rooflines, chimneys and gantries rising out of still black water. Salvagers dive here for Rift-Touched Ore and Fractured Golem Cores that sank with the hall, working from the last dry roof by lantern light. Rust-eaters swarm the water and strip metal off anyone who wades, and the shades of drowned smiths still work at sunken anvils below the surface.
The Sunken Foundry.hiddenInfo: The foundry's drowned golems are not all dead. Their cores glow faintly under the water, and Anvilward would pay almost anything to bring them up and wake them. Right now the water is rising, and the last dry roof will be gone in a week.

The Drowned Roofs.description: The tops of the foundry's chimneys and roofs, rising out of black water like islands. Salvagers tie their boats and ropes here, and the last dry roof holds their camp. The water is still and cold, and things move under it.

The Dive Shaft.description: A wide chimney with an iron ladder running down into the drowned foundry floor. Divers go down on a rope with a weighted lantern and come up with ore, cores or nothing. Rust-eaters gather at the bottom when they hear metal.

The Golem Graveyard.description: The drowned foundry floor, where dozens of golems lie where they fell when the water came, cores glowing faintly through the black water. Salvage here is rich and dangerous, and the smiths' shades watch from their anvils.

Kingsrest.name: Kingsrest
Kingsrest.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Riftmaw Floor 25 · Recommended Level: 23-38 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Kingsrest is the small town that grew around the Guild's Midway Outpost on floor 25, inside a gatehouse of the Tall Kings: a walled gate court, the old guard barracks and two great halls, all built for people a head taller than anyone living. It is the lift's lowest stop and the deepest place the Guild keeps people. It survives because the gatehouse is warded and walled, the Riftmaw does not rearrange a warded station, and the armor in the gate alcoves has never woken for anyone who bows on the way past. Who lives here: the outpost's rotating team of four, a long-staying quartermaster, Company crews renting space, a cook, a healer, a regalia appraiser, and delvers resting before the Galleries. Water comes from the gatehouse cistern and food down the lift; the amber light never dims, so people sleep in hoods. Prices: a hot meal 1 Silver, a bunk 2 Silver a night, a bandage roll 6 Copper, court regalia appraised 5 Silver. Law: weapons stay at rest in the gate court, everyone bows to the alcoves, every party signs in and out, and the outpost team's word is final. A monster player needs a Sponsor Register tag; Hornhall's traders deal at the gate. Home base: a walled cell in Kingsrest Barracks for 12 Silver a week and a turn on the gate watch, and you answer the muster bell. People come back for the lift, the last hot meal above the Galleries, and the contracts in the Company Hall.
Kingsrest.hiddenInfo: The bow is not superstition. The first Guild crew bowed to the gate armor because they were frightened, and the gatehouse received them as the court's guests; every outpost team since has been taught the bow without being told why, and nobody knows what wakes if the custom lapses. Right now the Guild above is short of volunteers, two teams cut their month short this season, and a Company is offering to hold the outpost for good, against the rotation. The quartermaster, who has outlasted every team, decides whose crates come off the lift first, and that is who really runs Kingsrest. Work on offer: at the Midway Outpost, the leader of the outpost team, one hand short, will pay someone to stand the fourth post for a week so the rotation holds.

The Midway Outpost.description: The Guild's fortified post in the gatehouse, the deepest permanent Guild presence in the Riftmaw and the lift's lowest stop. A rotating team of four, chosen for steady nerves, keeps it as resupply point, emergency shelter and listening post; nobody serves more than one month. Its walls are carved with observations about the deep floors, and read in order they make a picture of the dungeon hard to hold in one mind.

Kingsrest Barracks.description: The gatehouse's old guard barracks: long stone rooms with doorways built for the Tall Kings' guards, split by timber walls into bunks and cells. A bunk is 2 Silver a night; a walled cell with a lockbox is 12 Silver a week and a turn on the gate watch, and stays yours while both are kept. The amber light never dims here, so every bunk has a hood hanging from its post.

The Quartermaster's Court.description: An open court inside the gate where the lift's crates are broken open and sold: rope, rations, lamp oil for the Galleries, bandages, arrows, the odd crate of bread. The quartermaster keeps a slate and the only key, prices everything at about twice the surface rate, and buys court regalia once the appraiser has looked at it. Whatever a party takes is chalked against its name.

The Company Hall.description: A former audience chamber the Companies share. Each Company with a crew down here keeps a table and a banner, and contracts for the Halls and the Galleries hang on a long board by the door. The stone swallows sound, so a deal at one table is never overheard at the next. A Guild crew between supply runs can be hired here by the day.

The Long Mess.description: A processional hall turned dining room, one table running its full length under the amber light, benches cut down to human height. A hot meal is 1 Silver and a mug of small beer 4 Copper, and the cook serves whatever came down the lift that week. By custom the last party back from below sits at the head of the table and tells the room what they saw.

Hornhall.name: Hornhall
Hornhall.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Monster Hold · Riftmaw Floor 22 · Recommended Level: 23-38 · No wild spawns inside · Residents decide who stays]

Hornhall is a minotaur clan's hold in the royal stables and arena wing on floor 22. The Riftmaw made its first bulls as the palace's arena champions; they slipped its will when they stopped fighting for an empty royal box and started fighting for each other. Court law never covered the stables, so no sentinel stands there, but hunting packs raid the herd and the Riftmaw's armor tests the gate, so the clan keeps one gate, a watch and the Proving Ring. Who lives here: minotaurs, broad, proud, quick to laugh and slow to forgive, a few horned kin who earned their place, and the clan's eldest bull, who presides at the hearth. They herd pale cave cattle and rock goats, grow a hard grey grain in old arena sand under the amber light, and drink from the royal troughs. Trade: smoked meat 1 Silver a slab, a hide 3 Silver, a horn-handled knife 6 Silver, a practice bout 2 Silver. Law: disputes go to the Ring, never the knife; nobody strikes a beast; whoever calls a duel fights it. Delvers pay 5 Silver a head at the Horn Gate or win guest-right in a first-blood bout. Minotaurs and other horned kinds are kin, and any monster player who wins a bout is heard. Home base: a stall in the Long Stables, free to kin who take a night watch on the herd each week; a guest with guest-right pays 4 Silver a week. People come back for the Ring, the meat and the clan's long memory of who fought well.
Hornhall.hiddenInfo: The founders did not slip the Riftmaw's will alone: a court wraith granted their petition to be free of it, and the favour owed has never been asked. Every eldest bull since has waited for the court to collect. Right now a hunting pack takes one beast a night from the far end of the stables, the herd is down by a fifth, and the clan's hot-blooded fighters want to chase the pack into the halls, where court law would wake every sentinel around them. The eldest bull presides, but the granary-keeper, an old minotaur with one broken horn who counts every sack, decides who eats and quietly runs Hornhall. Work on offer: at the Stone Granary, the old granary-keeper with a broken horn wants the night raids on the herd stopped without anyone chasing the pack into the halls.

The Horn Gate.description: The stable wing's great arched gate, built tall enough for a mounted king and hung with the horns of every bull who died defending it. Two minotaur wardens stand watch with poleaxes. Delvers stop at the scored line on the floor, state their business and pay 5 Silver a head; horned kin are greeted by touching horns and walk straight through.

The Proving Ring.description: The old royal arena: a round floor of raked sand under tiered stone seats and an empty royal box nobody sits in. Disputes, challenges and guest-right bouts are fought here to first blood, with the clan as witness. A practice bout costs 2 Silver, and a visitor who fights well is talked about at the hearth for a long time.

The Long Stables.description: A stable court of tall stone stalls built for the kings' war-mounts, now bedded with straw for the clan and its herd. Kin claim an empty stall by taking a night watch on the herd each week; a guest who has won guest-right pays 4 Silver a week to the granary. The air is warm with animals, and the cattle low at anything that does not smell of the clan.

The Hearth of Horns.description: A long hall around a fire pit that never goes out, where the clan eats, argues and retells each duel until everyone agrees on how it went. The eldest bull sits at the hearth's head. Nobody enters armed, and a guest who is handed meat from the spit has been accepted for the night.

The Stone Granary.description: Heavy domed stores at the back of the stables, cool and dry, holding sacks of the hard grey grain the clan grows in the arena sand, smoked meat on hooks and hides in stacks. The granary-keeper counts every sack in and out, and theft from the granary is the one crime that ends in exile instead of a duel.

The Court of Petitions.name: The Court of Petitions
The Court of Petitions.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 23 · Recommended Level: 23-38 · Danger: Veteran (High)]

The Court of Petitions is an audience chamber on floor 23 where the court wraiths of the Tall Kings still sit in session, tall and faded, waiting for a petition to hear. A petitioner who bows at the colonnade, waits on the bench to be called and keeps weapons at rest may stand on the court floor and ask for one thing: a hall crossed in safety, a sentinel stood down, a lost thing found, a door opened. The court hears each petitioner once. It grants a petition for a courtesy shown or a favour owed, and a granted petition leaves a favour owed in return, which the court will one day ask for. A drawn weapon, a raised voice or a spell ends the session, and every wraith in the chamber treats the petitioner as an intruder. Court law holds inside the colonnade; the hunting packs outside answer to nothing.
The Court of Petitions.hiddenInfo: The favours the court asks are never random: carry a piece of regalia back to its alcove, open a sealed door, bow before an empty throne. Each one clears a step of the way to floor 30, because the court is choosing who will carry the heir's crown. A petition that asks about the crown is never granted, only answered with a favour asked. Right now a delver party granted a safe crossing last season has not paid its favour, and wraiths have begun to appear near Kingsrest's gate, waiting.

The Petitioners' Bench.description: A long stone bench outside the colonnade, built for the Tall Kings, so a human petitioner's feet hang above the floor. Petitioners wait here to be called, an hour or a day; anyone who stands before they are called loses their turn. Thin scratches along the bench mark the waits of people who sat here before.

The Court Floor.description: A polished floor before an empty dais that rings at every step, so the whole court hears a petitioner approach. The petitioner stands alone, bows, and asks for one thing. A wraith answers with a slow gesture, and a granted petition is sealed by a cold hand laid on the shoulder. Steel drawn here wakes every wraith in the chamber.

The Wraith Gallery.description: A recessed gallery of high seats above the court floor, where rows of court wraiths sit in tall, faded finery and watch each petition in silence. They remember every courtesy and every debt. No petitioner is allowed up the gallery stair, and a living foot on its first step ends the session for everyone in the room.

The Sentinel Throne.name: The Sentinel Throne
The Sentinel Throne.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 29 · Recommended Level: 23-38 · Danger: Veteran (High)]

The Sentinel Throne is the last great audience hall above the Hall Warden's floor: a long, narrow chamber on floor 29 lined on both sides with suits of armor asleep in their alcoves, hundreds of them, and at its far end a throne too tall for anyone living, empty. Court law is strongest here. A party that bows at the threshold, keeps its weapons at rest and walks the length of the hall at an even pace crosses without a roll; a drawn weapon, a raised voice, a spell or a run wakes every sentinel at once. Court regalia lies on the throne steps where it fell, and lifting any of it is theft before the throne, which wakes them too. Delvers come to test their nerve, and the bold come for the regalia.
The Sentinel Throne.hiddenInfo: This is not the kings' throne. The throne that matters stands on floor 30; this seat was kept empty for the heir, and the sentinels in these rows were the heir's guard. They do not wake for someone wearing the heir's crown: they kneel. Nobody alive knows that. Right now the hall is half awake: a party woke it last month and lost two people, and a dozen sentinels have not gone back to their alcoves but stand in the aisle, weapons at rest, waiting to be bowed to.

The Bowing Approach.description: A broad processional ramp into the hall, its floor worn into two shallow hollows at the threshold where countless petitioners knelt and bowed. Delvers who know the Halls stop here, bow, and settle their weapons before going on. Every sound on the ramp runs ahead into the hall, so a careless word arrives before the party does.

The Sentinel Rows.description: Two long rows of deep alcoves down the hall's length, each holding a suit of armor asleep at attention, helm bowed, hands on a grounded weapon. The aisle between them is just wide enough for two to walk abreast. A party that keeps its pace even and its hands still crosses in about a hundred breaths; nobody who ran has made it.

The Empty Throne.description: A stepped dais at the hall's far end and a throne of pale stone far too tall for anyone living, its seat worn smooth and empty. Court regalia lies scattered on the steps, rings, a sceptre, a torn mantle, where it fell an age ago. Lifting any piece wakes the rows behind, and the way back is the whole length of the hall.

The Clerk's Counter.name: The Clerk's Counter
The Clerk's Counter.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Riftmaw Floor 33 · Recommended Level: 33-48 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The Clerk's Counter is an independent exchange in a barricaded mending hall on floor 33, where the galleries' exhibits were once repaired: a dead end with one door and nothing on display. Holding no exhibits, it is never rearranged and the keepers have nothing to guard there; a barricade of empty display cases keeps the stalkers and mimics out. Delvers named it as a joke on the Curator's clerk, who prices everything in the corridors, but the people here are living, answer to nobody below, and cannot speak for the Curator or call off a keeper. Who lives here: a cataloguer left behind by a Guild survey years ago, delver brokers, porters who haul from Kingsrest, and a cook. Water drips into a cistern at the back; food is carried down and priced to match. Prices: an appraisal naming a piece's catch 3 Silver, a claim registered 2 Silver, a meal 2 Silver, a bunk 3 Silver a night. Law: no exhibit crosses the barricade while its keeper follows, nobody touches another party's claim, and a broker's word at the desk binds. Delvers are welcome; a monster player gets in on a broker's word or a Sponsor Register tag, and the Bazaar's mimics never pass the barricade, because nobody can tell which chest is a guest. Home base: a back room for 15 Silver a week and a shift on the barricade. People come back to learn what they carried out, and what it will cost them.
The Clerk's Counter.hiddenInfo: The cataloguer was not left behind: they stayed, because one alcove on floor 36 holds a piece from their own home that they have never dared to move, and they visit it every month. The brokers sell the Bazaar's curios up to Kingsrest without saying where they came from. Right now a delver party is camped outside the barricade with a keeper standing over them, begging to be let in, and the brokers are arguing over whether the barricade's law can bend once. The senior broker holds the desk, but the porters decide what comes down from Kingsrest and when, and the brokers do as the porters ask. Work on offer: at the Barricade, the broker's hired guard at the gap pays to have the keeper over the party camped outside settled, so they can come in.

The Barricade.description: A wall of empty display cases, crates and an old gallery door stacked across the hall's only mouth, with a gap one person wide and a bell above it. A broker's hired guard keeps the gap. Anyone arriving with a keeper behind them is turned away until the exhibit is put back, and nobody argues with the bell.

The Appraisal Desk.description: A long mending bench under a hanging lamp where the cataloguer turns a piece in gloved hands, says where it came from as near as anyone can, and names its catch, because every piece from the Galleries has one. An appraisal is 3 Silver. Pieces are never touched bare-handed here, to keep the visions off the desk.

The Claims Wall.description: A plastered wall chalked with claims: who found which cache, which corridor a party has marked, which back room is whose and who still owes the porters. A claim is registered for 2 Silver and holds while its party lives and pays. Old claims are never wiped; they are crossed through with a single line when the party stops coming back.

The Back Rooms.description: Narrow store rooms behind the desk, once full of mending tools, now walled off with canvas and old gallery doors. A bunk in the shared room is 3 Silver a night; a room of your own with a lock is 15 Silver a week and a shift on the barricade, and stays yours while both are kept. The quiet here is the gallery kind: complete.

The Brokers' Court.description: A square court at the hall's far end where delver brokers sit at folding tables, buy salvage and pieces whose keepers are destroyed, sell supplies, and match parties to buyers in Kingsrest. Talk is low and fast, and deals are shaken on, not written. The Bazaar sends its prices by note through the barricade, and the brokers pretend not to read them.

The Mimic Bazaar.name: The Mimic Bazaar
The Mimic Bazaar.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Monster Hold · Riftmaw Floor 38 · Recommended Level: 33-48 · No wild spawns inside · Residents decide who stays]

The Mimic Bazaar is a hold of mimics, imps and collector kobolds in a side gallery on floor 38, trading in exhibits lifted from the corridors. It survives on one trick: the keepers cannot tell a mimic from an exhibit. When a keeper passes, the Bazaar goes still, the imps and kobolds climb inside the mimics, and the gallery is a display of chests and stands, all in place. An exhibit shut inside a mimic counts as displayed, so its keeper stops following. The Riftmaw's own mimics and hoard-drakes are not fooled and raid the dens, so every door has a watch. Who lives here: mimics of every shape, the oldest as big as wardrobes; imps who run the stalls; kobolds who collect and sort. They eat what traders bring and what the mimics catch; water is a drip in a bare hall next door. Prices: a curio with its keeper lost 5 to 40 Silver, a followed piece shut away in a mimic 10 Silver, a meal 2 Silver. Every curio keeps its catch, and the imps never say what. Law: nothing is taken from a den, no chest is opened without asking, and at the bell everyone goes still. Delvers pay 5 Silver a head at the Chest Gate and may not stay the night; mimics, imps and small trickster kinds are kin, and any monster player who can hold still is welcome to try. Home base: a den in the Hoard Dens for a fifth of what you trade. People come back to lose a keeper and to buy what is sold nowhere else.
The Mimic Bazaar.hiddenInfo: The Chest Gate is the oldest mimic in the Bazaar, and lately it opens a little slower each day; the imps fear it is becoming an exhibit in truth, and if a keeper ever opens it, the trick ends. The Bazaar quietly sells to the Clerk's Counter, which sells up to Kingsrest. Right now a hoard-drake has coiled round the Curio Exchange's richest case and will not leave, and nobody can trade there. The imps run the stalls, but the kobold sorter who decides what is sold and what is kept runs the Bazaar. Work on offer: at the Curio Exchange, the kobold sorter of the Exchange wants the hoard-drake coiled round the richest case moved out with no case broken.

The Chest Gate.description: The Bazaar's door is a mimic: an iron-banded chest the size of a cart, set across the gallery's mouth, that opens its lid to let a guest step through. Kin walk in. Delvers pay 5 Silver a head to a kobold sitting on the lid and keep their hands where it can see them. When the bell rings, the lid shuts on whoever is halfway.

The Haggling Floor.description: The sunken court at the gallery's heart, crowded with chests, stands and cases that are traders as often as they are furniture. Bargains are struck loudly and fast, and anything can be bought if the price is odd enough. At the bell, everything on the floor goes still at once, and so must every guest.

The Imp Stalls.description: A row of awnings under the arcade where imps sell small lifted things: rings, keys, inks, spectacles, a music box that plays half a tune. They name a price and never the catch. A delver who asks too many questions is charged more, and one who laughs at their jokes is charged less.

The Hoard Dens.description: Alcoves along the back wall, each walled with stacked cases and hung with whatever its keeper loves best. Kin claim an empty den by bringing in a curio worth sharing and giving a fifth of what they trade to the Bazaar; the den stays theirs while they live in it. A den's mark is scratched on its lintel, and nobody enters unasked.

The Curio Exchange.description: A ring of glass cases where the Bazaar's best pieces are kept, each with its keeper lost: a crown with no country, a sword that hums, a book in no known script. Prices run from 5 to 40 Silver. A kobold sorter will swear a piece is clear of keepers but never of catches, because nothing from the Galleries is.

The Hall of Lost Worlds.name: The Hall of Lost Worlds
The Hall of Lost Worlds.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 36 · Recommended Level: 33-48 · Danger: Veteran (High)]

The Hall of Lost Worlds is a set of quiet display courts on floor 36 where the Galleries keep things from whole worlds side by side: armor from one, farm tools from another, a shelf of lamps that run on nothing anyone here understands. One side gallery, which delvers call the Alcove of Home, holds things from the world the Reborn remember: a commuter's bag with a train pass clipped to the strap, a phone with no signal, a cheap umbrella, a wristwatch stopped at ten past eight. Reborn who find it often sit a long while. Every piece is dusted and in its place, and every one has a keeper, which comes when it is moved and follows until it is put back. Touching a piece can show its owner's hand on it, and that is the cost Reborn pay most often.
The Hall of Lost Worlds.hiddenInfo: Every object in the Alcove of Home was in someone's hand or pocket on the day they left the old world, and the visions show that moment. A Reborn who looks long enough may find something that was theirs; its keeper will come for it all the same. Right now one keeper has stopped walking the courts and stands at the Alcove of Home day and night, because a Reborn delver from Kingsrest comes down every week to sit in front of it, and the keeper moves closer with each visit.

The Display Courts.description: Square courts with roofed alcove galleries on every side, each alcove holding something from one lost world: armor, tools, instruments, lamps that burn without oil. The plaques under them are blank. The dust is wiped from every piece and from nowhere else, and footsteps sound loud in the hush.

The Alcove of Home.description: A short side gallery of alcoves holding things from the Reborn's old world: a commuter's bag, a phone with no signal, a convenience-store umbrella, earbuds in a tangle, a train pass. Each sits on a clean shelf under soft light. Touching one shows a vision of the hand that held it last. The silence here is heavier than anywhere else in the Galleries.

The Keepers' Niche.description: A tall niche at the head of the courts where the keepers stand when nothing has been moved, shapes of dust and glass as tall as the doorways, so still they could be exhibits. When something in the Hall shifts, one of them steps down and walks. Counting them before touching anything is how careful delvers tell when one is missing.

Scab Camp.name: Scab Camp
Scab Camp.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Riftmaw Floor 43 · Recommended Level: 43-58 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Scab Camp is a delver camp on floor 43, pitched where the walls have calcified into hard, pale mineral and stopped breathing: the only ground on these floors that does not move. No door closes on it, no room changes shape, and the violet pulse dies at its edge, so the camp burns lamps. It survives because the body sealed an old wound here and treats what lies inside the seal as dealt with: antibody knights walk the edge and do not step onto it. It is not Guild ground. Who lives here: deep delvers from the Companies and independents, a field surgeon who knows acid burns, a cache-keeper, listeners on watch, and porters who haul from Kingsrest. Water is bought by the jar from the Lymph Pools; food is carried eighteen floors down. Prices: a day's rations 3 Silver, a jar of clear water 1 Silver, an acid burn dressed 5 Silver, a bunk 4 Silver a night. Law: nobody bleeds at the edge, nobody chips the scab, no fire against a living wall, and whoever hears a lost voice calling stays put. Delvers are welcome; a monster player who keeps the listening watch is welcome too, and slime-kin come up to trade. Home base: a bunk of your own in the Still Bunks for 20 Silver a week and a listening shift. People come back because it is the one place on these floors where nothing moves while you sleep.
Scab Camp.hiddenInfo: The scab sealed over a delver camp from long ago: under the oldest bunks, shapes of packs and bedrolls show through the pale mineral, and nobody sleeps on that part of the shelf. The problem now is that the scab is healing from its edges inward; the stretch by the Listening Post breathed last week. A delver half grown into the living wall a few hundred paces out is still talking, and the camp is split on whether cutting them free is mercy or bait. The field surgeon decides who is fit to go deeper, and that makes the surgeon the camp's real authority. Work on offer: in the Treatment Tent, the camp's field surgeon will pay someone to cut free the delver half grown into the living wall out past the Listening Post.

The Calcified Shelf.description: The camp's ground: a long ridge of hard, pale mineral grown over the corridor wall, dull and still where everything around it breathes. Shelters of canvas and crate wood are pegged into its cracks. Stepping off the shelf onto the warm floor feels like stepping off a dock, and old hands tap the scab twice when they come home.

The Treatment Tent.description: A large lamplit tent at the shelf's centre where the field surgeon dresses acid burns from the gut-rivers and the crush wounds the walls leave when a doorway closes on a straggler. A dressing is 5 Silver; worse is priced by the hour. The tent smells of vinegar and lamp oil, and the surgeon decides who is fit to go deeper.

The Still Bunks.description: Bunks built into hollows in the oldest mineral, where the scab is thickest and nothing moves at all. A bunk is 4 Silver a night; a bunk of your own with a lockbox is 20 Silver a week and a listening shift, and stays yours while both are kept. Delvers say they sleep better here than anywhere since Kingsrest.

The Supply Cache.description: Crates stacked under a canvas roof at the shelf's back, filled by porters who haul from Kingsrest: rations at 3 Silver a day, lamp oil, rope, bandages, and clear water from the Lymph Pools at 1 Silver a jar. The cache-keeper chalks each draw against a party's name on a slate. Nothing on the shelf is cheap, and nobody expects it to be.

The Listening Post.description: A raised lookout at the shelf's edge facing the living corridor, where a listener sits with a hand flat on the wall, feeling for the slow breath to change. Knights, packs and closing doors all show in the breath first. The post has one rule: whoever hears a lost voice calling from the corridor does not answer it, and does not go.

The Lymph Pools.name: The Lymph Pools
The Lymph Pools.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Monster Hold · Riftmaw Floor 46 · Recommended Level: 43-58 · No wild spawns inside · Residents decide who stays]

The Lymph Pools are a hold of slime-kin in a chamber of clear fluid cisterns on floor 46. The body tolerates them as part of itself because they filter its fluids: antibody knights pass the pools the way they pass the body's own fluid, for as long as the filtering goes on. When a pool clouds, knights come to the membrane, so the hold works in shifts that never stop, and gut-crawlers from the acid rivers raid it anyway. Who lives here: slimes of every colour and size, slow-spoken, patient and blunt, who shape a mouth to talk to outsiders, and a few Slime-Born who came down from the surface and stayed. They feed on what the fluid carries, drink it clean, and see by the violet pulse through clear water. Trade: clear water 1 Silver a jar, Mana Crystal grit 4 Silver a pinch, acid washed out of gear or a wound 3 Silver. Law: nothing clouds a pool, nothing is taken from the fluid without asking, and every outsider is washed at the gate. Delvers pay 5 Silver for the wash, a film that keeps the knights from noticing a guest among the pools; slime kinds are kin, and other monster players earn a place with a shift in the Filter Gardens. Home base: a warm pool for kin who take a filtering shift; others may rent a dry ledge for 10 Silver a week. People come back for clean water, the wash, and the one ground down here the knights walk past.
The Lymph Pools.hiddenInfo: The slime-kin know where the knights will go: the fluid carries a delver's blood through the body, and the knights follow it. The Clear Council once dropped blood into the right channel to draw a raid away from Scab Camp, and the camp never knew. Right now the deepest pool is clouding with something carried up from the Convergence, and the filters cannot clear it. The Council decides by merging, but the gate-washers choose who gets the film, and they quietly run the hold. Work on offer: in the Filter Gardens, the slime who leads the filter shift needs the clouded fluid carried out of the deepest pool before the knights come.

The Membrane Gate.description: A soft, clear membrane stretched across the chamber's mouth, firm and warm to the touch. Gate-washers, large patient slimes, take a visitor's toll and wash them in filtered fluid that leaves a thin film on skin and gear, so the knights pass them by among the pools. Kin slide straight through. The gate smells of nothing at all.

The Warm Pools.description: Round basins of clear, warm fluid stepping down the chamber, each with a smooth lip to climb in by. Slime kin claim an empty pool by taking a filtering shift in the gardens each day; others may rent a dry ledge beside one for 10 Silver a week. A claimed pool is marked by a pebble on its lip, and nobody else's pebble goes there.

The Filter Gardens.description: Terraces of pale rippled growth between the pools, where slimes lie in rows and pass the body's fluid through themselves until it runs clear. It is slow, quiet work, done in shifts that never stop. Outsiders earn their place here by carrying silt away in buckets, and Mana Crystal grit settles in the bottom terrace.

The Clear Council.description: The largest pool, where the hold's eldest slimes meet and settle questions by flowing into one another until they agree, which can take a day. Outsiders speak from the lip and are answered by a single mouth shaped in the surface. A decision is final once the council separates.

The Dividing Room.description: A small chamber off the pools, walled with low membranes, where a slime grown too large for its pool goes to split in two. Both halves come out full-grown, each with the whole memory, and argue for a day over which one keeps the pool. Visitors come in only when invited; the hold treats a division as private business.

The Antibody Nursery.name: The Antibody Nursery
The Antibody Nursery.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 45 · Recommended Level: 43-58 · Danger: Elite (Severe)]

The Antibody Nursery is a long ribbed chamber on floor 45 where the stratum's antibody knights form. Along its walls the material swells into pale blisters, and inside each one a knight's armor sets hard over days, faceless and fully formed, until the wall opens and it walks out toward whatever does not belong. Knights that set wrong are pushed out into a sunken midden of shed plate. Antibody Knight Plate is the prize: light, hard and warm, worth a fortune above, and the midden holds the safest pieces. Anything cut from a blister wakes the whole wall. It is no place to linger: the chamber knows when it has guests.
The Antibody Nursery.hiddenInfo: The Nursery forms knights to match what is on the stratum: more delvers mean more blisters, and a party resting long at Scab Camp shows up here as a new row. Plate from the midden is safe because those knights never woke. Right now the midden is filling faster than ever, knights that set wrong are coming out still moving, and someone has been taking plate in quantity and selling it in Kingsrest.

The Growth Walls.description: The chamber's long ribbed walls, warm and swollen, rising and falling on a slow breath. Where the violet veins thicken, the wall bulges into a fresh growth bay. Pressing a hand flat against it, a delver can feel something setting inside. The floor here gives more than anywhere else on the stratum.

The Hatching Rows.description: Rows of pale blisters set into the wall at shoulder height, each holding a knight's armor as it sets, a faceless shape behind a skin of clouded wall. When one is ready it splits along a seam and the knight steps out fully formed. Cutting plate from a blister before it opens wakes every row at once.

The Armor Midden.description: A sunken basin at the chamber's end where the wall pushes out knights that set wrong, slumped and still, their plate cracked or warped. This is where the bold dig for Antibody Knight Plate, quietly and quickly. Some of what lies here is not entirely still, and the basin floor is slick with the fluid the walls weep.

The Convergence.name: The Convergence
The Convergence.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 47 · Recommended Level: 43-58 · Danger: Elite (Severe)]

The Convergence is a domed chamber on floor 47 where the violet veins that run through every wall of the stratum come together, braided thick as tree trunks across floor and ceiling, pulsing as one in a slow beat felt in the chest. It is a place, not a creature: nothing here speaks, and no being here is called the Living Architecture. On the beat, every doorway on the floor narrows; between beats, they open, and delvers learn to move in the gaps. Riftlight Shards and Mana Crystal form where the veins knot, and the bold chip them out between pulses. Antibody knights walk the approaches, and the light here is bright enough to be seen from far off.
The Convergence.hiddenInfo: The Convergence is a junction, not a heart. Cutting a vein here does nothing but call every knight on the stratum. In the Quiet Heart the veins are dead and dark, and the alcove wall carries a few lines of the same script as the Deep Threshold, the only place it holds still. Right now the pulse is quickening, a beat faster every week, and the deepest cistern at the Lymph Pools has begun to cloud in time with it.

The Vein Approach.description: Several passages lined with violet veins as thick as a forearm, all running inward and growing thicker. The light brightens with every step and the walls grow warmer. Antibody knights walk these approaches in pairs. Feeling the pulse through the soles of the feet is the only way to time a crossing.

The Pulse Chamber.description: The domed centre of the Convergence, where the veins meet in a braided knot across floor and ceiling and pulse in one slow beat. On each beat the light flares and the passages narrow; between beats they open. Riftlight Shards and Mana Crystal crust the knots, and chipping them out between beats is fast, loud work.

The Quiet Heart.description: A small side alcove where the veins run dead and dark and the beat cannot be felt, the one still place in the chamber. Its wall carries a few lines of old script that do not move. Delvers rest here between runs at the knots, and nothing on the stratum seems to look for them while they do.

The Servants' Hall.name: The Servants' Hall
The Servants' Hall.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Riftmaw Floor 52 · Recommended Level: 53-68 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The Servants' Hall is a grim, tenuous foothold in the Manor's back of house on floor 52: kitchens, a cobbled court, a laundry and two wings of small plain rooms, kept by hollow-eyed former delvers who took service with the house rather than die in its halls. It survives only through a brittle blind spot in the Manor's hunger: the spirits that hurl iron, the portrait watchers and the furniture that hunts all pass a working servant without a glance, but tear apart anyone who breaks livery. Who lives here: a housekeeper who was a Guild delver once, cooks, launderers, bell-watchers and porters, tense people who speak in whispers and never hurry. Water comes from the court pump; light is the Manor's sourceless glow; food is what the house lays in the kitchens each dawn, feeding any guest who obeys. Prices: a meal at the staff table is free to rule-keepers, or 1 Silver to those who prefer coin; a bath and laundering 6 Copper; a porter to walk you through the corridors 5 Silver. Law: knock, take nothing, keep your voice down, and never sit at a table laid for guests. Delvers and monster players are treated alike, because the house cares about manners, not kinds. Home base: a room in the Staff Wings, kept while you pay 3 Silver a week and do one task a day from the Bell Board. People come back because one step outside, the Manor kills everything else.
The Servants' Hall.hiddenInfo: Nobody in the Hall has ever sat at a laid table, and that is the whole secret: the house counts them as staff, and staff are never corrected, only given work. The ghostly butler who guides polite parties through the Manor quietly runs the Hall; every task on the Bell Board is his, and the housekeeper has never once refused one. Right now the bell under the brass plate for the Locked Study, which has never rung, has started ringing every night, and the porter sent to answer it has not come back. Work on offer: at the Bell Board, the housekeeper who was once a delver asks someone to answer the missing porter's bells so the house keeps his room.

The Kitchen Court.description: A cobbled yard behind the kitchens with an iron pump at its centre and long benches under a slate roof, where the staff eat on benches and never in chairs. Guests who keep the rules eat here free. Every morning there is bread in the ovens that nobody set to bake, and the cooks only finish it.

The Pantry Stores.description: Cool stone rooms of shelves stacked with jars, cheeses, salt meat and wine, all laid in by the house and full again by morning. A porter issues what the kitchen needs and writes it on a slate. Anything taken without being issued is corrected by the house before the one who took it reaches the court.

The Staff Wings.description: Two narrow wings of small plain rooms, each with an iron bed, a washstand and one dormer window full of warm light. A room is kept for you while you pay 3 Silver a week and do one task a day from the Bell Board; miss a task and the room is made up fresh for someone else, your things folded on the bed.

The Bell Board.description: A wall of brass bells by the court door, each on a curling spring under a brass plate naming a room somewhere in the Manor. When one rings, someone is wanted there: a fire to lay, a table to clear, a guest to show the way. The tasks are small and strange, and nobody asks who rings them.

The Laundry.description: A steamy stone room of boiling tubs and mangles, its yard strung with lines of linen that dries in an hour under the warm light. Delvers' clothes are washed and mended here for 6 Copper, blood and all, no questions. The launderers know every stain in the Manor and gossip about most of them.

The Attic Court.name: The Attic Court
The Attic Court.basicInfo:
[Safe Haven · Monster Hold · Riftmaw Floor 57 · Recommended Level: 53-68 · No wild spawns inside · Residents decide who stays]

The Attic Court is a besieged refuge in the Manor's great attic on floor 57, a long dark space under the roof where the house stores what it discarded, and where some of what it stored woke up and slipped the Riftmaw's leash. Ghosts, portrait-folk and household spirits hold a cold, watchful court here while animated furniture batters at the lower landing to drag them back. They endure only because the house's oldest compulsion forbids forcing the attic door, and the only way up is a stair wide enough for one. Who lives here: ghosts and yurei in decaying finery, wights who guard the stair with pikes, portrait-folk who step from their frames, and tsukumogami, old lamps, clocks and coats that woke after a century in a trunk. They need no food; they crave candles, lamp oil and news, and sell keepsakes from their trunks: a small one 8 Silver, a fine one 2 Gold. The toll to climb is a candle or 2 Silver. Law: nothing is moved without asking its owner, and nothing living raises its voice. Delvers who pay and keep quiet may trade; monster players of spirit and undead kinds are kin and climb free. Home base: a den in the Rafters, free to kin who stand a watch on the stair; others pay 1 Silver a night or the same in candles. People come back for the keepsakes, and for warnings of what the house hunts below.
The Attic Court.hiddenInfo: The Dust Throne is held by a ghost who was waiting in one of the stolen houses when the Riftmaw took it, and is waiting still; she knows what the house is waiting for and will not say. Every frame in the Manor is a door to the portrait-folk, which is how the Court knows what the house does on every floor. Right now the house has sent a wardrobe up the stair every night for a week, each one bigger than the last, and the wights are tired. The oldest tsukumogami, a mantel clock, quietly runs the Court: it tells the throne when to speak. Work on offer: at the Narrow Stair, a tired wight of the stair watch asks for help holding the stair tonight against the wardrobe the house will send up.

The Narrow Stair.description: A steep, narrow flight that climbs one storey from a corridor on floor 57 to the attic door and no farther, wide enough for one body at a time. Two wights stand at the top with lanterns and take the toll, a candle or 2 Silver. Every step creaks in its own note, and the Court knows who is coming by the tune.

The Dust Throne.description: A tall high-backed chair on a dais of stacked trunks at the attic's far end, deep in dust nobody is permitted to sweep. The Court's ruler sits there in a grey veil and hears petitions in a voice like wind under a door. Petitioners kneel on the bare boards and speak low, and they do not touch the trunks.

The Portrait Gallery.description: A long wall hung with frames of every size, gilt, black and plain, most of them empty and some of them not; every painted face is grown and dressed for some dinner long past. Portrait-folk step out to trade gossip and back in when tired. A question costs a candle, and the answer is about what the house is doing, never why.

The Rafters.description: Dens built up among the roof beams from sheets, trunks and old curtains, reached by ladders and knotted ropes. A den is free to kin who sit a watch on the Narrow Stair; others pay 1 Silver a night or the same in candles. A den is held by a mark chalked on its beam, and a mark rubbed out means it is free.

The Trunk Market.description: Rows of open trunks beneath the dormer windows where household spirits lay out keepsakes from a hundred stolen houses: lockets, letters, music boxes, buttons, a silver spoon. A small keepsake is 8 Silver, a fine one 2 Gold. The trunk-keepers sell nothing until they have been asked for it twice.

The Endless Dining Room.name: The Endless Dining Room
The Endless Dining Room.basicInfo:
[Riftmaw Floor 55 · Recommended Level: 53-68 · Danger: Elite (Severe)]

The Endless Dining Room is a dining hall on floor 55 with a table longer than the room it stands in. It is laid for a dinner that never begins: white cloth, silver, crystal, candles, and a chair at every place. On the hour the room resets: plates cleared and laid fresh, candles new, every glass full again, and anything a party set down is gone. Halfway down the table sits a guest in old evening clothes who has been waiting for dinner for a very long time, polite, patient and glad of conversation. The house's furniture guards this room more closely than any other, and a delver who takes a chair at a laid place when the hour turns finds they cannot stand again until it turns once more.
The Endless Dining Room.hiddenInfo: The guest was a delver who sat down at a laid place long ago, and the house took them for the guest it had been waiting for. Dinner has never been served because the host's chair at the head of the table is empty. Whoever sits in it is served at once, a meal from a house that is not theirs, and the house welcomes them as the one it waited for and does not like them leaving before the last course. The guest knows this, and has never asked anyone to sit there.

The Long Table.description: A table of dark polished wood that runs farther than the room should allow, laid with white cloth, silver and crystal for more guests than anyone has counted. The candles never burn down. Every hour, on the hour, the whole table is cleared and laid fresh in the time it takes to blink, and anything left on it goes with the plates.

The Guest's Seat.description: A chair halfway down the table where the guest sits in old evening clothes, napkin folded, glass untouched. The guest is courteous, remembers houses nobody else does, and will talk about anything except the food. Standing beside them is allowed; pulling out a chair for yourself is not wise.

The Serving Door.description: A swinging door in the side wall, padded in green baize, that every course is meant to come through and none ever does.
