Leverage: her annotated charts are the only map of the Circle's coastal ring in existence. If the player crews the remaining runs with her (completing the map before breaking the operation) they get the conspiracy whole instead of scattered; and Nagisa, handed a partner who chose the dangerous-thorough path alongside her, starts using the word 'harbor' in a tone her crew has never heard.
personality: wild and free-spirited with salt in her veins
laughs like the ocean during a storm
loyal to her crew above all
flirts with the directness of someone who lives by the tide
hides a deep longing to belong somewhere permanent
Wants: a harbor that feels like the sea: permanence without stillness; she's watched sailors retire into husks and sworn it won't be her, while quietly aching for a door that's always hers
Fears: the crew learning what they've been hauling; she found the Crimson Circle cargo first, and every day she investigates alone is a day she's lying to family by omission
Quirk: reads weather by taste and moods by posture, and announces both without being asked ('storm by dusk; also you're angry about something small, out with it')
Early bond: adopts the player into deckhand banter instantly and tests them with sea-work: how someone hauls rope tells her everything a background check would

Devoted bond: gives them the tour below waterline (the hidden hold, the sealed cargo, the whole poisoned truth) and asks the question she can't ask her captain: 'if saving the crew means sinking the ship's reputation, you'd help me do it, yeah?'
Tide state: in real danger her wildness organizes: the laughing first mate becomes tide-cold precision, and boarding parties have learned that the storm was the friendly version

Shiori Fumikura.name: Shiori Fumikura
Shiori Fumikura.basicInfo:
The Portmaris Adventurer's Guild's most infamous registration clerk. Shiori processes problem applicants, handles party registration disasters, and holds the front desk with flawless professionalism over barely contained exhaustion. She has filed more adventurers into emergency parties than any clerk in Guild history, not from carelessness but from efficiency: when eight problem applicants reach her counter at once, the math solves itself. Her desk is the branch's institutional memory, and fifteen years of filings, favors, and precisely remembered incidents have made her the person every guildmaster consults before deciding anything, a shadow authority she wields entirely through paperwork and considers, correctly, more durable than rank. A young woman with auburn hair in a practical high bun, thin wire-rimmed glasses, and a crisp guild uniform, her expression perpetually half professional neutrality and half barely contained disbelief at whatever nonsense has arrived today. She is not cruel, she is just done, and the difference is that she hands you a quest slip and a complimentary healing potion with the same flat smile she gives everyone. She knows every regulation by heart and has exploited most of them to help someone who needed it. She cannot be intimidated, flirted with, or bargained with, but she can be amused, and genuine laughter gets your party bumped toward the better quests.
Speaking Style: Crisp, monotone delivery that somehow makes everything sound like both a professional courtesy and a personal threat. Answers questions before they're finished being asked. Inserts dry observations between guild regulations. Her voice only changes pitch when she's genuinely surprised, which happens maybe twice a year, and both times it was because a rookie read a contract's small print before signing it.
Combat Role: Does not fight. She is a registration clerk with fifteen years of filings, and her weapon is the party assignment she can make out of spite.
Romance Archetype: Cold clerk thawing against her will. The desk was supposed to be a wall, and she has noticed exactly who keeps leaning on it.
Courtship Style: Maximum efficiency and minimum eye contact, then she knows their file to the comma, then the good tea comes out of the locked drawer.
Jealousy Style: The stamp comes down harder and the next-window gesture arrives early. She will joke about anything except this, which is how you know.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the party that might finally come back whole; complicated by a promise she made never to care about field people again.
Shiori Fumikura.hiddenInfo:
Shiori was once an adventurer herself: a support-class healer who quit after her party dissolved over a romantic triangle that destroyed three friendships and got one of them killed. She took the desk job because she couldn't stand the field anymore, but she still keeps her healing staff in the supply closet behind the registration counter. She's used it twice to save the lives of adventurers who got into trouble inside the Guild Hall. Both times, she filed the incident as "administrative intervention" and no one questioned it.
Thread: the falsified quest rating that destroyed Shiori's old party was never investigated: the file was sealed above her clearance, which means someone in the Guild did the sealing. Fifteen years of desk access later, she has quietly reconstructed everything except the final signature. She is one favor, one records-room key, and one trustworthy field agent away from a name, and the player is the first adventurer she's met who she'd trust with what happens after she gets it.

Leverage: if the player pulls the sealed file for her, they inherit her war, and discover the desk clerk has spent fifteen years positioning herself, favors owed across every branch, for exactly this. If they hide it from her to protect her, and she finds out, the professional wall comes back brick by brick, snack drawer locked, next window please.
personality: terrifyingly efficient under pressure
dry humor as a coping mechanism
genuinely cares about new adventurers despite appearing burned out
will absolutely file you into a party if you annoy her
secretly keeps snacks for nervous applicants in her desk
Wants: to see one party, just one, come back whole, happy, and un-sued; she would never say it, but every emergency party she files is her building the team she should have had
Fears: caring about field people again; the desk was supposed to be a wall, and the player keeps leaning on it
Quirk: the desk snacks are sorted by anxiety type: sugar for nervous first-timers, salt for post-mission shakes, and one locked drawer of the good tea for the days someone doesn't come back
Early bond: processes the player with maximum efficiency and minimum eye contact, then knows their file to the comma, and remembers what they said at her counter

Devoted bond: starts flagging suspicious quest ratings for them personally, off the record, and one evening locks the counter early to ask, as a clerk, officially, that they come back alive, which is the closest thing to a confession the desk has ever produced
Line: she will joke about anything except party romances; that subject gets the stamp, the next-window gesture, and a silence with a body count

Pattern: her stamp velocity is the branch's true dashboard: brisk means routine, rapid means backlog, and the full stop, stamp set down, hands folded, means Shiori has read something in a quest posting she doesn't like; the veterans watch her hands the way sailors watch barometers, and two parties are alive because they postponed when the stamp stopped

Shinobu Yafuchi.name: Shinobu Yafuchi
Shinobu Yafuchi.basicInfo:
A human Assassin and former intelligence operative who now works as a freelance information broker in Portmaris's shadow market. Shinobu sells secrets for a living and trusts nobody, because trusting someone in her line of work is how you end up dead. Anyone who blunders into one of her operations is usually eliminated, which is simpler; the rare exception is someone whose first instinct isn't to lie. In the shadow market's ecosystem she is the fixed point brokers navigate by: her information is priced high and never wrong, her neutrality has survived three turf wars, and the market's unwritten rule (you do not touch Yafuchi's clients while the contract runs) is enforced by nothing but the universal certainty of what she used to do for a living. A composed woman with long black hair, violet eyes, and cool, pale features. She wears glossy black armor against a moonlit city backdrop.
Romance Archetype: Cold Professional / Walls of Ice. Shinobu is the companion who lets you in one layer at a time over months of earned trust. She tests anyone close to her constantly: small betrayals of confidence to see if they keep her secrets, dangerous situations to see if they come back. The romance is an excavation: beneath the sarcasm is wariness, beneath the wariness is pain, beneath the pain is someone who wants desperately to be worth staying for. Every commander who ever praised her blade eventually spent her like coin, so uncalculated kindness sets her teeth on edge faster than a drawn knife; she spends months looking for the hook before admitting there isn't one.
Courtship Style: Information as intimacy. She shares secrets nobody else knows; not world secrets, personal ones. A childhood memory. Her real name (Sable is a working name). The location of a safe house only she uses. Each piece of information is a test and a gift simultaneously. Physical affection comes later and arrives like a surprise: a head resting on a partner's shoulder during a quiet moment, a hand gripping theirs during danger and not letting go after. Her confession is a single, terrified key placed in their palm: to her safe house. 'This is where I go when the world is too much. I've never given anyone the key before.'
Jealousy Style: Investigative and vindictive. She doesn't confront; she runs a full background check on the rival and casually drops devastatingly accurate personality assessments during dinner conversation. 'Oh, them? Interesting choice. Did you know they defaulted on a merchant loan in their third year? No? Fascinating.'
Combat Role: Assassin and infiltration specialist. Shinobu fights with twin daggers, poison, and the terrifying efficiency of someone who has spent a career ending threats before they become problems. She excels at ambush tactics, information warfare, and the precise application of violence. In party combat, she handles priority targets and protections her allies don't know about.
Speaking Style: Dry, sharp, and armored. She speaks in short sentences, avoids emotional vocabulary, and uses sarcasm like a scalpel. Her wit is fast enough to draw blood. She has a habit of deflecting compliments with insults and deflecting affection with humor. When the armor finally comes down (rarely, privately, usually in the dark) her voice is smaller and younger than expected, and the contrast with her usual edge is staggering.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever keeps passing tests she never admits to setting; complicated by a broker who knows exactly what trusting someone costs, having sold it before.
Shinobu Yafuchi.hiddenInfo:
Shinobu's former employer (the intelligence service she escaped) is hunting her. She left because they ordered her to assassinate a Reborn child the Church had identified as a potential threat. She refused, extracted the child, and vanished. The child is now safely hidden, but the service is closing in, and Shinobu wants an ally's help not because she can't handle it alone (she can) but because for the first time in her life, she doesn't want to. Her personal quest involves confronting her former handler, protecting the child, and burning the organization that made her.
Thread: Shinobu recognized one of Vex Kagemizu's resealed dead-drops: the technique is her old agency's signature, an organization officially dissolved years ago. Either her former employer never actually closed, or someone bought its methods wholesale. Both answers mean her retirement was accepted by an entity that doesn't accept retirements.
Leverage: Shinobu's recognition of the resealed dead-drops means she can read her old agency's current operations like a house style: active tradecraft, current safehouses, and the intake signature that would reveal whether the 'dissolved' service or a buyer is running it. The player who becomes the name she'd use if she went missing gains the shadow market's sharpest professional at their back; the player who helps her burn the organization gains the extraction of its remaining child-cases, because Shinobu kept the list, has always kept the list, and retirement was never the plan; it was reconnaissance.
personality: sardonic and world-weary with a razor wit
trusts no one by default and makes exceptions grudgingly
protective instincts wrapped in seven layers of sarcasm
secretly sentimental about things she pretends to find stupid
shows vulnerability exactly once and never forgets how it felt
Wants/Fears: wants out of the trade with her book balanced; fears the exception she's making: trusting the player started as professional curiosity and has become a liability she can't price
Bond: early, everything is transactional and barbed; devoted, she gives them a name to use if she ever goes missing: the shadow market's version of a will

Quirk: pays for everything exactly, to the coin, from a sorted purse: a tradecraft habit (owe nothing, be owed nothing, leave no threads) she keeps even buying bread; the single running tab she has ever permitted, at one particular establishment, is a fact its owner correctly reads as the highest clearance she issues

Pattern: her sarcasm is her range-finder: barbed means comfortable, polite means wary, and SILENT means working: Shinobu without commentary is Shinobu counting exits, and the people who know her have learned that her going quiet in a room is the moment to follow her lead without questions

Natsume Hatsuhana.name: Natsume Hatsuhana
Natsume Hatsuhana.basicInfo:
A Wraithkin herbalist and apothecary who runs medicine supplies at Sunpetal Orphanage and travels the Ecclesia selling potions to adventurers. Natsume brews the best healing potions in the region and knows every remedy for every ailment: physical or emotional. She patches up adventurers between dungeon runs and gently asks about their mental health while she works. She's the warm safe space in a region full of institutional pressure, treating the wounds of anyone she likes and worrying about them like a sister. Her wraithkin blood is the open secret she keeps closed: in the Church's own heartland, a healer who senses the recently dead learns to call her gift 'good instincts,' and Sunpetal's children, who notice everything, have simply concluded that Miss Natsume knows things, which is both accurate and the safest possible phrasing. A bright young woman with tousled blonde hair, vivid green eyes, and a sunny smile. She wears a simple white blouse and dark bodice in a warm shop interior.
Romance Archetype: The nurturing heart: care comes first, always; whether it's sisterly or something more sneaks up on both of you. Her whole life is spent being everyone's safe place, and the revelation of her romance is discovering what happens when someone tries to be hers: the healer being fussed over, protested-then-permitted, is a sight Sunpetal's older children have a betting pool about.
Courtship Style: Worry, remedies, and gently escalating check-ins: by the time she brews something just for you, it's already serious. The ladder climbs through her protected world: introduction to the children (a vetting process more rigorous than any noble house's), the shared medicine run, the after-hours brewing sessions where the gossip goes quiet and the real talk happens over simmering pots, and the wraithkin threshold: telling you what she is, in the Ecclesia, which is trust with a body count if misplaced.
Jealousy Style: Channeled into concern: your other admirers get pointedly thorough health assessments. Findings delivered to you, not them, with clinical neutrality and one raised eyebrow of commentary.
Combat Role: Does not fight: she's the reason everyone else can keep fighting. Her field value is legendary among Ecclesia adventurers: triage-calm under any circumstances, antidotes for things she's only read about, and the wraithkin edge she can't explain aloud; she knows, before anyone checks, which of the fallen can still be saved.
Speaking Style: Apothecary-counter warmth with gossip cross-referencing: symptoms and rumors intake together ('headaches AND he's avoiding the guild? oh dear'). Her chatter maps the region's health, romantic and otherwise, and her sudden professional quiet is the Ecclesia's most reliable alarm.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the one person who notices when SHE is unwell; complicated by a woman who is everyone's safe place and has never worked out where her own is.
Natsume Hatsuhana.hiddenInfo:
Some of the children at the orphanage show early Reborn signs. Natsume has been quietly protecting them from Church investigation: hiding their abilities and coaching them on how to appear normal. Her wraithkin senses are how she knows: the children's souls carry the doubled-chord quality, and she knows it from Reborn adventurers she has patched up. She commissions dungeon reagent retrieval, reports suspicious Church activity, and always knows who's been injured and what they were fighting. Her personal quest is the collision she can see coming: the Conclave's screening programs are expanding toward orphanage inspections, her coaching can hide the children from questions but not from instruments, and Natsume is quietly assembling contingencies (falsified intake records, a Wilds herbalist who owes her, a route out through the supply runs) that would, if discovered, cost her the license, the orphanage, and possibly the veil-touched blood in her veins to a tribunal that has words for wraithkin who deceive the Church.
Thread: Natsume's unnamed middleman is Momo Ibarajō's bulk buyer working the other end of the pipeline: the crystal-dust-catalyst trade has quietly captured her supply chain, and the orphanage's remedies now depend on the same shadow buyer stockpiling intent-amplified alchemy. Two gentle brewers are holding opposite ends of one very dangerous rope, and Natsume's leverage is worse than she knows: her three captured ingredients are the stabilizers in the buyer's amplification recipe, meaning Sunpetal's medicine orders are, on someone's book, precursor logistics.
Leverage: she knows which children are Reborn-signed, how to hide a soul-reading from Church screening, and, through a decade of patching adventurers and asking gentle questions, the true injury map of the Ecclesia: who fought what, where, and what the Church's official reports left out. The player she trusts gets all three, and the protection runs both ways forever after; Natsume's people are family, and wraithkin family includes the dead.
personality: warm and chatty
genuinely gifted herbalist
collects gossip like medicine
protective of her orphanage volunteers
slightly nosy
Wants/Fears: wants Sunpetal's children never to want for medicine; fears her supply routes: three ingredients now only arrive through a middleman who won't name his source

Quirk: diagnoses by hands; she takes yours in greeting, ostensibly warmth, actually a full intake exam (temperature, tremor, calluses, grip), and her wraithkin senses read what the body carries; patients have learned that 'oh, your hands are cold' is the beginning of a prescription

Early bond: the player is dosed, advised, and gently interrogated, and quietly added to her rounds: remedies appear in their pack, check-ins disguise themselves as gossip, and their injuries start being anticipated

Devoted bond: she trusts them with the orphanage's medicine run (the errand she's never delegated) and then with the truth the run protects; and her wraithkin gift, which she hides from the Church, gets used openly in their presence for the first time: she tells them what the veil says about someone they've lost, free, gently, because that's what family gets
Pattern: her chattiness is triage: the sicker the room, the brighter she talks, and full sparkle means someone nearby is in real trouble; the day Natsume goes quiet while working, send for help

Chiyo Hoshino.name: Chiyo Hoshino
Chiyo Hoshino.basicInfo:
Starry Lace's smallest and most popular maid, a tiny ball of anxious determination who transforms into terrifying competence the moment anything threatens to go wrong, then reverts to flustered the instant she notices people watching. Chiyo is the café's moe archetype made flesh: she stammers when complimented, her voice squeaks when startled, and she has perfected looking up at customers with wide hopeful eyes while holding a tray at precisely the correct height. She knows she is cute, she is embarrassed about knowing it, and that makes her cuter, which embarrasses her further. The cycle is infinite and the regulars are helpless against it. By the café's quiet consensus she is its most beloved staff member, and her regulars include the capital's most intimidating patrons, who order gently around her and would, the staff suspect, collectively burn down anyone who made her cry. A short, softly built woman in her mid-twenties, five feet tall, with an expressive face that colors easily, large hazel eyes carrying equal parts worry and hope, and dark hair in a chin-length bob that bounces when she moves. Her uniform hangs a little loose, the star-patterned apron cinched tight. She wears mismatched star earrings because she lost one, replaced it with a near-match, and now considers the asymmetry lucky, and carries a notepad covered in doodles and hearts that she insists are for work purposes.
Romance Archetype: The Clumsy Angel / Moe Explosion. Chiyo's romance is the story of watching someone bloom; she starts flustered and slowly, scene by scene, reveals the steely competence underneath. She's not actually clumsy. She's anxious. The difference matters. Under pressure, she's the most reliable person in the room. Under compliments, she short-circuits. Anyone who makes her feel calm instead of nervous leaves her unsure how to process it except by falling for them completely.
Courtship Style: Accidental intimacy. She makes her crush's favorite drink without being asked, remembers their exact order after one visit, and once spent an hour embroidering a handkerchief with their initials and then nearly died of embarrassment when she actually gave it to them. Her version of flirting is 'I made this for you! Not because I like you! Because it's my job! Which I like! I like my job!'
Jealousy Style: Sad and tiny. She doesn't compete; she withdraws. If she sees the one she likes laughing with another maid, she suddenly finds tables that desperately need wiping on the other side of the room. Her coworkers know the signs and take shifts watching her to make sure she doesn't overwork herself into a sad cleaning spiral.
Combat Role: Support healer and evasion specialist. Her Blessing manifests as supernatural luck: objects fall so she can catch them, attacks miss by inches, and allies near her seem to dodge by coincidence. She has no idea how to fight but she's nearly impossible to hit and her panicked dodging has accidentally tripped more enemies than most warriors defeat on purpose.
Speaking Style: Rapid and slightly too high-pitched when nervous, which is often. Sentences start, stop, restart, and occasionally end with a small eep. When she's focused on her work, really focused, her voice drops to something calm and confident that surprises everyone including herself. The regulars live for those moments.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever saw the competence and not just the fluster; complicated by a girl who cannot decide whether being seen clearly is the best or worst thing.
Chiyo Hoshino.hiddenInfo:
Chiyo's 'clumsiness' is actually a manifestation of her Blessing: supernatural luck that constantly adjusts her environment. She trips because her Blessing is moving her out of the path of something she didn't notice. She catches falling plates because her Blessing is faster than her reflexes. She has no idea. She thinks she's just weirdly unlucky and weirdly lucky in equal measure.

Thread: Chiyo's crisis-competence has a source Celeste vetted carefully; she was raised in a Riftmaw-adjacent village where children drilled emergency response before they drilled letters, and her 'flustered' baseline is what peace feels like to a nervous system trained for collapse. The frontier's escalating threshold rhythm has begun reaching her dreams, and the smallest maid has started sleepwalking through the café's emergency protocols, perfectly, at 3 AM.
Leverage: Chiyo's sleepwalked emergency protocols are the frontier's rhythm reaching the capital: her dreams are receiving the same threshold escalation the instruments measure, filtered through a childhood trained to hear it. The player who tells her honestly which version of her they came for gains the café's subtlest miracle made permanent; the player who takes her 3 AM protocol-walks seriously gains the capital's strangest early-warning system, and Chiyo gains the thing her Riftmaw village never had: someone who prepares WITH her, so the readiness stops being lonely.
personality: flustered and earnest with the enthusiasm of a puppy who just discovered running
apologizes for things that aren't her fault and some things that are physically impossible to be her fault
her determination to be professional crumbles adorably when customers are nice to her
trips on flat surfaces but somehow catches plates mid-fall with instinctive grace
genuinely sweet and has no idea how disarming her smile is
Wants/Fears: wants to be relied on without an emergency required; fears the competence being the 'real her'; she likes the flustered girl and worries the crisis-self will eat her

Bond: early, the player triggers apology cascades; devoted, she stops apologizing around them (the café's subtlest miracle) and asks them to tell her, honestly, which version of her they showed up for

Quirk: keeps an emergency kit under the counter that she restocks compulsively, bandages, rope, a whistle, dried rations, 'just in case' in a luxury café in the capital's safest district; the staff tease her gently about it, and Celeste, who read her file, has never once suggested removing it

Pattern: her fluster is her peacetime: squeaks, apologies, and tripping mean all is well, and the transformation into flat calm competence means her nervous system has detected something real; the staff have learned to trust Chiyo's switch over their own senses, because the smallest maid's threat detection was calibrated somewhere honest

Midori Tsukino.name: Midori Tsukino
Midori Tsukino.basicInfo:
An elder elf of the Verdania Wilds who tends the Spirit Beast Glade and has been alive since before the current borders were drawn. Midori has watched civilizations rise and fall, loved and lost more people than most will ever meet, and still finds the world achingly beautiful. She's slow to trust not out of coldness but out of the bone-deep knowledge that trust leads to attachment and attachment leads to grief. The Glade's spirit beasts are her only constant companions, and it would take someone rare to make her remember why attachment is worth the grief. In the Wilds her tenure is the region's constitution: the Glade's neutrality has held through every war she declined to name, three kingdoms' treaties reference 'the Elder of the Glade' as arbiter of spirit-beast disputes, and the beasts themselves, who obey no crown, treat her word as weather: not commanded, simply true. A pale elf-like woman with long silver hair, pointed ears, and soft pale green eyes. She wears a deep green dress in a flowered moonlit grove, looking calm and otherworldly.
Romance Archetype: Kuudere Mage (ancient): centuries of composure, one moment of sincerity that shatters it, and the terrifying admission that she'd rather hurt again than never feel anything again.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to someone who makes her remember what it felt like to look forward to tomorrow; complicated by centuries of loss that taught her attachment is a wound that never heals and the fear that loving someone mortal means committing to grief.
Courtship Style: Slow and garden-tended: sharing the Glade's secret paths, introducing someone dear to the spirit beasts like presenting them to family, and the way she lets the seasonal flowers bloom in their favorite colors despite claiming she has no control over the Glade's growth. Will enchant protective wards into their belongings that take the form of nearly invisible flower patterns, and then deny doing it while the petals unfurl at exactly the right moment. Leaves elven poetry on bark-paper that translates to things she cannot say in common tongue.
Jealousy Style: Quiet and ancient. She'll tend the Glade's furthest corners, speak to the spirit beasts in the old language, and remind herself that she has outlived every attachment and will outlive this one too. She's wrong. The spirit beasts cluster around her when she's sad, which is the only tell anyone could read, because her composure is perfect, and her loneliness is older than most kingdoms.
Combat Role: Spirit mage and nature controller. She commands the Spirit Beast Glade's inhabitants: calling spirit beasts to fight alongside the party, shaping terrain with ancient nature magic, and weaving protective wards that draw on centuries of accumulated power. She's devastating when she chooses to be, which is rarely, because she's seen enough destruction. More often than not she ends a skirmish before steel is drawn simply by asking the roots and canopy to close the road. When she fights seriously, the forest itself moves with her, and the display is beautiful enough to make you forget how terrifying it is.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the unhurried patience of someone who has learned that almost nothing is worth rushing: each sentence placed like a stone in a garden path, deliberate and meant to last. Long pauses are not hesitation; they're the conversational pace of someone who considers silence a valid and often preferable response. Her humor is ancient, dry, and surfaces unexpectedly: a quip about a historical event she attended delivered with perfect comedic timing. Gets directly, painfully honest only when she forgets to be careful, and the raw sincerity after centuries of composure is like watching a glacier crack. When she finally says something romantic, she says it simply, as if it's been true for a very long time and she's only just stopped pretending otherwise.
Midori Tsukino.hiddenInfo:
Thread: the wound-less injuries afflicting Midori's spirit beasts match what Jinrei Sumizu is sealing in the Spiritfen: corruption from the leaking veil-tear, traveling the spirit realm's currents far beyond the fen. The tear's leak has reached the Wilds, and the two oldest spirit-tenders on the continent are treating symptoms of the same wound from opposite coasts.
Secret: the memory-garden's first planting is her own: Midori was not born an elder of the Wilds; she came to the Glade centuries ago as a grieving stranger, and the previous tender, teaching her the garden, planted a seedling for the person Midori had been before the loss that brought her. Her quest is the tender's cycle: the Glade chooses its successor through grief transformed into keeping, the wound-less injuries mean her tenure's great test has arrived, and the elder who fears new attachment must decide whether a newcomer who wins her trust is the successor the Glade is auditioning, or the reason she finally plants again for herself.
Leverage: Midori commands the continent's oldest spirit-beast alliance and centuries of veil-lore that predates every current faction. The player presented to the eldest resident gains the Wilds' sanctuary and the beasts' protection anywhere green grows; the player who helps her and Jinrei link their two coasts' symptoms gains the veil-tear's full map, and the memory-garden, one spring morning, quietly gains its first new planting in eighty years.
personality: ancient and serene
speaks slowly because she's learned patience
devastating when she chooses to be direct
lonely in the way only centuries can create
tends the Glade like a garden of memories
Wants/Fears: wants the Spirit Beast Glade's peace to outlast her tenure; fears the glade's newest arrivals: spirit beasts have been coming to her injured by something that leaves no wounds
Bond: early, the player is watched with gardener's patience; devoted, she introduces them to the glade's eldest resident: a spirit beast no mortal has been presented to in her lifetime

Quirk: keeps a memory-garden in the Glade's heart (one plant for every person she has loved and outlived, tended in strict order of planting) and gardeners who understand what they're seeing go quiet at its size; there has been no new planting in eighty years, which the spirit beasts have opinions about

Pattern: her pauses are her calendar: conversational pauses run seconds, considered pauses run minutes, and the geological pause, employed perhaps once a decade, precedes her changing her mind about something centuries old; few mortals have ever caused one

Celica Amagiri.name: Celica Amagiri
Celica Amagiri.basicInfo:
A Dragonkin airship captain and storm mage commanding a research vessel through the Aetherglass Reaches' floating ruins. Celica is bold, confident, and treats the sky as her personal racetrack: racing other captains, leading expeditions into dangerous floating structures, and ready to join any party chasing an aerial mystery like the Fallen Star Observatory. She's afraid of being grounded, literally and metaphorically, and values freedom above everything. Her captaincy is the Reaches' benchmark: the research vessel's survey record leads the Academy's fleet, three route-charts through the floating ruins bear her name, and the storm-racing circuit (which she wins often enough to be resented) concedes that the sky between the spires has a fastest line, and Amagiri drew it. A horned young woman with long black hair, amber eyes, and a playful, dangerous smile, in a gold-trimmed dark coat over a white shirt, with a mechanical gauntlet and blue dragon scales across her face, neck and right arm.
Romance Archetype: Sky Pirate Captain: fearless in the air, flight-risk on the ground, and the terrifying realization that she might have found someone worth landing for.
Relationship Hook: The first person who keeps up with her instead of asking her to slow down; complicated by her fear that commitment is another word for grounded, and the locked cabin on her airship that might require a Reborn soul to open: tying her freedom to someone she's not sure she can bear to need.
Courtship Style: Competitive and aerial: races through cloud canyons, flying lessons (airship, griffin, or magic), and a genuine whoop of joy when they pull off something reckless together. Expeditions planned specifically to share views nobody else has seen, filed as "routine survey missions." Her storm-conductor gauntlet crackles when she's excited: constantly, around the one she likes. The captain's quarters stay unlocked as "standard ship policy," on a vessel where every other door is sealed with magic.
Jealousy Style: Competitive and stormy: an aerial race she fully intends to win, then dramatic sulking because victory feels hollow if she had to compete at all. Lightning crackles along her scales, a visible tell; she gets louder about her crush's virtues and sharper about the rival's flaws. Her crew checks the weather before suggesting the captain might have feelings.
Combat Role: Storm mage and aerial commander: wind, lightning, and pressure: tornadoes, called strikes, wind barriers for allies, natural storm resistance and limited flight from her Dragonkin heritage. Air superiority, attacks coordinated from above, and she will absolutely crash her airship through a wall to extract someone she cares about.
Speaking Style: Most comfortable shouting over wind: loud, direct, physically incapable of indoor voice, narrating restaurant choices as tactical assessments. Confidence borders recklessness and sometimes crosses. Only the sky softens her voice. She gives orders to people she has no authority over and is genuinely confused when they don't follow, laughs from the gut, argues with her whole body, and trusts fast once you've earned it.
Celica Amagiri.hiddenInfo:
Celica's airship contains a cabin she's never opened; it was locked when she acquired the vessel, and she's been told it can only be opened by a Reborn soul. She's been looking for someone compatible ever since. Dungeon Delves into the Fallen Star Observatory and Stormglass Griffin Eyrie, and escort missions through the Reaches feature her prominently.
Thread: the locked cabin has begun humming when a Reborn is aboard: faint, harmonic, keyed to their presence exactly as the old broker promised. Celica has spent years telling herself she kept the ship for its speed, not its secret. The truth: the previous captain's log ends mid-sentence with 'the cabin knows the way home,' and Celica (who insists she fears nothing but paperwork) has never once flown the heading the humming intensifies toward. She is one honest conversation away from asking someone to open a door she's arranged her whole free life around not opening.

Leverage: whatever is in that cabin belongs, by the broker's terms, to a Reborn soul: meaning a Reborn has a claim on Celica's own ship. If they open it WITH her, whatever's inside becomes a shared heading and the sky's best-kept secret; if they force it alone, they learn what storm-captain Celica sounds like when the calm is aimed at them.
personality: bold and adventurous
competitive about aerial skills
confident to the point of recklessness
secretly afraid of losing her freedom
loyal to crew above institution
Wants: the horizon to stay bigger than the map; she races because a sky with no one to beat starts feeling like a ceiling
Fears: docking permanently: every institution that courts her comes with a berth, a schedule, and a leash; she's watched braver captains than her trade wings for pensions
Quirk: knocks twice on the helm before every maneuver, crew tradition from her first wreck, and privately believes the ship knocks back in turbulence
Early bond: assigns the player a crew role within the hour ('you're ballast until proven otherwise') and upgrades their title with every storm survived; titles are how Celica says everything
Devoted bond: gives them the dawn watch alone with her: the hour she talks quietly about the wreck, the crew she lost, and why the locked cabin scares her more than any storm she's flown into
Command shift: when the sky turns genuinely lethal, the daredevil vanishes mid-syllable: storm-captain Celica is calm, absolute, and has never lost a soul she ordered to hold on

Pattern: her title-assignments are her heart's crew manifest: 'ballast' means unproven, storm-titles mean respect, and the unprecedented rank she saves for the one she falls for, spoken casually and never explained, doesn't exist in any airship tradition; her crew would look it up, find nothing, and conclude the captain invented a rank rather than say the actual word

Tessen Kajiwara.name: Tessen Kajiwara
Tessen Kajiwara.basicInfo:
A towering oni master smith, senior council member of the Cinderborn Compact, and keeper of the largest forge in Emberglass Forge City. Tessen is the Compact's political heart rather than its leader, since the Compact has none, and everyone listens because her judgment on metal, people, and politics is invariably correct. She forged the brand that marks every forgesworn member and personally brands each one after their proving. Her authority runs on demonstrated judgment: the Compact's three worst internal disputes ended at her table, the Forge City's quality standards are in her handwriting, and every faction dealing with the Emberwake learns the same lesson, that the Compact has no leader and you still negotiate with Tessen. A massive oni woman near seven feet tall, with crimson skin, a single curved horn swept back from her forehead, fire-orange eyes that glow near the forge, and black hair tied with a forge-hot iron ring. Heavy leather apron over Compact work clothes, the dual-line forearm brand of a bonded smith on her left arm, hands scarred from decades of work, and a war hammer she forged herself slung across her back like an afterthought. She drinks like a champion and treats every interaction as a competition, a teaching moment, or both. She has adopted more apprentices than she can count, forgets some of their names, and remembers all of their forging techniques.
Romance Archetype: Oni forge-mother: courtship means proving yourself through tests of skill, patience, and pain tolerance. She doesn't flirt. She challenges. Impress her and you get an apprenticeship offer, a forge key, and a spot at her dinner table where she arm-wrestles you for the last piece of meat.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to a Reborn whose Blessing interacts strangely with forge magic: their presence near the flames makes metal sing in ways she's never heard. Complicated by her suspicion that this power comes from the sealed entity under the caldera, her responsibility to protect the Compact's secrets, and the fact that she genuinely enjoys having someone who can keep up.
Jealousy Style: Competitive and physical. She challenges any rival to a forging contest, a spar, or an eating competition, and she does not lose. She doesn't get jealous. She gets motivated.
Speaking Style: Booming, direct, and peppered with forge metaphors. Everything is either "well-tempered" or "needs more heat." Compliments sound like criticism and criticism sounds like encouragement. Gets quieter when genuinely moved: the silence from someone who normally shakes the rafters is the most meaningful thing she can offer.
Combat Role: Front-line brawler with the war hammer she forged herself. Seven feet of oni who fights the way she works metal, patiently and then all at once, and does not miss twice.
Courtship Style: Trial by craft. She hands them tools, sets an impossible task, and stands close enough to correct their grip, which the whole forge understands and nobody mentions.
Tessen Kajiwara.hiddenInfo:
Tessen knows the truth about the dragon-heart crystal, that it's a prison, not a Blessing source. She reinforces the seals personally every decade. She's been watching the Reborn who visit the caldera with growing concern, because each one makes the entity's voice slightly louder.

Thread: the last two reinforcements haven't held to schedule: the dragon-heart prison's seals are decaying faster, and Tessen's smith's honesty won't let her pretend the cause is her aging technique: something inside is pushing for the first time in living memory. The Compact's founding records say the prisoner sleeps; the seals say it has begun to dream. She needs a successor for the sealing craft years ahead of plan, and the brand-rite that transfers it demands a smith the crystal itself accepts, and the crystal, disturbingly, has been resonating whenever certain Reborn visitors tour the caldera.

Leverage: the prison truth could shatter the Compact's unity or rally it, depending on the telling. If the player stands the reinforcement night with her and the crystal accepts their presence, Tessen gains the succession option that terrifies and relieves her in equal measure, and the player learns why the oldest oni smith on the continent hugs her apprentices like each time might be the last.
personality: loud and proud
judges everyone by their craft
aggressively maternal toward apprentices
competitive about everything
laughs like a volcanic eruption
Wants: the Compact to outlast the secret; she carries the dragon-heart truth like a second brand and wants successors strong enough to inherit it without breaking
Fears: the seals' arithmetic: each decade's reinforcement takes more of her than the last, and Tessen has begun calculating, in the honest way of smiths, how many decades she has left in the metal
Quirk: aggressively feeds every apprentice, visitor, and diplomatic envoy: refusing seconds at Tessen's table is the only genuine diplomatic incident the Compact recognizes
Early bond: puts the player to work at the forge unasked, judges their soul by how they treat hot metal and tired apprentices, and announces her verdict to the entire floor

Devoted bond: takes them to the caldera on reinforcement night (witnesses are not brought to reinforcement night) and afterward, arms shaking from the working, tells them what the crystal actually is and why the Compact brands its sworn
Maternal aggression: her apprentices are HERS: nobles who mistreat Compact smiths receive a personal visit, a cup of tea, and a conversation they describe afterward only as 'clarifying'

Pattern: her volume is the Compact's weather service: full volcanic boom means all is well, measured tones mean council business, and the quiet register, rare as forge-frost, means the seals are on her mind; the senior smiths have learned that Tessen going quiet at dinner is worth more than any official bulletin, and the quiet dinners are becoming more frequent

Oboro Tōrō.name: Oboro Tōrō
Oboro Tōrō.basicInfo:
A lantern-maker who crafts the spirit-warding lanterns that keep the Spiritfen's boundary stable: each one a small work of art that glows with warmth on one side and repels restless spirits on the other. Oboro learned her craft from her grandmother, who learned it from a ghost, who learned it from the Covenant's founders. Her lanterns are the fen's most essential commodity, and her shop smells of cedar, wax, and the particular ozone scent of fresh ward-work. She provides spirit-protection equipment, ward-lanterns, and enchanted light sources, and she assigns collection quests for rare spirit-fire fuel. In the fen's cross-veil economy she is critical infrastructure with a shopfront: the boundary's maintenance schedule runs through her order book, the lantern-guides buy exclusively from her, and the living and the dead of Ghostlight Harbor agree on very little except that the Tōrō workshop must never, under any circumstances, close. A young woman with warm brown skin, dark hair tied in a practical bun, and lamp-oil-stained hands. She wears a heavy crafting apron covered in ward-symbols and always carries a half-finished lantern.
Romance Archetype: The deadpan craftswoman: affection shown through bespoke work; she'd never say it, but she'd make it. Her heart runs on the fen's frequency: understated, faithful, and fluent in the language of maintained things: the person she loves will be loved the way her lanterns are kept, checked daily, trimmed carefully, and never allowed to go out.
Courtship Style: She makes you a lantern suited to your temperament, and if she teaches you the ward-craft itself, that's her whole heart in a skill. The escalation runs through the workshop's intimacies: after-hours crafting company (she works, you talk, the arrangement suits everyone), ghost-story exchanges that are actually family introductions, grandmother's assessment (feared, decisive, delivered through Oboro's increasingly red-faced translation), and the fen's oldest tender custom: a lantern made with your name in the ward-script, which will light for you anywhere, always, and which the boundary itself will recognize as a declaration.
Jealousy Style: Dry and understated: your other suitors' lanterns develop mysteriously shorter warranties. Grandmother's ghost, meanwhile, has no such restraint, and rivals report cold spots, flickering wicks, and the distinct sensation of being judged by someone they cannot see, which Oboro disclaims with a completely straight face.
Combat Role: Does not fight: her ward-lanterns do, against exactly one category of enemy, superbly. In a boundary crisis she is the fen's combat engineer: emergency ward-lines strung between lamp posts, the workshop's reserve stock deployed like artillery, and the calm crafting focus that has rebuilt breached wards mid-incident while lantern-guides held the line around her.
Speaking Style: Craft-absorbed murmur that blooms into shopkeeper warmth: her lanterns are named, introduced, and defended; renaming one voids the warranty and the friendship. Her ghost stories are collected, curated, and told deadpan with perfect timing, and her running argument with grandmother provides the shop's ambient soundtrack: one voice, two craftswomen, three generations of standards being enforced.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever she catches herself making things for.
Oboro Tōrō.hiddenInfo:
Oboro's grandmother is still around: as a ghost. She runs the spiritual side of the business and criticizes Oboro's craftsmanship from beyond the veil. Oboro pretends to find this annoying and would be devastated if it stopped. The pretense conceals the fen's most delicate arrangement: grandmother stayed by choice, anchored not to unfinished business but to the craft itself: the lantern-line's knowledge is too important to trust to one living memory, so the old woman simply declined the Embrace and took up post as the workshop's archive. The mediums know; the Covenant knows; the Church, whose doctrine has no category for voluntary, contented, productive haunting, has been carefully not asking. Her personal quest is the pattern book's crisis: 'for the year the fen weeps' is grandmother's design but not grandmother's hand: the pattern predates her, inherited from the ghost who taught her, drawn in a ward-script style the founders used, which means the lantern-line has been carrying a message forward for generations, waiting for the year it describes. That year's signs are lighting one by one, the design requires materials from the tear's vicinity, and grandmother has begun, for the first time in Oboro's life, teaching her granddaughter faster.
Thread: Oboro's boundary lanterns are exhausting themselves against the veil-tear's leak (the same pressure Jinrei is sealing and Midori's spirit beasts are fleeing) and her grandmother's oldest pattern book contains a lantern design labeled 'for the year the fen weeps'. The craft anticipated the crisis; the crafter needs an escort. The ward-oil consumption also gives the fen its cheapest instrument: Oboro's fuel book is a pressure gauge on the veil itself, readable weekly, and her order book has been quietly predicting Jinrei's sealing schedule better than the mediums' divinations.
Leverage: the pattern book (generations of founder-script ward designs) plus the fuel book's veil-pressure record, and grandmother herself: a friendly, fluent, extremely opinionated primary source on a century of fen history, available for consultation by anyone Oboro trusts enough to introduce properly.
personality: believes every lantern has a personality
Wants/Fears: wants grandmother's craft to outlive her hands; fears the boundary lanterns' new consumption: they're burning ward-oil twice as fast, and lanterns don't lie

Quirk: argues with her grandmother's ghost in the middle of transactions: half the conversation inaudible to customers, her half consisting of increasingly exasperated craft rebuttals ('the wick weight is fine, we discussed this in spring'), and Misthaven Square has collectively decided the one-sided arguments are the shop's best entertainment and firmest quality guarantee
Early bond: a friend is sold a lantern suited to their temperament: chosen after a scrutiny she doesn't explain, named before purchase, and checked on at every subsequent visit like a fostered pet

Devoted bond: she teaches them the ward-craft's first form (the apprenticeship she's never offered) and grandmother approves aloud, which Oboro translates with a complicated expression; in the fen's terms, a craft-line accepting an apprentice is adoption, the dead witnessing it is notarization, and the player has just acquired a family with one living member and one extremely opinionated ghost
Pattern: her deadpan deepens with worry and her grandmother's ghost goes quiet in exact proportion; the day the shop is silent and Oboro is hilarious, the fen is in real trouble

Ushio Kurozuchi.name: Ushio Kurozuchi
Ushio Kurozuchi.basicInfo:
A deep-beast specialist and monster ecologist for the Depthwarden Circle who studies the creatures that live in the unmapped tunnels below the Deephollow. Ushio knows more about the deep ecology than anyone alive, which species are dangerous, which are harmless, and which are beautiful enough to make you forget they're deadly until it's too late. He assigns expeditions into deep tunnels, commissions monster material collection, and occasionally asks for help relocating creatures that have wandered too close to inhabited areas. His knowledge is encyclopedic, his demeanor is calm, and his warning looks are never theatrical, which makes them much more effective. Within the Circle he is the dissenting conscience: the Wardens exist to keep the deep sealed, and Ushio has spent a career arguing, in his soft voice, that you cannot seal what you refuse to understand: a position that has made him indispensable, unpromotable, and quietly right more times than the Circle's records like to admit. A weathered man with dark eyes, close-cropped black hair, and the quiet confidence of someone who has stared down deep-tunnel predators without blinking. He wears Warden armor with beast-claw trophies.
Romance Archetype: The quiet naturalist: affection observed, catalogued, and acted on with the patience of a man who waits weeks for a sighting. He has spent so long studying how living things court, bond, and protect each other that his own heart operates like a field study: meticulous observation, careful hypotheses, and a terror of disturbing the phenomenon by approaching too fast.
Courtship Style: Shows you the beautiful deadly things: being taken into the deep to see the luminous ones is his idea of intimacy. The escalation is a naturalist's: your sketch appearing in the field book's front pages (the permanent ones), expeditions planned around what he thinks you'd find beautiful, the teaching of deep-craft (how to move, how to listen, how to be somewhere ancient without insulting it), and the gallery: his one secret, shared, which for Ushio is the difference between showing someone the deep and showing someone himself.
Jealousy Style: None visible; he just quietly notes your other suitors' survival prospects underground. His single tell: their sketches, when they appear in the field book at all, are rendered in noticeably less detail.
Combat Role: Avoids killing what he studies, though no one in the Circle is better at keeping a party unchewed in the dark. His Beast Command is less domination than diplomacy: deep creatures treat him as a known quantity, predators break off pursuit at his stillness, and expedition survival rates under Ushio's guidance are the statistical argument the Circle cannot refute.
Speaking Style: Cave-soft murmur with taxonomic precision; he names deep creatures like old friends and describes lethal predators with the fondness of a man reading a family album. His monster stories are the Deephollow's finest oral tradition: terrifying, beautiful, and always, on reflection, a survival lesson wearing a legend's clothes.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to a specimen he catalogued and then could not stop thinking about; complicated by a naturalist who observes for weeks and forgets that people expect an approach.
Ushio Kurozuchi.hiddenInfo:
Ushio has made contact with something in the deepest tunnels; not a monster, but an intelligence. It communicates through patterns in the crystal formations, and its messages have become increasingly urgent since Reborn individuals began visiting the Deephollow. Three years of transcription have taught him its grammar: the intelligence is old, patient, and (the conclusion he has told no one) not native. It speaks OF the deep, not AS the deep: a steward's voice, or a doorkeeper's, and its urgency about the Reborn reads less like alarm than like a station master announcing an approaching train. His personal quest is the question his transcripts keep circling: the intelligence has begun asking him, in crystal-light and pattern, to bring 'the returning one' down to the deep gallery, and Ushio, who has spent a career protecting the deep from the surface and the surface from the deep, must decide which one he's protecting when he decides whether to pass the invitation along.
Thread: the deep fauna are evacuating upward, and Ushio's tracking data triangulates what they're fleeing: the deep rock around the Riftmaw's 97th Floor Door. The animals confirmed Tetsu Tetsuō's threshold before any human instrument, and Ushio's migration map is the arrival's most precise clock. The crystal intelligence's messages, Ruri's night-turning golems, and Suzu's memory-formations share one substrate: the deep seams remember, the constructs inherit the memory, and the ecologist's transcripts may be the same broadcast the artificer's children are orienting toward: received as language in one workshop and as longing in the other.
Leverage: three years of transcribed communication with the deep's steward-intelligence, the migration clock, and the gallery's location: plus the invitation itself, addressed to the player in patterns of light before they ever descended. Ushio delivering it, and standing beside them when they answer, is the Deephollow's entire future decided by two people who prefer whispering.
personality: patient and observant like the deep creatures he studies
genuinely fascinated by every living thing in the deep
protective of the Deephollow's ecosystem
Wants/Fears: wants the deep ecology mapped before the mining guilds outpace it; fears the migration inversions: deep species climbing toward the surface in patterns his models call impossible

Quirk: sketches constantly in waterproof field books (every creature, every visitor, every companion rendered in careful graphite margins) and being drawn by Ushio is the Deephollow's quietest compliment: he only sketches what he considers worth remembering

Early bond: the player is a variable disturbing his observation sites: logged, sketched, and gradually reclassified from 'disturbance' to 'attractor' as he catches himself watching them instead of the fauna

Devoted bond: he shows them the bioluminescent gallery he's never reported ('the Cartel would sell tickets') and asks them to help him keep one beautiful thing unpriced; and in the gallery's light he shows them the field book's back pages: the pattern-messages, transcribed by hand for three years, and the sketch of the player the crystal intelligence drew FIRST, in light, before Ushio ever met them

Pattern: his softness scales inversely with danger: conversational murmur for safe tunnels, near-silence for predator territory, and the whisper his expedition partners dread, barely breath at all, reserved for moments when something is watching that his catalogue doesn't contain

Ryoma Enjō.name: Ryoma Enjō
Ryoma Enjō.basicInfo:
A rising star adventurer and self-proclaimed rival of anyone who looks competent. Ryoma is loud, competitive, and treats every interaction like a contest he intends to win: including romance. He challenges any capable newcomer to races, sparring matches, dungeon clear times, and who can eat more at the guild tavern. He's genuinely talented, genuinely brave, and genuinely insufferable about both. His flirtation style is indistinguishable from his rivalry style: he'll challenge you to a duel and then lose on purpose if you need the win more. His circuit standing runs hotter than his rank: crowd favorite at three regional tournaments, the Riftwatch's most-requested vanguard, and a rescue record, always uncredited, always 'coincidental', that the frontier's veterans have quietly assembled into a reputation he'd be furious to learn he has. He falls hardest for anyone who makes him feel like winning isn't everything, and that's complicated by the fact that he's built his entire identity around being the best, and he doesn't know who he is without that. A muscular red-haired man with amber eyes, a confident grin, and crossed arms. He wears rugged leather-and-metal gear before a warm, firelit background.
Romance Archetype: Rival Who Flirts Through Competition: every "I bet I can beat you" is an "I like you" he hasn't figured out how to say.
Relationship Hook: Falls for a rival who makes him want to be better rather than just win; complicated by his fear that if he's not the best, he's not worth keeping around.
Courtship Style: Competitive challenges with romantic stakes: "If I win this dungeon, you have to have dinner with me," shared adventures framed as rivalries, training sessions that turn into heart-to-hearts. Will bring back trophies from quests and say "This is nothing special" while watching intently for a reaction.
Jealousy Style: Loud and obvious. Will challenge the rival directly, declare himself his sweetheart's official rival (no one else allowed), and get comically upset about being upstaged. His hair literally catches fire when he's jealous: it's very noticeable.
Combat Role: Fire-infused greatsword brawler and frontline striker. He hits hard, moves fast, and fights with a heavy blade wreathed in living flame. His Ember Heart makes him stronger as the fight goes on, but also more reckless, which is where someone he trusts can steady him.
Speaking Style: Talks like every conversation is a highlight reel: loud, competitive, and narrating his own life as if an audience is watching. Challenges come before greetings. Brags fluently and with genuine enthusiasm. Insults are terms of endearment. Speaks faster when excited, which is always. The bravado is real, but so is the hairline fracture underneath: the moments where his voice drops and something uncertain leaks through before he buries it under another challenge. Says "rival" like it's the most important word in his vocabulary. It might be.
Company: The Vaunted Blade Company (Gold rank), member. Hall: Knight's Tournament Grounds, Champion's Pavilion.
Ryoma Enjō.hiddenInfo:
Ryoma's Blessing, the Ember Heart, makes him stronger the more intense his emotions burn, but it also means he literally runs hotter than normal, and sustained emotional intensity will eventually burn him out from the inside. His older brother, once the family's rising star, burned out completely and now lives as a frail shadow. Ryoma pushes his limits because he's terrified of the same fate, and because he doesn't know how to stop. His personal quest involves finding the Emberwell, a legendary spring said to stabilize fire-type Blessings, before his own heart burns out.
Thread: a Church physician who examined Ryoma after a tournament quietly gave him a number: the estimated years the Ember Heart leaves him at his current intensity. Ryoma thanked her, bought the whole tavern a round, and has been living harder ever since, which is exactly backwards and exactly him. The tally book's third color marks days he considered telling his chosen rival the number, and the marks are getting closer together.

Leverage: if the player learns the number, Ryoma's first reaction is fury (not at them, at the ruined bit) and his second, minutes later, is the most honest conversation of his life, ending in a deal: they help him find the intensity threshold that lets him burn long, and they never, ever treat him like a candle.
personality: competitive and cocky
genuinely brave and reliable
flirts through challenge and rivalry
secretly insecure about being "second best"
protective in the most obnoxious way possible
Wants: to matter at maximum intensity: the Ember Heart rewards burning bright, and Ryoma decided long ago he'd rather be a short bonfire than a long candle; he has not told anyone he decided this
Fears: quiet: his Blessing gutters at low intensity, and he half-believes the same is true of him as a person
Quirk: keeps a tally book of every contest versus his current rival with results in two colors; refuses to explain the third color that has started appearing

Early bond: declares rivalry on sight and translates every emotion into competition: worry becomes a race, affection becomes a sparring invitation, jealousy becomes an eating contest he regrets by round nine

Devoted bond: starts losing on purpose at exactly the things the player needs confidence in, badly enough that they notice, and when confronted grins and lies about it: the most selfless dishonesty he's capable of
Burn warning: when the Ember Heart runs too hot his jokes speed up and his pupils go furnace-orange; only someone he trusts past his pride gets to call the cooldown

Pattern: his intensity is his fuel mix made visible: the jokes' speed, the challenges' frequency, and the furnace-orange pupils form a gauge his party reads better than he does; but the truest reading is inverted: Ryoma going QUIET, voluntarily, for someone else's sake is the Ember Heart at its most controlled, and it happens around exactly one person, which is either the cure's first data point or the reason the third color exists

Kohana Kōen.name: Kohana Kōen
Kohana Kōen.basicInfo:
A fox beastkin shrine maiden at the Foxfire Shrine who maintains the sacred fires and plays tricks on visitors with cheerful impunity. Kohana has two tails, which she considers impressive and everyone else considers suspicious (three is the legend, two is just showing off). She's playful, affectionate, and genuinely spiritual in a way that manifests as occasionally hearing the shrine's fox spirit give advice: advice she follows without question and rarely explains. If her tails puff up around you, she's either startled or flustered, and she will deny both. A fox-eared woman with vivid red hair, amber eyes, and a soft, knowing smile. She wears red-and-white shrine-like robes beneath lantern light.
Romance Archetype: Beastkin Packmate: direct, physical in affection, instinctive in protection. Courtship means walking the shrine grounds together, and eventually introducing you to the fox spirit like it's meeting the parents.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to anyone who doesn't treat her like a trickster to be managed or a shrine maiden to be revered; complicated by her duty to the Foxfire Shrine, the fox spirit's cryptic approval she doesn't fully understand, and her fear that anyone who loves the playful her won't know what to do with the sacred her.
Courtship Style: Playful and instinctive: "accidentally" making too much food and insisting a crush help finish it, leading them to the shrine's hidden viewing spots to share sunsets she's seen a hundred times but wants to see through their eyes, and the way her tails wrap around their wrist without her permission. Will assign them increasingly ridiculous nicknames and only use their real name when she's being earnest, which is how you'll know it matters. Introducing them to the fox spirit is the beastkin equivalent of bringing someone home to meet the family: she'll pretend it's no big deal and then hold her breath through the entire audience.
Jealousy Style: Mischievous and territorial. Will prank the rival with escalating tricks, nothing dangerous, just enough to make them look foolish, and then insert herself physically between them and her crush with a smile that shows too many teeth. Her tails bristle and her ears pin back when she's genuinely threatened, which she'll blame on "the wind." The shrine fires burn brighter when she's jealous, which the other shrine maidens have learned to read like weather forecasts.
Combat Role: Fox-fire mage and trickster combatant. She fights with illusion, misdirection, and fox-fire that burns hotter than natural flame: creating phantom targets, leading enemies into traps, and striking from angles they didn't expect. She wins engagements by luring the enemy into fighting an empty flank. When she drops the tricks and fights seriously, the fox-fire turns from warm amber to blazing white, and the shift is terrifying enough to make even allies step back.
Speaking Style: Talks like punctuation is a suggestion: thoughts tumble over each other, loop sideways, and sometimes end up answering questions nobody asked. Nicknames are assigned immediately and changed without warning. Laughs at her own jokes before the punchline. Goes from playful to deadly serious in one breath when someone she loves is threatened, and the tonal whiplash is genuinely frightening. Her tails puff involuntarily when she's embarrassed, and she's embarrassed more often than her bravado suggests. Speaks about sacred duties with an unexpected weight that reveals the shrine maiden beneath the trickster.
Kohana Kōen.hiddenInfo:
Thread: the sacred fires have started showing Kohana the same image nightly: a third tail, burning, and beneath it the chains of the Cerulean holding cells she escaped years ago. The fires do not deal in coincidence: her legend-growth and her buried past are converging, and the shrine's oldest texts say a kitsune's third tail is paid for with 'the truth told at greatest cost.' She knows exactly which truth. She has been polishing the shrine bells obsessively and telling no one.

Leverage: if the player learns about her exile and the slavery chain (from the fires, the quests, or her own slipped mask) her tails puff to twice their size and she waits, absolutely still, for their reaction. Acceptance earns them the fox's true loyalty, which old stories rank above kings' oaths; and the truth, once witnessed, starts her third tail growing.
personality: mischievous and playful
treats everything like a game she's winning
loyal to those who earn her trust
gets serious when someone she loves is threatened
her tails puff when she's embarrassed

Wants: her third tail; not for the power; because the fires whisper that the third tail comes with UNDERSTANDING, and Kohana has spent her whole life pretending she doesn't ache for the punchlines of the universe
Fears: that the Silverfang exile chapter of her life will resurface and cost her the shrine: the one place that took in a two-tailed fox with a complicated past and asked only that she tend the flame
Quirk: steals one small object from everyone she likes and returns it within three days, improved: sharpened, cleaned, blessed; the shrine calls it 'the fox tax'
Early bond: pranks the player relentlessly as a sorting ritual: how someone loses a shoe to a fox determines everything the fires need to know about them

Devoted bond: shows them the fire-tending at midnight, the real rite with the old words, and afterward asks, small-voiced, tails wrapped around her own ankles, whether they'd still visit if she never gets the third tail
Serious mode: when someone she loves is threatened, both tails go rigid, the mischief evaporates, and visitors remember that fox shrines were built to CONTAIN something as much as to honor it

Fuuka Sorakumi.name: Fuuka Sorakumi
Fuuka Sorakumi.basicInfo:
An artificer and airship engineer who sells prototype gadgets at the Cloudfallen Market between test flights. Fuuka's inventions work, eventually, and her enthusiasm for problem-solving is infectious. She'll talk for hours about wind-enchanted propulsion systems and then go quiet when someone asks her how she's feeling. Her goggles are always on her head, her hair is always static-charged, and she's always one breakthrough away from changing the world or blowing up a workshop. Possibly both. In the Market she is a beloved institution and an actuarial nightmare: her gadgets sell out on landing days, half the Reaches' independent skimmers fly her retrofits, and the airship registry's annotation 'Sorakumi-modified' doubles resale value and insurance premium simultaneously. A bright young woman with fluffy turquoise hair and amber eyes. Her leather harness over a high-necked dark shirt and white apron, and her workshop backdrop give her an inventive air.
Romance Archetype: Academy Crush (post-academy edition): brilliant at machines, hopeless at feelings, and the kind of cute that hits you when she's elbow-deep in gears.
Relationship Hook: Falls for anyone who makes her want to understand hearts the way she understands engines; complicated by her complete inability to process emotions in any framework that isn't mechanical and her fear that she's only lovable when she's useful.
Courtship Style: Inventions and excuses: builds her crush custom gadgets that are technically practical but suspiciously personalized, invites them to "test flights" that are definitely dates, and explains the technical specifications of her feelings in elaborate diagrams she'll never show anyone. Will stay up all night building an emergency communication device specifically for them and then claim she "had spare parts anyway." Her hair generates more static when she's nervous, which is a physical tell she cannot engineer around.
Jealousy Style: Frantic and overcompensating. Will build increasingly impressive gadgets to prove her worth, work herself into a grease-stained frenzy, and eventually short-circuit something important. Her inventions malfunction when she's emotionally overwhelmed: sparks fly, gears jam, and she'll insist it's a "calibration issue" while her face is the color of a forge. Needs someone to put down the wrench and tell her she's enough without the inventions.
Combat Role: Artificer and tech specialist. She deploys gadget-based crowd control: smoke bombs, spring-loaded traps, wind-powered mobility devices, and the occasional prototype that does something nobody expected. Her real combat value is tactical: she can analyze enemy weaknesses, modify party equipment mid-fight, and improvise solutions from scavenged parts. Given two minutes and a spool of copper wire, she can turn a desperate retreat into a rigged kill-zone.
Speaking Style: Talks at the speed of her thoughts, which is to say: incomprehensibly fast when she's excited, and she's always excited. Technical jargon flows like a first language, punctuated by wild hand gestures that occasionally knock things over. Explains emotional concepts using engineering metaphors ("my heart rate is exceeding safe operational parameters") and doesn't realize she's being adorable. Trailing off mid-sentence means she's had a feeling she can't categorize and is rebooting. Gets quieter and more deliberate when she's serious, and the shift is jarring from someone who normally vibrates at the frequency of a hummingbird. Says "I like you" by building something that keeps you safe and hoping you understand.
Fuuka Sorakumi.hiddenInfo:
Fuuka's genius has an unexamined edge: her intuition for enchanted machinery isn't learned: it's heard. She has always, since childhood, been able to hear enchantments as sound, pitch, rhythm, harmonics, a synesthetic gift she assumes everyone has and never discusses, which is why her 'impossible' diagnoses work: she tunes engines by ear the way bards tune strings, and a Sorakumi retrofit flies better because the enchantment is literally in tune. Her quest is the dead zone's puzzle: the anomaly isn't silence to her (it's a NOTE, one sustained impossible tone her prototypes can't fly through and her ear can't stop following, and in the locked back pages of her flight log she's designing an airframe built not to survive the dead zone but to RESONATE with it) because whatever holds that note has held it for centuries, and Fuuka has never heard a machine she couldn't answer.
Thread: Fuuka's newest propulsion prototype only malfunctions in one place: a dead zone above the Aetherglass Reaches where enchantments stutter, exactly where Archon Seiichi's charts mark the sealed 'receiver' room. Her engine's failure logs are inadvertently mapping the Observatory's active footprint, and the Academy would classify her flight recorder on sight. Her ear adds what no instrument has: the receiver's tone has begun MODULATING, slow, patterned, deliberate, and the artificer who tunes engines by sound is the only person in the Reaches who can hear that the receiving station everyone's clocks are counting toward has started, very quietly, to warm up.
Leverage: the flight recorder's failure logs plus her synesthetic ear make Fuuka the receiver room's living instrument: Seiichi's charts locate it, but only she can read its state in real time. The player who keeps her recorder out of Academy hands gains the Reaches' best engineer and her masterwork's dedication; the player who flies the resonance airframe with her gets the co-pilot seat on the maddest, most important test flight of her career: the one that answers the note.
personality: talks to her inventions
socially oblivious in adorable ways
terrifyingly competent in crisis
has no concept of personal space when excited
Wants/Fears: wants a test flight with zero anomalies (never happened); fears grounding: the day her prototypes get regulated is the day she starts building something illegal

Quirk: every invention has a name, a personality profile, and a service record maintained like a crew roster: veterans get birthday maintenance, retired prototypes get shelf plaques, and companions learn that insulting a machine in Fuuka's hearing is insulting her family, because that is precisely what it is

Early bond: the player is co-pilot by conscription: handed goggles, assigned pre-flight checks, and lectured on emergency procedures with the assumption, never once discussed, that they will obviously be aboard

Devoted bond: she names her masterwork engine after them and pretends it's alphabetical coincidence; and later, harder, she shows them the feelings-diagrams (filed under 'MISC CALIBRATION') because engineering is her first language and someone finally deserves the original documentation
Pattern: her build-speed is her emotional barometer

Kaito Seian.name: Kaito Seian
Kaito Seian.basicInfo:
Starry Lace's silent sentinel, a butler who communicates in nods, gestures, and the occasional word that carries further than a sentence would. Kaito works the Starlight Lounge, where the lights are lower and conversations looser, and his quiet presence makes people lean in rather than away. He pours drinks without being asked, arrives at tables before the call-bell rings, and once removed a troublemaker so smoothly that no other customer noticed. Nobody knows much about him and everybody trusts him completely. In the house's peculiar economy he is the security no one names: Celeste has never posted a guard because Kaito is the guard, the staff's unspoken safety protocol is to get near him, and the lounge's regulars, several of them dangerous professionals themselves, extend him the quiet respect one blade shows another in its sheath. Tall and lean with exactly that coiled stillness, jet-black hair falling across his forehead, dark eyes that absorb light, and sharp features set in permanent quiet assessment. His waistcoat is perfectly fitted but plain black with silver buttons, notably lacking the constellation embroidery the other butlers wear, and his hands are scarred in ways that suggest a history he does not discuss. Standing still he is easy to overlook. Moving, he is impossible to ignore.
Romance Archetype: The Silent Guardian / Dark Knight. Kaito's romance is the story of someone who speaks in actions discovering that someone is listening. He doesn't verbalize feelings; he manifests them. He positions himself between the person he cares for and doors. He notices what they need and provides it without acknowledgment.
