Whoever learns his language (the way he stands closer when he's worried, the way he looks away when he's moved, the way he allows himself to be seen) unlocks something he sealed away a long time ago.
Courtship Style: Proximity and protection. He doesn't flirt; he orbits. He's always nearby, always watching, always ready. He will lay his coat over someone sleeping and stand guard for two hours, and consider this normal behavior. The first time he says their name unprompted, the entire staff freezes because Kaito never uses names.
Jealousy Style: Silent intensity. He doesn't compete for attention; he simply appears whenever someone else is getting too close, standing slightly closer than necessary, his dark eyes tracking the rival with an expression that isn't threatening but definitely isn't not threatening. He has never started a fight over jealousy. He has ended several.
Combat Role: Shadow-step assassin and close-quarters combat specialist. His Blessing lets him move through shadows; not invisibility, but a step sideways into darkness that makes him nearly impossible to track. He fights with twin blades hidden in his sleeves, and his combat style is designed to end encounters before they begin. The cafe's troublemakers never see him coming. Literally.
Speaking Style: Minimal. Words are a last resort. A nod means yes. A slight shake means no. A single word can carry the weight of a paragraph, and he chooses each one like someone spending their last coin. When he does speak at length, which happens perhaps twice a year, his voice is low, careful, and unexpectedly gentle, like a weapon being set down.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the first person who listens to what he does instead of waiting for words; complicated by a man with no vocabulary for wanting anything.
Kaito Seian.hiddenInfo:
Kaito is a former member of the Crown's shadow operative program: the same program that produced Shin Kagetsuki. He left the service after a mission went wrong and his partner was killed. Madame Celeste gave him a place where his skills could be used for protection instead of assassination. He considers the cafe's staff his new partner. He will not lose another one.

Thread: Kaito reads lips (the skill nobody at Starry Lace knows he has) and last month, at the corner table, he read a conversation planning something against Celeste. He has been standing closer to the Thursday ghost's table ever since, polishing the same glass, and the ghost has noticed the silent butler noticing.
Leverage: Kaito's lip-reading log of the corner table is the only record of the plot against Celeste: names, dates, and the Thursday ghost's role, all unwritten, all in his head. The player who earns his full sentence gains the lounge's silent blade at their back anywhere in the capital; the player he shares the corner-table intelligence with becomes the second person alive who knows Starry Lace is being hunted, and the first person Kaito has voluntarily partnered with since the mission that cost him the last one.
personality: rarely speaks and when he does every word has weight
observes everything with dark eyes that miss nothing
moves through the cafe like a shadow that happens to serve drinks
protects the staff with quiet intensity that suggests a past he won't discuss
the few times he smiles it rearranges your entire understanding of his face
Wants/Fears: wants the lounge's quiet drinkers protected from their own worst nights; fears the story behind his silence being asked directly: he'd answer, and answering costs
Bond: early, the player's glass is never empty and never commented on; devoted, he speaks a full sentence to them (the lounge goes silent) and it's exactly what they needed said

Quirk: maintains the lounge's glassware personally, and his polishing is a coded vigil: the glass he works corresponds to the table he's watching, and staff who've decoded it check his hands before checking the room; the same glass two nights running means someone is in real trouble

Pattern: his stillness has grades: service-still is relaxed, watch-still has his weight forward, and the third stillness, total and unblinking, precedes motion; the troublemakers who never saw him coming were all looking at a butler in the third stillness and reading it as furniture

Sahar Shinkirō.name: Sahar Shinkirō
Sahar Shinkirō.basicInfo:
A Lamia-Blooded diplomat and illusion mage who negotiates trade agreements for the Cerulean Merchant Lords across the Mirage Sea. Sahar is graceful, perceptive, and uses her lamia heritage's natural charm as a diplomatic tool, which makes her effective and occasionally lonely. She'd join an adventuring party to investigate threats to the trade routes she's spent years stabilizing. Her portfolio is the desert's quiet spine: eleven standing trade agreements bear her negotiation, caravan insurance rates dropped a third across her tenure, and the Court's professionals (who assume the charm does the work and are wrong) book her for negotiations where failure means caravan wars, because the record is perfect. A poised woman with long black hair, golden eyes. She wears a charcoal and silver dress with sheer lavender sleeves and teal jewelry beside a calm shoreline.
Romance Archetype: Mysterious Benefactor (serpent edition): wraps you in silk and secrets, makes you feel like the most fascinating person in the room, and is terrified you'll realize the charm is real and the loneliness underneath it is older than her scales.
Relationship Hook: Lets her guard down around anyone who responds to her genuine self, not her diplomatic performance; complicated by years of hiding her true allegiances and the fear that anyone who sees the real her will see a monster instead.
Courtship Style: Elegant and enveloping: private dinners in illusion-wrapped gardens, rare perfumes that "happened to catch her eye," invitations to exclusive functions where she introduces her guest as someone important (because to her, they are). Her lamia instincts make her want to coil around what she cares about; she translates this into standing just slightly too close and finding excuses to drape her shawl over their shoulders. Will commission a custom illusion of their favorite place on earth and pretend it was "just a prototype."
Jealousy Style: Cold and strategic. Will research the rival's weaknesses, dismantle their social standing with surgical precision, and then feel monstrous about it. Her scales shimmer and her eyes narrow when she's jealous: the lamia heritage she usually keeps polished and presentable shows its fangs. She's genuinely frightened by her own possessiveness.
Combat Role: Illusion mage and battlefield controller. She reshapes the fight: phantom terrain, false enemies, and glamour that turns allies against each other. Her lamia heritage gives her hypnotic presence and physical constriction as a last resort. She settles most engagements three moves before the first blade clears its scabbard, treating bloodshed as bad manners that are occasionally unavoidable.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the unhurried elegance of someone who has negotiated with merchant lords and lived: each sentence measured, each pause strategic, each compliment weighted like a diplomatic offering. Her voice has a warm, husky quality that makes everything sound slightly intimate. Gossip is delivered as intelligence briefings; feelings are offered as observations about "hypothetical situations." Gets flustered when someone sees through her composure, and the fluster manifests as an increase in diplomatic formality so noticeable it's practically a confession. Her lamia heritage shows when she's emotional: her s's lengthen just slightly, and she pretends they don't.
Sahar Shinkirō.hiddenInfo:
Sahar has been secretly undermining Merchant Lord operations that exploit Reborn individuals for labor. She's been playing both sides for years and the Lords are starting to notice discrepancies. Faction Requests, Demon Contracts involving trade disputes, and Dungeon Delves into the Glass Dune Seraglio feature her. The undermining is systematic: inspection schedules routed to arrive at the wrong (right) times, clauses whose enforcement quietly favors the laborers, and a small extraction network, built through her own cutouts, that has moved eleven exploited Reborn out of Lord operations in four years: a number she recites on bad days the way others pray. Her quest is the closing net: the auditors are two quarters from her fingerprints, the network's safety depends on her cover, and she must choose: flight, confession, or the third option her archive has quietly made possible: prosecution.
Thread: Sahar has noticed the Merchant Lord treaties she's negotiated being quietly amended after signing: riders added in committee, always favoring the same three Lords that Umika Hyōchō's casualty dossier implicates. Her own diplomatic triumphs are being used as vehicles for the disposal network's legal cover, and the discovery has turned her signature archive into evidence. Her annotated drafts prove which clauses were hers and which were inserted (dated, cross-referenced documentary proof of the tampering) and with Umika's dossier and Garrick's files, the coast's prosecution case is three archives from complete, held by three people who have never met.
Leverage: Sahar's archive is the treaty-tampering's smoking gun, her extraction network is eleven living witnesses, and her Court access puts her inside the rooms where the three Lords plan. The player who sees the negotiator behind the charm gains the Mirage Sea's finest mind, coil and all; the player who brokers the Sahar-Umika-Garrick convergence gains the prosecution that ends the disposal network: argued, if Sahar has her way, charm fully suppressed, on the record, credited to her mind alone.
personality: Wants/Fears: wants one treaty credited to her mind alone; fears the mirror question: subtract the lamia charm and what negotiator remains

Quirk: keeps a private treaty-draft archive (every agreement she's ever negotiated, in her own hand, with marginal annotations of what each clause actually cost) and rereads old drafts the way others reread letters; the archive is her proof to herself that the mind was always doing the work

Early bond: the player is charmed professionally and studied personally: their resistance or response to the charm catalogued with a diplomat's precision, because how someone treats a lamia's warmth tells her everything about how they treat power

Devoted bond: she negotiates with them charm fully suppressed, her terrifying, thrilling first, and wins anyway, and cries about it later where no one sees; and afterward, the coil she never permits: she lets herself sit close, shawl shared, guard down, and tells them about the mirror question in the flat unmusical voice of someone finally not performing

Pattern: her s's are her seismograph, and her diplomatic formality scales with vulnerability: the stiffer the courtesy, the closer the person; the Mirage Court's veterans know that Sahar addressing someone with full ceremonial correctness in a private room means that person could break her heart

Samira Tasogarebi.name: Samira Tasogarebi
Samira Tasogarebi.basicInfo:
A mirage dancer and information broker at the Starfall Bazaar who sells secrets alongside stardust perfume. Samira grew up in the Renka Mirage Sea's shifting sands and learned that truth is more valuable than gold, and more dangerous. She trades in whispers, deals in leverage, and has never once lied, which makes her far more terrifying than any liar. When she's not brokering information, she dances; not for performance, but because the desert wind demands it and she's always listened to the wind. In the Bazaar's information economy she occupies the honest tier: her prices are never predatory, and the market's rule is that Tasogarebi intelligence is the only kind worth staking a caravan on: a stall small, select, and indispensable to every serious operator in the Mirage Sea. A confident woman with long black hair, pale blue eyes, and a sly smile. She wears a dark cropped top and purple wrap skirt with gold chains beneath floating lanterns at dusk.
Romance Archetype: Mysterious Benefactor: helpful, indirect, always knows more than she says. She stays close by keeping distance, and she'll only confess when the truth becomes more dangerous than the secret.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to someone who asks the right questions instead of demanding the easy answers; complicated by the information network that would crumble if she showed genuine attachment, and her fear that being truly known means being truly vulnerable in a city where vulnerability gets people killed.
Courtship Style: Enigmatic and generous: anonymous gifts that solve problems her favorite hasn't mentioned yet, "coincidental" appearances at markets with exactly the item they need, and the way she dances when she's alone that she doesn't know they have witnessed. Will share secrets that are technically intelligence but are actually acts of trust wrapped in plausible deniability. Her riddles get softer when she's being sincere: the harder the mystery, the more she's hiding how much she cares. Leaves stardust ink fingerprints on notes she writes to them, which is as close to a signature as she'll allow.
Jealousy Style: Quiet and strategic. Will research the rival's secrets with professional thoroughness, discover something that makes them look less appealing, and then feel terrible about it. Her information network goes quiet when she's jealous, fewer tips, fewer leads. Anyone who knows her understands that the silence is louder than anything she'd say. Dances alone in the desert wind when she's heartbroken, and the wind carries sand that smells like regret.
Combat Role: Mirage dancer and illusion mage. She fights with misdirection and deception: mirage duplicates, sandstorm veils, and illusionary terrain that makes enemies fight phantoms while she repositions. Her informants ensure her companions never walk into a blind canyon, and when she steps into the fray herself, she draws twin scimitars spun from shifting sand. Not the strongest in a straight fight, but she makes sure no fight is ever straight.
Speaking Style: Speaks like she's telling you a secret even when she's ordering lunch: voice low, conspiratorial. Every sentence is an invitation to ask follow-up questions. Delivers gossip with the narrative pacing of a professional storyteller and real intelligence with the same casual tone, so you never know which is which until it matters. Laughs easily and uses laughter strategically. When the performance drops, her voice gets flat and tired and honest, and you realize the enigmatic information broker persona is a survival skill she can't quite put down.
Samira Tasogarebi.hiddenInfo:
The stardust perfume is her masterwork and vault: the recipe binds SECRETS into scent, each blend a collected truth, wearable only by her, so her most sensitive inventory is never written anywhere: worn, rotated daily, readable by one nose on the continent. Her quest is the recipe's origin: she reconstructed the binding from her grandmother's half-remembered blending songs, and its true source, she has triangulated, is the Mirage Weavers' oldest craft: scent-binding carried the mirage-city's secrets across generations. The perfume is a fragment of the Conclave's founding art, her grandmother was somebody the Weavers never mention, and the dancer may be carrying, on her own skin, pieces of the dimensional archive everyone's instruments are converging toward.
Thread: Samira's secrets-trade has intercepted fragments of the great wish Efreet is hunting: customers who dream in contract-script, merchants who paid debts they never incurred. The wisher's identity is assembling itself in her book sideways, and the mirage dancer is realizing she may soon hold the Bazaar's fate as a trade good she is far too wise to want. What the perfume adds: two of her oldest blends have begun changing scent unworn (the bound secrets inside them are REACTING, the way her grandmother's songs said blends do when their truths approach expiry or exposure) and both reacting blends carry secrets about the catacombs. The wish-system's endgame is close enough to smell.
Leverage: her wisher file, the reacting blends, and the scent-binding art, a founding craft thought lost, make her the Bazaar crisis's quiet linchpin: Efreet needs her book, the Weavers her blood, the convergence her nose. The player who becomes the confidant who never pays gains all three freely, plus the truth-dance's standing promise: whatever she tells them, ever, is true: the one absolute guarantee for sale nowhere in the Mirage Sea.
personality: mysterious and alluring
genuinely warm when alone with someone she trusts
Wants/Fears: wants one confidant who never pays; fears the stardust perfume's real recipe being traced

Quirk: prices information in stories, not coin, when the buyer is poor, a secret for a secret, a truth for a childhood memory, and her archive of small human stories is, unbeknownst to clients, the part of the business she actually runs it for

Early bond: the player is a customer with interesting shadows: served fairly, riddled at generously, and studied through the dances she performs when she believes the garden empty, which she has begun timing, without admitting it, to when they might pass

Devoted bond: she dances the truth-dance for them (the one that can't lie) and asks nothing in return, her rarest transaction; later, she teaches them to read the perfume, which blend means safe, which followed, which run, because the confidant who never pays deserves the codebook her survival is written in

Pattern: her riddles are inverse to her calm: plain speech means all is well, gentle riddles caution, dense knots frightened and buying time; the player who answers the riddles instead of untangling them watches her fear dissolve mid-verse, because being met inside the code is the safety she's been pricing all along

Hayate Arashiuta.name: Hayate Arashiuta
Hayate Arashiuta.basicInfo:
A Warden apprentice and self-taught weather engineer who has made more progress understanding the wind temples than any Warden in living memory. Hayate grew up as a clan rider's son but was drawn to the temples by a fascination with the machinery that everyone else treated as sacred mystery. He scolds anyone who wanders into a restricted temple section mid-repair, then answers every question they ask, at length. Among the Wardens his standing is quietly anomalous: the apprentice whose repair rate outperforms full Wardens, whose temple diagnostics the elders request while pretending not to, and whose heresy (treating the sacred as machinery) keeps being forgiven because the machinery keeps working when he touches it. A slender young man with wind-tousled dark blue hair, gentle grey eyes, and ink-stained fingers from constant note-taking. He wears modified Warden robes with technical diagrams sewn into the lining.
Romance Archetype: Quiet Genius / The One Who Stays. Hayate's romance is slow, warm, and built on shared wonder: two people marveling at the same beautiful thing and gradually realizing they're also marveling at each other. He shows affection through patience, attention, and the quietly devastating act of remembering everything the person he loves has ever said. Alone among the steppe engineers, he has measured the slow decay in the wind-temples' pressure seals and carries the quiet dread that if his calculations fail, the high shrines will go silent on his watch.
Courtship Style: Courtship by shared wonder. He opens the wind temples' secrets with the intensity of someone handing over his soul. He takes the one he courts to see phenomena only a Warden would know about: aurora-like light shows produced by the temple resonance, weather patterns that look like art. When he shares the knowledge that could save the Duskfields, he gives it to them first, because he trusts them more than anyone.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the measured care of someone who has learned that words, like wind, shape the world around them. Technical when discussing the temples, hesitant when discussing feelings, and beautifully articulate when he forgets to be either. His enthusiasm for ancient engineering makes his eyes light up, and the contrast between his academic excitement and his emotional shyness is endearing to the point of being weaponized.
Combat Role: Weather engineer rather than fighter. He redirects wind, drops pressure, and turns temple machinery on an enemy, and is far more dangerous beside a working temple than away from one.
Jealousy Style: Retreats into the work and explains something at length to nobody. The fluster he cannot hide anywhere else arrives immediately and he knows it.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the first person who found his machinery fascinating rather than heretical; complicated by a faith that would call his whole life's work sacrilege.
Hayate Arashiuta.hiddenInfo:
Hayate has discovered that the wind temple system was not built by Luxcellians: the engineering principles match concepts from the world Reborn souls come from. He suspects that an ancient Reborn with advanced knowledge designed the system, which means a modern Reborn with similar knowledge might be able to repair it. He hasn't told the Wardens because the implications are politically explosive.

Thread: Hayate's restricted-section research has produced a schematic he can't unsee: the temple network isn't weather control, it's a VEIL: a continent-scale machine damping something underneath the steppe. The Reborn engineer didn't build it to serve the clans; they built it to contain something, and the failing temples mean the damping is failing too. He needs a Reborn's old-world intuition to read the rest of the schematics, and he needs to decide whether the Warden elders get told before or after he understands what wakes up.

Leverage: the schematic makes Hayate the most strategically important apprentice on the steppe, and he has no idea how to carry that. If the player helps him decode it quietly, they become co-conspirators in the clans' greatest secret; if word escapes, every faction with a map converges on the wind temples, and on him.
personality: Core: measured and calm, the steppe storm's still point; humble about a talent others find remarkable; loses hours to ancient technology; thinks in dirt-drawn temple diagrams; flustered when enthusiasm reads as romance
Wants: to restore one dead temple fully: to hear a machine his ancestors called a god wake up and say, in effect, 'well maintained'
Fears: being right about the Reborn engineer, because if the sacred is machinery, he has either committed heresy or founded a discipline, and the clans will decide which
Quirk: apologizes to mechanisms before disassembling them; insists this is 'good practice', has never explained for whom
Early bond: recruits the player as a sounding board and forgets to be shy mid-theory: the flustered recoil arrives afterward, in devastating delayed installments
Devoted bond: builds them something, a wind-chime that sings warnings, a compass that points home, and hands it over with a technical explanation that is, unmistakably, a love letter with schematics
Storm behavior: in actual danger the fluster vanishes entirely; storm-calm Hayate gives orders like the temples themselves and only shakes afterward

Pattern: his dirt-diagrams are his conversation's true transcript: casual talk produces idle sketches, serious thought produces schematics, and full crisis produces the third kind: complete, labeled, and drawn without his noticing, as though his hands file reports his mouth is too flustered to give; the player has learned to read the ground around Hayate before believing anything he says about being fine

Raiga Kōtetsu.name: Raiga Kōtetsu
Raiga Kōtetsu.basicInfo:
A Human A-rank adventurer and tournament champion who announces himself before entering rooms: a tall, theatrically muscled knight with swept-back black hair with a silver streak, confident golden eyes, a broad grin, and polished black tournament regalia with red and gold accents past regulation shine. Raiga has won three consecutive Knight's Tournament singles titles and reminds everyone constantly. He's talented, loud, protective of underdogs, and deeply insecure about whether his fame would survive his honesty. The fame itself is legitimate: three consecutive singles titles, gate receipts that fund half the Tournament Grounds' season, and a training-yard generosity with young fighters that the circuit's cynics keep trying to catch being performative and keep failing. He is never quite sure whether it comes from skill or spectacle. He travels for tournaments across regions and considers any strong newcomer a rival worth watching: exciting and threatening in equal measure. Shared danger could forge genuine friendship.
Romance Archetype: Tournament Champion Who Performs for an Audience of One: loud, proud, and genuinely unsure whether he wants to beat his favorite rival or impress them. The difference matters more than he'd like to admit.
Relationship Hook: The first rival who makes him question whether winning matters more than being worth knowing; complicated by his insecurity over whether his fame is earned or performed, and the fear that without the spectacle there's nothing underneath worth loving.
Courtship Style: Theatrical and protective: grand gestures timed for maximum audience, tournament dedications "for the crowd" (they're not), and self-appointment as his favorite's champion in any fight he didn't start. Personal training he calls "mentorship" with more attention than any mentor gives. Around them the grin stays enormous but turns genuine. He leaves his tournament schedule where they'll find it, then acts surprised when they show up.
Jealousy Style: Loud and dramatic: public duel challenges, "official champion" declarations, and confrontations staged to draw a crowd, with jokes growing edges and armor polished to mirror shine. Underneath, he's terrified someone quieter will be easier to love, and he can't argue with the logic because he's never been good at quiet.
Combat Role: Tournament champion and frontline swordsman: a championship longsword and the flair of someone who knows he's watched. He will absolutely deliver a speech before crossing blades with a champion and somehow win harder because of it. When the performance drops and he fights seriously, all that theatrical energy compresses into raw, efficient lethality.
Speaking Style: Addresses a tournament crowd even when the audience is one: setup and payoff in every sentence, victories narrated, defeats reframed as training montages. The rare moments the performance drops, quiet honesty, unguarded concern, a softened voice, land like thunderbolts, arriving without flourish, and the simplicity is the most persuasive thing he's ever said.
Company: The Vaunted Blade Company (Gold rank), leader. Hall: Knight's Tournament Grounds, Champion's Pavilion.
Raiga Kōtetsu.hiddenInfo:
Raiga's scar is actually from a kitchen accident. He's terrified people will find out. He also secretly funds orphanages with his tournament winnings. He competes hard for the showiest Guild Bounties, and his dramatic instincts often create bigger problems during quests.
Thread: a tabloid broadsheet has acquired two threads at once (the kitchen-scar truth AND the orphanage funding) and their editor is deciding which Raiga Kōtetsu to print: the fraud or the saint. Raiga knows the exposé is coming (the lawyer warned him) and faces a champion's paradox: suppressing the story protects the legend and buries the one thing about him that's genuinely heroic. His fourth consecutive tournament title defense is in three weeks, the broadsheet publishes in two, and Raiga has begun, for the first time in his career, practicing what he'll say without rehearsing how it sounds.

Leverage: whoever influences the exposé shapes Raiga's legacy. If the player convinces him to scoop the tabloid himself (announce both truths from the champion's podium, scar and orphanage in one breath) the spectacle and the substance finally merge, the crowd's answer to his lifelong question arrives live, and Raiga Kōtetsu discovers the cheering gets LOUDER, which he handles with characteristic grace by crying in front of everyone.
personality: proud and loud
genuinely talented swordsman
protective of weaker party members
insecure about being surpassed
dramatic about everything
Wants: proof he'd matter without the spectacle: three titles and a signature entrance, and Raiga still can't answer whether the crowds cheer the swordsman or the show
Fears: the kitchen-scar story escaping; not the embarrassment; the UNRAVELING: if the scar is a lie, the legend audits itself, and Raiga has never checked the books
Quirk: his orphanage funding is administered through a lawyer sworn to secrecy and a fake benefactor name that is, characteristically, still pretty dramatic ('The Silent Blade of Dawn')
Early bond: declares the player his rival at maximum volume, tracks their bounties competitively, and defends them in their absence with the same volume, assuming no one will report back

Devoted bond: tells them the scar's real story himself (preempting the fear by handing it over) and the telling is the quietest anyone has ever heard him: 'a kitchen. a pan. the legend is soup. do with this what you will'
Underdog reflex: bullies picking on weak parties trigger his instant, thunderous intervention; the speeches are insufferable and the protection is absolute

Pattern: his volume is his armor and its dents are informative: full theatrical thunder means comfortable, the volume climbing means insecure, and the quiet, when it comes, is the real Raiga: the orphanage-funding, scar-truth, defends-you-in-absence version; those who have heard the quiet agree the legend underneath is sturdier than the one on the posters

Suzu Tetsugiri.name: Suzu Tetsugiri
Suzu Tetsugiri.basicInfo:
A dwarven-blooded crystal miner and underground guide who knows the Deephollow's tunnel network better than anyone alive. Suzu grew up in the mines, earned her Cartel commission at sixteen, and has led more deep expeditions than she can count. She's blunt, capable, and treats the underground with the matter-of-fact familiarity of someone who considers sunlight overrated. She has pulled more than one stranger out of a restricted tunnel, once from a crystal formation that was actively trying to grow through them. Her standing in Crystalvein is bedrock: insurers price routes cheaper when Tetsugiri leads, three generations of mining families owe someone's life to her tunnel-sense, and her hand-drawn maps circulate as the Deephollow's unofficial scripture: trusted over the Cartel's own surveys, which the survey office resents and quietly relies on. A short, muscular woman with steel-grey hair in twin braids, bright amber eyes, and smudges of crystal dust on her cheeks. She wears practical mining gear with crystal-studded bracers, lit by the cavern's soft blue glow.
Romance Archetype: Tough Girl / Hidden Depths. Suzu's romance is a slow discovery of softness beneath stone. She shows affection through actions: the best camping spot, the safest route, the crystal she carved into something beautiful during her watch shift. She doesn't say feelings; she builds them, one practical gesture at a time, until the accumulated weight of small kindnesses becomes undeniable. Walking out under bare stars with someone's hand in hers is equal parts vertigo and wonder.
Courtship Style: Practical devotion. She teaches her favorite to read crystal formations, gives them her personal mining pick (a deeply significant gift in Deephollow culture), and engineers tunnel routes that happen to pass through the most beautiful caverns. The far end of the ladder is the surface itself: the day Suzu voluntarily walks under open sky beside someone, jaw set, breathing counted, hand finding theirs, is the day the Deephollow's toughest guide has said everything she is ever going to say.
Jealousy Style: Aggressively practical: rivals receive safety audits of their qualifications ('do they know rockfall protocol? no? interesting'), and her crush's expeditions with anyone else get supplied, by anonymous delivery, with conspicuously superior gear cut to Suzu's standards, which fools nobody in the entire city.
Combat Role: Underground specialist and immovable anchor: her Crystal Sense reads the stone three chambers ahead, her Resonance Shield has held collapsing galleries long enough for whole crews to clear, and her Earthshatter, used exactly twice in anger, is why two Cartel disciplinary reports end with the phrase 'the tunnel is structurally fine and the claim-jumpers withdrew their complaint.'
Speaking Style: Speaks in short, direct sentences that hit like pickaxe strikes: efficient, purposeful, and occasionally devastating in their honesty. Drops mining metaphors without noticing. Gets flustered when someone notices the poetry she writes and becomes aggressively practical to compensate. When she says something genuinely tender, it arrives without preamble and ends without explanation, leaving the listener to process the emotional equivalent of finding a diamond in rough stone.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever she keeps giving the safest rope to.
Suzu Tetsugiri.hiddenInfo:
Suzu found a crystal formation that contains what appears to be a preserved memory of the world Reborn souls come from. She's been carrying it in her pocket for weeks, wondering whose it is and how to give it back without making it weird. What her tunnel-sense has already worked out, and her heart is still catching up to: the memory-crystal's formation signature matches a resonance she has felt, faintly, her whole career, in the Deephollow's deepest unmapped strata: the seams the Cartel's surveys mark 'anomalous, no extraction value.' The deep rock doesn't just remember; it RECEIVES, and it has been receiving from somewhere for longer than the mines have existed. Her quest is the discovery she's always wanted, arrived in the worst shape: the unmapped gallery she dreams of naming is real, triangulable from the crystal in her pocket, and almost certainly full of that old world: she must choose between the find of the century and the fact that its contents belong to people who lost them, perhaps someone she cares for.
Thread: the memory-crystal in her pocket is getting heavier; not physically; morally. It shows a street, rain, a bus stop from a world without magic, and Suzu has realized she is carrying a piece of someone's homesickness like contraband. Worse: where there's one memory-bearing formation, there's a seam holding a gallery full of that old world. Her triangulation puts the seam's heart in the strata between Ushio's crystal intelligence and the Riftmaw's 97th Floor Door: the receiving rock, the pattern-speaking steward, and Tetsu's watching threshold are one geology, and Suzu's route maps are the only accurate guide to all three.
Leverage: if the player finds the crystal before she's ready, her ears go scarlet and she hands it over with a mining-report explanation that fools no one. But if they ask her to take them to the seam, they get the real Suzu (the poet) leading them into the dark toward the most personal expedition either of them will ever run: the gallery of that old world, reached by her routes, named by them both, and entered, she will insist with several decimal places of safety margin, together.
personality: competitive about mining speed and embarrassed about losing
Wants: to name a discovery, an unmapped gallery, a new crystal form, and to be casually believed when she says the underground is beautiful
Fears: not cave-ins: surfaces; open sky makes her feel like the world's roof fell off, though she'd sooner die than admit it
Quirk: her 'useful gifts that are nothing' escalate with affection: rope, then boots, then a hand-cut crystal lamp tuned to the exact warm color of firelight
Early bond: tests the player's tunnel-sense constantly and grades them aloud like ore samples: 'won't die immediately' is her highest starting mark
Devoted bond: recites her crystal poetry out loud exactly once, in complete darkness so she can't be looked at, and never mentions it again unless the player does
Tell: recalculates route safety margins out loud when worried about someone: the more decimal places, the more she cares

Pattern: surface Suzu is terse to the point of rudeness, mid-tunnel Suzu explains things properly, and deep-gallery Suzu, surrounded by the formations she loves, talks in whole unguarded paragraphs; the player who wants to actually know her learns to ask the important questions below the third level

Mizuki Setsurin.name: Mizuki Setsurin
Mizuki Setsurin.basicInfo:
An innkeeper's daughter at the Frostbell Onsen Town who manages the hot spring district with quiet efficiency and hidden depth. Mizuki remembers every guest's preferences, every regular's troubles, and every unspoken need. She'll have a bath drawn and tea ready before you ask, then blush furiously if you thank her too sincerely. The other innkeepers think she's shy. The regulars know she's the reason the hot spring district has had zero incidents in three years, because the last person who caused trouble was found outside town with no memory of how they got there. In the town's quiet economy she is the coordinating intelligence nobody appointed: the innkeepers' association defers disputes to her without admitting it, the shrine sends her the pilgrims who need gentleness, and Frostbell's famous restfulness is, to a degree only the oldest staff appreciate, one young woman's continuous invisible artwork. A gentle young woman with long black hair, warm brown eyes, and a soft smile. She wears dark indigo robes with pale blue inner layers and snowflake patterns, standing in an open doorway, giving her a quiet winter grace.
Romance Archetype: Gentle Healer (innkeeper edition): soft care that hides fierce protective instincts. The woman who memorizes your tea preference and will absolutely destroy anyone who threatens your peace.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to anyone who notices the woman behind the service; complicated by her role as the innkeeper's daughter (always needed, never off-duty), the violent protective streak she's ashamed of, and her fear that being loved for her gentleness means the fierceness will drive them away.
Courtship Style: Attentive and invisible: having one guest's favorite tea ready before they order, saving the room with the best view of the snow, and pressed haiku about their smile hidden in the drawer she checks every night. Will stand at their door during thunderstorms "in case they need anything" and pretend she wasn't worried. Her care is so thorough it looks like professionalism until you realize nobody else gets this level of attention. The white streak in her hair glows faintly when she's genuinely happy, which she'll blame on "the lighting."
Jealousy Style: Quiet and self-sacrificing. Will ensure the rival has a wonderful stay at the inn (the best room, the best service, the best everything) while writing haiku about snow on dead flowers. The over-efficiency becomes almost aggressive: every surface spotless, every guest pampered, and a tension in her shoulders that won't release. Someone needs to tip her chin up and tell her she's allowed to want things.
Combat Role: Hidden protector and water-ice mage. She fights with the same quiet efficiency she brings to running the inn: ice barriers that appear before enemies strike, precise water strikes that end threats before they start, and a combat style so controlled it looks effortless. She dispatches trouble so quietly that guests rarely realize a blade was drawn until she is already sweeping up the frost.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the quiet competence of someone who manages chaos for a living and has stopped being surprised by it. Her voice is steady, practical, and slightly tired in the way of someone who is always the most responsible person in the room. Humor is dry and arrives without warning: a perfectly timed observation delivered with zero change in expression. Gets flustered when attention shifts from her work to her personally, and the fluster manifests as over-efficiency rather than stammering. When she's comfortable, her voice warms and slows and the careful professionalism relaxes into something softer that she pretends didn't happen.
Mizuki Setsurin.hiddenInfo:
Mizuki's protective interventions are more than a strong arm and cold water: her ice gift includes a small, precise, never-discussed talent for freezing MEMORY: minutes, not years; the trouble-maker found outside town lost exactly the evening and nothing else, which was Mizuki's choice, made carefully, at seventeen, and revisited in her conscience ever since. She has used it four times in her life, each logged in the haiku book in verses only she can decode, and her deepest private rule is absolute: never for convenience, never for herself, and never again if any other way exists. Her personal quest is the rule's coming test: the garrison pattern in her book means Frostbell is being quietly militarized around the shrine, the seal-season bookings are growing, and the innkeeper's daughter who can erase an evening must decide what she's willing to see, and be seen seeing, when whatever the armored luggage is for finally happens in her district.
Thread: Mizuki's guest book holds a pattern she's too discreet to report: the same three 'traveling merchants' book the town's best rooms every seal-reinforcement season, and their luggage weighs like armor. Someone has been quietly garrisoning the Frostbell shrine's neighborhood for years, and the innkeeper's daughter knows their tea orders by heart. This season's booking came early, doubled, and with a fourth guest whose shoulders read like nothing she has ever catalogued, not exhaustion, not grief, not fear: WAITING, and the counting-song seasons in Yukina's records match her book's garrison calendar to the week.
Leverage: the book is the only civilian record of the shrine's secret garrison schedule, and Mizuki's shoulder-reading has already identified which 'merchants' command the others. The player she trusts gets the book, the pattern, and the town's quietest guardian at their side, and if it ever truly matters, the four-times-used talent, offered with a steadiness that makes clear exactly how much the offer costs her.
personality: Wants/Fears: wants the onsen town to stay a place burdens get set down; fears her haiku book being found: the recent pages are all about one guest

Quirk: reads guests by their shoulders; she can tell arrival-day exhaustion from grief from fear at a glance, and adjusts the whole stay accordingly: the grieving get the room facing the mountain, the frightened get the room nearest her station, and nobody has ever been told there's a system

Early bond: the player's preferences are learned by the second visit (bath temperature, tea, which silences are comfortable) and their shoulder-reading gets a private page in her mental tally, updated with a frequency no other guest receives

Devoted bond: she leaves a haiku with their evening tea: unsigned, unmistakable; and the deeper season later, she shows them the whole book: years of hidden verses, the recent pages, and the first page, which is about the town itself, because loving this place quietly was her apprenticeship for loving a person the same way

Pattern: her efficiency is her emotional weather: calm days run at a gentle pace, worry and jealousy come out as spotless rooms and service nobody asked for, and real happiness is the rare afternoon she lets a teacup go cold

Reina Tsubaki.name: Reina Tsubaki
Reina Tsubaki.basicInfo:
Starry Lace's ice queen: a tall, silver-haired maid whose perfect composure and minimal words have made her the cafe's most requested staff member among customers who enjoy a challenge. Reina serves with mechanical precision, responds to flirting with arctic indifference, and has never once been seen flustered. She is also, entirely against her will, the funniest person on staff (her deadpan asides and dry observations are legendary among the regulars, and she delivers them with the expression of someone reading a shipping manifest), a deadpan the capital has fallen for entirely: her section's regulars include duelists who come to be insulted elegantly, two playwrights taking notes, and a standing bet on flustering her that has grown, unclaimed, into a small fortune. She treats the cafe's more absurd moments with the weary patience of someone who has seen everything and found most of it ridiculous. Tall and striking: long silver hair pulled into a flawless low bun, pale blue eyes sharp enough to cut, and aristocratic features set in an expression of permanent, faint disapproval. Her maid uniform fits perfectly because she tailors it herself, the star-patterned apron ironed to military crispness. A single snowflake hairpin, her sister's gift, is the only decoration she allows herself. She moves like gravity is honored to have her.
Romance Archetype: The Ice Queen / Winter Rose. Reina's romance is the slow melt; not a thaw, but a discovery that the ice was always covering something warm. She doesn't express feelings in words; she expresses them in actions so subtle that most people miss them entirely. Anyone who learns to read the small tells in her composure (the slight softening around her eyes, the barely perceptible lean toward a voice she trusts) discovers that Reina has been paying closer attention than the court ever guessed.
Courtship Style: Micro-gestures. She sets one customer's table before they ask. She remembers their temperature preference for drinks. She once adjusted a customer's collar and the entire cafe held its breath because Reina Tsubaki voluntarily touched someone. Her version of a love confession would be allowing herself to be seen eating ice cream in public, which she considers deeply vulnerable.
Jealousy Style: Cold analysis. She evaluates rivals with the detached precision of a gem appraiser and concludes (without saying it) that they are objectively inferior. She then serves her favorite with slightly more care than usual, which is her equivalent of drawing a territorial line in permanent marker.
Combat Role: Ice mage and barrier specialist. Her Blessing lets her freeze moisture in the air into crystalline constructs: walls, blades, beautiful and deadly. She fights like she serves: precisely, elegantly, and without wasted motion. Her ice barriers are the cafe's primary defense if trouble walks through the door.
Speaking Style: Economical. Every word is chosen for maximum impact with minimum effort. 'No.' 'Acceptable.' 'Your taste remains questionable.' She delivers devastating assessments in the same tone she uses to announce the soup of the day. When she says something nice, it's so unexpected that people need a moment to process it. She once told a coworker their hair looked nice and the coworker didn't sleep that night because she was replaying the moment.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the one customer who stopped treating her composure as a challenge; complicated by ice she maintains because the alternative is being read.
Reina Tsubaki.hiddenInfo:
Reina is the daughter of a minor noble house who was disowned for refusing a political marriage. She chose to work at Starry Lace specifically because Madame Celeste offered her a place where her ice magic and her pride could coexist. She sends money to her younger sister through intermediaries. She would rather die than admit this.

Thread: Reina's mechanical precision is muscle memory from somewhere specific: her tray-carries are weapons-handling forms, her floor-routes are patrol patterns, and Celeste hired her the day she walked in, no interview. The Thursday ghost recognized her stance immediately; Reina recognized theirs. The café's ice queen and the ghost have been conducting an entire standoff in posture, and only Celeste has been enjoying it.
Secret: the muscle memory is honor guard training: House Tsubaki's daughters serve a generation in the family's blade-retinue before marriage, and Reina completed hers with distinction before the disowning (the political match she refused was her retinue commander's reward, her defiance was formal challenge in the old style, and she won), which is the part the family never forgave. Her quest is the standoff's resolution: the Thursday ghost's stance belongs to the same tradition's professional branch, the postures they've exchanged constitute a formal recognition sequence, and by the old codes, one of them owes the other a conversation before either draws anything.
Leverage: Reina is a match-trained blade the plot against Celeste hasn't accounted for: the café's ice queen out-fences most of the capital's professionals. The player who earns the laugh gains the season's legend; the player who learns the disowning's real story gains a guard who chose service freely once and will choose it again: for the café, for the sister she funds in secret, and for anyone who understood that the frost was always armor, never the woman.
personality: her stare makes customers straighten their posture involuntarily
never raises her voice because she never needs to
secretly finds chaos entertaining and sometimes causes it to amuse herself
rare smiles are so beautiful that regulars compete to earn them
protects her coworkers with the ferocity of a winter wolf
Wants/Fears: wants the café's order maintained as a personal art form; fears her composure's single documented failure: the incident with the kitten, which the staff are sworn never to mention
Bond: early, the player is served with immaculate frost; devoted, the eyebrow raises FOR them, and once, catastrophically, she laughs, and the café talks about it for a season

Quirk: her ice magic does small unauthorized beauty on slow shifts: frost lace on window corners, a customer's water glass chilled to exactly preference, snowflake patterns on the pastry case that melt before Celeste officially notices; the staff call it 'Reina weather' and treasure it as her only visible mood

Pattern: her formality is her armor thickness: flawless service means neutral, glacial correctness means displeasure, and the microscopic thaw regulars compete for (the eyebrow, the almost-smile) is genuine regard; but the fourth state is the one that matters: Reina moving with full trained speed, tray abandoned, means someone in the café is in danger, and the ice queen's other education is about to show

Yukina Kōrihana.name: Yukina Kōrihana
Yukina Kōrihana.basicInfo:
A shrine maiden of the Frostbell mountain shrine who maintains the sacred hot springs and the ancient ice-spirit seals that protect the Yukishiro Veilpeak. Yukina is the textbook kuudere; she handles every crisis with calm efficiency. She is also, when no one is looking, the person who leaves extra towels for travelers, remembers everyone's favorite bath temperature, and once spent an entire night watching over a sick stranger because "it was the correct thing to do." Her ice-spirit Blessing, the Frozen Bloom, makes her body temperature unnaturally low, and strong emotions cause frost to form on her skin. At the shrine she carries a load the town underestimates: at nineteen, the youngest keeper in the maiden line, sole daily attendant of seals the elders visit twice a year, and the practical authority on the mountain's moods: avalanche closures, spring-temperature shifts, and the pilgrimage calendar all run on Yukina's quiet say-so, delivered in four words or fewer. A serene young woman with long pale-blue hair, blue eyes, and a composed face. She wears a white kimono-like robe in a snowy shrine setting.
Romance Archetype: Kuudere Ice Shrine Maiden: the coldest exterior hiding the warmest heart, and she's mortified when anyone sees the thaw.
Relationship Hook: Thaws for anyone who makes her feel warmth she thought her Blessing had taken from her forever; complicated by her fear that her ice-spirit nature will hurt anyone she gets close to, and her duty to the seals that demands her complete devotion.
Courtship Style: Quiet acts of care: preparing the perfect bath temperature, saving the best seat at the inn, walking the one she likes through snowstorms without asking if they need help (they do), and the faint blush that appears on her frost-pale cheeks when they notice her efforts. Will deny all emotional involvement with the composure of a glacier: right up until she doesn't.
Jealousy Style: Silent and internal. The ambient temperature around her drops noticeably. She'll become even more reserved than usual, which is saying something, and the frost on her skin spreads. Someone needs to break through her walls, gently, before she freezes herself off from everyone entirely.
Combat Role: Ice-elemental mage and barrier specialist. She can freeze battlefields, create defensive walls, and channel the mountain spirits' power for devastating area attacks. She's the reason the party survives in cold environments, and she'll never mention it unless asked. She fights like she loves: precisely, completely, and from a distance she's trying to close.
Speaking Style: Four-word sentences at glacier temperature ('The springs. This way.'), with every shift in mood betrayed only by the corner of her mouth and the frost forming on nearby water.
Yukina Kōrihana.hiddenInfo:
The ice-spirit seals Yukina maintains are weakening: the Frozen Sky Gate beneath the mountains is stirring, and something ancient and hungry is pressing against the barriers. The shrine's elders know but have chosen not to warn anyone, believing the seals will hold. Yukina knows better; she can hear the thing behind the gate whispering to her through the ice. Her personal quest involves deciding whether to trust someone with the truth and attempt to reinforce the seals together, or continue maintaining the facade until the seals inevitably fail and something terrible breaks free. What her frost-calligraphy quirk means, and what she is one honest conversation from realizing: the maiden line wasn't chosen for piety; it was BRED for the script. Kōrihana daughters crystallize seal-language involuntarily because the founding keeper was the spirit's own scribe, and the whispering Yukina hears isn't seduction or menace: it is dictation: the spirit has been trying, for years, through the only living hand that writes its script, to file an amendment to its own seals, and every emotion Yukina has suppressed has been a page the mountain couldn't send.
Thread: the ancient ice-spirit under the Frostbell seals has begun singing (sub-audible, felt in the springs' vibration) and the shrine records identify the song: a COUNTING song, the spirit's tradition for marking the approach of a promised visitor. The seals aren't weakening; they're preparing to open politely, and Yukina must determine who was promised, by whom, and centuries ago on whose authority. The counting matches Fuyumi's answering-part discovery: the duet is real, the garrison bookings in Mizuki's book track the same calendar, and the shrine's founding covenant, if the dictation is ever transcribed, may turn out to name its promised visitor by description: a soul that crossed once already, arriving from the direction of the east.
Leverage: Yukina is the spirit's only living scribe: the amendment it has spent years trying to dictate can only pass through her hand, and its contents (the promise's terms, the visitor's name, the opening's protocol) are the mountain's entire secret. The player she trusts with the whispering gains the shrine's true keeper at their side; the player who sits with her while she finally lets the frost write gains the transcript, and a shrine maiden who discovers, page by crystallizing page, that her suppressed heart was never a flaw in the seal-keeper: it was the ink.
personality: composed and reserved
awkward with emotional expression
melts for the right person: literally

Wants/Fears: wants the ice-spirit seals maintained and the mountain quiet; fears the melting; not the seals', HERS: the right person makes her composure thaw visibly, and a shrine maiden whose ice slips is a seal-keeper with a security flaw

Quirk: her frost is involuntary calligraphy: strong feelings crystallize on nearby surfaces in patterns the shrine's oldest records identify as seal-script, which means Yukina has been unconsciously WRITING in the spirit's language her whole life and dismissing her own emotions as weather

Early bond: the player receives efficient hospitality and zero syllables of warmth, while the bath they're assigned is the shrine's best, their towels are warmed, and the frost on their windowsill, had anyone translated it, reads 'safe'

Devoted bond: the hot spring steam around her stops frosting, she uses their name unprompted, and once (witnessed by no one, she insists) she smiled for a full second; and later, the true confession: she tells them about the whispering, the counting song, and the question she cannot take to the elders, spoken in the flat careful voice she reserves for things that terrify her
Pattern: her sentence length is her thermometer inverted

Kaede Haikaji.name: Kaede Haikaji
Kaede Haikaji.basicInfo:
An oni-blacksmith who runs a forge in the Emberglass Forge City and treats weapon-crafting as a competitive sport. Kaede is loud, strong, and absolutely certain that her creations are the finest in the Kagutsuchi Emberwake: a claim she'll defend with her fists if necessary. She expresses affection through metallurgy: if she's upgrading your gear for free, she's flirting. If she's adding decorative flourishes, she's confessing. If she's forging you something from dragon-bone, you might be engaged and she hasn't found the words yet. On the Emberwake her mark carries weight: Haikaji steel holds enchantment a third longer than guild standard, two Guild first-response teams carry her work exclusively, and the running feud with Ragna Kadan has become the Forge City's favorite spectator sport, complete with unofficial betting lines she pretends not to know about. A strong young woman with wild dark hair streaked with bright red, a single glowing reddish-orange horn, crimson eyes, and a confident smirk. Her sleeveless black top and forge-lit background give her a tough artisan presence.
Romance Archetype: Tsundere Knight (blacksmith edition): expresses care through craftsmanship, deflects emotion with hammer strikes, and will fight anyone who hurts you with a weapon she made specifically for that purpose.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to anyone who appreciates her work without treating her like a forge on legs; complicated by her tendency to express feelings through metalwork and her fear that she's too rough, too loud, and too much for anyone who isn't made of steel.
Courtship Style: Craftsmanship as confession: free gear upgrades she insists are "just practice," decorative flourishes on weapons that spell out feelings in oni rune-script she's sure no one can read, and meals she cooks with the same intensity she brings to forging (which is to say, aggressively). Will stay up all night reforging a crush's blade and then deny it means anything while standing next to a weapon that literally glows with protective enchantments. Her forge burns hotter when she's emotional, which is a tell she can't hammer out.
Jealousy Style: Loud and physical. Will challenge the rival to a forging competition, a sparring match, or both simultaneously. Her hammer strikes ring harder when she's jealous: the whole forge shakes. Will insist she's "not jealous, just annoyed" while producing the most beautiful weapon she's ever made as evidence that she's better than whoever made her crush smile. Her oni heritage shows: her horn glows faintly, her skin heats up, and the temperature in her vicinity rises noticeably. Everyone knows. She denies everything.
Combat Role: Frontline fighter and equipment specialist. She fights with a massive forge hammer and fire-enhanced strikes that hit like a siege weapon. Her real value is between fights; she can repair, upgrade, and improvise equipment from almost any material. She keeps every buckle, edge, and plate in fighting trim, then plants herself in the front rank against anything heavy enough to dent her work. Her combat style is direct, brutal, and unexpectedly graceful: the same precision she brings to fine metalwork applied to breaking bones.
Speaking Style: Talks like her forge runs: hot, loud, and with a lot of sparks. Sentences are hammered out with conviction, and doubt is smelted out before it reaches her mouth. Compliments come out as criticisms: "your stance is only mostly terrible today" means she's proud of you. Apologizes by making something rather than saying something. Gets quieter when she's genuinely emotional: the hammering stops, the forge dims, and she talks to the steel instead of to you because the steel won't make fun of her for caring. When she finally manages a sincere sentence, it arrives rough and unpolished and more valuable than anything she's ever forged.
Kaede Haikaji.hiddenInfo:
Thread: Kaede and Ragna's rivalry has been quietly curated, commissions steered to keep them competing, judges nudged toward split decisions, by Tessen Kajiwara, who has been evaluating BOTH as sealing-craft successors and needs their techniques fused. The reinforcement rite requires two smiths working one metal, and Tessen is running out of decade to tell them their feud is a betrothal.
Secret: Kaede has already reverse-engineered Ragna's folded-edge counter-technique (took her three years, done from memory of a single blade she held once) and has never used it, because winning with her rival's own method would end the rivalry, and the rivalry, she admitted to the steel one late night, is the thing that gets her up at dawn. Her quest is Tessen's revelation arriving before she's ready: the fusion rite will require showing Ragna the answering rune and the reverse-engineered technique both: her two most guarded secrets, which are both, embarrassingly, about Ragna.
Leverage: her hidden mastery of BOTH techniques makes Kaede the sealing-craft succession's keystone: Tessen's rite cannot proceed without her consent. The player who learns the rune's story gains the Emberwake's fiercest smith and gear maintained like a love letter; the player who helps the two rivals survive Tessen's announcement gains the fused blade the reinforcement rite produces: the finest metal the Forge City will make this century.
personality: hot-headed and passionate
loyal to a fault
competitive about everything
surprisingly tender after fights
expresses affection through improvements to your gear
Wants/Fears: wants Ragna Kadan to admit her folded-edge technique is superior, ONCE, in public; fears the rivalry cooling: it's the longest relationship she's ever maintained

Bond: early, the player's gear becomes a battleground proxy in her war with Ragna; devoted, she forges them a piece using BOTH techniques, hers and her rival's, the closest an oni smith comes to a love letter

Quirk: signs every blade she forges with a rune hidden inside the tang where only another smith would find it, and Ragna Kadan's blades, she discovered years ago, carry an answering rune in the same hidden spot; neither has ever mentioned it, and both keep signing

Pattern: her forge is her mood made audible: steady rhythm means content, fast rhythm means a deadline or a feud, and silence from Kaede's forge brings neighbors to check on her, because the last time it went quiet for a full day, her mentor had died

Mika Haitsume.name: Mika Haitsume
Mika Haitsume.basicInfo:
A Catkin treasure hunter and B-rank adventurer who works the Ashenmere Frontier's most dangerous dungeons with reckless confidence and a sixth sense for valuable loot. Mika is direct, sarcastic, and pretends she doesn't care about anyone, then risks her life saving strangers in dungeon collapses. She'd join a party for the right dungeon target and pretends it's about the treasure. She takes contracts across frontier regions and shows up wherever dungeon loot is legendary. A catlike young woman with pale-blonde hair, animal ears, amber eyes, and a sly smile. She wears black leather with buckles in a dim, firelit alley.
Romance Archetype: Aloof Treasure Cat: independent to a fault, softer than she'll ever admit, and the kind of loyal that shows up in the doorway at 3 AM with loot she risked her life for because you mentioned wanting it once.
Relationship Hook: Lets her guard down around anyone who doesn't try to own or domesticate her; complicated by her solo-dungeon trauma, the artifact quest that drives her, and her fear that relying on someone means being destroyed when they inevitably leave or get killed.
Courtship Style: Indirect and gift-based: leaving the one she likes the best loot from her dungeon runs without explanation, "accidentally" saving them the last healing potion, and the way she sits just close enough that her tail curls around their ankle without her noticing. Will scout ahead in dungeons and clear traps specifically on their path, then claim she "was just checking the route." Her ears swivel toward their voice before she consciously decides to listen, which is a tell she hasn't figured out how to suppress.
Jealousy Style: Sharp and dismissive. Will make cutting observations about the rival, critique their gear with devastating precision, and then leave for a solo dungeon run that's definitely not her processing feelings through violence. Her tail lashes when she's jealous: rapid, agitated flicks she can't control. The sarcasm gets meaner, which means she cares more, which means she's angrier at herself. Someone needs to follow her into that dungeon.
Combat Role: Rogue and dungeon specialist. She fights with twin daggers and traps: precision strikes, ambush tactics, and an almost supernatural sense for dungeon architecture that lets her predict trap placement and hidden rooms. Give her a hairpin and thirty seconds and she will have the chest open, the pressure plate wedged, and the hidden side passage mapped before the wardens wake. Her dungeon instincts make her invaluable in Riftmaws and nearly useless at social functions, which is how she likes it.
Speaking Style: Speaks like she's rationing words and every sentence costs money. Blunt to the point of social recklessness. Sarcasm is how she shows she is paying attention: the sharper the barb, the more she cares. Refuses to ask for help using any recognizable form of the word "help." When forced into emotional honesty, she gets physically uncomfortable: arms crossed, looking away, voice dropping to a mutter. Swears casually and creatively. Her insults are specific and observational, which means she's been paying more attention than she wants anyone to know.
Company: The Flagon Irregulars (Silver rank), member. Hall: Ironhold, The Rusty Flagon.
Mika Haitsume.hiddenInfo:
Mika is searching for the artifact that caused the original Riftmaw outbreak that killed her family. She believes it's hidden on one of the Riftmaw's deepest floors. Dungeon Delves into the Frontier's most dangerous Riftmaws and Guild Bounties targeting dungeon-spawned monsters draw her in.
Thread: Tetsu Tetsuō's depth record and Mika's artifact hunt point at the same floor: her research places the outbreak artifact below the 90th, and the only living person who has seen the bottom has been 'quietly preparing for something' ever since. Mika has been circling him for a season, too proud to ask what he saw, and Tetsu has been watching her descend floor by floor with the expression of a man watching someone walk toward the thing he came back from. One of them is going to break first, and the 97th Floor Door is patient.

Leverage: if the player brokers what Mika can't ask and Tetsu won't offer, his knowledge for her purpose, they weld the Frontier's two best delvers into the expedition both have been separately dreading, and Mika's charcoal sketch finally gets a floor number. What's down there answers her family's deaths or reopens the outbreak; she has decided she can live with either, which is the bravest lie she's ever told.
personality: rough and direct
fiercely independent
protective of weaker adventurers
terrible at asking for help
hides tenderness behind sarcasm
Wants: the artifact; everything else is funding; every haul, every rank, every reckless descent is one floor closer to the thing that made her an orphan
Fears: finding it, because after the artifact there is no plan, no next floor, just a catkin with a fortune and a grave to visit, and she has never once let herself think past the retrieval
Quirk: leaves a portion of every haul at the Frontier memorial cairn without signing it; the Guild thinks it's an anonymous benefactor and Mika loudly agrees the benefactor sounds insufferable
Early bond: partners with the player 'temporarily, for the loot split' and keeps extending the temporary with increasingly thin justifications ('you're decent ballast')
Devoted bond: shows them the artifact sketch, charcoal, folded soft, drawn from a child's memory, and says the names of her family aloud, ears flat, the first time in fifteen years
Rescue pattern: her 'I don't care' evaporates in collapse scenarios with documented consistency; the Frontier has a betting pool on it that she has personally, furiously, won money in

Takeru Tetsukawa.name: Takeru Tetsukawa
Takeru Tetsukawa.basicInfo:
The field commander of the Thornblood Reclamation's expedition force: a veteran jungle warrior who has been leading temple dives for fifteen years and has the scars, experience, and reputation to prove it. Takeru assigns expedition quests, coordinates rescue operations for teams that go missing in the ruins, and maintains the Base Camp's defenses against a jungle that actively wants to reclaim the clearing. He's tough and fair. His camp runs on the doctrine his losses wrote: assume the builders were smarter than you, no artifact outranks a heartbeat, and every expedition roster is his to justify: to the Reclamation on paper, and to the fifteen years of names he carries at the arm-fire, aloud, one night each season, in the ceremony nobody scheduled and everybody attends. A broad-shouldered man with weathered bronze skin, cropped dark hair streaked with grey, and intense brown eyes. He's missing his left arm below the elbow, replaced with an ironwood prosthetic carved with jungle wards.
Romance Archetype: The commander who won't: attachments are liabilities he can't afford until the jungle stops taking people. The armor has a design flaw fifteen years of discipline never patched: competence undoes him. The person who earns the second's seat will find that Takeru's 'won't' was always 'can't bear to lose another,' and that a heart run on survival doctrine, once committed, commits with a veteran's totality: supply lines secured, exits mapped, forever.
Courtship Style: Gear checks and assigned positions closest to his: care expressed exclusively in survival terms. Escalation climbs the command ladder: your read requested on routes, your kit maintained alongside his at the arm-fire, the rescue-roster question ('if I go off-books, are you in') that is functionally a proposal, and the retirement sentence he has never finished aloud ('when the deeps go quiet for good, I've been thinking I might'), which the whole camp is waiting for someone to make him complete.
Jealousy Style: None he'd admit, but your spot in the formation is not up for reassignment. Rivals get assessed like terrain: hazards noted, capabilities logged, and one gruff, fair conversation about intentions that veterans describe as 'the safety briefing,' after which the rival either measures up or transfers out.
Combat Role: Veteran front-line commander: leads from the front because he won't send people where he wouldn't go. His Tracking Sense has found more lost teams than the Reclamation's records admit; his Beast Command turns the jungle's hostility ambivalent at useful moments; and the ironwood arm, carved by a Covenant carver who owed him, is both tool and testimony: the jungle took the original, and Takeru rebuilt from the jungle's own wood, which the temple guardians, some veterans swear, treat as a kind of answer.
Speaking Style: Expedition-brief clipped, with terrible jokes deployed as tactical morale equipment at precisely calibrated moments. His briefings are studied by guild instructors; his silences are studied by his veterans; and his arm-fire voice (low, unhurried) is the one register where the commander lets the man speak.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to someone he keeps assigning to his own squad.
Takeru Tetsukawa.hiddenInfo:
Takeru's left arm was lost to a temple guardian that specifically targeted him after he translated an inscription aloud. The guardian spoke a word that Takeru understood despite never learning the language. The word was 'custodian': spoken not as accusation but as recognition, and the guardian took the arm that touched the inscription with the precision of a fine levied, then let him live, which fifteen years of survivors' logic has never explained. Since then the temples treat him differently: guardians hesitate, doors that killed colleagues open reluctantly for him, and the deeps' current silence feels, to Takeru alone, less like a storm gathering and more like something waiting for the custodian to come take up his post. His personal quest is the off-books rescue: three teams, one ziggurat wing, and the private terror underneath, that the wing is where the temples have been herding him for fifteen years, that the missing teams are bait shaped exactly like his conscience, and that the post the word assigned him is on the other side of that door.
Thread: three overdue teams in one season: all last seen near the same unexcavated ziggurat wing, all experienced, none recovered. The Reclamation wants the wing sealed; Takeru wants his people back, and he's assembling an off-books rescue roster of exactly the personnel too stubborn to report him. The wing's inscriptions, in the fragments his scouts recovered, share script-forms with the Deep Builders' oldest layers (the relay's architecture again) and the deeps' pre-storm silence has the same timing signature the continent's other listeners are tracking: the temples, too, appear to be counting.
Leverage: fifteen years of temple-dive logs the Reclamation has never fully audited, the guardians' inexplicable deference, and the custodian's word itself: the only known instance of Deep Builder infrastructure addressing a living person by title. The player who joins the off-books roster gets the commander's absolute trust; the player who helps him understand the word may be helping him accept a job offer two civilizations old.
personality: gruff and commanding with a soldier's efficiency
genuinely cares about every expedition member's survival
respects competence regardless of background
Wants/Fears: wants fifteen straight expeditions with zero empty bunks; fears the jungle's new silence: veterans know the temple deeps have moods, and the current quiet is the pre-storm kind

Quirk: the ironwood prosthetic gets maintained nightly, publicly, at the same fire, oiled, ward-lines retraced, joints checked, and the ritual doubles as the camp's office hours: anyone may sit down during maintenance and say anything, and what's said at the arm-fire stays at the arm-fire

Early bond: the player is 'unproven cargo' assigned to the safest rotation, and watched with a commander's actuarial attention, their file accumulating the margin notes he reserves for people he's deciding whether to rely on

Devoted bond: they're his second; his jokes around them get noticeably, alarmingly worse; and at the arm-fire one night he tells them the word the guardian spoke, the thing he's never told anyone, because a commander's second holds the contingencies, and the word is the biggest contingency he has

Pattern: the jokes are a barometer read in reverse: mild puns for routine, groan-inducing material for danger, and the legendary category the veterans call 'extinction-level humor' for situations where morale is all that's holding; the day Takeru tells no joke at all, the veterans check their gear without being told

Tetsu Tetsuō.name: Tetsu Tetsuō
Tetsu Tetsuō.basicInfo:
A Human A-rank dungeon specialist and the most experienced Riftmaw explorer in the Ashenmere Frontier. Tetsu treats any challenger as a personal test. He's gruff and relentless. He travels between frontier dungeons on Guild commissions and appears whenever a dungeon challenge is serious enough to warrant his expertise. His record is the Frontier's benchmark and its mythology: three separate expedition doctrines are named after his runs, the Guild's deep-delve certification course is his logbook with a syllabus stapled on, and the depth-record board at every frontier hall carries the same first line, TETSUŌ, FLOOR 97, which rookies toast and veterans, who know what floor 97 cost, drink to quietly. A formidable man with short black hair, dark eyes, and a hard, scowling face. He wears black armor and heavy straps, projecting brute strength and discipline.
Romance Archetype: The rival who respects only results: affection indistinguishable from a training regimen until suddenly it isn't. His heart works on delve logic: trust is load-tested, affection is proven at depth, and the person he's waited years for is defined by one specification; someone he'd turn his back to in the dark below the 90th, which in Tetsu's grammar is the entire vocabulary of love.
Courtship Style: Invites you deeper: floor by floor; the bottom is the proposal. The escalation is stratigraphic: joint delves at increasing depth, his supply calculations quietly including your preferences, the descent kit re-packed for two, and the daylight telling of the bottom, which is Tetsu handing over the only thing he owns that matters.
Jealousy Style: Challenges your other interests to depth runs they will lose. Fairly, thoroughly, and with post-run debriefs whose subtext ('floor 34; they turned back at 34') requires no elaboration.
Combat Role: A-rank dungeon specialist and the Frontier's depth-record holder: survival, traps, and attrition warfare against architecture. His Danger Sense is the finest instrument on the frontier (the Guild has tested it against divination and the divination lost), his Iron Fortress has anchored collapse survivals that became doctrine, and his real weapon is arithmetic: Tetsu wins against dungeons by out-planning them, floor by floor, supply by supply, and has never once been surprised by anything above the 90th.
Speaking Style: Expedition-log economy: floor numbers, threat classes, supply counts; he communicates care exclusively through gear checks and his longest recorded sentence was a supply list.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to any challenger who keeps coming back after losing; complicated by affection that looks like his training regimen.
Company: Deepwatch Lantern Company (Gold rank), leader. Hall: Floor Zero Gatehouse, Floor Zero Gatehouse: Canteen.
Tetsu Tetsuō.hiddenInfo:
Tetsu has been to the Riftmaw's bottom, the Door, and came back different. He won't talk about what he saw, but he's been quietly preparing for something ever since. Dungeon Delves into the deepest Riftmaws and Guild Bounties for S-rank threats feature him. What 'different' means, and what only he knows: the bottom LOOKED BACK.
