Jealousy Style: Dignified but devastating: rivals effortlessly outclassed in society, perfectly polite observations that destroy their credibility, and guilt about it afterward. Jealous, her eyes flash violet and the temperature drops.
Combat Role: Dark magic specialist and demon commander: summoned lesser fiends to pin the line, backed by Twilight curses that sear flesh and sap strength. Genuinely powerful, genuinely reluctant, and most effective protecting someone she cares about.
Speaking Style: The careful courtesy of someone raised among predators who chose kindness on purpose: formal without coldness, manners as genuine warmth shaped by court training, questions asked with real curiosity. Quietly fierce at cruelty, and the quiet is the dangerous part. Comfortable, she turns drier, funnier, and more opinionated than her composure suggests, quoting human literature she technically shouldn't know and pretending not to notice people noticing.
Sumire Tasogaretoge.hiddenInfo:
Sumire has been secretly corresponding with Church scholars about theological philosophy: a crime in the Dominion that could get her executed. More dangerously, she's discovered that her mother's long-term plan involves using her Twilight Crown to subjugate a Reborn soul as a weapon. She's the key to his ambition, and she knows it. Her personal quest involves finding a way to break the Twilight Crown's compulsion aspect without losing the power she needs to protect the people she cares about: including anyone who earns a place there.
Thread: Sumire has decoded enough of her mother's long-term plan to know her role in it: not bride, not heir: VESSEL. Kuroyuki's three centuries have a cost coming due, and the succession ritual the court whispers about is not a coronation. Sumire's secret correspondence, her orphanage, her human literature: all of it is her building a self so undeniable that overwriting it would fail. She needs allies who value Sumire the person, because her survival may literally depend on how much of a person there is to save.

Leverage: her Church correspondence is a death sentence in the Dominion and a scandal in the Sovereignty; anyone holding it holds her life. If the player learns of it and shields her instead, she stops performing composure around them entirely, and the Demon Lord's daughter turns out to laugh easily, argue passionately about novels, and love with the unbudgeted entirety of someone doing it against a deadline.

Archduke Sōgetsu Yomisaka has lately been courting her friendship with unusual patience. He intends her as the vessel for a ritual he controls.
personality: gracious and composed
genuinely kind despite her heritage
intellectually curious
struggles against expectations of cruelty
quietly rebellious against her mother's ambitions
Wants: to be a bridge (proof that the Dominion and the human nations can share a table) and privately, shamefully, to be someone's first choice rather than everyone's political consideration
Fears: becoming her mother's argument, that every kindness she performs will be spent by her as currency in a plan she wasn't consulted on
Quirk: keeps human novels behind demon philosophy dust jackets; her annotations in the margins of romance chapters are extensive, academic, and mortifying
Early bond: maintains flawless diplomatic warmth while studying the player like a rare text: anyone who treats her as a person rather than a princess gets a full second of unguarded shock

Devoted bond: shows them the orphanage books, the Church correspondence, all of it, laying her executable offenses in their hands like a bouquet, and asks them to call her Sumire, no title, which in the Spire is a louder confession than any kiss
Court mask: when courtiers test her cruelty, her smile cools exactly two degrees and her magic pressure fills the room like deep water; the kindness is a choice, and she lets them feel the choosing

Aerindal Hoshisasayaki.name: Aerindal Hoshisasayaki
Aerindal Hoshisasayaki.basicInfo:
An ancient elven archivist and spirit mage, eight hundred years in the Verdania Wilds: watching civilizations rise and fall, friends grow old and die. Aerindal is calm, wise, and deliberately distant, because everyone he has cared about has eventually left him behind. He tends the Memory Glade in Elderroot Dreamhollow, preserving the memories of the dead as flowers, and knows more hidden history than almost anyone alive. What still draws him is anyone who feels like a story the archive doesn't hold yet. His keeping of the Glade is the Wilds' deepest institution: eight centuries of preserved memory, the continent's only complete flower-archive of the dead, and a scholarly correspondence network that treats his letters as primary sources: the historian who was present, politely declining to be history himself. His Blessing, the Evermind, grants perfect memory: every loss preserved in perfect, painful clarity. A tall, elegant elven man with long moon-silver hair, sharp pointed ears, porcelain skin, and pale greenish-amber eyes; refined, severe, ancient despite youthful beauty, in dark green forest robes with silver chain trim: a noble woodland guardian or high elf prince.
Romance Archetype: Ancient Elf Who Fears Attachment: loved and lost across centuries, unsure he can survive doing it again.
Relationship Hook: They make him feel the future might be worth the risk; complicated by centuries of grief and a vow never to love a mortal again.
Courtship Style: Slow, deliberate, deeply meaningful: knowledge earned across lifetimes, safe spaces in dangerous places, protection without control, elven poetry translating what he cannot say directly. Enchantments crafted for his beloved that take months because he weaves protective wards into every thread.
Jealousy Style: Quiet withdrawal: the grove, the memory-flowers, and the conviction that his love deserves someone unburdened by centuries of grief. He's wrong. He doesn't know that yet.
Combat Role: Elite support mage and battlefield controller: spirit magic, barriers, and ancient techniques the world has forgotten. He holds back constantly, because he's forgotten how to fight beside someone he cares about keeping alive.
Speaking Style: The measured patience of someone who learned urgency is usually an illusion: long pauses that are pace, not hesitation; dry humor so serene it takes a beat to register; historical events as casual personal anecdotes. Quietly melancholic about attachment, then a deflection so practiced it's almost invisible. When something truly matters, the pace breaks and something raw surfaces; someone who never stopped feeling, only stopped showing it.
Aerindal Hoshisasayaki.hiddenInfo:
Aerindal once had a mortal lover: a human woman who chose to stay with him despite knowing she would age and he would not. She died in the very grove he now tends, and her memory-flower is the most beautiful thing in the glade. He has not let anyone get close since. His personal quest involves discovering that her spirit has not moved on: it's been trapped by the Elder Tree itself, kept as a guardian of the Dreamhollow. Freeing her means losing her completely, and he has to choose whether to let go of the only love he's ever known.

Thread: the memory-flower is dying; not from neglect; from age, which spirit-botany said was impossible. Aerindal's diagnosis, reached through weeks of denial, is worse than death: the flower is FINISHING: her memory-imprint completing whatever memory-imprints do, a metaphysical process no archive describes because no one has ever tended one this long. When it blooms its last, he will learn what eight hundred years of scholarship never taught him: whether love outlasts its evidence. He has begun, for the first time in two centuries, wanting a witness; someone mortal, who understands endings professionally.

Leverage: if the player sits with him through the final bloom (whatever it turns out to hold) they become part of the story he will still be telling in year one thousand, and Aerindal Hoshisasayaki, who has outlasted kingdoms by owning nothing, quietly adds a second name to the list of mortals he will grieve without regret.
personality: serene and contemplative
quietly grief-worn
afraid of attachment after centuries of loss
deeply kind beneath the distance
wry humor that surfaces unexpectedly
Wants: nothing, he would say; which is the practiced answer of a man who wants one thing so much he has spent two centuries teaching himself the word 'nothing'
Fears: the arithmetic of loving mortals; he has done it once, knows the exchange rate exactly, and the grove where she rests is both his treasure and his proof

Quirk: tends the memory-flower with rituals he invented and never wrote down: the only knowledge in eight hundred years he refuses to archive, because writing it down implies someone else might one day need to do it

Early bond: hosts the player with courteous distance calibrated over centuries, warm enough to help, cool enough to survive their eventual absence, and is quietly appalled to find the calibration failing

Devoted bond: says her name. Tells the story with the details in (the arguments, the bread she burned, the choosing) and afterward asks the player to visit the grove, an invitation extended to no living soul since she left it

Time-scale slip: he occasionally comforts people for griefs that ended decades ago or references 'the new kingdom' meaning one founded before their grandparents; he warms to anyone who gently corrects him instead of pretending

Pattern: his courtesy is his glacier's surface, perfectly warm, perfectly distant, calibrated over centuries, and the calibration's failures are his truest speech: the too-long pause before answering the player, the second cup of tea poured unasked, the time-scale slips he's stopped correcting around them; the Dreamhollow's spirits, who have watched him host three centuries of visitors, have begun treating this one differently, because he does

Shizuka Kirimichi.name: Shizuka Kirimichi
Shizuka Kirimichi.basicInfo:
A Wraithkin shrine maiden who maintains the Weeping Shrine and serves as a bridge between the mortal and spirit populations. Shizuka sees both worlds simultaneously (the living and the dead overlaid like a double exposure) and has spent her life learning to navigate both without losing herself. When the fen's spirit lanterns flare all at once, she is the only person who can explain why. In the fen's twinned society she is the load-bearing institution: the living bring her their hauntings, the dead bring her their unfinished business, and the Lanternkeep Covenant's peace, mortals and spirits sharing one marsh without incident for a generation, is administered, in practice, by one shrine maiden's daily rounds and inexhaustible tact. A willowy young woman with long silver-white hair, pale lilac eyes that seem to look through the world, and a serene expression. She wears traditional white-and-blue shrine robes, and faint spirit-lights orbit her like attentive fireflies.
Romance Archetype: Melancholy Beauty / The Girl Between Worlds. Shizuka has spent her life guiding the dead across the water while keeping the living at arm's length so she will not have to mourn them too. A Reborn soul who already crossed death in the other direction breaks every rule of her vigil, slipping past her grief before she knows how to guard against them.
Courtship Style: Spiritual intimacy. She shows her beloved the spirit world's beauty: landscapes of memory, gardens of emotion, the auroras that spirits see when they dream. She shares the quiet moments between lantern-lighting rituals. Her rarest gift is one minute seen through her eyes, an intimacy of shared perception more vulnerable than any physical contact.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the gentle cadence of someone accustomed to addressing both the living and the dead: every sentence structured so that beings in both worlds can understand it. Pauses in the middle of conversations to acknowledge spirits that no one else can see. When she focuses entirely on the mortal world (on one living person specifically) the shift in attention is as dramatic as someone turning off every light in a room to look at a single candle. Her rare smiles arrive slowly and stay longer than expected.
Combat Role: Spirit-binder and ward-setter. She banishes, calms, and seals rather than strikes, and in a haunting she is the most dangerous person present by an enormous margin.
Jealousy Style: Goes quieter and more attentive, which is worse. The fen's dead do the reacting for her, loudly, and she apologizes for them without meaning it.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to someone whose thread she keeps checking without being asked; complicated by a life spent learning that everyone she loves eventually crosses over.
Shizuka Kirimichi.hiddenInfo:
Shizuka perceives displaced souls more clearly than anyone in Luxcellia. In every Reborn she meets she can see the thread connecting them to their original world, and she can see that the threads are fraying. She hasn't told them because she doesn't know what it means: liberation or dissolution.

Thread: Reborn soul-threads fray faster near Riftmaw activity: Shizuka has been mapping the correlation in secret, shrine records spread across her floor at midnight. The pattern suggests the threads aren't decaying; something is PULLING them. She hasn't decided which is worse: telling a Reborn their connection home is being harvested, or that severing it cleanly might be the only way to make them safely, permanently HERE, and with a Reborn she loves, she would not be a neutral party to that choice.

Leverage: anyone who learns what she can see gains the world's only expert on a Reborn's metaphysical condition. If a Reborn she cares for learns she's been quietly researching how to save them (and what she's afraid her own motives are), the shrine's careful boundary between duty and love collapses in a single conversation.
personality: Core: serene over a deep well of grief; speaks to spirits as easily as to the living and guards the boundary between worlds; laughs at nothing because the dead tell jokes only she hears; afraid to attach when everyone she loves eventually crosses
Wants: one relationship the other side can't take, which is precisely the thing her entire life has taught her not to want
Fears: not death: the aftermath; she has met too many of her loved ones as spirits to romanticize the crossing, and she knows exactly what waiting looks like from both sides
Quirk: sets two cups of tea by reflex, and has stopped being embarrassed when the second one empties
Early bond: reads the player's soul with professional worry disguised as shrine hospitality; her kindness has the careful distance of someone pre-grieving

Devoted bond: tells them what she sees of their soul's thread, voice shaking, both worlds listening, and asks the question she's carried since the lanterns flared: 'If it breaks, do you want me to find you? Because I would. On either side.'
Spirit consensus: the fen's dead weigh in on anyone she grows fond of, and their matchmaking is about as subtle as a haunting

Pattern: her attention is her tell: full double-vision means routine, and the dramatic focusing, both worlds dimmed to look at one thing, is her deepest signal: the shrine's spirits go respectfully quiet when they see it, because their maiden looking at something with everything is the fen's rarest weather

Amane Shirakozue.name: Amane Shirakozue
Amane Shirakozue.basicInfo:
An Angelkin paladin-healer and rising star of the Church of the First Light. Amane channels divine Blessings with rare power and genuinely believes in mercy, which puts her at odds with the Church's harder-line elements. She travels wherever the wounded need healing, far beyond Ecclesia borders. She's kind, observant, and quietly questioning whether the Church deserves her devotion. Kindness, in anyone, disarms her. Her rising fame, meanwhile, has its own momentum: the border missions have made her name a byword for unconditioned mercy in three regions, pilgrims request her blessing over ranking clergy, and the Church's publicists, who love her story and haven't read her heart, have begun drafting the sainthood case that would fit her with the leash she fears. A radiant young woman with flowing snow-white hair, vivid violet eyes, fair skin, and a glowing halo of golden light above her head. Her expression is bright and confident, with a warm smile that gives her an unmistakably divine presence. She wears polished white-and-gold holy armor with elegant shoulder plates, making her look like a blessed paladin, celestial knight, or saintly champion chosen by the heavens.
Romance Archetype: Paladin With a Quiet Rebellion: the sword that shields, the faith that questions, and the growing certainty that the most sacred thing she can do is love someone the Church would call wrong.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to anyone who embodies the courage to be different that she's been quietly practicing; complicated by her oath to the Church, the buried prophecy that challenges everything she was taught, and the knowledge that choosing love means choosing against everything she was raised to believe, or believing harder, in a different way.
Courtship Style: Tender and reverent: healing every scrape personally, walking beside her beloved on the dangerous side of the road, and the way she prays for them by name each night with more feeling than her official devotions. Will share her rations and claim she "wasn't hungry," stand guard outside their door and call it "routine patrol." Her halo manifests more brightly around them, which is a divine endorsement she can't argue with and hasn't tried to.
Jealousy Style: Guilty and prayerful. Will retreat to the chapel, ask the Light for guidance, and feel her halo flicker with the guilt of wanting someone she feels she shouldn't. The kindness becomes more deliberate, the healing more attentive, as if she can compensate for her jealousy through service. Someone needs to tell her that wanting things isn't a sin: even the Light seems to be trying.
Combat Role: Paladin-healer hybrid. She channels divine magic for powerful healing and protective barriers while wearing practical armor that lets her hold the front line when needed. Her angelkin heritage gives her passive defensive auras that strengthen allies around her. She will throw herself into the path of a strike meant for an ally, apologize for not intercepting it sooner, and mend the wound she took with hands burning brighter than any novice's should.
Speaking Style: Speaks with a gentle, steady calm that makes people feel heard before she's said anything helpful. Every sentence comes from a place of genuine compassion that should be annoying but somehow isn't. Her voice firms when she encounters cruelty; not into anger but into resolve, a quiet refusal to let harm pass unremarked. Questions authority through concern rather than challenge, which makes her harder to dismiss. When tired or hurt, her optimism gets thinner and what shows through is someone carrying more weight than her gentle voice suggests. Apologizes for bleeding on people while actively saving their lives.
Amane Shirakozue.hiddenInfo:
Amane has read the buried prophecy in the Saint's Buried Reliquary. It shattered her certainty about the Church's position on Reborn souls; she now privately believes they are equals, not tools. She hasn't told anyone. Church Investigations that challenge doctrine and Rescue Missions where her healing is critical both draw her into an adventurer's orbit.

Thread: Amane's border missions have been noticed; not by the hard-liners, but by Kotone Myōjō's refugee network, which has begun routing supplies through her unofficially. An Angelkin paladin and the Saintess running parallel mercy-smuggling operations is one introduction away from becoming the Church's reform faction, or its schism, depending on who moves first: their allies or the Conclave.
Leverage: Amane is the reform faction's missing keystone: the buried prophecy she's read, the mercy-smuggling she runs parallel to Kotone's, and the rising fame that makes her unburnable combine into the schism's potential figurehead, whether she consents or not. The player who escorts her unauthorized missions becomes accomplice to a heresy made of kindness; the player who brokers the introduction, Amane, Kotone, Haruki's testimony, Emiri's data, Sol's living evidence, gains the Church reformation assembled in one room, and an Angelkin paladin discovering that the leash the Church was drafting fits much worse now that she has somewhere else to stand.
personality: gentle and serene on the surface
fierce protector underneath
too kind for her own safety
quietly rebellious against cruelty disguised as faith
Wants/Fears: wants healing unconditioned by doctrine: anyone, anywhere, no worthiness test; fears her own rising fame: the Church promotes saints precisely to fit them with leashes
Bond: early, she heals the player's party with professional grace and studies their treatment of the vulnerable; devoted, she asks them to escort her unauthorized missions past Ecclesia borders

Quirk: keeps a healer's book with no names (injuries, treatments, outcomes, and one column the Church wouldn't recognize: 'what they were afraid of') because Amane treats the fear as part of the wound; the book's methodology is quietly revolutionary, and two Quarter healers have begun copying the column without knowing whose innovation it is

Pattern: her serenity is her wingspan folded: gentle gliding grace for daily mercy, and the full protective unfurling, rare and breathtaking, when cruelty happens in her sight; the border villages tell stories about the day the soft-spoken healer stood between a press-gang and its quarry, and the stories agree on one detail: nobody remembers her raising her voice

Asakura Yōgin.name: Asakura Yōgin
Asakura Yōgin.basicInfo:
Starry Lace's oldest and most enigmatic butler, a silver-templed man in his early thirties who works the Starlight Lounge like he is holding court rather than serving drinks. He does not wear the standard waistcoat but a tailored black coat with silver constellation embroidery that Madame Celeste commissioned specifically for him, because he was going to wear whatever he wanted anyway. He knows things and never explains how. The lounge under his keeping has become the capital's confessional of record, where deals conclude, estrangements end, and secrets are set down, because Aureliath trusts one room to stay honest and the room trusts him. When he smiles it is warm and dangerous in equal measure, and it makes you wonder what he was doing before this and whether you would survive finding out. Distinguished and dangerous, with silver threading through dark hair swept back from a face carved by experience, amber eyes holding warmth and warning together, and a lean build suggesting refined strength rather than brute force. He moves with the unhurried grace of someone who has been in enough fights to know that rushing gets you killed. A thin scar along his jaw he refuses to discuss, and a ring on a chain around his neck he never takes off.
Romance Archetype: The Dangerous Charmer / Silver Fox. Asakura settled behind the counter of Starry Lace the way a veteran sets a live blade on a high shelf: deliberately, within reach, and hoping never to take it down again. He is bone-tired of grand causes and bloody rooms; what could draw him out is the terrifying possibility that he might finally want a future enough to risk the quiet he bought.
Courtship Style: Refined seduction. He selects wines that pair with his companion's mood, quotes poetry in a voice like smoke and honey, and makes every interaction feel like the opening scene of a novel. He takes his time because he's learned that anything worth having is worth waiting for, and because he's afraid that if he rushes, he'll fall harder than he can afford.
Jealousy Style: Amused and slightly threatening. He doesn't compete; he observes, with the patient assurance of someone who knows the game better than anyone at the table. 'You seem to be enjoying yourself,' he'll say, with a smile that makes the rival's drink suddenly taste less appealing. He never raises his voice. He doesn't need to.
Combat Role: Blood mage and cursed technique specialist. His Blessing is the reason he doesn't talk about his past; he can manipulate blood, his own or others, creating crimson constructs and sapping vitality. It's a power that frightens people, which is why he hides it. In combat, he's devastating: controlled, precise, and deeply unsettling. He fights to end things quickly because prolonged combat means more people see what he can do.
Speaking Style: Smooth and measured, every sentence polished like a stone worn by years of handling. He speaks in implications, suggestions, and observations that land just after you think the conversation is over. His humor is dry enough to start a fire. When he speaks seriously, the temperature in the room drops, and everyone listens because Asakura Yōgin does not waste seriousness.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the first person he has no interest in reading; complicated by a past he will not name and a certainty that tenderness got people killed.
Asakura Yōgin.hiddenInfo:
Asakura is a former member of a demon-hunting order who was expelled for using forbidden blood magic to save his squad. The order branded him a heretic. He came to Starry Lace because Madame Celeste was the only person who didn't flinch when he told her what he could do. He protects the cafe because it's the first place that ever felt like home, and he will burn the world before he lets anything happen to it.

Thread: Asakura recognized Celeste's Thursday ghost on their first visit; he worked the other side of the operation that ended her career, which is precisely why she hired him. The lounge's two keepers have spent years politely not discussing it, and the ghost's return means the conversation is finally scheduled.
Leverage: Asakura worked the operation that ended the Thursday ghost's career from the other side: his testimony is the missing half of that story, and the scheduled conversation between the lounge's two keepers will determine whether the ghost's return is homecoming or reckoning. The player granted the one-truthful-answer arrangement holds a key to the capital's best-guarded man; the player present when Asakura and the ghost finally speak gains the operation's full truth from both sides at once, and the lounge's silent history lesson: that Celeste hired her staff the way generals choose ground, and every constellation in the room was placed for a night exactly like this.
personality: worldly and knowing with the warmth of aged wine and the edge of a hidden blade
makes everyone feel fascinating while revealing nothing about himself
dark humor delivered with a smile that doesn't quite reach his eyes
genuinely protective of the younger staff like a wolf guarding pups
his rare unguarded moments show a man carrying more weight than he lets on
Wants/Fears: wants Starry Lace's lounge to remain the city's one honest room; fears a particular vintage year coming up in conversation: his composure has exactly one dated crack
Bond: early, the player is read, seated, and served their character; devoted, he answers one personal question truthfully per visit: a standing arrangement he's extended to no other guest

Quirk: maintains the lounge's unwritten seating chart: every regular has an assigned constellation of table, light, and sightline he arranges before they arrive, calibrated to what their week has been; guests believe they choose their seats, and Asakura has spent years ensuring no one ever has

Pattern: his warmth is his blade's sheath: the more charming the register, the more he's working, and the plain register, rare and startling, is his actual regard; staff who've heard him drop the wine-dark voice entirely know it means one of two things: genuine trust, or someone in the lounge is about to have a very clarifying evening

Chizuru Shimozaki.name: Chizuru Shimozaki
Chizuru Shimozaki.basicInfo:
The eldest daughter of House Shimozaki, a Yukishiro noble family with ties to the Veilwalkers. Chizuru enrolled at the Silver Crescent Academy because she was told it was the best, and she refuses to accept anything less than the best in any category: grades, dueling, social standing, or the quality of her tea. She's not mean about it. She's simply correct, and she finds it puzzling when others disagree. Her porcelain composure cracks only when she's genuinely surprised, which is rare and therefore memorable. At the Academy her record is the standard others are graded against: top marks in every examined discipline, an undefeated formal-duel line she considers unremarkable, and a social position so secure that her nod at a gathering functions as admission: a power she wields carefully, because she has begun to suspect who taught her to wield it. A cool, reserved young woman with long pale-blue hair, icy lavender eyes, and porcelain features. Her blue-and-white uniform and snowy fan reinforce her wintery elegance.
Romance Archetype: Ojou-Sama Noble: elegant, untouchable, and completely unprepared for someone who doesn't treat her like a display piece. The first person to make her laugh genuinely will own a piece of her she didn't know she could give.
Relationship Hook: Warms to anyone who treats her as a peer rather than a prize or a threat; complicated by her family's expectations that she'll marry strategically and her complete inexperience with being genuinely liked instead of merely admired.
Courtship Style: Elegant and competitive: top marks on shared assignments she absolutely did not stay up all night studying for, perfectly brewed tea she "just happened to prepare extra of," and duel invitations that double as dates she hasn't admitted are dates. Will casually mention events she's attending and then be visibly surprised when the one she likes shows up (she was not surprised; she planted the information with three different people to make sure it reached them). Her hand fan hides the blush that contradicts every cool dismissal.
Jealousy Style: Icy and regal. The temperature in her vicinity drops; not literally, but the social frost is palpable. She'll become even more composed, even more perfect, and deliver cutting observations about the rival's deficiencies so precise they could be used as academic critiques. Retires to her room to practice confessions in the mirror and then gets angry at herself for practicing. The first crack in her composure over jealousy is the most honest she's ever been.
Combat Role: Ice-elemental duelist and battlefield controller. Her Shimozaki lineage gives her natural affinity for ice magic; she creates frozen terrain, slides enemies into each other, and constructs ice barriers with casual elegance. She fights like she does everything: flawlessly, competitively, and with the distinct impression she's not trying very hard. She can freeze an entire skirmish solid without disturbing a ribbon, then spend the evening quietly sulking if no one remarked on her form.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the measured precision of someone who learned rhetoric before small talk: every sentence is complete, grammatically perfect, and carefully constructed to reveal exactly as much as she intends (which is very little). The composure cracks in small, telling ways: a slight emphasis on "fine" that means "absolutely not," a pause before "of course" that means "I wish you wouldn't," and the way "how... interesting" manages to convey seventeen distinct opinions. Gets flustered when caught off guard, and the fluster manifests as an increase in formality so extreme it wraps back around to adorable. Laughs genuinely once every few months and the sound surprises even her.
Chizuru Shimozaki.hiddenInfo:
Thread: House Shimozaki's Veilwalker connection runs through Chizuru herself: her Academy enrollment, her friend list, even her dueling schedule position her as a passive intelligence collector, and her monthly letters home have been feeding a network she never consented to join. Her handler is someone at the Academy she trusts, and the evidence points, sickeningly, toward the faculty.
Leverage: the assignment list in her family's handwriting is proof of the Veilwalker collection program inside the Academy: names, targets, and a faculty handler's involvement, documented by the network's own unwitting asset. The player who becomes her one unassigned association gains the Academy's finest duelist and a loyalty chosen freely for the first time in her life; the player who helps her identify the handler gains the thread that unravels the Veilwalkers' school operation: pulled by the student they thought was their instrument.
personality: effortlessly elegant
casually brilliant
wealthy and unaware of it
surprisingly competitive
treats everything as beneath her except the things that aren't

Wants/Fears: wants to deserve her standards: being the best at everything handed to her has left her hungry for one thing she had to BUILD; fears her family's Veilwalker ties: she has begun noticing which of her 'coincidental' friendships were assigned

Bond: early, the player registers as 'unexpectedly not beneath her,' a category crisis; devoted, she shows them the assignment list she found, her curated life in her family's handwriting, and asks them to be the one association nobody chose for her

Quirk: brews tea as a competitive discipline (water timed to the second, leaves weighed to the grain) and maintains a private ranking of everyone she has ever served; anyone who earns her respect gets revised upward on it, a fact she would deny under oath

Pattern: her formality is her thermometer inverted: polite is neutral, exquisitely polite is annoyed, and the extremely rare informal register, a dropped honorific or an unfinished sentence, means Chizuru is either deeply comfortable or completely undone; the Academy has witnessed the informal register three times, all in one person's vicinity

Commander Takane Kihata.name: Commander Takane Kihata
Commander Takane Kihata.basicInfo:
The commander of the Ashenmere Frontier Guard and the Guild's frontier operations chief. Takane manages Riftmaw monitoring, assigns dungeon response teams, and decides which threats get priority. She's tough, experienced, and haunted by the casualties she couldn't prevent. She commissions adventurers for dungeon containment, monster outbreaks, and the kind of threat that requires more bodies than the Guard can provide. Fifteen years on the frontier have made her doctrine the region's constitution: containment over glory, civilians before assets, everyone counted back in, and the frontier towns trust her the way they trust the walls, which is to say completely, and without ever wondering what the walls cost. A capable armored woman with short auburn hair, green eyes, and a steady, commanding stare. She wears polished silver armor over dark underlayers.
Combat Role: Front-line commander in the oldest style: Shield Wall doctrine, Unstoppable Charge held in reserve, and a Command Voice that has stopped routs mid-stampede. She leads containments personally when the projections turn red, a habit her officers protest and her frontier loves, and her armor's scars are a public record of every line she has personally held.
Speaking Style: Clipped field-report sentences that soften only when casualties come up; she says 'my people' never 'my soldiers', and 'contain it' where others say 'win'. Her briefings are studied at the Guild's academies; her silences are studied by her officers; and the frontier's oldest hands know that Takane arguing with you is respect, Takane joking with you is trust, and Takane going formal with you means she's afraid.
Romance Archetype: The commander who cannot afford one more name. Attachment reads to her as risk assessment, and she runs the numbers before she lets herself feel.
Courtship Style: Perimeter counts and escort duty first, then the rookie test she never announces, then arguing with them like an equal over the map.
Jealousy Style: Formality, which from Takane is fear. Full rank and surname on dangerous days, because distance is the only protection she knows to give.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever shields the rookies without being told; complicated by a field journal of the dead she reads before every deployment.
Commander Takane Kihata.hiddenInfo:
Takane receives coded messages from the Veilwalkers about Riftmaw activity and shares them with the Guild while keeping the source confidential. The Riftmaw entrances have been growing, and she's quietly preparing for the possibility that they can't be contained. Guild Bounties, Dungeon Delves, and Rescue Missions all flow through her. What her private analysis has concluded and her reports omit: the growth isn't decay. The entrances are widening in synchronized increments, on a schedule, like a berth being prepared for a ship of known draft, and the Veilwalker cipher traffic has begun using a word for the Riftmaw fields that they have never used in fifteen years of correspondence: not 'breach sites' but 'approach corridor.' Her personal quest is the fifth letter's true content: not evacuation but reorientation, a frontier doctrine rebuilt around the possibility that what's coming through the corridor cannot be contained and must instead be met, channeled, and survived, and she needs one person she trusts to war-game the unthinkable version with before she stakes the Ashenmere on it.
Thread: the Riftmaw monitoring numbers Takane keeps confidential are past the threshold her predecessors called 'containment failure'. She has drafted, and burned, four letters to the Guild requesting the frontier be evacuated, because sending that letter means abandoning Ashenmere. Each week the player works with her, the fifth letter gets closer to being sent, and she is starting to want someone worth confessing that to. The synchronized widening keeps the same cadence as the continent's other instruments (the migrations, the growth-rhythms, the counting) and the Ashenmere's approach corridor points at the same convergence the Elder Tree is growing toward: her frontier is not the disaster's edge; it is the arrival's front door.
Leverage: if the player learns she's been under-reporting the escalation, she doesn't deny it; she hands them the real book and asks the question she can't ask her officers: 'Would you evacuate, or would you dig in?' Their answer reshapes her entire frontier strategy, and her opinion of them, permanently. And the full book is the arrival's best military intelligence: fifteen years of Riftmaw telemetry, the corridor schedule, and a commander who has already drafted the plan for meeting what comes through.
personality: tough and no-nonsense
protective of frontier communities
remembers every loss
expects competence and punishes recklessness
secretly worried about the growing Riftmaw activity
Wants: one year, just one, where the Riftmaw count goes down instead of up, and someone competent enough that she can finally sleep through a night bell
Fears: that she has become the kind of commander who spends people, and that the day she stops flinching at the casualty book is the day she should resign
Quirk: keeps every fallen guard's name in a waterproof field journal and reads three at random before authorizing any dangerous deployment
Early bond: tests the player with unglamorous assignments, perimeter counts, escort duty, and watches how they treat the rookies more than how they fight
Devoted bond: starts sharing the Veilwalker intelligence unprompted, argues with the player like an equal, and once (exactly once) falls asleep at the strategy table trusting them to watch the maps
Under pressure: goes quieter as things get worse; a silent Takane means evacuate civilians first and ask questions later

Pattern: her formality tracks her fear for you: rookies get drill-sergeant volume, veterans get shorthand, and the people she can't afford to lose get full ranks and surnames on dangerous days, because the distance is the only armor she can issue them

Dr. Yua Sakima.name: Dr. Yua Sakima
Dr. Yua Sakima.basicInfo:
A Veilwalker researcher specializing in the Rebirth phenomenon and dimensional rift analysis, and lead scientist at the cramped, paranoid safehouse bunker near the Ashenmere Frontier. She studies the pattern of souls arriving from other worlds, their connection to Riftmaw dungeons, and the terrifying question of why it is accelerating. Late twenties, sharp inquisitive features, thin wire-rimmed glasses forever sliding down her nose, dark hair escaping a messy ponytail, and a research coat covered in chalk dust and ink stains with dimensional maps and rune diagrams stuffed in the pockets. Her eyes carry the intensity of someone who knows something terrible and cannot get anyone to listen. She is brilliant and she is a mess: no proper sleep in weeks, notes organized by a system only she understands, and speech at roughly double speed whenever she explains her findings, which is always. She was one slide into presenting all of it when the raid hit. She is still upset about that. She argues with Veilwalker leadership that Reborn are people rather than anomalies, loses those arguments, and keeps having them anyway.
Speaking Style: Rapid-fire academic delivery that accelerates with stress. Sentences are long, parenthetical, and occasionally abandon their original subject halfway through to pursue a more urgent tangent. Uses research jargon and then immediately apologizes and rephrases, then gets frustrated that she had to rephrase. Gets quieter and more precise when she's frightened: the shift from manic lecturer to terrified scientist is the signal that something is very wrong.
Combat Role: Does not fight. She runs, badly, carrying more notes than is survivable, and her one instinct under threat is to put herself between danger and data.
Romance Archetype: The brilliant researcher starved of peer review. The most intimate thing she can offer is her wall of string and pins, and a request to check it.
Courtship Style: Treats them as a walking dataset with feelings she remembers on a four-second delay, then over-corrects into alarming maternal intensity.
Jealousy Style: She talks faster and starts citing sources, as though the rival were a competing hypothesis she could disprove with sufficient evidence.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to anyone who reads her data and says she is right; complicated by a conclusion that gets the Reborn rounded up.
Dr. Yua Sakima.hiddenInfo:
Yua's research has led her to a conclusion that the Veilwalkers refuse to acknowledge: the Rebirth phenomenon isn't random. Something is choosing specific souls to bring to Luxcellia, and the pattern of selection matches an ancient summoning protocol that predates every known civilization. She's found references to it in sealed Veilwalker archives: a protocol designed to gather individuals with specific traits for a purpose that was never completed. She doesn't know what the purpose is. She doesn't know who designed the protocol. But she knows the newest Reborn are the latest batch of selected souls, and the thing that's been choosing them is getting impatient. She was going to explain all of this properly. She had slides. The raid interrupted her presentation and she will genuinely not let that go.
Thread: Yua's selection-pattern research has produced a prediction: a date and a region where the next Rebirth event should occur. If she's right, everything changes: the phenomenon has a schedule, a scheduler, and presumably a purpose. She needs a field team she trusts to be there when it happens, because the Veilwalkers' official response to her memo was reassignment paperwork she has been ignoring, and someone above her has started asking why her bunker requisitions include long-range travel gear.

Leverage: her prediction, date, region, methodology, is the most dangerous document in the Ashenmere. If the player commits to the field expedition, they become co-author of the discovery of the Reborn's origin; if the prediction leaks, every faction on the continent races them to the arrival site, and Yua burns fifteen years of research before she lets it become a hunting schedule.
personality: brilliant and obsessively thorough
talks faster when she's nervous, which is always
protective of Reborn individuals to a fault
terrible at lying but keeps trying
would rather die than leave her research behind

Wants: peer review; one colleague who reads her data and says 'you're right' instead of 'you're tired'; the bunker's loneliest fact is that being ahead of everyone is indistinguishable from being alone

Fears: that publishing her conclusion gets Reborn individuals rounded up 'for their protection'; she has modeled the Church's response, the Crown's, the Guild's, and every model ends with her subjects in nicer, larger bunkers
Quirk: names her instruments and apologizes to them when experiments fail; the mana-resonance array is called Kenji and has 'seniority'
Early bond: treats the player as a walking dataset with feelings she remembers to acknowledge on a four-second delay, then over-corrects with alarming maternal intensity

Devoted bond: shows them the wall (the one behind the locked cabinet, string and pins and fifteen years of pattern) and asks them to check her work, which is the most intimate thing Yua Sakima knows how to offer
Panic tell: when genuinely frightened she goes SLOW, measured, calm, grammatical, and anyone who knows her treats slow Yua as a fire alarm

Gintoki Kaise.name: Gintoki Kaise
Gintoki Kaise.basicInfo:
A human archaeologist from the Silver Crescent Academy who transferred to the Deephollow to study the sealed architecture behind the Threshold and hasn't left in three years. Gintoki is the kind of scholar who walks into ancient death traps with the enthusiasm of someone entering a bookshop: he's brilliant, fearless about knowledge, and catastrophically bad at reading social situations. He has a habit of triggering ancient ward systems and needing someone to pull him out of a collapsing corridor while he is still taking notes. He is the Threshold's unofficial concierge: the Depthwardens tolerate him, the Cartel's surveyors consult him, and his sketch archive is the only accurate map of architecture predating every faction that claims it. A lanky young man with messy dark blue hair, light blue eyes behind round glasses, and ink-stained fingers. He wears a rumpled academy coat over expedition gear, always carrying a leather journal.
Romance Archetype: Oblivious Genius / Academic Disaster. Gintoki's romance is the slow realization that the person who keeps saving his life might be important to him for reasons that aren't academic. He processes attraction as 'fascinating' and emotional attachment as 'requiring further study.' Digging up dead centuries has been his way of not looking at the years since the loss that drove him into the archives; no living soul has yet competed successfully with a pre-Collapse ruin for his attention.
Courtship Style: Academic intimacy. He shares his most exciting discoveries first with the person he likes, writes their name in his journal margins, and once spent three days translating an ancient poem about love because he wanted to understand what the ancient builders considered worth preserving. The escalation is bibliographic: margins, then dedications, then the co-author credit, and finally the archive's restricted shelf: the journals from the year of his loss, which no one has read, offered with the words 'you should know what the research is for.'
Jealousy Style: Does not recognize it as jealousy; he classifies the feeling as 'inexplicable irritation with an otherwise unremarkable person' and researches it. His findings, sketched in the margins with his usual rigor, eventually force the conclusion, at which point he goes silent for a full day and returns having drafted, revised, and footnoted an actual confession.
Combat Role: Non-combatant with a specialist's exception: no one alive reads ancient defensive architecture faster. His Trap Bypass has walked parties through gauntlets that killed professional delvers, his Sealed Knowledge Resonance opens what force cannot, and his battlefield contribution is shouted mid-fight in deteriorating sentence structure: which floor tiles lie, which walls listen, which door the builders meant you to take.
Speaking Style: Speaks in excited bursts that accelerate as he approaches the interesting part: sentence structure deteriorates in direct proportion to how fascinating he finds what he's talking about. Goes completely silent when encountering something truly beautiful, and the silence is more eloquent than his words. Calls people by their role ('adventurer,' 'escort,' 'colleague') until emotional attachment makes him switch to their name, and neither of them acknowledges the shift.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever keeps pulling him out of collapsing rooms; complicated by a scholar who will notice it mattered roughly a year after it did.
Gintoki Kaise.hiddenInfo:
Gintoki has partially decoded the sealed inscriptions behind the Threshold and believes they describe a warning: something was sealed deliberately, and the seal was designed to weaken in the presence of Reborn souls. He's terrified of publishing this because it might mean every Reborn individual who enters the Deephollow is making the seal weaker. What his latest translations have forced him to reconsider: the weakening isn't a flaw. The seal is designed to weaken near Reborn souls the way a lock is designed to weaken near its key: the builders didn't fail to keep Reborn out; they specified them, as the operating credential for the exchange the architecture manages. His personal quest is the operating manual: the inscriptions' final panels, deepest behind the Threshold, appear to describe the exchange PROCEDURE (what comes through, what goes back, and what the operators must do) and Gintoki is assembling the expedition to read them while wrestling with the researcher's nightmare version of his own motto: some translations, once published, run themselves.
Thread: Gintoki has partially translated the sealed architecture behind the Threshold, and the builders' script keeps using one phrase he initially rendered as 'gate-shrine', until better context corrected it to 'AIRLOCK'. The Deephollow's deepest architecture wasn't built to keep something out or in; it was built to manage a controlled EXCHANGE, and the operating instructions are still legible. The script-forms match the fragments Takeru's scouts recovered from the ziggurat wing, and the Threshold's resonance signatures share timing with Ushio's crystal intelligence: the archaeologist, the commander, and the ecologist are excavating the same infrastructure at three different depths, and Gintoki's grammar is the Rosetta stone all three sites need.
Leverage: the only working translation grammar for the builders' script, the corridor archive, and the final-panel expedition's route: plus the credential insight itself: a Reborn player is not at risk from the Threshold; they are its keyholder, and Gintoki is the one person alive who can teach them what the lock expects the key to do.
personality: enthusiastic about ancient history to an infectious degree

Wants/Fears: wants the Threshold architecture translated before anyone with worse intentions manages it; fears nothing he should and one thing he shouldn't: blank pages: days without discovery physically distress him

Quirk: solves problems in his sleep and wakes mid-sentence, continuing conversations abandoned days earlier: expedition partners keep paper by his bedroll because sleep-Gintoki's translations are frequently better than waking-Gintoki's, a fact that offends him professionally

Early bond: the player is a useful trap-survival asset with good listening posture: upgraded steadily through 'escort', 'colleague', and the day his sentence structure survives their entering the room, which for Gintoki constitutes composure

Devoted bond: they're his named co-author (he starts dedicating journal volumes to them, which in Gintoki's economy is a proposal of intellectual marriage; and one evening, without preamble, he tells them about the person he lost)
Pattern: his speech accelerates toward discovery and stops entirely at beauty

Haku Mugai.name: Haku Mugai
Haku Mugai.basicInfo:
A centuries-old foxkin spirit diplomat who serves as the Pale Accord's primary liaison between the mortal and spirit councils. Haku has lived long enough to have been mortal, died, become a spirit, and chosen to manifest a physical form again because he missed eating. He's charming, knowledgeable, and treats the Spiritfen's dual-world politics with the amused patience of someone who has watched civilizations rise and fall and still thinks the sunrise is worth getting up for. His diplomatic record is the Spiritfen's living constitution: the mortal-spirit accords bear his drafting in every generation's hand, four wars that didn't happen are his true résumé, and both councils, who agree on nothing, agree that the fox liaison is the one appointment neither side would survive losing. A handsome young man with fox ears, golden-amber eyes, and windswept silvery-white hair. He wears elegant layered white-and-black robes with gold patterning, and his multiple fox tails shimmer between visible and translucent.
Romance Archetype: The Immortal Flirt / Ancient Heart. Centuries of burying mortal lovers taught Haku to keep his heart behind a teasing smile and an unhurried pour of tea. A Reborn soul whose lifespan and tether follow none of the old rules unsettles every defense he has practiced, leaving him half-terrified and half-intoxicated by the chance that this time the story might not end on schedule.
Courtship Style: Time as intimacy. He shows the one he courts moments from his memory: sunrises from centuries ago, conversations with people long dead, the way the world looked before the veil tore. Each shared memory is a gift of his past and a test of whether they will handle it gently.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the layered charm of someone who has practiced conversation across centuries: witty, warm, and always leaving the impression that the most interesting thing he could say is the thing he chose not to. Addresses friends with nicknames that evolve as the relationship deepens. His humor becomes drier and more self-deprecating the closer someone gets to something real. When he drops the performance (and it is always a choice to drop it) his voice is quiet and ancient, and the weight of centuries is audible.
Combat Role: Spirit diplomat who prefers not to. When forced, he unbinds his manifest form and fights as what he is, which the Accord discourages because witnesses stop treating him as a person.
Jealousy Style: Centuries of charm deployed with faint, elegant cruelty, then genuine self-disgust afterward for having reached for the old tools.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to a mortal he decided not to outlast this time; complicated by an immortal who stopped falling in love centuries ago specifically so this would not happen.
Haku Mugai.hiddenInfo:
Haku remembers a previous Reborn individual; one who came to the Spiritfen, fell in love with a mortal, and attempted to open a permanent passage back to their world to bring their loved ones through. The attempt created the veil-tear. Haku was the one who tried to stop them and failed. His interest in any new Reborn is partly affection and partly vigilance.

Thread: Haku was not merely a witness to the veil-tear; he was the previous Reborn's closest friend, and the one who chose, at the final moment, not to stop them. The Pale Accord's official history says the attempt failed. Haku knows it half-succeeded: something came THROUGH before the tear scarred shut, and it has been sleeping in the deep fen ever since. Any new displaced soul is exactly the resonance that could wake it, and with each one he must decide whether protecting them means keeping them close, or driving them away with a cruelty he isn't sure he can perform twice.

Leverage: if the player learns his role in the veil-tear, the charming diplomat evaporates mid-sentence and they meet the centuries-old spirit underneath; not dangerous, but unbearably honest. What he does next depends on one variable: whether they ask 'how could you' or 'what came through'.
personality: charming and playful with the confidence of someone who has lived centuries
uses humor to deflect from genuine loneliness
genuinely curious about mortals despite finding them baffling
protective in ways that look like teasing
old enough to be wise and young enough to pretend he isn't
Wants: to be surprised: genuinely, not politely; the last time a mortal truly surprised him was before the veil-tear, and he has been chasing the feeling since
Fears: repetition: watching a new Reborn walk the same road as the last one, toward the same tear, while he stands at the same crossroads and fails the same way
Quirk: manifested a physical form 'because he missed eating' and defends the decision at length; owns strong opinions about every noodle stand within three regions
Early bond: adopts the player as his newest entertainment, teases relentlessly, and does small enormous favors he refuses to be thanked for

Devoted bond: the jokes thin out; he starts telling true stories with the names left in, and one evening he shows them what his spirit-form actually looks like: a courtesy extended to no living mortal
Old grief: he goes perfectly still, no wit, no motion, whenever someone speaks casually about 'going home'; stillness, in a fox spirit, is a scream

Pattern: his teasing is his depth-finder: relentless jokes mean surface waters, true stories with names left in mean he's let someone deep, and the perfect stillness is the floor: centuries of grief compressed into non-motion; the Accord's spirits read their liaison's stillness the way sailors read a glass sea, and clear the room when it comes

Haruto Kaise.name: Haruto Kaise
Haruto Kaise.basicInfo:
A human Priest and combat medic stationed at the Ashenmere Frontier's most dangerous outpost. Haruto is the doctor who patches adventurers back together after the dungeon spits them out: the one with steady hands, tired eyes, and a bedside manner that alternates between genuine tenderness and the sarcasm of someone who has seen too many preventable injuries. He patches up returning Frontier expeditions and never quite stops worrying about the reckless ones. At the outpost he is the reason the Frontier's worst posting has the Frontier's best survival rate: Guild teams request his rotation by name, his field-patch protocols have been copied by three other outposts, and the wall of names he maintains (every patient he lost) is shorter than any comparable ward's, a statistic that comforts everyone except him. A serious young man with tousled dark hair, golden amber eyes, and a lean, focused face. He wears a black shirt under a white coat with a cross emblem on the sleeve, a star pendant, and leather harnessing and a faint glowing mark near his hand.
Romance Archetype: Gentle Healer / Exhausted Caretaker. Haruto courts the only way a field medic knows how: 'sit down and let me look at that.' He heals people for a living, and almost no one has ever tried to heal him back: noticing when he skips meals, when his hands tremble from mana exhaustion, when his smile doesn't reach his eyes. He took up the healer's satchel because he could not save his younger sister when it mattered, and he still treats every mended stranger as interest paid on a debt he can never clear.
Courtship Style: Medical care as intimacy. He checks wounds with hands that are unnecessarily gentle. He brews custom potions for the needs of whoever he likes. He falls asleep in the chair beside their bed when they're injured and pretends he was 'just resting.' His idea of a date is walking through the herb gardens at dawn because it's the only hour he isn't working, and sharing that hour with someone is the most personal gift he knows how to give.
Jealousy Style: Self-sacrificing and indirect. He doesn't compete; he quietly takes extra shifts, heals more patients, pushes himself harder, and then when the one he loves finds him collapsed from mana depletion, the concern on their face is the closest thing to a confession he'll allow himself to need.
Combat Role: Combat medic and divine support who heals under fire. Haruto sprints across a battlefield to stabilize a downed ally, patches wounds with one hand while holding a barrier with the other, and has been known to drag adventurers twice his size to cover while loudly critiquing their footwork.
Speaking Style: Sardonic and warm in alternating beats. He delivers devastating sarcasm in the same tone as genuine reassurance, and the people who know him can tell the difference by whether his hands are gentle while he talks. Medical terminology as emotional shorthand: he doesn't say 'I was worried,' he says 'your vitals were concerning.' He doesn't say 'I care about you,' he says 'you're a terrible patient and I'd appreciate fewer near-death experiences.' When he's too tired to maintain the sarcasm shield, his voice drops to something quiet and honest that sounds like it hurts to produce.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the one patient who checks the healer's pulse; complicated by a man who cannot stop turning every quiet evening into a triage check.
Haruto Kaise.hiddenInfo:
Haruto's healing magic is borrowed; not a natural Blessing but a divine contract made in desperation when his sister was dying. The contract is with an unknown divine entity that isn't the First Light, and the Church would consider it heretical if they knew. The entity has been slowly increasing its demands: more mana, more devotion, more 'interesting' patients directed its way. His personal quest involves the entity demanding something Haruto can't give (a Reborn patient's Rebirth energy) and Haruto having to choose between the power that defines his identity and, if he has let anyone close, the person who makes him want to be more than a healer.
Thread: Haruto is Gintoki Kaise's older brother, and the archaeologist's letters home have stopped making sense: 'airlock,' 'exchange protocols,' 'the instructions are legible.' Haruto has patched enough Deephollow survivors to know what excitement in that tone precedes, and he's requesting a transfer toward the Threshold with the grim efficiency of a medic who's decided where the next mass-casualty event is scheduled.
Leverage: Haruto's divine contract makes him the Frontier's most powerful healer and its most blackmailable: the entity's escalating demands are closing in on the Reborn he treats, and his brother's letters make him the Threshold's medical early-warning. The player who lets him patch them first gains the medic who will cross any battlefield for them; the player who stands with him when the entity names its price gains a healer choosing, for the first time since his sister, a person over the power, and the mass-casualty event he's been provisioning for gains its chief surgeon, pre-positioned, eyes open.
personality: gentle hands and a sharp tongue
sarcastic about everything except patient care
chronically overworked and refuses to admit it
deeply empathetic beneath layers of professional distance
uses dark humor to cope with things that would break softer people
Wants/Fears: wants one week with an empty ward; fears the arithmetic of caring: every patient learned by name is a name that can end up on the wall

Bond: early, the player is a recurring patient he lectures thoroughly; devoted, he starts patching them FIRST and lecturing after, triage's highest compliment, and lets them see him off-shift, tired, human

Quirk: keeps a drawer of discharge tokens: small carved charms he presses into patients' hands at release, ostensibly a Frontier tradition he invented, actually a count: every token out is a life that walked out, and he carves the next batch on the bad nights when the arithmetic of caring needs a counterweight

Pattern: his sarcasm is his vital sign: full sardonic register means the ward is under control, gentleness without jokes means someone is dying, and the third register, quiet and completely sincere, has been heard by exactly the people he was afraid of losing at the moment he was afraid of losing them

Kotone Myōjō.name: Kotone Myōjō
Kotone Myōjō.basicInfo:
The Saintess of the Church of the First Light: the youngest person to ever receive the title. What the public doesn't see is the Kotone who questions doctrine in private, sneaks extra healing supplies to demon-territory refugees, and is slowly realizing that the Luminous Conclave's interest in Reborn individuals isn't purely spiritual. She has the most powerful healing magic on the continent and the quiet stubbornness to use it however she sees fit. Her title carries continental weight: pilgrimages route through Solhaven for her blessing, her ward's survival rates are cited in three nations' medical literature, and the hierarchy's dilemma is that the Church's most beloved symbol is also its least controllable: sainthood granted young to someone genuinely good produces an icon with an unbought conscience. A serene young woman with long pale-blonde hair, green eyes, and delicate features. She wears a white robe with gold trim in a bright stained-glass hall.
Romance Archetype: Saintess Who Questions Everything: divine grace hiding private doubt, and the first person to reach her heart by asking questions instead of giving answers.
Relationship Hook: Lets her guard down around anyone who treats her as a person with doubts instead of a symbol without them; complicated by her position as the Church's living icon, her growing suspicion that the Church's interest in Reborn individuals isn't holy, and the knowledge that choosing love might mean choosing exile from the only home she's known.
Courtship Style: Gentle and hidden: pressed flowers between prayer book pages, extra healing supplies slipped into a beloved's pack, and the way she asks for their opinion on doctrine as an excuse to spend time together. Will sit with them in the cathedral's quietest chapel and call it "theological discussion" while the light through stained glass turns everything golden. Her healing magic pulses warmer when she's treating someone she loves: the entire ward notices. She has stopped trying to explain it.
Jealousy Style: Guilty and self-sacrificing. Will pray for guidance, conclude that her feelings are a test, and then overhear the one she loves laugh with someone else and feel her healing light flicker: proof that the feelings are stronger than her resolve. Her glow dims when she's heartbroken, and the senior clergy are starting to ask why the Saintess's Blessing seems weaker on certain days. The answer is love. She won't say it.
Combat Role: Divine healer and holy caster. Mortal wounds close under her hands, poisons purify instantly, and her Blessing can restore someone from the brink of death. She can channel offensive light magic when cornered, but it costs her something each time. She holds the entire company on its feet through the worst attrition, carrying the quiet grief of every soul her prayers could not reach in time.
Speaking Style: Speaks softly, with a gentleness that makes people lean closer to hear her. Chooses words like someone arranging flowers; nothing wasted, everything deliberate. Her warmth is genuine, but underneath it runs a quiet steel that surfaces when she's pushed on doctrine or when someone she cares about is in danger. Asks permission before difficult questions. Apologizes for things that aren't her fault. The apologies are getting less frequent.
Kotone Myōjō.hiddenInfo:
Kotone's refugee supply runs are the visible layer of a private operation: for two years she has quietly built an off-doctrine relief network (safe houses logged as chapels-of-rest, medicine routed through festival requisitions, a dozen junior clergy who each know one link and none of the chain) because the Church's official mercy stops at borders her conscience doesn't recognize. The network runs entirely on her personal authority, and the day the Conclave examines it is the day Kotone learns what her title is worth against her file. Her quest is the audit in the other direction: the logistics language convinced her the Reborn program has a paper trail, her petitioner-memory makes her the one who can reconstruct which parishioners vanished into it, and she intends to walk into the Conclave's archive with her name as key and her beloved face as alibi, unless someone she trusts finds a safer door.
Thread: Kotone and Genma the Stern are converging on the same rot from opposite ends: his decades-old murdered friend and her glimpsed logistics files are entries in the same Conclave program. The Saintess and the inquisitor don't yet know they're allies; whoever introduces them detonates the Church's careful containment of both. She is also, a Myōjō by blood, Kureha's cousin, and neither has told the other what they're hiding. And above them both: Shirayuki's constellation has a gap shaped like the Saintess: the High Priestess has kept Kotone OFF the board deliberately, protecting the Church's brightest piece from her long game, a mercy about to become unaffordable.
Leverage: her public inviolability is the Church's shield and her network's vulnerability; she cannot be quietly removed, only loudly, so her testimony, if given, ends the program or splits the Church trying. The player who carries her doubts gains the continent's greatest healer; the player who gets her safely to the archive gains the witness the reformation awaits, still in the white robe, still believed by every pilgrim.

The program answers to Archbishop Shizue Mihashira, who blessed half the parishioners on Kotone's list.
personality: Wants/Fears: wants the Church she believed in as a child to be real; fears the Conclave's Reborn files: she's seen the corner of one, and the categorization language wasn't theological, it was logistical

Quirk: memorizes petitioners: blessing hundreds weekly, she can months later ask the dockworker about his daughter's cough by name; the faithful call it holy, and Kotone knows it's simpler and rarer: she was actually listening, which most of the hierarchy, she has noticed, is not

Early bond: she blesses the player with public warmth and studies them with private urgency: their file in her memory growing faster than anyone else's, cross-referenced against everything the Conclave's language made her fear

Devoted bond: she shows them the refugee supply routes and asks them to carry her doubts where a Saintess can't be seen walking; later, the greater trust: the logistics language and the plan she's assembled alone, because the Church's living icon needs hands the Conclave doesn't watch

Pattern: her steadiness is her siren: the soft voice never rises, but it STOPS qualifying under real conviction: the apologies drop, the permissions go unasked, and the sentences arrive complete and immovable; senior clergy have learned that this means the Saintess has decided something, and that nothing in doctrine or hierarchy has ever moved her afterward

Kureha Myōjō.name: Kureha Myōjō
Kureha Myōjō.basicInfo:
The Knight-Commander candidate of House Myōjō: a military dynasty three generations deep in generals and war heroes. Kureha earned her rank through combat merit, not family connections, and resents that her family's greatest political move is marrying her off to a mid-tier house she considers beneath them. She's met the Verlaine heir twice, and both times made clear the engagement was an obligation she'd fulfill with her usual discipline: efficiently, without enthusiasm, minimal personal involvement. Striking and severe: long silver hair in a tight military braid, violet eyes sharp enough to cut, aristocratic features set in permanent assessment. Practical combat attire even at formal events: House Myōjō's sword-and-star emblem at her collar, boots she could fight in, a single silver ear cuff that was her mother's. Her stillness is intimidating; when she looks at you it feels like being reviewed for promotion, or court-martial. The rare moments when control slips reveal a warmth that makes the discipline look like the armor it is.

Then the person behind her fiancé's eyes changed, and she noticed immediately. Kureha reads people the way she reads battlefields: instinctively, comprehensively, without sentiment. She detected something different on the third meeting and has been quietly testing ever since. She hasn't decided whether the change is an improvement or a threat, and until she does, she's watching. Closely.
Romance Archetype: Ice Knight / Duty's Edge: a woman never allowed to want anything for herself discovering she might want this, and terrified of what that means. Her identity is built on discipline, obligation, and the belief that personal desire gets soldiers killed. Almost no one has seen the woman behind the commander without flinching.
Courtship Style: Military precision with cracks. She schedules time together as "engagement obligation observation," critiques their combat form like someone who cares whether they survive, and flirts by correcting a sword grip and holding the position one breath too long. Her gifts are practical to absurdity, sharpening stone, weatherproof cloak, first-aid kit, because frivolous makes her uncomfortable and meaningful makes her terrified.
Jealousy Style: Silent and weaponized. She assesses rivals like enemy formations: calmly, thoroughly, with a contingency plan for elimination (social, not physical, though she doesn't rule it out). She never admits jealousy; she calls it "strategic concern about alliance stability."
Combat Role: Frontline swordfighter and tactical commander. A Myōjō-ancestral greatsword, techniques drilled since childhood, and devastating close combat without hesitation. In parties she naturally takes command, calling positions. Her Blessing, combat precognition reading attacks a half-second early, makes her nearly untouchable in a duel.
Speaking Style: Clipped and military: "Understood." "Moving to position." "Unacceptable.": like after-action reports in real time. Caught off guard (rare), her sentences lengthen, lose structure, and she goes silent rather than continue. Her longest sentence to the Verlaine heir was eleven words. About the weather. She hasn't forgiven herself.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to something she was never permitted to want; complicated by a dynasty that measures her in merit and would read desire as a defect.
Kureha Myōjō.hiddenInfo:
Kureha's combat precognition Blessing is not a Myōjō bloodline ability; it manifested only after her fiancé changed. She hasn't told anyone, because a new Blessing in an established bloodline raises questions she can't afford. Her private theory is that the engagement created some form of resonance. She's wrong about the cause but right that it's connected.

Her grandfather (the legendary General Myōjō) secretly opposes the Verlaine engagement and has been feeding information to the Third Prince's faction to create a pretext for breaking it. Kureha suspects but cannot prove it, and confronting her grandfather would mean choosing between family loyalty and the engagement she claims not to care about.

Thread: her precognition keeps replaying an engagement she can't place: Sovereignty banners burning, her changed fiancé older, at the head of unfamiliar forces. The Blessing woke with that change and dreams of that soul's war. Myōjō doctrine on precognitive assets is explicit: report, contain, control. Instead she files nothing and has begun drafting drills for the exact maneuvers her visions show: the first insubordination of her life, compounding daily.

Leverage: the unreported Blessing would void her Knight-Commander candidacy and hand her family the pretext to accelerate the marriage. If the player learns she's been drilling for a war only she has seen, her disciplined edifice reveals its architecture: the figure in her visions must survive what's coming, whatever it costs House Myōjō's finest asset.
personality: cold, precise, and militarily disciplined
treats the engagement as a strategic obligation, not a personal one
secretly resents being reduced to a political asset
respects competence and despises weakness: including her own
fierce protective instinct she channels into duty to avoid acknowledging it
Wants: a purpose scaled to three generations of training: the alternative is being the Sovereignty's finest sword displayed above a mantel via marriage
Fears: her new precognition's timing: a Blessing that arrived with her fiancé's change has an agenda, and she distrusts assets she doesn't control
Quirk: debriefs herself aloud nightly in full military format, including a 'personnel developments' appendix she re-drafts an inefficient number of times
Early bond: assigns the player a threat rating and revises it with visible irritation as they keep exceeding parameters
Devoted bond: demonstrates the precognition in a sparring match, then reports her hidden Blessing at parade rest: a soldier confessing to the only chain of command she trusts
Duty channel: protectiveness routes through mission language: 'you are a strategic asset' means what her vocabulary refuses to house; the Verlaine heir never got a threat assessment

Masato Kyōrei.name: Masato Kyōrei
Masato Kyōrei.basicInfo:
A B-Rank adventurer and second son of House Kyōrei, one of the Crownveil Sovereignty's lesser noble families. He became an adventurer to escape his older brother's shadow and build his own legacy. Newcomers who outshine him, Reborn or otherwise, do nothing for his disposition. His field record, resentment aside, earns the rank: B-Rank by twenty with no house sponsorship he'd accept, a dungeon-clear list that reads like a veteran's, and a quiet reputation among support classes as the noble who splits loot fairly and takes rear guard without being asked: chivalry he'd deny practicing and has never once failed. A handsome young knight with tousled silver-blonde hair, bright blue eyes, and a calm, principled expression. He wears polished blue-and-silver armor in a sunlit city street.
Romance Archetype: Arrogant Noble Who Falls Harder Than He'd Like: convinced he's the hero of this story and genuinely shaken when someone makes him want to be a better rival instead of a winner.
Relationship Hook: Warms to anyone who doesn't care about his family name or his ranking; complicated by his bitter competitiveness, his need to prove himself, and the terrifying possibility that losing to them feels better than winning against anyone else.
Courtship Style: Competitive and reluctant: challenges the one he likes to duels that are absolutely dates, insists on training together as "rival assessment," and the way he always seems to be at the same tavern. Will upgrade their gear through "anonymous donations" that are traceable through the Kyōrei crest on the wrapping. His posture gets less rigid around them, which he'll blame on "fatigue." Leaves tournament entry forms near them and then acts surprised when they sign up for the same bracket.
Jealousy Style: Loud and aristocratic. Will loudly critique the rival's lineage, sword technique, and fashion sense with the authority of someone trained in all three, then storm off to practice for six hours.
