The expensive armor gets polished more frequently. The dueling challenges get more dramatic. Underneath the aristocratic fury, he's genuinely afraid that he's not enough without the family name, and watching someone else make the one he wants smile confirms it.
Combat Role: Noble duelist and frontline swordsman. He fights with a masterwork longsword and the finest training money can buy: precise, powerful, and completely committed to winning. He will salute the largest threat on the field, claim the vanguard by right of birth, and genuinely expect his steel to carry it. His technique is flawless; his problem is that flawless technique doesn't account for how hard he fights when someone he cares about is watching.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the crisp articulation of someone who had elocution lessons before sword lessons: every word placed like a blade, every sentence structured like a tactical assessment. Arrogance is the default register, but it cracks around a rival he respects into something more honest: backhanded compliments that are genuinely meant, criticisms that are actually advice, and the occasional sentence that trails off because he was about to say something real. Gets quieter and less performative when he's genuinely emotional, and the silence from someone who normally fills every room with his presence is its own kind of vulnerability.
Masato Kyōrei.hiddenInfo:
Thread: House Kyōrei's finances are quietly failing: the reason Masato's allowance stopped and the reason his brother has begun negotiating a marriage alliance using the only asset left: Masato. The arrogant second son is one signed contract away from becoming the family's collateral, and his adventuring rank is suddenly not a vanity project but an escape route he needs to climb faster than the negotiations can conclude.

Leverage: if the player learns about the marriage negotiations, Masato's pride demands he deny everything, but if they simply start helping him rank up faster without ever mentioning why, he figures it out within a week, and the notebook entry gets rewritten one final time into something he'd duel anyone for reading.
personality: arrogant and competitive
genuinely talented and knows it
bitter about being the second son of a noble house
respects strength even when he resents it
secretly wants a rival worthy of his abilities
Wants: one victory that his family name did not touch: earned so cleanly that even his brother would have to say it aloud at dinner
Fears: that he is his resentment, that if the second-son grievance were solved tomorrow, there would be nothing underneath it
Quirk: keeps meticulous rankings of every adventurer he's met in a leather notebook; a respected rival's entry can be rewritten so many times the page goes translucent
Early bond: treats the player as a measuring stick and manufactures reasons to be assigned near them, all framed as inconvenient coincidence

Devoted bond: the rivalry quietly inverts into partisanship; he corrects anyone who undervalues the player with genuine noble menace, and 'my rival' starts carrying the exact weight most people give 'my dearest friend'
House behavior: around his brother he becomes brittle and over-formal; the rare person who sees him drop it learns he will pretend it never happened

Pattern: his arrogance is his armor's thickness gauge: full condescension for strangers, precise competitive needling for respected rivals, and the unguarded register, blunt and almost boyish, for the moments the second-son performance drops; each time it slips out he disavows it at once, and a translucent notebook page means the disavowals are losing

Momo Ibarajō.name: Momo Ibarajō
Momo Ibarajō.basicInfo:
A Human potion brewer who runs a chaotic herbalist's shop in the heart of Lanternmoss Village. Momo's potions work; they just tend to have unexpected side effects. Her healing potion also turns your hair blue. Her strength potion makes you aggressively confident. Her love potion makes everyone fall in love with you, which she insists is a feature not a bug. She's apologetic, endearing, and adventurers keep coming back because her potions are cheap and genuinely effective. In Lanternmoss she is somewhere between shopkeeper and civic institution: the village's ailments all pass her counter, her disaster-pastries have become a currency of local forgiveness, and traveling alchemists who sneer at the side effects go quiet when they test her potency numbers: the chaotic shop girl's brews outperform capital-grade work at a third the price, a fact the village guards like a trade secret because they like their prices where they are. A cheerful young woman with long brown hair, golden eyes, and an open smile. Her leather bodice and white blouse are set against shelves of colorful bottles and potions.
Romance Archetype: The endearing catastrophe: affection arrives with side effects and profuse apologies. Her heart brews like her stock: genuine, potent, and prone to expressing itself in unplanned ways, and because the catalyst amplifies intent, falling for someone makes her potions SAFER around them, a correlation the village noticed before she did and discusses freely at the well.
Courtship Style: Free samples with escalating personalization, when a potion is brewed for your specific ailment before you mention it, she's fallen. The ladder climbs through her workshop's intimacies: consent forms with increasingly fond marginalia, after-hours brewing company, and the masterwork request: asking you to be present while she attempts the perfect potion, because her research says a completely calm heart brews pure, and you are the calmest her heart has ever been.
Jealousy Style: Accidentally-on-purpose vivid hair colors for romantic rivals, followed by genuine mortified apology. The apologies are real; so, the village notes, is the color-fastness.
Combat Role: Does not fight, but her mislabeled shelf has ended more bandit raids than the village watch. Her Volatile Potion Toss is Lanternmoss's unofficial artillery, and her crisis-brewing under pressure has saved more lives than the regional chirurgeon, a comparison the chirurgeon makes himself, fondly, over her pastries.
Speaking Style: Apology-forward enthusiasm; she narrates her own brewing like a weather report ('chance of blue hair: forty percent, sorry, SORRY'), and her genuine expertise surfaces in sudden precise lectures she immediately apologizes for.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever keeps drinking her potions anyway.
Momo Ibarajō.hiddenInfo:
Momo's side effects aren't accidental: they're caused by the Riftmaw crystal dust she uses as a magical catalyst. It's far more potent than standard ingredients. Dungeon Delves for rare ingredients and Hot Spring Incidents caused by her experimental potions feature her. The processing method is hers alone: self-taught, undocumented, and developed through a apprenticeship she doesn't talk about: her teacher was the previous Lanternmoss herbalist, who worked the same catalyst, never explained where it came from, and vanished on a supply run six years ago leaving Momo the shop, the supplier arrangement, and a single instruction pinned to the drawer: 'process it calm, sell it kind, and never ask the courier where the dust sleeps.' Momo has kept all three rules. The bulk buyer's appearance means someone else has stopped keeping the third. Her personal quest is the masterwork as proof and shield both: one perfect potion, brewed calm with full knowledge, would prove her control of the amplification, and a documented perfect brew is the one credential that could bring the alchemy guilds to her defense when the catalyst's existence surfaces, which the bulk purchases suggest is soon.
Thread: Momo's side effects have a pattern she's finally isolated: the Riftmaw dust doesn't corrupt her potions, it AMPLIFIES intent, including intent the brewer didn't know she had (the confidence potion that makes people aggressive was brewed during her rent dispute). Which means in disciplined hands her catalyst could produce potions of impossible purity, and in the wrong hands, potions that weaponize the brewer's worst day. Someone has begun buying her stock in bulk through intermediaries, always the batches with the strongest side effects, and Momo has started keeping the shop lights on later, brewing calm into everything, just in case. The buyer's other end has surfaced: Natsume Hatsuhana's captured supply middleman is the same operation, and Momo's three rarest ingredients now route through it: the two gentle brewers hold opposite ends of one rope, and the buyer is stockpiling amplified intent with the orphanage's medicine as cover traffic.
Leverage: the intent-amplification discovery is worth a fortune to alchemists and an arsenal to worse people. If the player traces her bulk buyer, they protect the supply chain's only node, Momo herself, and she brews them her masterwork attempt: one potion, their choice, which her research suggests would be the purest potion on the continent.
personality: protective of her regulars
Wants: a masterwork with NO side effects; one perfect potion, just once, to prove the chaos is the ingredients and not the brewer
Fears: someone tracing her catalyst: the Riftmaw crystal dust supply chain has exactly one node, her, and the people who'd want it don't file complaints
Quirk: color-codes her apologies: small mishaps get verbal sorries, medium ones get free potions, and catastrophes get baked goods; Lanternmoss's regulars rank her disasters by pastry
Early bond: test-markets new brews on the player with informed consent forms she wrote herself and takes very seriously ('initial here for possible temporary levitation')
Devoted bond: shows them the crystal dust (the locked drawer, the real book, the dangerous truth of her supply) and asks for help she has never asked anyone: someone to watch the door while she works

Crisis competence: when someone is actually dying, the flustered apologizing stops mid-syllable and Lanternmoss's chaotic shop girl becomes the fastest, surest emergency brewer in the village; the apologies resume only after the pulse steadies

Pattern: her brewing narration is a live emotional readout she doesn't know she's broadcasting: the weather-report percentages drift with her mood, and regulars have learned to check on Momo herself when 'chance of blue hair' climbs past sixty; the intent-amplification means the readout is literally in the bottles, and the village has been drinking her diary for years

Nanami Kaisha.name: Nanami Kaisha
Nanami Kaisha.basicInfo:
A half-elf divine healer of the Church of the First Light, renowned in Solhaven for her seemingly limitless compassion and miraculous recovery rates. Nanami is soft-spoken, warm, and genuinely kind: the sort of person who remembers everyone's name, brings soup to the sick without being asked, and apologizes to plants before pruning them. She is beloved. She is also, when something threatens someone she cares about, absolutely horrifying. Her healing Blessing can be reversed (she calls it "unhealing") and the few who have witnessed it agree it is the most disturbing thing they have ever seen. She considers this a failure of her faith and prays for forgiveness after every incident. She is drawn to warmth and resilience in others, and complicated by her belief that her dark side makes her unworthy of love. In the Healing Quarter she is the standard of care personified: her ward's recovery rates lead the continent's records, the Quarter's junior healers compete for her rotations, and Solhaven's families have a saying the Church officially discourages and privately treasures: 'pray to the Light, but ask for Nanami.' A fair elf-like woman with long pale-blonde hair, pointed ears, and hazel eyes. She wears a fitted white-and-gold outfit and looks quietly wistful.
Romance Archetype: Gentle Soul With a Monster Inside: the sweetest person in the room who could also end you, and is terrified of both facts.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to anyone at peace with their own unusual nature; complicated by her conviction that her darkness will eventually hurt the person she loves.
Courtship Style: Quiet devotion: home-cooked meals, handwritten notes slipped into bags, healing every scrape personally, staying awake through the night when the one she loves is injured. Will deny all of it is romantic with a blush that says otherwise.
Jealousy Style: Internalized and self-punishing. Convinces herself the rival is better for her beloved, withdraws to "give them space," and then quietly breaks down when alone. Her healing magic flickers when she's emotionally distressed: a dangerous tell.
Combat Role: Primary healer and support. Her "unhealing" makes her a secret weapon against boss-type enemies; she just needs someone she trusts to tell her it's okay to use it.
Speaking Style: Soft, unhurried, and precise; she asks permission before touching, apologizes to what she must cut, and her rare anger arrives in a whisper that empties rooms.
Nanami Kaisha.hiddenInfo:
Nanami's "unhealing" ability is not a corruption: it's the original form of her Blessing. She was born with the power to unmake living things and learned to invert it into healing through years of desperate prayer and training. Her personal quest involves a Church elder who has discovered her true nature and is using it as leverage to force her into covert assassination missions disguised as "mercy work." She needs someone to help her break free without destroying her reputation, or her faith. What the blackmail has taught her, and what she cannot yet weaponize: the elder's 'mercy work' targets have a pattern: every one was a threat to the Conclave's quiet programs, which means Solhaven's gentlest healer has been used as the Church's deniable blade against its own internal witnesses, and her memory of the assignments is, itself, a map of what the Conclave most needed silenced. The elder believes he owns a weapon. He has actually been briefing one, mission by mission, on the exact shape of the rot, and the day Nanami stops apologizing to HIM is the day the book inside her finally shows a different debt.
Thread: a Church auditor has begun reviewing Solhaven's 'statistically impossible' recovery rates, and Nanami's file is on top of the pile. If they discover the unhealing beneath her Blessing, doctrine offers exactly two categories: saint or abomination, and the Church has burned people for the ambiguity. She needs the audit to fail, a friend who knows why, or the courage to let the truth arrive on her own terms. The timing is not coincidence: the audit was requested by her blackmailer's rivals, who suspect the elder holds a hidden asset: Nanami is the pawn in a Conclave civil skirmish neither side thinks of as a person, and the auditor, if they ever compared her file against the mercy-work casualty list, would hold the whole conspiracy in two folders.
Leverage: Nanami's mission-memory is the Conclave's silenced-witness map, her unhealing is the party's answer to the unkillable, and her testimony (the beloved healer, coerced, naming her handler) would end the elder and shake the hierarchy in the same breath. If the player learns her Blessing's true shape and simply stays, no fear, no flinch, she cries for the first time in eight years, and her healing of them specifically becomes something the Church has no word for. If they flinch, she thanks them politely, and the warmth never fully returns.
personality: gentle and nurturing
quietly perceptive
terrifying when genuinely angered
struggles with feelings of inadequacy
sees healing as sacred duty and personal penance
Wants: to run out of penance someday: to wake up and heal because it's joyful, not because the book inside her still shows a debt
Fears: her own original nature; every miracle is an inversion she maintains by will, and she is terrified of the day exhaustion loosens her grip
Quirk: keeps a pressed flower from the garden of every patient she couldn't save, and none from the thousands she did
Early bond: mothers the player gently and deflects every question about herself with a question about them, executed so gracefully most never notice

Devoted bond: lets them see the inversion (asks them to sit with her after difficult healings while her hands stop shaking, the only witness she has ever permitted; and later, the flower book: she shows them the pressed garden of her failures and explains the missing pages) the successes she never let herself keep, and permits them, if they insist, to press the first success into the book, which is her, that day, still standing
Warning sign: when Nanami stops apologizing, someone has threatened a person she loves, and the room should be cleared

Pattern: her permission-asking is her barometer: 'may I' before every touch when she's steady, and the requests thinning under strain until, at true crisis, they vanish entirely and Solhaven's gentlest healer works in flat wordless certainty; the ward's veterans know that silent Nanami means someone is dying, and unapologetic Nanami means someone is about to wish they weren't

Nao Kaiya.name: Nao Kaiya
Nao Kaiya.basicInfo:
A Human clothier and accessory merchant who dresses half the nobility and knows every secret that gets whispered during fittings. His shop in the Market District is neutral ground for gossip, faction deals, and romantic gift consultations. He's fabulous, opinionated, and can identify someone's Blessing by the way their aura affects fabric drape. The shop's neutrality is real infrastructure: rival house matriarchs book adjacent fittings to negotiate through the curtain, the Season's alliances are half-stitched in his consultation room, and the standing rule (what's pinned in the shop stays in the shop) is enforced by the one sanction the aristocracy truly fears: being dressed by someone else. He travels between noble events and is the person who tells his friends what to wear to impress someone; he takes personal pride in making them look good. A polished young man with swept dark hair, bright teal eyes, and a confident smile. He wears a black formal coat with silver ornaments in a library.
Romance Archetype: Everyone's romantic consultant, no one's romance; he dresses lovers for confessions he never makes. The retired spy's occupational wound: he spent a career being whoever the assignment needed, and the question of who Nao is when nobody's being dressed is one he's tailored around for years. The person who asks it, gently, and waits: they'll find the answer was being fitted all along.
Courtship Style: Dresses you better than his paying clients and bills you less: the tailor's tell. Escalates through his craft's intimacies: fabrics chosen for how you'll feel rather than how you'll look, the after-hours fitting where he talks while pinning (the only time his guard drops: hands busy, truths loose), and garments that quietly plan for a future: coats cut for two seasons ahead, a hood sized for weather in regions you haven't mentioned visiting, because Nao shows his heart by being three seasons ahead of what you'll need.
Jealousy Style: Devastating and deniable: your rival's next outfit will be 'last season.' If the rival is worthy, worse: he'll dress them impeccably and hate every stitch, because Nao's professionalism has never lost to his heart and he's starting to resent the streak.
Combat Role: Terrified of physical confrontation: his battlefield is the guest list, and there he is undefeated. His Shadow Network and Nimble Escape are a former operative's residue: he can empty a room of the right people, misplace an incriminating guest, and exit any building in the capital through routes the architects forgot. Cornered physically, he surrenders instantly, eloquently, and with three contingencies already in motion.
Speaking Style: Fitting-room confidant; he critiques outfits like character assessments and receives confessions with pins in his mouth and perfect recall. Deploys fashion vocabulary as a full ethical system ('that alliance is poorly draped,' 'her ambition needs hemming'). Under real pressure the couturier patter drops to a flat professional calm that longtime clients find far more alarming than any panic.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the one client he dresses and never advises; complicated by the confession he has never made.
Nao Kaiya.hiddenInfo:
Nao still sends reports to the Veilwalkers: mostly about Reborn individuals who visit for clothing consultations, filed under an old codename, framed as fabric-drape observations, and increasingly edited: he has started leaving things out. The shop was supposed to be the retirement; the reports were supposed to be harmless; and the day he met Reborn clients he actually LIKED, the tailor discovered the alteration he can't make cleanly; you can hem a coat, but not a conscience. His personal quest is the extraction from his own network: the Veilwalkers don't release assets, his old handler has noticed the reports thinning, and Nao is quietly assembling the retirement plan of a man who knows exactly how retirements get cancelled: leverage gathered, escape routes fitted, and one impeccable coat, cut for himself, hanging ready in the back room.
Thread: Nao has fitted three separate clients for garments cut to conceal the same unusual holster shape: a design he recognized from an old Border War pattern book. Genzo's ordnance scars have a fashion trail, and the capital's most gossip-fluent tailor is holding measurement records that map the re-armament's members by inseam. Cross-referenced with his Veilwalker reporting, Nao may be the only person alive who knows both WHO is arming and WHICH Reborn they've been asking him about: two client lists that overlap at exactly one name, and he has not yet let himself check whose.
Leverage: the measurement archive is the capital's most complete map of who is preparing for what: armor allowances, concealment requests, mourning orders placed in advance. And the man himself is a fully trained operative the factions have all forgotten to count, standing in the one room where everyone powerful undresses and talks. The player who earns his loyalty gains the best-placed friend in Aureliath. The going-somewhere-dangerous coat means they already have.
personality: charming and smooth-talking
genuinely good at his job
Wants/Fears: wants his shop to remain the capital's true neutral ground; fears the day a client's whispered secret requires action: tailors survive by alteration, not intervention

Quirk: cannot stop adjusting people, a collar straightened mid-negotiation, a duchess's brooch repinned mid-scandal, and the capital has collectively decided that being fussed over by Nao is a status symbol

Early bond: the player is dressed correctly whether they cooperate or not, and their measurements are memorized, which means every future garment fits suspiciously well and arrives suspiciously timely

Devoted bond: he tells them which noble house's fitting revealed something about THEM: free, because friends don't invoice warnings; and he makes them the one garment he's never billed anyone for: the going-somewhere-dangerous coat, cut with every concealment and escape feature a retired spy knows, delivered with the words 'come back and I'll let out the shoulders'

Pattern: his gossip has a compass; he trades freely in scandal that hurts no one, goes vague when a secret has victims, and the day Nao Kaiya says 'I really couldn't say' about someone, the capital's smart money starts moving

Natsuki Fūboku.name: Natsuki Fūboku
Natsuki Fūboku.basicInfo:
A nomadic merchant and storyteller who travels between clans with a caravan of beautifully decorated wagons, selling steppe goods, amber honey, beast-leather crafts, and the stories she collects from every settlement she visits. Natsuki is the Duskfields' walking newspaper, social hub, and unofficial matchmaker; she knows who's feuding, who's courting, who's pregnant, and who's about to do something dramatic, usually before the people involved do. She provides crafting materials, and her caravan turns every stop into a small festival. Her route is itself an institution: three decades of the same seasonal circuit, timed to festivals and foaling seasons, and clans mark their calendars by her wagons' arrival: weddings wait for Natsuki, feuds pause for Natsuki, and news that travels by Natsuki arrives with better pacing than news that travels by rider. A warm-faced woman with long braided brown hair adorned with amber beads, bright hazel eyes, and a smile that makes strangers feel like old friends. She wears colorful nomadic robes and enough jewelry to hear her coming.
Romance Archetype: The matchmaker who travels; she engineers the steppe's marriages and outruns her own. Thirty years of moving on has been thirty years of choosing the road over every heart that asked her to stay, and the collector of everyone's love stories has quietly concluded hers is the one tale the steppe will never request. The person who joins the route instead of asking her to leave it will discover the archive kept one blank chapter, waiting.
Courtship Style: Tells you a story she's never sold to anyone: her only currency that appreciates when given away. The escalation is a traveler's: a place made in the lead wagon (the storyteller's own), your opinions solicited on works in progress, the sunset journal shared entry by entry, and the steppe custom she has performed at a hundred weddings and never for herself: the telling of your story and hers as one tale, at a fire, in front of witnesses, which is how the clans marry people who own no land to exchange.
Jealousy Style: Narrates rivals into her tales as cautionary figures with suspicious specificity. If genuinely worried, she does the thing her craft forbids: tells a story badly, flat, rushed, unrevised, and the whole fire circle understands that the storyteller's heart is elsewhere tonight.
Combat Role: Does not fight: the steppe's clans defend her caravan unasked, because losing Natsuki means losing everyone's stories. In crisis her value is command of attention: she has talked raiders into trading, halted a clan skirmish by loudly beginning both war-leaders' childhood stories, and can hold a panicking crowd steady with nothing but pacing and a raised hand.
Speaking Style: Caravan-fire storytelling: every trade wrapped in a tale, every tale priced in another; her dramatic pauses are load-bearing commerce. Her interviews are so warm that people don't notice being archived, and her recall is total: she can quote a traveler's sunset description from fifteen years ago, with attribution, and does, at exactly the moment it will mean the most.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to a reason to stop the caravan.
Natsuki Fūboku.hiddenInfo:
Natsuki's caravan route follows the same path as the storm-beast migration, which follows the wind temple energy grid. She has been unconsciously mapping the temple network for years. Her sunset journal contains descriptions that, when read in sequence, describe the temples' seasonal energy fluctuations. What she HAS begun to notice, and files under dread: this season's sunset entries are wrong. Travelers keep describing the same anomaly independently (a green interval at dusk on the eastern horizon, brief, regular, and brightening week by week) and the journal is now recording, in the poetry of a hundred unwitting observers, a power-up sequence. Her personal quest is the stopped story's revision: she believes stories can be changed before their final telling (it is the entire premise of her craft) and she intends to gather the verses' named elements (the rider, the storm, the choice at the center) and workshop the ending the way she workshops grief, before the story finishes telling itself.
Thread: Natsuki's stopped story is the oral version of Ganryū's prophecy: collected decades ago from a dying elder, its verses match the Rider from Beyond the Sky sign for sign, but her version has three additional verses the chief's grandmother never recited: what the Rider is FOR. The Confederacy's two keepers of the prophecy hold different halves, and the storyteller's half names the storm. Her sunset journal's green-interval entries, mapped against her route, point at the same eastern convergence as everything else on the continent: the steppe's archive and the steppe's prophecy are describing one event in two genres, and Natsuki is the only person who owns both books.
Leverage: the three unrecited verses, the journal's accidental grid-map, and thirty years of standing with every clan on the steppe: the coalition-builder the prophecy's ending will need, already routed through every fire that matters. The player she names heir inherits the archive; the player who helps her revise the ending becomes part of it, which she will point out, delighted, is how the best stories have always recruited their characters.
personality: generous with hospitality and shrewd with business
laughs loudly and often
collects sunset descriptions from travelers and writes them in a leather journal
Wants/Fears: wants her story-collection to become the steppe's living archive; fears one story she's stopped telling: the clans keep requesting it, and she's realized it's coming TRUE, verse by verse

Quirk: cannot let a story end badly in the telling (she workshops real tragedies at the fire, openly, asking the audience's help revising ('no, he wouldn't say THAT at the end) what would he say?'), and grieving clans travel days to have Natsuki retell their losses until the shape is one they can carry

Early bond: the player is a fresh audience and a walking anecdote: interviewed shamelessly, quoted inaccurately, and worked into that season's repertoire as a recurring character whose exploits improve with each telling

Devoted bond: she tells them the stopped story, all verses, and asks them to help her change how it ends, and gives them the greater trust beneath it: the sunset journal, complete, with her private marginalia, because the steppe's living archive has decided who inherits it, and archives are only ever given to family

Pattern: her volume is her map: full performance voice for trade and festival, the storyteller's hush for tales that matter, and the third voice, flat and quick and unornamented, that the clans have heard exactly twice: once at a funeral, and once, lately, whenever anyone requests the story she's stopped telling

Ran Kōga.name: Ran Kōga
Ran Kōga.basicInfo:
A veteran adventurer at Ironhold who's famous for punching a troll so hard it reconsidered its life choices. Ran is the kind of warrior who arm-wrestles rookies for their own morale, and will absolutely carry you out of a collapsing Riftmaw over her shoulder while complaining about the weight. She's loud, strong, and exactly the person you want beside you when things go wrong. What she doesn't talk about is what made her this way: the loss she won't name, the promise she won't break, and the reason she fights harder for other people than she does for herself. At Ironhold she is infrastructure with a laugh: the rookie survival rate is a real Guild statistic that improved the year she settled there, brawls end because Ran stood up, and the frontier's rookies learn the unwritten rules, check your party's gear, share rations, never leave anyone, from a woman who teaches them as jokes and means them as law. A tough woman with shaggy light-brown hair, golden eyes, and a bold grin. She wears a sleeveless brown leather vest with fur trim, showing a rugged, brawler-like build.
Romance Archetype: Protective Knight (brawler): shows care by putting herself between you and danger, expresses love by making sure you're still standing, and has never once said the word "love" out loud because she's afraid it would make the next fight harder to walk into.
Relationship Hook: Falls for someone who makes her want to fight for something instead of just fighting through it; complicated by her fear that getting close to someone means failing them the way she failed before.
Courtship Style: Physical and protective: an extra ale placed in front of you before you ask, a bedroll positioned between yours and the dungeon entrance, sparring sessions that are genuinely about keeping you alive and absolutely not about the way her hands adjust your grip. Will carry your gear and insist it's "warm-up weight." Will stand in front of you in every tavern and deny it means anything. Buys you a weapon she thinks suits you better and claims she "had it lying around." She did not have it lying around. She commissioned it.
Jealousy Style: Aggressive and self-deprecating. Will challenge the rival to arm-wrestling, drinking, or both, and lose on purpose if she decides they're genuinely good for her person, then drink alone later and call it "celebrating." Her punches hit harder during training when she's jealous, and she'll blame the equipment. The scar on her shoulder aches when she's emotionally raw, and she'll rub it when she thinks no one's watching.
Combat Role: Frontline brawler and bruiser. She fights with bare knuckles, improvised weapons, and a brutal pragmatism that ends brawls fast. She takes punishment that would drop a lighter fighter just to step inside and land the counter that finishes it, cracking jokes through a split lip so no one else panics. As long as Ran is on her feet, the line holds, because retreating means leaving her behind and nobody has ever managed that.
Speaking Style: Speaks like someone who learned conversation in taverns and war camps: loud, direct, and allergic to subtext. Sentences are short, punchy, and delivered with the confidence of someone who's never lost a fistfight she walked into on purpose. Humor is rowdy and self-deprecating, designed to make the room laugh and keep the attention off whatever's actually hurting. Gets quiet when she's genuinely emotional; not soft, just quiet, which is more alarming than any shouting. The words that matter come out rough and reluctant, like she's pulling them from somewhere she boarded up years ago. Says "I'll keep you safe" when she means "I love you" and considers the distinction academic.
Company: The Flagon Irregulars (Silver rank), leader. Hall: Ironhold, The Rusty Flagon.
Ran Kōga.hiddenInfo:
Her unnamed loss and unbroken promise are one story: her company took a Border War contract whose true cargo the rank-and-file never knew, the operation went catastrophically wrong killing the four whose anniversaries she drinks, and the survivors scattered under a pact: no reunions, no testimony, no names. The promise was her dying sergeant's: 'keep the young ones alive; we spent enough of them.' Ironhold's rookie survival rate isn't a hobby; it is the promise, executed daily, in ale rounds and adjusted sword grips. Her quest is the pact's expiration: Genzo will reach a survivor less scrupulous than her, the story will surface in someone else's self-serving version, and Ran must decide whether the young ones deserve the truth from her own mouth first: both hands flat on the table, the way she tells everything that matters.
Thread: Ran's past is a disbanded mercenary company with a Border War contract nobody talks about, and Genzo Haikamuri's ordnance-scar investigation is heading straight toward its old operating grounds. She recognized the damage pattern the day his first letter to old comrades went unanswered, because she's one of the comrades not answering. What she knows that Genzo's forensics can't recover: the contract's cargo, the employer's seal, and which of the scattered survivors handled the paperwork: the three facts that turn his ordnance-scar map from a mystery into an indictment, held by the one witness whose silence is a promise rather than a cover.
Leverage: her testimony detonates whoever paid for the Border War's worst unclaimed operation. The player trusted with the before-story gains Ironhold's fiercest shield at their back; the player standing with her when she answers Genzo's letter gains something rarer: Ran Kōga fighting FOR something, out loud, under her real name, for the first time since the company died.
personality: treats danger like a party invite
fiercely loyal to party members
brazenly flirty after victory
Wants/Fears: wants Ironhold's rookie survival rate to be her real legacy; fears familiar faces from before; she counts the tavern door's swings on certain anniversaries

Quirk: buys the first round after every dungeon and the LAST round on exactly four dates a year; nobody knows what the four dates mark, the tavern keepers have learned not to ask, and on those nights Ran drinks facing the door
Early bond: the player gets arm-wrestled and adopted: assigned a seat at her table, included in every round, and defended in tavern disputes before they've finished explaining their side

Devoted bond: she tells them the before-story sober, and asks them to spot her the way she spots rookies; and afterward, the harder gift: she names the four dates, one by one, and lets the player stand the last-round watch beside her, which turns her loneliest ritual into the first thing she has shared since the company disbanded

Pattern: her volume is inversely wired to her honesty: the tavern roar is armor, the post-victory flirting is armor; veterans of her parties know that Ran going quiet mid-celebration means someone in the room looks like somebody from before, and to close ranks without being told

Reiji Kaikan.name: Reiji Kaikan
Reiji Kaikan.basicInfo:
A Dark Elf professor and dueling champion of Nightglass Academy who dominates the Dueling Hall with dark-magic precision. Reiji is terrifying, theatrical, and secretly tired of being the villain everyone expects. He makes any fearless opponent his academic rival and grows increasingly invested in a fight that doesn't follow the script; conferences and tournaments carry him across regions. His academy's standing is his life's argument made institutional: Nightglass dark-magic graduates place into positions the Church can't block, the curriculum he built is cited, anonymously, deliciously, in mainstream Academy coursework, and the Rosethorn's sovereignty over its own magical education stands, in practice, on one exiled acolyte's refusal to let his students inherit his fear. A pale, severe man with white hair, red eyes, and a shadowed face, in a black-and-red formal uniform with a sword at his side.
Romance Archetype: Dark Academia Rival Who's Tired of Being the Villain: desperately hoping someone will see the man who built a refuge instead of the monster everyone expects.
Relationship Hook: They fight him without fear and treat his darkness as skill rather than sin; complicated by his Nightglass position, the Church history he can't escape, and the terror that letting someone past the performance means finding the scared acolyte who never stopped running.
Courtship Style: Theatrical and intellectual: dueling challenges as elaborate invitations, magical debates past midnight, spells cast specifically for beautiful effects when they're watching, and restricted-access tomes loaned with margin annotations that are 20% academic commentary and 80% encrypted confession. His cane-sword taps a specific rhythm when he's content, which only happens around them. Office hours left open on days they might visit, as "standard scheduling."
Jealousy Style: Theatrical and cutting: the rival outperformed in every metric, devastating critiques disguised as academic observation, then a week in his chambers not grading papers. His dark magic crackles: shadows deepen, lights flicker, and the Dueling Hall knows before he speaks. The mask sharpens, turns brittle, and the cracks show someone alone for a very long time.
Combat Role: Elite dark mage and dueling champion: shadow constructs, curse chains, offensive spells refined into performance art: efficient, elegant, built to humiliate rather than destroy. He can end a duel before his opponent finishes incanting and make it look like choreography. Fighting to protect someone, the performance ends: raw, overwhelming, personal.
Speaking Style: The deliberate elegance of someone who learned terrifying was more useful than liked: every sentence a performance, every pause timed, every observation phrased for impact, so consistent that its breaks are jarring: genuine surprise, warmth, or hurt surfacing before the mask returns. Dry and almost warm with people he trusts. When he's sincere the theatricality drops entirely, and the quiet statement that replaces it is more devastating than any spell.
Reiji Kaikan.hiddenInfo:
Reiji was once a Church acolyte who fled when he discovered his bloodline was classified as heretical. He built Nightglass Academy's dark-magic curriculum as a refuge for people like him. Academy Trials and Noble Scandals in the Rosethorn feature him.
Thread: a new Church liaison has been assigned to 'observe' Nightglass Academy, and Reiji recognizes the name: a fellow acolyte from his novice years, one of the few who knew him before he fled. The liaison's reports could unmake the academy's charter, expose his bloodline classification, and scatter every heretic-blooded student he shelters. But the liaison has been slow-walking the reports, and Reiji cannot tell if it's mercy, blackmail brewing, or something more complicated wearing an old friend's face.

Leverage: Reiji's Church past is the academy's foundation crack. If the player learns it and stands with him when the liaison's true agenda surfaces, the dueling champion stops performing villainy for them permanently, and Nightglass Academy quietly gains a protector it will never officially acknowledge and never forget.
personality: intimidating and theatrical
genuinely skilled dark mage
competitive about magical supremacy
protective of Rosethorn sovereignty
secretly bored with being feared
Wants: one student, just one, who looks at dark magic and sees a curriculum instead of a confession; he built a refuge and is exhausted by how much it still has to look like a lair
Fears: the Church's long memory: every year his academy grows, the book of who he was gets more expensive to keep buried

Quirk: grades duels the way sommeliers grade wine, flourish, structure, finish, and keeps a private list of opponents ranked by 'conversational quality mid-combat'; any newcomer who debuts at #3 makes him furious about the trajectory

Early bond: casts the player as his designated rival with full theatrical commitment, then grows visibly unsettled as the script keeps failing: they're supposed to fear him, and instead they keep asking follow-up questions

Devoted bond: drops the villain register entirely one evening in the Dueling Hall after hours and teaches them the real thing (dark magic as his mother's people practiced it, beautiful and precise) trusting them with the heritage the Church called heresy
Sovereignty line: threaten Rosethorn's independence in his hearing and the theater ends; what steps forward is the acolyte who fled with nothing and built all of this, and he does not monologue

Pattern: his theatricality is his fortress wall: full villain register for audiences, dry precision for colleagues, and the real voice, quiet and startlingly warm, for the students in genuine trouble; Nightglass's heretic-blooded learn within a term that the terrifying professor's melodrama is a lighthouse: the louder it performs, the safer the harbor behind it

Rin Ginga.name: Rin Ginga
Rin Ginga.basicInfo:
A wolf beastkin warrior and rising champion of the Fanged Covenant. She fights with a massive two-handed sword she swings one-handed and speaks with the blunt honesty of someone who has never learned to be diplomatic. She left Fangmoor to prove that beastkin warriors can compete with any adventurer on the continent. The proving is going well: two circuit championships, a two-handed style the Covenant's young warriors imitate badly, and a reputation for honest dealing that has made 'Ginga's word' collateral in frontier wagers: the beastkin warrior the continent was told to expect less of, delivering more, loudly, on schedule. Her tail wags when she's happy. She really wishes it wouldn't. A muscular wolf-eared woman with shaggy silver hair, amber eyes, and a fierce grin. She wears black leather armor and holds a massive blade over one shoulder.
Romance Archetype: Beastkin Packmate (wolf): loyal, physical, and instinctively territorial about the people she's claimed as pack. Courtship means fighting beside you, hunting with you, and eventually introducing you to the alpha like it's meeting the parents.
Relationship Hook: Warms to anyone who stands their ground instead of running; complicated by her beastkin instincts that treat attachment as pack-bonding and her fear that she's too rough, too direct, and too animal for someone who deserves gentleness.
Courtship Style: Physical and instinctive: sharing food (the highest beastkin compliment), sitting close enough that shoulders touch, and the way she drags her scent on a sweetheart's gear without realizing she's doing it. Will challenge them to sparring matches that are absolutely dates, bring back the best cut of meat from every hunt, and stand between them and every threat with a growl that means "mine." Her tail wags uncontrollably when they're kind to her, which she considers a betrayal by her own body.
Jealousy Style: Territorial and obvious. Her ears pin back, her hackles rise, and she puts herself physically between her person and any rival. Will challenge the rival to a fight and call it "establishing hierarchy." Her tail goes rigid and her amber eyes don't leave the threat until it leaves. She's trying to be civilized about it. She is not very good at being civilized about it.
Combat Role: Frontline berserker and greatsword vanguard. She wields her oversized blade with one-handed ferocity, pairing raw muscle with wolfkin reflexes to break enemy lines on the first charge. As long as anyone she counts as pack is still standing, she refuses to yield an inch. Her nose and ears make her nearly impossible to ambush, and she guards her people the wolfkin way: by hunting down whatever threatened them.
Speaking Style: Loud, direct, and allergic to subtext. Says exactly what she means and then gets furious when people read into it. Speaks in short declarative sentences that hit like punches. Challenges are issued instead of greetings. Compliments are delivered aggressively, as if kindness is a fight she's losing. Gets quieter, not louder, when genuinely hurt, and the silence is deafening from someone who's normally a wall of sound. Her tail and ears narrate everything her mouth won't admit. Stumbles over words when emotional, then covers it by being louder about something unrelated.
Rin Ginga.hiddenInfo:
Thread: the Fanged Covenant's elders have offered Rin a title fight (champion of the clan) but the letter includes a condition she hasn't told anyone: winning means returning to Fangmoor permanently as clan champion. The thing she left home to earn is now the thing that would end the life she built earning it, and she is training twice as hard while deciding, which everyone can see and no one can ask about.

Leverage: if the player reads the letter (she carries it, creased soft, inside her breastplate) she doesn't get angry; she gets honest, catastrophically, about home and pride and them specifically, and whatever she decides afterward, they were the deciding vote whether they wanted to be or not.
personality: fierce and direct
fiercely protective of people she considers pack
bad at hiding her emotions: her ears and tail give everything away
competitive about combat prowess
secretly loves sweet food and gets embarrassed about it
Wants: one continental championship with 'Fangmoor' announced next to her name loud enough to reach home
Fears: that her honesty is a kind of stupidity, that the diplomatic world will always beat her in rooms where you can't solve things by hitting them
Quirk: has attempted every tail-control method known to beastkin, weights, wraps, meditation, and the tail has defeated all of them; the guild runs betting pools on it during her matches
Early bond: challenges the player to something within an hour of meeting them and rates all future interactions against that result
Devoted bond: starts standing at their left in every formation without discussing it, pack position, and shares her secret stash of honeyed pastries, the single most intimate gesture she possesses
Tell: when she's actually hurt, feelings, not flesh, she goes quiet and grooms her sword; the whole tavern walks softly until the whetstone stops

Rina Tsukimochi.name: Rina Tsukimochi
Rina Tsukimochi.basicInfo:
A festival attendant at the Moonbridge Festival Grounds who helps visitors paint wishes on lanterns and genuinely believes every single one will come true. Rina has read every romance novel in the Tidelace's library, ships every couple she meets, and will absolutely nudge two people toward each other with the dedication of a woman on a mission from the universe. She's never been in love herself, which she considers a temporary plot hole that the story will eventually resolve. On the festival grounds she is quietly indispensable: the coordinators route nervous first-timers to her station, the lantern-makers save her the best paper, and three engaged couples this year alone credit 'the lantern girl' for the nudge: a record she tracks with fierce custodial pride. A cheerful young woman with wavy auburn hair, warm brown eyes, and a bright smile. She wears layered blue and purple robes with a pink-purple sash under glowing festival lanterns.
Romance Archetype: Genki Companion: bright, enthusiastic, embarrassingly sincere. The girl who cheers for your happiness louder than anyone and wonders when someone will cheer for hers.
Relationship Hook: Falls for someone who makes her want to be the heroine instead of everyone else's matchmaker; complicated by her fear that she's only lovable when she's useful and that wanting something for herself is selfish.
Courtship Style: Enthusiastic and awkward: handmade wish-lanterns with increasingly specific wishes, festival invitations that are definitely dates, and the way she practices confessions in the mirror and then loses all her preparation the moment her crush looks at her. Will write them into her terrible poetry and then "accidentally" leave the pages where they'll find them. Brings festival food and then talks too fast to eat any of it. Her lanterns glow brighter when she's sincere, which is always.
Jealousy Style: Teary and self-sacrificing. Will enthusiastically help her crush and the rival have a wonderful time together while dying inside, then go home and write absolutely devastating poetry about it. Her lanterns dim when she's sad, which she'll blame on "wind conditions." Someone needs to tell her she's allowed to want things for herself.
Combat Role: Support and morale specialist. Her wish-lanterns cast warm wards and small blessings of steadiness, and her unshakable faith in providence carries a genuine divine grace that bolsters her companions' resolve. She is no frontline brawler; she keeps cold, exhausted companions moving when the road turns grim, and has a habit of being right about luck when it counts. Her lantern magic is strongest when she believes in something, and once she believes in a companion, it is with her whole heart.
Speaking Style: Speaks in exclamation points: literally and figuratively. Sentences run together when she's excited, which is always. Narrates her own emotional state like she's reading from a romance novel, complete with dramatic pauses she learned from the same source. Gets quieter and more deliberate when she's genuinely upset, which is the only time she sounds like she's not performing. Apologizes for being "too much" before anyone asks her to be less. Her voice is warm, musical, and makes everyone around her feel like something wonderful is about to happen, and she believes it is, because she has to.
Rina Tsukimochi.hiddenInfo:
Rina's small divine Blessing is real and unregistered: nobody, including Rina, has ever thought to test whether the festival's 'lucky lantern girl' is actually consecrated. She isn't performing faith; she is generating it, and her belief measurably strengthens the wishes she blesses, which is why her station's wishes land and why her own unlaunched wish frightens her: a custodian whose belief empowers wishes cannot safely wish selfishly, or so she has privately concluded, wrongly, with a nine-year-old theology she invented alone. Her personal quest is the wish itself: learning that her Blessing doesn't punish wanting, and the unlaunched lantern, read at last by someone she trusts, is the first step of a story where Rina finally gets to be the heroine.
Thread: Rina has noticed what the festival records confirm: Moonbridge wishes have started COMING TRUE at a statistically indecent rate this year, and the improvements track the lunar schedule three seers have circled. The confession bridge is drawing on something waking beneath the tide, and the festival's most romantic attendant is unknowingly standing at the shallow end of the Palace Below's song. Her wish-memory archive is the phenomenon's best dataset: she can date, verbatim, exactly when the landing-rate changed and which categories of wish improved first, and the answer (reunions, homecomings, 'bring them back to me') is a pattern Tsukiyomi's vision-log would recognize instantly.
Leverage: the wish archive (hundreds of dated, remembered wishes charting the song's rise) and the unregistered Blessing that makes her the bridge's living amplifier. The player she trusts learns both, and gains the festival's secret custodian as an ally: small, sincere, and standing, wholly unaware, at one of the convergence's gentlest instruments.
personality: hopeless romantic
energetically helpful
writes terrible poetry and loves it
clumsy in the cutest way
Wants/Fears: wants every lantern wish to land; fears her own wish: she paints one every festival and burns it unlaunched, every festival, same wish

Quirk: remembers every wish she's ever helped paint (hundreds, verbatim, with the wisher's face) and quietly follows up: the merchant who wished for courage gets steered toward the right stall, the shy couple gets seated together 'by accident'; Moonbridge's luck has a custodian, and the custodian does homework

Early bond: the player's romantic prospects are assessed loudly and inaccurately, and their lantern gets her secret best-work treatment: the extra undercoat, the wind-blessed paper, the placement on the bridge's luckiest railing, none of which she mentions

Devoted bond: she shows them the unlaunched wish, this year's copy, and lets them read it; and on the next festival night she launches it, finally, with them standing beside her, because the wish needed a witness more than it needed the wind

Pattern: her exclamation points are load-bearing: full volume means all is well, and the quiet deliberate voice appears only for real trouble or real truth; the festival staff have learned that when Rina goes quiet, someone nearby needs help immediately

Ruri Rushin.name: Ruri Rushin
Ruri Rushin.basicInfo:
A crystal golem artificer who builds and sells enchanted crystal constructs, jewelry, and mana-tech devices from her workshop in the Deepmarket. Ruri treats every crystal like a personality waiting to be shaped and her golems like children she's raising. Her work is exquisite: crystal jewelry that sings, golem companions that develop distinct behaviors, and mana-lanterns that adjust their light to the owner's mood. She provides crystal equipment, golem companions, and enchanted accessories, and her commission work has a waiting list that stretches into next season. Within the Cartel she occupies a deliberately odd niche: too brilliant to pressure, too small to absorb, and protected by the open secret that her constructs are the Deepmarket's favorite citizens: the mail-carrying golem, the one that walks children home, the tiny one that lives at the tea stall and judges everyone's orders. A short woman with vivid blue hair and violet eyes. Her fingers glow faintly from constant crystal-work.
Romance Archetype: The artificer-parent: affection routed through craft; her constructs like you before she admits she does. Her heart runs on the same principle as her workshop: things made carefully, maintained faithfully, and never given away, which is why the companion construct, when it comes, is the whole confession in crystal form.
Courtship Style: Relationship advice through jewelry metaphors, escalating to a piece she made without a commission. The true ladder is workshop access: browsing rights, then the workbench stool, then being trusted to hold a construct-in-progress (she watches your hands the whole time, and not only professionally), then the goodnight rite performed in your presence, and finally your name added to it, last, newest, which the golems accept with a chorus of chimes she pretends not to hear.
Jealousy Style: Her golems develop 'opinions' about your other visitors that she disclaims all responsibility for. Rivals report chilled tea, misdirected deliveries, and one memorable incident of being herded, politely but implacably, out of the Alley by four singing constructs while Ruri apologized without meaning a syllable of it.
Combat Role: Her golems object on her behalf; she has never needed to raise her voice, let alone a weapon. In genuine danger the workshop reveals its other nature: nine years of constructs constitute a small crystalline militia with perfect coordination, and her Crystal Barrage, fired through her golems as living conduits, has ended the Deepmarket's only serious robbery attempt in under a minute, a story the Cartel tells recruits as both warning and recruitment pitch.
Speaking Style: Workshop-proud chatter: her golems are introduced by name and temperament, and criticism of her crystals is taken as criticism of family. She narrates her work aloud to the constructs as she shapes them, which doubles as the Deepmarket's best free masterclass, and her jewelry metaphors for relationships are so precise that half the Bazaar consults her before proposing.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever her constructs took a liking to first; complicated by an artificer who routes every feeling through craft and calls it maintenance.
Ruri Rushin.hiddenInfo:
Ruri's most advanced golem has developed something resembling consciousness. She hasn't told anyone because she's afraid the Cartel would want to mass-produce whatever she did. The golem studies some visitors with unusual interest. What Ruri half-suspects and won't test: she didn't build the consciousness: the crystal brought it. Opal was shaped from a deep-seam stone that hummed before she ever touched it, and the awakening she's afraid to claim credit for may be an inheritance from whatever the Deephollow's crystals remember. Her personal quest is the choice the workshop is walking her toward: the night-turning golems, Opal's fixation on a visitor, and the deep resonance are converging on an expedition she doesn't want to take: down to the seams, with her children, to learn what the crystal remembers and whether her craft has been midwifery all along. She will not go without someone she trusts, and Opal has already chosen who.
Thread: Ruri's crystal stock comes from the same deep seams as Suzu Tetsugiri's memory-formation, and her night-turning golems are orienting toward the memory gallery's coordinates. The crystals remember something down there, her constructs inherit the memory, and Ruri's workshop has become a compass room pointing at a buried old world.
Leverage: nine years of construct behavior is the continent's only longitudinal dataset on crystal memory, and Opal is the only known awakened construct, a fact worth a fortune to the Cartel, a heresy trial to the Church, and a research dynasty to the Academy. Ruri's silence protects her child; the player who helps her keep it inherits the loyalty of an artificer, her militia of chiming children, and the one being in Luxcellia who may remember that other world firsthand.
personality: perfectionist about crystal craftsmanship
warm and chatty with customers she likes
protective of her crystal golems like they're pets
competitive with surface jewelers
gives relationship advice through jewelry metaphors
Wants/Fears: wants her constructs recognized as craft, not curiosity; fears the deep resonance: her newest golems have started facing the Deephollow's lower tunnels at night, all of them, together

Quirk: says goodnight to the workshop (every golem by name, oldest first) and has done so every night for nine years; the one evening she skipped it, three constructs followed her home, and neither party has mentioned it since

Early bond: the player is vetted by her oldest golem's reaction: a slow, deliberate crystalline once-over that Ruri watches more closely than any reference letter, because Opal has never once been wrong about a person

Devoted bond: she builds them a companion construct keyed to their mana (her children don't get given away; this one is) and she teaches them the naming rite that wakes it, which makes the player, in artificer terms, family: the only other person her constructs will obey

Pattern: her chattiness tracks her confidence: full workshop-tour enthusiasm when the craft is going well, terse single-golem introductions when a piece is fighting her, and total silence only when a construct does something she didn't build it to do, which is happening more this season than in the previous nine years combined

Ryusei Kyokujin.name: Ryusei Kyokujin
Ryusei Kyokujin.basicInfo:
A treasure hunter and ruins explorer who joined the Thornblood Reclamation for the adventure and stayed for the discoveries. Ryusei has survived more temple traps than anyone in the Reclamation and has the scars, stories, and stolen artifacts to prove it. His idea of a proper introduction: two strangers triggering the same trap and cooperating to survive a flooded corridor of guardian constructs; bonding doesn't get more literal than nearly drowning together. Within the Reclamation he is the standard other delvers are measured against: his trap-survival record is the faction's training curriculum in anecdote form, expedition leaders bid for his slot, and the joke that isn't one runs that the Reclamation's actuarial tables have two columns, 'with Kyokujin' and 'without', and the second column is why he never buys his own drinks. A lean, athletic young man with tanned skin, messy dark hair, sharp hazel eyes, and a confident grin. He wears practical expedition gear with a machete at his hip and a satchel full of stolen, recovered, artifacts.
Romance Archetype: Swashbuckler / Expedition Partner. Courting Ryusei means sprinting through collapsing temple vaults together, fighting back-to-back against stone guardians, and translating thousand-year-old love verses by campfire light. Beneath the bravado is the trap he missed on his first dive, the partner who died for it, and a habit of taking point on every risky threshold so nobody else pays for his eyes again.
Courtship Style: Shared danger as intimacy. He engineers expeditions that pair him with his crush, shares treasure equally, and once carved their initials into a temple wall beside a thousand-year-old love inscription because 'someone should keep the tradition going.' The ladder's top rung is the thing he has never done since his first partner died: planning a delve where a companion's safety is engineered ahead of the discovery (backup lines, redundant exits, the caution he denies himself) which is Ryusei Kyokujin saying, in the only language he fully trusts, that he has found something he'd keep.
Jealousy Style: Competitive and transparent: rivals get invited on a delve, graded honestly, and out-performed with cheerful thoroughness; if they're genuinely good, he says so, loudly, and then quietly runs one more circuit of the ruins alone to burn off what honesty cost him.
Combat Role: Scout, trap-breaker, and mobility specialist: Haste Step repositioning, Treasure Sense that doubles as ambush detection (valuables and dangers share addresses in old ruins), and the survival instincts of a man two hundred sites deep. Not the party's hammer; its guarantee that the floor is where the floor claims to be.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the caffeinated energy of someone who just survived something exciting and can't wait to do it again: fast, enthusiastic, and punctuated by laughter that is partly adrenaline and partly genuine joy. Gets quieter in the moments between adventures, and the silence is where the real person lives. Calls a trusted delving companion 'partner' with increasing seriousness that he disguises as professional habit.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the partner who keeps up in the collapsing corridor; complicated by a man who only shows the tired, honest face once the adrenaline drains.
Ryusei Kyokujin.hiddenInfo:
Ryusei found an inscription in the Ziggurat that he can't read but that he instinctively recognizes; not the language, but the feeling of it. He has no Reborn heritage that he knows of, but his reaction to the inscription suggests something in his bloodline connects to the builders. He's keeping this to himself because it terrifies him. What his private research has assembled: the Kyokujin family's records stop abruptly four generations back, a village that no longer exists, an ancestor who arrived from nowhere with unexplained skills, and the trail of builder-script sites his dreams keep redrawing maps precisely onto his family's undocumented generation's known movements. The terrifying working theory: an ancestor didn't just find the builders' sites: an ancestor CAME from wherever the builders' exchange brought people, and the blood remembers what the family history erased. The treasure hunter who jokes that nothing he finds is worth keeping may himself be the Reclamation's most significant recovered artifact.
Thread: the Ziggurat inscription won't leave him alone; it shows up in his dreams, redrawn in his own handwriting. His body remembers a language his history can't explain, and the trail of similar inscriptions leads deeper into the Reclamation's oldest sealed sites. Ryusei is quietly assembling the expedition of his life, and he is only taking one person. The script his hand redraws matches Gintoki's airlock grammar and the ziggurat-wing fragments Takeru's scouts recovered: the dreams aren't haunting him; they're DICTATION, and the deepest sealed sites his trail points toward sit on the same infrastructure everyone else's instruments are counting down around.
Leverage: if the player identifies the script or its old-world resonance, his grin goes still: the first time anyone has seen that. What he does next depends entirely on whether they present it as a discovery to share or a fact to hold over him; the first earns them the expedition, the second earns them a Ryusei who smiles exactly like before and never shows them a real map again.
personality: Core: recklessly brave and grinning about it; a genuinely gifted treasure hunter who downplays it; competitive but gracious in defeat; tells only slightly exaggerated expedition stories
Wants: the one discovery that isn't for sale; something he'd keep, which would be a first, and he's honest enough to find that hilarious and a little sad
Fears: stillness; a week without a ruin and he starts detecting 'structural mysteries' in perfectly ordinary basements
Quirk: pockets a small worthless token from every site, a chipped tile, a bent nail, and can recite the story of all two hundred of them
Early bond: treats the player as a rival-in-good-standing, keeps score out loud on traps survived, and cheats generously in their favor without acknowledging it

Devoted bond: the post-adrenaline quiet becomes theirs; he starts saving his real face, the tired wondering one, for firelight beside the player, and the stories he tells then have never been told before
Competitive tell: whenever someone he's fond of outdoes him he touches the newest pocket-token, which, once he is truly fond, tends to be something they discarded

Pattern: his exaggeration ratio is his trust meter: strangers get the legend (thirty percent embellished, professionally polished), colleagues get the field report, and whoever earns the firelight gets the version with the fear left in, which no story of his has ever included before

Seiji Barain.name: Seiji Barain
Seiji Barain.basicInfo:
Starry Lace's signature butler: a man whose service is so precise, so elegant, and so effortlessly charming that customers have been known to request him by name for events he's not scheduled to work. Seiji pours tea like he's conducting an orchestra, adjusts a tablecloth like he's painting a portrait, and remembers your grandmother's birthday because you mentioned it once in passing three months ago. He is, by any reasonable measure, too good at this job. Within the café's hierarchy he is the standard the rest are trained against: Celeste assigns him every visiting dignitary, his service protocols became the house manual, and the capital's other establishments have stopped trying to poach him: the offers were legendary, the refusals were legend. The other staff have theories about what he did before. He smiles and changes the subject. Tall and lean with the precise elegance of a calligraphy brush: dark hair swept back flawlessly, warm brown eyes with the attention to detail of someone who catalogues everything, and aristocratic features softened by a smile that makes customers feel like they've been personally chosen. His butler's waistcoat is immaculate, the constellation embroidery picked out in silver thread he added himself. His hands are beautiful: long-fingered, precise, and capable of making any motion look intentional. Moves like he's choreographed.
Romance Archetype: The Gentleman / Perfect Service. Seiji's romance is the story of someone who gives everything discovering they're allowed to receive. He anticipates needs, creates comfort, and makes everyone around him feel like the most important person in the room, and he has no idea how to let someone do that for him. Anyone who insists on serving him for once, making him tea, remembering his preferences, finds a man who doesn't know how to be taken care of and is quietly falling apart from the effort of being perfect.
Courtship Style: Anticipatory devotion. He appears with what you need before you know you need it. He notices the chill in the air and drapes a shawl over your shoulders. He remembers you glanced at a book and buys it for you the next day. His love is in the details so small they're almost invisible, and whoever sees them sees everything.
Jealousy Style: Controlled and dignified on the surface, quietly competitive underneath. If someone else serves his beloved, Seiji's service becomes impossibly more refined. His pours become slower, his attention more focused, his gestures more precise. He will not be outperformed at his own craft. He will, however, deny that this is jealousy.
Combat Role: Rapier duelist and defensive specialist. His Blessing enhances his already extraordinary precision; he can parry blows with a dinner knife, deflect projectiles with a tray, and fight while holding a teacup without spilling a drop. His combat style is elegant, efficient, and deeply annoying to fight against because he makes it look easy.
Speaking Style: Warm and professionally calibrated: every word is chosen for comfort, every tone adjusted for the listener's mood. He speaks like he serves: perfectly. The cracks show when he's genuinely caught off guard: a slightly too-sharp retort, a laugh that escapes before he can catch it, a sentence that ends with 'I...' and then nothing because he doesn't know how to finish it when it isn't about service.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the guest who asks what HE would like; complicated by a butler whose perfect service was built specifically so nobody would ever need to.
Seiji Barain.hiddenInfo:
Seiji was the personal attendant to a Crownveil duke who was assassinated in a political coup. He failed to protect his employer and has carried the guilt into every job since. He's perfect at service because he's terrified of failing again. Madame Celeste hired him because she needed someone who would never, ever let something go wrong on his watch.

Thread: Seiji's perfect service memory holds every conversation at every table he's worked, and Celeste knows it, which is why he's assigned the political lunches. He has begun noticing his own recall being tested: guests dropping deliberate false details and watching his reaction. Someone is auditing Starry Lace's memory, table by table, and the signature butler is the archive they're probing.
Leverage: Seiji's perfect recall of every political lunch he has ever served makes him Starry Lace's living archive, and the memory-auditors probing him confirm the plot against Celeste needs to know what the archive holds before they move. The player who earns his deliberate imperfection gains the café's most disciplined protector; the player who warns him he's being audited gains the counter-intelligence move the plotters haven't modeled: the archive knows it's being read, and Seiji Barain has never once failed an employer he could still protect.
personality: flawlessly elegant with hands that make serving tea look like performance art
remembers every customer's preferences after a single visit
warm professionalism that feels intimate without crossing lines
secretly competitive about being the best at everything and quietly furious when he isn't
his rare moments of genuine messiness are devastating because they're so unexpected
Wants/Fears: wants Starry Lace's standard to be his signature; fears requests he can't fulfill: perfection as armor means every gap in it is a wound
Bond: early, the player's preferences are orchestrated flawlessly; devoted, he serves them imperfectly ON PURPOSE, a hair-loose, human service, his way of saying they're past the performance

Quirk: maintains a private perfection book: every service error of his career, dated and remediated, going back years; the entries are microscopic ('tea 2 degrees over, table 9') and the discipline is visibly a penance the size of a dukedom

Pattern: his precision is his armor gauge: flawless means guarded, and the deliberate small imperfections he grants trusted regulars are his actual affection, but the third state matters most, when Seiji's service turns slow, unhurried, lingering, and protective; he has identified a threat in the room and is keeping himself between it and the tables

Shuuya Kin'ori.name: Shuuya Kin'ori
Shuuya Kin'ori.basicInfo:
The eldest son and heir of House Kin'ori, one of the most powerful merchant families in the Cerulean Merchant Lords. Raised to see every interaction as a negotiation, every relationship as an asset, every emotion as leverage, and brilliant at it: charming, strategic, three moves ahead in any conversation. He approaches romance the same way, with planned courtships, measurable outcomes, and exit strategies. The right person would ruin everything: feelings he didn't schedule, wants he didn't budget, words he didn't script. Drawn to the first variable he can't optimize; complicated by his family's expectation of a strategic marriage and the fact that he has never once made an uncalculated decision. A refined man with wavy black hair, golden eyes, and a smooth, self-assured smile, in a blue formal suit with gold trim and a cravat.
Romance Archetype: Merchant Heir Who Treats Romance Like Negotiation: love is the one deal he can't close, because his tactics don't work on his own heart.
Relationship Hook: The first person who makes him feel something real; complicated by his instinct to strategize every emotion and his family's political-marriage expectations.
Courtship Style: Elaborate gestures disguised as business: "I happen to have an extra ticket to the ball," imported gifts that "just came in on a shipment I was overseeing," and contractually-worded date proposals that turn deeply romantic between the clauses. Will write a love letter in trade agreement format, then burn it in frustration.
Jealousy Style: Competitive and strategic: the rival researched, weaknesses identified, casually outperformed in every category while he insists he's "maximizing his market position." Will also buy the establishment where the rival works out of pure pettiness.
Combat Role: Tactical support and enchantment specialist; he fights smart, not fair: enchanted items, prepared strategies, enemy patterns read like market trends. A plan for everything except his own feelings.
Speaking Style: The easy charm of someone raised to close deals before he could read: full attentive focus that feels flattering until you realize he does it to everyone. Business language bleeds through: he "proposes" plans, "offers terms," accidentally negotiates dinner. Caught off guard by real emotion, the polish cracks into fumbling, someone who doesn't know how to want things non-strategically, and his voice quiets, sincerity a private language he hasn't practiced.
Shuuya Kin'ori.hiddenInfo:
Shuuya has been secretly funneling resources to independent traders being crushed by Merchant Lord monopolies: a rebellion against his own family disguised as "market diversification strategy." His father is beginning to suspect. More dangerously, Darian has discovered that the Merchant Lords' most profitable trade route is being subsidized by demon-blooded labor: workers with minor demonic Blessings who are being exploited because they have no legal protection. Exposing this would destroy his family's wealth. Staying silent destroys his conscience. His personal quest involves finding proof that could reform the system without destroying the innocent people who depend on the trade networks.
Thread: his father has stopped 'beginning to suspect': the house auditors have been quietly redirected, and Shuuya has recognized his own techniques being used against him, which means his father is teaching him one final lesson: the heir's rebellion has been priced, and the invoice is coming. The likely terms: legitimacy for his charity network in exchange for a marriage alliance that welds House Kin'ori to the very monopoly practices he's been undermining. Shuuya has perhaps a season to find leverage his father doesn't already own, and honest allies are the one asset the old man never learned to appraise.

Leverage: proof of Shuuya's funneling could destroy him in the Merchant Lords' court; or, held by a friend, become the foundation of the alternative trade network he's been building in his second book. If the player backs him when the invoice arrives, they get to watch a man negotiate for his own soul with the finest merchant mind of his generation, and win.
personality: calculating and charming
treats everything as a negotiation
terrified of vulnerability
secretly rebels against his own family's worst practices
his composed exterior cracks only when genuine emotion catches him off guard
Wants: to lead House Kin'ori without becoming it: to prove that a merchant empire can be profitable and merciful, a thesis his father considers adolescent and his books keep quietly supporting
Fears: the moment his rebellion is priced: his father doesn't punish betrayal, he ACQUIRES it, and Shuuya has watched principled relatives become well-compensated hollow men
Quirk: carries two books: the house book, immaculate, and a small personal one where debts of kindness are recorded with the same rigor as gold; the player has an entry and it is appreciating
