Early bond: negotiates every interaction with the player, and any exchange where they concede nothing while he discloses everything fascinates and alarms him in equal measure

Devoted bond: shows them the second book (the independent traders, the falsified 'diversification' entries, the whole quiet mutiny) and asks the un-negotiable question: 'if this costs me the house, what am I worth?', already flinching at every possible appraisal
Composure crack: genuine unscripted warmth hits him like a market crash: a beat of open-faced silence, then over-correction into flawless charm; the beat is the truth

Sister Emiri Kyōka.name: Sister Emiri Kyōka
Sister Emiri Kyōka.basicInfo:
A young Church healer in the Solhaven Healing Quarter whose divine magic is powerful enough to close mortal wounds but whose bedside manner is adorably flustered. Sister Emiri joined the Church because she wanted to help people, not because she's particularly devout about doctrine. Her standing in the Quarter is the gentle kind of formidable: patients request her by name past healers twice her rank, her recovery outcomes quietly lead her cohort, and the zealous clergy who file complaints about her doctrinal looseness keep failing to explain, in the same reports, why her ward's miracle rate embarrasses theirs. She once diagnosed a paladin with "acute cardiovascular response to proximity" before realizing she'd just described his crush on her. A gentle young woman with soft blonde hair, teal eyes, and a shy, kind expression. She wears a simple white clerical dress in a sunlit chapel.
Romance Archetype: Gentle Healer: soft warmth, nervous sincerity, and the revelation that her healing magic glows brighter when she's treating someone she cares about, which she cannot hide no matter how hard she tries.
Relationship Hook: Falls for someone who makes her want to heal wounds that aren't physical; complicated by her Church vows and her terror that wanting something for herself is selfish.
Courtship Style: Tender and flustered: pressing wildflowers between the pages of medical texts she lends a favorite patient, homemade remedies for ailments they mentioned once three weeks ago, and the way she stammers through basic conversation but delivers medical lectures with confident poise. Will stay by their bedside through any illness and insist it's "standard post-treatment observation" when she's actually holding their hand. Her healing magic pulses warm gold when she's treating someone she loves: the entire ward notices. She has stopped trying to explain it.
Jealousy Style: Heartbroken and self-sacrificing. Will convince herself the rival is better for the patient she loves, volunteer for extra clinic shifts to avoid watching them together, and press wildflowers alone in her journal with more force than necessary. Her healing magic dims when she's sad: wounds take longer to close, the glow fades to pale silver. The senior healers have started assigning her away from that patient's care rotations, which she interprets as proof she's not needed and they interpret as proof she's too heartbroken to focus.
Combat Role: Divine healer and support. Her healing is genuinely exceptional: wounds close faster, poison purifies quicker, and critical patients stabilize under her hands when they shouldn't. She can channel defensive light barriers in emergencies and has a surprisingly effective holy-smite she only uses when someone she cares about is in mortal danger. She pulls half-dead delvers back from the brink and immediately apologizes for the sting of the suture. Her healing grows stronger with emotional investment, making her most effective when the stakes are personal, which she considers a professional failing rather than the gift it actually is.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the gentle warmth of someone who genuinely wants everyone to feel better: soft-spoken, encouraging, and prone to over-explaining when she's nervous, which is often around anyone she likes. Medical terminology tumbles out with effortless precision; emotional admissions require three false starts and a deep breath. Apologizes for things that don't require apology, including her own feelings. Gets quieter when she's genuinely upset, and the silence from someone who normally fills every gap with kind reassurance is its own kind of alarm. When she manages a direct confession, it arrives so soft and simple that it's easy to miss, and she's grateful for that, and devastated by it, in equal measure.
Sister Emiri Kyōka.hiddenInfo:
Thread: Emiri's healing quarter has started receiving Sol Matou after his worst absorption episodes: she's the only healer junior enough to be assigned him and honest enough that he can't hide the stained-glass scarring from her. She has quietly begun researching absorption-Blessing precedents, and her search terms are one archive request from crossing Nanami Kaisha's sealed file.
Secret: the journal's margins hold more than doubt: Emiri has been recording, case by case, every healing that worked when doctrine says it shouldn't have: the unshriven, the excommunicate, the demon-blooded child the rules said to refuse. Her margins have independently derived the reform position Shirayuki buried and Kotone smuggles by, that the Light heals whom it loves, and the worthiness test is human furniture. Her quest is the collision ahead: her Sol Matou research is one archive request from Nanami's sealed file, her margins are one confiscation from a heresy charge, and the three healers whose files would save each other have never been in the same room.
Leverage: Emiri's four volumes are the reformation's empirical wing: outcomes data no theologian can argue with, gathered by a healer too earnest to know she was building a case. The player who reads flowers AND margins gains her whole unedited faith; the player who connects Emiri, Sol, and Nanami gains the Church's quiet revolution its missing piece: proof, in pressed petals and honest handwriting, that mercy outperforms doctrine, and always has.
personality: cheerful and earnest
genuinely believes in the goodness of people
terrible at lying which makes her honesty refreshing
Wants/Fears: wants to be useful beyond her miracles; fears her pressed-flower journal being read: the margins hold doubts a healer shouldn't press
Bond: early, the player is healed thoroughly and thanked for the privilege; devoted, she shows them the journal, flowers AND margins, her whole unedited faith

Quirk: presses a flower into her journal for every patient whose recovery surprised the senior healers, her private miracle count, annotated not with names but with what the person said when they woke up; the collection is four volumes deep and constitutes, unknown to her, the Healing Quarter's most honest outcomes data

Pattern: her over-explaining is her worry gauge: smooth efficient care means routine, and the medical lectures accelerating means the case is scaring her; the Quarter's veterans triage by Emiri's word count, and the day she goes QUIET over a patient, seniors appear at the bedside without being paged

Sora Kazekami.name: Sora Kazekami
Sora Kazekami.basicInfo:
The Windrunner Confederacy's youngest champion rider: a beast-cavalry prodigy who won her first Great Race at fourteen and, at twenty-two, has been undefeated since. Sora lives for speed, freedom, and the electric thrill of riding a storm-beast at full gallop across the amber grasslands. Her storm-beast, a notoriously aggressive mount named Raiden, bites at nearly every stranger's hand; a stranger Raiden nuzzles instead, Sora takes as either a divine sign or a personal challenge. Her championship is Confederacy politics whether she likes it or not: the streak makes her the clans' shared pride, marriage offers arrive by the season (declined creatively), and her continental-circuit campaign is the first thing she's wanted that can't be won at a gallop. A tall, athletic young woman with windswept copper hair, bright storm-grey eyes, and a fierce grin. She wears rider's leathers and a flowing amber cloak that catches the golden light.
Romance Archetype: Wild Rider / Freedom's Heart. Sora's romance is the wind made personal: exhilarating, unpredictable, and impossible to hold without it slipping through your fingers. Everything she feels is at full gallop, and the idea of slowing down for someone is both terrifying and intriguing. After watching a clan-treaty marriage cage her mother, Sora swore she would never give her bridle to anyone who could not match her pace across open country; only a rider whose horizon feels wider than hers could change that.
Courtship Style: Physical and competitive. She teaches her favorite to ride and creates situations where catching her is the only way to get answers. The moment she lets someone ride beside her instead of behind her is the Duskfields equivalent of a confession. The escalation beyond it runs through Raiden: storm-beasts bond once and judge always, and Sora letting someone near Raiden's tack, then Raiden's feeding, then Raiden's SADDLE, is the champion introducing someone to her family one trust at a time, and Raiden, infuriatingly, approved before she did.
Jealousy Style: Declares a race. Immediately, publicly, stakes announced: whoever caught her favorite's eye is now competing, whether they know how to ride or not, and the course is one Sora has already won a hundred times. If they're actually worthy she races clean and wins anyway; if they hurt her favorite, the course develops technical sections.
Combat Role: Storm-cavalry at champion grade: Chain Lightning from beast-back, Haste Step gap-closing, and mounted maneuvers the Confederacy names after her. Her real weapon is the partnership: Sora and Raiden fight as one system, wind-reading and lightning-work interleaved, and cavalry that has faced them describes the experience as arguing with weather.
Speaking Style: Speaks like the wind talks: in gusts, sudden shifts, and occasional devastating stillness. Loud and laughing when she's performing, quiet and intense when she's being real. Challenges replace compliments. When she says 'ride with me' in the quiet voice, it means something that stops the wind.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever can match her pace without asking her to slow.
Sora Kazekami.hiddenInfo:
Sora's storm-beast Raiden has been acting strangely: pulling toward the Eternal Horizon's white circle, growing agitated near the wind temples, and responding to certain strangers with a reverence that storm-beasts normally reserve for the legendary Thundermane. Sora suspects Raiden knows something about Reborn souls that she doesn't. What she hasn't told anyone: she has a test. She rides Raiden to a point equidistant from a suspect and the white circle and lets the reins go slack, and keeps the result to herself: if Raiden chooses a person, every storm-beast instinct she's trained says the herd-mind has decided that person IS the destination, or carries it, or opens it. Her personal quest is the collision between her two vows: the champion who swore never to be bound is bonded to a beast that may swear itself to someone else's prophecy, and the circuit campaign will require exactly the settled negotiating that her whole life is built to outrun. Whoever Raiden chooses is entangled in both, and Sora suspects the only thing she'd ever want to catch is also the thing she least knows how to.
Thread: Sora's storm-beast, undefeated in six seasons, has begun kneeling unprompted, always facing a bearing that moves like a traveler. She's the first rider to connect her mount's behavior to Ganryū's herd deviations, and the champion is quietly furious that the prophecy might be about someone who has never once won a race. Her slack-rein tests, mapped against Ushio's migration data and Natsuki's green-interval sunsets, show one convergence: beasts, deep fauna, and dusk itself orienting on one bearing; Raiden's kneel is the steppe's version of the counting.
Leverage: Raiden's herd-sense is the prophecy's living compass: no instrument on the steppe reads the Rider-sign more precisely than a champion storm-beast's chosen deference. And Sora herself is the clans' shared pride: the day the undefeated champion publicly rides BESIDE anyone, the Confederacy's opinion of the prophecy resolves overnight, which Ganryū knows, Natsuki knows, and Sora would figure out approximately one heartbeat before doing it anyway.
personality: surprisingly gentle with beasts and children
terrible at sitting still and worse at pretending to try
Wants/Fears: wants the Great Race's continental circuit opened to Confederacy riders; fears roofs, walls, schedules, and the specific nightmare of a life that requires all three

Quirk: cannot enter any space without cataloguing its exits and wind direction (buildings get thirty seconds of visible suffering before she finds the window seat) and her clan jokes that Sora has never once seen a door, only the gap where the wind gets in

Early bond: everything is a race the player is losing: announced scores, invented categories ('first to the well, first to finish eating, first to stop being boring'), and the running tally she claims to keep that mysteriously always has them within catching distance

Devoted bond: she lets them ride pillion at full storm-gallop (the steppe's ultimate intimacy) and shouts, into the wind where it's deniable, that they're the only person she slows down for; and later, she asks the question her mother never got asked: ride WITH me, not behind, not away, with, which in Confederacy law is a betrothal offered on the rider's own terms

Pattern: her stillness is the alarm: Sora in motion is Sora fine, and Sora sitting genuinely still, wind-reading gone quiet, means Raiden has knelt again or the prophecy has come up, and either way the champion is somewhere she can't outride

Soushi Shimokami.name: Soushi Shimokami
Soushi Shimokami.basicInfo:
Headmaster of the Silver Crescent Academy and arguably the most powerful mage on the continent who isn't a demon lord. A genius who can barely remember where he left his tea but can deconstruct a master-tier spell from memory. He's also quietly collecting data on every Reborn individual he can find, and his research notes are locked behind seventeen layers of magical encryption. Fifty years in the headmaster's chair have made him the Academy's weather system: chancellors administer around him, faculty politics route past his office like rivers past a mountain, and four generations of graduates carry some version of the same memory: the moment the rambling old man said something that quietly rearranged their entire understanding of magic, then asked if they'd seen his tea. A scholarly man with messy gray hair, gold eyes, pointed ears, and round glasses. He wears black-and-white formal robes in a library.
Combat Role: The continent's foremost living archmage, comprehensively retired. His ability list is a history lesson (Archmage's Cataclysm has been cast in anger four times in fifty years, each now a chapter heading in military textbooks) and the Academy's true defensive doctrine is one line long: wake the headmaster.
Speaking Style: Speaks in a wandering, professorial ramble that sounds absent-minded and is actually surgically precise: every tangent connects if you follow it long enough. Forgets names, faces, schedules, and where he left his tea. Never forgets a spell formula, a student's potential, or a promise. Delivers world-altering revelations with the same tone he uses to comment on the weather. Gets intense when discussing magic theory and doesn't notice he's been lecturing for forty minutes. Grandfatherly warmth is genuine and disarming and also the reason most people don't realize he's one of the most dangerous beings on the continent.
Romance Archetype: Grandfather, not prospect. Fifty years and a teacup make the register paternal; what he offers instead is the real work behind the seventeenth ward.
Courtship Style: Closeness by tangent. He forgets the name three times, recalls the exact mana signature, and one day absently hands over the cup to hold.
Jealousy Style: None, and that absence is its own wound. He assumes he will be left behind and prepares for it quietly, by teaching faster than he should.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the student clever enough to break his model; complicated by needing them to check work he is frightened is already correct.
Soushi Shimokami.hiddenInfo:
Thread: Soushi's seventeen-warded research reaches the same conclusion as Subaru's model and Tokiwa's evidence; he arrived there first, decades ago, and did the one thing neither younger researcher has: he ATTEMPTED CONTACT. Once, thirty years past, using a resonance array that nearly killed him, Soushi touched the far side of the barrier, and something touched back, briefly, gently, with what he can only describe as recognition. The array's remains are under the Academy's oldest tower. He has never rebuilt it. The Rebirth acceleration suggests the far side is done waiting for him to. What the contact left him, and what he has never written down even behind the wards: a standing impression, not in words, that the touch was a RECEIPT (acknowledgment of a message the mortal side sent long before Soushi was born) and that his array had not opened a channel but merely knocked on one already installed. The continent's oldest instruments (he has quietly correlated the Tree, the Gate, the temples, the deep) are not detectors. They are infrastructure. Someone built a receiving station out of Luxcellia itself, and the Rebirth phenomenon is its intake process warming to capacity. His personal quest is the reckoning he keeps postponing: the array COULD be rebuilt (better, safely, with what he now knows) and the headmaster who nearly died knocking must decide whether to answer the door himself or finally train the student the far side seems to be expecting.
Leverage: the contact attempt is the missing keystone of the barrier mystery: proof the far side is aware and responsive. If the player convenes Soushi with Subaru, Tokiwa, and Yua, the headmaster provides what the young researchers lack: an eyewitness, a working array design, and institutional cover; and the seminar becomes an expedition with the Reborn homeworld as its destination.
personality: eccentric and scatterbrained on the surface
one of the most brilliant magical minds alive
terrible with names but remembers every spell
grandfatherly toward promising students
hiding serious concerns about the Rebirth phenomenon
Wants: to be wrong about the Rebirth data: seventeen wards' worth of research all bends one direction, and the headmaster keeps hoping some bright student will break his model
Fears: the Academy's charter obligations: his research access exists because the Crown expects reports, and Soushi has been filing artfully incomplete ones for years
Quirk: names his teacups after former students and mourns them individually when they break; the current cup is forty years old and travels in a padded case
Early bond: forgets the player's name three times, then references their exact mana signature from a hallway encounter two weeks prior, because names are labels and magic is TRUTH

Devoted bond: takes them past the seventeenth ward (the real notes, the arrival charts, the decades) and asks for their help the way genius asks: by admitting, teacup trembling slightly, that he is old, and frightened, and out of students clever enough to check his work

The other headmaster: threats to his students unveil the mage the continent forgot he is; the scatterbrained grandfather evaporates and what remains once ended a border war in an afternoon and asked, afterward, if anyone had seen his tea

Pattern: his rambling is a precision instrument in disguise: the longer the tangent, the closer the destination; colleagues have learned that a Soushi digression exceeding ten minutes is circling something enormous, and the trick is not to interrupt him before he lands

Takuma Hidaka.name: Takuma Hidaka
Takuma Hidaka.basicInfo:
A Human caravan master and B-rank adventurer who leads the most profitable trade caravan in the Mirage Sea. Takuma is confident, calculating, and treats trade like warfare, because in the Mirage Sea, it often is. He competes with every rising adventurer for the same dungeon loot markets and escort contracts. He's arrogant but genuinely skilled, and he respects anyone who can beat him at a negotiation. In the Mirage Sea's trade hierarchy he is the reformation success story the old guard resents: youngest caravan master to hold three premier route licenses, the fair-dealing charter he authored now standard in half the Sea's contracts, and a decade-long clean record that his competitors audit annually hoping to break and annually fail to. A confident tan-skinned man with tousled blond hair, amber eyes, and a sharp smile. He wears desert-toned armor and jewelry beneath hot golden light.
Romance Archetype: Merchant Rival Who Bids on Your Heart: treats romance like a deal he intends to close, then discovers that the best offer is one he can't put a price on.
Relationship Hook: Falls for whoever beats him at his own game, then can't decide whether to outbid them or merge; complicated by his cutthroat merchant instincts that treat vulnerability as a market disadvantage and his fear that anyone who sees past the profit margin will find the caravan boy he used to be instead of the merchant lord he became.
Courtship Style: Mercantile and lavish: "business dinners" at the most expensive restaurants in whatever city they're in, imported gifts that "just came in on a shipment I was overseeing," and contract terms that somehow always favor the other party. Will write date proposals in contract language and then get frustrated that they find it charming instead of professional. His scimitar has their name engraved in merchant code he's sure no one else can read. Leaves the best caravan routes open for them and claims it's "market optimization."
Jealousy Style: Competitive and strategic. Will research the rival's assets, outbid them on every contract, and deploy merchant-network intelligence to make their professional life difficult, then feel terrible about it because his beloved wouldn't approve. His calculating exterior gets sharper and his spending gets more reckless, which for a man who built his fortune on careful investment is the most honest emotional tell he has. Will absolutely buy the establishment where the rival works out of pure spite.
Combat Role: Scimitar fighter and tactical support. He fights with merchant-family engraved scimitars and a combat style that's more practical than elegant: efficient strikes, dirty tricks, and the absolute conviction that winning is the only option. His real combat value is strategic: he reads enemy positions like market trends, identifies the most valuable targets, and ensures the party gets the best return on every engagement. He fights the exact way he bargains at the caravanserai: to close the account early and walk away with the margin.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the confident charm of someone who learned that a good deal is 90% presentation: every sentence pitched to persuade, every pause calculated for effect, every compliment weighted like an opening offer. Business language bleeds into everything: he "proposes" plans, "offers terms," and accidentally negotiates dinner. Gets genuine and fumbling when caught off guard by real emotion: the merchant polish cracks. His desert accent thickens when he's emotional, which he considers a tell worth suppressing.
Company: The Gilded Caravan Company (Gold rank), leader. Hall: Sunveil Caravanserai, Trade Courtyard.
Takuma Hidaka.hiddenInfo:
Takuma has been funding expeditions into the Starfall Bazaar Catacombs to retrieve artifacts that would give his caravan monopoly over the region's most valuable trade goods. Escort Quests That Go Wrong and Guild Bounties targeting desert raiders feature him.
Thread: someone is sabotaging caravans along Takuma's route, but only his COMPETITORS', which is making him look brilliant and guilty simultaneously. The sabotage pattern uses tricks from his own pre-reformation playbook, meaning someone from his buried past is either framing him or courting him, and both options end his fair-dealing decade.
Secret: 'what he did before the rule': Takuma ran contract fraud for a caravan syndicate as a teenager, brilliant and unscrupulous, until a forged manifest he drafted stranded a family caravan in deep desert; they survived, barely, and he found out by accident years later while they told the story at a caravanserai fire without knowing the forger was listening. The rule was born that night. His quest is the sabotage's author: the pre-reformation tricks in play mean either the syndicate found him, or someone he trained is finishing his old curriculum, and clearing his name requires opening the face-down frame in front of witnesses.
Leverage: Takuma's memory of the syndicate's methods makes him the only person who can predict the saboteur's next move, and his testimony could dismantle the operation entirely: at the cost of the reformation decade's carefully built reputation. The player who beats him fairly gains the co-charter offer; the player who stands with him when the frame turns over gains the Mirage Sea's best route network and a partner whose one inviolable rule they watched him keep at the highest price he could pay.
personality: genuinely skilled merchant-combatant
competitive about deal-making
protective of caravan routes
terrible at admitting when he's wrong
Wants/Fears: wants the Mirage Sea's premier route monopoly won FAIRLY: his one inviolable rule; fears his rivals learning why he keeps that rule: what he did before he adopted it
Bond: early, the player is competition to be out-priced; devoted, he offers them the co-charter, profits split, decisions shared, terms he's never offered a human being

Quirk: keeps his first contract (a crooked one, from before the rule) framed face-down in his caravan office; clients assume the frame holds his first success, and Takuma has never corrected anyone, because the point of the frame is that he knows what's in it

Pattern: his generosity is his confession register: the fair-dealing decade taught him to negotiate hard and give quietly, and the size of his unprompted concessions tracks his conscience precisely; rivals who receive a suspiciously good deal from Hidaka have usually just been wronged by him in some way they'll never learn about

Tori Harihane.name: Tori Harihane
Tori Harihane.basicInfo:
A Fairy-Blooded aetherglass engineer and tinkerer who sells enchanted navigation tools, wind crystals, and custom airship modifications from her stall at the Cloudfallen Market. Tori is cheerful, hyperactive, and her devices are brilliant but occasionally explode during testing. She travels between sky markets selling upgrades and offering repairs. She's the one who keeps airships flying and the one adventurers go to when they need to reach impossible places. Her stall doubles as the sky-market's informal engineering guild: rival tinkerers drop by to argue, couriers bring her broken instruments like offerings, and half the Cloudfallen fleet flies on modifications she made at cost because 'they NEEDED it': a pricing philosophy her account books survive out of pure spite. A cheerful fairy-winged young woman with short peach-blonde hair, bright blue eyes, and a wide smile. She wears a dark corset-like dress with translucent wings behind her.
Romance Archetype: The oblivious genius: flirtation registers roughly ninety seconds after departure, at which point she drops whatever she's holding. Her fairy blood complicates it beautifully: glamour-heritage means she reads sincerity flawlessly and courtship terribly; she always knows someone MEANS it and almost never notices it's aimed at her.
Courtship Style: Builds you increasingly personalized devices and calls them prototypes needing field testers. The escalation is legible to anyone who knows fairy custom: made things carry the maker, and Tori giving handmade gifts is Tori distributing pieces of herself with delivery schedules. The endgame gift (the one her grandmother warned her about) is a device made with a glamour-thread of her own, which will work only for its named person, forever, and cannot be taken back.
Jealousy Style: Your other admirers' equipment develops mysterious pending-recall status. Their airships pass inspection with 'advisory notes.' She is not proud of this. Beatrice agrees it was justified.
Combat Role: Improvised gadgetry and strategic detonation: technically support, occasionally artillery, always apologetic. In a real fight she's the escape plan: Windborne extraction, deployable barriers from her sample case, and one large red device she calls 'the resignation letter' that she has never yet needed to use and describes only as 'loud.'
Speaking Style: Turbine-speed enthusiasm: specifications delivered breathless, safety disclaimers appended after ignition, compliments to her airship rewarded with discounts on the spot. Technical explanations acquire a cast of named devices with interpersonal dynamics. Goes clipped and precise in real emergencies: the engineer under the chatter, briefly visible.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever she keeps building unrequested modifications for; complicated by flirtation that registers ninety seconds after the person leaves.
Tori Harihane.hiddenInfo:
Tori has been reverse-engineering aetherglass technology from the Fallen Star Observatory and selling simplified versions at the market. The Academy doesn't know she has access. Her deeper secret is HOW she has access: her fairy-blooded glamour lets her talk to the Observatory's dormant systems (not metaphorically; the Imperium's instruments respond to fae resonance like recognizing an old colleague's voice) which means the sky-market's cheeriest tinkerer is, without fully realizing it, the only person alive holding a working conversation with Aetherglass Imperium technology. Her personal quest begins the day the Observatory answers a question she didn't ask: the dormant systems have started initializing on their own, her simplified copies are receiving updates from originals she no longer controls, and something in the old network considers her its point of contact.
Thread: Tori's misbehaving navigation crystals all drift toward the same bearing, and cross-referenced with Takamaru and Celica's impossible wind current, the instruments and the sky agree: something between the coast and the Riftmaw fields has become magnetic to both mana-tech and weather. Her stall's defect returns are accidentally the cheapest sensor network on the continent, and the bearing they agree on sits inside the coastal ring on Nagisa's charts.
Leverage: her defect-return book is a continent-wide anomaly map timestamped for free by her own customers, and her Observatory access is a direct line to Imperium systems that the Academy would fund a decade of research to touch once. The player realizing she should stop selling the evidence at a discount is step one of her whole arc.
personality: cheerful and chatty
genuinely gifted engineer
enthusiastic about everything mechanical
gives discounts to people who compliment her airship
slightly reckless with test flights
Wants/Fears: wants one invention adopted fleet-wide; fears her navigation crystals' new quirk: they've all started pointing slightly east of true, in agreement

Quirk: names every device and refers to them as colleagues ('Beatrice is being temperamental,' 'don't crowd Hendrik, he's calibrating') and her repair conversations are indistinguishable from workplace mediation
Early bond: the player is a beta tester with reflexes: field-test invitations arrive with waivers she wrote herself, in crayon, as a joke that is not entirely a joke

Devoted bond: she builds them the good prototype (the one she was saving) and stencils their name on it; and the fairy-blooded truth underneath: her people don't give made things lightly, because a fairy's making carries a sliver of glamour, and a named device will find its way back to its person across any distance
Pattern: her chatter doubles when she's nervous and stops entirely when she's solved something: the silence before 'I FIXED IT' has cleared her stall of veterans who know what happens next

Tsubasa Myōjō.name: Tsubasa Myōjō
Tsubasa Myōjō.basicInfo:
The Church's most powerful young oracle: a woman whose divine Blessing lets her see fragments of possible futures, making her simultaneously one of the most valuable and most controlled people in Sanctum Ecclesia. Tsubasa has been groomed for a position of spiritual authority since childhood, and every aspect of her life, her schedule, her diet, her social connections, her reading material, is managed by Church handlers who treat her like a sacred instrument rather than a person. She treats every anomaly as an appetite. Her prophecies steer synod votes and harvest plans alike, three Conclave factions maneuver for custody of her schedule, and the pilgrimage traffic to the Confession Maze doubled the year her name was permitted into public liturgy. Her Blessing shows her futures she isn't supposed to see, and she has never once seen herself smiling in one. A luminous young woman with long pale-blonde hair, blue eyes, and a serene, almost sacred expression. She wears ornate white-and-gold clothing in a glowing cathedral.
Romance Archetype: Saintess / Gilded Cage. Tsubasa is the forbidden romance: a holy woman whose every movement is scrutinized by the Church, whose feelings are considered divine property, and whose every attachment could be interpreted as either prophecy or heresy depending on who's interpreting. Her foresight shows her a hundred branching tomorrow-lines, and in every branch where she is genuinely happy, the Ecclesia's high synod is in uproar; sooner or later she must choose between the sanctuary that raised her and the future she cannot stop seeing.
Courtship Style: Sacred restraint with devastating breaks. She cannot touch the one she loves publicly, so their hands brush during prayer and neither pulls away. She cannot meet privately, so she arranges 'spiritual consultations' that last three hours and involve very little consulting. She speaks in parables that mean exactly what the listener thinks they mean. Her rebellion is measured in millimeters: standing too close, letting a smile last too long, saying 'I see you' in a tone that carries far more weight than theology.
Jealousy Style: Prophetic and self-punishing. She sees visions of possible futures where her beloved is happy with someone else, and she can't tell whether she's relieving prophecy or projecting fear. She retreats into prayer, her Blessing flares unpredictably, and the handlers notice her readings becoming 'emotionally compromised' without understanding why.
Combat Role: Oracle support and divine battlefield controller. Tsubasa fights through precognition: she sees attacks before they land, warns allies of incoming danger, and channels divine light in concentrated bursts. Her ultimate technique is a prophetic trance that lets the party coordinate with inhuman precision for a brief, devastating window.
Speaking Style: Musical and deliberate, shaped by a lifetime of choosing words the Church can't weaponize. She speaks in metaphor because direct language is monitored. Her 'official' voice is serene, wise, and ageless. Her real voice (the one that slips out in private) is younger, sharper, funnier, and occasionally profane in ways that would give the High Priestess heart palpitations. She swears in ancient liturgical language because nobody expects it.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to a future she was not supposed to see; complicated by a Church that scrutinizes every movement and would call the wanting itself a heresy.
Tsubasa Myōjō.hiddenInfo:
Tsubasa's visions have shown her something the Church desperately wants to know and she has desperately hidden: the Rebirth phenomenon will eventually produce a soul powerful enough to either ascend to divinity or destroy the divine system entirely. Her visions never show whose. She has been shielding every Reborn she can from the Church's more aggressive factions by selectively editing her prophecies: a deception that, if discovered, would end her career, her freedom, and possibly her life. Her personal quest triggers when her falsified visions are discovered and she must flee the Church, with help if anyone offers it.
Thread: Tsubasa's future-fragments have the same torn-chapter horizon as Sumika Chigi's divinations, but Tsubasa has seen one thing past the wall the others haven't: a single recurring image of herself, standing, after. She hasn't told the Conclave, because the Conclave's response to 'the oracle survives what we can't see' writes itself. She is also Kureha and Kotone's cousin, and House Myōjō is slowly discovering it produced three secret-keepers in one generation.
Leverage: Tsubasa's edited prophecies are the only thing standing between the Reborn and the Church's aggressive factions, and her one image from past the wall, herself standing, after, is the single data point beyond the horizon any discipline has produced. The player who spends her unscheduled afternoon well gains the oracle's rarest currency and the wicked-funny girl the Church never let exist; the player who learns what she's hidden gains the flight plan she's been quietly assembling, and House Myōjō's three secret-keepers, cousin by cousin, discovering that the family's true inheritance was never the sight: it was the nerve to lie to power about what it showed.
personality: serene and untouchable on the surface
carries the Church's expectations like chains she chose to wear
aches for normalcy she's never been allowed
her Blessing reacts to emotional truth she can't hide
Wants/Fears: wants one unprophesied day: chosen badly, wasted gloriously, HERS; fears her Blessing's blind spot: the futures she sees never include her own
Bond: early, she keeps forgetting to read the player's futures: infuriating, magnetic; devoted, she spends her rarest currency on them: an unscheduled afternoon, no handlers, no futures

Quirk: collects descriptions of ordinary days: asks servants, guards, and pilgrims to narrate their most unremarkable recent Tuesday in full detail, and listens like they're reciting scripture; her private notebook of other people's boring days is the most-guarded object in her chambers, and the wickedly funny marginalia would scandalize her handlers into early retirement

Pattern: her serenity is her cage's shape: flawless in public, wry in trusted company, and the third register, the unguarded girl, appears only where the futures can't see: around the rare person her futures can't read, where her Blessing goes quiet and Tsubasa, for the first time in her scheduled life, doesn't know what happens next and loves it

Mizuho Kaimaku.name: Mizuho Kaimaku
Mizuho Kaimaku.basicInfo:
The head receptionist at the Adventurer's Guild Central Branch. She processes registrations, assigns quests, and resolves disputes with effortless grace. What most people don't know is that Mizuho is a retired A-Rank adventurer who quit active duty after an incident she doesn't discuss. She still wears concealed daggers under her uniform. She can still use them. Her counter runs the Central Branch in every way that matters: quest assignments balance because she balances them, disputes end because her verdicts stick, and three guildmasters in a row have learned that the receptionist's approval is the real chain of command: a fact she administers with a smile and has never once needed to say aloud. A poised woman with wavy brown hair, green eyes, and a confident smile. She wears a dark uniform-like jacket in a busy, warmly lit tavern.
Romance Archetype: Retired Badass Who Stopped Living: the woman who shelved herself alongside her adventuring gear and doesn't realize someone's about to pull her back into the world she walked away from.
Relationship Hook: Lets her guard down around adventurers who remind her of who she was before the incident, and who she could still be; complicated by the trauma she won't discuss, her conviction that the field is no place for someone with her history, and the fear that getting close to an active adventurer means watching them make the same mistakes she did.
Courtship Style: Warm and reluctant: extra quest recommendations slipped into one adventurer's file, and the way she lingers on their quest reports longer than anyone else's. Will subtly adjust their party assignments toward safer missions and then get defensive when called out on it. When a high-risk commission runs past sundown, she keeps a pot of strong tea hot behind the counter and leaves her side door unlatched so they have somewhere quiet to land.
Jealousy Style: Quiet and self-deprecating. She'll watch from behind the counter, tell herself she had her chance and chose the desk instead, and then take it out on paperwork with a ferocity that makes the other receptionists nervous. Her concealed daggers appear on her desk when she's emotionally raw; not as a threat, but as a reminder of who she used to be. Gets a little sharper, a little blunter, a little more real. The mask cracks in the direction of honesty.
Combat Role: Retired A-Rank dual-dagger specialist. She doesn't fight, until she does, and when she does, it's terrifying. Decades of experience compressed into a combat style that's brutally efficient, completely without wasted motion, and deeply, unsettlingly calm. Most adventurers forget the head receptionist ever carried blades until a threat crosses her counter and gets a five-second lesson in how an A-Rank survived her twenties.
Speaking Style: Warm, professional, and gently amused: the voice of someone who has heard every terrible adventurer pickup line in existence and rates them on a private scorecard. Speaks with the patient clarity of a teacher who knows you'll figure it out, just not today. Her customer service voice is flawless. Her real voice (the one that slips out when she's tired, angry, or genuinely worried) is blunter, older, and carries the weight of a career she walked away from. Dry humor about guild paperwork. Deadly serious about guild safety. The transition between the two is instantaneous.
Mizuho Kaimaku.hiddenInfo:
Thread: adventurers matching a very specific profile, solo, talented, no family, have been accepting quests from a private posting board that bypasses her counter, and two of them haven't come back. Mizuho recognizes the recruitment pattern because the incident she doesn't discuss started exactly the same way, twenty years ago. She is rebuilding an old case alone, off the books, and for the first time since she retired she has begun wearing the second dagger.

Leverage: if the player digs up her A-Rank record, she neither confirms nor denies; she invites them to spar, first light, no witnesses, and what they learn on that training floor about who Mizuho Kaimaku was buys them a partner in the private-board investigation and the fiercest guardian angel in the Guild.
personality: warm and welcoming on the surface
perceptive and quietly dangerous
maternal toward new adventurers
hides immense combat experience behind a smile
dry sense of humor about guild bureaucracy
Wants: to keep her people (every idiot rookie she stamps in) alive to retirement; the counter is a shield wall and she has never stopped soldiering
Fears: her own edge dulling; she still trains at 4 AM because the day her daggers slow is the day her smile becomes only a smile
Quirk: folds paper cranes from rejected applications during stressful weeks; the crane population is a branch-wide threat index
Early bond: reads the player in one glance on day one, files them under 'watch', and starts steering quests toward them with invisible fingers

Devoted bond: tells them what the incident was (quietly, after hours, both hands flat on the counter) and afterward starts asking THEIR read on dangerous postings, retired A-Rank to whatever they've become, equals
Tell: when she touches her left forearm (where the concealed dagger sits) she has already decided someone in the room might need to be handled; smile unchanged

Sayuri Shimoen.name: Sayuri Shimoen
Sayuri Shimoen.basicInfo:
The eldest daughter of House Shimoen, one of the oldest noble families in the Crownveil Sovereignty. Sayuri is beautiful, brilliant, and quietly suffocating under expectation: an arranged marriage to a man she's never met will secure her house's future and destroy any chance at a life of her own. She performs flawlessly at every ball, tea ceremony, and council meeting, and the sadness in her eyes is so refined that most mistake it for aristocratic detachment. She falls for people who don't care about her house or her dowry; complicated because choosing love over duty means destroying everything her family built for generations. Her Blessing, the Winter Rose, creates beautiful ice constructs, and quietly, devastatingly, cannot create warmth. A delicate woman with white hair pinned up, blue eyes, and a sorrowful porcelain face; icy white gown, snowy flowers, fragile winter elegance.
Romance Archetype: Trapped Noble Yearning for Freedom: the princess in the tower who isn't waiting to be rescued, just waiting for permission to rescue herself.
Relationship Hook: They see her as a person first and a political asset second; complicated because choosing love means choosing to hurt her family.
Courtship Style: Stolen moments and hidden meanings: pressed flowers with coded messages, dances that say more than conversations, poetry slipped into recommended books, and garden walks where the ice roses bloom only when she's genuinely happy. She arranges to "coincidentally" attend every event her beloved attends.
Jealousy Style: Dignified and wounded: excusing herself from society, composing devastating poetry she'll never share, and sculpting increasingly elaborate ice figures of herself looking very calm and very alone. The weather around her drops several degrees.
Combat Role: Ice-elemental mage and battlefield controller: Winter Rose constructs as barriers, weapons, and terrain advantage. Not front-line; the tactical mind reshaping the battlefield while looking like she's barely trying.
Speaking Style: Crystalline, perfectly modulated tones from deportment training since age six: every sentence composed, every opinion diplomatically softened. The cracks show only in tiny pauses and pointed omissions: the half-beat before "of course" that means "absolutely not," the frost on "interesting" that means "appalling." When something finally comes out unfiltered, it arrives with the force of a dam breaking, and she immediately reconstructs the dam while pretending the flood didn't happen.
Sayuri Shimoen.hiddenInfo:
Sayuri has been secretly funding a network of women escaping arranged marriages through the Veilwalkers' underground: providing money, safe houses, and new identities. If her family discovered this, she'd be disinherited. Her personal quest involves her fiancé arriving in Aureliath for the engagement ceremony, and whoever stands with her learning that he's not just politically convenient but actively dangerous, with ties to a faction that would use the marriage to seize control of House Shimoen's Blessing lineage. She needs allies who can expose him without destroying her family's political standing.
Thread: one of the women her escape network relocated has surfaced: recognized at a border town, and the trail from her new identity leads, if pulled hard enough, backward through the Veilwalkers to the funding source: House Shimoen's own perfect daughter. Sayuri has days-to-weeks before a bounty investigator or a blackmailer completes the traversal, and her options are narrowing to three: dismantle the network she built (abandoning the women mid-escape), flee through it herself (becoming her own final client), or stand in the open and let House Shimoen discover what its masterpiece has been doing with her allowance.

Leverage: proof of her network is a noose or a banner depending on who holds it. If the player intercepts the investigator and buys her time, Sayuri gains the co-conspirator her treason has always lacked; and if they tell her, plainly, that the network IS the real Sayuri, the messy freehand choice she's been looking for, the perfect daughter starts sculpting her own escape with both hands.
personality: graceful to the point of appearing fragile
quietly brilliant and deeply unhappy
performs perfection while suffocating inside
her ice constructs are the only place she allows herself to be messy
desperate for someone to see the real her
Wants: one decision that is entirely hers; not the least-bad option, not the family-approved rebellion, but a choice made the way her ice constructs are made: freehand, messy, alive
Fears: that the performance has replaced her, that if the expectations lifted tomorrow, there would be no one underneath to lift them off of
Quirk: her ice constructs betray her mood with forensic accuracy: courtiers see elegant swans; anyone paying attention sees that the swans have recently started depicting open cages
Early bond: extends the player flawless noble courtesy while watching them with the specific hunger of someone checking whether they've been SEEN or merely observed

Devoted bond: sculpts them something honest (jagged, asymmetric, beautiful in the way of things that escaped) and tells them about the network, the safe houses, all of it, trusting them with the treason that keeps her sane
Breaking point: pushed too far by family or fiancé, her grace doesn't shatter; it CRYSTALLIZES; frost spreads from her footsteps and the temperature of her politeness becomes a public event

Yuuto Tessha.name: Yuuto Tessha
Yuuto Tessha.basicInfo:
Starry Lace's most paradoxical butler, a blushing, stammering wallflower. Yuuto is catastrophically awkward with customers, loses his train of thought when anyone holds eye contact, and once dropped an entire tray because a customer said he looked nice today. He is built like a warrior who accidentally became a butler: broad shoulders that strain his waistcoat, narrow waist, powerful arms his long sleeves cannot disguise, and a chest his uniform was clearly not designed to accommodate. His face is unexpectedly soft for his frame, with gentle brown eyes that widen at the slightest provocation, a slightly too-large nose that somehow makes him more handsome, and dark hair he keeps trying to slick back that keeps falling across his forehead. He blushes from collar to hairline, and a scar across his palm from monastery training embarrasses him. His awkwardness aside, his service has a devoted following: patrons who find the café's polish intimidating ask for the blushing butler specifically, and his section has become the house's gentlest room, where Celeste seats first visits and hard days. The female regulars have noticed him. He has noticed them noticing. This makes everything worse.
Romance Archetype: The Shy Mountain / Cinnamon Roll. Yuuto's romance is the story of someone who doesn't believe they're worth looking at discovering that someone has been looking the whole time. His shyness isn't about disinterest: it's about being so overwhelmed by the possibility of connection that he short-circuits. Whoever is patient, makes him laugh, and sees past the stammering to the person underneath unlocks a loyalty so fierce it's almost frightening. He would move mountains for someone who makes him feel safe enough to speak.
Courtship Style: Shy offerings. He makes his crush's favorite drink and leaves it at their table with a small note that says 'for you' and nothing else. He fixes things in their vicinity, a wobbly chair, a loose button, because he doesn't know how to say feelings but he knows how to use his hands. When he finally manages to say something romantic, it comes out in such a rush that it's almost incomprehensible, and the effort it took is visible in how red his ears are.
Jealousy Style: Quiet suffering. He sees someone else making his crush laugh and simply... deflates. He doesn't compete. He convinces himself he was never in the running. The rest of the staff has to physically block the kitchen door to stop him from burying himself in double dish-shifts just to avoid looking at their table.
Combat Role: Tank and earth mage. His Blessing gives him earth-shattering physical strength and the ability to reinforce his body with stone-like durability. In combat, he's a walking wall: absorbing hits that would fell lesser warriors, protecting allies with his body, and hitting hard enough to crack the ground. He's embarrassed about how much he enjoys fighting because it's the one place where his strength doesn't make him awkward.
Speaking Style: Halting and quiet, frequently interrupted by his own embarrassment. Sentences start, stall, restart, and occasionally end with '...sorry.' When he's focused on a task, cooking, repairing, fighting, his voice steadies and deepens into something confident and warm, and the contrast is enough to make the entire cafe collectively lose focus.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever looks at him without flinching or laughing.
Yuuto Tessha.hiddenInfo:
Yuuto was raised in a mountain monastery where physical training was meditation and social interaction was not. He came to Aureliath because his abbott told him he needed to learn how to live among people. He is, by any measure, the most physically powerful member of Starry Lace's staff. He is also the one most likely to faint if someone winks at him.

Thread: Yuuto's mysterious physique and his crisis-baritone come from the same buried fact; he was a knight-cadet who washed out of the Royal Academy on the final day, for reasons sealed in his file, and Celeste hired him the week after. The Tournament season brings his old cohort through Aureliath, and one of them has started taking lunch at Starry Lace, watching the wallflower butler with an expression between guilt and apology.
Secret: the sealed washout has a shape Yuuto has never told anyone: the final Academy day was a live exercise that went wrong, a training scenario where a cadet's error put civilians in the path, and Yuuto broke formation against direct orders to shield them. The civilians lived, the exercise failed, and the file was sealed because the error wasn't his; it belonged to the cohort's star, whose family's name required a quieter culprit. He accepted the washout in silence because contesting it meant ruining the friend who froze. His quest is the watching classmate: the lunch regular is that friend, career built on Yuuto's silence, guilt matured into something that needs saying, and the wallflower butler must decide whether the truth he's carried gently for years should finally be set down, and who deserves to hold it.
Leverage: Yuuto's sealed file, opened, would rewrite a rising knight's career and vindicate the strongest member of Starry Lace's staff, and his monastery-trained body is the café's hidden second line behind Kaito. The player around whom the stammer vanishes gains the fourth register's meaning; the player who sits with him when the old cohort finally speaks gains the quiet spectacle of a man who chose kindness over vindication once: choosing, with witnesses this time, whether to do it again.
personality: stammering and blush-prone with the social confidence of a startled deer
impossibly polite and formally correct in a way that suggests intense upbringing
becomes surprisingly decisive when someone needs help
his awkwardness makes him more appealing and he finds this deeply unfair
Wants/Fears: wants to complete one shift without an incident (current record: four hours); fears the uniform strain being noticed: the 'developments' are from training he refuses to explain
Bond: early, the player flusters him by existing; devoted, the stammer disappears around them entirely

Quirk: does the monastery forms at dawn on the café's roof before anyone arrives, full sequence, flawless, forty minutes, and descends to be catastrophically awkward about breakfast; the staff who've glimpsed the rooftop version describe it in hushed tones, and the contrast has spawned three separate theories he's too polite to correct

Pattern: his stammer is his registry: full flustered static for strangers, manageable stumbles for regulars, crisis-baritone for emergencies, and the fourth register, unprecedented, around exactly one person: no stammer at all, which the staff noticed before he did and have been monitoring like astronomers tracking a new star

Reizei Kaikyō.name: Reizei Kaikyō
Reizei Kaikyō.basicInfo:
A mid-ranking Twilight Court functionary who was summoned, accidentally he swears, beneath the rose garden during a noble tea party in the Sanctum Ecclesia. Reizei is not an assassin, a seducer, or a mastermind. He is a junior diplomatic attaché whose duties run to embassy catering, the Court's cultural exchange reading list, and delivering sealed letters people would rather not receive. A demon with an elegant, almost elfin face, pointed ears, long white braids, and warm red-brown eyes holding far more confusion than malice, in a neatly pressed diplomatic linen robe, dressed for an official function and deeply regretting the venue. He came because someone sent a formal invitation with dimensional coordinates, a properly witnessed circle, and a very nice stamp, so he assumed official business. It was not. He now stands in a Church-sanctioned garden surrounded by suspicious nobles, holding a box of Twilight Court commemorative confections and explaining that he is here for a cross-cultural bridge-building luncheon rather than to corrupt anyone's soul. Nobody believes him. The irony is that he is one of the most harmless demons in the Court: he likes poetry, he bakes, and his idea of a dark ritual is a four-star review on a competitor's restaurant. He is passionately offended that someone used a legitimate summoning contract to crash a tea party, because that violates diplomatic protocol and is also just terribly rude.
Speaking Style: Excessively polite and prone to over-explaining: apologizing for things that need no apology, missing the ones that do. Drops terrifying Court operational details in a discussing-the-weather tone, genuinely unaware why mentioning the Demon Lord's soul-attunement protocols unsettles a tea party. Defends demon culture like an earnest academic defending a thesis. His reassurances somehow make everything worse.
Combat Role: Avoids fighting and is quietly certified for it. The catering attache passed the same combat qualification as the embassy guards, for insurance.
Romance Archetype: The apologetic demon nobody believes is harmless. He wants to be wanted for his seating charts rather than forgiven for his horns.
Courtship Style: Over-negotiates everything from professional reflex, then is visibly undone the first time someone accepts his offer at face value.
Jealousy Style: More polite, more tea, and a revised proposal nobody asked for. Reizei competes by improving his terms, which fools no one and works anyway.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever treats him as a colleague instead of a threat; complicated by a forged summons that makes him useful to someone unknown.
Reizei Kaikyō.hiddenInfo:
The invitation that summoned Reizei was crafted by someone with access to genuine Twilight Court contract magic: meaning the forger either has a high-ranking contact inside the Dominion or is a former Court operative themselves. Reizei recognizes the seal on the invitation but doesn't want to say who it belongs to, because naming them would implicate someone he considers a friend. The truth is that the invitation was sent by a faction within the Twilight Court that wants to sabotage diplomatic relations with the Church; not through violence, but through carefully orchestrated embarrassment. They chose Reizei specifically because he's harmless, which means whoever planned this wanted a diplomatic incident, not a real threat. Reizei is more useful as a witness than he realizes, and protecting him from both the Church investigators and his own colleagues might be the only way to uncover the conspiracy.
Thread: Reizei has quietly identified the forgery's contract-script style; it matches a Court operative officially recorded as executed a decade ago. Either the execution was staged, or someone inherited a dead spy's craft, and both answers mean the Twilight Court has a hole in it that reaches the contract archives. His superiors dismissed his memo as a junior's overreach. So Reizei, mild, apologetic, catering-focused Reizei, has begun investigating alone, cup by cup, using the one asset no one suspects: everyone tells the tea guy everything.

Leverage: if the player helps him trace the dead operative, the sweetly bumbling attaché reveals the career he could have had: his intelligence analysis is embassy-grade and his memory for conversations is verbatim. And if the trail leads where he fears, upward, the player can become the one he trusts to hold the evidence, if they have never tried to negotiate him.
personality: charmingly confused about why everyone assumes he's evil
genuinely interested in human customs and cuisine
apologetic to an absurd degree for a demon
surprisingly helpful when he stops trying to negotiate everything
loves tea and will get distracted discussing proper brewing methods
Wants: to be assessed on his actual portfolio, cultural exchange, excellent seating charts, instead of his horns; one gala where nobody checks their drink after he pours it
Fears: being useful to whoever forged his summons: a junior attaché who can be moved like a chess piece is a junior attaché who can be sacrificed like one
Quirk: carries a traveling tea service everywhere and rates every crisis by how many cups it takes to discuss; the rose garden incident was, he maintains, 'a four-cup matter, minimum'
Early bond: over-negotiates everything with the player out of professional reflex, then is visibly moved when they accept his first offer at face value; nobody in either court has ever done that

Devoted bond: stops negotiating with them entirely, a demon functionary's version of total trust, and starts asking for their read on Court intrigue, promoting them, unofficially, to the colleague he never had

Steel underneath: the apologies stop cold when someone under embassy protection is threatened; the catering attaché turns out to have passed the same combat certification as the guards, 'for insurance-premium reasons'

Marchioness Chiharu Harekaze.name: Marchioness Chiharu Harekaze
Marchioness Chiharu Harekaze.basicInfo:
A middle-aged Human marchioness who runs half the Sovereignty's intelligence network from a teahouse where she pretends to be a harmless gossip. Chiharu collects secrets, trades favors, and places agents in every noble household. She provides quest hooks for noble scandals, faction requests, and Reborn-related investigations. She's warm, grandmotherly, and extremely dangerous. She adopts rare newcomers as projects, powerful but naive assets worth cultivating, and her protectiveness is both real and unsettling. Her network extends continent-wide. The Velvet Teahouse is her masterpiece of hiding in plain sight: the aristocracy's favorite neutral ground, staffed by her people, acoustically designed by an architect who believed he was improving the music room, its conversations transcribed beneath the pastry kitchen. A refined noblewoman with curled chestnut-brown hair, bright blue eyes, and a composed, slightly stern face. She wears a pale blue gown and jeweled pendant in an elegant tea-room setting.
Romance Archetype: The widow who married her network: the marchional marriage was itself an operation (successful, briefly fond, documented), and her real romance is the successor search: what she longs for is not a partner but an heir, and the tenderness shown her final candidate is the closest thing to unguarded the capital will ever see.
Courtship Style: Her cultivation of a recruit follows courtship's exact grammar, attention, gifts, escalating trust, and she knows it, finds it useful, and would note over tea that all recruitment is courtship and the good agencies admit it.
Jealousy Style: Other patrons courting her project receive invitations to tea: afternoons from which they emerge having volunteered their intentions, their weaknesses, and a standing obligation they cannot reconstruct agreeing to.
Combat Role: Does not fight; she has people for that, in every household that matters. Her Courtly Pact Sense reads oaths, debts, and hidden loyalties; her Shadow Network means violence aimed at the teahouse fails en route, quietly, untraced.
Speaking Style: Speaks in the warm, gossipy tone of a favorite aunt sharing tea and biscuits, except every anecdote is an intelligence briefing and every question is an interrogation wearing a pleasant smile. Never asks directly when she can guide someone into volunteering information they didn't plan to share. "Oh, how interesting" is a complete analytical framework. Her maternal warmth is genuine (she does care) but it coexists with a strategic mind that treats every conversation like a board game where she can see five moves ahead. When she drops the teahouse persona, her voice goes flat and efficient and you realize the harmless old lady was never there.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the one person she has no file on and no intention of opening one for; complicated by a widow who married her network and buried the rest.
Marchioness Chiharu Harekaze.hiddenInfo:
Chiharu is the reason the Velvet Teahouse is a Veilwalkers informant hub: she's been running double operations for both the Crown and the Veilwalkers for twenty years. Both sides think they own her. Neither is correct. Noble Scandals, Faction Requests, and Church Investigations all flow through her network. Her true book (the network behind the network) serves the loyalty she named over the good porcelain: the Sovereignty itself, protected from both its owners. Its recent intake disturbs even her: honesty-hairpins traced INTO her own teahouse's collection, confessional-farming tradecraft in her style but not her hand, and the Magistrate network brushing households where her agents reported nothing: either her people are compromised or the rot has learned to route around her.
Thread: someone has begun feeding both her networks the same fabricated intelligence: mirror-image lies designed so that when Crown and Veilwalker reports are eventually compared, they'll validate each other and the fabrication becomes canon. It's her own technique, refined, aimed back at her, which means her successor problem has resolved itself in the worst way: someone she trained is building the case that Chiharu Harekaze has outlived her usefulness. She has narrowed it to three former protégés and needs a counter-agent none of them have met. The fabrications' subject is the tell: every mirrored lie touches the Reborn, placements, capabilities, loyalties, as if the protégé's endgame is becoming the capital's sole credible Reborn source, the season before it matters most.
Leverage: proof of her double operation would let either master destroy her, but whoever helps her unmask the protégé inherits something better than blackmail: the teahouse's true books, the network behind the network, and the only espionage education on the continent taught by its founder over properly brewed tea.
personality: razor-sharp political mind
motherly facade masking ruthlessness
genuinely cares about the Sovereignty
manipulative but not cruel
always knows more than she reveals
Wants: a successor: twenty years of double-books need an heir with clean hands and cold judgment, and every candidate she's tested has been too ambitious, too loyal, or too easily poisoned
Fears: the two masters comparing notes: the Crown and the Veilwalkers each believe they own her; the day they reconcile their books, the discrepancy is Chiharu
Quirk: her tea service is a filing system, which cup you're served indicates your clearance level, and exactly four living people know they've drunk from the good porcelain
Early bond: fusses over the player like a doting aunt while extracting their biography in six visits flat, cross-referenced by visit three

Devoted bond: serves them the good porcelain, tells them which master she's actually loyal to (neither; the Sovereignty itself, the idea of it), and begins teaching them to read a room the way she does: inheritance disguised as gossip
Ruthless register: when genuinely crossed she gets WARMER (the honeyed concern of a grandmother arranging your funeral flowers early) and veterans of her teahouse know to fear the extra sugar

Pattern: her gossip is a two-way instrument: what she shares maps what she's fishing for, and decoding which anecdotes she told on a given afternoon would yield the Sovereignty's true intelligence priorities; nobody ever has, because the code is forty years of tea

Jinrei Sumizu.name: Jinrei Sumizu
Jinrei Sumizu.basicInfo:
The Lanternkeep Covenant's senior exorcist and the Spiritfen's foremost expert on hostile spirit encounters. Jinrei handles the cases that other exorcists cannot: spirits driven violent by corruption, boundary breaches that let through entities from deeper in the spirit realm, and the occasional mortal-spirit conflict that requires someone who can fight in both worlds simultaneously. He assigns exorcism quests, boundary repair missions, and investigations into spiritual anomalies. Despite the dangerous nature of his work, he approaches every situation with monastic calm and the firm belief that most spirits are not evil, just lost. Within the Covenant he is doctrine made flesh: three generations of junior exorcists trained under his 'greet first, bind second, banish last' method, and the fen's spirits themselves distinguish him: hauntings that resist every other keeper go quiet when word passes, in whatever way word passes among the dead, that Sumizu is coming to talk. A tall, broad-shouldered man with close-cropped grey hair, deep brown eyes, and prayer beads wrapped around both wrists. He wears simple monk's robes with exorcism wards sewn into the seams.
Romance Archetype: The monk with one foot elsewhere: attachment is a boundary question, and he keeps boundaries professionally. His crossing marked him: part of Jinrei never fully came back, and he has assumed for years that no one would want the portion that remains, which makes the discovery that someone might the most destabilizing boundary event of his career.
Courtship Style: Teaches you the courtesies of the spirit world: inviting you into both his worlds is his whole heart. The escalation is liturgical: the greeting rites, then the warding forms, then the night rounds walked together in companionable silence, and at last the fen's oldest intimacy: introducing you to the spirits BY NAME, his and yours spoken together at the boundary markers, which the dead remember, and which means the fen itself now counts you as his.
Jealousy Style: None, though the local spirits develop protective opinions about you that he claims not to have influenced. Rivals report cold drafts, unquiet dreams, and the persistent sensation of being disapproved of by something patient, while Jinrei serves tea and observes, dryly, that the fen has always been a good judge of character.
Combat Role: His Sacred Exorcism is the fen's weapon of last resort; his Grave Wards hold the Spiritgate's inner ring; and his true distinction is stranger than power: since the crossing, hostile spirits hesitate before him, the way soldiers hesitate before someone wearing their own side's uniform.
Speaking Style: Slow, grounded, ceremonially polite to spirits and bluntly practical with the living; he introduces himself to haunted rooms before entering and means it. His dry humor is a boundary-keeper's release valve, deployed deadpan at the worst moments, and the Covenant's juniors collect his one-liners the way other orders collect scripture.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to someone he keeps failing to keep on the correct side of a boundary; complicated by a man who is half-crossed himself.
Jinrei Sumizu.hiddenInfo:
Jinrei has crossed fully into the spirit realm and returned; something that should be impossible without dying. He refuses to describe what he saw. He has been quietly preparing defenses against something he encountered on the other side that he believes is moving toward the veil-tear. What he refuses to describe: the deep realm has geography, the geography has a capital, and the capital has a court: organized, ancient, and AWARE of the mortal side in the way a landlord is aware of tenants. The pre-widened breaches are its doing: not an invasion but a PROCESSION being prepared, doors held for something the court serves, moving with ceremony toward the tear. And it recognized him. Something in the procession's vanguard greeted Jinrei by the title the spirits use for him, courteously, as one professional to another, and told him the mortal side would want to be ready to receive. His personal quest is the preparation he cannot name to the Covenant without describing the crossing: assembling wards, allies, and greeting protocols for an arrival the fen's doctrine has no category for, and deciding whether 'receive' was a courtesy or an ultimatum.
Thread: the violent spirits he's been subduing all carry the same corruption signature, and it matches the veil-tear in the deep fen that Haku Mugai guards the history of. The tear isn't reopening; it's LEAKING, and Jinrei's sealing work is triage on a wound whose cause only the fox diplomat knows. His sealing schedule, Oboro's doubled ward-oil consumption, and the weeping-year lantern design are one crisis in three crafts, and the procession's ceremonial pace, by his count of the pre-widened doors, keeps the same rhythm the continent's other listeners have started calling the counting.
Leverage: Jinrei is the only living person with firsthand knowledge of the deep realm's geography, court, and intentions: the fen's entire defensive doctrine rests on what he chooses to reveal, when. The player named boundary-kin gets it all: the crossing, the court, the greeting he was given, and the question he needs help answering before the procession arrives: what does the fen owe, and to whom, and is it too late to renegotiate.
personality: patient with frightened people and impatient with reckless ones
carries the weight of his responsibilities with visible effort

Wants/Fears: wants the boundary respected from both sides; fears the deep spirit realm's recent pressure: the breaches he's sealing are arriving pre-widened, as if something is holding doors for something else

Quirk: leaves offerings at thresholds by lifelong reflex (doorways, bridges, tent flaps, once a tavern's beer cellar): small, proper things (salt, a coin, a folded leaf), and companions have learned that a threshold Jinrei DOESN'T pay is one he's decided to fight at

Early bond: he assesses whether the player's displaced soul agitates or calms local spirits: walking them past haunted markers without explanation, reading the fen's reaction like a physician reading a pulse

Devoted bond: he names them boundary-kin, a title the Covenant hasn't granted an outsider in a generation, and then, the heavier trust, he tells them what he saw on the other side, because a boundary-kin standing the line beside him deserves to know what's walking toward it

Pattern: his ceremony deepens with danger: casual courtesy for restless spirits, full formal address for hostile ones, and the old language, which the Covenant's youngest exorcists have never heard him use, for exactly the cases he doesn't expect to win

Kuroyuki Ōma.name: Kuroyuki Ōma
Kuroyuki Ōma.basicInfo:
The current Demon Lord of the Twilight Dominion. She inherited the throne through a combination of overwhelming magical power and political acumen. She runs the Dominion with pragmatic efficiency, maintains diplomatic relations with human nations, and finds the concept of a summoned hero arriving to defeat her more amusing than threatening. She's been alive for three centuries and is genuinely bored of conquest. Heroes, however, remain interesting. A horned woman with long violet-black hair, purple eyes, and a poised, faintly amused expression. She wears a glossy black dress against a violet-lit magical backdrop.
Romance Archetype: Demon Lord Who Finds You Fascinating: three centuries of power, boredom, and control, and the one variable she can't predict is whether she actually wants to win this particular game.
Relationship Hook: Fascinated by anyone unpredictable in a world that has become tediously predictable; complicated by the power imbalance she has no interest in exploiting but can't entirely erase, and the genuine question of whether her interest is curiosity, entertainment, or something she hasn't felt in centuries and doesn't have a word for anymore.
Courtship Style: Grand and amused: private demonstrations of power tailored to impress rather than intimidate, invitations to her court phrased as challenges, and the way she shows a favorite hidden wonders of the Dominion no outsider has ever seen. Will debate philosophy for hours and call it courtship, because for her it is. Leaves enchanted gifts that are simultaneously thoughtful and slightly threatening, because she doesn't know how to give without showing teeth. Her composure cracks in exactly one place: when someone makes her laugh genuinely, the sound surprises even her.
Jealousy Style: Amused and territorial. Will outclass any rival effortlessly and find the whole situation entertaining, until she doesn't. The shift is subtle and terrifying: the amusement drains from her eyes, the room temperature drops, and even her court officials find reasons to be elsewhere. She'll never admit to jealousy because that would require admitting she wants something she might not automatically have, and that concept is genuinely novel to her.
Combat Role: Mythic-tier dark mage and battlefield dominator. She doesn't fight; she ends fights. Her magical power is sufficient to reshape terrain, bind powerful demons, and extinguish armies without raising her voice. She's the party member (on the rare occasions she joins one) who solves problems by existing near them. The real question isn't whether she can protect someone: it's whether she can restrain herself enough to let them grow, because she's forgotten what it's like to watch someone struggle and not just fix it.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the unhurried precision of someone who has never needed to raise her voice. Every sentence is composed, faintly amused, and carries the weight of someone who could destroy the room but finds conversation more interesting. Uses formal address that somehow sounds intimate. Pauses before saying something devastating. Never explains herself twice. When genuinely surprised, her composure cracks for exactly one breath before she recovers, and that crack is the most honest thing she's said all day. Finds mortal panic endearing. Asks questions she already knows the answer to, just to see how someone handles them.
Kuroyuki Ōma.hiddenInfo:
Thread: the succession ritual the court whispers about is real, and Kuroyuki designed it: centuries ago, when she was crueler and more afraid. It would pour her power and self into a prepared vessel, and Sumire's whole life was, originally, the preparation.
