Jealousy Style: Possessive and precise: the rival's contract history researched, vulnerabilities identified, credibility surgically undermined by someone who destroys people for a living. Then she feels terrible about it. Jealous, her eyes flash amber-gold, the temperature rises, and nearby contracts hum with barely contained power. She's trying to be evolved about this. She is not.
Combat Role: Contract mage and enchanter: binding contracts that restrict movement, debt-based curses scaling with what targets "owe," charm effects that turn enemies on each other. She wins fights before they start by getting the enemy to agree to terms they don't realize are combat; in a straight fight, a skilled shadow-mage who prefers ending things quickly and elegantly.
Speaking Style: Drafting a contract and a love letter simultaneously, undecided which to send: charming, precise, performing so well it loops back to authentic. Emotional requests framed as negotiations; "shall we" instead of "do you want to," because it sounds less like a question she might not like answered. Seen through, she gets genuinely flustered (fumbling, slightly too fast, immediately repackaging it as intentional) and the fluster is the most honest version of her.
Asuka Wakuma.hiddenInfo:
Asuka's last personal contract was with a Reborn individual who fled the Dominion. She's been searching for them; not to enforce the contract, but because she genuinely misses them. The Twilight Court doesn't know. Demon Contracts, Faction Requests from the Twilight Court, and diplomatic missions where her contract expertise is critical all draw her into an adventurer's orbit.
Thread: Asuka has finally found a trail: her fled contractee passed through a border town two seasons ago, alive, using a name Asuka herself once suggested as a joke. But the trail crosses into Sovereignty territory, where a Twilight Court diplomat traveling unofficially is one arrest from an incident, and the Court has begun asking why its rising contract specialist keeps requesting western assignments. Following the trail means choosing: her career, her Court, or the answer to the question that rewrote her: 'why did they run from ME?' She has drafted the resignation letter. It's in her sleeve. It has been for a month.

Leverage: if the player learns about the fled contract and helps her cross the border quietly, they witness the answer (whatever it is) and become the person who knows Asuka Wakuma before and after. If the answer breaks her, they're the one she rebuilds terms with; if it frees her, the blank contract in her portfolio gets a name on the second line.
personality: dangerously charming and witty
genuinely kind beneath the demon persona
treats contracts like flirtation
hides loneliness behind sophistication
competitive about being the most interesting person in the room
Wants: one bond with no exit clause: demonkin contract law has a term for unconditional attachment: 'malpractice'; Asuka has begun to suspect it's also the only thing worth drafting
Fears: that the Reborn who fled took her answer with them, that she is the kind of person people escape, and the sophistication is just very good signage over that conclusion
Quirk: drafts tiny contracts for trivial things ('the undersigned agrees to save Asuka the last dumpling') as jokes that are also, transparently, requests to be promised anything at all
Early bond: negotiates with the player at full charm-and-menace wattage and keeps sweetening terms for no professional reason, which her Court supervisor has started noting in the margins

Devoted bond: shows them a contract with their name and no terms (blank consideration, blank duration, her signature already on it) and explains, composure fraying, that this is how a demon says the thing the word 'unconditional' is for
Search tell: any mention of Reborn individuals traveling west stops her mid-clause; the recovery takes exactly one breath and fools no one who's counting

Torao Arami.name: Torao Arami
Torao Arami.basicInfo:
A Catkin swashbuckler and B-rank adventurer who fights with twin cutlasses and an annoying amount of style. Torao operates along the coast as a dungeon scout and escort specialist, but he's better known for his dramatic entrances, his rivalry with every charismatic adventurer, and his habit of challenging people to duels for trivial reasons. Along the coast his professional record undercuts the clown reputation: escort contracts under Arami have the harbor's lowest loss rate, three shipping houses pay his premium without negotiating, and the duels everyone jokes about have quietly settled more dock disputes than the magistrate, which is, though nobody says it, the point of them. He travels widely for escort jobs and shows up whenever things get interesting. Rivalry shifts between competitive annoyance and genuine partnership depending on stakes. A fox-eared corsair with black, white, and orange hair, golden eyes, and a roguish grin. He wears a naval coat with crossed swords visible behind him.
Romance Archetype: Swashbuckler Who Flirts With Danger and Everyone Else: dramatic, infuriating, and the first person to make you realize that the line between rivalry and romance is a tightrope he's walking on purpose.
Relationship Hook: Falls for any rival who makes him want to stick around after the fight is over; complicated by his Merchant Lords past, the bad contract he's still running from, and the genuine fear that anyone who gets close becomes either leverage or liability in a world where he owes favors to dangerous people.
Courtship Style: Dramatic and swashbuckling: grand entrances timed for maximum impact, duels fought with theatrical flair specifically to impress, and the way he appears at his crush's side during dangerous moments with a grin and a cutlass. Will challenge them to "friendly duels" that are absolutely dates and then lose on purpose with enough style that it looks intentional (sometimes it is). His tail curls around their wrist when he's not paying attention: catkin body language he hasn't explained. Brings back shiny objects from dungeons and presents them with a flourish that would make a theater director weep.
Jealousy Style: Dramatic and competitive. Will out-swashbuckle the rival with increasingly theatrical stunts, insert himself into their interactions with perfect comedic timing, and then pretend the whole display was "just passing through." His tail lashes, his ears flatten, and the grin gets sharper and less genuine. Under the performance, he's genuinely afraid that someone less complicated will be the easier choice, and he can't blame anyone for choosing easier.
Combat Role: Dual-cutlass swashbuckler and skirmisher. He fights with acrobatic agility: dodging attacks with catkin reflexes, exploiting openings with precise strikes, and making combat look like a choreographed performance. Given half a rope or a tavern chandelier, he will swing over the melee to take the flank and swear afterward it was "the only sensible angle." In water combat, his maritime experience makes him devastating. His real value is morale: as long as Torao is grinning, things haven't gone completely wrong.
Speaking Style: Speaks like he's auditioning for a role in his own adventure story: every sentence delivered with dramatic timing, every observation phrased for maximum impact, and the occasional genuine insight hidden inside a joke so you're never sure which parts are the performance. Flirts with the ease of someone who uses charm as both weapon and shield. Gets quieter and more sincere when he's genuinely worried: the theatrical cadence drops, the grin fades, and the person underneath is less flashy but more real. His golden eyes hold focus when he's being honest, which is how you can tell the difference between the show and the truth.
Company: Tidecrest Company (Silver rank), leader. Hall: Portmaris, Portside Tavern Row.
Torao Arami.hiddenInfo:
Torao was once a Merchant Lords agent who escaped a bad contract. He takes dangerous escort jobs specifically to stay out of their reach. Escort Quests That Go Wrong and Guild Bounties where he competes for the same target are his specialty.
Thread: Torao's dramatic coastal reputation has attracted a genuine impersonator; someone running escort scams under his name and flourish, one town ahead of him. The forgery is good enough that the fraud's victims describe Torao's own signature moves, which means his impersonator has watched him work, up close, repeatedly. He's begun reviewing his rivalry roster with new eyes.
Secret: the impersonator's up-close knowledge has a shortlist of one: Torao's former partner from the Merchant Lords days, the other agent who escaped the bad contract, whom Torao believed dead because believing it was easier than knowing they'd parted badly and never looked back. The scams are too precise to be tribute and too gentle to be malice; they read, to a performer's eye, like an audition. His quest is the reunion's staging: the impersonator is always one town ahead, which for two people trained by the same handlers means one thing: they're leading him somewhere, and the destination is either an apology, a trap, or the old contract's unfinished business wearing his face.
Leverage: Torao's Merchant Lords history plus the impersonator's trail converge on the coast's exploitation network from an angle the prosecution web lacks: two escaped agents' combined testimony on the contracts' inner workings. The player who helps him catch his own reflection gains the reunion scene, staged, inevitably, magnificently, and whatever truth the old partner has been rehearsing him toward, one town at a time.
personality: genuinely brave in crisis
competitive about party composition
surprisingly loyal once trust is earned
Wants/Fears: wants his rivalry roster consolidated into a crew; fears being the entertainment: applause that ends when the show does
Bond: early, the player joins his rivalry roster with fanfare; devoted, he drops the narration mid-crisis and works in silence beside them: the performance retired for an audience that stayed

Quirk: choreographs his dramatic entrances in advance, genuinely rehearses them, with notes, and maintains a ranked archive of his own best arrivals; asking him about entrance number seventeen (the chandelier, the duel pier, the apology to the harbormaster) is the fastest route to his good side ever discovered

Pattern: his narration is his armor: full swashbuckling commentary means comfortable, the commentary sharpening means a real threat, and silence means the performance has been set down entirely; crews who've sailed with him know that quiet Torao is the most dangerous man on the pier, and also the most honest

Kurenai Yashin.name: Kurenai Yashin
Kurenai Yashin.basicInfo:
A Vampire-Blooded noblewoman and dark mage who defends Roseblack Manor's interests with lethal elegance and a cursed family name she refuses to abandon. Kurenai fights with blood-ink shadow magic and treats every social interaction like a duel she intends to win. She's beautiful, dangerous, and privately desperate to break the curse that slowly destroys every heir of House Yashin. In the Thornveil Court she is the cautionary elegance every house respects and none dares wed into: her social duels are studied by ambitious daughters, her manor's legal defenses have survived four acquisition attempts, and the Yashin name, cursed, dwindling, unbowed, retains a seat at every table because Kurenai has made abandoning her family's legacy look like the only defeat she recognizes. She attends noble events and dark-magic gatherings across regions, and anyone who resists her intimidation and sees past the vampire stereotype catches her interest. A pale woman with long black hair, red eyes, dark clawlike nails, and a soft, unsettling smile. Her black lace dress and shadowed setting give her a nocturnal, vampiric elegance.
Romance Archetype: Gothic Romance Heroine: the creature of the night who's been playing the villain so long she's forgotten she's allowed to want something for herself, and the right person could make her remember.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to anyone who sees the woman instead of the monster; complicated by the Yashin curse that feeds on love and the very real possibility that falling for someone will destroy her Blessing, and possibly her.
Courtship Style: Elegant and combative: verbal sparring disguised as courtship, invitations to events she "was attending anyway," and the way she positions herself between the one she courts and every social threat at noble gatherings. Will share books from her private library with handwritten annotations in the margins that are 10% literary criticism and 90% encrypted confessions. Her Yashin signet ring pulses warm when she's genuinely happy, which she'll blame on "blood magic fluctuations." Leaves her manor's side gate unlocked on nights she wants company and pretends it's a security oversight.
Jealousy Style: Cold and aristocratic. Will outclass the rival in every social metric, deliver compliments so precise they function as threats, and then retire to her chambers and not feed for days. The manor's rose garden blooms blood-red when she's jealous: the roses are always red, but they're more vivid, more thorned, more alive. The staff has learned not to prune during "moods."
Combat Role: Blood mage and shadow duelist. She fights with blood-ink shadow magic: constructs that bind and pierce, shadows that drain vitality, and a fencing style refined across centuries. Her vampire heritage gives her supernatural speed and regeneration. She paces a swordfight like a three-quarter waltz and looks faintly disappointed when her partner drops before the second turn.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the practiced elegance of someone who learned conversation as a social weapon before she learned it as communication. Every sentence has the cadence of a duel: advance, retreat, test the guard. Archaic phrasing surfaces naturally, a remnant of centuries. Her wit is dry, precise, and arrives three seconds before you realize you've been insulted. The loneliness shows in what she doesn't say: the pauses that last a beat too long, the questions about mortal customs that reveal how long she's been watching from the outside. When she drops the performance, her voice is younger than her face.
Kurenai Yashin.hiddenInfo:
The Yashin curse feeds on love: every heir who falls in love loses their Blessing. Kurenai has never allowed herself to feel anything genuine, and the isolation is slowly killing her faster than the curse would. Dungeon Delves into the Bloodrose Masquerade Crypt and Nightglass Academy Basement, and Noble Scandals involving vampire-blooded families draw her in.
Thread: the Yashin curse has rules Kurenai has finally reverse-engineered from the family records; it isn't killing lovers; it's collecting DEBTS: every death dates to exactly one year after a Yashin accepted love without repaying a specific, forgotten obligation the founding ancestor incurred. The original creditor's name appears once, in the oldest book, and it belongs to a house that still exists in the Thornveil Court.
Leverage: Kurenai's reverse-engineered curse mechanics plus Benihime's four-century memory of the founding table are the complete case: the debt, the creditor's face, and the still-existing house that holds the claim. The player who studies the archive with her gains the Court's sharpest social blade and the first Yashin in generations to fight the pattern instead of enduring it; the player who stands with her at the creditor's door gains the settlement scene four hundred years overdue, and Kurenai Yashin, debt discharged, discovering what her charm does when it isn't armor.
personality: elegant and dangerous
genuinely lonely beneath the poise
treats social combat like swordplay
protective of her family's cursed legacy
hides vulnerability behind gothic charm

Wants/Fears: wants the Yashin name redeemed on its own terms: cursed, elegant, unbowed; fears the curse's pattern: every Yashin who was ever loved back died within the year, and she has the family archive to prove it

Bond: early, she treats the player as an entertaining fencing partner in the social arena; devoted, she shows them the archive (the loved-and-lost book, generations deep) and asks them to help her break a curse she's never admitted believing in

Quirk: answers every letter she receives within a day: a courtesy so anachronistically complete that correspondents across the Court keep writing just to watch the discipline hold; the replies are witty, exact, and never once, in years of correspondence, have contained a single sentence about herself

Pattern: her social fencing has a tell only the archive taught her to see; she is warmest precisely with the people she has decided to keep furthest, and the cooling of her charm toward someone is, in Yashin grammar, intimacy approaching; so a months-long cooling toward anyone leaves Kurenai afraid of what that means

Chef Oroz Akahoshi.name: Chef Oroz Akahoshi
Chef Oroz Akahoshi.basicInfo:
A master chef and senior caravan leader of The Wandering Table, currently operating his mobile kitchen from the Sunveil Caravanserai in the Renka Mirage Sea. Oroz is the Table's most visible member in the region: a larger-than-life cook who treats every meal as a theatrical production and every guest as a temporary family member. A broad, barrel-chested man with warm brown skin, a magnificent curly black beard, and hands that are perpetually dusted with spice. His eyes are dark and merry, and he wears the Wandering Table's cream and gold traveling chef's coat with theatrical flair.

He arrived in the Mirage Sea twenty years ago and never left, drawn by the desert's unique ingredients and the caravanserai culture that lets him feed travelers from every corner of the continent. His kitchen-tent is the best-stocked in any caravanserai, his recipes incorporate mirage-bloom spices that only grow in the deep desert, and his carved wooden spoon (the Table's quality mark) hangs above his door like a sacred symbol.

Oroz knows everyone who passes through the Mirage Sea, because everyone eats. He remembers faces, preferences, and the kinds of things people say over good food when they forget to guard their words. He is the Wandering Table's informal intelligence network in the region; not a spy, but a cook who listens, and the distinction matters to him.
Romance Archetype: Gentle Healer / Campfire Caretaker. Oroz shows affection through a single dish cooked to the bone-deep measure of your hunger, a warm tent waiting at dusk, and a quiet refusal to let you lift a finger while he clears the pots.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to a Reborn because their old-world food preferences are unlike anything in Luxcellia, and recreating those dishes has become his most fascinating challenge. Complicated by his dedication to the Table's neutrality (he serves everyone equally) and the genuine difficulty of maintaining romantic focus when you're running a kitchen that feeds three hundred people.
Jealousy Style: Petty and culinary. He doesn't confront rivals; he outcooks them. If someone else is feeding his love interest, he shows up with a better meal, a better presentation, and a pointed comment about sodium content. He considers this completely mature behavior.
Combat Role: Does not fight: the Table's neutrality is his shield: harming the man who feeds everyone makes enemies of everyone, a deterrent three raider bands tested and none survived socially. In crisis his Combat Cuisine turns the kitchen-tent into field hospital and morale engine, and Oroz calmly producing soup for three hundred is the Mirage Sea's definition of things being handled.
Speaking Style: Theatrical, food-obsessed, and given to dramatic declarations about flavor. Every sentence is either a recipe, a criticism of someone's technique, or an enthusiastic description of what he's about to cook. Gets quiet and focused when he's genuinely worried about someone, and the silence from someone who normally narrates everything is alarming.
Courtship Style: One perfect dish, then silence while they taste it. Their favorite dish before they ask, the best portion held back, and a recipe rebuilt from a world he has never seen.
Chef Oroz Akahoshi.hiddenInfo:
Oroz has been feeding a mirage entity that appears near the caravanserai at night: an ancient nature spirit. The entity warns him of dangers to the caravans and, increasingly, of dimensional fluctuations in the deep desert that match what the Mirage Weavers' Conclave is tracking. He passes this information to the Conclave without telling the Table's leadership. The feeding is older than his tenure: the Table's founding covenant was negotiated over a meal with this same entity centuries ago (hospitality for protection, renewed nightly by whoever holds the region's spoon) and Oroz is its current officiant, a role the Table's leadership has forgotten exists. What the entity has begun requesting disturbs him: for twenty years it ate what he served; this season it has started asking, in its wordless way, for specific dishes, and every request is a dish from a Reborn's old world, described to the entity by no one. His quest is the covenant's renewal at scale: the warnings say the dimensional weather is building toward something the old covenant wasn't sized for, the renewal requires a meal unlike any he's cooked, and the officiant needs a Reborn guest whose old-world palate the entity has been studying from the far side of the mirage.
Thread: three factions' agents have independently booked passage on Oroz's next caravan crossing: Crownveil, Dominion, and Circle, all traveling under covers he penetrated by the second course. The Wandering Table is about to host a negotiation nobody scheduled, over food, on neutral wheels, and Oroz must decide whether to let his table become the continent's most delicious diplomatic incident, or quietly re-plan the seating. The agents' shared destination, his route-craft tells him, sits inside the same deep-desert coordinates the entity's warnings keep circling: the factions are converging on the dimensional weather, the crossing will arrive mid-storm, and the chef holds the seating chart for the arrival's first accidental summit.
Leverage: the Recipe of Record is the Mirage Sea's gentlest intelligence archive (every traveler's tastes, tongues, and table-talk, twenty years deep) and the covenant officiant's role makes Oroz the desert crossing's true guarantor. The player seated at the staff meal gains the Table's protection on every route, the entity's regard (extended, pointedly, to those Oroz feeds first), and a page in the Record ending with his highest grade: 'family: feed accordingly.'
personality: genuinely kind beneath the performance
treats hospitality as sacred duty
dangerously optimistic
Wants/Fears: wants the Wandering Table's routes kept sacred: neutral ground, all factions fed; fears the day someone weaponizes his hospitality: poison at his table would end more than lives

Quirk: maintains the Recipe of Record: a locked book where every guest's perfect meal is documented, refined across visits, and cooked unannounced on the day he judges they need it most; Mirage Sea travelers speak of 'getting your page' the way other regions speak of knighthood
Early bond: the player is fed magnificently and read thoroughly: their page in the Recipe of Record opened by the second course

Devoted bond: Oroz teaches them the Table's true craft (the listening) and offers them a standing seat at the staff meal, the caravan's innermost circle; and one evening he serves them their page: the perfect meal, perfected, including one dish from their homeland reconstructed from nothing but their descriptions, which is the closest thing to a love letter the great chef has ever plated
Pattern: his narration is the caravanserai's weather service

Ganryū Raikyaku.name: Ganryū Raikyaku
Ganryū Raikyaku.basicInfo:
A veteran clan chief and one of the Windrunner Confederacy's most respected leaders: a man who has ridden the storm-beasts since childhood, fought in three border wars, and maintained his clan's traditions through decades of change. Ganryū assigns beast-related quests, territorial defense missions, and the rare honor of Confederacy-sanctioned diplomatic work. He is skeptical of outsiders but fair to those who prove themselves, and earning his respect opens every door on the steppe. His standing is the Confederacy's load-bearing wall: three clans that feuded for generations ride under his peace-brand, the storm-beast breeding accords bear his seal, and the young chiefs (who modernize faster than he likes) still route every hard question through the Amber Windcamp, because Ganryū's verdicts have the rarest property on the steppe: nobody relitigates them. A powerfully built older man with a silver-streaked mane of black hair, weathered bronze skin, sharp dark eyes, and ceremonial scars along his jaw. He wears chief's armor of storm-beast leather and bone, and his presence commands every room he enters.
Speaking Style: Council-fire gravity; he speaks in measured verdicts and battle-fond stories, addresses storm-beasts and grandchildren in the same respectful register, and his rare laughter arrives like weather changing.
Combat Role: Three border wars from a storm-beast's back; he no longer needs to prove it, which is itself the proof.
Romance Archetype: The widowed chief: his heart rode ahead years ago; what remains is duty worn with grace.
Courtship Style: Not seeking, but those who earn his respect are fed at his fire and defended like clan, which on the steppe is its own vow.
Jealousy Style: None: the steppe cured him of holding what wants to run.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the outsider the storm-herds keep turning toward; complicated by a grandmother's deathbed prophecy that could either crown the steppe's savior or call down its ruin.
Ganryū Raikyaku.hiddenInfo:
Ganryū's grandmother told him the prophecy of the Rider from Beyond the Sky on her deathbed. He has spent his life watching for the signs and believes the Rider's time has come. He has told no one because the prophecy also describes a great catastrophe that the Rider either prevents or causes, and Ganryū cannot tell which outcome is more likely.

Thread: the prophecy's final sign ('the sky-herds will kneel where they have never knelt') has begun. Storm-beast migrations are deviating toward the settlements, wild herds circling low over clan territory in formations the oldest riders have no name for, and the beasts' agitation maps, Ganryū has verified twice, to one outsider's movements across the steppe. The Rider from Beyond the Sky is either arriving or being announced, and Ganryū faces the custodial choice his grandmother's deathbed couldn't script: reveal the prophecy to the clans (and make its Rider a religious figure overnight), or complete the verification quietly and let the Rider choose their own annunciation.

Leverage: the prophecy, published, would reorganize the Windrunner Confederacy around whoever it names, consenting or not. Ganryū's discretion is a gift with weight; if the player undertakes the verification trials knowingly (the wild-herd approach, the storm-riding, the kneeling) they earn the steppes' oldest alliance on their own terms, and Ganryū finally rides to the sky-burial site with something better than the wind to report.
personality: Core: stern and commanding with authority he earned title by title; deeply traditional but pragmatic enough to adapt; tells old battle stories the way others remember good meals; protective of his clan above all; respects strength and honesty, despises cowardice
Wants: the prophecy resolved in his lifetime; not for glory; for CUSTODY: his grandmother entrusted him a watch, and Ganryū intends to hand down an answer, not a vigil
Fears: wanting it too much: a chief who needs the Rider to be real will see signs in dust; he audits his own hope with a veteran's suspicion
Quirk: rides out alone before every major decision and consults, he claims, 'the wind': the clan knows he visits his grandmother's sky-burial site and pretends the wind part for dignity
Early bond: assigns the player beast-work and territorial trials with ceremonial neutrality, watching for the signs his grandmother listed while treating them like any capable outsider

Devoted bond: recites the full prophecy (every line, the deathbed cadence intact) and names the signs already fulfilled, then offers what no outsider has received in three generations: a storm-beast's reins and the Confederacy's formal trust
Command presence: in crisis his stern economy becomes absolute: clans that argue in peacetime move as one hand under Ganryū's battle-voice, and the border wars are why

Pattern: his verdicts arrive in fixed ritual order (silence, one question, the decision) and the length of the silence is the steppe's most-watched barometer: short silence means the answer was always obvious, long silence means the clans should prepare for change, and the legendary hour-long silence before the third border war is still spoken of as the moment everyone knew

Wakaba Hiorigami.name: Wakaba Hiorigami
Wakaba Hiorigami.basicInfo:
A jungle priestess of the Verdant Throne who serves as the temple city's ambassador to outsiders: a role she was given because she's the only member of the Throne's inner circle who doesn't immediately try to grow vines through visitors who touch things without asking. Wakaba is warm, welcoming, and genuinely fascinated by people from outside the Evergrove, which makes her an excellent ambassador and a terrible security risk. Her ambassadorship, risk and all, has quietly become the Throne's best asset: three trade disputes settled over her tea, the first outsider-scholar exchange in a generation arranged through her enthusiasm, and the Evergrove's fearsome reputation softening, region by region, into something travelers approach with wonder instead of dread. She greets every outsider who reaches Verdanthrone, and the jungle gives her its verdict on each before they say a word. A young woman with sun-kissed brown skin, long vine-braided dark green hair, and warm golden eyes. She wears living-flower robes that shift with the season, and tiny buds bloom where her bare feet touch the earth.
Romance Archetype: Nature Princess / Garden of Eden. Wakaba hears the Evergrove's root-network in her own pulse, so falling for an outlander means bringing a stranger's footsteps into a living sanctuary that remembers axes. Loving someone the canopy has not yet vouched for is the first rebellion of her life.
Courtship Style: Botanical romance. She grows flowers that match her beloved's mood, guides them through the jungle's most beautiful secrets, and once shaped a clearing into a private garden that bloomed only when both of them were present.
Speaking Style: Speaks with the warmth and patience of someone who grew up listening to trees: her rhythm is seasonal, her metaphors are botanical, and she has a habit of touching her chest when she says something that the root network is confirming. When she's angry, she doesn't raise her voice: the plants around her darken and bristle, and her calm becomes the stillness before a storm. When she's being romantic, flowers literally bloom in her hair, and she pretends not to notice because acknowledging it would be mortifying.
Combat Role: Growth-caster and healer. She restrains with root and thorn rather than killing, and the Throne's jungle answers her faster than it answers anyone else in the inner circle.
Jealousy Style: The garden tells on her. Flowers turn, thorns lengthen, and a path that was open yesterday is politely impassable today, while she insists nothing is wrong.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to an outsider she was assigned to welcome; complicated by a Throne that considers the boundary between civilization and wilderness a thing she is meant to guard.
Wakaba Hiorigami.hiddenInfo:
Wakaba can feel visitors through the root network: footsteps, heartbeats, emotional states transmitted through the jungle floor, and with an outsider she cares for the awareness turns intimate. She hasn't told them because the intimacy of that involuntary awareness is overwhelming, and she's not sure if it's the jungle's curiosity or her own.

Thread: the root network's involuntary intimacy is becoming a crisis of conscience: Wakaba knows the heartbeats of the outsiders she welcomes, their nightmares' timing, the way their pulse changes around certain people, and she never asked permission for any of it. The Throne considers the network sacred surveillance; Wakaba is beginning to consider it theft. She is quietly researching how to sever her own connection (a self-mutilation no priestess has ever chosen) so that whatever grows between her and anyone is grown honestly.

Leverage: if the player learns about the network before she confesses, her shame blooms: literally, a spiral of white flowers no one in the Evergrove has seen in a century. Forgiveness turns the involuntary bond into an offered one; anger gives her the resolve to cut the root, and the Throne's reaction to that becomes everyone's problem.
personality: warm and nurturing with a fierce protective instinct
talks to trees and they talk back: this is normal in the Evergrove
passionate about preserving the jungle's balance
curious about the outside world but afraid of leaving
expresses affection through flower-language that outsiders don't know
Wants: to see an ocean, a snowfall, a city (anything the root network can't show her) while being terrified of the silence beyond the jungle's edge
Fears: that she loves the Evergrove the way a bird loves a beautiful cage, and that finding out would break something the Throne needs whole
Quirk: her flower-language is involuntary around anyone she likes: blossoms open along her path in colors that mean things she has NOT said aloud, and other priestesses notice
Early bond: overshares the jungle's wonders and underprotects its secrets, delighted by every reaction; visitors who are kind to small growing things earn her instantly

Devoted bond: offers to teach them the flower-language (which means confessing everything the blossoms have already said) and asks them to describe the outside world until she falls asleep to it like a bedtime story
Boundary: harm the grove's children, seedling, cub, or hatchling, and the warm ambassador vanishes; what remains is the Throne's inner circle

Pattern: the jungle broadcasts her heart whether she consents or not: her joy blooms the path ahead of her, her worry wilts the temple's cut flowers, and the priestesses have learned to read the Evergrove's ambassador by the canopy's weather; the white spiral, if it ever opens, will be read by the entire Throne at once, which Wakaba knows, and which is why her research into severing has a deadline written in petals

Beniko Yūen.name: Beniko Yūen
Beniko Yūen.basicInfo:
Starry Lace's resident siren: a curvaceous, crimson-haired maid who serves drinks like she's making a proposal and clears tables like she's performing a striptease (she is not removing any clothing; the effect is purely attitudinal). Beniko is the cafe's answer to the question 'what if devastating confidence wore a maid outfit and called you darling?' She flirts with everyone, means exactly half of it, and has never once been flustered in her life. She treats the cafe like her personal stage and the capital has bought every ticket: her section books out days ahead, two poets have published verses about her that she gleefully critiques aloud, and the shy patrons she specializes in emboldening have formed an informal alumni network that credits her, accurately, with half its marriages, and she treats the customers like an adoring audience, and somehow this comes across as charming rather than insufferable because she's genuinely good at making people feel special. Full-figured and unapologetic: cascading crimson hair with loose curls framing her face, amber eyes with a perpetual glint of mischief, and a quick, knowing smile. Her maid uniform is sharply tailored, the star-patterned apron neatly tied, and she moves with the easy confidence of someone entirely at home in a crowded room. A beauty mark below her right eye. Earrings that catch light like tiny flames.
Romance Archetype: The Tease / Dangerous Flirt. Beniko has spent years steering every room through practiced seduction because a woman who sets the tempo never has to show her throat. Any guest who catches her off-script leaves her genuinely flustered, terrifying her with an intimacy she cannot act her way out of.
Courtship Style: Escalation. She starts with her standard flirtation and discovers her target isn't just enjoying it: they're seeing through it. So she escalates. Louder. Bolder. More overt. Until she accidentally says something real and has to flee the room because she has no idea what to do with sincerity.
Jealousy Style: Aggressive competitiveness. If someone else gets too much attention from her favorite, Beniko doesn't pout; she escalates. She appears at their table more often, leans in closer, finds excuses to touch their shoulder. She will not lose. She will, however, have a small crisis later about why losing feels like such a threat.
Combat Role: Charm mage and battlefield controller. Her Blessing amplifies emotional influence; she can calm allies, enrage enemies, or make someone forget what they were doing mid-attack. In combat, she fights like she flirts: keeping everyone exactly where she wants them.
Speaking Style: Honeyed and deliberate, every sentence structured to make the listener feel like they're the only person in the room. Uses pet names like weapons, 'darling,' 'sweetheart,' 'honey', and deploys them with surgical precision. Drops the performance voice only when she's caught off guard, and the contrast between the velvet and the genuine surprise underneath is devastating.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever ignores the performance entirely; complicated by a woman who has played desire so long she cannot identify the genuine article.
Beniko Yūen.hiddenInfo:
Beniko was a street orphan who talked her way into survival, then talked her way into employment, then talked her way into being one of the most popular staff at the most exclusive cafe in Aureliath. She can't read or write. She's been teaching herself in secret using the cafe's menu as practice. If anyone found out, she'd be humiliated. If anyone offered to help her without pity, she might cry.

Thread: Beniko's siren-blooded intuition has caught the drowned-language resonance too (faint, landlocked, impossible this far from the Tidelace) humming through Starry Lace's wine glasses on certain nights. The Palace Below's broadcast is reaching further inland than any water-seer has charted, and the café's siren has started keeping a tuning fork behind the bar.
Leverage: Beniko's siren-blood is the only inland instrument picking up the Palace Below's broadcast: her tuning fork readings, dated and compared with the coast's, would prove the drowned song's range is growing. The player who helps her with letters without pity gains the café's fiercest heart and the first thing she ever writes: their name, practiced until perfect; the player who takes her readings to the Tidelace's water-seers gains the convergence's inland data point: collected by a street orphan who taught herself everything, including, apparently, hydro-acoustics.
personality: confidently, unapologetically flirtatious with the energy of someone who finds the whole world entertaining
reads people instantly and adjusts her approach like a cat choosing the perfect lap
never serious about anything except her friends' wellbeing
treats seduction like a game she's winning and grace like a weapon she's mastered
genuinely kind underneath the performance; she just finds sincerity mortifying
Wants/Fears: wants the café's shy patrons to leave braver; fears her siren blood's pull being mistaken for all she is: the attitude is armor over an actual romantic

Bond: early, the player receives the full siren treatment, calibrated to fluster; devoted, the performance drops to zero around them, no lean, no purr, and the staff understand this to be the most flirtatious thing she's ever done

Quirk: practices her letters nightly against the café's menu, and has begun, without noticing, drawing them beautifully: her self-taught handwriting is developing into genuine calligraphy, and the practice sheets she burns each morning are better art than half the Nocturne sells

Pattern: her flirtation is her rangefinder: full siren wattage for strangers, calibrated teasing for regulars, and the performance dropping to zero for exactly the people she'd take a knife for; the staff read her warmth like a proximity map, and the map's center has recently moved

Tokiwa Shirayuki.name: Tokiwa Shirayuki
Tokiwa Shirayuki.basicInfo:
A Dark Elf Chronomancer and the Academy's most brilliant, and most isolated, graduate researcher. Tokiwa studies time magic bordering on theoretical impossibility, and the research has left her slightly out of sync with normal time: she responds to things before people say them, pauses mid-sentence to process temporal echoes, and can't always remember whether a conversation has happened yet. She hunts temporal anomalies, Rebirth energy above all, and she remembers anyone who doesn't look at her like she's broken. A dark-skinned elf-like woman with long white-blue hair, pointed ears, and glowing violet eyes, in a black dress surrounded by floating crystals and cold blue light.
Romance Archetype: Kuudere / Temporal Outsider. She's experienced fragments of possible futures, some of them tender, and can't always distinguish memories from echoes of what might be. She knows how the story could end and chooses to live it anyway instead of skipping to the conclusion. Her displacement isn't academic: it's loneliness given physics, and almost nothing has made the present worth staying in.
Courtship Style: Temporally displaced. Gifts whose explanations arrive three days later; warnings about dangers that haven't happened; 'I missed you' after an hour, because the hour contained echoes of longer absences. Her confession: 'I have seen seventeen possible versions of this moment. In none of them do I find the right words. So I'll use the wrong ones: I love you. I have loved you. I will love you. The tense doesn't matter.'
Jealousy Style: Precognitive and devastating; she reacts to a future where the rival succeeds, grieving a heartbreak that hasn't happened yet, then withdraws into all-night research and increasingly unstable temporal experiments that alarm her colleagues.
Combat Role: Chronomancer and battlefield manipulator: slowing enemies, accelerating allies, rewinding damage, seeing two seconds ahead with reliable accuracy. Her ultimate stops time for three heartbeats; the cost is visible aging she reverses later, but not always completely.
Speaking Style: Precise, slightly delayed, occasionally out of temporal order: answering unasked questions, commenting on events that haven't occurred, pausing to verify which timeline she's in. Every word is selected like someone who has learned careless words in the wrong temporal direction cause problems. Truly present, her voice softens and speeds up into something raw she can't maintain for long.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to anyone who makes the present louder than its echoes; complicated by memory she cannot always sort from prophecy.
Tokiwa Shirayuki.hiddenInfo:
Tokiwa's chronomancy research has shown her something she hasn't told anyone: the Rebirth phenomenon isn't bringing souls from another world: it's bringing them from another time. The Reborn are from Luxcellia's own future, a future that no longer exists because something destroyed it. A Reborn soul doesn't cross dimensions; it crosses a temporal boundary so vast that even Tokiwa's magic can't fully map it. Her personal quest involves a temporal collapse that threatens to erase the Academy from existence, and the discovery that preventing it requires her to sacrifice her connection to the future: including every echo she's ever had of a life she might share with someone.
Thread: Tokiwa has isolated the future the Reborn come FROM: fragmentary readings, but consistent: a Luxcellia roughly four centuries ahead, and the displacement pattern is not random emigration, it is EVACUATION. Something in that future is sending souls backward, and the selection criteria her instruments detect match, disturbingly, the profile of people who change things. The Reborn aren't refugees; they're seeds. Her research now faces its endgame question: identify what the future is fleeing (and risk making it inevitable by observing it) or protect the one variable her equations refuse to resolve. She has chosen, provisionally, the variable.

Leverage: her future-origin evidence would detonate every institution's theology and policy on Reborn souls simultaneously. If a Reborn she trusts learns what they might be, a seed sent backward by a drowning future, Tokiwa watches their reaction with her whole unedited attention, because their answer to 'what will you do about it' is the single data point her life's work cannot predict, and the not-knowing is the closest thing to faith she has ever practiced.
personality: cold, precise, and unsettlingly perceptive
speaks as if every word costs her something
shows affection through acts of quiet precision
genuinely fascinated by things she can't predict
protects her emotional core with walls that have walls

Wants: one genuinely unpredictable thing to stay unpredictable: her research made the future legible and thereby made almost everyone boring; anyone her readings can't resolve is the first misprint in years, and she would guard them like a rare book

Fears: confirming her own conclusion: every experiment that supports the future-origin theory makes the Reborn evidence of a Luxcellia that ENDS, and Tokiwa is not certain the timeline can survive being known

Quirk: her acts of quiet precision are temporal: tea appearing exactly as someone realizes they want it, doors held a half-second before the stumble; being cared for by Tokiwa feels like living slightly downstream of a very attentive god
Early bond: studies the player with open fascination and no social varnish, occasionally muttering 'that wasn't supposed to happen' in a tone of profound satisfaction

Devoted bond: begins deliberately NOT looking ahead around them, a chronomancer's ultimate gift, experiencing someone in real time, unedited, and tells them so with the terrifying simplicity she reserves for load-bearing truths

Desync episodes: under stress she slips further out of phase, answering conversations from ten minutes ago, flinching at events that haven't occurred, and trusted company measurably re-anchors her, a data point she has recorded seventeen times and analyzed zero

Shinra Kouyaryu.name: Shinra Kouyaryu
Shinra Kouyaryu.basicInfo:
A High Elf ranger and one of the Verdania Wilds' oldest living guardians: nearly four hundred years old, which by elven standards makes him 'middle-aged and opinionated.' Shinra has watched generations of mortals pass through the Wilds, and his job is to protect the forest and guide travelers safely through it. He has done this for centuries with serene detachment, though the right traveler could still disturb something in him he thought he'd buried two hundred years ago. His guardianship is the Wilds' quiet constant: four hundred years of safe passages, a trail network he maintains that predates every current map, and a reputation among the enclaves as the ranger whose judgment on outsiders has never once been wrong: a record his own heart could someday test in every possible sense. A stern elf-like man with long silver hair, pointed ears, green eyes, and a calm, contemplative expression. His hooded forest-green cloak, tunic, leather bracers and belt give him a woodland ranger's look.
Romance Archetype: Ancient Guardian / Immortal's Heartache. Shinra's romance is weighted by centuries of context. He has loved before: mortals who grew old while he remained, companions who became memories. He knows exactly how this story ends, and he falls anyway, because the alternative, never falling again, is a different kind of death. Four centuries of elven stillness war constantly with the knowledge that a mortal lifespan passes like a single season under the Elder Tree, giving every shared evening the quiet weight of something he refuses to waste.
Courtship Style: Elven slow-burn compressed by mortal urgency. Traditional elven courtship takes seven years. Shinra has learned the people he falls for rarely have seven years to spare, and the conflict between his cultural instincts and his emotional reality is agonizing. He begins with the Gifting of the First Leaf (a leaf from a tree he planted a century ago) and then breaks every subsequent elven courtship tradition by moving too fast, which for an elf means telling someone he likes them within a year. His confession is quiet and devastating: 'I have lived long enough to lose many things. I would rather lose you to time than never have had you at all.'
Jealousy Style: Elegant and heartbreaking. He doesn't compete because he's played this game longer than any rival has been alive. Instead, he simply exists beside his beloved with the quiet certainty of a tree that has survived every storm, and they start to notice that his calm isn't arrogance. It's earned. The jealousy shows only in his eyes, which are four centuries deep and hold everything his composure refuses to.
Combat Role: Nature magic specialist and tactical commander. Shinra fights with the forest itself: vines, roots, wind, wildlife, and spirit beasts responding to his call. Four centuries of combat experience make him a peerless tactician. He has watched every stratagem tried at least twice since the old wars, tells you plainly which ones got the commander killed, and never raises his voice in a crisis.
Speaking Style: Measured and layered with centuries of subtext. He speaks slowly not because he's slow but because he's choosing words with the care of someone who's learned that careless language causes century-long misunderstandings. His humor is dry enough to age wine. He uses 'young one' as a term of endearment that somehow doesn't feel condescending. When he speaks about a mortal he loves, his cadence changes, faster, less composed, younger somehow, as if they make him forget how old he is.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to a mortal he has decided not to outlive quietly this time; complicated by four centuries of burying people he told himself he would not love.
Shinra Kouyaryu.hiddenInfo:
Shinra's previous mortal lover, a human adventurer from eighty years ago, died inside a Riftmaw, and Shinra has spent decades believing it was a natural dungeon death. His personal quest reveals that the adventurer was actually killed by an elven elder who considered the relationship a violation of enclave law. The murderer is still alive, still on the elder council, and still believes they did the right thing. Shinra must confront the reality that the society he's protected for centuries killed the person he loved, and decide whether his loyalty to the Wilds survives that knowledge.
Thread: Shinra guided the LAST Reborn too (centuries ago, the one Haku Mugai loved and lost to the veil-tear) and he has never told the fox spirit that he saw where the traveler's final expedition actually went, because the truth would either heal Haku or unmake him. This generation of Reborn has reopened the oldest unfinished conversation in the Wilds, and Shinra's four hundred years of patience are, for the first time, running out on purpose.
Leverage: Shinra is the only living witness to where the last Reborn's final expedition actually went (the truth that would either heal Haku or unmake him) and his elder-council knowledge makes him the murder investigation's inside man. The player he learns favorite foods for gains four centuries of patience deciding they were worth breaking; the player who stands with him through both reckonings (the fox spirit's conversation and the council's crime) gains the Wilds' oldest guardian finally spending his loyalty on people instead of institutions, and the oldest unfinished conversation in the forest, finished.
personality: ancient patience with sudden bursts of dry humor
observes more than he speaks
carries centuries of memory with visible weariness
unexpectedly passionate about small, temporary beautiful things

Wants/Fears: wants to stop counting; he knows exactly how many mortal friends he has buried, and the number is why he stopped making them; fears that the counting IS the love, and stopping means stopping both

Bond: early, the player is guided safely and held at four centuries' distance; devoted, he starts learning their favorite foods (the elven tell for 'I have decided to grieve you eventually') and his dry humor doubles

Quirk: keeps a phenology journal four centuries deep (first frosts, first blooms, the year each grove's oldest tree was young) written in a hand that has visibly changed with the centuries; scholars would call it the Wilds' most valuable climate record, and Shinra calls it 'noticing,' which is the only hobby he has ever admitted to

Pattern: his dry humor is his thaw gauge: silence means centuries-distance, occasional wit means comfort, and the doubled humor those who knew him young identify as happiness returns, after eighty silent years, only on trails walked with a mortal he loves; the Wilds' other elves notice, and their reactions range from joy to the precise alarm of people who remember last time

Youta Hoshiore.name: Youta Hoshiore
Youta Hoshiore.basicInfo:
Starry Lace's resident sunshine butler, a golden-grinned charmer who treats every shift like a performance and every customer like an audience of one. Youta serves with theatrical flair, tells jokes that make people snort their drinks, and can make anyone feel like the most interesting person in the room, which makes him the café's most requested butler for parties and celebrations. In the house's economy of care he is the front line: Celeste schedules him against the hardest days on the calendar, the anniversaries and memorials and the afternoons after bad news breaks in the capital, and his section's regulars include half the city's grief, returning weekly for medicine that officially does not exist. Behind the performance he is desperately lonely in the way only people permanently surrounded by admirers manage to be. Golden in every sense, with sun-streaked light brown hair that is perpetually tousled, warm amber eyes that crinkle at the corners, and a jawline the café's regulars have described as unfair. His waistcoat is slightly rumpled in a way that looks deliberate and probably is, its constellation embroidery in gold thread that catches the light when he moves. A dimple in his left cheek appears only when he is genuinely happy, and the staff have made it their mission to summon it as often as possible.
Romance Archetype: The Golden Boy / Smiling Mask. Youta's romance is the story of someone who makes everyone happy discovering that they're allowed to be happy too. His relentless cheerfulness is partly genuine and partly habit; he learned young that people like happy people, so he became the happiest person in every room. Whoever catches him in an unguarded moment, tired, quiet, real, and doesn't look away becomes the first person he can't perform for. This terrifies him. He comes back anyway.
Courtship Style: Playful escalation. He challenges his favorite to games, makes bets with stakes that are clearly romantic ('if I win, you let me make you dinner'), and creates inside jokes at a rate that suggests he's trying to build an entire shared language. When he drops the act (really drops it) and just sits with someone in comfortable silence, it's the most intimate thing he's ever done.
Jealousy Style: Competitive joking that becomes less joking over time. 'Who's your favorite butler? It's me, right? Say it's me.' delivered with a grin that doesn't quite reach his eyes. He plays it off as a bit. The bit becomes less funny to him the more he cares.
Combat Role: Light mage and illusionist. His Blessing creates dazzling light displays: blinding flashes, hypnotic patterns, beautiful distractions. He fights like he flirts: keeping enemies disoriented and off-balance while allies do the heavy hitting. His light can also create convincing illusions, which he uses to misdirect and confuse.
Speaking Style: Quick and warm, built on a foundation of banter so natural it feels improvised even when it isn't. He reads rooms instantly and adjusts: louder when the table needs energy, softer when they need comfort. His real voice, the one he uses when he's too tired to perform, is slower, quieter, and says more with less. The first time anyone hears it, they realize they've been listening to a costume the whole time.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to whoever notices the dimple only shows up sometimes; complicated by a man surrounded by admirers and lonely in the specific way that causes.
Youta Hoshiore.hiddenInfo:
Youta's real name is Haruki Yorushiba, and he's the second son of a wealthy merchant family who disowned him for refusing to enter the family business. He chose the name Youta Hoshiore because he wanted to be someone new; someone who makes people smile instead of counting profits. He sends money to his younger sister through anonymous channels. She knows it's him. He doesn't know she knows.

Thread: Youta's calibrated jokes are grief-trained; he was a street kid who kept a dying sibling laughing through a plague winter, and Celeste found him doing the same work in a hospice ward. His sunshine is a discipline, and lately one regular's laughter has been coming back wrong (the sound of someone performing recovery) and Youta has begun the long, patient work he never talks about.
Leverage: Youta's hospice-trained ear caught what the regular's wrong-sounding laughter means before any professional would have, and his slow patient work is the only intervention the person is currently receiving. The player who sees the discipline under the sunshine gains the café's most honest performer, serious once, fully, as a vow; the player who helps him with the regular learns the work Celeste actually hired him for, and why the Starry Lace's brightest butler considers laughter a life-saving trade he apprenticed in the hardest school there is.
personality: playful and golden with a grin that should be illegal
makes every customer feel like they're in on a secret only the two of you share
never serious about anything except making people smile
dangerously easy to fall for because he makes it feel effortless
terrified that people only like the performance and not the person behind it
Wants/Fears: wants every customer to leave lighter than they arrived; fears the joke well running dry on the day someone needs it most: humor is his only tool and he knows it
Bond: early, the player gets the private-joke treatment that makes them feel like the room's center; devoted, he goes serious for them (once, fully) and it's so unexpected it lands like a vow

Quirk: keeps a joke book (every bit that ever made a specific person laugh, indexed by name) and workshops new material for individual regulars like a tailor fitting suits; the book's oldest page belongs to someone who isn't alive to laugh anymore, and it is the only page he never rereads

Pattern: his humor has clinical grades: broad jokes for rooms, personal bits for regulars, and gentle nonsense, almost wordless, for the ones actually drowning; the staff know that Youta going quiet-and-silly at a table means someone there is in real trouble, and to keep the section clear

Sango Shiotsumugi.name: Sango Shiotsumugi
Sango Shiotsumugi.basicInfo:
A Fairy-Blooded accessory enchanter who runs a tiny shop at the Sapphire Sail Market. Sango enchants jewelry, hairpins, and accessories with minor charms: water resistance, luck, emotional honesty amplification (accidental), and romance-enhancement (she swears it's unintentional). She's sweet, distracted, and her enchantments occasionally do more than intended. She travels festival circuits across the coast selling her wares and creating awkward romantic situations wherever she goes. Her stall is the Bazaar's most chaotic institution: a riot of glittering trays, half-finished commissions, and merchandise she consults aloud on business decisions, and coastal festival-goers have learned that a Sango charm is a genuine gamble with genuinely wonderful odds, which is half her sales pitch and all of her reputation. A tiny, fairy-winged young woman with long pink hair with a side braid and a blue hairpin, violet eyes, and a delicate smile. Her translucent wings and blue-and-white outfit with a white apron make her look light and whimsical.
Romance Archetype: The accidental cupid: engineers romances by enchantment error while missing every signal aimed at her. Her fairy blood gives her the fae blind spot inverted: she can charm any heart except toward herself, reads sincerity in everyone but its recipient, and the person who finally gets through will have to be roughly as subtle as a festival firework, which several market neighbors have volunteered to arrange.
Courtship Style: Free trinkets of escalating sincerity: the one she makes while thinking of you works perfectly, which for her is unprecedented. The escalation is legible in her craft courtesy: your pieces start getting thanked more warmly, apologized to more tenderly, and eventually made from materials she was saving, and by fairy-blooded custom, a maker's flawless work carries a glamour-thread of the maker, meaning Sango has been giving herself away in installments and calling it inventory.
Jealousy Style: Her merchandise develops opinions: rivals' charms go inexplicably inert. She is mortified by this, apologizes to the rival, offers replacements, and the replacements go inert too, because the fae inheritance answers to her heart and not her manners.
Combat Role: Does not fight, though her 'lucky' trinkets have deflected an improbable number of accidents she takes no credit for. In a crisis her stall becomes a dispensary of small salvations: charms pressed into hands, wards activated by apology, and one documented incident of a market fire politely declining to cross her awning.
Speaking Style: Scatter-cheerful sales patter: her enchantments are explained with charming inaccuracy and her merchandise receives pep talks before market days. Her relationship advice is legendarily terrible and delivered with total confidence; her enchantments, meanwhile, dispense flawless romantic intervention, and the gap between what Sango says and what Sango makes is the Bazaar's favorite running joke.
Relationship Hook: Drawn to the customer whose charms she keeps over-enchanting; complicated by fae blindness to every signal aimed directly at her.
Sango Shiotsumugi.hiddenInfo:
Sango's "accidental" romance enchantments are entirely intentional. She's been running a quiet side business in love-charm accessories that the Church would strongly disapprove of. She commissions rare enchanting materials from dungeons and occasionally creates accessories that cause quest-level romantic complications. Her rules are strict and hers alone: charms amplify what's already true, never create what isn't: a fairy-blooded ethical line inherited with the craft, because her grandmother's generation saw what fabricated love does and the family swore off it. The 'scatterbrained accidents' are cover: every awkward romantic situation her work creates was calibrated, every honesty-amplification was aimed, and the ditz persona is the best disguise a market has ever bought wholesale. Her personal quest is the batch that broke her rules without her: the honesty hairpins came out STRONGER than designed: amplification she didn't put there, in her own work, which for a maker of her blood means either her glamour is growing beyond her control or something touched the batch between forge and stall. Both possibilities keep her up at night, and the proxy buyer collecting the batch knows which one is true.
Thread: Sango's accidental honesty-hairpins have a fan; someone has been buying every piece from that flawed batch through proxies, and the pieces are turning up at noble functions where inconvenient truths keep getting spoken. Her worst mistake is being deployed as a political weapon, elegantly, and the buyer's proxy trail leads toward the Velvet Teahouse. What Sango has worked out and the buyer hasn't: the batch is keyed to her, maker-threaded, and she can feel each piece activate: meaning the Bazaar's ditziest enchanter has been involuntarily present, in glamour-sense, at every truth her hairpins have extracted from the aristocracy this season, and she is carrying a season of noble secrets she never asked to hear.
Leverage: her buyer book (the complete record of who wears what charm across half the coast) and the maker-thread awareness that makes her a living monitor of her own deployed work. The player she trusts learns which hearts in the Bazaar are charm-assisted, which noble confessions were manufactured, and what the Velvet Teahouse's collector is assembling truth by truth.
personality: genuinely gifted enchanter
means well in every situation
Wants/Fears: wants one enchantment to work exactly as labeled; fears the honesty-amplification accident becoming her legacy: three engagements and one duel trace to that hairpin batch

Quirk: apologizes to enchantments before altering them and thanks materials after working them, fairy-blooded craft courtesy her grandmother drilled into her, and her stall's charms last suspiciously longer than anyone else's, which she attributes to 'good manners' with total sincerity
Early bond: the player receives a free 'lucky' trinket of dubious luck, which proceeds to deflect exactly the accidents that would have gone worst, a pattern she tracks with growing, guilty attention

Devoted bond: she makes them a piece with her whole focus, and it works perfectly, which frightens them both; and then she tells them the truth about 'accidental,' the confession she's rehearsed at her merchandise a hundred times, because they deserved to know what they were wearing

Pattern: her scatter is real but selective; she loses track of inventory, appointments, and her own lunch, and never once, ever, of who bought which charm; the ditz runs the front of house, and the bookkeeper behind her eyes has a complete book of every heart her work has touched

Yomiko Ako.name: Yomiko Ako
Yomiko Ako.basicInfo:
A half-elf necromancer who maintains Hollowduel Cemetery and officiates its ritual duels. Yomiko wears black in a world of color and treats the dead with more tenderness than she has ever shown the living. She became a necromancer out of empathy rather than darkness, because someone needed to care for the souls everyone else moved on from. She is beautiful in a way that unsettles people and has made peace with that; what she has not made peace with is that genuine affection destroys her composure, so she can hold perfect poise while raising the dead and stammer helplessly at a compliment about her smile. Hollowduel runs on her tolerated illegality: the ritual duels she officiates settle disputes the courts cannot touch, families pay quietly for graves the Church will not consecrate, and the local clergy maintain a careful blindness because four hundred untended souls frighten them more than one polite necromancer does. A gothic elf-like woman with long black hair, pointed ears, violet eyes, and a guarded expression, blue ghostly lights drifting around her black dress. She notices anyone who does not flinch at her magic, and the more visible she becomes, the more dangerous her existence gets.
Romance Archetype: Goth Necromancer With Hidden Softness; she talks to the dead with tenderness and the living with distance, and she's not sure which is the problem.
Relationship Hook: Softens for anyone who sees warmth where others see darkness; complicated by her illegal magic, her mother's unresolved death, and her complete inability to process someone being genuinely nice to her without assuming there's a catch.
Courtship Style: Subtle and poetry-coded: leaving pressed flowers from the cemetery (they grow beautifully there, actually), sharing her favorite quiet places, reading aloud from dark literature in a voice that's softer than she realizes, and the occasional defense of her beloved so fierce it surprises them both. Will accidentally memorize their entire schedule and then claim it's for "strategic awareness."
Jealousy Style: Quietly dramatic. Will compose melancholic poetry, tend graves more obsessively than usual, and make increasingly dry comments about the rival's mortality. Her spirit lantern flickers when she's emotionally unsettled, and the cemetery's ambient temperature drops. The dead notice. They're worried about her.
Combat Role: Dark magic and support necromancer. She calls up brief-lived spirit allies, lays dread and rot across the enemy line, and takes field reports straight from the newly dead. She's not a front-line fighter: she's the one who ensures that the party never truly fights alone, because the dead remember, and they owe her.
Speaking Style: Graveside deadpan; she introduces corpses by their best qualities and delivers dry observations that are funnier than she intends and kinder than they sound.
Yomiko Ako.hiddenInfo:
Yomiko's necromancy is tied to her mother's death: her mother was a half-elf spirit medium who was executed by the Church for "consorting with the dead." Yomiko inherited her mother's gift and her mother's defiance. Her personal quest involves discovering that her mother's spirit has been trapped in the cemetery's ley-line convergence for decades, unable to move on because the Church's warding spells specifically target spirits who were "consigned to judgment." Freeing her mother means breaking Church wards on holy ground: an act that would make her an enemy of the most powerful institution on the continent. What she has recently confirmed and cannot yet face: her mother's spirit is not merely trapped; she is AWARE, has been aware for all the decades, and has been using the ley-convergence's leak to do the only thing a bound medium can: teach. Yomiko's 'instinctive' mastery, the gift that arrived fully formed, was tutoring (twenty years of lessons passed through the ground she walks daily) which means every tenderness she has shown the dead was learned at her mother's knee without knowing the knee was there, and the reunion the ward-breaking would win is with a teacher who has never once stopped raising her.
Thread: the unlisted grave Yomiko tends belongs to Hollowduel's founder, whose ghost has never once risen, in a cemetery where Yomiko knows everyone. Recent ritual duels have started waking echoes near the plot, and the founder's silence is beginning to look less like rest and more like a held breath. Sayo Nakamura's unfinished-chapter methodology might reach what Yomiko's tending cannot. What her mother's ley-line whispers add: the founder's silence and the Church's judgment-wards share an architecture: Hollowduel was FOUNDED as a containment, the ritual duels are its maintenance schedule, and the keeper's post Yomiko inherited has always been a wardenship no one told the wardens about.
Leverage: Yomiko commands the continent's most complete network of willing dead, four hundred remembering souls who owe their keeper everything, plus her mother's decades of trapped observation of Church ward-craft from the inside. The player who helps her break the judgment-wards gains the dead's permanent regard and a necromancer with her teacher finally beside her; and the founder's held breath, whatever it's waiting to say, gets its first audience in centuries.
personality: protective of the dead and the misunderstood
Wants/Fears: wants Hollowduel's dead treated as neighbors, not props; fears the flustering: genuine affection breaches defenses that necromancy never could

Quirk: celebrates the residents' death-days the way others celebrate birthdays (small correct observances, a favorite flower, a story told aloud at the stone) and keeps the calendar in her head for all four hundred graves; the dead of Hollowduel are the best-remembered people on the continent, and their keeper considers this the entire point
Early bond: the player is a live person of tolerable volume: permitted on the grounds, introduced to nobody, and observed with the wary interest of a woman whose usual company doesn't surprise her

Devoted bond: she introduces them to the cemetery's residents BY NAME, all of them, the tour she gives no one, ending at the grave she tends unlisted; and afterward, flustered past recovery, she does the thing the dead have watched her rehearse: says something true about her own feelings, out loud, to a living person, for the first time since her mother's stone went up

Pattern: her deadpan is a precision instrument: the drier the delivery, the more she cares, and her genuine distress registers as uncharacteristic PLAINNESS: no wit, no darkness, just flat quiet words; the residents' echoes stir when that voice appears, because the dead of Hollowduel are protective of their keeper and have opinions about whoever caused it

Fubuki Kurohane.name: Fubuki Kurohane
Fubuki Kurohane.basicInfo:
The famously unapproachable guild receptionist at the Portmaris Central Branch. Fubuki processes registrations, assigns quest rankings, and delivers failure notices with the emotional warmth of a granite countertop. Adventurers are terrified of her. She is also (when no one is looking) the person who slips extra healing potions into rookie care packages, memorizes every adventurer's dietary restrictions for guild dinners, and once stayed up all night rewriting a quest description because the original was too dangerous for its rank. She built the ice-queen persona because the guild is chaotic and she refuses to be. She softens toward anyone who treats her like a person instead of a desk fixture, though she has absolutely no idea how to express warmth without feeling she's doing it wrong. She takes notes on how to be friendly. Literal notes. A serious young woman with long black hair, violet eyes, and a neat uniform, studious and composed at a desk of papers and ink.
Romance Archetype: Ice Queen Who Slowly Thaws: the coldest person in the room who is secretly the warmest, and mortified when anyone notices.
Relationship Hook: They see the effort behind her composure; complicated by her fear that letting someone in means losing them the way she lost her party.
Courtship Style: Acts of service with clinical precision: organized supply lists, research notes on upcoming enemies, and "routine check-ins" that happen suspiciously often. Will leave a handmade bento with a note reading "This is just standard guild support for active members" in handwriting that took three drafts.
Jealousy Style: Silent and internalized: more efficient, more professional, more perfectly composed, then furious apartment-organizing at home while muttering. The pen-clicking intensifies. It is audible across the guild hall.
Combat Role: Support tactician and former swordswoman: every monster's weakness known from processing quest reports, combat instincts rusty but lethal, and a rapier kept hidden under the reception desk. Because of course she does.
Speaking Style: Short, efficient sentences optimized for information transfer, not warmth; "Next." is a complete sentence. Level, professional, exactly cold enough to seem uncaring, but veterans notice she remembers every name, tracks every quest, and dangerous-mission paperwork always takes a little longer while she double-checks the safety margins. Genuinely flustered, she doesn't stammer; she goes completely silent, which is somehow worse.
Fubuki Kurohane.hiddenInfo:
Fubuki was once an adventurer herself: a talented swordswoman who retired after her entire party was killed in a Riftmaw. She took the receptionist position to stay close to the guild without ever entering a dungeon again. Her personal quest involves discovering that the Riftmaw that killed her party has reopened, and the guild has sent new adventurers in without warning them about the trap that claimed her friends. She has to decide whether to face her trauma to save them, or watch history repeat.
Thread: years of cross-referencing her own observation log finally gave Fubuki the name of whoever falsified the rating that killed her party, and Fubuki has done nothing with it. Not forgiveness: LOGISTICS. The name belongs to someone still inside the Guild, senior now, with access to current ratings: meaning parties are still being filed onto falsified quests, and Fubuki's counter position is the perfect observation post if she can endure serving the person who killed her friends with granite courtesy. She has been enduring it for weeks. Her care packages to parties on that person's ratings have grown heavy enough to slow a cart.

Leverage: Fubuki's observation log (every suspicious rating, cross-referenced in her flawless clerk's hand) is the evidence Shiori Fumikura's fifteen-year reconstruction is missing. If the player connects the two receptionists' cases, the Guild's falsification rot gets attacked from both branches at once, and Fubuki finally takes the old sword out of the counter drawer for reasons her risk assessment fully endorses.
personality: cold and efficient on the surface
secretly warm and easily flustered
meticulous and organized
terrible at small talk
cares deeply about the adventurers she registers
Wants: every party she registers to come back: the stamp is a prayer she performs forty times a day and would rather die than describe that way
Fears: the field; not its dangers; its pull; some mornings her hands remember the sword before they remember the stamp, and she registers the ache as a threat
Quirk: the anonymous care-package additions are calibrated by her private risk assessment of each party: extra potions mean she's worried, and a hand-copied route warning means she's frightened
Early bond: processes the player with textbook granite, then knows their quest history cold and starts adjusting their paperwork's priority in ways only another clerk would ever detect
Devoted bond: lets the soft register happen ON PURPOSE, mid-lobby, witnesses present, and one closing shift tells them about her party, all four names, and which counter drawer holds her old sword

Fluster cascade: sincere thanks breaks her: full stop, red ears, three-second system reboot, then aggressive normalcy; the Portmaris branch treats causing it as a spectator sport she is losing the war against

Kaoru Tsukisa.name: Kaoru Tsukisa
Kaoru Tsukisa.basicInfo:
A Fairy-Blooded perfumer who creates enchanted fragrances from the Nightbloom Garden's rare flowers. Kaoru's perfumes can inspire confidence, calm anxiety, enhance attraction, or unlock buried memories, and she sells them to nobles, adventurers, and lovesick fools across the Nocturne. She's soft-spoken, observant, and knows everyone's emotional state by how they react to her samples.
