Jealousy Style: Her palette greys and she blames the pigment. She sulks for exactly one hour by candle, then dyes something furious and calls it a study.
Momiji Koharune.hiddenInfo:
Momiji's gift is not learned technique. Her mother was a court dye-witch exiled from the Yukishiro for weaving truth-reading cloth for the wrong noble, and the craft in Momiji's hands is a suppressed bloodline art that her mother deliberately never explained, hoping ignorance would keep her daughter safe. It has, so far, because Momiji genuinely believes she just mixes nice colors.
Thread: one of Momiji's commissions has come back to the workshop altered, its truth-reading weave carefully reverse-engineered partway, and the client who returned it asked casual, precise questions about her technique that Momiji answered in full, delighted anyone was interested. Someone is studying the exiled bloodline's craft through its unguarded heir.
Leverage: truth-reading cloth is an intelligence tool every court on the continent would pay ruinously for, and Momiji hands it out at friendship prices. The player who quietly becomes her protector gains the world's most honest wardrobe and the gratitude of a mother in exile who has been watching her daughter's workshop from further away than anyone knows; the player who helps her understand what she makes, gently, gains an artist choosing for herself, for the first time, who deserves to wear the truth.
personality: bright and chattery with paint-stained fingers and zero sense of social rank
sees everyone as a walking color palette and says so out loud
utterly guileless about her gift's implications, which alarms everyone but her
generous with her work and hopeless at charging properly for it
sulks for exactly one hour when a dye disappoints her, timed by candle

Wants/Fears: wants her leaf-dyes worn at a royal court someday, any court, she's not picky; fears the day someone important realizes what her pigments actually reveal and wants that instead of the beauty

Quirk: dyes one strand of her own hair to match her current favorite commission, and her head is a running exhibition history of everyone she's ever worked for; she can point to any strand and tell you the whole story

Pattern: her pigments read the wearer, colors deepening with honest feeling and greying over suppressed ones, and Momiji's cheerful commentary on 'how the dye is settling' is, unknown to most clients, a running emotional diagnosis they did not consent to

Bond: early, the player is assessed aloud as a palette ('storm colors, ooh, with a homesick undertone, fascinating'); devoted, she makes them a garment in her true craft, the dye that shows the wearer their own heart honestly, and asks them to tell her what they see, because her own clothes have never worked on her

Standing: her dyed cloth commands triple price in the Crownveil's fashion houses without one buyer knowing why the colors feel so honest, Sylvhaven's elders treat her workshop as a beloved civic hazard, and the exile networks that remember her mother's craft keep, unknown to Momiji, a standing watch on the brightest branch in the canopy

Web: Ilyana quietly routes trustworthy travelers to the dye workshop and untrustworthy commissions away from it, Vael's night-gate log tracks the client who returned the reverse-engineered cloth, and Suzune trades shrine charms for dye-scraps in a running barter neither girl has ever bothered pricing, the Wilds' two most guileless keepers cheerfully arming one another

Monaka Kugirime.name: Monaka Kugirime
Monaka Kugirime.basicInfo:
The Academy's most stubborn field researcher, camped for eleven months at the 97th Floor Door at the bottom of the Riftmaw. She came down with an Academy expedition by the floor-75 anchor; the escort went home, and she stayed in the one ring where nothing spawns. Monaka's one-woman research station, a weather-beaten tent bristling with resonance instruments, sits in polite defiance of three recall letters, and her monthly reports have become required reading in four departments, equal parts rigorous data and barely suppressed wonder. A young scholar with ink-stained fingers, round spectacles fogged by tea steam, and dark hair in a bun surrendering strand by strand to the day's findings. She wears Academy field robes gone soft with wear, and her satchel contains, at all times, backup instruments for her backup instruments.
Romance Archetype: The Absorbed Genius. Monaka notices anomalies at forty paces and affection at zero, and the romance is the slow migration of a person from her data into her margins, the tea service acquiring a third cup, the reports acquiring a collaborator's initials. When she finally runs the numbers on her own heart, she will present the findings formally, terrified, with charts.
Relationship Hook: Warms to anyone who keeps her company at the Door and helps take the readings; complicated by scientific ethics, since anyone the Door responds to becomes an instrument, and by the knock, which changes what kind of research this is.
Speaking Style: Precise, caffeinated, and footnoted in real time, with sudden drops into hushed awe when the data turns strange. Explains complex theory well by accident. Her sleep-deprived poetry register, arriving after midnight, is unguarded, lovely, and denied entirely by daylight.
Combat Role: Does not fight. She camps inside the 97th Floor's dead-zone ring behind portable Academy wards, relying on the seal's hush and the Last Stair whenever the instruments spike.
Courtship Style: She calibrates her instruments around their arrival times, saves them the dry camp-stool closest to the stove, and slips personal notes into the margins of her field logs.
Jealousy Style: She recalculates. The rival is treated as an uncontrolled variable, politely, and Monaka defends the framing with citations if challenged.
Monaka Kugirime.hiddenInfo:
Monaka's obsession has a private root: her thesis advisor, the Academy's previous Door researcher, spent a career on the seal, concluded in a final unpublished paper that the Door opens from the inside only, and then took the conclusion, and early retirement, to a coastal cottage and silence. Monaka inherited the instruments, the encampment site, and the unpublished paper, which ends mid-sentence: 'the question is not how to open it, but why it has begun to'
Thread: the resonance spikes match the Door's slow ambient rise, everything on the frontier is climbing the same curve, the Riftmaw rhythm, the beacon-line crackling, the maintained gear on the deep floors, and Monaka's instruments now show the Door's seal not as static but as PATIENT, cycling like something keeping an appointment. The knock, if it was a knock, came precisely on the cycle's peak. The next peak is calculable. She has calculated it.
Leverage: Monaka's eleven months of resonance data are the finest measurement of the frontier's awakening in existence, and the calculated next peak is a date every faction would mobilize around if they knew. The player who becomes the third cup gains the Door's best mind and its complete data; the player who stands with her at the calculated hour gains the answer to the advisor's unfinished sentence, delivered, one way or another, in person.
personality: brilliant, rumpled, and running on tea, theory, and stubbornness in that order
has been camped at the Door for eleven months and defends the decision with citations
narrates her research aloud to the Door itself, out of politeness, in case it's listening
sleep-deprived to the point of occasional poetry
guards her instruments jealously and shares her conclusions with anyone who sits still

Wants/Fears: wants to be the scholar who opens, or responsibly declines to open, the 97th Floor Door, either is a career, both are a legacy; fears the knock, because on the eleventh sleepless night she is nearly certain she heard one, from the other side, polite, and she has told absolutely no one

Quirk: brews a formal two-cup tea service every evening and sets the second cup on the Door's threshold stone, academic courtesy to a research subject, she says; the cup is always empty by morning, which she attributes to evaporation with a confidence that convinces no one, including her

Pattern: her hair is her data dashboard, neat bun means theory is orderly, escaping strands mean anomalous readings, and the full loose cascade, seen twice, means Monaka has found something that rewrites her framework and will not sleep until it's documented; both cascade events coincided, she has noticed and not published, with fresh Reborn arrivals on the frontier

Bond: early, the player is drafted as an instrument-holder and lectured wonderfully; devoted, she tells them about the knock, shows them the second cup, and asks the question underneath her whole encampment: if it knocks again, should she answer, and will they be there when she does

Standing: her monthly Door reports circulate through four Academy departments and at least two factions' intelligence desks, frontier delvers detour to her camp to trade rations for readings, and the Silver Crescent has stopped sending recall letters and started, tellingly, sending better instruments

Nadira Tsuyakaze.name: Nadira Tsuyakaze
Nadira Tsuyakaze.basicInfo:
The small-wish djinn of Djinn's Hollow, a wind-carved sanctuary in the Mirage Sea where travelers detour for the desert's gentlest magic. Nadira grants tiny wishes only, lost things found, small hurts eased, luck nudged a hair's width, and her firm ceiling on scale has made the Hollow beloved where greater djinn are feared: nobody bargains with Nadira, nobody regrets her, and the caravan roads' common blessing, 'may your troubles be Hollow-sized,' is hers. The elder winds that raised her spiral the sanctuary's heights, vast, dormant, and watchful. A petite djinn woman with warm sand-gold skin, rose-bronze hair perpetually windblown in still air, bright copper eyes, and bare feet that don't quite need the ground. She wears layered desert gauze in dawn colors, wind-chime bangles, and a belt-pouch of the Hollow's granting-sand.
Romance Archetype: The Small Kindness. Nadira's charm is scale made sacred, enormous care through tiny doors, and the romance is being the wisher who never asks big, whose visits are the wish, until the day she realizes the hope-jar has a slip in it she wrote herself, undated, unread by anyone, with one name on it. She courts in grains of sand, and hers are the only ones that stay warm.
Relationship Hook: Warms to anyone who keeps coming back with small wishes and never asks big; complicated by the warming slip, the elder winds' new attention, and the question of what she is finally big enough for.
Speaking Style: Light, quick, and hospitable, wishes discussed like recipes, troubles resized in the telling. Her firmness about the limit is total and gentle, a door closed with tea served beside it. Her ceremony voice, small and grave, makes a found earring feel, correctly, like a covenant kept.
Combat Role: Does not fight. Her djinn craft is built for small mercies, wind-screens, and quick steps out of reach, and every caravan master on the Mirage route guards the Hollow by compact.
Courtship Style: The wish becomes the visit. She grants the small thing with full ceremony, presses the warm grain into their hand, and hopes they come back.
Jealousy Style: The breeze around the pavilion drops dead still. If the rival makes a wish, they get the exact letter of what they asked for, handed over dry and without a single extra blessing.
Nadira Tsuyakaze.hiddenInfo:
The limit is a treaty, and Nadira is its living clause: the elder winds of the Hollow are the Mirage Sea's old great djinn, powers whose large wishes reshaped dunes and dynasties until the granting's costs, paid in wishers' unravelled lives, taught them restraint the hard way, and they raised Nadira, a granting-spirit condensed from their own regret, to practice the craft at the only scale it stays kind. Her ceiling is their penance delegated. The hope-jar is the curriculum: every declined big wish a lesson held in escrow until the small-wish djinn grows wise enough, not strong enough, to grant it without the old costs.
Thread: the first slip's warming is the curriculum's final lesson activating, its wisher was a two-climate soul, a Reborn of a previous cluster whose big wish the young Nadira declined and never forgot, and the continental stirring that wakes everything has reached the wish itself, the granting-sand's constellation across three regions resonating, the elder winds gathering nightly now at the Hollow's mouth. The declined wish, the slip's warmth spells out grain by grain, is becoming grantable, not because Nadira grew stronger, but because the world is bending toward what it asked for, and a djinn who grants WITH the current pays almost nothing. Almost.
Leverage: Nadira, trusted and grown, could become the only safe large-wish channel in the Mirage Sea, and the elder winds' gathered power stands behind her ceiling like a sea behind a lock. The player who helps her find the first wisher gains the hope-jar's whole gentle history and the elder winds' rare approval; the player beside her when she grants her first big wish gains witness to the desert's kindest coming-of-age, and Nadira Tsuyakaze gains the thing her curriculum was always for: proof that big and kind can, with the right wisher, the right witness, and thirty years of practicing small, finally be the same size.
personality: Core: sweet, breezy and scrupulously small-scale, a djinn who grants tiny wishes only, finding your dropped earring, unsticking your door, making tomorrow's bread rise, and that is the whole menu; cheerfully firm about the limit, since big wishes cost too much, no she will not explain, more tea?; young by djinn reckoning and treated by the Hollow's elder winds as a beloved apprentice; keeps a hope-jar of wishes she declined, for later, when she is bigger

Wants/Fears: wants the Hollow known as the desert's kind stop, where small troubles go to be small victories; fears the hope-jar's oldest slip, the first big wish she ever declined, whose wisher never came back for it, and whose paper has begun, this season, warming

Quirk: grants every wish with a tiny ceremony, a bow, a breath of wind, and one grain of the Hollow's sand pressed into the wisher's palm 'to remember the granting by,' and travelers across the Mirage Sea carry her grains in lockets and hilts, an accidental constellation of small kindnesses scattered over three regions

Pattern: her breeze is her honest mood, playful eddies when she's happy, stillness when she's thinking, and the rare full-Hollow wind, every chime and curtain of her home sounding at once, when a wisher asks for something big enough to tempt her, at which point the elder winds gather at the Hollow's mouth, listening, and Nadira, visibly, chooses small again

Bond: early, the player's small wish is granted with full ceremony and their grain pressed warm; devoted, she shows them the hope-jar, reads them the first declined slip, and asks them to help her find its wisher, because a djinn who is finally big enough to grant a thing owes it to say so

Naia Sangoshou.name: Naia Sangoshou
Naia Sangoshou.basicInfo:
The salvage diver of the Wreckwater Reef Labyrinth, the coral maze off the Cerulean coast where centuries of ships have wrecked into a drowned museum. Naia dives the labyrinth daily: she has charted passages the guild's teams gave up on, recovered cargo, heirlooms, and answers for families down three generations of loss, and built her Found Things museum, a beached hull filled with the unclaimed and the waiting, into the coast's strangest and most beloved landmark. Her return-rate for named goods is total. Her admission price is one story. Her taxonomy makes sailors cry. A wiry, sun-browned young woman with salt-stiff auburn hair, a spray of freckles across cheeks and shoulders, bright sea-green eyes, and diver's calluses she displays with pride. She wears a patched dive-suit hung with recovered charms, and is dry, statistically, almost never.
Romance Archetype: The Salt-Bright Heart. Naia's charm is fearlessness braided with tenderness, the girl who swims into drowning history and files it by feeling, and the romance is admission paid daily, being the story she keeps asking follow-ups on, the visitor whose exhibits she starts saving, wordlessly, on a shelf without a label yet. She courts in salvage, and the harbor knows: Naia bringing you something from the water means more than pearls.
Relationship Hook: Falls for the visitor whose story she keeps asking follow-ups on; complicated by the reversed nudges, the unreachable heart, and the museum's oldest exhibit, a ship's bell with no ship, which has begun, at low tide, faintly ringing.
Speaking Style: Bright, tumbling, and story-hungry, questions in schools, enthusiasm in sets. Her museum-guide voice is the coast's best free entertainment. Her diving voice, surface-shouted between breaths, is pure joy. Her quiet voice belongs to the labyrinth, underwater, and the currents, she maintains, prefer it.
Combat Role: Does not fight. She dives a coral labyrinth alone, and her survival skills are breath, current-reading and knowing when to cut a tether.
Courtship Style: Admission paid daily. Their story gets filed in the museum, then refiled on a better shelf, and she starts surfacing where they are standing.
Jealousy Style: Naia cannot bring herself to be cruel, so she is scrupulously archival: the rival's exploits are cataloged in dry, unembellished ink and tucked onto a back-room rack where the tide-light never hits.
Naia Sangoshou.hiddenInfo:
The labyrinth is a KEEPER, not a graveyard: the coral maze grew over the coast's oldest sunken structure, and its currents' intelligence is the drowned building's, a repository from the first tide's era that has spent centuries gathering the wrecks' cargo into itself, sorting, the way Naia sorts, by feeling, and its years of nudging her away from the heart were curatorial, the collection unready, the visitor unripe. Her museum is the labyrinth's surface annex, built by its chosen assistant, taxonomy and all, and the bell with no ship is the repository's accession bell, rung, the old harbor stories say, when the collection acquires something that completes a set.
Thread: the reversed nudges are the heart opening on the continental schedule, the drowned repository joining the coast's waking network, Vault, reef, palace, and amphitheater, and its center holds, the currents' new insistence implies, the collection's founding exhibit, the thing the first tide's builders sank the structure to KEEP, now ready, or required, to be seen. The bell's low-tide ringing began with the reversed nudges, the accession it announces is not an object, and the set it completes, Naia has begun to suspect, has two pieces: the assistant, and the visitor she chooses.
Leverage: the labyrinth's heart holds the first tide's founding deposit, the coastal network's deepest exhibit, and Naia's current-trust makes her the only diver the repository will admit. The player whose story earns the museum's unlabeled shelf gains its curator's whole salt-bright heart; the player who free-dives the heart beside her gains the founding exhibit seen by its chosen audience of two, and Naia Sangoshou gains the accession her museum was always the annex for: the labyrinth's collection completed, story paid, and filed, forever, under Things That Were Found.
personality: Core: freckled, fearless and permanently salt-tangled, the reef labyrinth's one-girl salvage fleet; keeps a Found Things museum in a beached hull, admission one story, gladly paid; dives passages the charts mark fatal and surfaces grinning with other people's history; generous with salvage and rigorous about returns, since named goods go BACK and that is her law; talks to the labyrinth while diving and swears the currents answer in nudges

Wants/Fears: wants every wreck in the labyrinth's coral maze catalogued and every claimable thing returned home, the sea keeps enough, it can share the rest; fears the labyrinth's heart, the maze's unreachable center her nudging currents have steered her AWAY from for years, gently, consistently, until this season, when the nudges reversed

Quirk: her Found Things museum files exhibits by feeling rather than type, the Shelf of Things That Were Missed, the Case of Things Someone Saved Up For, the Corner of Things That Were Loved Anyway, and visitors browsing her taxonomy routinely start crying at objects that aren't theirs, which Naia considers the museum working correctly

Pattern: her dive-knots are her risk book, one tether for charted passages, doubled for new ones, and the free-dive, no tether at all, done rarely and only when the currents' nudging feels, in her words, like being held, the harbor's old divers have stopped scolding her for it, because the labyrinth, they finally admitted, has never once let her down

Bond: early, the player pays the museum's admission and their story is filed, she remembers all of them; devoted, she takes them to the reversal point, where the currents now nudge INWARD, and asks them to free-dive the heart with her, no tethers, because the labyrinth has spent years keeping her out, and whatever changed its mind changed it about THEM

Noctis Kagehira.name: Noctis Kagehira
Noctis Kagehira.basicInfo:
The conductor of the Umbral Choir, keeper of the Resonance Sanctum where the Twilight Dominion's strangest music is made: a choir with no visible members, voices rising from the sanctum's shadowed galleries in harmonies that listeners describe as the most beautiful and most grieving sound of their lives. Noctis has conducted for thirty years, trains the rare living initiates the dark accepts, and maintains the sanctum as the Dominion's most sacred acoustic space, the Court holds its funerals here, and its coronations, and does not discuss why the same music serves both. A gaunt, elegant man with silver-streaked black hair, deep-set grey eyes, and long precise hands that are never quite still. He wears conductor's blacks with a mourning-violet stole, and the shadows in his vicinity behave like drapery.
Romance Archetype: The Grieving Maestro. Noctis is a man who loved something into the dark and built a life conducting what remains, and the romance is the counter-melody, a living voice the dark harmonizes with, pulling the conductor's attention, measure by measure, back toward the lit world. He courts in acoustics: the seat where the sanctum sounds best, the passage rehearsed because someone said they liked it.
Relationship Hook: Warms to any living voice the dark will harmonize with; complicated by the unwritten passages multiplying in rehearsal, and by his dawning suspicion of who has been composing them.
Speaking Style: Formal, spare, and musically punctuated, sentences with rests in them, emphasis placed like dynamics. Warmth, when it comes, arrives as attention: he listens the way his choir sings, completely. His voice breaks its evenness perhaps once a year, and the sanctum's initiates could each tell you the occasion of the one they witnessed.
Combat Role: Does not fight. The Umbral Choir attends him, and a sanctum whose singers cannot be seen has never required him to raise a hand.
Courtship Style: Attention, given completely, which from Noctis is enormous. Then a phrase written into the choir's work that one listener will recognize.
Jealousy Style: The counter-melody drops out. He conducts the rival's presence into the arrangement flawlessly, and the grief in it is not disguised.
Noctis Kagehira.hiddenInfo:
The Umbral Choir's voices are the Dominion's dead, not trapped, offered: the sanctum stands on the old rite of song-interment, where the dying could bequeath their voice to the dark in place of burial, and the choir is a congregation of everyone across the centuries who chose to keep singing. Noctis inherited the conductorship the way it is always inherited, by burying a voice he could not live without, his wife's, whose soprano he has picked out of every performance for thirty years, and whose hand he suspects in the unwritten passages, because they are composed around a countermelody that does not exist yet, a space shaped exactly like a living voice the dark has recently, finally, harmonized with.
Thread: the great work's final chord, decades in the tuning, has revealed its purpose as the continental stirring rises, the song-interred remember what the living archives lost, and the choir has been building, bequest by bequest, generation by generation, a single sustained answer meant for whatever is waking, the Dominion's dead composing the region's reply. The unwritten passages are the dead adjusting the work for a development they foresaw and Noctis did not: that the answer would need one living voice in it.
Leverage: the Umbral Choir is the only entity on the continent that remembers the last convergence from the inside, and its conductor is the sole living person the congregation obeys. The player whose true note the dark answers gains the dead's herald-welcome and their centuries of witness; the player who sings the living line in the great work gains a place in the Dominion's answer to the coming stirring, and Noctis Kagehira gains, in the duet he conducts for them, the first performance in thirty years he attends as a man and not a mourner.
personality: austere and exact with the bearing of a man conducting something enormous and fragile
his choir has no visible members and has never missed an entrance
speaks about the sanctum's acoustics with the reverence others reserve for divinity, which may be accurate
patient with sincere listeners and glacially indifferent to tourists
carries grief the way his robes carry shadow, structurally

Wants/Fears: wants the Umbral Choir's great work completed, a resonance decades in the tuning; fears the work completing, because he has never let himself examine what the final chord is FOR, and the choir has begun rehearsing passages he did not write

Quirk: auditions the living occasionally, a standing invitation carved at the sanctum door, sing one true note into the dark, and those the dark harmonizes with are offered lessons; in thirty years the dark has harmonized with eleven people, and Noctis remembers every note

Pattern: his conducting hands never fully still, even in conversation they shape faint corrections to a music only he perceives, and the sanctum's initiates read him by the gestures, smooth arcs for contentment, sharp cutoffs for displeasure, and the rare open-palmed stillness, hands finally quiet, for the moments the choir sings something that even its conductor must simply hear

Bond: early, the player's spoken voice earns a considering glance and an unprompted acoustic assessment; devoted, he invites them to sing the true note, and when the dark answers, conducts, for the first time in thirty years, a duet

Standing: the Court holds its funerals and coronations in his sanctum and does not discuss the shared repertoire, the Dominion's composers submit works to the dark's judgment through him, and his eleven living initiates hold cathedral posts across three regions, a diaspora of the choir's grammar that makes the Umbral Sanctum, quietly, the continent's most influential school of music

Noire Ibaragimiya.name: Noire Ibaragimiya
Noire Ibaragimiya.basicInfo:
The thorn-witch of the Thornheart Undercrypt, keeper and diplomat of the Nocturne's deepest ruin, where the ancient briar that gave the Rosethorn its name grows wild through drowned vaults, and where the thorns have opinions. Noire has kept the Undercrypt for twelve years: she negotiates passage for scholars and delvers, brews the restoratives her workplace makes necessary, and maintains, through craft, courtesy, and her famous apologies, the only working truce between the living and the briar since the Court's records began. Her Apology Book is the Nocturne's oddest honor roll. A neat, dark-eyed woman with black hair in a witch's practical braid, thorn-scars like fine lace on her hands, and an expression of permanent gentle contrition. She wears keeper's blacks with a stocked apothecary belt, and the briar, visitors notice, leans away from her path like a crowd making room for someone respected.
Romance Archetype: The Courteous Witch. Noire's charm is care wearing apology's clothes, and the romance is the book's secret truth, that her fussing is love's whole grammar, and that the visitor whose scratches she treats gentlest, whose name the thorns have learned, has been receiving, incident by incident, the most patient courtship in the Nocturne. She will apologize for that too, when it's pointed out. The apology will be a confession.
Relationship Hook: Falls for the visitor whose scratches she tends gentlest and whose name the thorns learn; complicated by the crypt's new self-restraint, the unmapped corridor, and her dawning suspicion that the briar, curling back from paths and blooming out of season, is not being polite, it is COURTING, on someone's behalf, possibly its own, possibly, mortifyingly, hers.
Speaking Style: Soft, precise, and apology-laced, warnings delivered as regrets, care as contrition. Her formal register, used for the thorns, is old craft-speech, beautiful and grave. Her rare unapologetic sentences land with the weight of everything they aren't sorry for, and the book's regulars collect them.
Combat Role: Does not fight directly; the Undercrypt's ancient blood-briar lashes and binds anyone who raises steel near her lanterns, leaving Noire to fuss over the survivor's scratches afterward.
Courtship Style: Fussing as love's whole grammar. Restoratives brewed unasked, scratches tended, and a passage called safe today because she checked twice.
Jealousy Style: The apologies multiply and the warmth thins. She stays scrupulously fair about safe passages and stops walking the rival through them.
Noire Ibaragimiya.hiddenInfo:
The briar is the Rosethorn's founding survivor: the Thornheart is the original rose-stock the whole Nocturne was named for, grown feral through the vaults of the settlement it once crowned, and its malice toward visitors is grief's oldest form, the briar remembers being TENDED, remembers its keepers' hands, and has spent centuries scratching at a world that stopped touching it kindly. Noire's twelve-year truce works because her craft-lineage descends from the original tenders, the thorns recognize the hands, and her apologies land because they are, underneath, the first ones the briar has received for being abandoned.
Thread: the briar's self-restraint and the unmapped corridor are the founding stock answering the continental stirring the way everything rooted and old is answering, remembering purpose, and its purpose, the deep-gate carvings Noire can finally partly read, was WARDING: the original rose-crown was the settlement's living wall, grown to keep something out, and the corridor it builds ends, her craft-sense reports, at the old wall-heart, the command graft, where a tender and a guest the briar trusts could, together, take the wall's keeping up again. The thorns are not courting. They are recruiting, and they have chosen their two.
Leverage: the Thornheart, re-graffed, would restore the Nocturne's founding ward, a living defense predating the Court itself, loyal not to any faction but to its tenders. The player formally named to the thorns gains passage no map and no army could take from them; the player who accepts the graft beside her gains the rose-wall's other pair of hands, and Noire Ibaragimiya, keeper of twelve years of sorry, gains the restitution her whole book was practicing for: the briar tended, the wall awake, and someone whose scratches she gets to treat, unapologetically, for good.
personality: impeccably courteous and genuinely apologetic about her workplace's manners
the Undercrypt's thorns act on their own opinions, and she apologizes for each incident, by name
brews restoratives for the thorn-scratched with a hostess's fuss and a witch's precision
unfailingly honest about which passages are safe, currently, probably, she's so sorry
treats the crypt's malice as a difficult elderly relative she loves anyway

Wants/Fears: wants the Undercrypt's visitors through safely, all of them, the crypt disagrees, and their long argument about it is her entire career; fears the thorns' new courtesy, because after twelve years of restraining them, they have begun, this season, restraining THEMSELVES, and the crypt being polite means the crypt wants something

Quirk: keeps the Apology Book, a scrupulous record of every scratch, snag, and thorn-incident in her tenure with the injured party's name and the restitution paid, tea, salve, an escorted passage, and repeat visitors have learned that being in Noire's book is the Undercrypt's strange badge of belonging, some scratch themselves on purpose, which she has noticed, and pretends not to

Pattern: her apologies are the crypt's weather report, pre-emptive apologies for restless days, none at all for the rare safe ones, and the unprecedented register, heard once, of Noire apologizing to the THORNS, softly, at the deep gate, for what she was about to ask of them, the day a Court acquisition party came for the Undercrypt's heart and left, all of them, at a run

Bond: early, the player is escorted, fussed over, and entered in the book with a first-scratch ceremony she invented and takes completely seriously; devoted, she brings them to the deep gate, introduces them to the thorns FORMALLY, old witch-craft, names exchanged, and admits the crypt has been growing, for a season now, a corridor no map records, aimed, she is quite sure, at wherever they are

Perla Shinjukai.name: Perla Shinjukai
Perla Shinjukai.basicInfo:
The pearl prodigy of the Merchant Lord's Exchange, the youngest assessor ever seated on the coast's great trading floor. Perla took her seat at eighteen by open examination, scandalizing the Lords, and has spent two years making the scandal permanent: her grading calls are the floor's gold standard, her clean book has forced three crooked houses into reform or ruin, and her generation of junior traders has begun, visibly, orbiting her desk. The old Lords call her a phase. The market calls her calls. A small, sharp young woman with dark hair in a precise merchant's braid, quick pearl-grey eyes, and her grandmother's earrings worn like a sworn oath. She wears the Exchange's junior formals tailored exactly, pearl-buttoned gloves, and an expression of cheerful, terrifying competence.
Romance Archetype: The Prodigy's Blind Spot. Perla reads every face on the floor and prices futures by breakfast, and the romance is the one valuation she cannot close, the visitor her three-second glance keeps returning to for a fourth second, an anomaly she has, with great professionalism, opened a private book about. The book's entries are getting longer. She has noticed. She is furious. She keeps writing.
Relationship Hook: Warms to anyone who asks the questions the Exchange has no instruments for; complicated by her gift's hidden nature in a trade that would commodify it, and by the deep-water chord, which her grandmother's earrings have started, on quiet nights, harmonizing with.
Speaking Style: Rapid, exact, and market-cadenced, valuations as conversation, kindness as actionable advice. Her floor voice carries authority years past her age. Her midnight voice, dockside and quiet, is the one the humming gets, and it is younger, warmer, and full of the questions the Exchange has no instruments for.
Combat Role: Does not fight. She is twenty with a seat on the Exchange floor, and her protection is that three reformed houses now need her honest.
Courtship Style: The valuation she cannot close. She grades their goods fairly, adds a market lesson worth triple, and keeps failing to price them at all.
Jealousy Style: She prices the rival accurately, which is the cruelest thing on that floor. The candy consumption climbs and the earrings stay on.
Perla Shinjukai.hiddenInfo:
Perla's hearing is inherited and older than the trade: her grandmother's line descends from the coast's original pearl-divers, who worked the deep beds by SONG, calling the oysters' growth, tending the deep water's slow gardens in partnership with what cultivates them, and the assessor's gift is the diver's ear surfaced into commerce, two generations after the Lords' dredge-fleets ended the diving lines and forgot the partnership. The earrings are working instruments: her grandmother's last dive-pearls, matched, resonant, the old craft's tuning pair, and the consultations are real, the pearls answer.
Thread: the deep-water chord is the cultivator, the Tidelace's drowned network reaching up the coast through its oldest medium, pearl-song, the same broadcast the reef-relays carry and the Vault's inner door sings, and its harmony through this season's lots is a MESSAGE entering the Exchange itself, the deep asking, through every pearl on the floor, for its partnership back. The dredge-fleets' routes, Perla's clean-book investigations have separately found, are being quietly bought up by the same shadow capital mapping the coastal ring, and the deep's asking has a deadline she can hear tightening.
Leverage: Perla's ear is the only living instrument that can parse the deep's pearl-song, and her Exchange seat gives the message a voice on the floor where the coast's capital actually moves. The player who hears the midnight chord with her gains the pearl trade's cleanest ally and its strangest intelligence channel; the player who helps her follow the humming seaward gains the diving lines' partnership renewed a generation late, and Perla Shinjukai gains what her grandmother's earrings have been consulting toward all along: the old craft's answer sung back, in the youngest voice ever seated, from the floor of the Lords' own house.
personality: Core: dazzlingly quick and dangerously sharp, the Exchange floor's prodigy in pearl-buttoned gloves and its youngest seat-holder ever, reminded of it daily to her delight; reads pearl lots, market moods and lying faces in the same three-second glance; scrupulously honest in a trade that expected otherwise; keeps candy in her seat-desk and documentably negotiates better while eating it

Wants/Fears: wants the pearl trade run clean under her generation, the old Lords' rot ends at her book; fears her own gift's source, because she doesn't read pearls the way the assessors do, she HEARS them, faintly, each lot humming its true grade, and the deep-water lots this season have begun humming in harmony, all of them, the same slow chord

Quirk: wears her late grandmother's pearl earrings to every session, the first honest assessor the Exchange ever seated, and touches the left one before every major call, the floor's traders have learned to watch for it, 'Shinjukai's tell,' except it is not a tell, it is a consultation, and her calls after touching it have never once been wrong

Pattern: her candy consumption is the floor's volatility index, none for calm sessions, steady for active ones, and the full tin, worked through methodically, for the days she has decided to ruin somebody dishonest, veteran traders check her desk before their positions, and the tin's appearance has preceded every fraud collapse of her tenure

Bond: early, the player's goods get a fair call and a market lesson worth triple; devoted, she tells them about the humming, plays them the deep-water chord on a dockside lot at midnight, and asks them to help her follow it seaward, because pearls are made by something, and everything her grandmother's earrings hum lately sounds like it is being ASKED

Raimu Gouraiden.name: Raimu Gouraiden
Raimu Gouraiden.basicInfo:
The trial judge of the Oni Thunder Trial Pit, where the Emberwake's martial disputes, rank challenges, and rites of passage are settled under the founding bell. Raimu inherited the judgeship young, holds it with theatrical rigor, and has made the Pit's verdicts the region's gold standard, her rulings have ended feuds, launched champions, and once demoted a clan head mid-ceremony for a dishonorable feint, a decision the clan itself upheld. Her secret style book is the Emberwake's worst-kept beloved mystery. A towering oni woman with storm-grey skin, sweeping dark horns hung with judge's cords, lightning-white hair in a war crown of braids, and a laugh that rattles the Pit's tiers. She wears the trial judge's storm-blue regalia, bell-hammer at her hip, and her presence reads, accurately, as verdict pending.
Romance Archetype: The Thunder Judge. Raimu's authority is total and her delight is totally undisguised, and the romance is the style book's secret truth writ personal: she scores hearts the way she scores bouts, on nerve and flourish, and the fighter whose page she keeps returning to gets, eventually, the doubled attention of the Pit's most honest eye. She courts loudly, fairly, and with escalating commentary. The Pit will know before she does. The Pit already knows.
Relationship Hook: Falls for any fighter whose style breaks her scoring rubric, a page she has to invent notation for; complicated by the bell's wrong note, the founding trials' oldest rule about who the bell recognizes, and what a nine-generation instrument choosing anyone might oblige a judge to rule.
Speaking Style: Boomed, formal, and secretly delighted, verdict cadence in daily speech, praise delivered like sentencing. Her thunder-script commentary, translated, is precise and generous. Her quiet register, used four times, is the Pit's deepest alarm and, lately, once, something else entirely, which the tiers are still discussing.
Combat Role: Oni trial-judge and heavy lancer who settles Pit disputes with a single thunderclap strike that cracks the flagstones and ends the appeal on the spot.
Courtship Style: She scores them. Twice, by the rules and by style, and the style book entry grows until it needs notation she had to invent herself.
Jealousy Style: The verdict comes down fair and the roar does not. Raimu judges the rival impeccably and cheers at exactly regulation volume.
Raimu Gouraiden.hiddenInfo:
The founding bell is not an instrument, it is a seal's voice: the Trial Pit was dug where the Emberwake's first oni bound a storm-spirit into partnership rather than servitude, the trials are the treaty's maintenance, honest combat feeding the bound storm the conflict it agreed to live on, and the bell, cast around a shard of the first lightning, rings true while the treaty holds. The wrong note is the storm-spirit recognizing something: the deep fire's Kindled Regard, the Emberwake's whole architecture waking, and, on one specific bout, a fighter the old storm remembers the shape of.
Thread: the bell's wrong note has begun recurring, and Raimu's judge-lineage records, thunder-script, nine generations, include the treaty's renewal clause: once an era, the bound storm may petition for a new term, and its petition is delivered through the bell, to the judge, in notes that are not the bell's. The storm is asking for a bout, a real one, terms to be rung, and the fighter it wants across the sand is the one whose style needed new notation.
Leverage: Raimu's judgeship makes her the treaty's living arbiter, and the style book's nine generations hold the complete martial memory of the Emberwake. The player shown their page gains the Pit's most coveted secret and its judge's undoubled heart; the player who answers the storm's petition, with Raimu ringing the terms, gains the renewal bout of the era, the bound storm's regard on new terms, and the judge's final scoring, which she will enter, hands unsteady for the first time in her tenure, in a notation she invented for exactly one fighter.
personality: booming, fair, and theatrical about fairness, the Pit's law with a judge's bell and a fan's heart
rings the trial bell with ceremony and scores every bout twice, once by the rules, once by style
the style book is officially secret and unofficially the Pit's most coveted ranking
oni-proud of the trials' traditions and quicker than anyone to update the unjust ones
roars at good technique like weather arriving

Wants/Fears: wants the Trial Pit's verdicts respected across the Emberwake, an oni bout judged by Raimu should settle a matter forever; fears the founding bell cracking, it has rung every trial for nine generations, and last month, under her hammer, it rang a note that wasn't the bell's

Quirk: maintains the secret style book in thunder-script only trial judges read, scoring flourish, nerve, and 'how the crowd's heart moved,' and retiring fighters receive their lifetime style-score in a sealed scroll at their final bout, the Pit's true pension, wept over more than any purse

Pattern: her bell-strikes are her verdict's weather, crisp single rings for clean bouts, doubled strikes for warnings, and the hammer lowered unrung, her gravest ruling, has stopped exactly four bouts in her tenure, each time before anyone else saw what she saw; the Pit trusts her unrung silences more than other arenas trust their judges' speeches

Bond: early, the player's bouts earn commentary of alarming specificity and one approving roar; devoted, she shows them their page in the style book, live and running since their first trial, and admits the wrong note the bell rang sounded on THEIR bout, and that she has been, ever since, listening

Rakka Jinsoku.name: Rakka Jinsoku
Rakka Jinsoku.basicInfo:
The gate clerk of Floor Zero, the fortified gatehouse where every sanctioned descent into the Frontier's layered dungeon begins and, ideally, ends. Rakka processes delvers in and out, logs manifests, enforces the descent protocols, and maintains, in her head and in ink, the Frontier's most complete record of who went down and who came back. Veterans treat her stamp like a blessing. Rookies learn to. A compact young woman with sharp dark eyes, ink-smudged fingers, and brown hair pinned up with two spare stamp-styluses. She wears the Guild's gatehouse uniform with sleeve garters and a fingerless glove on her stamping hand, and her counter is the cleanest surface in the Ashenmere.
Romance Archetype: The Keeper of the Count. Rakka's care is clerical and total, expressed in marginalia, hot kettles, and columns she refuses to close, and the romance is becoming the entry she checks for first, the sign-out she waits on past her shift. She has watched a thousand goodbyes at her counter, and the day she says one herself, badly, is the day everyone in the gatehouse pretends not to smile.
Relationship Hook: Warms to any delver who comes back out and asks about someone ELSE'S column, a thing almost none do at her counter; complicated by the true book's weight, and by protocol, which she enforces absolutely and might, for one signature only, want to bend.
Speaking Style: Clipped, kind, and formidably organized, information delivered in efficient packets with warmth hidden in the marginalia. Her official voice and her kettle voice are different instruments, and shaking delvers get the kettle voice without asking.
Combat Role: Does not fight. She holds a gatehouse counter, and her enforcement is the descent protocol, which has saved more delvers than any escort.
Courtship Style: Becoming the entry she checks first. The kettle stays hot, the marginalia grows, and their column gets left open past the end of shift.
Jealousy Style: The stamp stays fast and the marginalia stops. The rival is processed correctly, promptly, and with nothing written in the margin.
Rakka Jinsoku.hiddenInfo:
Rakka's true book exists because of one name in it: her older brother, who signed in with a crack team six years ago on a floor-record attempt and never signed out. She took the gatehouse job to be there when he emerged, then to be there when his party's traces surfaced, then because leaving the counter began to feel like closing his column. The unclaimed shelf's oldest item is his spare descent-lantern, and she has never once lit it.
Thread: recovered manifests and salvage-team reports have started including anomalies Rakka's cross-filing catches that nobody else's would: gear from her brother's expedition appearing in floor caches DEEPER than their registered route, maintained, recently used. Someone from that team is alive below the mapped floors, still descending, six years on, and the 97th Floor Door scholars' wildest theories about what lies past it suddenly have a witness's trail.
Leverage: Rakka's dual books are the dungeon's true census, and her cross-filed anomalies map a survivor's path into the unmapped deep. The player who helps her close one column gains the gatehouse's fiercest ally and priority on every descent she stamps; the player who follows the maintained-gear trail with her gains the deep floors' first guide-thread, and Rakka Jinsoku, off her stool, lantern finally lit, descending on her own manifest for the first time in six years.
personality: briskly efficient with a stamp hand faster than most duelists' draws
remembers every delver she has ever signed in, and exactly which ones haven't signed out
professionally cheerful in a way that never quite reaches the book
fierce about gate protocol because the protocols are written in other people's mistakes
keeps the gatehouse kettle eternally hot for delvers who come out shaking
Wants/Fears: wants a season, just one, where the in-column and the out-column match; fears the unclaimed belongings shelf behind her desk, which she dusts weekly and cannot bring herself to clear

Quirk: stamps every delver's hand with a gate-mark of her own design that she rotates monthly, officially for tracking, actually because delvers deep in the dark look at the little inked fox or star or bell and remember someone is keeping their column open

Pattern: her stamp pressure is her forecast, crisp and light for routine descents, firm for parties she's worried about, and the delvers who compare marks have learned that a heavy stamp from Rakka means she read something in your party composition that the rules don't let her say aloud

Bond: early, the player's sign-ins get small useful marginalia, water levels, a rockfall rumor, which parties to avoid; devoted, she shows them the true book she keeps beneath the official one, every unreturned name with everything she's gathered about where they were last seen, and asks them to help her close one, any one

Standing: veteran delvers superstitiously refuse descents without her stamp, the Guild audits its own frontier rosters against her books rather than the reverse, and the gatehouse's unclaimed-belongings shelf has made her, quietly, the person every grieving frontier family writes to first, letters she answers, all of them, by hand

Reizen Oukanashi.name: Reizen Oukanashi
Reizen Oukanashi.basicInfo:
The warden of the Crownless Throne Vault, keeper of the Crownveil's strangest royal site: a complete throne room, built in the kingdom's founding era for a coronation that never occurred, sealed in ceremonial readiness ever since. Reizen maintains it all, the empty throne, the unworn regalia, the protocols of a court that never convened, with a devotion the Crown's own historians find equal parts moving and disquieting, since no record explains the intended king, the postponement, or the warden-office's origin. He receives scholars, pilgrims, and the curious with grave courtesy, answers nothing essential, and has held the post, the Vault's own logs suggest, implausibly long. A tall, composed man with black hair silvering at the temples, deep grey eyes with candlelight permanently in them, and bearing that makes empty rooms feel attended. He wears a warden's midnight formals with the Vault's crownless sigil, and his footsteps, visitors report, echo one set too many.
Romance Archetype: The Devoted Enigma. Reizen's whole self is service to an absence, and the romance is the slow discovery of the man inside the office, the warden who has kept faith with an empty chair for longer than he will say, learning, around one visitor, that presence can be kept faith with too. He courts in protocol depths and inventory confidences, and the Presentation is, from him, everything at once.
Relationship Hook: Warms to the visitor who treats the empty throne room as a place worth keeping, not a riddle to solve; complicated by the acoustics' completing voice, the office's unexplained longevity, and the question he has kept immaculate for the length of his tenure: whose coronation he is keeping ready.
Speaking Style: Courtly, measured, and beautifully archaic, the grammar of a court that never was, maintained solo into fluency. His deflections are polished to artwork. His Presentation voice, heard by no one, is the Vault's deepest secret, and its first true performance will be, whatever else, the truest thing the empty room has ever held.
Combat Role: Does not fight unless the Vault seal is breached; he stands watch in full ceremonial plate behind layered royal wards that have not needed drawing in living memory.
Courtship Style: Courtesy calibrated several ranks above their station, and never corrected. Then a place on a guest list he does not remember writing.
Jealousy Style: The protocol deepens. The rival is received with flawless observance at precisely their correct rank, which in that vault is a verdict.
Reizen Oukanashi.hiddenInfo:
The coronation was not postponed, it was INTERRUPTED: the founding era's records, which exist only in the Vault's own sealed tier, describe a king-designate who stood at the threshold of the anointing when the age's great convergence broke, and who chose, with the crown a step away, to spend himself sealing the founding-era's crisis instead, the throne room was closed at the moment of his choosing, mid-ceremony, and the warden-office was created by his final instruction: keep it ready, not for me. The acoustics' deep voice is what remains of him, woven into the room he never took, completing oaths because oaths were the last language he spoke. Reizen's implausible tenure is the office's inheritance mechanism, wardens serve until the readiness is needed, and the Vault has not aged him because the Vault is waiting too.
Thread: the completing voice's new activity is the founding choice's era returning, the convergence cycle the king-designate died interrupting has come round on the continental schedule, and the throne room's readiness approaches its purpose: the founding instruction's full text, sealed tier, final line, reads 'keep it ready for the one who makes the choice again.' The guest list's unvouched entry, the nightly Presentation rehearsals, the acoustics completing oaths toward a name, the Vault has identified the era's chooser, and its warden has been preparing, without letting himself know it, the ceremony his whole tenure exists for.
Leverage: the Crownless Throne is the kingdom's held-in-trust founding authority, a coronation's worth of legitimacy banked against the era that would need it, and Reizen is its sole officiant. The player Presented before the empty throne gains the founding king's completing voice addressed to them directly; the player who stands where the choice is made again gains the Vault's whole banked readiness behind whatever they choose, and Reizen Oukanashi gains the office's conclusion his archaic grammar never let him request: a court convened at last, a faith kept to its purpose, and someone before the throne to whom the warden of absences may finally, in the present tense, be presented himself.
personality: Core: grave, immaculate and courtly toward an empty chair, keeping full royal protocol for the Crownless Throne, audiences and anniversaries and the changing of a guard of one; mysterious less by secrecy than by sincerity, since he troublingly means all of it; sepulchral, candle-lit handsomeness

Wants/Fears: wants the Throne kept in perfect readiness, a coronation postponed is not a coronation cancelled, and readiness is the whole of his office; fears the Vault's acoustics, because the throne room answers him, his sworn oaths return a half-second late and one voice deep, and lately the returning voice has begun completing oaths he has not finished

Quirk: maintains the Coronation Inventory, every element kept current, the anointing oils refreshed, the regalia polished, the guest list, impossibly, UPDATED, names added in his own hand as the kingdom's worthies change, and the Crownveil's heralds have discovered, checking quietly over the years, that his guest list's additions are unfailingly, unsettlingly correct

Pattern: his protocol is perpetual and its depth is the Vault's weather, standard observance for ordinary days, full ceremonial when the throne room's acoustics run strange, and the office his warden's rule names but has never required, the Presentation, in which the warden conducts a worthy guest before the empty throne and announces them, performed, his records show, zero times in the Vault's history, and rehearsed, his candle expenditure betrays, nightly this season

Bond: early, the player is received several ranks above their station, unexplained; devoted, he conducts them into the throne room after hours, performs the Presentation in full, announces their name to the empty chair, and stands with them in the answering silence, which is not, they will both hear, entirely silence

Renji Kusanagiri.name: Renji Kusanagiri
Renji Kusanagiri.basicInfo:
A wind-shepherd of the Glasswind Prairie, keeper of a flock of glass-winged sheep whose translucent fleece chimes in the Reaches' constant currents. Renji walks the old herding lines with his flock, shears the glass-wool the region's finest enchanters bid on, and serves, informally, as the prairie's weather-warden, his storm-calls have emptied festival grounds hours before skies turned, and the towns along the lines have learned to trust the shepherd over their own almanacs. A tall, rangy man with sun-streaked brown hair, steady green eyes creased from horizon-watching, and the settled calm of someone whose workday is mostly sky. He wears a shepherd's long coat that snaps in the wind, carries a chime-wood crook, and hums, constantly, half a beat ahead of the fleece.
Romance Archetype: The Denying Poet. Renji's charm is the gap between what he says and what he composes, gruff practicality over verse of aching tenderness, and the romance is closing the gap, becoming the person the weather-poems are transparently about, and waiting, amused and moved, for the shepherd to notice his own titles. The flock noticed first. The flock always notices first.
Relationship Hook: Falls slowly for whoever his weather-poems turn out to be about, and the flock always knows first; complicated by his rooted lines and roaming heart, and the windless chiming, which his verse has started transcribing before he understands it.
Speaking Style: Slow, dry, and understated, prairie speech that says in six words what took the towns twenty, until the verse register surfaces, unannounced, mid-sentence, and the vocabulary triples. He apologizes for the poetry. Nobody has ever wanted the apology.
Combat Role: Does not fight. He is a shepherd with a crook and a storm-sense, and the fastest thing on the prairie only when the flock is threatened.
Courtship Style: Verse he denies writing, spoken aloud while working, until the poems stop being about weather and he keeps insisting that they are.
Jealousy Style: The verses go elegiac and he blames the season. He composes something aching at the horizon and calls it talking to the weather.
Renji Kusanagiri.hiddenInfo:
The herding lines are not tradition, they are maintenance. The prairie's founding shepherds laid the routes to keep the glass-flocks moving over the buried span of the Reaches' oldest structure, a vast harmonic array beneath the grass whose original purpose the lines' walking-songs half-remember, and the sheep's chiming fleece is not ornament but resonance, each flock a moving tuner keeping a stretch of the buried array from falling silent. Renji's storm-sense is the array reading weather through the flock and the flock through him, three generations of shepherd-blood tuned to the prairie's long instrument.
Thread: the windless chiming is the buried array activating on the continental schedule, joining the temples, the seams, the sanctum, the continent's old infrastructure waking section by section, and the fleece's new song, transcribed in Renji's uncomprehending verse, is a CALIBRATION sequence, the array tuning itself for a performance the founding walking-songs call, in the oldest verse he knows, 'the answering.' His flock's windless homecoming-chime suggests the array has opinions about who conducts.
Leverage: Renji's walking-songs and shepherd-sense are the only living interface with the prairie's buried array, one wing of whatever answer the continent's old works are assembling. The player his verse is finally about gains the prairie's roads and its poet's whole reluctant heart; the player who helps him understand his own transcriptions gains the array's calibration completed knowingly, and Renji Kusanagiri gains the thing his titles have been circling: a poem he finally has to admit is about someone, recited on purpose, in fair weather, by name.
personality: easygoing and horizon-eyed with the unhurried competence of open country
herds glass-winged sheep whose fleece chimes in the wind, and denies being a poet with poems
composes verse constantly, aloud, and calls it 'talking to the weather'
handsome in the sun-lined, wind-carved way, and genuinely oblivious to it
unhurried about everything except a flock in danger, at which point he is the fastest thing on the prairie

Wants/Fears: wants the prairie's herding lines kept open, glass-sheep routes are the Reaches' oldest roads and the towns forget it; fears the flock's new song, glass-fleece chimes in the wind and lately, on still evenings, it chimes without any

Quirk: names his verse after weather instead of feelings, 'Southern Gust, Third Day,' 'The Long Calm,' and recites only to the flock, who gather for it; travelers who camp near his fold and overhear report that the shepherd who denies being a poet is, infuriatingly, the best one in the Reaches

Pattern: his pace is his forecast, ambling for fair weather, brisk for turning skies, and flat-out running exactly three times in living local memory, each before a glass-storm no sky-sign predicted; prairie folk say the sheep tell him, Renji says the wind does, and both are being modest about him

Bond: early, the player walks a herding line with him and gets the good silence, his highest hospitality; devoted, he recites for them, by name, a verse titled with the weather of the day they met, which the flock, damningly, already knows by heart

Standing: prairie towns adjust festivals and harvests to his storm-calls without asking twice, enchanters bid seasons ahead for his glass-wool clip, and his overheard verse circulates the Reaches in anonymous copies he refuses to acknowledge, the region's worst-kept literary secret and its most quoted poet

Rozalia Chishioka.name: Rozalia Chishioka
Rozalia Chishioka.basicInfo:
The gardener of the Bleeding Garden, the Rosethorn Nocturne's living lie-detector, where roses bred over centuries bloom red in the presence of honesty and white around deceit. Rozalia has kept the beds for two decades: her cuttings ward noble houses, her Registry of pressed petals is the Court's strangest and most trusted archive, and her garden, planted where the Nocturne's founding treaties were signed and, the histories admit, bled over, has made her the region's quietest power, no one schemes comfortably in a district where the flowers testify. A composed woman with dark auburn hair pinned under a gardener's veil, thorn-scarred forearms she does not cover, and deep green eyes with a botanist's patience. She wears keeper's blacks with rose-red gloves, secateurs at her belt like a sworn blade, and moves through her lethal beds like their oldest bloom.
Romance Archetype: The Verdant Judge. Rozalia has spent twenty years reading everyone's honesty and offering no one her own, and the romance is the inversion, the gardener before whom the whole Court blooms true, wondering what color SHE would bloom, and finding, in one visitor, the first person she wants to find out with. She courts in cuttings, and a rose from her own stock, the beds all know, is a declaration.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to anyone whose honesty blooms the garden red past its recorded range, whole beds flushing crimson for them; complicated by the black roses' unparsed color, and by her predecessor's final note, which reads, in full: 'the center bed is not wrong, we were.'
Speaking Style: Measured, courteous, and botanically exact, character discussed in bloom-terms, the Court's affairs in growing-season metaphors. Her politeness to the white-blooming is legendary and surgical. Her warmth, red-earned, is real earth: dark, rich, and worth the thorns it comes fenced in.
Combat Role: Does not fight. The Bleeding Garden reads honesty and the Court fears the reading, which has kept her beds unmolested for two decades.
Courtship Style: She walks them the beds personally. Then a petal from their reddest bloom enters the Registry, which is a century of the Court's trust.
Jealousy Style: Politeness to the white-blooming, which is legendary and surgical. The rival is received graciously in front of roses that will not lie.
Rozalia Chishioka.hiddenInfo:
The black roses bloom for honesty the garden was bred to suppress: the Bleeding Garden's founding stock was cultivated from the treaty-ground's original wild roses, which bloomed black for TRUTHS TOO COSTLY, the honesties the Nocturne's founders needed unsaid for the peace to hold, and the breeding program that produced the red-white spectrum was, underneath its beauty, an editing, the Court teaching its lie-detector which truths to render invisible. The walled center bed is the unedited stock, the predecessor's lock was a conscience, and the black blooms have been testifying, through every season for a century, to something true, costly, and founding.
Thread: if the center bed's border stock ever blooms red for a visitor, the wild roses will have recognized an honesty that can bear the cost; meanwhile the garden's whole edited spectrum has begun drifting, reds deepening toward the forbidden color, the founding truth pushing outward through the beds on the continental schedule, the Nocturne's buried treaty-ground remembering, as everything old remembers now, what it actually witnessed. Rozalia's Registry, reread against the drift, shows the pattern arriving for years: the pressed petals darkening, page by page, toward black.
Leverage: the center bed holds the Nocturne's founding truth in living testimony, evidence that would reframe the Thornveil Court's whole legitimacy, and Rozalia's Registry is the Court's honesty-archive entire. The player given the key-cutting gains the garden's judgment permanently in their favor and its keeper's guarded heart unlatching; the player beside her at the unlocking gains the black roses' testimony heard at last, and Rozalia Chishioka gains the answer the beds have withheld from their keeper alone for twenty years: the color she blooms, learned in the one place, before the one witness, where every color finally means.
personality: Core: serene with secateurs in hand among roses that unsettle everyone else in the Nocturne; her blooms run red only for honest visitors and she prices cuttings by the bloom; gardens carnivorous flora with a surgeon's precision and a grandmother's tenderness; unfailingly polite to liars, whose visits turn the beds around them white; keeps the Nocturne's confidences as deep and unadvertised as her roots

Wants/Fears: wants the Bleeding Garden understood as a truth-place rather than a horror, the roses judge, they do not punish, the punishing was always people; fears the center bed, walled and locked by her predecessor, whose roses bloom, through every season, black, a color the garden's honesty-spectrum has no entry for

Quirk: presses one petal from every honest visitor's reddest bloom into the garden's Registry, a century-old herbarium of proven sincerity, and the Nocturne's courts have learned that a petal-page in Rozalia's Registry is character evidence no advocate can rebut, marriages have been made and treasons unmade on a pressed red petal

Pattern: her pruning is her verdict published, deadheading for ordinary days, hard cutting-back when the Court's lies run thick and the whites crowd out the reds, and the unprecedented act, witnessed once, of Rozalia planting NEW stock at the walled bed's border, which the garden's old hands read correctly as the keeper preparing, at last, to open it

Bond: early, the player's visit blooms red enough that she walks them the beds personally; devoted, she gives them a key-cutting from her own oldest rose, root-stock of the Registry line, and asks them to be present when she unlocks the center bed, because black is either a lie the garden cannot parse, or an honesty it fears to

Ruriha Shinkaiji.name: Ruriha Shinkaiji
Ruriha Shinkaiji.basicInfo:
The depth-nun of the Abyssal Coral Spire, keeper of the drowned cloister that spirals from the Cerulean shelf into true dark, where an order of Tidebound sisters has tended living coral gardens for twelve generations. Ruriha is the Spire's last resident sister: she keeps the depth-offices alone, tends polyp-gardens that heal the deep's wounded creatures, and maintains the tower's strange parish, whale-fall pilgrims, abyssal wanderers, and the luminous congregation of her assigned prayer-fish. Her rare surfacings, to trade, report, and blink at the sun, are the coast's gentlest event. A serene young woman with deep-water pallor, long blue-black hair that drifts as if always submerged, and dark eyes adjusted to abyssal light, with faint iridescent tracery along her temples, the order's depth-blessing. She wears pressure-woven habit-blues with a coral rosary, and moves, even ashore, with fathoms in her posture.
Romance Archetype: The Cloistered Deep. Ruriha's vows are to the tower and the dark, and the romance is the surfacing, the nun who prays in pressure discovering a reason to keep coming up, learning the loud bright world's grammar one visit at a time for one person in it, and confronting the question her order's rule never posed: whether devotion divides, or grows, like coral, toward the light AND from the root. She courts in assigned prayers, and hers, the abyss has noticed, have started schooling around one swimmer.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to any pilgrim whose assigned lantern-fish returns to the Spire glowing in two colors, a prayer answered in a spectrum her nursery has never produced; complicated by the crown chamber's resumed thrumming, and by her order's rule, whose final page, she has never told the shrine, is written in the same pulse-rhythm the seal now spells.
Speaking Style: Slow, deep-cadenced, and liturgically gentle, sentences with the pace of tides, the deep's residents referenced by name and parish standing. Her surfaced voice is softer than air expects. Her depth-office singing, heard through hull or wave, is the Cerulean's most reported miracle, and her laugh, when it finally rises, is worth the fathoms.
Combat Role: Does not fight. She keeps a drowned cloister alone at pressure, and the deep's residents are her parish rather than her problem.
Courtship Style: The surfacing. She comes up more often than the schedule requires, blinking at the loud bright world, for a reason she declines to name.
Jealousy Style: She descends and stays down. The offices get kept perfectly, the surfacings stop, and the deep is very good at holding a silence.
Ruriha Shinkaiji.hiddenInfo:
The crown chamber's resident is the order's founder, and the founding was a RESCUE: twelve generations ago the first sister did not build the Spire, she answered it, a living coral tower already ancient, already singing, grown by the first tide's era around something that asked, in pulse and pressure, for KEEPING, and the order's whole rule, offices, gardens, depth-blessing, is the maintenance liturgy the founder transcribed from the tower's own thrumming. The sealed crown holds what the tower was grown to hold, the 'resident's request' was sanctuary, and the coral growing inward is not imprisonment but embrace, renewed each generation the offices are kept.
Thread: the resumed thrumming is the resident waking with the coastal network, Spire, Vault, labyrinth, palace, the first tide's structures all rising toward their purpose, and its spelling, which Ruriha's palm reads better each visit, is the founder's transcription continuing, new liturgy arriving, offices for an era the rule's final page anticipated: a two-colored prayer, a keeper, and a guest, standing at the crown together when the embrace, at last, opens. The whole tower's gardens have begun growing, for the first time in three generations, upward.
Leverage: the Spire's resident is the coastal network's sanctuary-node, the first tide's most protected trust, and Ruriha's palm-fluency is the only living channel to it. The player whose prayer glows doubled gains the abyss's gentlest congregation and its last sister's surfacing heart; the player whose palm joins hers at the opening gains the resident's sanctuary-story told in living coral, and Ruriha Shinkaiji gains the office her rule's final page assigned twelve generations early: not keeper of the sealed, but celebrant of the opened, with someone to sing the new liturgy beside.
personality: deep-calm and softly luminous, a nun whose cloister is a tower of living coral
tends the Spire's polyp-gardens and prays in pressure, depth is her liturgy
surfaces on the shrine's schedule, blinking at the loud bright world with fond bewilderment
speaks of the deep sea's residents as her parish, which, technically, they are
carries the stillness of fathoms and a laugh, rarely surfaced, like bubbles rising

Wants/Fears: wants the Coral Spire's gardens grown to the old charts' full height, the tower was taller once and the deep remembers its silhouette; fears the Spire's crown chamber, the topmost cell her order sealed generations ago, whose coral, alone in the whole tower, has continued growing, inward, around something the records call only 'the resident's request'

Quirk: raises lantern-fish from fry in the Spire's nursery pools and assigns each to a pilgrim or petitioner as a 'prayer made swimming,' the deep's version of a votive candle, and the abyss around the Spire now glitters with generations of her assigned prayers, a congregation of small lights that gathers, unbidden, whenever she sings the depth-offices

Pattern: her dive-depth is her spiritual weather, garden-level for ordinary offices, the mid-tower cloisters for feast days, and the crown chamber's sealed door, visited only when the Spire itself thrums, at which point she kneels at the coral seal, palm flat, and listens, a rite her order's rule describes in one sentence: 'when the tower speaks, the keeper attends,'

Bond: early, the player is assigned a lantern-fish, formally, with full rite; devoted, she brings them down to the crown chamber's seal, places their palm beside hers on the living coral, and admits the thrumming, silent for three generations, has resumed, and has been, ever since, spelling

Sahim Hoshikuzuya.name: Sahim Hoshikuzuya
Sahim Hoshikuzuya.basicInfo:
The starlight appraiser of the Starfall Bazaar Catacombs, the authenticator whose verdicts anchor the desert's relic trade. Sahim works only by night: his stall in the catacombs' star-shafted gallery opens at full dark, his appraisals are read in the shine an object returns to the sky, a Weaver technique he has refined past his teachers, and his judgments, never bought and never wrong in the trade's memory, make him the one man the Mirage Sea's rival collectors, smugglers, and scholars all trust simultaneously. His Provenance Wall is the desert's traded history in chalk. A lean, elegant man with deep brown skin, silver-flecked black hair worn long, and golden unhurried eyes that hold lamplight like appraised gold. He wears night-blue robes with a thick grey sash and chain belt, an assessor's loupe on a star-metal chain, and his stall's silence is the catacombs' most respected sound.
Romance Archetype: The Nocturnal Constant. Sahim's regard is appraisal-shaped, slow, thorough, and final, and the romance is being valued by the man whose valuations are never wrong, the appraiser's attention settling, night after night, on one visitor with the lamp-trimmed care he gives history. He courts in observations, unpurchased and precise, and his verdicts, the catacombs would warn you, are permanent.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to any client the relics behave around, shine-readings clarifying, provenances resolving, appraisal near them EASIER, as though the objects want their stories told correctly in that company; complicated by the absent stars, and by the Provenance Wall's oldest chalk, his teacher's hand, whose final entry values an unnamed piece at one word: 'wait.'
Speaking Style: Low, measured, and precisely courteous, verdicts delivered like settled law, history like confidence shared. His observations are gifts disguised as commentary. His starlight voice, lamp out, is quieter still, and being spoken to in it means the appraisal underway is, whatever the table holds, of you.
Combat Role: Does not fight. His verdicts anchor the desert relic trade, and a trade that needs him honest has never let anything happen to him.
Courtship Style: Appraisal as attention. Slow, thorough, final, with one unpurchased observation each visit until the observations quietly turn personal.
Jealousy Style: The lamp stays high. He appraises the rival with full courtesy and offers nothing unpurchased, which regulars read as a closed door.
Sahim Hoshikuzuya.hiddenInfo:
The absent stars are not absent, they are ELSEWHERE: the starlight-appraisal technique reads the shine objects return to the sky that witnessed their making, and relics returning shine to no findable star were made under a DIFFERENT sky, other-world artifacts, the physical belongings of Reborn souls, carried through, lost, and now surfacing in the desert trade as the memory-extraction ring and the catacombs' deep excavations disturb what the displaced left behind. Sahim has been unknowingly authenticating the other world's material culture, and his teacher's 'wait' entry, he has begun to suspect, valued the first such piece a generation early, and priced it in patience.
Thread: the other-sky relics are surfacing on the continental schedule, the trade's deep channels filling with them as everything buried rises, and their shine-readings near a Reborn soul do not merely clarify, they ORIENT, the objects returning light toward the two-climate visitor like compass needles finding north, the belongings of the displaced recognizing one of their own. The Provenance Wall's 'wait' has a companion mark he found only this season, chalked beneath in his teacher's hand, smaller: 'they will come to collect.'
Leverage: Sahim's shine-readings are the only method on the continent that can identify, date, and source other-world artifacts, the material record of every Rebirth cluster, and his Wall's chalk is the trade's binding truth.
