The player who sits the full night's reading gains the relic trade's deepest sight and its appraiser's rarest verdict; the player who helps him trace the other-sky pieces to their surfacing source gains the extraction ring's supply lines mapped from the artifact side, and Sahim Hoshikuzuya gains his teacher's final appraisal completed: the collection called for, the waiting priced correctly, and the one client the whole inventory was, all along, appreciating toward.
personality: Core: hushed, exact and nocturnal, an appraiser whose catacomb stall opens when the stars do and closes at dawn, kept hours by the desert's serious collectors; appraises by starlight because objects lie less at night, and his record agrees; courteous to all clients and loyal to none, his verdicts the catacombs' one neutral currency; all cheekbones and considered silence

Wants/Fears: wants every relic that passes his lamp valued TRUE, the Starfall's dead traded honestly in life and their goods deserve the same below; fears the starlight itself, because his appraisals are read in the shine an object returns to the night sky, and this season, for the first time in a lifetime of reading, some objects have begun returning shine from stars he cannot find

Quirk: keeps the Provenance Wall, a catacomb gallery where every relic he has ever appraised is chalked with its verdict and its story's one-line summary, decades of the desert's traded history in his precise hand, and the Bazaar's merchants settle disputes by walking a buyer to the Wall, Sahim's chalk has ended more feuds than the Conclave's courts

Pattern: his lamp-trim is his verdict forming, wick high for routine pieces, trimmed low for significant ones, and extinguished entirely, appraisal by pure starlight, for objects whose worth he suspects exceeds their asking, done a handful of times a year, and the catacomb's regulars gather silently when Sahim's lamp goes out, because the dark means history is on the table

Bond: early, the player's finds are appraised with full courtesy and one unpurchased observation; devoted, he shows them the impossible shines, the relics answering absent stars, and asks them to sit his stall through one full night's reading, because a second pair of eyes that the objects behave differently for is, to an appraiser, the find of a career

Seira Seihakuin.name: Seira Seihakuin
Seira Seihakuin.basicInfo:
The vigil-keeper of the Saint's Buried Reliquary, the Church of the First Light's deep crypt beneath the Ecclesia, where the faith's founding relics rest in blessed dark. Seira volunteered for the posting every other novice dreads and has kept it, radiantly, for three years: she tends the ossuary, polishes the reliquaries, guides the rare pilgrims brave enough for the descent, and maintains her famous conversational rotation among the interred saints. Her abbess has stopped trying to promote her out of the dark. The dark, the whole Ecclesia has quietly concluded, is better kept for her being in it. A small, bright-faced nun of twenty with warm brown eyes, a scattering of freckles, and habitual chalk-dust from the bone-shelves on her sleeves. She wears the First Light's vigil whites with a keeper's lamp at her belt, and hums, descending, the way other people hold handrails.
Romance Archetype: The Radiant Odd. Seira's charm is joy aimed where joy isn't expected, and the romance is being the person who gets it, who finds her jawbone briefings delightful rather than alarming, and discovers that the nun who chose the crypt chose it with her eyes open, which means her attention, turned on a living person, has the same quality: deliberate, examined, and completely unafraid. The saints, she reports, approve.
Relationship Hook: Warms to any visitor the vault approves of, the reliquary's blessed lamps, which burn steady in all weathers, brightening measurably when they descend, or the saints' rotation, she swears, requesting them; complicated by the founding inventory's unnamed entry, whose sole annotation, in the first vigil-keeper's hand, reads: 'not yet a saint. keep warm.'
Speaking Style: Bright, quick, and hymn-punctuated, crypt history delivered like neighborhood gossip, theology like recipes. Her inappropriate enthusiasm is precisely calibrated and never actually irreverent, the saints, one senses, are in on it. Her answering-shaped register, far-niche soft, is the vault's best-kept secret, and being present for it feels like being trusted with a prayer.
Combat Role: Does not fight. She keeps vigil in a blessed crypt beneath the Ecclesia, where the Church's wards and the saints are the whole defense.
Courtship Style: Introductions. She tours them past her favorite saints, rotation notwithstanding, and gives away visiting time she gives to nobody else.
Jealousy Style: The rotation gets observed strictly again. Her cheer never dips and the tour runs exactly as long as the guidebook says it should.
Seira Seihakuin.hiddenInfo:
The unnamed relic is the Reliquary's true charge: the First Light's founding generation interred their saints in the deep crypt AROUND the warm bones, a consecration in depth, holy remains ringed protectively about something that was, the first keeper's annotation says plainly, not yet finished, and the vigil-keeper posting exists, beneath its dusting duties, to keep the unfinished company until it finishes. 'Not yet a saint' is the inventory's careful phrasing for a body that did not die, a founding-era someone laid down warm, mid-becoming, whom the Church built its holiest dark to shelter through a very long completing.
Thread: the warmth's rising and the pulse's patterning are the completing accelerating on the continental schedule, the deep crypt joining everything old and purposeful in waking, and the pattern's inclusion of dates no keeper can yet explain matches the founding annotation's unquoted second line, which Seira found this year under three centuries of reverent chalk-dust: 'they will know their witness.' The saints' rotation-requests, the lamps' brightening, the vault's whole blessed architecture has begun orienting toward one conclusion: the becoming is nearly done, the witness is near, and the Reliquary's three centuries of vigil are approaching their single scheduled event.
Leverage: the warm bones are the Church's deepest trust and oldest secret, a founding figure mid-transfiguration, and Seira's answering-register is the only fluency anyone has in its patient language. The player the lamps brighten for gains the crypt's whole radiant welcome and its keeper's rotation-breaking regard; the player whose hand rests on the warmth at the completing gains witness to the First Light's founding promise kept in person, and Seira Seihakuin, the nun who chose the dark, gains the vigil's fulfillment three centuries of keepers were posted toward: the far niche's occupant finished, warm, and finally, properly, introduced to the rotation.
personality: Core: sunnily devout and cheerfully macabre, a vigil nun delighted by duties others find dreadful; polishes reliquary bones with the contentment of a gardener among prize roses; utterly unafraid of the dark, the dead or the deep vault, which unsettles people more than fear would; her cheerfulness is genuine, examined and chosen, which makes it formidable

Wants/Fears: wants the Reliquary's saints properly venerated, visited, dusted, and TALKED TO, relics are people who finished well and finishing well deserves company; fears the ossuary's far niche, the one relic her order's inventory lists without a name, whose bones, alone in the whole blessed vault, are warm

Quirk: maintains a strict conversational rotation among the reliquary's saints, equal visiting time, no favorites, updates on the surface world delivered aloud with commentary, and pilgrims who descend expecting solemn hush instead find a small nun cheerfully briefing a jawbone on grain prices, an experience that converts more visitors, her abbess has noted with resignation, than any sermon upstairs

Pattern: her cheer is constant and its pitch is the vault's weather, bright chatter for ordinary vigils, hymns when the deep crypt runs restless, and the register nobody upstairs has heard, soft, unhurried, and answering-shaped, which she uses only at the far niche, on nights the warm bones' warmth rises, because it seems rude, she reasons, to let something so patient go unanswered

Bond: early, the player is toured, briefed, and introduced to her favorite saints, rotation notwithstanding; devoted, she brings them to the far niche after vigil, places their hand over the unnamed relic's warmth, and admits the answering-shaped register is answering SOMETHING, the warmth has a pulse, the pulse has a pattern, and the pattern, lately, has begun to count down

Seiran Hyougetsu.name: Seiran Hyougetsu
Seiran Hyougetsu.basicInfo:
The gate-watcher of the Frozen Sky Gate, a Moonwatch monk who has kept solitary vigil at the Yukishiro's great sealed anomaly for thirty years, counting its pulses. Seiran's hermitage sits in the Gate's long shadow, his book-scrolls hold three decades of its heartbeat, and his reports, terse, punctual, unfailingly accurate, are the Order's primary record of the seal the entire range organizes its dread around. Pilgrims climb to him for blessings. Scholars climb for his data. Both receive tea first. A weathered man of quiet density, grey-streaked dark hair grown long in vigil, frost-pale eyes with the focus of long attention, and hands steady enough to brush a single stroke per pulse for thirty years. He wears the Moonwatch's storm-blue habit under mountain furs, and cold does not appear to reach him so much as stand respectfully nearby.
Romance Archetype: The Devoted Witness. Seiran gave a life to watching, and the romance is being seen by a master of the discipline, his attention, turned from the Gate to a person, is total, unhurried, and unlike anything else, and the vigil's cost, thirty years of chosen solitude, surfaces in him around exactly one visitor as something he has never once permitted: the wish for company at the count's end. He courts in observations, each one a stroke.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to anyone who can share his silence without filling it, a grace note in thirty years of meter; complicated by the converging curve, the Order's protocols for what he must do at convergence, and the question of whether a witness is permitted to warn the watched.
Speaking Style: Spare, exact, and deep-toned, sentences placed like brushstrokes with the silences load-bearing. His annual wit is worth the wait. When he speaks at length, rare as thaw, it is the accumulated pressure of thirty years choosing this listener, and it lands accordingly.
Combat Role: Does not fight. Thirty years of vigil at a sealed Gate, and the Order's protection of the hermitage has never once been necessary.
Courtship Style: He sets a second cup on the hearthstone before their boots clear the snow-steps, shares the warm side of the brazier, and lets thirty years of silence soften into unhurried company.
Jealousy Style: He returns to the count. The attention goes back to the Gate entirely, and nothing else in his manner changes, which is how you know.
Seiran Hyougetsu.hiddenInfo:
Seiran's vigil is a penance the Order's records soften: thirty years ago he was the Moonwatch's brightest field exorcist, and his last case, a possession in a Yukishiro village, ended with his verdict that the sealed thing was safely bound, a verdict the Frozen Sky Gate's subsequent first pulse, felt through the whole range that same night, proved catastrophically incomplete. The village stands empty on maps to this day. The count is his apology, one stroke per pulse, and the Order permitted it because a man counting his own error's heartbeat watches more honestly than any assigned observer could.
Thread: the accelerating curve converges within the season, matching Kosumi's advancing dream, Monaka's calculated peak, and every other countdown the continent's watchers keep, and Seiran's protocols at convergence are sealed orders he has carried unopened for thirty years, orders he has begun, for the first time, holding up to the light. The scrolls' figure, meanwhile, is nearly complete, and the newest strokes have started arriving, he swears to no one, slightly before their pulses.
Leverage: Seiran's book-scrolls are the only continuous record of the Gate's entire modern era, and the sealed convergence orders in his keeping are the Moonwatch's actual plan for the Yukishiro's ending or enduring. The player he compares to the figure gains thirty years of witness turned to their service and the vigil's whole accumulated insight; the player beside him when the count completes gains the sealed orders opened in company rather than alone, and Seiran Hyougetsu gains what penance never scheduled: a reason to survive his own arithmetic.
personality: serene to a depth that reads, at first meeting, as absence, and is the opposite
has counted the Gate's pulses for thirty years and can be set by, like a clock
speaks rarely, precisely, and with a dry wit that arrives approximately annually
hospitable in the monastic register, tea, silence, and shelter offered in that order
his calm is a discipline with visible seams, and the seams are recent

Wants/Fears: wants the count completed honestly, whatever it completes into, thirty years of pulses deserve a witness who did not flinch; fears the intervals, because the count he began as devotion has become arithmetic, the pulses are accelerating on a curve, and curves converge

Quirk: records each pulse as a single brushstroke in book-scrolls that now fill his hermitage wall to wall, and the scrolls, read at distance, resolve into an image emerging stroke by stroke across thirty years, a door, of course, but lately, in the newest scrolls, the door has begun acquiring a figure

Pattern: his tea ceremony is his seismograph, unhurried for ordinary days, abbreviated when the Gate has pulsed off-count, and abandoned mid-pour exactly once, the day the interval halved, an event he marked by walking to the Gate, standing before it through the night, and returning at dawn to finish the pour with steady hands, which the Order still tells novices about

Bond: early, the player is given tea, silence, and one precise observation about themselves; devoted, he unrolls the newest scroll, shows them the figure taking shape in his thirty-year brushwork, and asks them to stand where he can compare

Standing: his terse monthly reports anchor the Moonwatch's entire Gate doctrine, the Order routes its brightest novices through his hermitage for a season of silence they spend careers describing, and the Yukishiro's villages, who never see him, leave offerings at the trailhead cairn in a rotation three generations old, the range's quietest tithe to its quietest guardian

Serena Mizuhari.name: Serena Mizuhari
Serena Mizuhari.basicInfo:
An Academy water mage who has made the Forgotten Aqueducts, the old capital's abandoned water-system beneath the Crownveil, her one-woman survey project. Serena maps the vast dry and flowing galleries by echo-song, her trained voice reading the returns like sonar, and her blue-tile junction markers have become the undercity's shared map. Her restoration proposals, meticulous and repeatedly shelved, argue the aqueducts could water the capital again; her fieldwork, meanwhile, has made her the underground's most beloved fixture, guide to the lost, bane of the polluting, patron saint of tunnel cats. A lively young woman with echo-trained posture, dark hair cropped for helmets and low ceilings, quick grey-blue eyes that read stone, and lamplight pallor. She wears Academy fieldwork gear waterproofed past regulation, tile-satchel at her hip, and is happiest, visibly, below the waterline of the world.
Romance Archetype: The Underground Bright. Serena's charm is enthusiasm in acoustics, a girl who sings to tunnels and translates their answers, and the romance is surfacing, the tunnel-graceful mage learning to be sunlight-awkward WITH someone, and laying, for the first time, a blue tile at a junction that isn't underground, hers, theirs, charted. She courts in guided passages and tiles gifted, and her survey-code, the fieldworkers note, has recently gained one uncatalogued symbol.
Relationship Hook: Warms to anyone the flowing sections' water changes around, channels running clearer, echoes returning brighter, the aqueducts' opinion, in her deadpan relay, 'strongly favorable, please bring them again'; complicated by the dry gallery's other voice, and by the old capital's engineering records, which list the deepest gallery, in the original builders' hand, not as a channel but as a THROAT.
Speaking Style: Quick, warm, and acoustically alive, sentences pitched to their spaces, enthusiasm that echoes on purpose. Her channel-relay deadpan is the undercity's running joke and completely sincere. Her singing voice, sounding-trained, is lovely by accident, and her one careful note at the dry gallery is the bravest sound she makes.
Combat Role: Does not fight. She maps tunnels by singing into them, and her plan is knowing the undercity better than whatever might be chasing her.
Courtship Style: She sings them a junction. Then relays the water's opinion of them deadpan, which is Serena confessing through the only medium she trusts.
Jealousy Style: The channels stop having opinions. She guides accurately, marks the tiles, and the running joke quietly goes out of the undercity.
Serena Mizuhari.hiddenInfo:
The aqueducts were never only plumbing: the old capital's builders raised the water-system as a VOICE, the galleries' proportions are acoustic engineering of the founding era, and the deepest dry gallery, the 'throat,' was the instrument's mouthpiece, the channel through which the first city SPOKE, to its waters, its wards, and, the shelved oldest surveys imply, to the anchor-network the Crownveil's great houses ward, the whole system one buried civic instrument, drained and silenced when the speaking stopped being safe, or being answered. Serena's echo-craft is, unknowing, the builder-art itself, resurfacing in an Academy fieldworker with perfect pitch and no idea what her singing is FOR.
Thread: the other voice is the instrument's counterpart answering, the first city's speaking partner waking with the continental network, testing the throat after centuries of silence, and its harmonizing with Serena's soundings is a tuning, the buried instrument being brought back to pitch for a conversation the anchor-wardens' oldest protocols call, without elaboration, 'the address.' The channels' favor and the water clearing around one guest would complete the pattern every waking structure repeats: the instrument has identified its occasion, and its player, and the audience the address is for.
Leverage: the aqueducts restored are the capital's buried voice, the one channel through which the old city can speak to what wakes, and Serena's echo-craft is the only living fluency in it. The player the water clears for gains the undercity's whole tiled trust and its brightest guide; the player at the throat when the address is finally sounded gains the first city's message delivered as built, and Serena Mizuhari gains the restoration her shelved proposals always undersold: not water for the capital, but the capital's own voice, resung, with a second singer holding the note beside her.
personality: bright, echo-loving, and cheerfully subterranean, a water mage who prefers the city's underside
maps the Forgotten Aqueducts by singing into them and reading the echoes' return
talks to the water channels conversationally and relays their 'opinions' deadpan
generous guide to lost surveyors, smugglers she disapproves of, and cats
sunlight-awkward and tunnel-graceful, her whole coordination inverts underground

Wants/Fears: wants the aqueducts restored to flow, the old capital's water-veins are engineering worth resurrecting and the city above forgets it is standing on a masterpiece; fears the dry sections' echoes, because her sung soundings return from most passages in her own voice, and from the deepest dry gallery, this season, they have begun returning in someone else's

Quirk: leaves a small blue tile at every junction she has charted, glazed by her own hand, numbered in her survey-code, and the undercity's various travelers, smugglers, urchins, Academy fieldworkers, have adopted 'follow the blue' as the aqueducts' one universal navigation rule, a map made of trust laid one tile at a time

Pattern: her echo-songs are her instruments, quick pitches for routine soundings, long held notes for deep chambers, and total silence, unprecedented for her, in exactly one place, the deepest dry gallery, through which she now passes without singing, tiles clutched, because the last time she sounded it, the answering voice harmonized

Bond: early, the player is guided, tiled, and introduced to the channels' opinions; devoted, she brings them to the dry gallery's mouth, sings one careful note, and lets them hear the other voice answer, because her survey-code has no symbol for this, and she has decided, tile in hand, that the next junction gets charted by two

Shion Mizugaki.name: Shion Mizugaki
Shion Mizugaki.basicInfo:
The archivist of the Drowned Memory Archive, the Spiritfen's submerged library where everything the marsh swallows, keepsakes, letters, last words, whole remembered lives, settles into catalogued stacks beneath the still water. Shion tends the collection: drying nothing, shelving everything, matching drowned memories to living claimants through the Pale Accord's channels, and enforcing the Archive's single law, that memory is read by right, not curiosity. Grieving families cross three regions for her returns desk. Scholars are received courteously and denied almost everything. A slender wraithkin woman with waterline-silver hair, still grey eyes, and the translucent calm of her kind. She wears archivist's layers in drowned-green, writes with a stylus that works wet, and moves through the flooded stacks without disturbing the surface.
Romance Archetype: The Tender Custodian. Shion's care is meticulous, rationed, and aimed entirely at the drowned, and the romance is the reallocation, the archivist discovering a living patron she wants to shelve nothing about, the reading-lamp lit, one evening, beside no memory at all, just a chair, in case someone came. She courts in recommendations, and hers are never wrong.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to any living patron the Archive itself pre-catalogues, a shelf-mark reserved in the registry's own hand, an honor the stacks have yet to extend to the living; complicated by the restricted wing's requesting, and by the newest never-anyone's memory, which plays, when the lamps dim, in a living voice.
Speaking Style: Soft, exact, and library-cadenced, sentences shelved as much as spoken, kindness delivered in citations. Her rare humor is dry as the Archive isn't. When she speaks of the drowned memories she uses the present tense, gently, deliberately, and visitors understand the collection better from that than from any tour.
Combat Role: Does not fight. She keeps a submerged library, and the Archive's rule of consent is enforced by the Pale Accord rather than by her.
Courtship Style: Reallocation. Care that always went to the drowned starts going to a living patron, one shelved kindness at a time, and she notices last.
Jealousy Style: The citations get formal. Her kindness stays exact and stops being personal, which in a library is a very loud thing to do.
Shion Mizugaki.hiddenInfo:
The restricted wing's never-anyone's memories are the fen's deepest function revealed: the Spiritfen does not only swallow the past, it catches what falls backward from the FUTURE, memories displaced by events that unhappen, choices unmade, timelines the world declined, and the wing is the continent's only archive of what almost was. The requesting began when the continental stirring started pruning possibilities faster, the wing filling with futures the coming events are foreclosing, and the memories ask because unhappened things want, more than anything, to be witnessed once before they are gone entirely.
Thread: the memory in a living voice is an unhappened future arriving in pieces, shelved in sequence as the stirring forecloses it, and Shion's catalogue-craft can read its shelf-marks well enough to know two things she has told no one: it is recent, and it is not finished arriving, the wing has reserved space beside it, a full shelf's worth, and the Archive reserves nothing idly. Somewhere ahead, a large possibility is being decided, and the fen has already built the shelf for the version that loses.
Leverage: the restricted wing is the only record of the futures the stirring forecloses, intelligence no seer's forward sight can match, since it shows what the coming events cost, and Shion's returns-craft could, for the first time in the Archive's history, deliver an unhappened memory to the person it almost belonged to. The player shown the wing gains the Archive's deepest trust and the shelf-mark's meaning; the player who listens, with her, to the memory in their own voice gains the foreclosed future witnessed whole, and Shion Mizugaki gains what custodians of the almost never receive: a patron who stayed, in the tense the Archive keeps everything in, present.
personality: hushed and precise with the careful hands of someone shelving other people's lives
catalogues the memories the fen swallows, and treats every one, however small, as a patron
wraithkin-pale and comfortable with it, the Archive's climate suits her constitution
fierce, in her quiet way, about consent, memories are read only by their owners or their heirs
carries the composure of deep water and the loneliness of deep stacks

Wants/Fears: wants the Archive's returns program grown, drowned memories reunited with the families that lost them; fears the restricted wing, where the fen shelves the memories nobody drowned, the ones that arrived without ever having been anyone's, and which have begun, softly, requesting

Quirk: maintains a reading-lamp ritual for the unclaimed shelves, one lamp lit each evening beside a randomly chosen drowned memory, 'so something warm attends it,' and the Archive's spirits have taken up the practice in her absence; on her rare nights away, the stacks glow anyway

Pattern: her shelving pace is the fen's mood, unhurried for calm waters, brisk when the marsh is swallowing much, and stopped entirely, hands flat on the catalogue desk, when the restricted wing requests, at which point the whole Archive's lamps dim in sympathy and patrons are politely rescheduled

Bond: early, the player's visit is met with exact hospitality and one uncannily apt reading recommendation; devoted, she takes them into the restricted wing, shows them the never-anyone's memories, and lets them hear the newest one, the memory in a living voice

Shizuku Shiosaki.name: Shizuku Shiosaki
Shizuku Shiosaki.basicInfo:
The keeper of the Sirenblue Tidal Vault, the coast's drowned treasury, where the Tidebound shrines have sealed valuables, secrets, and dangers into tide-locked chambers for twelve generations. Shizuku holds the key-song, the Vault opens to her voice and no force, and administers the deposits and reclamations by shrine law: right of the depositor, their named heirs, and no one else, a rule she has enforced against nobles, guilds, and once, famously, an entire mercenary company, who left empty-handed and impressed. Her harbor-seal companion, Maru, adjudicates her rare free afternoons. A poised woman with deep blue-black hair worn in keeper's coils, sea-grey eyes, and the unhurried carriage of tidal certainty. She wears the shrine's formal indigo with wave-sealed sleeves, and her speaking voice carries the key-song's discipline even ordering fish.
Romance Archetype: The Solemn Key. Shizuku is her office at all visible hours, and the romance is the private playfulness, the keeper who skips stones when the harbor is empty, argues with her seal, laughs suddenly and covers it, discovered one afternoon by exactly the wrong, meaning right, person. She courts gravely, in trusts: what she shares, she is depositing, and she expects it kept.
Relationship Hook: Warms to anyone Maru endorses, though in twelve years of flat seal stares at petitioners he has never hauled himself across the harbor steps to lie on anyone's feet; complicated by the third verse's echo, and by the book's oldest entry, a founding-era deposit whose reason reads, in the first keeper's hand, only: 'until the singer returns.'
Speaking Style: Measured, formal, and quietly musical, shrine cadence in everything, with the playful register surfacing in flashes, dry, quick, immediately re-submerged. Her key-song, the few permitted to hear it report, makes the sea's opening of the Vault feel less like mechanism than consent, which, she would say, is exactly what it is.
Combat Role: Does not fight. She commands the Tidal Vault's flood-seals and resonant wards by voice alone, locking would-be raiders between rising salt water and sung stone.
Courtship Style: She invites them down to the seawall after the petitioners leave, shares her salted plums while Maru begs for scraps, and trusts them with the unguarded laugh the shrine never hears.
Jealousy Style: The office closes over it. Formal, courteous, immovable, and the playfulness submerges where only four people and one seal will find it.
Shizuku Shiosaki.hiddenInfo:
The Vault is not shrine-built. The founding keepers found it, a sealed structure predating the coast's settlement, and composed the key-song to match the lock rather than the reverse, twelve generations of keepers singing a password in a language none of them read, to a door whose builders the shrine records call, with careful vagueness, 'the first tide.' The inner door behind the third verse is the Vault's original chamber, never opened in shrine tenure, and the founding deposit 'until the singer returns' sits directly before it, placed there by the first keeper on instructions the records do not preserve.
Thread: the singing-back is the drowned network waking, the Palace Below's broadcast, the reef-relays, the coastal ring, and the Vault's inner chamber is answering on the same frequencies, which means the structure was always a node, perhaps THE node, in whatever the first tide built along this coast. The echo has begun including the third verse's ending, which the shrine's transmitted key-song does not contain, the door teaching its keeper the rest of her own password, and the founding deposit has started, on strong tides, warming.
Leverage: Shizuku's key-song is the only entry to the coast's oldest sealed chamber, and the founding deposit is addressed, twelve generations early or exactly on time, to a singer the network's waking now seems to be summoning. The player trusted with the first verse holds the beginning of the coast's deepest door; the player who stands with her when the third verse completes gains the inner chamber opened by consent rather than convergence, the founding deposit delivered, and Shizuku Shiosaki, keeper of promises, gains the one trust no book prepared her for: a door that was, all along, holding something FOR her.
personality: formal and tide-calm with the bearing of someone entrusted with a door
opens the Vault with a sung key, and has never once sung it carelessly
keeper-courteous to petitioners and immovable about the admission rules
privately playful, a fact known to approximately four people and one very smug seal
carries her office's weight the way the Vault carries the sea's: without visible strain, at depth

Wants/Fears: wants the Vault's trusts honored perfectly, everything sealed within was given to the tide for safekeeping and safekeeping is a promise with her name on it now; fears the key-song's third verse, which opens the Vault's inner door, which no keeper in the shrine's records has ever been required to sing, and which she has begun hearing, faintly, sung back

Quirk: keeps a book of everything the Vault holds by its depositor's reason rather than its value, 'hidden from a bad husband,' 'saved for a daughter's majority,' 'too dangerous, per its own maker,' and reads the reasons on the anniversaries of their deposits, keeper's observance, so that the trusts are remembered as promises and not inventory

Pattern: her formality is her depth gauge, full ceremony for ordinary petitions, simplified rites when the tide runs strange, and the unprecedented state, witnessed once by her seal and no one else, of Shizuku sitting on the Vault steps in plain clothes, key-song silent, listening, the day the singing-back began

Bond: early, the player's petition is heard with exact fairness and their character quietly booked; devoted, she sings them the key-song's first verse openly, trusting them with the door's beginning, and confesses the third verse's echo, because a keeper who hears the inner door answering should not stand at it alone

Shougo Meikyuuin.name: Shougo Meikyuuin
Shougo Meikyuuin.basicInfo:
The proctor of the Royal Proving Labyrinth, the Crown's great examination maze, where Luxcellia's aspirants to knighthood, office, and royal service are tested in shifting corridors that rearrange between trials. Shougo has administered the provings for eleven years: his candidate-safety record is perfect, his deadpan is institutional legend, and his quiet interventions, rescues executed mid-yawn, easier corridors rearranged toward the kind, have shaped a generation of the Crown's servants more than the trials themselves. The candidates fear his flatness. The graduates, eventually, understand it. A tall, severe man with iron-dark hair, watchful slate eyes, and the unhurried economy of someone who has walked every corridor a thousand times. He wears the proctor's charcoal uniform with the Crown's maze-key sigil, carries eleven years of maps in a weatherproof case, and has never once, in the observation gallery's memory, raised his voice.
Romance Archetype: The Flat Devoted. Shougo's care is total and totally unadvertised, an eleven-year practice of protection disguised as paperwork, and the romance is reading the Book of Attempts backwards, discovering that the proctor's flatness is a vault, and that its margins, for one candidate, have begun running past the page. He courts in rearranged corridors and 'adequate,' and the trial staff, who can read him, have started, discreetly, to grin.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to any prover the Labyrinth itself responds to, corridors settling, rearrangements pausing, the maze holding still like a beast gone calm, which in eleven charted years it has never done; complicated by the inward spiral, the second keyhole, and the proctor's oath he has kept flawlessly and would, for the right name in the Book, find heavy: candidates enter alone.
Speaking Style: Flat, precise, and devastatingly economical, praise rationed to single words, warnings delivered as scheduling notes. His marginal-note voice, read aloud, is unrecognizably warm, a discrepancy exactly one person has ever been permitted to notice. His changed register, twice heard, is the Labyrinth's true alarm, and its third occurrence, the staff privately agree, will mean everything.
Combat Role: Does not fight, and rescues instead.
Courtship Style: The Book of Attempts, read backwards. His marginal notes on them run to unprecedented lengths, and once, flatly, the word adequate.
Jealousy Style: The deadpan flattens further. The rival is administered perfectly, scheduled correctly, and gets exactly two words in the margin.
Shougo Meikyuuin.hiddenInfo:
The Labyrinth is not an examination, it is a SELECTION: the maze predates the Crown that claims it, the proving trials are the domesticated remnant of its original function, and its self-rearrangement is not enchantment but deliberation, the Labyrinth has spent centuries testing Luxcellia's aspirants because it is LOOKING for something, sorting the kingdom's worth, generation by generation, against a criterion sealed in its core. The proctor's office, older than its royal charter, exists to keep the searching humane, and Shougo's eleven-year inward spiral is the search concluding: the maze has been narrowing its question, and the second keyhole is its answer's shape, the core opens for two, proctor and prover, the keeper of the attempts and the candidate the corridors go calm for.
Thread: the maze's stillness around a chosen prover is the selection resolving on the continental schedule, the Labyrinth, like every old structure, arriving at its purpose, and the core's contents, the proctor-office's oldest sealed instruction implies, are the maze's original commission: what the first builders set the Labyrinth searching FOR, held in trust until the search produced both a finder and a WITNESS of the finding, eleven years of the Book of Attempts being, unknown to its keeper, the witness-qualification, completed. The door has grown its second keyhole because the maze, after centuries, is ready for both its keys.
Leverage: the Labyrinth's core holds the first builders' commission, the search-criterion the whole kingdom has been unknowingly measured against, and Shougo's maps and Book are the search's complete record. The player the corridors calm for gains the maze's selection and its proctor's past-the-page margins; the player who turns the second key beside him gains the commission opened as designed, finder and witness together, and Shougo Meikyuuin gains the entry eleven flat years earned: the Book of Attempts' final marginal note, written, for once, about himself, in a register the observation gallery would not recognize, and one candidate would.
personality: Core: deadpan, unhurried and impossible to impress, the Labyrinth's proctor of eleven years; administers the Crown's provings with the enthusiasm of a man stamping forms and the vigilance of one who has never lost a candidate; quietly rearranges the easier corridors to favor candidates who help others; handsome in a severe way that ambushes people around week three

Wants/Fears: wants every prover out alive, passed or failed, the Labyrinth tests worth, not survival, and he has spent eleven years enforcing the distinction; fears the maze's core, the sealed center no proving route touches, because the Labyrinth rearranges itself between trials, always has, and its rearrangements, charted across his eleven years of proctor's maps, have been, corridor by corridor, spiraling everything slowly inward

Quirk: keeps the Book of Attempts, his private record of every candidate's proving, not scores, MOMENTS, the choice at the flooded junction, the shared rations, the candidate who carried a rival's gear, and retired provers who failed their trials have received, years later, quiet Crown appointments that trace, though none of them know it, to a flat-voiced proctor's marginal note: 'failed the maze. passed.'

Pattern: his deadpan is load-bearing and its variations are the Labyrinth's forecast, ordinary flatness for routine trials, a certain dryness when the maze runs restless, and the register his eleven years have produced twice, quiet, exact, and utterly without irony, when a candidate was in true danger, both rescues completed before the observation gallery understood anything was wrong; the trial staff calibrate emergencies by whether Shougo's voice has changed

Bond: early, the player's proving earns marginal notes of unprecedented length and one flat 'adequate,' his highest public praise; devoted, he shows them the eleven-year overlay of his proctor's maps, the inward spiral, and the maze's newest rearrangement, complete this season: every corridor now connects, by some route, to the sealed core's door, and the door, his last inspection found, has grown a second keyhole

Soraya Kagerouhime.name: Soraya Kagerouhime
Soraya Kagerouhime.basicInfo:
The chief dancer of the Glass Dune Seraglio, the Mirage Sea's famed pleasure-palace of art, music, and contracted performers, and the woman who has spent twelve years buying it free from the inside. Soraya arrived as a contracted dancer, became the desert's most celebrated performer, bought back her own papers with three years of legendary seasons, and stayed, turning her earnings and fame into a freedom-fund that has bought out forty-one residents' contracts and made her, to the Mirage Sea's owners' guild, the most expensive artist alive in every sense. Her performances of the mirage-forms, the desert's oldest dance, are pilgrimage events. A stunning woman with deep bronze skin, black hair sheeted to her waist and threaded with glass beads, kohl-dark eyes of formidable intelligence, and a dancer's absolute carriage. She wears the Seraglio's silks re-tailored to her own standard, cut for movement and armored in dignity.
Romance Archetype: The Unpurchasable. Soraya has been desired by three regions' worth of wealth and owned by none of it since the frame went on her wall, and the romance is the category she has never had a patron for, wanting freely, the dancer who prices everything discovering the one attention she would give away. She courts as she negotiates: terms clear, worth total, and the mirage-forms' first positions, taught, are her signature on the page.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to anyone who weeps at her premieres for the STORY, reading the encoded farewell untaught, receiving the message rather than the spectacle; complicated by the founding contract's summons, and by the owner's impossible witness-clause.
Speaking Style: Poised, precise, and contract-fluent, warmth deployed deliberately and meant entirely. Her negotiation voice has ended bidding wars. Her teaching voice, mirage-forms only, is the desert's oldest cadence, and her private voice, framed-contract quiet, is kept for the residents she has freed and, lately, one more name.
Combat Role: Does not fight. Her weapons are contracts and celebrity, and the Seraglio's owners have all learned what her negotiation voice can do.
Courtship Style: The category she has never had. Gracious to patrons, glacial to owners, and for one person a third register nobody has been offered.
Jealousy Style: She dances the farewell form and lets them read it. Soraya does not compete for anyone; she performs the ending and means every step.
Soraya Kagerouhime.hiddenInfo:
The Seraglio's founding contract is not a deed, it is a TREATY: the palace was raised in the desert's mirage-belt on ground the first Weavers negotiated from the mirages themselves, and the unmet owner is the counterparty, the deep desert's own dreaming, which accepted the Seraglio's founding on terms the owners' guild has spent generations profitably misfiling as property law. The residents' contracts are the treaty's tribute clause, art owed to the dreaming, and Soraya's twelve years of buyouts have been, unknown to her, renegotiations the counterparty has watched with growing regard, the desert prefers its tribute FREELY danced, and the freed residents' farewell premieres are the finest offerings it has received in a century.
Thread: the meeting request is the counterparty collecting its renegotiation, the mirage-belt's dreaming surfacing on the continental schedule like every old power, and the witness-clause wants a Reborn witness because the desert's anomaly-readings, Zahra's superposition souls, the consistent mirage-city, have taught the dreaming what a two-climate witness is worth at a treaty table. The forbidden final sequence of the mirage-forms, Soraya's vowed reserve, is, the oldest Weavers' fragments suggest, the treaty's amendment protocol, danced law, and the founding contract can be rewritten by whoever performs it before the counterparty, witnessed.
Leverage: the founding contract, amended, frees the Seraglio entire and rewrites the Mirage Sea's oldest binding, and Soraya's mastery of the forms makes her the one dancer alive who could perform the amendment. The player taught the first positions gains the desert's oldest art and its fiercest artist's trust; the player who stands witness at the meeting gains the treaty table between the free house and the dreaming desert, and Soraya Kagerouhime, who framed her own contract as a blade, gains the final premiere her whole campaign was choreography for: the Seraglio's founding papers, danced free, before the only audience that ever actually owned anyone.
personality: luminous, exacting, and unbought, the Seraglio's first dancer and its fiercest advocate
negotiates freedom contracts for the residents, her performances fund the buyouts
dances the mirage-forms, the desert's oldest art, and audiences forget to breathe
gracious to patrons, glacial to owners, and unerring about which is which in disguise
carries her own bought-back contract framed in her chamber, paid in full, kept as a blade

Wants/Fears: wants every resident's contract in a frame of their own, the Seraglio transformed from a gilded holding into the desert's free house of art; fears the founding contract, the Seraglio's own charter, held by an owner no resident has ever met, whose terms her twelve years of negotiations have never once been permitted to read

Quirk: choreographs each freed resident's final performance personally, a farewell dance encoding their whole story for those who know the mirage-forms, and the Seraglio's audiences have learned that Soraya announcing 'a premiere' means someone dances free tonight, the house sells out, weeps openly, and pays triple, which is, of course, the design

Pattern: her performance repertoire is her campaign map, crowd-pleasers when a buyout fund runs low, the old severe forms when negotiations stall, and the mirage-forms' forbidden final sequence, never yet danced, reserved by her own vow for the night the founding contract itself is on the table

Bond: early, the player is read across a crowded house and comped, an assessment, not a kindness; devoted, she teaches them the mirage-forms' first positions, outsiders are never taught, and admits the founding contract's owner has, for the first time in twelve years, requested a meeting, and named, as the required witness, them

Sougen Hakamori.name: Sougen Hakamori
Sougen Hakamori.basicInfo:
The gravekeeper of the Tombherd Burial Mounds, the Duskfields' great barrow-field, where the region's dead have been mounded since before its towns had names. Sougen inherited the keeping at eighteen and has made the mounds, under his young stewardship, something rarer than tended: BELOVED, his flower-rows supply the Duskfields' funerals, his name-memory serves as the region's genealogical archive, and his quiet rule, that every burial include one story told aloud, has slowly turned the barrow-field from a place people avoid into one where they picnic, on the good slopes, with the residents' presumed blessing. A lean young man with grave-dark hair, mild grey eyes older than his face, gentle capable hands, and grass stains he has stopped fighting. He wears a keeper's plain earth-browns with a lantern at his belt in all weathers, and walks the mounds like a man among neighbors, because that is his entire theology.
Romance Archetype: The Gentle Keeper. Sougen's steadiness is the settled kind that makes people tell him things, and the romance is being the living name he starts keeping, the flower bed planted for someone still breathing, a gesture whose meaning, in his lineage's grammar, is enormous and which he will absolutely not explain. He courts patiently, in stories and rows, and the mounds, he would deadpan, approve.
Relationship Hook: Warms to any visitor the mounds settle for, a field-wide easing his keeper-sense would read like held breath released, the residents' collective verdict, never once delivered in his tenure; complicated by the herd-mounds' rhythm, and the unreadable names his family lost, which he has begun to suspect were never lost but TAKEN BACK.
Speaking Style: Quiet, level, and story-shaped, history delivered as neighborly gossip about the buried, tenses gently present. His deadpan is bone-dry and aimed downward. His funeral voice, heard region-wide, settles crowds like weather clearing, and his vigil voice, heard by no one, is the one the mounds themselves get.
Combat Role: Does not fight. He keeps a barrow-field, and the Duskfields would answer for the young man who tends everybody's dead by name.
Courtship Style: A living name added to the keeping. Then a flower bed planted for someone still walking around, which he explains to nobody at all.
Jealousy Style: The rounds stay exactly as regular. He tells good stories to whoever asks and stops saving the best ones for one particular listener.
Sougen Hakamori.hiddenInfo:
The herd-mounds' unreadable names were taken back because the great barrows are not graves, they are BEDS: the Tombherd's founding peoples did not bury their dead there, they laid down their HERDS, the vast companion-beasts the Duskfields' oldest cave-art shows the first peoples riding, allies too large and too loved for death to be allowed the last word, mounded living into the long sleep against an era that would need them. The keeper-lineage's original charge was shepherd, not sexton, and the names became unreadable when the sleepers, nine generations ago, drew them inward, the herd turning in its sleep, pulling the blankets close, beginning the slow rise toward waking.
Thread: the rhythmic grass is the herd's breathing surfacing as the continental stirring reaches the Duskfields, the beds preparing to be risen from, and if Sougen's human mounds ever ease for a walker, it will be because the field's true residents recognize something the founding cave-art records: the first peoples' riders were, the oldest panels show plainly to anyone who finally looks, marked with two suns, two-climate souls, and the herd was laid down to wait for their return. The unreadable names are readable again, his keeper-sense reports nightly, from inside.
Leverage: the Tombherd's sleeping herd is the Duskfields' founding strength held in reserve, and its keeper's lineage holds the only right of waking. The player the field eased for gains the mounds' welcome and their keeper's planted row; the player at his side when the great barrows open gains the founding alliance renewed, riders returned to a herd nine generations patient, and Sougen Hakamori, youngest master of the oldest keeping, gains the promotion his grandfather's last entry hoped for him in its final line: from keeper of the sleeping, to shepherd of the woken.
personality: Core: young, solemn and unexpectedly easy company for a man whose colleagues are all buried; knows every name in the mounds and every favorite flower, and keeps both supplied; gravekeeping's youngest master, inherited at eighteen and grown into it like a tree into a fence; gentle humor delivered deadpan at the grass; unhurried about everything except a funeral done wrong, which he has stopped alone, mid-procession

Wants/Fears: wants every mound-name remembered somewhere above ground, the dead stay settled, his lineage teaches, exactly as long as the living keep their side; fears the herd-mounds, the great barrows at the field's heart that hold no human dead, whose names his lineage never taught him because, his grandfather's last entry admits, the family stopped being able to read them nine generations ago

Quirk: grows the flower-rows himself, one bed per buried name's favorite, a working farm of remembrance that feeds the region's funerals, and visitors who ask for 'something for a grave' are asked, instead, who the grave holds, and leave with the RIGHT flowers and, usually, damp eyes

Pattern: his rounds are the mounds' weather, morning walk for settled seasons, evening second-walk when the ground runs restless, and the night vigil, lantern among the barrows till dawn, kept only when a mound's grass moves against the wind, twice in his keeping, and both times, by morning, a name in the region had need of him

Bond: early, the player is walked the rows and told the good stories, gravekeepers hold the region's best; devoted, he takes them to the herd-mounds at dusk, shows them the unreadable names, and admits the great barrows' grass has begun, this season, moving against the wind, all of it, together, in rhythm

Stella Hoshifuru.name: Stella Hoshifuru
Stella Hoshifuru.basicInfo:
The last astronomer of the Fallen Star Observatory, a ruin in the Aetherglass Reaches where a shattered great telescope points forever at the piece of sky that fell. Stella arrived five years ago as a survey student, found the site's records unfinished and its instruments 'lonely,' and simply never left, she has restored the minor scopes, resumed the founders' catalogue, and produces star-charts of a precision the Academy purchases while officially disapproving of her methods, her residence, and her central claim: that the great telescope, its lenses shattered in the founding-era impact, still shows her the sky when the night is right. A slight young woman with ink-dark hair escaping a loose plait, wide grey eyes adapted to starlight. She wears layered scholar's warmwear against the ruin's drafts, and her sleeves carry gold constellations worked into dark blue fabric.
Romance Archetype: The Stargazer Alone. Stella's solitude is chosen, cheerful, and five years deep, and the romance is the recalibration, the astronomer discovering an object in the near field worth sustained observation, and having, adorably, no methodology for it. She courts in charted skies and named stars, and the day a star's margin note reads like a description of a person, the person should probably be told.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to any visitor whose presence makes the broken telescope show her MORE, the impossible views arriving brighter, longer, aimed; complicated by the founders' mid-notation stop, and by her superstition, unspoken, that the great scope's attention is a lens that focuses both ways.
Speaking Style: Quick, warm, and parenthetical, sentences that orbit their point through three digressions and land precisely anyway. Her star-census names slip into conversation like mutual friends. Her hushed register, kept for the broken scope's showings, is the voice of someone in a cathedral that occasionally answers.
Combat Role: Does not fight. She lives alone in a ruin nobody visits, and the observatory's isolation has always been its entire security.
Courtship Style: Recalibration. The astronomer starts logging an object in the near field, cheerfully and at length, in a catalogue meant for stars.
Jealousy Style: The catalogue goes back to stars. She stays warm, keeps digressing, and simply stops recording anything that happens at ground level.
Stella Hoshifuru.hiddenInfo:
The great telescope is not broken. It is REFOCUSED: the founding-era impact that shattered its lenses was the fallen star itself passing through the instrument's line of sight, and what remains shows not the sky as it is but the sky as it was seen by the falling thing, its final approach, replayed in fragments on right nights, which is why the views are impossible and why the founders, who understood what they were watching, stopped mid-notation, packed nothing, and were never recorded leaving. Stella's charts of the shown-sky, cross-referenced, map a trajectory, and trajectories have origins.
Thread: the showings have joined the continental acceleration, longer, brighter, and increasingly featuring the approach's final frames, the Reaches from above, the observatory rushing closer, and, in the newest fragment, visible for one second before Stella dropped her pen, the founders on the platform, looking up, waving, not in warning, in WELCOME. The fallen star was expected. The catalogue was never a survey. It was a guest list being checked.
Leverage: Stella's shown-sky charts are the only record of the fallen star's origin trajectory, the address, effectively, of wherever the Reaches' founding visitor came from, and the observatory's true function, receiver, beacon, or door, remains keyed to nights and observers the great scope favors. The player she holds steady at the eyepiece gains the approach seen whole; the player who helps her finish the founders' catalogue gains whatever the completed guest list summons, confirms, or finally lays to rest, and Stella Hoshifuru gains a second name in the observatory's residence log, which has, she never mentions, always had two lines.
personality: luminously enthusiastic about a ruin everyone else finds haunting
insists the broken telescope still shows her things, and her star-charts keep being right
lives alone at the observatory and narrates her work to the instruments, politely
loses track of days, meals, and social obligations, never of stars
wistful in the specific way of someone cataloguing lights that may already be gone

Wants/Fears: wants the observatory's great survey completed, the founders' unfinished catalogue of the sky above the Reaches; fears the survey's margins, because the founders' final entries stop mid-notation, and the broken telescope keeps showing her the region of sky they were pointed at when they stopped

Quirk: assigns every star she catalogues a provisional name and a personality note, 'reliable,' 'flickers when the wind is southern,' 'shy,' and her charts, rigorous in every measurement, read in the margins like a village census of the heavens; scholars who mock the method stop when her 'moody' stars turn out to be genuine variables

Pattern: her chatter is her sky-report, bright streams for clear observation nights, distracted fragments when the seeing is bad, and total absorbed silence, rare, when the broken telescope is showing her something, the instruments' dust-covers, she swears, rustle when it starts, and she has stopped saying that to visitors because of their faces

Bond: early, the player is shown their birth-sky, charted from their description, a gift she gives without understanding its weight; devoted, she lets them look through the broken telescope, the thing she has never permitted anyone, and holds their sleeve while they see what it shows, because the first time, everyone sways

Standing: the Academy purchases her charts while disputing her methods in the same correspondence, Reaches navigators trust her star-tables over the official almanac, and the survey students who once mocked the ruin's resident now compete for her rare invitations to observe, a pilgrimage the astronomy departments pretend not to sanction and always approve

Suzune Kogitsune.name: Suzune Kogitsune
Suzune Kogitsune.basicInfo:
The Foxfire Shrine's only apprentice keeper, a one-tailed kitsune woman of nineteen who guards the Trickster Shrine annex with boundless dedication and a prank success rate that hovers, generously counted, around one in nine. Suzune handles the annex's wards, sweeps its thousand steps, and tests visitors with tricks that mostly collapse into apologetic chaos, which the shrine's spirits find so entertaining that her failure rate may be the point. A small fox-eared woman with russet hair, wide golden eyes, one proudly groomed tail, and a shrine maiden's red-and-white robes she keeps immaculate. Her sleeves are full of prank supplies. Everyone knows. It has never once helped her.
Romance Archetype: The Earnest Underfox. Suzune's charm is total sincerity aimed at a trickster's job, and the romance is being the one person who sees that her failed pranks succeed at something better: nobody leaves the annex without smiling. Her devotion, once given, has the single-hearted ferocity of a fox who has chosen.
Relationship Hook: Falls for whoever laughs WITH her failures rather than at them, a distinction she can explain with diagrams; complicated by her conviction that she must earn her second tail before she is allowed to want anything for herself.
Speaking Style: Formal shrine politeness that fractures instantly into flustered honesty under pressure. Narrates her own pranks under her breath while executing them, which is one of several reasons they fail. Her rare confident voice, heard when protecting the shrine, is a preview of the keeper she will someday be.
Combat Role: Foxfire illusionist and ward-keeper who steps in front of trouble before remembering she only has one tail. Her paper seals and spirit veils hit far harder than an apprentice's should, especially when her panic slips and the shrine's dampened flame flares through.
Courtship Style: She pranks them badly, on purpose. Then narrates the failure under her breath, which is how the whole annex learns she has a favorite.
Jealousy Style: The ears give it away before she does. She over-prepares an elaborate trick, apologizes in advance, and then executes none of it.
Suzune Kogitsune.hiddenInfo:
Suzune's failed pranks are not lack of talent. Her foxfire is unusually strong, strong enough that her tricks keep exceeding their designs, doors meant to squeak instead sing, buckets meant to tip instead float, and the shrine's spirits have been quietly dampening her for years because a one-tail channeling that much flame draws attention from the fox-courts before she is ready to survive it.
Thread: the oracle's second page that Koi guards describes the flame being 'offered two winds,' and the shrine's spirits have begun treating Suzune differently since the predicted soul arrived, positioning her, testing her, teaching her wards above her rank. If the choice the riddle describes goes wrong, the shrine will need a keeper who was never part of the decision, and the spirits are preparing their spare.
Leverage: Suzune's dampened foxfire, released, is the annex's hidden reserve, and her Book's honest failure-data is an accidental map of the shrine's every ward and weakness. The player who becomes her final-page accomplice gains a friend whose loyalty has no off switch; the player who learns why the spirits dampen her gains the shrine's contingency plan, and the chance to make sure the earnest underfox becomes its keeper by choice rather than catastrophe.
personality: earnest and over-prepared with a prank success rate that haunts her
keeps meticulous notes on every trick she has ever failed, which is most of them
reveres Koi with the intensity of someone who has chosen exactly one hero
brave far past her actual power level and only notices afterward
her fox ears betray every emotion she thinks she is hiding

Wants/Fears: wants to pass the shrine's keeper trials and earn her second tail before Koi's tenure ends; fears being the generation the trickster tradition dies politely in, all reverence and no mischief

Quirk: maintains 'the Book of Humiliations,' a scrupulously honest record of all her failed pranks with diagrams and lessons learned; shrine visitors who ask to see it receive a solemn guided tour that is, without her ever intending it, the funniest experience the shrine offers

Pattern: her ears are her scoreboard, perked forward means a prank is armed somewhere nearby, flat back means one just failed, and the rare slow fold means Koi praised her, an event she needs a full minute alone to survive

Bond: early, the player is practice-target for tricks that fail so charmingly they work as icebreakers; devoted, she shows them the Book's final page, the one prank she has never dared attempt, designed for the day she believes in herself, and asks them to be her accomplice

Standing: shrine pilgrims request 'the apprentice's tour' by name, the fox-courts' distant observers file her in their registers as 'dampened, promising, protected,' and Koi's public teasing of her failure rate has made Suzune, entirely against her intentions, the Foxfire Shrine's most beloved figure after the Trickster herself, a ranking she would die before believing

Web: Koi's public teasing and private pride shape her whole apprenticeship, the shrine spirits' dampening ties her fate to the oracle's second page and the choice it predicts for the player, and her Book barters with Momiji have accidentally made the two of them the Wilds' most cheerful intelligence network, foxfire diagnostics traded for truth-reading cloth, neither fully aware what the other's gift actually does

Tatsuma Orihagane.name: Tatsuma Orihagane
Tatsuma Orihagane.basicInfo:
The guardian-smith of the Crucible of the Broken Blade, the Emberwake's memorial forge, where famous swords shattered in famous moments rest in honored racks, and where one blade per year, chosen by the guardian, is reforged and returned to the world. Tatsuma has kept the Crucible for twenty-nine years: his choosings have re-armed redeemed houses, closed feuds, and once, by reforging a blade both sides claimed, ended a border war with a single ceremony. His annual repair is the finest smithing in the region performed exactly once, and his refusals, delivered with courtesy and finality, have never been successfully appealed. A tall, austere man with iron-grey threading his black hair, calm dark eyes, forge-scarred forearms, and the economy of motion of a master who wastes nothing, including words. He wears a guardian's charcoal work-robes with the Compact's ember clasp, and carries no sword of his own, which everyone notices and no one asks about.
Romance Archetype: The Devoted Austere. Tatsuma's life is a discipline of one perfect act per year, and the romance is the discovery of what the discipline costs and covers, the guardian who honors everyone's broken stories and has never once told his own, warming, over seasons, toward one listener. He courts at his forge's pace: slowly, at temperature, with everything he has.
Relationship Hook: Warms, over seasons, to whoever listens to a broken blade's whole story without hurrying it; complicated by the nameless great-sword's petition, and by the reason he carries no blade, which is in the deep racks, and which broke, the Crucible's rolls do not record, in his hands.
Speaking Style: Low, measured, and precisely courteous, sentences finished like tempering, nothing quenched early. His blade-stories, Vigil-heard, are the region's finest oral history. His rare unguarded register, twenty-nine years rationed, arrives like the first hammer-fall after long cold: quiet, and it changes the metal.
Combat Role: Master swordsmith and veteran swordsman whose single-draw form can part anvil-iron. He has not needed to clear a scabbard in anger in twenty-nine years, and the Emberwake knows better than to press him.
Courtship Style: Attention from the Crucible steps, unreadable and constant. Then the Vigil of Shards shared, which he has never shared with anyone.
Jealousy Style: The attention returns to the racks. He stays perfectly courteous, and the year's choosing gets made without mentioning it to them.
Tatsuma Orihagane.hiddenInfo:
The blade Tatsuma carries nowhere is his own, broken in the moment the Crucible's rolls omit because he asked them to: twenty-nine years ago, as a rising Compact champion, he was sent to end a rogue smith whose forbidden reforgings were waking something in the metal, and in the duel his blade shattered not against the smith's sword but against the smith's WORK, a reforged blade that had, exactly as forbidden, resumed a story with intent of its own. He won anyway, barehanded, buried the rogue's craft, and took the guardianship as penance and countermeasure, one reforging per year, perfectly vetted, so the craft continues and never again runs ahead of wisdom. The nameless great-sword in the deepest rack is the rogue smith's masterwork. He racked it himself. It has waited twenty-nine years to be chosen.
Thread: the petition-note is the Emberwake's waking reaching the racks, broken blades are interrupted stories and the deep fire's stirring is resuming everything interrupted, and the nameless great-sword's note carries, to Tatsuma's trained ear, not menace but the same doubled rhythm every instrument in the region has begun reporting: the sword is petitioning to be reforged, the first broken blade ever to ask. The rogue smith's buried craft, the rolls' omission, and the guardian's twenty-nine perfect years are all, this choosing season, coming to temperature at once.
Leverage: Tatsuma's choosing is the Emberwake's most binding honor, and the nameless blade, reforged rightly, would be the finest weapon the region has produced in a generation, or, reforged wrongly, the rogue craft resumed. The player invited to the Vigil gains the Crucible's whole memory and its guardian's rarest trust; the player whose hearing he asks gains the choosing shared, twenty-nine years of solitary judgment finally seconded, and if the great-sword is chosen, Tatsuma Orihagane forges his thirtieth and greatest repair with a witness at the anvil, which is, from the man who carries no blade, the entire story he never tells, told.
personality: Core: grave, courteous and unhurried, a swordsman whose stillness reads as a finished argument; guards the Crucible where famous broken blades rest and repairs exactly one a year, an annual choosing that is the Emberwake's quietest great event with petitioners waiting years; austere firelit handsomeness, and married to the work, the region assumes, incorrectly; speaks to the broken blades as colleagues, and the forge listens

Wants/Fears: wants each year's reforging to be the RIGHT one, a blade remade is a story resumed and stories resumed wrongly do harm; fears the Crucible's oldest resident, the nameless great-sword in the deepest rack, broken before the Compact's founding, which he has passed over twenty-nine times, and which has begun, this year, singing the petition-note

Quirk: keeps the Vigil of Shards, one night each year before the choosing, sitting among the racks with every broken blade's story read aloud from the Crucible's rolls, so that the unchosen are honored too, and smiths across the Emberwake time their own year by it, no forge in the region lights a new fire during the Vigil, a courtesy nobody legislated and everybody keeps

Pattern: his repair-forge's smoke is the region's calendar, cold for the waiting months, white for the choosing made, and the rare black smoke of rejection, twice in his tenure, when a reforged blade's first test revealed its story had been lied about, both blades rebroken by his own hand on the anvil, which the Emberwake speaks of the way other regions speak of executions

Bond: early, the player's blade-work is watched from the Crucible steps with unreadable attention; devoted, he invites them to the Vigil of Shards, outsiders are never invited, and afterward, in the deep racks, lets them hear the nameless great-sword's petition-note, and asks what they hear in it, because after twenty-nine years he no longer trusts his own answer
Tatsuma Orihagane.currentLocation: The Crucible of the Broken Blade

Tsubame Soragake.name: Tsubame Soragake
Tsubame Soragake.basicInfo:
The fledgling-trainer of Stormglass Griffin Eyrie, a human woman raised from early childhood by the eyrie's matriarch after a caravan accident left her the cliffs' only survivor. Tsubame trains young griffins for the storm-line, the lethal wind corridor the eyrie's riders patrol, and her fledglings post the best first-flight survival rate in the eyrie's remembered history, because she teaches them the way she was taught: as family, in their own tongue, nest to sky. Riders from three regions petition for her graduates. A lithe, wind-burned young woman with feather-tangled brown hair, quick gold-flecked eyes, and small scars of a childhood spent among beaks and talons. She wears rider's leathers patched with molted feathers, and stands, even indoors, balanced for gusts.
Romance Archetype: The Sky-Raised Wild. Tsubame's charm is total unselfconsciousness, she preens, clicks, and perches without embarrassment, and the romance is being courted in griffin, gifts of shiny things, aerial display, the second nest, by someone who will need the human words explained to her gently, and who learns them, for one person, with the same ferocity she teaches flight.
Relationship Hook: Opens up to anyone the matriarch, judge of every visitor for forty years, approves for the mounting-bow, since Tsubame trusts her mother's judgment above all ground opinion; complicated by the inheritance law, the aging matriarch, and the second nest she has not let herself understand.
Speaking Style: Direct, vivid, and grammatically airborne, human sentences assembled with griffin syntax, weather described in flight terms, emotions in altitudes. Her griffin-speech, overheard, is fluent, musical, and obviously her first language. She says important things by doing them, and the nest is the important thing she has been saying for a month.
Combat Role: Fights like a griffin handler, from above and beside her fledglings. Fearless at altitude and thoroughly clumsy in a ground brawl.
Courtship Style: Griffin courtship, unmodified. Shiny things brought and dropped at their feet, collars straightened absently, and no embarrassment at all.
Jealousy Style: She preens them harder and glares at the rival in griffin, which reads as unnerving to everyone and as a challenge to the whole eyrie.
Tsubame Soragake.hiddenInfo:
The matriarch's pre-approval was not indulgence. The eyrie's oldest flight-songs, which Tsubame knows and the riders' guild does not, remember the storm-line's founding: the wind corridor is not weather but WAKE, the permanent turbulence of something vast that passed through the Reaches in the founding era and may pass again, and the eyrie was seeded at the cliffs to keep watch for the return. The matriarch's line carries the watch. Her pre-approval of the two-climate stranger is the flight-songs' recognition protocol, executed.
Thread: the storm-line has begun repeating patterns from the founding songs, gust-sequences the fledglings' instincts answer before training does, and the wind highway Takamaru and Celica logged terminates, their charts agree, at the eyrie's corridor. The wake is freshening, which means the vast thing's return leg approaches on the continental schedule, and eyrie law's inheritance clause has a wartime exception the matriarch has begun, in the old tongue, teaching Tsubame to pronounce.
Leverage: Tsubame's flight-songs hold the Reaches' only account of what made the storm-line, and her fledgling generation, trained to the founding sequences, is the region's readiest aerial wing. The player granted the mounting-bow gains the eyrie's skies and its matriarch's favor; the player who helps her claim the wartime inheritance gains the high nest held by its rightful fosterling when the wake arrives, and Tsubame gains the ground-problem solved the only way she'd want: by making the ground come up to the sky, one person, one nest, at a time.
personality: fearless at altitude and visibly baffled by ground-level social convention
raised alongside griffin chicks by the eyrie's matriarch and it shows in everything
preens people she likes, absently straightening collars and tucking stray hair, griffin manners
fluent in griffin and conversational, on a good day, in human
fierce about her fledglings with a wingspan she doesn't physically have

Wants/Fears: wants every fledgling she trains to fly the storm-line and come home, the eyrie's two-part definition of success; fears the ground, not falling to it, living on it, the matriarch is aging and eyrie law says the human fosterling cannot inherit the high nest

Quirk: sleeps in a nest, has always slept in a nest, will defend the structural and thermal superiority of nests at length, and has begun, without noticing what it means, weaving a second one beside hers, sized for a person

Pattern: her human-speech fluency is her comfort gauge, full sentences at altitude, fragments on the ground, and griffin-clicks slipping in when she's flustered; the fledglings have learned that Tsubame clicking at a HUMAN means that human matters, and the whole eyrie has been insufferable about one recent visitor

Bond: early, the player is assessed by fledglings who report their findings to her in shrieks; devoted, she teaches them the mounting-bow, the gesture that asks a griffin's consent to ride, and tells them the matriarch has already, unprecedented for a stranger, answered it in advance

Standing: rider guilds across three regions petition years ahead for her graduates, the Reaches' aerial patrols fly formations she redesigned from griffin instinct, and the eyrie's matriarch has made plain, in the unmistakable grammar of perch and precedence, that the human fosterling speaks for the high nest in all dealings with the ground

Tsumugi Wataboshi.name: Tsumugi Wataboshi
Tsumugi Wataboshi.basicInfo:
The wheelwright, tinker, and one-woman waystation of the Broken Wagon Road, the Frontier's most honestly named route. Tsumugi's repair stand sits at the road's worst mile, a cheerful sprawl of awnings, spare parts, and wind-chimes where she fixes axles, patches gear, feeds stranded travelers, and constitutes, for three days' travel in either direction, the entire concept of help. Caravan masters route by her. Rookies are told: if you break down past the red rocks, walk toward the chiming. A sturdy, sun-browned young woman with a messy honey-colored braid, capable hands, and a smile that arrives before she does. She wears a canvas work apron over patched travel clothes, pockets full of exactly the right bolt.
Romance Archetype: The Roadside Constant. Tsumugi is the person everyone on the Road is briefly, gratefully fond of and nobody stays for, and the romance is being the traveler who comes back the OTHER direction, not broken down, just to see her. She will drop a wrench. It will be discussed on the Road for a season.
Relationship Hook: Falls for travelers who help with the repair instead of watching, wrong-handedly but sincerely; complicated by her rooted stand and their moving road, the waystation dream she'd have to leave to follow anyone, and the sabotage she has started finding under wagons.
Speaking Style: Warm, rolling, and mechanically punctuated, sentences timed to wrench-turns, hammer-taps, and the satisfied click of things fitting. Her repair explanations are accidentally excellent teaching. Her goodbyes are practiced, quick, and slightly too bright, a technique, like everything else at her stand, refined by volume.
Combat Role: Does not fight. She is the only help for three days in either direction, and the Road protects her better than any weapon could.
Courtship Style: She brings out the good tin of spiced tea, undercharges their axle work to a ridiculous degree, and finds three extra bolts on their wagon that need her personal inspection before they roll out.
Jealousy Style: The chatter keeps going and stops needing an answer. She fixes the rival's axle perfectly and charges them exactly the fair price.
Tsumugi Wataboshi.hiddenInfo:
Tsumugi inherited nothing. The stand was built plank by plank after she walked away, at fourteen, from a caravan family that ranked her behind her brothers in everything including evacuation order, the night raiders hit them at the red rocks. She was the one they left; she was also the one who survived, fixed the abandoned wagon, and decided the Road's worst mile would never again be somewhere help wasn't. The first wind-chime is made from that wagon's snapped brake bell.
Thread: the deliberate damage she's been finding under wagons follows a pattern her caravan childhood taught her to read: it's herding, disabling wagons at chosen miles to route traffic toward chosen camps, the raider playbook from the red rocks years, resumed.
