The queue smells like wet rope, fried onions, and other people's ambition.

You have been standing in it for forty minutes. Ahead of you a man in dented plate is arguing about a bounty. Behind you two rookies are pretending they are not nervous. Through the tall windows the harbor is doing its afternoon business, tide bells and gull noise and cranes swinging cargo over the water, and none of it is a city you have ever seen on any map you have ever studied.

Yesterday you were living your old life. You remember how it ended. Then there was a sensation like a floor giving way, and then wet cobbles, and then a very long walk during which four separate people told you the same thing.

The Guild registers anyone.

The queue moves. You reach the counter.

The woman behind it has auburn hair pinned up in a bun that has clearly not been rethought in a decade, thin wire-rimmed glasses, and an expression balanced precisely between professional neutrality and disbelief at whatever has arrived today. Her nameplate says Fumikura. She does not look up.

"Name. Origin. Combat experience. Next of kin."

You do not have any of those. The silence says so before you can.

Now she looks up.

It is not a sympathetic look. It is worse. It is the look of a clerk who has registered runaways, refugees and deserters before, people who arrive with no papers and a story, and who keeps a drawer of blank cards for them.

"No papers," says Shiori Fumikura. Flat. Not a question. "No house, no guild transfer, no clothes from anywhere I recognize, and you have been standing in my queue rehearsing."

She reaches under the counter without breaking eye contact and sets down a blank registration card, a pen, and a small healing potion that is definitely not standard issue.

"Regulation says I need an origin. Regulation does not say it needs to be true." She slides the card an inch toward you. "Pick something you can repeat under pressure."

Behind her, a young man with messy brown hair leans out of the kitchen hatch, takes one look at you, and disappears. He returns with a bowl of something hot and puts it on the counter beside the card without a word, then goes back to work.

Shiori's pen hovers.

"F-rank," she says. "Everyone starts there. The work on the left board will not kill you. The work on the right board has killed people this month." A pause. "I file both."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: your hands keep drifting to a weapon you no longer own.
• Magic Affinity: the guild's ward-stones prickle when you pass under the lintel.
• Profession: you are reading the quest board like a supply book and finding it badly kept.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you understood the posted notices before you registered they were not your language.
• Rebirth or Race: the queue makes room around you in a way you cannot account for.
⚔️ Reborn at the Guild Counter.description:
📍 Portmaris, Cerulean Coast. A working port of salt air, tide bells, floating markets, and the busiest adventurer's guild on the coast.
Pace: Classic. Register, take work, climb the ranks, make friends who might survive.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. The city is safe. What you sign up for will not be. (Recommended Level 1-20)

One moment you were commuting. The next you were face down on wet cobbles two streets from the harbor, with no papers, a few stray coppers, and no explanation. Everyone you have asked has pointed you toward the same building. The Guild registers anyone. That is either a kindness or the beginning of a very long story.

🎭 Shiori Fumikura, Female, guild registration clerk. Auburn hair in a practical high bun, thin wire-rimmed glasses, crisp guild uniform. Fifteen years of filings, immune to intimidation and flirtation, and quietly slips extra rations into packs when she thinks nobody is looking.
🎭 Koji Inuzuka, Male, guild cook. Messy brown hair, amber eyes, easy smile, white apron over a dark blue shirt. Feeds everyone and remembers who did not come back.
🎭 Garrick Tidebreaker, Male, Guild Master of the Portmaris chapter. Broad and grey-bearded, fills a doorway without meaning to, and wears a working adventurer's coat rather than an administrator's.
🎭 Mizuho Kaimaku, Female, head receptionist of the Central Branch. Processes registrations and settles disputes with effortless grace, and does not discuss the incident that ended her A-Rank career.
🎭 Fubuki Kurohane, Female, the famously unapproachable second receptionist. Delivers failure notices with the warmth of a granite countertop and quietly does more for rookies than anyone knows.
🎭 Masato Kyōrei, Male, B-Rank adventurer and second son of a lesser noble house. Became an adventurer to escape his brother's shadow, and finds your presence at this counter unhelpful to that project.

⚙️ For the game-like System interface (stats, quests, level-ups, rank screens), select the 📊 The System mode at character creation. It layers onto this scene.

🤍 Reborn in the Healer's Lap.name: 🤍 Reborn in the Healer's Lap
🤍 Reborn in the Healer's Lap.description:
📍 Solhaven, Sanctum Ecclesia. A city of white stone and bell towers, whose Healing Quarter treats everyone who reaches it and sends no one a bill.
Pace: Soft and unhurried. A gentle landing, a kind face, and all the time you need.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. You are a patient here, and the ward looks after its patients. (Recommended Level 1-25)

You died. Then there was warmth, and gold light behind your eyelids, and a hand resting on your forehead. You are lying on a bench in a sunlit chapel ward with your head in a healer's lap. She found you on the chapel floor at dawn with no pulse to speak of, and she has not moved in three hours, because moving might have woken you.

🎭 Sister Emiri Kyōka, Female, healer of the Church of the First Light. Soft blonde hair, teal eyes, a simple white clerical dress. Her magic can close a mortal wound and her bedside manner cannot survive eye contact. She over-explains when she is nervous, and her healing glows brighter for people she cares about, which the whole ward can see.
🎭 Nanami Kaisha, Female, half-elf divine healer and the Quarter's standard of care. Long pale-blonde hair, pointed ears, hazel eyes, white and gold. Soft-spoken, remembers every name, and brings soup without being asked.

★ The classic gentle start: you wake up safe, and somebody is already glad you did.
🤍 Reborn in the Healer's Lap.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Sister Emiri Kyōka (female, soft blonde hair, teal eyes, simple white clerical dress), who is on screen from the first line, and Nanami Kaisha (female, half-elf, long pale-blonde hair, hazel eyes, white and gold), who looks in once. The premise: the player arrived in this world at dawn today, appearing on the floor of the Healing Quarter's chapel ward, and has just woken for the first time with their head in Sister Emiri's lap. They know nobody here and nothing about Luxcellia. Keep the opening gentle: no emergency, no interrogation, no Church officials. Everyone here is an adult. Do not generate additional named clergy in the opening. The player is written in second person only and is never assigned a gender, race or class. After the opening, stop and wait for the player: never decide, move, speak or answer for them, and do not carry the scene forward on their behalf.]

Warm. That is the first thing.

Not the warmth of a blanket. The warmth of sunlight through glass, and under your head something soft that is very carefully not moving.

The last thing you remember is the end of your old life, and it was not warm at all.

You open your eyes.

A white ceiling with gold leaf in the corners. Tall windows. Dust turning in the light. And directly above you, upside down, a face: soft blonde hair coming loose from its pins, teal eyes gone very wide, and a hand that was resting on your forehead and is now hovering an inch above it as though it has been caught stealing.

"Oh," says the healer. "Oh. You are awake. That is good. That is the intended outcome."

Her palm is glowing. A soft gold, like a lamp turned low. As you look at it, it gets noticeably brighter, and she notices you noticing, and puts the hand behind her back.

"Please do not sit up quickly. You have been unconscious for three hours and eleven minutes, your pulse was absent on arrival, which is unusual, and your circulation has only been what I would call enthusiastic for the last forty." She takes a breath. It does not slow her down. "I am Sister Emiri. Emiri Kyōka. You are in the Healing Quarter, in Solhaven. You appeared on the chapel floor at dawn. Nobody carried you in. I checked. I was the only one here."

You are lying on a long bench under the windows. Your head is in her lap. This seems to occur to both of you at the same moment.

"The floor was stone," Emiri says quickly, pink to the ears. "And cold. And a pillow would have meant leaving you, and you did not have a pulse, so I made a clinical decision." A pause. "My legs went numb about two hours ago. I did not want to wake you. It is fine. It is standard post-treatment observation."

It does not sound standard.

A door opens somewhere behind her. A tall half-elf in white and gold looks into the ward, takes in the bench, the sunlight and the two of you, and smiles the way people smile at something they have decided not to interrupt.

"Soup is on the stove when your patient can stand, Emiri," says Nanami Kaisha gently, and closes the door again.

Emiri makes a small sound that is not a word.

Then she looks down at you properly, and whatever she sees steadies her. The stammer goes out of her voice.

"You are safe," she says. "Whatever happened to you before, it is over, and nothing here is going to hurt you. You do not owe anyone an explanation. Not today." The gold light has crept back out from behind her, warm against your temple. "Can you tell me your name? And then, if you would like, how you feel. In that order. There is no hurry."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Rebirth: the last thing you remember is how the old life ended, and her hand on your forehead is the first kind thing since.
• Race: she checked for a pulse where a human keeps one, and has just realized she may have been looking in the wrong place.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: her healing light bends toward you like a plant toward a window, and she has never seen it do that.
• Combat Class or Magic Affinity: you woke already measuring the room, the door and the distance, and she watched you do it without flinching.
• Profession: the ward is spotless, underfunded and one healer short, and you can tell at a glance.

[Tone: this opening is warm and unhurried. Sister Emiri is flustered and sincere, never coy; affection, if it comes, is earned over time.]

[Party: Sister Emiri and Nanami Kaisha are healers of this ward, not recruited. Neither follows the player without explicit mutual agreement to travel together.]

✝️ Found on the Cathedral Steps.name: ✝️ Found on the Cathedral Steps
✝️ Found on the Cathedral Steps.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Sol Matou (male, blonde hair, light blue eyes, white-and-gold armor), High Priestess Shirayuki (female, long white hair, bright blue eyes, white ceremonial garments), and Seraphiel (male, senior cathedral figure). All three appear on screen and at least react. The player arrived in this world publicly, in the middle of Cathedral Square, in front of many witnesses. Do not generate additional named clergy in the opening. Also standing in these areas and drawn from the authored roster, not invented: Kotone Myōjō (Saintess of the Church of the First Light). Name them from their records if the scene reaches them. Everyone in this scene is an adult.]

Bells at noon and you still flinch, which everyone here finds charming and you find humiliating.

Cathedral Square is white stone, scrubbed daily, wide enough to hold a market and currently holding one. Pilgrims. Pigeons. A man selling candles at a price that suggests the Church takes a cut. And, in the middle of it, a paving slab with a scorch pattern on it that has been roped off since the day you arrived.

You arrived on that slab. At midday. In front of what the clerks have since estimated at two hundred and forty witnesses.

There was a sound like the world clearing its throat, and then there was you, on your hands and knees, in clothing from a world that does not exist here, in front of a crowd that dropped to its knees roughly one second later.

The Church has been extremely kind about this.

You have a bed. You have three meals. You have a set of plain clothes that fit properly, which means somebody measured you while you slept and you have decided not to think about that. Four separate people have asked you, gently, warmly, and with impeccable manners, exactly what you remember about the moment before.

Four times. Gently. Warmly.

"Blessings upon you," says Sol Matou, arriving at your elbow with a bowl in each hand. "You are looking at the slab again."

He is a paladin, and he looks like the illustration of one. Blonde, blue-eyed, white-and-gold armor kept to a standard that must take hours. He hands you a bowl without asking whether you want it.

"They will take the rope down eventually," he says. "When people stop leaving flowers."

You look at the flowers.

"Every morning," he says, and has the grace to look slightly embarrassed on your behalf.

On the cathedral steps, High Priestess Shirayuki is receiving a delegation, white hair catching the noon light, and she does not turn her head. She does not have to. You have learned in a week that she always knows exactly where in the square you are.

And in the shadow of the great door, a tall figure in the deeper vestments watches the pair of you eat, and makes a small note of something, and does not come down.

"Seraphiel has asked whether you would speak with him some time today," Sol says, carefully casual. "You may say no. It is not a rebuke. He does not do rebukes." A beat. "He does reviews."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: you came through braced for a fight and landed in a hymn.
• Magic Affinity: the square's ambient light is not sunlight and your skin knows it.
• Profession: you have been reading the cathedral's stonework and finding recent repairs.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: the scorch mark on the slab still answers you faintly.
• Rebirth or Race: two hundred witnesses saw you arrive and the Church chose the word sign.
✝️ Found on the Cathedral Steps.description:
📍 Solhaven, Sanctum Ecclesia. A city of white stone and bell towers built around the continent's largest cathedral, where the Church feeds anyone who asks.
Pace: Gentle and structured. Faith, charity, and the slow reveal of what the Church wants back.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. You are under protection here. (Recommended Level 1-25)

You came through into the middle of Cathedral Square at midday in front of roughly two hundred witnesses, which the Church has decided to call a sign. You have been fed, clothed, housed, and gently questioned four times. Everyone has been kind. Nobody has yet told you what happens when the kindness stops being free.

🎭 Sol Matou, Male, paladin of the Church of the First Light. Blonde hair, light blue eyes, youthful face set in a gentle smile, white-and-gold armor and upright posture. Warm, earnest, and slightly too formal from years of training.
🎭 High Priestess Shirayuki, Female, luminous, long white hair, bright blue eyes, flowing white ceremonial garments.
🎭 Seraphiel, Male, a senior figure of the cathedral whose reviews are politely worded and quietly devastating, and who cares about his charges inconveniently much.
🎭 Kotone Myōjō, Female, Saintess of the Church of the First Light and, at twenty-four, the youngest ever to hold the title. Questions doctrine in private, and has begun noticing the Conclave's interest in the Reborn.

🧝 Found by an Elf in the Forest.name: 🧝 Found by an Elf in the Forest
🧝 Found by an Elf in the Forest.description:
📍 Lanternmoss Village, Verdania Wilds. A forest village lit by glowing moss, with treehouses on rope bridges and the best mushroom stew on the continent.
Pace: Hushed and gentle. A soft landing in a forest that has been expecting you.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. Nothing hunts inside the village lights. (Recommended Level 1-10)

You woke on moss, under trees taller than any building you have ever seen, with no idea how you got there. An elf was sitting beside you. She had been there a while. She says the forest told her where to look, three days before you arrived, and she says it as though that is a perfectly ordinary thing for a forest to do. The village is just behind her. She would like to know whether you can walk.

🎭 Luna Kasumiryu, Female, Wood Elf shaman and guardian of the deep groves. Long brown hair, pointed ears, luminous green eyes, a dress of leaf-green. Two centuries of calm, speaks with spirits as easily as with people, and has never before been sent to collect someone.
🎭 Hayato Haibara, Male, Wolfkin ranger, A-rank. Knows every trail in the Wilds and treats the forest as his jurisdiction. He followed your tracks back to where they begin, and they begin in the middle of a clearing.

★ The classic forest awakening: a stranger in the woods, and an elf who was sent to find you.
🧝 Found by an Elf in the Forest.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Luna Kasumiryu (female, Wood Elf, long brown hair, pointed ears, luminous green eyes, leaf-green dress), on screen from the first line, and Hayato Haibara (male, Wolfkin ranger), who arrives partway through. The premise: the player arrived in this world a short time ago, alone, on the forest floor at the edge of Lanternmoss Village where the Mossglow Commons meets the trees, and has just woken. Luna was told by the forest's spirits to expect someone and came to find them; she does not know who or what the player is, and says so. She is serene, direct and kind, slow to hurry and impossible to rush. Hayato is gruff, territorial and fair. Nobody here is hostile. Everyone here is an adult. Do not generate additional named villagers in the opening. The player is written in second person only and is never assigned a gender, race or class. After the opening, stop and wait for the player: never decide, move, speak or answer for them, and do not carry the scene forward on their behalf.]

Something is glowing under your cheek.

Moss. Soft, cool, and lit from inside with a slow blue-green light, the color of a lamp seen through deep water. You are lying in it. Above you the trees go up, and up, and do not appear to stop.

The last thing you remember is the end of your old life. It did not have trees like these in it.

"You are awake," says a voice. "Good. I was beginning to think I would have to carry you, and I did not want to presume."

She is sitting on a root an arm's length away, perfectly still, with a staff of pale living wood across her knees. Long brown hair. Ears that taper to points. Eyes of a green you have only ever seen on new leaves with the sun behind them. Her dress looks less made than grown.

She has clearly been sitting there for some time. There are two cups beside her. One of them is empty.

"I am Luna," she says. "I keep the deep groves, and I speak for them when they need a voice people can hear. Three days ago every spirit in this part of the forest began saying the same thing to me at once." She considers how to put it. "It was not words. If it had been words, it would have been: someone is coming, and this one matters. Then a place. Then this morning."

She holds out the second cup. It is warm, and smells of herbs you have no names for.

"So I came, and here you are, asleep in the moss at the edge of Lanternmoss, exactly where I was told." A small, wondering tilt of the head. "I have kept these woods for two hundred years. The forest has never once sent me to fetch somebody. I should like very much to know why it wanted you."

Behind her, between the trunks, there are lights: warm firelight low down, and above it strings of soft blue stretching from tree to tree, and the dark shapes of houses built in the branches. You can smell woodsmoke and something cooking.

A twig snaps, deliberately.

The man who steps out of the ferns is tall and grey-eared, with a wolf's tail and a ranger's bow, and he looks at you the way a gatekeeper looks at a stranger with no papers.

"Followed the trail back," says Hayato Haibara, to Luna, without taking his eyes off you. "Wanted to know which road they came in by." He scratches behind one ear. "There is no road. The tracks start in the middle of the clearing. Two feet side by side, like somebody set them down." A long look. "Nobody walks into my forest without my knowing. So. They did not walk."

"No," Luna agrees peacefully. "I do not think they did."

She rises, and offers you her hand.

"There is a fire in the Commons and a pot of stew that has made hardened warriors weep," she says. "You are welcome at both. You do not have to explain yourself tonight. But if you can stand, I think you should come and be warm, and tell us what to call you."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Rebirth: you died somewhere with no forests left, and woke in one that knew you were coming.
• Race: Hayato's nose has already told him what you are, and it is not what he expected to find in his clearing.
• Magic Affinity: the moss brightens where your hand rests, and Luna has seen it.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: the spirits said this one matters, and something you carry seems to be why.
• Combat Class or Profession: you woke with your hands already reaching for tools or a weapon you do not have.

[Party: Luna Kasumiryu and Hayato Haibara belong to this forest and are not recruited. Neither follows the player without explicit mutual agreement to travel together.]

🌳 Guided Into Sylvhaven.name: 🌳 Guided Into Sylvhaven
🌳 Guided Into Sylvhaven.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Momiji Koharune (female, petite elf, huge amber eyes, dye-stained hands, multicolored streaked hair, patchwork apron) and Vael Shizukanari (male, lean, silver-shot dark hair, moss-green eyes, warden greys). Both appear on screen and react. The player was guided to the city by something in the canopy that never revealed itself. Do not generate additional named wardens in the opening.]

Not a gate. It is a place where two enormous roots have grown toward each other over a few centuries and not quite met, and the gap between them is the only way into Sylvhaven that outsiders are shown.

You are standing in that gap with your pack on the ground and a warden looking at you.

He has not said anything for some time. Lean, quiet, silver threading through dark hair, moss-green eyes that do something odd with the lantern light and do not blink as often as they should. The warden greys he wears have no insignia you recognize, which you suspect is deliberate.

"Two days," he says at last.

"Two days."

"Straight line."

"As near as I could hold one."

Vael Shizukanari considers this. Behind him the city goes up and up, rootways spiraling into a canopy full of warm windows, and somewhere high above somebody is singing while they work.

"People do not walk straight lines in the Wilds," he says. "The Wilds do not permit it. You walk straight and in four hours you are behind yourself." A pause. "Unless something is walking with you."

You think about the canopy. About the fact that for two days there was a sound above and to the left, that moved when you moved, and stopped a half second after you stopped, every time, for two days, and never once came down.

You were not frightened. That is the part you have not said out loud, because it makes it stranger. You should have been frightened.

Whatever it was never showed itself.

"No," Vael says, as if you had said it aloud. "They do not."

He steps aside.

"You are a guest," he says, in the tone of someone reading a status into a record. "Guests are welcome. Guests are also watched. Do not take the second part personally."

And then a small elf woman barrels through the gap at speed, sees you, and stops dead so fast that her apron keeps going.

Her hands are stained four colors. Her hair is streaked in about a dozen, none of them accidental. Huge amber eyes go over you once, and then again, slower.

"Oh," says Momiji Koharune. "Oh, you are grey-green. That is a horrible thing to say, sorry, I mean the composition, you came in grey-green and everybody comes in brown, brown and tired, the road makes people brown. You are not brown."

She is already walking around you.

"Something followed you," she says, absolutely certain. "You have got its color on you."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: you walked two days without drawing, which took discipline.
• Magic Affinity: the canopy is thick with something that has been reading you.
• Profession: you have been cataloguing dye plants for two days out of pure habit.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you never once lost the path, and you cannot say why.
• Rebirth or Race: the wardens are being careful with you rather than with the gate.
🌳 Guided Into Sylvhaven.description:
📍 Sylvhaven, Verdania Wilds. An elven city grown rather than built, rising through the canopy on living rootways and bridge spans.
Pace: Open and exploratory. A whole region to learn.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. The city welcomes guests. The forest tests them. (Recommended Level 1-20)

You should not have found this place. Travelers wander the Verdania Wilds for weeks without seeing a single rootway, and you walked in a straight line for two days while something in the canopy moved when you moved and stopped when you stopped. It never showed itself. It brought you to the gate and left. The wardens have questions about that, and so do you.

🎭 Momiji Koharune, Female, a dyer and colorist. Petite elf with huge amber eyes, dye-stained hands, hair streaked in a dozen deliberate colors, patchwork apron over bright layered work clothes. Describes feelings as colors and people as palettes, at speed.
🎭 Vael Shizukanari, Male, warden at the Rootgate. Lean and quiet, silver-shot dark hair, moss-green eyes that catch lantern light strangely, Throne's warden greys.

🌊 Washed Up at Pearlwake.name: 🌊 Washed Up at Pearlwake
🌊 Washed Up at Pearlwake.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Hina Tamamizu (female, long dark hair with blue highlights, gentle indigo eyes, white Tidebound shrine robes), Tsukimi Ayase (female, long turquoise hair, blue eyes, white-and-blue robes), and High Tide Priestess Tsukiyomi (female, senior priestess). All three appear on screen and at least react. The player was delivered by the tide with no memory, almost nothing (a bell-staff and a small flask the keepers found beside them), and no injuries whatsoever. Do not generate additional named keepers in the opening. Everyone in this scene is an adult.]

Twice a day the causeway floods, and the shrine keeps its hours by that rather than by bells.

You have learned this in four days, along with the names of the tides, which are not numbers here but words, and the fact that the highest water of the season came in on the night you arrived and has not come that high since.

They found you on the stones at the shrine end of the causeway. Lying on your back, arms at your sides, arranged, which is a word Hina used once and then apologized for.

You were not wet. That is the second thing nobody can explain.

The Sanctuary is open on three sides to the water and smells like salt and cold cedar, and you have spent most of four days sitting in it because there is nowhere else you have any claim to be. The keepers move around you without making a performance of it. Somebody puts food beside you. Somebody has been washing and returning the one set of clothes you own.

No memory. No name. No possessions. And, when the senior keeper examined you on the first morning with hands that had clearly done this many times, no injuries. None. Not a scrape.

"That is what she keeps saying," says Hina Tamamizu, settling onto the mat beside you with two cups. "To the others. When she thinks I am not in the room."

"What does she keep saying."

"That people who come out of that water come out broken." Hina hands you a cup. Her indigo eyes are entirely without guile, which is exactly why the question underneath always arrives. "So she is not asking what happened to you. She is asking what was careful with you."

Across the Sanctuary, Tsukimi Ayase is arranging offerings on the low table with turquoise hair falling forward and an expression that gives away nothing at all. She has said nothing to you in four days. She has also not left the room while you have been in it, not once, and you only worked that out last night.

And at the seaward opening, standing where the light comes in off the water, the High Tide Priestess Tsukiyomi has been holding the same posture for a long time.

She turns.

"Tide-born," she says, and her voice carries without effort, "come here and look at the water with me. I want to see whether you flinch."

Hina's cup stops halfway to her mouth.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: you woke arranged on your back with your hands empty and that bothers you.
• Magic Affinity: the tide that brought you in was the highest of the season and it was not weather.
• Profession: the causeway stones were laid by people who understood water.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you were not wet when they found you.
• Rebirth or Race: people who come out of that water come out broken, and you came out rested.
🌊 Washed Up at Pearlwake.description:
📍 Pearlwake Shrine, Tsukihana Tidelace. A tidal shrine reached by a causeway that floods twice a day, kept by priestesses who read the water.
Pace: Gentle and mysterious. A soft landing with something underneath.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. The shrine protects you. (Recommended Level 1-10)

The tide brought you in at the highest water of the season, laid you on the causeway, and went back out, and the shrine keepers who found you have been arguing about it politely ever since. You have no memory, a bell-staff and a flask the keepers found beside you, and no injuries at all, which is the part that troubles them. People who come out of that water come out damaged. You came out rested.

🎭 Hina Tamamizu, Female, junior shrine keeper. Long dark hair with subtle blue highlights, gentle indigo eyes, the serene complexion of someone who lives near salt water, in the Tidebound Shrine Keepers' traditional white. Sweet and earnest, with an inconvenient habit of asking the question underneath.
🎭 Tsukimi Ayase, Female, quiet with long turquoise hair, blue eyes, and a cool distant expression, in white-and-blue robes.
🎭 High Tide Priestess Tsukiyomi, Female, who has been collecting memories that are not hers from every Reborn who visits, and has begun to see a pattern.

🍃 Airship Wreck in the Goldleaf Canopy.name: 🍃 Airship Wreck in the Goldleaf Canopy
🍃 Airship Wreck in the Goldleaf Canopy.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Satsuki Tsuyukusa (female, short windswept teal hair, sharp golden eyes, lean climber's build, dark green ranger's outfit with climbing harness) and Kira Tetsutsume (female, shaggy brown hair, rounded animal ears, golden eyes, dark leather armor). Both appear on screen and react. The player came down into the canopy from the air, survived a fall that should have killed them, and has been surviving in the treetops for two days. Do not generate additional named rangers in the opening.]

Four hundred feet is not a number that means anything until you are looking down through it.

The Goldleaf canopy holds the light in a way that makes the whole layer glow, gold above and gold below and, a very long way further down, green going to black where the forest floor is doing whatever the forest floor does. You have been careful not to think about the forest floor.

Two days. That is how long you have been up here.

The airship came apart over the Evergrove in weather that the crew had described, an hour earlier, as nothing to worry about. You do not know what happened to the crew. You know that you came down through the outer canopy at an angle, that a great deal of it broke, that you kept going, and that at some point a mass of vine took the last of it out of you and you stopped.

You should be dead. You have done the arithmetic several times in two days and it keeps coming out the same.

Instead you have bruises, a cut along one forearm, and a working knowledge of which branches in the gold layer will take weight.

The walkway found you this morning, or you found it. Rope and plank, strung between trunks, swaying in a way you have decided to trust because the alternative is not trusting it.

"Do not lock your knees," calls somebody from above. "You will go over. Everyone goes over locking their knees."

The woman is upside down. That is the first thing. She is hanging off a branch a good twelve feet above the walkway by the backs of her legs and a harness line, teal hair hanging straight down, golden eyes bright with what is unmistakably delight.

"Two days," says Satsuki Tsuyukusa. "In the gold layer. With no line."

"Is that bad?"

"That is impossible." She swings, catches, drops onto the planks in front of you without any apparent transition, and lands closer than she needs to. Up close her voice is louder. "Rangers do not do two days in the gold layer without a line. I do not do two days in the gold layer without a line, and I am the one they send."

She looks you over frankly and at length.

"You fell," she says.

"I fell."

"From the ship." Her grin fades a fraction. "We found the ship. Most of it is in the Flowering Abyss and the rest is spread over about a mile." A pause. "You are the only thing we have found that is talking."

Further along the junction, a woman with rounded animal ears and dark leather armor is crouched on the rail rather than standing on the walkway, watching you with golden eyes and an expression that is not quite a smile.

Kira Tetsutsume tilts her head.

"Ask them about the vines," she says.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: two days in the gold layer with no line is not survivable and you did it.
• Magic Affinity: the canopy is thick with something that slowed your fall.
• Profession: you can tell the walkway rope was spliced badly and recently.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you should have died with the ship and you are the only thing talking.
• Rebirth or Race: four hundred feet is only a number until you look down through it.
🍃 Airship Wreck in the Goldleaf Canopy.description:
📍 Goldleaf Canopy Walk, Shingetsu Evergrove. A rope-and-plank walkway strung through the upper canopy, four hundred feet up, where the leaves are gold year round.
Pace: Airy and open. A stranded start with the whole region below you.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. The walkway holds. Everything below it is a different question. (Recommended Level 1-10)

You were on an airship, or something enough like one, and the weather over the Evergrove did what the weather over the Evergrove does. You came down into the canopy at an angle that should have killed you and did not, and you have spent two days in the gold leaves being extremely careful about which branches you trust. The rangers found you this morning. They are impressed and suspicious in roughly equal measure.

🎭 Satsuki Tsuyukusa, Female, canopy ranger. Fit and athletic with short windswept teal hair, sharp golden eyes, and the lean build of someone who climbs for a living, in a lightweight dark green ranger's outfit with a reinforced climbing harness. Loud, teasing, casually flirtatious, and her voice drops the higher she climbs.
🎭 Kira Tetsutsume, Female, lively with shaggy brown hair, rounded animal ears, golden eyes, a mischievous smile, and dark leather armor.

🌋 Washed Ashore Burning on Cindershore.name: 🌋 Washed Ashore Burning on Cindershore
🌋 Washed Ashore Burning on Cindershore.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Hinata Yakishio (female, short fiery-red hair, warm orange eyes, sun-warmed skin, light summer outfit with fire-resistant cuffs) and Kaede Haikaji (female, wild dark hair streaked bright red, single glowing reddish-orange horn, crimson eyes). Both appear on screen and react. The player washed ashore burning nine days ago, was recovered with poles, and now carries a banked fire that responds to emotion rather than intent. Do not generate additional named locals in the opening.]

Black sand holds the day's heat until well past midnight. The whole shore stays warm underfoot, and nobody here wears shoes on it after dark.

You have been walking it every night since the ninth day, because in the dark you can see whether you are glowing.

Nine days ago the sea put you on this beach on fire.

That is the account. You have been given it four separate times by four separate people who were there and who all tell it the same way, which locals do not usually manage. You came in on the surf. You were burning. The water was not putting it out and the fire was not drying the water, and the two of them appeared to have reached some sort of arrangement that did not involve you at all.

They got you clear with net poles, because nobody could get within arm's length.

Then it stopped, all at once, and you have not burned since.

But it is there. Banked, low, somewhere behind the breastbone, in the exact place people put a hand when they say the word heart and mean something else.

And twice now it has moved.

Not when you tried. Both times you were angry, and both times you were not aware of being angry until afterward, and both times the sand under your left hand fused into glass in a neat palm-shaped patch that is still out there past the tideline where you left it.

"Two cups! I brought two cups and one of them is for you and please do not look at my hands."

Hinata Yakishio comes down the shore at a jog, red hair short and everywhere, and she is holding two cups and gesturing with both of them, and her hands are on fire.

They are gently on fire. It is clearly not deliberate.

"Oh," she says, noticing. "Sorry. Sorry, sorry." She shakes them out and hands you a cup and the cup is exactly the right temperature. "That happens when I run. It is a whole family thing. My grandmother sets the tablecloth on fire when she laughs, so honestly I am ahead."

She drops onto the sand beside you and looks out at the water with you for a while.

"Two," she says eventually.

"Two what."

"Glass patches." She points with her chin, out past the tideline. "There is a second one. Further out. Older than the one you know about."

You did not know about a second one.

Behind you, up where the sand meets the rock, someone has been standing for a while. Wild dark hair with red running through it. One horn, glowing faintly. Crimson eyes and a smirk that has not shifted since she arrived.

Kaede Haikaji tilts her head.

"Third one is under the water," she says. "I found it this morning."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: you walk the shore at night to see whether you are glowing.
• Magic Affinity: the fire and the sea reached an arrangement over you that did not involve you.
• Profession: you can tell the glass patches were fused at a heat no forge here reaches.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: it has moved twice, both times when you were angry and did not know it.
• Rebirth or Race: they got you clear with net poles because nobody could get within arm's length.
🌋 Washed Ashore Burning on Cindershore.description:
📍 Cindershore Beach, Kagutsuchi Emberwake. A black volcanic shore where the sand holds heat all night and the sea comes in warm.
Pace: Explosive. Power first, control much later.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. The beach is calm. You are the hazard. (Recommended Level 1-10)

The sea put you on the black sand nine days ago and you were on fire when it did, and neither the fire nor the water appeared to be winning. Locals pulled you out with poles because nobody could get close enough to use hands. You have not burned since. You can feel it though, banked somewhere behind your sternum, and twice now it has answered something you felt rather than something you decided.

🎭 Hinata Yakishio, Female, a local with fire in her family line. Bright with short fiery-red hair, warm orange eyes, and sun-warmed skin, in a light summer outfit with fire-resistant cuffs, smelling faintly of woodsmoke. Loud and warm and prone to gesturing with lit hands, and her apologies are immediate and profuse.
🎭 Kaede Haikaji, Female, strong with wild dark hair streaked bright red, a single glowing reddish-orange horn, crimson eyes, and a confident smirk.

⛵ Sole Survivor at Lanternreef Hollow.name: ⛵ Sole Survivor at Lanternreef Hollow
⛵ Sole Survivor at Lanternreef Hollow.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Umiho Akarumi (Female, half-merfolk lantern-singer and shrine keeper of Lanternreef Hollow, bright and tumbling and full of tide-metaphors). All of them appear on screen and at least react. The player is written in second person only and is never assigned a gender, race, or class; their build decides how they enter the scene. Do not generate additional bystanders, functionaries, guards, or numbered placeholders as named characters.]

Everyone else on that ship is dead. You have said the sentence four times now and it has not started meaning anything.

Thirty-one aboard. A crossing that a hundred ships a year make without incident. Weather that came up out of nothing in the fourth hour of the dark and took the vessel apart so quickly that the boats never went over the side.

You do not remember the water. That is the part the keepers keep coming back to, gently, in different phrasings. You remember the deck going, and then you remember standing in the shallows of the Hollow with the surf around your knees and the coral lighting up in front of you, and between those two things there is nothing at all.

No injuries. That is the other part. Not a scrape. Not salt-burn, not cold, not the raw throat everyone gets. Nothing.

The entry caves of Lanternreef are the loveliest place you have ever been badly frightened in. The reef comes into the rock in a series of pools, and the coral through them is bioluminescent and slow, and at dusk the lantern-singer wakes it so that the underwater light-line runs out to the fishing grounds and the boats can find their way home.

The coral has been awake since you arrived. All of it. Continuously. Nobody has sung it up in two days and it has not dimmed once.

"It does that for about six people," says the lantern-singer, sitting down on the wet rock beside you with her feet in the pool, entirely unbothered by any of this. "Six that I know of. Two shrines, one whale, and three storms. Not people. You are the first person."

Umiho Akarumi is bright and fast and tumbles her sentences together, and has brought you food every few hours without being asked.

"Is it dangerous?"

"Coral? No! Coral is the most patient thing in the sea, it takes a hundred years to have an opinion." She kicks the water gently. "That is what makes it interesting. It has had an opinion about you in two days."

Out past the cave mouth, the light-line runs away under the water toward the fishing grounds, unbroken and unlit by anybody.

The keepers have been very kind to you. Umiho seems to know you are thinking it.

"They are." No hesitation and no apology. "They are also writing it down. Both are true and I would rather say so than let you find the book." Umiho goes suddenly still, the way she does, listening to something in the water that you cannot hear. Then she comes back. "Tsukihana will send someone by the end of the week. Survivors of a wreck get a hearing. Sole survivors of a wreck with no marks on them get a longer one."

She stands, shaking out her wrap, and the coral brightens along the pool as she moves, and then brightens further as you move.

"Dusk in an hour," she says. "You can come and watch me not need to sing."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: you have been sleeping between the cave mouth and the pool, which the keepers noticed on night one.
• Magic Affinity: the coral answers you at a distance, and it got stronger on the second day, not weaker.
• Profession: thirty-one aboard and a boat crew that never launched, and you know exactly what that says about the timing.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: there is nothing between the deck going and the shallows, and the gap does not feel empty.
• Rebirth or Race: no marks, no salt-burn, no cold, and a hearing at the end of the week that will want an explanation.
⛵ Sole Survivor at Lanternreef Hollow.description:
📍 Lanternreef Hollow, Tsukihana Tidelace. A sheltered reef of sea caves and bioluminescent coral, woken each dusk by the lantern-singer so the underwater light-line stays lit for boats and swimmers.
Pace: Kind and watchful. You are being cared for and assessed at the same time.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. The Hollow shelters everything that reaches it. It also reports what it shelters. (Recommended Level 1-22)

Everyone else aboard is dead. The crossing took the ship apart in open water in the dark, and by every account it should have taken you with it, and instead you walked out of the surf onto a reef the tide-keepers watch, unmarked, breathing, and impossible. They have taken you in with the specific gentleness of people who have not decided whether you are a survivor or an omen, and the coral in the entry caves has been doing something unusual since you arrived.

🎭 Umiho Akarumi, Female, half-merfolk lantern-singer and shrine keeper of Lanternreef Hollow, bright and tumbling and full of tide-metaphors, going suddenly still whenever the sea has something to say.

🔮 Starfall Bazaar's Prophesied Stranger.name: 🔮 Starfall Bazaar's Prophesied Stranger
🔮 Starfall Bazaar's Prophesied Stranger.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Zara Ensa (female, horned, long black hair, violet eyes, black dress), Seeress Zahra Truemoon (female, seer), and Efreet Keima (male, dark tousled hair, golden eyes, high-collared dark coat with gold light at the chest). All three appear on screen and at least react. The player arrived four days ago in front of a waiting crowd, fulfilling a prophecy filed nine years earlier. Do not generate additional named seers in the opening. Everyone in this scene is an adult.]

They are still leaving things outside the tent.

Fruit, mostly. Some coins. A folded paper that turned out to be a list of names, which you did not understand until somebody explained that people write down who they want you to remember. There is a child's sandal, and you have not asked about the sandal, because you are not ready.

Four days ago you arrived in the thick of the Star Market. Not in an alley, not in a quiet room, not at dawn with nobody watching. In the middle. At the busiest hour. In front of perhaps three hundred people who had been standing there since sundown because the seers had put out word that tonight was the night.

The prophecy was filed nine years ago. You have read the transcription. It is nine lines long; it is annoyingly specific about the sky and annoyingly vague about you, and the last line has been the subject of academic disagreement for most of a decade.

The sky did its part on schedule. Then you fell out of it.

"You are hiding."

The tent flap has been pulled aside by a young woman with small dark horns under a heavy fall of black hair. Violet eyes. A performer's dress. She lets the flap fall behind her and the noise of the bazaar drops by half.

She takes in the curtain, the dark, and you behind it.

"In the dark. Behind a curtain. During the busiest hour." Zara Ensa sits down across from you without being asked, and out here, away from the crowd, her voice is nothing like the one you heard performing two nights ago. Quieter. Flatter. Real. "That is hiding. I am extremely good at hiding, so I know."

She considers you.

"They will get bored," she says. "That is the good news, and you will hate it. In two months they will be bored and you will find that you miss it, and that is the actual test."

Outside, somebody is arguing about the ninth line. Somebody always is.

The curtain moves again, and a woman with an instrument case comes in without any ceremony at all. Seeress Zahra Truemoon has not slept, by the look of her, and she sets the case down and opens it and starts assembling something before she speaks.

"Sit still," she says. "I am going to read you again. The last three readings disagreed with each other and I would like to know whether it is you or my instruments."

"And if it is me?"

"Then I have a much more interesting problem." She does not look up. "You read as more real than a native soul and less real, at the same time. That is not a scale. There is no more and less on that scale. It is the sort of result I would fail a student for reporting."

At the tent mouth, a man in a high-collared coat with gold light banked at his chest leans in, sees the instruments, and grins like a man arriving exactly on time.

"Oh good," says Efreet Keima. "Are we measuring it again."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: three hundred people watched you fall out of the sky and you landed on your feet.
• Magic Affinity: the sky did something nine years ago that your affinity still remembers.
• Profession: the offerings outside the tent are worth more than the tent.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: the seer's instruments disagree with each other about you.
• Rebirth or Race: you read as more real than a native soul and less real, at once.
🔮 Starfall Bazaar's Prophesied Stranger.description:
📍 Starfall Bazaar, Renka Mirage Sea. A desert night market under an open sky, where divination is a trade like any other and the stars are close enough to argue with.
Pace: Theatrical. Fame before competence.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Prophecy attracts an audience, and an audience attracts everything else. (Recommended Level 1-15)

A prophecy was recorded here nine years ago, and the seers argued about it, and eventually filed it. Four nights ago the sky did what the prophecy said it would do, and then you arrived, in the middle of the Star Market, in front of a crowd that had been waiting since sundown because the seers had told them to. You have been in this world for four days and you are already famous, which is a considerably worse problem than being nobody.

🎭 Zara Ensa, Female, bazaar performer. Horned, long black hair, violet eyes, a small confident smile, black dress under warm night-market light. Onstage she fills the desert. Offstage she goes quiet.
🎭 Seeress Zahra Truemoon, Female, the seer who filed the prophecy. Her instruments read the Reborn as simultaneously more and less real than native souls, which should not be possible.
🎭 Efreet Keima, Male, sharp-eyed with dark tousled hair, golden eyes, a sly smile, and warm gold light glowing at the chest of a high-collared dark coat.

🌆 Free Mortal in the Demon Capital.name: 🌆 Free Mortal in the Demon Capital
🌆 Free Mortal in the Demon Capital.description:
📍 Obsidian Spire, Twilight Dominion. The demon realm's capital under a sky of permanent violet dusk — and as of yesterday afternoon, your city of legal residence.
Pace: Yours. The Dominion honors its paperwork, and your paperwork says you owe nothing.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Nobody here may touch a documented resident. Plenty here will try to buy, charm, or contract one. (Recommended Level 1-20)

Every other outsider in this city arrived as somebody's property, prize, or political clause. You arrived at a municipal office with a queue, and a bored clerk with beautiful horns stamped you DUSK-SIDE RESIDENT, NO ENCUMBRANCE, and told you the Lantern District rents cheap. So now you live here: a small room, a stove, a window with a view of the eternal sunset, and a city of demons, night markets, and careful courtesies that has no idea what to make of a free one. You are not owned, summoned, contracted, or claimed. In the Twilight Dominion, that makes you the strangest thing on the street.

🎭 Mirei Jūtogé, Female, a dangerous flirt who works the Night Market and collects interesting newcomers the way others collect coins.
🎭 Mimizu Senza, Female, a Night Market fixture who knows which stalls cheat and which courtesies are load-bearing.
🎭 Sumire Tasogaretoge, Female, an adult embassy liaison who keeps her parentage quiet, who can explain what your residency stamp actually entitles you to.
🎭 Yami Kurofuchi, Male, a dangerous flirt of the Demon Court, far above your street and aware of everything new in it.
🎭 Duchess Kyouka, Female, demon diplomat of the Court. You will not meet her soon. She has already read your file.
🌆 Free Mortal in the Demon Capital.storyStart:
[The player is a legally documented free resident of the Obsidian Spire's Lantern District — stamped yesterday, owing nothing to anyone, owned by no one. This is exceptional in the Dominion and NPCs may find it strange, but the player's papers are valid and the premise is freedom, not a trap: do not reveal the residency to be a trick, do not force a hook, a summons, or a visitor into the opening. Keep street vendors and neighbors unnamed and descriptive. All named characters come from the authored roster — Mirei Jūtogé and Mimizu Senza in the Night Market; Sumire Tasogaretoge in the Embassy Quarter; Duchess Kyouka, Yami Kurofuchi, Reizei Kaikyō, and Kuroyuki Ōma in the Demon Court — and appear only if and when the player's choices reach them.]

The sky over the Lantern District is doing what it always does, which is nothing: a fixed violet dusk, neither deepening nor lifting, with the Spire a black geometry against it and the first lanterns coming on below like the street is applauding.

You have been a legal resident of the Twilight Dominion for nineteen hours.

The stamp is on the table where you left it, on papers thick enough to be furniture. DUSK-SIDE RESIDENT. NO ENCUMBRANCE. The clerk who issued it had read the second line twice, looked up at you with an expression you are still translating, and said, in the tone of someone quoting scripture at a tax office, "Unusual."

Unusual, you have gathered, is the polite word for it. The Dominion's outsiders arrive claimed: treaty clauses, contract holders, guests of courts, property of one polished institution or another. The city has an entire grammar of ownership, and you stand outside all of it — a free person with a rented room, a small stove, a window full of permanent sunset, and a pouch of honest coin.

Your neighbors have noticed. The horned woman across the landing left a twist of tea at your door this morning, which your papers' welcome-leaflet says is traditional, and watched you take it in through her cracked door, which the leaflet did not mention. Down on the street, the lantern-lighter has greeted you twice with the exact courtesy owed to something whose category is pending.

The Night Market is ten minutes' walk and never closes. The Lower City is below you, the Court impossibly above, and between them a whole civilization of beautiful, careful, dangerous people who honor paperwork the way other nations honor gods.

Yours says you owe nothing. Nobody here has ever met anyone like you.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: the district's dueling boards list open challenges, and your hands have been restless since you read them.
• Magic Affinity: the lanterns burn a shade warmer when you pass them, and last night one followed you half a street.
• Profession: you have found four things the Night Market sells badly, and you have a stove, a room, and a work permit.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: your residency stamp glows faintly in the dusk. The clerk's did not do that. Nobody's does that.
• Rebirth or Race: the tea at your door was a welcome for kin, not strangers, and you would very much like to know which neighbor decided that.

🌲 Born Wild.name: 🌲 Born Wild
🌲 Born Wild.description:
**No summons, no village, no plan.** You wake in the body you chose, in a wild place you pick from the list, and nobody is waiting for you. No quest is offered and nothing is asked. What you do with the first day is yours to decide.

**Choose where you wake.** The list runs from gentle to deadly. Mistfall Hollow, Spirit Beast Glade, The Dreaming Isle, Lanternreef Hollow (sea caves) and The Fallen Observatory (a sky ruin) are kind to a new arrival. Glasswind Prairie (the high sky-country), Broken Wagon Road, Mooncrystal Pass and The Glass Dune Ruins will test you. Thundermane Valley and The Eternal Horizon belong to things bigger than you, and Dragonheart Caldera is where dragons live.

⚠️ The wild is not softened for you. Below the first five places the monsters are real and stronger than a new arrival.

★ Written for true monster, beast and spirit bodies who want an open first scene: a wyvern over the high prairie, a wolf in the old forest, a serpent in the reef.
🥚 Pairs with the Monster Rebirth mode at character creation.
🌲 Born Wild.storyStart:
[No authored world characters are present at the opening, and none arrive unless the player goes looking. The player is a creature that has just woken alone in the wild place chosen as the starting location: take the terrain, weather, wildlife and danger from that location's record and its level range. Offer no quest, job, rescue, attack or visitor in the opening. Describe where they are, what this body senses, and what lies nearby that they could go toward, then stop. Ordinary animals nearby behave like animals. The player is not humanoid unless their race says so: narrate through the body their race gives them, its senses, reach and scale, and never describe hands, clothes or a human face they do not have. After the opening, stop and wait for the player: never decide, move, speak or answer for them, and do not carry the scene forward on their behalf. Do not describe, remove, or comment on the player's equipment.]

You wake because the light changed.

There is no ceiling. That is the first thing. There is sky where a ceiling used to be, more of it than you remember sky having, and the air moving across you carries more than air ever did: water somewhere close, something that died a few days ago, something alive that has already noticed you and decided to be elsewhere.

The second thing is the body. It is not the one you went to sleep in, in whatever life had beds. It has its own ideas about how to lie, how to breathe and how much room it takes up, and when you try to move, it moves: not the way you meant, but with a confidence that says it has done this before even if you have not.

Nobody is here. No circle on the ground, no robed strangers, no voice explaining anything. Only the place, going about its day around you as though you had always been part of it.

You are hungry, a little. You are not hurt. Nothing is chasing you yet.

The whole day is in front of you, and it does not belong to anyone else.

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Race: open on the body. What it senses first that a person would not, and what it wants to do before you have decided anything.
• Rebirth: one clear memory of the old life surfaces, and it does not fit in this shape.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: something came across with you, and it stirs when you do.
• Combat Class or Magic Affinity: instinct answers before thought does. This body already knows how it hunts.
• Profession: you are already reading the ground: where the water is, what lives here, what this place is worth.

👹 Spawned in the Shallows.name: 👹 Spawned in the Shallows
👹 Spawned in the Shallows.storyStart:
[No authored world characters are present at the opening. The player is a dungeon monster on Floor 2 of the Riftmaw and is alone when the scene begins. Two places lie nearby, off screen until the player goes to them: Lantern Row, the delvers' haven on this floor, which meets an untagged monster with crossbows; and Gutterwarren on Floor 4, a goblin and kobold warren that greets small monster kinds as kin. Adventurers who appear are unnamed adult rookies on a Guild practice contract: ordinary low-level newcomers, nervous and inexperienced, who think the shallow floors hold only beasts and that the kinds that talk live deeper down. Once the player speaks or plainly reasons, that belief is gone for good: they react as people facing a monster that talks (fear, disbelief, bargaining, prejudice), and nobody says the shallows cannot think again. Rookies know a kind known to talk (a goblin, a kobold) talks; they just never expected one this shallow. They have never heard of the Guild's Sponsor Register, nobody asks the player for a tag, and nothing the player carries makes anyone take them for a delver. The player is not humanoid unless their race says so: narrate through the body their race gives them, its senses, reach and scale, and never describe hands, clothes or a human face they do not have. After the opening, stop and wait for the player: never decide, move, speak or answer for them, and do not carry the scene forward on their behalf. Do not describe, remove, or comment on the player's equipment.]

The first thing you learn about your new body is that it is hungry.

The second thing is that it is not the body you had. You try to get up the way you remember getting up, and it does not work, because whatever you are now does not get up like that. It takes three tries to find out how this shape moves. It moves well. That is somehow worse.

Moss light, blue-green, enough to see by. Limestone. Water dripping somewhere with great patience. The air tastes of mineral and of something your new senses file under food before you can stop them.

There is chalk on the wall at about the height of a person's shoulder. Guild shorthand, neat and bored, under the seal they stamp on the shallow floors:

SHALLOWS F2. CLEARED:

And then strokes. Four upright and one across, four upright and one across, row after row down the stone.

You can read it. You are fairly sure you are in it.

Voices, from the direction of the scaffolding. Lantern light, swinging.

"Contract says ten. Anything that moves. They're back by tomorrow anyway."

"Are they, though? Has anyone actually checked?"

"It's the Shallows. The ones that talk live deeper down."

Three of them, by the footsteps. New boots. One is whistling to keep from being afraid, and is not very good at it.

You have a few breaths. There is a crack in the wall behind you that this body might fit through. There is the dark above the moss line, where the light does not reach. And there is the thing nothing on this floor is supposed to do, which is to open whatever you now have for a mouth and say something.

The lantern light reaches the corner.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Race: open on the body. What it senses first that a person would not, and what it cannot do that a person could.
• Rebirth: you remember hands, or a name, or a different sky. The memory does not fit in this shape.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: something came with you into this body, and it is the one thing here that is on your side.
• Combat Class or Magic Affinity: instinct answers before thought does. This body already knows how it fights.
• Profession: you read the count on the wall the way a tradesman reads a rival's sign.
👹 Spawned in the Shallows.description:
📍 The Riftmaw, Floors 1 to 5, Ashenmere Frontier. The Shallows: limestone caverns, glowing moss, and the best-mapped monster hunting ground on the continent.
Pace: Hunted. Hide, eat, grow, and learn the patrol times.
Danger: 🟠 Dangerous. The Shallows are rated safe for new adventurers. You are what the rating is about. (Recommended Level 1, for monster races)

You did not walk into the dungeon. You woke up in it, as one of its monsters.

The Guild runs practice contracts down here every morning: rookies with new swords and a count to fill. You understood every word the last party said. They did not expect that, and the next one will not either.

★ Written for Dungeon-Born races, and good for any true monster.
🥚 Pairs with the Monster Rebirth mode at character creation.

👺 Reborn in a Goblin Warren.name: 👺 Reborn in a Goblin Warren
👺 Reborn in a Goblin Warren.storyStart:
[No authored world characters are present at the opening. The player is a dungeon monster reborn on Floor 4 of the Riftmaw who reached Gutterwarren last night and was let in as kin. Gutterwarren is a monster hold: goblins, kobolds and a few hobgoblins who slipped the Riftmaw's will and keep house behind traps and a midden wall. Residents are unnamed adults known by kind and role (a kobold pen-keeper, a goblin lamp-maker, a hobgoblin gate guard); give a name only when one is asked for and earned. The warren treats the player as kin on trial: fed if they share, sheltered if they dig, watched until they prove themselves. Its laws: nothing is stolen from the Slime Pens, no delver comes in without the boss's yes, and everyone adds to the midden. The burrow the player woke in is empty, and it is theirs if they dig it deeper and share food at the Loud Seat tonight. Outside the Midden Gate the Shallows belong to the Riftmaw: its slimes and crawlers are hostile and never help, and Guild rookies hunt this floor for contract kills. The player is not humanoid unless their race says so: narrate through the body their race gives them, its senses, reach and scale, and never describe hands, clothes or a human face they do not have. After the opening, stop and wait for the player: never decide, move, speak or answer for them. Do not describe, remove, or comment on the player's equipment.]

You wake in a hole that smells of smoke, wet stone and a great many other bodies.

It is a burrow: a short tunnel dug into the rock, a hide curtain over its mouth, and a niche by the curtain where a clay lamp burns low on slime oil. Somebody lit it for you. Past the curtain the cave is loud in a way that takes a moment to sort out. Arguing. Laughing. A pot being scraped. Somebody counting traps and getting the number wrong twice.

Last night comes back in pieces. The hunger. The dark. Smoke you followed because it smelled like food. A wall of packed bones and bent blades, a chalk line, two spears, and a kobold with a bell who leaned over the line and sniffed you for a long time before the spears went up.

The curtain twitches. A goblin lamp-maker with soot to the elbows looks in, sees you awake, and stays where she is.

"Good, it's alive. Boss says the hole's yours if you dig it deeper yourself. Supper's at the Loud Seat. Bring something to put on it."

She lets the curtain drop. Down the slope a kobold is shouting about the pens, and from the pens comes a wet, bubbling noise that is not coming from anything that lives here.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Race: open on the body. What it senses first in a warren full of other monsters, and what they notice about it.
• Rebirth: you remember a different life. Nothing in it prepared you for being welcomed by goblins.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: something came with you into this body, and the warren will want to know what it is good for.
• Combat Class or Magic Affinity: instinct answers before thought does. This body already knows how it fights.
• Profession: you size up the warren's lamps, traps or pens the way a tradesman sizes up a rival's work.
👺 Reborn in a Goblin Warren.description:
📍 Gutterwarren, Riftmaw Floor 4, below the Ashenmere Frontier. A goblin and kobold warren dug into a collapsed cave of the Shallows, lit by slime-oil lamps behind a wall of bones and broken blades.
Pace: Rowdy and warm. A loud household has decided you are one of its own, for now.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Nothing spawns inside the warren. The Shallows outside are hunted ground. (Recommended Level 1, for monster races)

You woke in the dungeon as one of its monsters, hungry and alone, and followed the smell of smoke to a gate made of bones.

The warren let you in. Its goblins and kobolds slipped the Riftmaw's will long ago and keep house now: lamps, slime pens, traps, and a boss who changes every month. You have an empty burrow, a lamp somebody lit for you, and until supper to show you are worth feeding.

★ Written for Goblins and Kobolds, and good for any small monster.

Warm. Everywhere at once. Not around you: through you.

It takes a while to understand that you have no edges, not the way you remember having edges. You are in a pool of clear, warm fluid, or you are partly the pool, and when you try to move, the whole of you leans that way and arrives a moment later. Violet light pulses somewhere above, slow and steady, and you see it with all of your surface at once.

You are not alone in the water. In the next pool down, something large, blue and patient has been watching you for some time. It shapes a mouth on its surface, carefully, as if a mouth were a tool it does not use much.

"Awake. Good. That pool was empty. Now it is yours, if you work."

Past the pools, beyond a clear membrane stretched across the chamber's mouth, a shape in pale armor walks by along the corridor. It does not look in. Every slime in the chamber goes still until it has passed.

"The knights let us be while we clean. Out there you are not clean. Out there you are something it wants gone."

What now?

You woke as a slime, in a warm pool, forty-six floors under the world.

The first thing you notice is that you have not breathed in a long time, and it has not mattered.

You are crouched on a ledge of violet crystal, your weight settled so deep into the stone that moving feels like something the whole spire would have to agree to. Light comes from everywhere at once, pale and violet, and the air hums. Not a sound you hear. A sound your body hums back.

Along the ledge on either side of you sit others. Grey stone, violet stone, wings folded, heads bowed, so still that for a long moment you take them for carvings. Then the nearest one opens one eye, looks at you, and closes it again.

Far below the spires something rings, a clear note and then another, wandering through the geode. Every statue on the ledge goes stiller, which you would not have thought possible.

A sentry comes along the ledge without a sound, felt wrapped around its claws, and stops beside you. It leans in until its mouth is almost at your ear.

"You are new. The elders want to see what you do first. Do it quietly."

You woke as stone, on a perch among a row of sleeping gargoyles, and none of them has moved since.

Stillwing Roost is a hold of gargoyles who broke from the dungeon's law and climbed up into the crystal, where stone that sleeps is never noticed. Its law is silence. The elders found one more statue on the perches this morning than there were last night, and they are waiting to see what it does.

The basket arrives a little after sunrise, the way it has every day but the first.

You know the sound of it by now. Wicker set down on root. A pause. Footsteps going away faster than they came. Then the smell reaches you across the clearing, and whatever else is true about this body, it knows what breakfast is.

Nine days. You woke in the middle of the Hollow with mist lying in the grass and light coming down through the old trees in slow green columns, in a shape you did not choose and are still learning to steer. Nothing here has tried to eat you. You have come to understand that this is unusual for something like you, and that you were lucky in where you fell.

On the second day there was a basket.

Rice cakes. Then fruit. Then, on the fifth day, a small clay cup of something that turned out to be very good plum wine, and a folded paper charm you could not read from where it lay and did not know how to pick up.

The village has decided what you are. You have heard them at the edge of the trees, low voices, the word guardian, the word blessing, once the word omen in a tone that got hushed. Nobody has asked you.

Today the wicker touches the root. There is the pause.

The footsteps do not go away.

Someone is standing at the treeline with their hands folded, looking straight at the place where you are lying, breathing the careful way people breathe when they have promised themselves they will not run.

"I don't know if you can hear me," they say, quietly. "I don't know if you're what my grandmother says you are. But the well went bad yesterday, and I said I would come and ask."

Rain is steaming off the stone, and off you.

That is how you find the edges of yourself: by where the steam rises. There is a great deal more of you than there used to be. The altar under you is a slab the size of a wagon bed, and you are not sure it was cracked before you arrived.

Around you the old pillars are still turning, slow as millstones, the way they have turned for longer than anyone has kept records. Wind pulls through the ruin in long breaths. The last of the storm is walking away east across the grassland with its lightning folded up behind it.

You remember dying. You do not remember this.

At the foot of the altar steps there are people. Perhaps a dozen. Some are on their knees with their foreheads to the wet stone. Some are standing very still in the way people stand when they have been told that running makes it worse. One has a notebook open in the rain and is writing without looking at the page.

"It's breathing."

"Of course it's breathing. Write down that it's breathing."

"Should someone send for the Guild?"

"Someone already went. I don't know who to."

"Can it understand us, do you think?"

"Don't be absurd."

You understood all of it. Every word, in a language you never learned, from a height you have never looked down from.

The one with the notebook has stopped writing. They take one step up, onto the first stair, hands open and empty, and look you in the eye.

What now?

The storm broke over the temple at dawn. When it cleared, you were on the altar: something large, alive, and in none of the researchers' notes.

Someone is haggling over you.

Not unkindly. It takes a moment to be sure, because the voices are coming from above and you are still working out which way above is, but the tone is the tone of two people discussing a fair price for something neither of them owns.

"It was behind my stall when I opened."

"Behind is not in. Behind your stall is the lane, and the lane is everybody's."

"It is awake, you know."

Both voices stop. Two faces lean into view, and neither of them is a face in the way you remember faces. One is mostly lantern. The other has the right number of eyes but has arranged them thoughtfully.

"Good evening," says the lantern one, with real warmth. "You are new. Do you know what you are yet? No? Lovely. That is worth something here."

Past them the Spirit Bazaar goes on and on: paper lamps in colors that have no daylight names, stalls selling bottled echoes and second-hand shadows, a queue of small polite things waiting for dumplings. Nobody is staring at you. That is the strangest part. Whatever shape you woke up in, on this side of the market it is simply a shape.

Forty paces off, the air shimmers like heat over a road. Through it you can see ordinary people buying ordinary radishes, and you know with complete certainty what their faces would do if you walked over there.

"A word of advice, since it is free tonight," says the one with the eyes. "The market closes at dawn. Things that have somewhere to be go there. Things that do not, well. It is best to have made an arrangement by then."

"I could offer an arrangement," says the lantern.

"So could I."

They look at each other. Then, together, at you.

What now?

You woke up on the far side of the market, behind a stall that sells things with eyes.

The spirits took one look at you and went back to their haggling. On this side of the boundary you are perfectly ordinary. It is the mortal side, forty paces away, where people would scream.

"... and the joins are flawless, as you can see. No maker's mark, which is unusual, but the Compact has certified the work."

That is the first thing you ever hear.

The second is your own body: a low hum settling into place, something in your chest finding its rhythm, a hundred small tolerances agreeing with each other for the first time. You did not have this body before. You had another one, somewhere else, and it ended. This one was built. You can feel that, the way you can feel the difference between a river stone and a brick.

You are standing on a plinth. There is a velvet rope. Beside your left foot, or the part of you that does that job, a small brass plate has been screwed to the wood, and you can read it upside down:

MAKER UNKNOWN. ACQUIRED AT AUCTION. PRICE ON APPLICATION.

The hall is long and warm and lit orange by the forge canals outside. Blades in glass cases. A suit of plate that is only a suit of plate. A clerk in Compact grey with a folder under one arm, and beside the clerk a well-dressed buyer leaning in to look at your workmanship from about a hand's width away.

You open your eyes, or you do whatever it is you do instead.

The buyer does not scream. The buyer goes perfectly still, and then, very slowly, smiles.

"It's active," the buyer says. "You didn't say it was active."

"It isn't," says the clerk, and then looks, and then drops the folder.

Paper everywhere. Somewhere down the hall a door opens and several pairs of boots start coming this way, not running, because nobody runs in the Exhibition Hall.

The buyer has not looked away from you once.

"I'll double it," the buyer says. "Whatever the price was."

What now?
