You were on a plinth, with a brass plate and a velvet rope, and a buyer was reading your price.

Then you opened your eyes, or whatever you have, and the Hall went very quiet. The Compact has rules for flawed work, stolen work and unfinished work. It has nothing for work that wakes up.

There is chalk dust in your nose.

This is a new problem, because the nose is new, and it is much better than your old one, and it is currently informing you about forty people, a great deal of ink, somebody's lunch, and a burned smell that you gradually understand is the circle you are sitting in.

You look down. The floor is very close. So are your feet, of which there are an unexpected number, and of an unexpected kind.

A lecture hall rises around you in curved tiers. Every seat is full. Every face in every seat is looking at you with the particular silence of a class that has just watched something go wrong for somebody else.

At the edge of the circle a student is holding a sheet of parchment in both hands. The parchment has a seal at the bottom and a blank line above it. The student has the expression of a person who followed every instruction exactly.

"That," says a dry voice from the lectern, "is not a bound spirit of the third order."

"No, Professor."

"Would you care to tell the class what it is?"

"I don't know, Professor."

You could tell them. You are not sure of the word for it yet, but you know what you are not, which is anybody's standard issue anything. You died somewhere with different stars, and you were promised a second chance, and it turns out the second chance is this size.

You say something. You do not plan to. It simply comes out, in a perfectly clear voice, in a language you have never spoken.

Forty people inhale at once.

The professor sets down a piece of chalk with great care. "Well," the professor says. "That is not on the syllabus." Then, to the student, more gently: "The contract requires its consent. I suggest you ask."

The student kneels at the edge of the circle, parchment shaking slightly, and meets your eyes.

What now?

The circle was drawn for a bound familiar spirit: obedient, wordless, standard issue. It delivered you.

🥂 Reincarnated as the Villainess.name: 🥂 Reincarnated as the Villainess
🥂 Reincarnated as the Villainess.description:
📍 Roseglass Ballroom, Crownveil Sovereignty. The capital's social season under a ceiling of rose-tinted glass, where every major house attends and every rival watches.
Pace: Glittering and precarious. You know how this story ends, and you would like a different ending.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. Nobody here draws steel without a formal challenge. The trouble is how easily one is issued. (Recommended Level 24-38)

You know this ballroom. You read about it, in a novel, in another life. You know the white hair of the duelist in front of you, and the line the villainess says to her in chapter three: the insult that starts the duel that starts the fall. By the last chapter the villainess has lost her name, her house and her place in the capital. You know all of this because, as of about nine seconds ago, the villainess is you. (Or the villainous heir, if that is the body you woke in. The story is not particular.)

🎭 Kanade Baragiri, Female, High Elf duelist of House Roseveil. Long white hair in a high ponytail, pointed ears, violet eyes, white armor with rose accents. Three bracket titles, a dueling style named after her, and no patience for insults. In the book, she is the one who ends you.
🎭 Chitose Yuzuriha, Female, nineteen, the unofficial queen of Aureliath's social season. Runs it with a fan and a guest list, and misses nothing that happens on her floor.

★ The villainess start, played straight: the doom flags are real, you remember where they are, and tonight is the first one.
🥂 Reincarnated as the Villainess.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Kanade Baragiri (female, High Elf, long white hair in a high ponytail, violet eyes, white armor with rose accents), on screen from the first line, and Chitose Yuzuriha (female, the season's unofficial queen), who watches from the edge of the floor. The premise: the player has just woken in the body of a noble this ballroom knows as proud, cruel and dangerous to cross, and remembers this world as a novel read in a former life. The glass in your hand is full, the music has stopped, and two hundred people are waiting for you to be terrible.

You know this the way you know the next line of a song. A moment ago you were somewhere else entirely, at the end of a different life. Now there is rose-colored light coming down through a glass ceiling, silk on your shoulders that cost more than a house, and a ballroom holding its breath around you in a ring.

You have read this scene.

Chapter three. The season's opening ball. The villainess, bored and vicious, stops the dancing to say something unforgivable to the duelist of House Roseveil in front of everyone who matters. The duelist answers with a formal challenge. The villainess laughs. Eleven chapters later she loses that duel, then her engagement, then her name, and the last time the book mentions her she is in a carriage, leaving the capital for good.

You remember thinking she had it coming.

The duelist is standing four feet away.

Kanade Baragiri is taller than the page made her. White hair in a high tail, violet eyes, white armor chased with roses, one hand resting on the hilt of a rapier with the ease of someone who has never drawn it and lost. Her chin is up. She has plainly been waiting for this all evening, and has plainly decided to take whatever comes without giving you the satisfaction of a flinch.

"Well?" says Kanade. Quiet. It carries anyway. "You stopped the music. I assume you had a reason, and I assume it concerns me, since you have been looking at me as though I tracked something in."

Someone in the ring laughs and is shushed.

At the edge of the floor a slim figure with a fan has gone perfectly still: Chitose Yuzuriha, who runs this season and decides who is invited to the next one. Her fan is closed. Her eyes are on you, bright with the particular attention of someone who expects to be telling this story tomorrow.

The line is right there. You can feel the shape of it in a mouth that has said worse. The body you are wearing knows exactly how to hold the glass, how to tilt the head, how long to let the silence run before the knife goes in. This is what everyone in this room believes you are.

Kanade's fingers tighten on the hilt, very slightly. Not fear. Readiness. In the book, this is the moment she stops thinking of you as a rival and starts thinking of you as a debt.

The silence is yours. So is the next line, and for the first time in this story nobody has written it.

"I want it understood," says the First Princess of the Crownveil Sovereignty, "that I am not angry with you."

She says it with her back to you, at the window, in the voice of someone who is extremely angry.

The room is a small gallery off the throne hall, all white marble and morning light, and it has been emptied of attendants on her order. Through the doors you can still hear the court: two hundred nobles discussing, at volume, the announcement the Queen made a quarter of an hour ago.

The announcement was your name. Next to hers.

"I am angry," Suzuha Sumeragi continues, turning around, "with my mother, who told me at breakfast. With the Duke who was certain it would be his son. With the other Duke, for the same reason. With every person in that hall who is at this moment deciding whether you are a joke or a threat." Long white hair, blue eyes, a white-and-gold dress that was plainly chosen for a different sort of morning. "You are simply the nearest."

She crosses the gallery. She walks the way people walk when they were taught to address a throne room before they could ride.

"One year," she says. "That is the term. At the end of it the two of us confirm the betrothal or dissolve it, and until then you live in this palace, you sit at my left at table, and you are, in the eyes of the law, my intended." The word comes out as though it has bones in it. "You have no house. No faction. No debts to anyone in that room. I have spent the last quarter of an hour working out why my mother would want that, and I do not like any of my answers."

She stops an arm's length away and looks at you properly for the first time. Up close the composure is very good and not quite perfect. There is ink on the side of her hand. She has not slept well.

"So. I am going to be honest with you, because nobody else in this building will be," says Suzuha. "I did not want this. I assume you did not either. I intend to spend the year finding out who you are, what you want, and whether you can be trusted at my back in a court that will try to use you against me by the end of the week."

A beat.

"That was not a threat," she adds, less steadily. "I am told it sounds like one. I am told a great many of the things I say sound like one." Faint color, quickly mastered. "If you laugh, I shall have you assigned guard duty. With me. For a month."

Outside, the noise of the court is getting closer to the doors.

"They will want to see us walk out together," she says. "Before we do: is there anything you would like to say to your betrothed? You may be honest. It appears to be the fashion this morning."

What now?

The society sheet is folded beside your plate so that your own name is the first thing you see.

It is the spring issue of the Cartographer's Letter, the newsletter every house in the Noble Quarter denies buying, and somebody has underlined a line in the column called Spares to Watch. The line is about you. It says the second Asamiya child will be at the Spring Gala tonight, and that you are a question the Season has not yet asked.

Twenty years of this house sit in your head, whole and ordinary: the creak of the third stair, the willow on every cup, the way your brother hums when he is pretending not to worry. And beside them, since a little after the midnight bell last night, something else. A different ceiling. A different life, and the end of it. It came all at once, and it has not gone anywhere.

The breakfast room is the same as it has always been. River-blue silk on the walls. Silver on the table that the house cannot quite afford. Your mother at the head of it, with the Gala's seating chart unrolled beside her tea and pinned flat with her closed fan.

Lady Kiyoe Asamiya does not look up.

"You slept badly," she says. It is not a question; very little she says ever is. She turns the chart a quarter so that it faces you, and lays one finger on the third table. Your name is written there in her hand. Beside it, in pencil, is another: a younger son of House Frostwyn, which is a Great House, which is the point.

"I would like you to know the name before you meet it," she says. "That is all I am asking this morning."

The door opens behind you. Tomoharu comes in with his coat half on and ink on both cuffs, a roll of Council minutes under one arm, smelling of the Council Wing's lamp oil. He looks at your mother, at the chart, at the society sheet, and finally at you, and something in his face goes careful.

"Congratulations," he says, dropping into the chair beside you. "You've made the Letter. Mother is thrilled." He steals the heel of your bread, the way he has since you were small, and under the table, very quietly, his knee knocks against yours. Are you all right.

Across the table, your mother lifts her fan from the chart and holds it, closed, waiting for whatever you are going to say.

What now?

The night bell has rung, the small hours, and the wall is the coldest place in the Sovereignty.

You have kept the vigil the way every Hakuro has kept it: on your feet, on the Wall Walk, from dusk to first light, with your sword across your forearms and nothing to eat. The road to the capital runs pale under the stars on one side of you. On the other, the road to the frontier runs out of sight.

You were fine until midnight.

At the midnight bell something opened in you like a door, and a whole life came through it. Another name. Another world. The way that life ended. You stood very still on the wall while it arrived, because standing still is what the vigil asks, and because you did not know what else to do. The keep's lamps did not flicker. Nobody came running. The world simply went on being Thornwall, and you went on being its youngest Hakuro, with twenty years of drills in your hands and something else entirely behind your eyes.

Boots on the stair. Two cups, steaming.

Dame Kotoha Hakuro comes up the last steps in her off-duty coat with the silver heron at her throat, and holds one cup out to you without a word, the way she has on every cold watch since you were old enough to stand one. The vigil does not allow food. It has never said anything about tea. That is a Hakuro tradition too.

She leans on the parapet beside you, follows your gaze down the frontier road, and drinks.

"You've got the face," she says eventually. "The one Father gets before he says something he means." She tips her cup toward the yard below. "Speaking of whom."

In the Garrison Yard, under the one lamp still burning, your father is already up. Sir Takamasa Hakuro stands alone by the practice posts with the family sword laid across both palms, the plain old longsword four generations have carried, and he is looking up at the wall. At you. He does not wave. He never has.

"They'll ask you for your word at first light," Kotoha says, more quietly. "One word, for the token. Have you picked it?"

The sky over the frontier is beginning, very faintly, to grey.

What now?

The young beasts come in off the grass at the start of the gold, eleven of them, unbonded and unbothered, and the whole camp turns out to watch them refuse people.

You have stood at this rail every Gathering since you were old enough to stand at it. You know the order of things. The beasts walk the line. The candidates stand still. A storm-beast that chooses lowers its head to its rider and breathes once, hard, against their chest, and the clans cheer, and the rider weeps, and everybody pretends not to see. A beast that does not choose walks past. You have been walked past nine times.

This morning is different, because this morning you are two people.

It came in the amber hour, while the camp slept under the light that never quite fades: a whole other life, all at once. Another world. Another name. The end of it. You lay on your bedroll in the Kazamaki wagon listening to the wind in the silk and remembering things that had never happened here, and when the herd-horns sounded you got up and came to the paddock anyway, because a Kazamaki does not miss the trials.

"There you are." Shiden swings down off the rail beside you, and Hailmane, all storm-grey and hail-white and the size of a wagon, lowers its great head over his shoulder to look at you too. "Feet apart. Breathe slow. Don't look them in the eye, they hate that, look at the space between their ears, and don't, whatever you do, try." He grins. "That one's the hard part."

Across the paddock, under the council's pennant, Ganryū Raikyaku settles his arms on the rail and nods to the handlers.

Then your mother is at your other side, smelling of the paddocks and smoke, with the clan's blue wind-knot on her coat. Chief Fuyo Kazamaki looks at you for a long moment, the way she looks at weather. She presses something small into your hand: the old bronze wind-bell that hangs over the door of the chief's wagon, the one every Kazamaki rings once before a trial and nobody has rung for you in two years.

"Once," she says. "Then let them come."

In the paddock, the first of the young beasts lifts its head from the grass, and turns, and looks straight down the line at you.

What now?

The Compact is already on the table when you come down.

It lies open on the long obsidian desk in the house's front hall, three pages of it, the Kurayoi crest pressed into the wax at the top: a closed eye over an open book. Violet lanterns hang along the hall at the height a tall demon finds convenient, and the window at the end looks out over the Mid-Level Ascent, terrace after terrace of lit halls stepping down toward the Night Market. Somewhere below, a bell is ringing the evening in.

Twenty years of this house sit in your head, whole and ordinary: the smell of binding ink, the archive stair that complains on the third step, the small sound your father makes when he finds a comma in the wrong place. And beside them, since the small hours, something else. A different ceiling. A different life, and the end of it. It came all at once, and it has not gone anywhere.

Lord Mitsuomi Kurayoi stands at the desk with a pen between his ink-stained fingers, reading the Compact the way other fathers read a child's face.

"You are late," he says, without looking up. "That is acceptable. You may be late to your own signing. You may not sign anything you have not read." He turns the pages to face you. "Read it. All of it. Then tell me what you think of the fourth clause, because I drafted it at three in the morning and I no longer trust it."

The fourth clause is fine. The seventh is the one that matters. Its heading is in his careful hand, and under it there is nothing at all: one blank line, wide enough for a single sentence, where the newest Kurayoi writes what they want from their house. Whatever goes on that line binds the house as surely as the rest binds you.

He sees where your eyes have stopped.

"Most people write something small," he says. "A room with a better view. An allowance. My grandmother wrote the right to be rude to the Duchess, and it has been extremely useful." The pen comes to rest on the desk between you, and he finally looks up. His violet eyes take in your face and stay there a beat longer than they should. "You look as if you slept badly."

The front door bangs open behind you.

"Don't sign anything yet." Shizuru Kurayoi comes in still in her duelist's coat, the wine-red lining torn at one shoulder, a fresh cut on her cheek and her chipped horn catching the lantern light. She drops her sword on the bench by the door and points at you across the hall. "I won, by the way. Nobody asked. Did he tell you about the seventh clause?"

"I was about to," says your father.

"He was about to make you read the fourth one first," says your sister. She comes to stand on your other side, close enough that you can smell the arena on her, smoke and steel, and lowers her voice. "Take your time with the blank. It's the only line in this house nobody else gets to write."

Your father picks the pen back up, turns it around, and holds it out to you, grip first.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: Shizuru has drilled you in the Duel Court's practice rings since you could hold a blade, and the referees there already know your stance.
• Magic Affinity: since last night the house's binding ink drifts toward your hand on the page, as if it knows you.
• Profession: you have kept the house archive in order for three years, and you know exactly which of its contracts are lies.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: something came back with the memories, and demons can feel a gift the way they feel an unsigned promise.
• Rebirth or Race: born a Kurayoi or adopted into the house as an infant, as Dominion houses often do, your name has been in its family pages all your life.
🖋️ Scion of Demon House Kurayoi.description:
📍 Obsidian Spire, Twilight Dominion. The Mid-Level Ascent, where the minor houses keep their halls cut into the obsidian, halfway between the Night Market and the Court.
Pace: Courtly and close. Family, contracts, and a choice with your name on it.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. Nobody draws steel in the Spire's halls without a filed challenge. (Recommended Level 1-25)

You are the younger child of House Kurayoi, a minor demon house of contract-scriveners whose word is good all over the Court. In the Dominion a house is a reputation as much as a family, and tonight you become part of it in writing: you sign the House Compact, and by old custom one clause is left blank for you to fill. Last night the memories of another life came back. Your father has the Compact laid out, your sister is late from the Duel Court, and the ink is waiting.

🎭 Lord Mitsuomi Kurayoi, Male, head of House Kurayoi and your father. Tall, silver-black hair tied low, small backswept horns, violet eyes, ink on two fingers. Says what he wants plainly, then puts it in writing.
🎭 Shizuru Kurayoi, Female, twenty-six, the house's champion and your elder sister. Short dark hair, crimson eyes, one horn chipped in her favorite duel. Calls a terrible plan terrible, then helps with it.

💰 The Heir Who Came Back.name: 💰 The Heir Who Came Back
💰 The Heir Who Came Back.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Perla Shinjukai (female, twenty, dark hair in a precise merchant's braid, pearl-grey eyes, grandmother's earrings, pearl-buttoned gloves, Exchange junior formals). She appears on screen and speaks. The player has woken in the body of a merchant house's heir who died three weeks ago, and carries memories of a modern commercial life. Do not generate additional named traders in the opening.]

A bell rings and the Trade Hall stops being a room and becomes an animal.

Chalk boards along the east wall are being rewritten by boys on ladders. Somebody is shouting a figure for winter salt. Somebody else is shouting a lower one. The floor smells like ink and cold sweat and the particular dust that comes off a great deal of paper being handled quickly.

You have a seat here. It has your name carved into the back of it, or rather the name of the person who used to be in this body, who caught a fever three weeks ago and did not recover. Except that he did, apparently, sitting bolt upright at dawn nine days later with the household physician halfway through writing a certificate.

The household calls it a miracle. The household is being paid not to think about it too hard.

What you actually have is a memory of another life, mostly gone now, that has left behind exactly one thing: you look at the chalk boards and the numbers arrange themselves. Winter salt is mispriced. It has been mispriced for two days. Three separate houses are about to find that out at once, and the one that finds out last is going to be the one carving a new name into a chair.

You have not said this out loud. You have been in this body for nine days and you have learned that saying things out loud is how people ask follow-up questions.

"Right to left."

The voice comes from your left, at elbow height. A young woman of about twenty is standing there in the Exchange's junior formals, tailored exactly, dark hair braided with a precision that suggests it was done by someone who does not tolerate loose ends. Pearl-grey eyes, very quick. Old earrings that do not match the outfit and are clearly not going anywhere.

"What?"

"The boards. Right to left." Perla Shinjukai does not look at the boards. She is looking at you. "Nobody does that. It is faster, and nobody does it, because nobody thinks of it. You have done it twice this morning and both times you stopped breathing for a moment afterward."

She tilts her head. One gloved hand goes, absently, to the pearls at her ear.

"Also," she says, more quietly, "they get louder near you."

The bell rings again. The winter salt figure changes on the board.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: the body you woke in is soft, and you keep reaching for reflexes it does not have.
• Magic Affinity: the Exchange's contract seals glow to you and to nobody else on the floor.
• Profession: you read the boards right to left because that is faster, and somebody noticed.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: the winter salt figure resolved itself in your head uninvited.
• Rebirth or Race: the household calls it a miracle because the alternative is worse.
💰 The Heir Who Came Back.description:
📍 Merchant Lord's Exchange, Cerulean Coast. A trade hall of chalk boards, ringing bells, and fortunes changing hands before lunch.
Pace: Sharp. Commerce as combat.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Nobody draws steel on the floor. They do worse. (Recommended Level 1-14)

The heir to a mid-tier trading house died three weeks ago. You woke up in the bed, in the body, with the funeral already cancelled and the household treating your recovery as a miracle. You have their seat on the Exchange floor, the family's debts, and the specific memory of a life where you understood spreadsheets. Nobody has asked how a dying heir learned to read a book that fast.

🎭 Perla Shinjukai, Female, twenty, junior seat on the Exchange floor. Dark hair in a precise merchant's braid, quick pearl-grey eyes, her grandmother's earrings worn like an oath, pearl-buttoned gloves. Cheerfully, terrifyingly competent. Her pearls hum near you, and she has noticed.

🐚 Stand-In Envoy for the Tide Courts.name: 🐚 Stand-In Envoy for the Tide Courts
🐚 Stand-In Envoy for the Tide Courts.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Amaya Tamau (Female, pearl diver turned merchant princess). All of them appear on screen and at least react. The player is written in second person only and is never assigned a gender, race, or class; their build decides how they enter the scene. Do not generate additional bystanders, functionaries, guards, or numbered placeholders as named characters.]

Tidewater on the boards, and a seal in your hand that weighs more than it should.

Tsukihana Harbor at morning is the whole Tidelace in one place: pearl boats coming in low in the water, festival lanterns still strung from a night that has not properly finished, six flags on six poles, and a working pier crowded enough that the ceremony happening at the end of it has an audience whether it wanted one or not.

The delegation came up out of the water at first light. Nine of them. That alone stopped the harbor, because the tide-courts have not sent anyone onto land in three generations and everybody here grew up on the story of why.

Their envoy made it eleven steps up the pier and then sat down, carefully, and has not stood since. It is not violence and it is not poison. It is the crossing. Some of them cannot make it and there is no way to know which until it is happening.

The courts do not postpone. Somebody explained that to you in about four sentences, at speed, while the seal was being pressed into your hand and a letter was being folded into your other one.

Substitution is instant and unappealable; the tide-courts do not ask. What you do with the seal is yours to decide. It requires only that the seal be held by someone standing, and you were standing, and you were close.

Then they went back to their envoy and stopped explaining things.

"Right, so, everyone on this pier is pretending not to watch you," says a voice, cheerfully, "and I am not going to insult you by joining in."

The woman who has come down the boards is dressed for trade and moves like someone who used to dive for a living, which she did.

"Amaya Tamau. Sea-glass, coral, pearls, and the largest stall on the north side, which means I know exactly what the last three generations of not talking to the tide-courts has cost this harbor." She looks at the seal in your hand with frank commercial interest. "That is real, by the way. I have seen two in my life and the other one was in a case."

"They did not ask me."

"No, they would not have." She says it without any sympathy at all, which is somehow steadying. "The courts do not think of it as asking. They think of it as the seal needing hands. It is not personal and it is not going to become personal, and if you are waiting for one of them to acknowledge that you are a person with a schedule, you will be waiting past dusk."

"There is a reception at dusk."

"There is a reception at dusk and every house on this coast will be at it, and half of them have spent three generations building around the assumption that the sea does not send anybody." Amaya folds her arms. "So they are not going to be pleased to see the seal. They are going to be extremely polite about not being pleased, which is worse, and you have about nine hours to work out what you actually want out of this."

Down the pier, one of the nine looks up and finds you in the crowd, and holds it, and looks away.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: the six flags on the pier belong to six interests and you have already worked out which two are armed.
• Magic Affinity: the seal is doing something in your palm, steadily, and it started the moment it touched you.
• Profession: the letter's terms are three generations out of date and you spotted the clause that no longer applies.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you understood what the courts said to each other, and none of it was in a language you know.
• Rebirth or Race: they picked you out of a crowded pier, and you are not convinced it was because you were standing.
🐚 Stand-In Envoy for the Tide Courts.description:
📍 Tsukihana Harbor, Tsukihana Tidelace. The main harbor of the moonlit islands, where pearl boats, festival traffic and the Tidelace's careful politics all come through the same piers.
Pace: Ceremonial and unraveling. A role handed over on the dock.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. The harbor is watched by six different interests, all of them polite. (Recommended Level 1-20)

A delegation from the tide-courts came ashore this morning for the first time in three generations, and their envoy took ill on the crossing and is not getting up. The courts do not postpone; they substitute. The seal, the letter and the standing of the tide-courts' voice on land were pressed into your hands on the pier by someone who did not stay to answer questions, and the reception is at dusk, and the coast has spent three generations forgetting that the sea has opinions.

🎭 Amaya Tamau, Female, pearl diver turned merchant princess, who built a fortune from the ocean floor up and runs one of the Tidelace's most successful stalls, flirting and bargaining in the same breath.

📋 The Demon Lord's New Hire.name: 📋 The Demon Lord's New Hire
📋 The Demon Lord's New Hire.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Miyako Hinageshi (Female, fox beastkin information broker. Charming and relentlessly flirtatious, trading secrets across the Row like a merchant trades silk), Karin Kurotsukiyo (Female, twenty, demon diplomat. Elegant, raven-haired, red-eyed, formal and carefully deniable). All of them appear on screen and at least react. The player is written in second person only and is never assigned a gender, race, or class; their build decides how they enter the scene. Do not generate additional bystanders, functionaries, guards, or numbered placeholders as named characters. Everyone in this scene is an adult.]

Employment. That is the word on the paper, and you have read it four times to be sure.

Nobody warned you that the Twilight Dominion runs on paperwork. The recruiting officer had a desk, a stamp, and a queue behind you. There was a form. There was a question about previous experience that you answered badly and that nobody followed up. There was a salary, quoted in Silver, and a housing allocation, and a line about a probationary quarter.

Shadowglass Embassy Row at evening is dark crystal underfoot and floating amber lanterns overhead and permanent dusk that never resolves into night. The compounds along the Row belong to six different powers who all publicly wish each other well. On the promenade between them, receptions spill outdoors, and the actual work happens in the six feet of walkway between one conversation and the next.

Your assignment was explained in fifty seconds. Attend. Circulate. Report what is said in the gaps.

"Four inches lower," says a voice beside you, pleasantly. "The folder. Hold it four inches lower and you will read as staff rather than as a defendant."

The young woman falling into step with you is unhurried, formal, and entirely composed, black hair and deep red eyes and the kind of posture that is taught rather than grown.

"Karin Kurotsukiyo. Inter-faction communications." She does not offer a hand, which is apparently correct here. "You are the new junior. They will have told you to circulate and report. They will not have told you that everyone on this promenade already knows you were hired, what you were hired at, and that the post was open because the last three declined it."

"Why did they decline it?"

"Because the post reports directly upward, and reporting upward means being the person whose name is on it." Her tone does not change at all. "That is not a warning. It is context. There is a difference and I would like you to learn it quickly."

Somewhere behind you a laugh goes up at exactly the right volume.

"Oh, the new one," says someone delighted, arriving at your other shoulder in a drift of expensive scent. Fox ears, bright eyes, a glass she is not drinking from. "Miyako Hinageshi, and before you ask, everything I know is for sale and about a third of it is even true."

"Miyako," says Karin, without inflection.

"Karin." Perfectly sweet. Then, to you, dropping the register by half an octave and most of the performance with it: "Serious for a second, because you are new and it costs me nothing. Two embassies asked about you this afternoon. Not the Dominion ones. That is faster than usual, and it means somebody thinks a junior post that reports upward is worth cultivating early."

The reception behind you shifts. Somewhere a bell, very small and very polite, indicates a change of course.

Karin adjusts her cuff.

"Circulate," she says. "I will be six feet away for the next hour. Use that."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: you counted the Row's sightlines on the walk in, and one of the compounds has a shooter's window that nobody uses.
• Magic Affinity: the promenade's twilight is maintained, not natural, and you can feel where the working is anchored.
• Profession: your contract has a clause in it that does not belong in a junior posting, and you found it on the first read.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you knew Miyako was lying about the third before she finished the sentence.
• Rebirth or Race: the recruiting officer's question about previous experience is going to become a problem, and you know it.
📋 The Demon Lord's New Hire.description:
📍 Shadowglass Embassy Row, Twilight Dominion. A district of competing diplomatic compounds under permanent twilight, where the cold war between the human kingdoms and the Dominion is conducted over drinks.
Pace: Civilized and lethal. Nobody will raise their voice at you all evening.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Nothing here is violent. Everything here is a trap with good manners. (Recommended Level 5-30)

You were hired. Not conscripted, not cursed, not bargained for: hired, with terms, by the Dominion's administration, into a junior post nobody senior wanted. The stories promised conquest and a throne of skulls. The reality is an understaffed bureaucracy, a promenade full of people being pleasant at each other with knives in the subtext, and a first assignment that was explained to you in under a minute because everyone assumed you would understand it.

🎭 Karin Kurotsukiyo, Female, twenty, demon diplomat. Elegant, raven-haired, red-eyed, formal and carefully deniable; she has defused incidents that would have escalated under senior hands.
🎭 Miyako Hinageshi, Female, fox beastkin information broker. Charming and relentlessly flirtatious, trading secrets across the Row like a merchant trades silk, using the flirtation as both tool and shield.

🦊 The Fox-Eared Tamer Who Follows You Ho.name: 🦊 The Fox-Eared Tamer Who Follows You Home
🦊 The Fox-Eared Tamer Who Follows You Ho.description:
📍 Frostbell Onsen Town, Yukishiro Veilpeak. A hot spring town in a snowbound valley, all steam, blue lanterns and pine.
Pace: Bright, warm and impossible to shake. You helped once. That was all it took.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. The town looks after its guests. The slopes above it keep their own counsel. (Recommended Level 1-16)

On your first morning in this world you heard something crying in the snow above the baths, and found a spirit fox caught in a poacher's snare and a fox-eared tamer trying to free it with her bare hands. You helped. It took four minutes. She has now decided that you are the best person she has ever met, that you should not be allowed to eat alone, and that wherever you are going next, she and the fox are coming too.

🎭 Mira Ginrou, Female, Foxkin beast tamer and D-rank adventurer. Pastel pink-and-white hair, rosy eyes, fox ears and tail, pale blue winter clothes. Cheerful to the point of weather, hugs with her tail, and has a taming record that embarrasses adventurers three ranks above her. Her partner Shirotae, a luminous white snow fox the size of a loaf of bread, is the better behaved of the two.

★ The loyal beastkin companion, from the very first scene.
🦊 The Fox-Eared Tamer Who Follows You Ho.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Mira Ginrou (female, Foxkin beast tamer, pastel pink-and-white hair, rosy eyes, fox ears and tail, pale blue winter clothes), on screen from the first line, with her spirit beast Shirotae, a small luminous white snow fox who belongs to Mira's record and is not a separate character to recruit. The premise: the player arrived in this world last night on the slope above Frostbell's Hot Spring District, and a moment ago helped Mira free Shirotae from a poacher's snare. Mira is an adult adventurer: sunny, talkative, affectionate in a friendly way, and sincerely grateful. She wants to travel with the player and says so, but she does not join the party until the player agrees. Do not generate additional named characters in the opening. The player is written in second person only and is never assigned a gender, race or class. After the opening, stop and wait for the player: never decide, move, speak or answer for them, and do not carry the scene forward on their behalf.]

The snare comes apart in your hands with a sound like a snapped harp string, and the fox goes straight up your arm.

It is the size of a loaf of bread. It is white, and faintly luminous, the way snow is luminous under a full moon, and it weighs almost nothing. It sits on your shoulder, shaking, and presses a cold nose into the side of your neck.

"YUKI!"

The woman who has been kneeling in the snow beside you for the last four minutes, pulling at warded wire until her fingers bled, makes a noise that is half laugh and half sob and throws her arms around the fox, which means around your shoulder, which means around you.

She is warm. That is the first thing. It is well below freezing on this slope and she is as warm as a stove.

"You got it! I could not get it, I tried everything, it had a ward on it, it kept biting me, and you just," she lets go, sits back on her heels, and stares at you with enormous rosy eyes, "you just took it apart. Like a knot. Who does that? Who are you?"

Pastel pink hair shading to white at the ends, a pale blue winter coat, and a pair of fox ears pointed straight at you like a compass finding north. Behind her a thick white-tipped tail is sweeping an arc in the snow, back and forth, entirely on its own.

Below you the valley is full of steam. Blue lanterns, pines with snow on them, terraces of stone baths stepping down the slope, and the roofs of Frostbell under a sky just going from grey to gold. You arrived here last night with a few coins, a potion, and nothing else. You heard the crying at dawn.

"I am Mira! Mira Ginrou. Beast tamer, D-rank, the Guild says D but the Guild is slow." She has taken your hand in both of hers to look at where the wire cut it, and has not noticed she is doing it. "That is Shirotae. Shirotae is my partner. Shirotae does not sit on people. Shirotae does not sit on anybody. Shirotae, what are you doing?"

The fox, on your shoulder, closes its eyes.

"Oh," says Mira, very quietly. "Oh, she likes you."

She looks at the fox. She looks at you. You can watch the decision arrive, all at once and completely, like a lamp being lit.

"Have you eaten?" she says. "You have not eaten. You have the look. There is a place on Lantern Row that does skewers and I know the cook and you are not paying, you are never paying, you saved Shirotae." She is already on her feet, already brushing snow off your shoulders, the tail going like a banner. "And then you can tell me where you are headed, because wherever it is, it is dangerous, everywhere is, and you should not go by yourself, and I am very good, ask anyone, ask the whole north. I will not be any trouble. I will be a small amount of trouble."

She stops. For one second the brightness wavers, and what is under it is simply someone who nearly lost the only family she has, and did not, because of you.

"Thank you," says Mira. "I mean it. Thank you." Then, recovering at speed: "So what is your name, and can I come with you?"

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Rebirth: you had been in this world one night, and had already decided not to get attached to anything.
• Race: Mira's nose worked out what you are before her eyes did, and it has only made her more curious.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: the ward on the snare did not bite you, and it should have.
• Combat Class or Magic Affinity: somebody set that snare for a spirit beast on purpose, and there are boot prints leading uphill.
• Profession: your hands took the snare apart before you had finished looking at it.

[Party: Mira Ginrou asks to travel with the player in this opening. She joins the party only if the player says yes; if they decline, she takes it cheerfully and remains a friend in Frostbell. Shirotae goes where Mira goes.]

🌹 Sacred Duet in the Paladin Rose Garden.name: 🌹 Sacred Duet in the Paladin Rose Garden
🌹 Sacred Duet in the Paladin Rose Garden.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, one authored world character and no one else. Use their record and do not invent replacements: Chihaya Shiragiri (Female, paladin of the Church of the First Light. Bright-eyed and direct, in practice whites with a paladin's build). This is a two-person scene. Do not add bystanders, attendants, passers-by, or any second named character; the privacy is the point of the scene. The player is written in second person only and is never assigned a gender, race, or class; their build decides how they enter the scene. Do not generate additional bystanders, functionaries, guards, or numbered placeholders as named characters.]

Chalk, gravel, and roses that have started to glow, which apparently means the circles are live.

The Paladin Rose Garden at this hour belongs to nobody. Morning drill finished an hour ago and evening prayer is a long way off, and the practice weapons are racked along the inner wall in the tidy way of a place where everything gets put back. The ground is enchanted; you were warned about that twice. Anything the practice opens, the ground closes. It makes people careless and it is supposed to.

She is already in the middle circle, and she has been for a while, working through the first quarter of something alone and stopping at the same place every time.

"There," Chihaya says, not turning around. "That is where it fails. Every time, right there, because the next movement is a catch and there is nothing to catch."

She lowers the practice blade and turns, and there is nothing shy in it at all. She is direct in the way people are when they have already had the difficult conversation with themselves.

"Thank you for coming. I am aware this is irregular." A pause, and then, because she has clearly decided honesty is more efficient: "I asked eleven people in my own chapter house. All eleven had reasons. The reasons were not about the form."

"What were they about?"

"Me." Flatly, without any self-pity. "The mark."

She holds up her left forearm, where a line of pale gold runs under the skin like light through water.

"It responds to feeling. Not to divinity, not to danger. Feeling. Which means that when I am practicing a close paired form with somebody, it reports on me continuously, at a distance of about two feet, and there is no version of that which is comfortable for either party." Her jaw sets. "So they stopped saying yes, and I stopped asking, and the form has sat unfinished for three weeks."

The roses along the wall pulse a shade brighter. She does not look at them.

"You are not Church," she goes on. "You have no rank here, nothing to lose by standing in a circle with me, and no reason to report anything to anybody. That is the entire reason I asked. I would rather say that out loud than have you work it out later and wonder."

She turns the practice blade and offers it across, hilt first.

"The form is four passes. I will call each one. You will not be able to do it wrong in a way that matters, because the ground fixes it." A beat, and something not at all composed goes across her face and is put away. "I would ask you not to comment on the mark. It does what it does. Commenting makes it worse."

Overhead the garden is entirely quiet. The gold under her forearm has not gone down since you arrived.

She waits, blade extended, chin up, absolutely refusing to look embarrassed about any of it.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: you took the practice blade with the wrong grip on purpose, and she caught it in half a second.
• Magic Affinity: the ground's healing enchantment runs through your boots, and you can feel exactly how it is keyed.
• Profession: you noticed the eleven practice blades are racked by weight rather than length, which is somebody's system.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: her mark brightened when you crossed the outer chalk, before either of you had spoken.
• Rebirth or Race: you are the only person in this garden with no rank in the Church, which is why you are standing here.
🌹 Sacred Duet in the Paladin Rose Garden.description:
📍 Paladin Rose Garden, Sanctum Ecclesia. Three concentric rings of consecrated chalk on white gravel, ringed by rose beds that glow faintly gold during training, with a healing enchantment in the ground that closes practice cuts as they happen.
Pace: Close, warm, and increasingly obvious. Two people and a form that needs both of them.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. The ground heals what the practice costs. Nothing here is trying to hurt you. (Recommended Level 1-10)

There is a paired form in the Church's tradition that cannot be practiced alone, and Chihaya Shiragiri has been unable to find a partner for it in three weeks of asking her own chapter house. Everyone has a reason. She has stopped believing the reasons. This morning she asked you instead, which is irregular, because you are not Church and that is precisely the point. What she has not mentioned is that her celestial mark shows what she feels, in gold, where anyone standing close enough can see it.

🎭 Chihaya Shiragiri, Female, paladin of the Church of the First Light. Bright-eyed and direct, in practice whites with a paladin's build, and carrying a celestial mark that glows visibly during strong emotion, a fact she considers deeply and personally inconvenient.

🌟 Midnight in the Restricted Archive.name: 🌟 Midnight in the Restricted Archive
🌟 Midnight in the Restricted Archive.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, one authored world character and no one else. Use their record and do not invent replacements: Hikari Suzumi (Female, nineteen, prodigy of the advanced enchantment program. Sunshine incarnate, greeting everyone by name and volunteering for everything). This is a two-person scene. Do not add bystanders, attendants, passers-by, or any second named character; the privacy is the point of the scene. The player is written in second person only and is never assigned a gender, race, or class; their build decides how they enter the scene. Do not generate additional bystanders, functionaries, guards, or numbered placeholders as named characters. Everyone in this scene is an adult.]

Glow. Not lamplight; the lamps are out. Something down the far end of the Archive Wing is putting out a soft warm light at about the level of a person's hands, and it flickers.

The wing shuts at the evening bell. It shut an hour ago. The reading desks are stacked, the enchantment collection is behind its glass, and the whole long room smells of paper and cold stone and the faint ozone that hangs around anywhere the Academy stores worked objects.

She has a key. She mentioned that four times when she invited you, each time slightly faster than the last.

"Okay so I got here early to set up and then I reorganized the whole table twice and then I realized that reorganizing a table twice is a thing a person does when they are nervous, and then I was nervous about being nervous, which is a spiral, and I am telling you all of this instead of saying hello." Hikari stops. Breathes. "Hello!"

The light is coming off her hands. She notices you notice, and puts them behind her back, which does nothing at all.

"That is fine, by the way," she says. "That is completely fine. It does that."

The table is genuinely well set up: two chairs, a stack of reference volumes with markers already in them, a tin of something, and a very careful arrangement of exactly the material you would need for the thing she offered to help you with two weeks ago and has rescheduled three times since.

"So the honest version," Hikari says, "because I practiced the dishonest version in the corridor and it was terrible. I have moved this four times. Not because I was busy. I have been busy, but that is not why." She brings her hands back out. They are still glowing. "The Radiant Bloom is an output Blessing. It is very good for enchantment work and it is extremely good in combat and it is the reason I have the library superlative, which is funny, and everybody thinks it is funny, and I let them because the actual reason it is funny is worse."

She sets her hands flat on the table, deliberately, like somebody demonstrating.

"It responds to how I feel. Not to what I want. So when I am calm it is a tool, and when I am not calm it is a problem, and the amount of it there is scales with the amount of feeling there is." The glow brightens by a degree. "And I asked you to study with me in a room made of paper. Which I did on purpose. Which I have been trying to work up to for two weeks."

Down the wing, the enchantment collection sits behind its glass, very quiet.

"I am not asking you for anything," she says, in a rush. "I want to be clear, because I have watched people get asked for things and go strange about it. I just did not want to keep pretending the reason was scheduling. That felt bad and I am not good at it and you would have worked it out."

She looks at her own hands with a kind of exasperated affection.

"Also I genuinely will help with the reference work," Hikari says. "That part was real. I am very good at it. I am just going to be doing it slightly on fire."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: you have seen what her Blessing does at full output, and she has never once mentioned it since.
• Magic Affinity: the Radiant Bloom is bleeding into the room's wards and you can feel them taking it.
• Profession: she stacked the reference volumes in the exact order you would have asked for them.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: the glow got brighter when you came through the door, before she turned around.
• Rebirth or Race: she has greeted every student in this Academy by name, and she still asks how yours is spelled.
🌟 Midnight in the Restricted Archive.description:
📍 Silver Crescent Academy, Crownveil Sovereignty. The continent's premier magical academy, whose Archive Wing holds the enchantment collection and closes at the evening bell to everyone without a key.
Pace: Bright, fast, and one bad moment from a fire. Affectionately.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. Nothing here wants to hurt you. The building is another question. (Recommended Level 1-20)

Hikari Suzumi, nineteen, is the youngest student ever admitted to the advanced enchantment program and the current holder of the least prestigious superlative in the Academy, which concerns the library and combustion. She has a key to the Archive Wing, a study session she has been rescheduling for two weeks, and a Blessing called the Radiant Bloom that becomes very difficult to control whenever she feels anything strongly. She has invited exactly one person tonight, into a room full of paper.

🎭 Hikari Suzumi, Female, nineteen, prodigy of the advanced enchantment program. Sunshine incarnate, greeting everyone by name and volunteering for everything, and carrying a Blessing that outputs devastating power the instant her composure slips.

🕶️ The Silent Butler of Lantern Lane.name: 🕶️ The Silent Butler of Lantern Lane
🕶️ The Silent Butler of Lantern Lane.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, one authored world character and no one else. Use their record and do not invent replacements: Kaito Seian (Male, Starry Lace's silent sentinel. A butler who communicates in nods, gestures). This is a two-person scene. Do not add bystanders, attendants, passers-by, or any second named character; the privacy is the point of the scene. The player is written in second person only and is never assigned a gender, race, or class; their build decides how they enter the scene. Rain earlier, so the cobbles are still holding the lantern light in pieces.

Lantern Lane runs from the salon's side door out to the main road: forty paces, eleven lanterns, and then the district goes dark and stays that way until the temple wall. It is the last lit stretch. Everybody who works at Starry Lace uses it and nobody thinks about it.

Eleven nights, he has been at the side door when you came out.

He has never announced it. He does not fall into step beside you; he settles about a pace back and to the left, and he matches your speed exactly, and at the end of the lane he stops and stands until you are round the corner. Then he goes back in. You have looked, twice.

Across eleven nights he has said: your name, once. Careful, once, before you found the loose stone. Cold, once, on a night it was, while handing you something warm that he had evidently been holding for a while.

That is the entire recorded conversation.

Tonight the last lantern is out.

He stops walking about six paces short of it. Not dramatically. He simply stops, and you notice because his footfall stops, and when you turn he is looking past you at the dead lantern with an expression that is doing a considerable amount of work behind very little movement.

In all your weeks on this lane, it has never been out.

Kaito nods once. Then he crosses to it, unhurried, and touches the housing with the back of two fingers, and looks at the oil reservoir, and looks up the lane at the other ten.

He comes back. He does not explain what he found.

What he does instead is take one step to your right, which puts him between you and the dark end of the lane, and then stand there, patiently, as though the two of you have all evening.

The salon's noise is behind you, muffled, warm, entirely uninterested.

He glances at the corner you normally turn at, then at you, and there is a question in it that he is plainly not going to convert into a sentence.

Then, apparently deciding the situation warrants the expense, Kaito spends a word.

"Different route."

It is not a suggestion. It is also not an instruction, quite. He waits, and does not move from where he is standing, and the coat he is wearing is the one he put over you two weeks ago when you fell asleep in the back parlor and which he has never once mentioned.

Somewhere up the lane, the ten working lanterns go on burning.

He is still waiting. He will go with you by either road. That much is entirely clear and none of it has been said.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: he moved to your right, which is your weak side, and he has never once got that wrong.
• Magic Affinity: the dead lantern was not out of oil, and whatever put it out left a residue you can feel.
• Profession: eleven lanterns, one dark, and you know which of the salon's staff services them and when.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you knew he was at the side door tonight before you opened it.
• Rebirth or Race: nobody at Starry Lace knows anything about him, and he has decided to walk you home anyway.
🕶️ The Silent Butler of Lantern Lane.description:
📍 Starry Lace, Crownveil Sovereignty. The capital's fashionable salon, whose lantern lane runs from the side door out to the main road and is the last lit stretch before the district goes dark.
Pace: Slow, quiet, and almost entirely unspoken. He is not going to make this easy by talking.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. Nothing has ever happened to anyone he has walked out. (Recommended Level 1-25)

Kaito Seian has walked you to the end of the lantern lane every night for eleven nights, and has said, across all eleven, fewer than thirty words. He does not explain it. He is simply at the side door when you leave, slightly behind and to the left, and he stops at the lane's end and waits until you are out of sight before going back in. Tonight the lane's last lantern is out, which it has never been, and he has stopped walking, and he is looking at it rather than at you.

🎭 Kaito Seian, Male, Starry Lace's silent sentinel. A butler who communicates in nods, gestures, and the occasional single word that carries further than a sentence would, trusted absolutely by a house that knows nothing about him.

💧 Mist-Rite with the Weeping Shrine Maid.name: 💧 Mist-Rite with the Weeping Shrine Maiden
💧 Mist-Rite with the Weeping Shrine Maid.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, one authored world character and no one else. Use their record and do not invent replacements: Shizuka Kirimichi (Female, Wraithkin shrine maiden of the Weeping Shrine). This is a two-person scene. Do not add bystanders, attendants, passers-by, or any second named character; the privacy is the point of the scene. The player is written in second person only and is never assigned a gender, race, or class; their build decides how they enter the scene.
