• Rebirth or Race: you have no claim, no license and no history here, which is precisely what makes your signature usable.
🐫 Emergency Leader of the Desert Caravan.description:
📍 Goldlotus Oasis, Renka Mirage Sea. A lush desert city of silk tents and blue water, whose bazaar trades in the goods that survive a crossing and the paperwork that permits one.
Pace: Hot, hurried, and consequential. A decision made at the speed of a departing caravan.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. The oasis is watched. The crossing that starts tomorrow is not. (Recommended Level 1-16)

The caravan's trade master died three days out and the caravan came back for him, which cost them the season. Forty wagons cannot cross the Mirage without a name signed to the book, that name has to be accepted by the oasis clerks by dusk, and every senior hand has a reason it cannot be theirs. For reasons nobody will explain to your face, the argument has stopped and everyone is looking at you.

🎭 Nadiya Hanau, Female, oasis herbalist. Young, earnest to a fault, genuinely gifted with desert medicine and hopeless at anything requiring social grace; she stammers when complimented and is currently the only person here being honest with you.

🌿 The Skill They Laughed At.name: 🌿 The Skill They Laughed At
🌿 The Skill They Laughed At.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Momo Ibarajō (female, long brown hair, golden eyes, leather bodice over white blouse), Luna Kasumiryu (female, long brown hair, pointed ears, luminous green eyes, leafy green dress), and Hayato Haibara (male, wolf-eared, shaggy black hair, golden eyes, fur-trimmed cloak). All three appear on screen and at least react. The player was born in this village and carries a Blessing the village considers worthless. Do not generate additional named villagers in the opening. Also standing in these areas and drawn from the authored roster, not invented: Zorin Ryūen (Dragonkin fire mage). Name them from their records if the scene reaches them.]

Mossglow Commons at morning is the best thing in the world, and you have never once said so out loud, because you would never hear the end of it.

The light comes down through the canopy in slow green columns. The bridge walks creak the way they have creaked your whole life. Somebody's kettle is going. Somebody's goat is loose again. Two houses over, a woman is arguing gently with a shelf.

You are eighteen today, which in Lanternmoss means nothing in particular, because your appraisal happened years ago and everyone remembers how it went.

The elder read the Blessing off the stone. There was a pause. A short one, but the kind that has weight in it. And then somebody at the back, who has since apologized twice and meant it once, laughed.

Useless, the village decided, kindly. Not cruelly. Lanternmoss is not a cruel place. Just useless, in the way a very ornate spoon is useless, and the matter was closed.

You have not argued. Arguing would have meant demonstrating, and demonstrating would have meant explaining what you worked out in the third year, alone, behind the herb sheds, and you have never quite been ready for that conversation.

"Seventy percent," says Momo Ibarajō.

Momo Ibarajō is on the path with a crate of bottles balanced against one hip, long brown hair coming out of its tie, golden eyes narrowed at you with the specific suspicion of someone who has known you since you were both small and covered in mud.

"Seventy percent of what."

"Chance of you doing something today." She sets the crate down, which is never a good sign. "Rising. Sorry. Sorry, that came out as a forecast again."

At the well, Luna Kasumiryu straightens from filling a jar, pointed ears catching the movement before her eyes do. Green light seems to like her. She looks at you the way she has looked at you a few times this year, thoughtfully, as though a sum is coming out differently than expected.

And on the far side of the commons, leaning against a post with his arms folded, Hayato Haibara is watching too. Wolf ears forward. Golden eyes steady. He has been in this village four months and has not yet explained why.

Something crashes in the treeline, hard, and much closer than anything should be at this hour.

The goat stops complaining. The kettle keeps going.

Momo says, very quietly, "That is not a deer."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: you have been quietly training behind the herb sheds for six years.
• Magic Affinity: the treeline went wrong before the crash, and only you flinched.
• Profession: your useless skill is not useless; it is just not a weapon.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: the thing behind your ribs picks today, of all days, to stir.
• Rebirth or Race: the village has been kind to you and has never once asked what you can do.
🌿 The Skill They Laughed At.description:
📍 Lanternmoss Village, Verdania Wilds. A moss-lit forest village of bridge walks, herb gardens, and houses grown into the trees.
Pace: Warm, then explosive. Small life, enormous secret.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. The village is peaceful. The forest is not. (Recommended Level 1-10)

You were born here, in a farming family, and at your appraisal the village elder read your Blessing aloud and there was a pause, and then somebody laughed. It is a useless skill. Everyone agrees it is a useless skill. You have spent eighteen years quietly discovering that it is not, and today somebody is finally going to see you use it properly.

🎭 Momo Ibarajō, Female, village potion brewer. Long brown hair, golden eyes, open smile, leather bodice over a white blouse, surrounded by shelves of alarmingly colorful bottles. Narrates her own brewing like a weather report and apologizes constantly for side effects.
🎭 Luna Kasumiryu, Female, warm-eyed with long brown hair, pointed ears, and luminous green eyes in a leafy green dress.
🎭 Hayato Haibara, Male, stern and wolf-eared, shaggy black hair, golden eyes, fur-trimmed cloak, protective stare.
🎭 Zorin Ryūen, Male, Dragonkin fire mage and self-declared rival of every strong adventurer in the Wilds. Loud, passionate, genuinely powerful, and issuing a challenge to somebody at all times.

🌻 Aging Out of Sunpetal Orphanage.name: 🌻 Aging Out of Sunpetal Orphanage
🌻 Aging Out of Sunpetal Orphanage.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Natsume Hatsuhana (female, tousled blonde hair, vivid green eyes, white blouse and dark bodice). She appears on screen and speaks. The player was born in this world, raised in this orphanage, and carries fragmentary memories of a previous life they have never told anyone about. Do not generate additional named staff or children as major characters in the opening.]

They strip the bed while you are still in the room. Not unkindly. There is simply a queue.

Sunpetal's courtyard is warm brick and laundry lines and a fig tree that has been dying for eleven years without ever quite committing. Fourteen children are doing the loud parts of the morning in the far corner. A younger one is sitting on the step by the kitchen watching you with the flat, assessing stare of somebody working out whether they are allowed to be sad about this.

You grew up here. You know the count of steps to the well. You know which flagstone rocks.

You also know, and have never once said, that you remember being older than this. Not clearly. It comes in pieces, mostly useless: the taste of a drink that does not exist in Sanctum Ecclesia, a song with no words you can hold, the shape of a room with a window that opened the wrong way. You worked out at about six that saying any of it aloud would get you sent to the cathedral for examination, and you decided you would rather stay.

So you stayed. And now the calendar has run out.

There is a canvas bag by the gate with your name inked on the flap. A spare shirt. A comb. Twelve copper, counted out by somebody who wished it were more.

"Do not open it here," says a voice behind you. "They watch you open it and then everybody cries and it takes an hour."

The woman leaning in the gate arch has tousled blonde hair, green eyes, and the specific ease of someone who has stood in that exact spot before. She is maybe two years past her own gate day. She has an apothecary's satchel over one shoulder and flour on her sleeve.

You know her. Natsume.

"Somebody has to come and get you." Natsume Hatsuhana pushes off the arch. "Nobody came and got me. I have been fixing that ever since; it is a whole thing, do not make it a whole thing."

She looks at the bag. Then at you. Then, more carefully, at your face.

"You have got the look," she says.

"Which look."

"The one where you are remembering something that did not happen here." She says it lightly, and she says it exactly right, and she does not press. "Right. The shop needs somebody who can count and does not faint. That is the offer. It is not a big offer."

Behind you, in the dormitory window, the mattress goes over.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: you have been fighting the older kids since you were nine and winning since eleven.
• Magic Affinity: the courtyard well has always tasted of something the other children could not name.
• Profession: you have run the orphanage's accounts in your head for two years.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you remember a life with a window that opened the wrong way.
• Rebirth or Race: the gate bag has your name on it in somebody's careful hand.
🌻 Aging Out of Sunpetal Orphanage.description:
📍 Sunpetal Orphanage, Sanctum Ecclesia. A walled courtyard of sun-warmed brick, laundry lines, and too many children for the beds available.
Pace: Very gentle. A small life, chosen deliberately.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. Nothing threatens you here except the calendar. (Recommended Level 1-10)

You were born in this world and orphaned early, and you have spent your whole remembered life inside these walls with a second life rattling around behind your eyes that you have never mentioned to anyone. Today you turn eighteen, old enough that the orphanage cannot keep you. There is no ceremony. There is a bag by the gate with your name on it and a bed being stripped behind you.

🎭 Natsume Hatsuhana, Female, apothecary's assistant and orphanage graduate. Tousled blonde hair, vivid green eyes, sunny smile, simple white blouse and dark bodice. Takes symptoms and gossip in at the same counter and cross-references them.

🎐 Born to the Festival Circuit.name: 🎐 Born to the Festival Circuit
🎐 Born to the Festival Circuit.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Minato Shiohibana (male, spiky teal hair, amber eyes, colorful beads and patterned clothes, stringed instrument), Chisa Ruriiro (female, long pink-tinted hair with small flowers, rose-gold eyes). Both appear on screen and at least react. The player was born into a festival family and works the circuit. Do not generate additional named festival workers in the opening.]

Nine towns a year, every year, since before you could walk.

That is the circuit. Your family has a stall and the stall has a route and the route does not change, so you have grown up knowing nine sets of streets and nine sets of faces and belonging, in any meaningful sense, to none of them. Circuit children are friendly with everyone and close to nobody. It is not sad. It is just the shape of it.

Moonbridge is the best stop. You have thought so since you were small. The plaza fills with lanterns on cords strung between the bridge posts, the water takes the light and doubles it, and for three nights the whole coast comes here to do the thing this festival is famous for.

Moon nights are confession nights. That is the entire tradition. You come to Moonbridge, you find your person, and you say it out loud where the lanterns can hear.

Festival workers stay out of it. That is also tradition, and it is a sensible one, because a circuit family leaves in four days.

You have never once found that rule difficult.

Today, three separate people have found a reason to come to the stall.

"Four," says Minato Shiohibana, without looking up from his tuning pegs. "You have not counted the one from this morning because you decided she wanted directions."

"She did want directions."

"She asked you for directions to the bridge." He plucks a string, winces, adjusts. "She is from here. She grew up eleven streets that way. She has been crossing that bridge her entire life."

He finally looks up, amber eyes bright with the specific delight of a man who has been waiting all day to deploy this.

"Four," he says again, happily.

Across the plaza, a young woman with pink-tinted hair and small flowers pinned into it is helping string a new cord of lanterns and is doing a very poor job of it, because she keeps looking over here and losing the loop.

Chisa Ruriiro drops the cord entirely, catches it, and does not look over for a whole ten seconds afterward, which is somehow more obvious.

Out on the bridge somebody has been standing alone at the rail for the better part of an hour, watching the water, clearly waiting to say something they have rehearsed.

The first lanterns go up.

Minato sets his instrument across his knees.

"Right," he says. "So what are you going to do."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: nine towns a year teaches you which crowds are about to turn.
• Magic Affinity: the moon nights here do something to the water that only you seem to notice.
• Profession: you can strike and set a stall faster than anyone on the circuit.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you know who is going to confess tonight before they do.
• Rebirth or Race: circuit children are friendly with everyone and close to nobody.
🎐 Born to the Festival Circuit.description:
📍 Moonbridge Festival Grounds, Tsukihana Tidelace. A festival that moves along the coast all year and stops here for the moon nights, all lanterns, music, and confessions.
Pace: Light and tangled. Romance as the main quest.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. Nothing worse than embarrassment. (Recommended Level 1-10)

Your family runs a stall on the festival circuit, so you have grown up in nine towns a year and belonged to none of them. Tonight is the first moon night at Moonbridge, which is the night people confess, and by long tradition the festival workers are supposed to stay out of it. You have never had trouble with that rule before. Three separate people have found a reason to talk to you today.

🎭 Minato Shiohibana, Male, festival musician. Charismatic with spiky teal hair, amber eyes, a mischievous grin, colorful beads and patterned clothes, and a stringed instrument he is always holding. He tunes conversations like instruments and has an appetite for romantic gossip.
🎭 Chisa Ruriiro, Female, long pink-tinted hair with small flowers in it, sparkling rose-gold eyes, and a smile that makes the lanterns look dim.

❄️ Snowpetal's Winter Prophecy Child.name: ❄️ Snowpetal's Winter Prophecy Child
❄️ Snowpetal's Winter Prophecy Child.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Kosumi Hyōsetsu (female, flowing lavender-white hair, violet eyes, dark starry dress) and Hayase Fuubuki (male, messy light-brown hair, warm hazel eyes, gangly build, Moonwatch colors). Both appear on screen and react. The player was born in this village under a prophecy the whole village knows and has been waiting on for eighteen years. Do not generate additional named villagers as major characters in the opening. Everyone in this scene is an adult.]

Every household came out when you were born. All of them, in a blizzard.

You have been told this so many times, so casually, at so many meals, that you were nine years old before it occurred to you to ask whether that was normal, and the woman you asked laughed and said of course not, dear, and then changed the subject in a way you did not have the vocabulary to challenge at nine.

Snowpetal is small. Forty-one households. Steep roofs against the drift, a shrine at the top of the slope, a schoolhouse with one room and two teachers.

And a prophecy, which is four lines long, and which every single person here can recite.

It is about a child born in a particular winter, and it names three things that will follow. The first was a thaw out of season, which happened in your fourth year, and which the whole village stood outside and watched with expressions you did not understand at the time.

The second was the shrine bell cracking without being struck. That was six years ago. You were in the schoolhouse. You heard it go.

The third line is the one everyone stops reciting before they reach.

You turn eighteen this month. And last week you found out, entirely by accident, that the schoolhouse wrote to three academies on your behalf in the autumn, with letters of recommendation, describing you in terms that made your ears go hot, and that nobody thought to mention it to you because it did not occur to them that you might have an opinion.

It is not malice. That is what makes it so hard to be angry about. Every single person in this village has been kind to you for eighteen years.

They have also all been waiting.

"You found the letters," says Kosumi Hyōsetsu.

She has taken the shrine steps in the cold without a cloak, lavender-white hair moving in a way the air does not account for, and she has clearly been there some time.

You start to wonder how she knows, and let it go.

"Mm." She looks at the snow. "I did not dream it. Everyone assumes... but no. Nagi told me. She felt guilty. She has felt guilty since the autumn, which is why she has been giving you the good bread."

That lands somewhere complicated.

There is still the third line, the one nobody will say in front of you.

Kosumi's violet eyes come up and, for once, do not drift.

"Nobody knows what it means," she says. "That is the truth of it. It is four words and they have been argued about for two hundred years and everyone has decided privately what they think and nobody says it out loud because." A long pause. Snow settles on her sleeve. "Because if they say it out loud in front of you, then it is a thing they did to you."

At the bottom of the slope, a young man in Moonwatch colors is standing in the road with a travel pack at his feet, plainly having just arrived, plainly looking for someone.

Hayase Fuubuki sees you on the steps and his whole face changes with relief.

"Oh good," he calls up. "You are real."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: the schoolhouse wrote to three academies about you without asking.
• Magic Affinity: the shrine bell cracked without being struck and you heard it go.
• Profession: forty-one households and you know what every one of them owes.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: two of the three lines have happened and you were there for both.
• Rebirth or Race: the whole village came out when you were born, in a blizzard.
❄️ Snowpetal's Winter Prophecy Child.description:
📍 Snowpetal Village, Yukishiro Veilpeak. A small mountain village of steep roofs and deep drifts, with a shrine, a schoolhouse, and one very specific old story.
Pace: Warm and unsettling. Everyone is kind and everyone is waiting.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. Nobody here will harm you. (Recommended Level 1-10)

You were born in this village and the entire village turned out for it, which you did not learn was strange until you were nine. There is a prophecy. It is short; it is old; it is about a child born in a particular winter, and it names three things that will happen. Two have happened. You are eighteen this month, and the schoolhouse has already written to the academies on your behalf without asking you.

🎭 Kosumi Hyōsetsu, Female, dream mage and village seer. Dreamy with flowing lavender-white hair, violet eyes, and a gentle expression, in a dark starry dress. She speaks in fragments and trailing sentences that drift like snowfall, thoughts arriving half-formed.
🎭 Hayase Fuubuki, Male, twenty, gentle-faced with messy light-brown hair, warm hazel eyes, and a lanky frame, in Moonwatch colors.

🦅 Chosen by the Rogue Griffin of Griffin.name: 🦅 Chosen by the Rogue Griffin of Griffinheart Roost
🦅 Chosen by the Rogue Griffin of Griffin.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Mei Kumotsuki (female, lithe, short silver-white hair, soft amber eyes, leather and fur-lined canvas handler uniform) and Takamaru Yagami (male, winged, tousled dark hair with a white streak in the bangs, blue eyes, rugged leather gear). Both appear on screen and react. The player has been spontaneously bonded by a griffin that rejected three approved candidates, and has no standing at the Roost. Do not generate additional named handlers in the opening. Everyone in this scene is an adult.]

She is asleep against your leg and has been for about forty minutes, and you have not moved, because the last time you moved it opened one eye.

The nesting ledges run along the cliff in tiers, cut back into the rock and roofed with turf, and the wind comes up the face all day so that everything on the Roost smells like cold stone and feathers. Below the ledge you are sitting on there is a very long way down and then the Reaches.

Yesterday you were here as a spectator. That is the entire extent of your business at this place. A carter you had cadged a ride from was delivering feed, and you helped unload it, and you stood at the back of the yard to watch a bonding trial because everyone else was watching.

Three candidates. All approved, all tested, all from families who have done this for generations. Each one went up to the ledge and did the thing they were supposed to do, and the griffin, a big grey-and-bronze female, looked at each of them the way you would look at furniture.

Then she came down off the high ledge. Past the first candidate. Past the second. Past the handlers, who were saying her name in the calm voices people use when something is going wrong.

Across the yard. Past the feed carts.

And she put her head against your chest, and made a sound that the handlers tell you she has never made, and that was that.

"You are still not moving," says Mei Kumotsuki.

She has been on the ledge lip six feet away most of the night, arms around her knees, silver-white hair flat to her head in the wind, and she has been there most of the night. The handler uniform is fur-lined at the collar and worn through at both elbows.

The griffin opens one eye.

"She does that. It signifies nothing." A pause. "That is not why you are not moving."

"No."

Mei nods, satisfied, and goes back to watching the griffin rather than you.

"There is no procedure," she says eventually. "That is what the yard has been arguing about since yesterday. There is a procedure for a failed bonding and a procedure for a bond breaking when a rider dies. There is nothing for this. Nobody wrote one, because it does not happen."

"What do the families say?"

"They say a great deal." Her amber eyes flick to you, briefly, and there is something bracing in them. "They will keep saying it. You should know now that I am not going to be much help with the people part. I am good at this part."

She tips her head at the sleeping griffin.

On the ledge above, a young man with wings folded back and a white streak in his dark hair drops into a crouch on the rock, entirely at ease four hundred feet up, and grins down at you.

"So," says Takamaru Yagami. "You are the scandal."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: she came to you past three trained candidates and you were carrying feed sacks.
• Magic Affinity: the roost's updraft is not entirely weather and you noticed on arrival.
• Profession: you helped unload because idle hands bother you, and that is why you were in the yard.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: she made a sound the handlers say she has never made.
• Rebirth or Race: the bonding families have opinions and are already writing them down.
🦅 Chosen by the Rogue Griffin of Griffin.description:
📍 Griffinheart Roost, Aetherglass Reaches. A cliff of nesting ledges where griffins are raised, bonded, and very occasionally refuse to cooperate.
Pace: Warm and stubborn. A bond you did not ask for and cannot return.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. The griffins are trained. The politics are not. (Recommended Level 1-10)

Bonding is done by bloodline, by testing, and by the handlers, in that order, and it takes years. Yesterday a griffin that has refused three approved candidates in a row came down off the high ledges, walked past all of them, and put its head against your chest. The Roost is now dealing with a bond it did not authorize, involving a person with no standing, and nobody can undo it because nobody has ever needed to.

🎭 Mei Kumotsuki, Female, griffin handler. Lithe with short silver-white hair, soft amber eyes, and the quiet alertness of someone who reads animal body language for a living, in the Roost's leather and fur-lined canvas handler uniform. Gentle with griffins, briskly impatient with people, and she does not consider that a flaw.
🎭 Takamaru Yagami, Male, winged with tousled dark hair with a white streak in the bangs, blue eyes, a reckless grin, and rugged leather gear in brown, beige and white.

🦌 Four Spirit Beasts Waiting at the Glad.name: 🦌 Four Spirit Beasts Waiting at the Glade
🦌 Four Spirit Beasts Waiting at the Glad.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Midori Tsukino (Female, elder elf and keeper of the Spirit Beast Glade, alive since before the current borders were drawn), Shion Tsukinoshizuku (Female, twenty, spirit medium studying the glade's luminous creatures, serene and slightly delayed). All of them appear on screen and at least react. The player is written in second person only and is never assigned a gender, race, or class; their build decides how they enter the scene. Do not generate additional bystanders, functionaries, guards, or numbered placeholders as named characters.]

Four. That number has not changed in six days and you have checked it more often than you want to admit.

They were at the treeline when you came through, already waiting, in the specific arrangement of creatures that have agreed among themselves who stands where. They did not approach. They fell in. And when you stopped walking they stopped walking, and when you slept they arranged themselves around the place you slept, and when you tried, twice, to leave before dawn, they were simply ahead of you on the path.

The glade at dusk is where the rangers said to bring them, and now you understand why. The clearing runs down to a threshold where the light goes strange, and the spirit beasts come in as the sun drops, dozens of them, luminous and unhurried, and the whole place lights from the ground up.

Your four came in with you and then stopped at the edge, together, and turned to face the glade rather than entering it. Which everybody here appears to find significant.

"They are not glade-born," says the elder, from a stump she has almost certainly been sitting on since before the border was drawn. "That is the first thing. Whatever they are, they did not come from here, and they are being extremely polite about it."

Midori Tsukino does not look old so much as continuous.

"So where did they come from?"

"They came from wherever they were before they decided." She says it entirely without mystery, as a matter of record. "I have kept this threshold for a long time and I have seen the Wilds attach itself to eleven people. Two of them were rangers. One was a child who wandered in. None of them were asked first, and none of them could give it back."

Nearer the threshold, a young woman has been crouched with one hand out for several minutes, and now she straightens and comes over with an expression of careful concentration.

"They will not tell me why," Shion Tsukinoshizuku says, in the slightly delayed way of someone translating as she goes. "I asked properly. That usually works." She glances back at the four. "They answered, but the answer was not about you. It was about a direction. They keep giving me a direction and a distance and I do not think either of those is here."

"They want to go somewhere."

"They want you to go somewhere, you specifically," Midori says, "which is a different sentence, and it is the one the rangers were too polite to say." She stands, without any particular effort. "Here is what I can offer. The glade will feed them tonight. It will not feed them tomorrow, because they are not its business, and by dusk tomorrow you will be the only source of anything they need."

The largest of the four shifts its weight and the ground reports it.

Shion is still frowning at the direction.

"North and a little east," she says. "And it is not a place. It is a distance from you. It moves when you move."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: the four arranged themselves in a formation on the first night and it is a good one.
• Magic Affinity: you felt the glade decide something the moment you crossed the threshold behind them.
• Profession: you have been feeding four creatures for six days and you know exactly what that has cost you.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: they were waiting at the treeline before you chose that path, and you chose it at random.
• Rebirth or Race: Midori has counted eleven in her lifetime, and she has been looking at you since you said hello.
🦌 Four Spirit Beasts Waiting at the Glad.description:
📍 Spirit Beast Glade, Verdania Wilds. A threshold clearing where luminous spirit beasts gather at dusk, watched over by an elder elf and studied, carefully, by those the glade permits.
Pace: Hushed and decided. Something has chosen and is waiting for you to catch up.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Nothing in the glade will harm you. What follows you out might frighten a village. (Recommended Level 1-28)

Four of them were waiting at the treeline when you came through, and they have not left. Not tamed, not summoned, not bargained for: simply arrived, and settled, and entirely unwilling to be anywhere else. The Wilds do this occasionally, the rangers say, to people the forest has formed an opinion about. Nobody can tell you what the opinion is. The largest of the four does not fit through any door you have tried, and dusk is coming, and the glade is filling up.

🎭 Midori Tsukino, Female, elder elf and keeper of the Spirit Beast Glade, alive since before the current borders were drawn, who has outlived more people than most will meet and still finds the world worth attending to.
🎭 Shion Tsukinoshizuku, Female, twenty, spirit medium studying the glade's luminous creatures, serene and slightly delayed, most fluent when relaying what the beasts are saying.

🐺 Clanless in the Trial Ring.name: 🐺 Clanless in the Trial Ring
🐺 Clanless in the Trial Ring.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Kiba Tetsurō (male, muscular, wolf-eared, shaggy silver hair, golden eyes, fur cloak over armor plates) and Reika Silverfang (female, wolfkin, silver-gray ears and tail, sharp amber eyes, ash-silver hair, faint scar across one cheekbone, leather hunting gear). Both appear on screen and react. The player woke recently in a beastkin body with no clan and no explanation. Do not generate additional named clan members in the opening.]

Packed earth, swept flat, ringed by roots thicker than your waist.

You have been standing at the edge of it for a while now, and you have spent most of that time managing your own body. The ears turn toward sounds before you decide to look. The tail has opinions. Your sense of smell has become an unbearable amount of information, and you have learned in four days that the polite thing to do is pretend you cannot smell any of it.

Beastkin are born. Everyone has told you this. Born, bloodline, generations, a whole architecture of family that you fell into the middle of without a single thread connecting you to it.

So you are clanless, which is not an insult here. It is a category. It has a procedure.

The procedure is the ring.

"Stop thinking."

The man crossing the ring toward you is built like a door and moves like something much quicker than a door. Shaggy silver hair, wolf ears up and forward, golden eyes, a fur cloak thrown back off one shoulder over armor plates that have been repaired more than once. He stops closer than a stranger should stand, and does not seem to notice that he has.

"You smell wrong," says Kiba Tetsurō. It is not hostile. He says it the way you would remark on weather. "Wolf. But new. Like a coat somebody just put on."

He waits, and seems to find his answer in your face.

He grins, wide and entirely delighted, and something in the set of his shoulders drops out of assessment and into welcome.

"Good." He steps back one pace, which somehow reads as generous. "Ring is simple. You stand. Someone comes. You do not have to win."

"I do not have to win."

"You have to still be standing in your own way when it stops." He taps two fingers against his sternum. "That is the whole test. Everyone gets it wrong the first time because they think it is about the fighting."

From the far side, a woman drops out of the roots and lands without sound. Ash-silver hair, wind-tangled. Amber eyes that go over you once, top to bottom, and miss nothing. A thin old scar across one cheekbone.

Reika Silverfang folds her arms.

"He is telling you it is easy," she says. "It is not easy. He has just forgotten, because he was six."

Kiba's ears flick back, briefly, and he does not argue.

The roots are filling with people. Nobody is jeering. That is somehow worse.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: the new body already knows how to fight and you did not teach it.
• Magic Affinity: you can smell the ward-lines drawn around the ring.
• Profession: you notice the ring is swept in a pattern, and the pattern is a record.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: your ears turned toward the challenge before it was spoken.
• Rebirth or Race: everyone here can tell you are wearing this shape rather than born to it.
🐺 Clanless in the Trial Ring.description:
📍 Silverfang Trial Grounds, Verdania Wilds. A packed-earth ring under old trees where the wolf clans settle everything that matters.
Pace: Physical and direct. Earn a place or leave without one.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Nothing here wants you dead. Several things want you humbled. (Recommended Level 1-30)

You went to sleep human. You woke up with ears that move on their own, a tail you keep sitting on, and senses that will not turn down. Beastkin are born, not made, and no clan on the continent has a story that explains you. The Silverfang have a tradition for people with no clan, and it involves standing in that ring.

🎭 Kiba Tetsurō, Male, Silverfang warrior. Muscular and wolf-eared, shaggy silver hair, golden eyes, cocky grin, fur cloak over armor plates. Speaks in short physical sentences and does most of his real communicating with proximity and posture.
🎭 Reika Silverfang, Female, athletic wolfkin with silver-gray ears and tail, sharp amber eyes, wind-tousled ash-silver hair, a faint scar across one cheekbone, practical leather hunting gear.

🦊 Midnight Bargain at Foxfire Shrine.name: 🦊 Midnight Bargain at Foxfire Shrine
🦊 Midnight Bargain at Foxfire Shrine.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Kohana Kōen (female, fox-eared, vivid red hair, amber eyes, red-and-white shrine robes) and Koi Yuzuha (female, fox-eared, long honey-blonde hair, golden eyes, fitted black dress with white sleeves, fluffy tail). Both appear on screen and react. The player made an unremembered bargain with a fox at a crossroads and now owes an unspecified debt. Do not generate additional named shrine staff in the opening.]

There are one hundred and eleven lanterns at the Foxfire gate. You counted them twice while waiting for someone to come out, and got a different number both times.

The forest behind you is doing its early evening business, insects and settling leaves and the occasional crack of something large enough to be a deer. The road you came in on is not visible from here, which is interesting, because you can see the whole clearing.

You remember being lost. That part is solid. Cold, and increasingly stupid about it, walking a road that kept arriving at the same fallen tree.

You remember a fox.

It sat squarely in the road with its tail curled over its feet and it did not run, and it asked you, in a perfectly ordinary voice, what you would give to stop being lost.

And you answered.

That is the part that will not come back. You know your mouth moved. You know you said something specific, because the fox tipped its head as if writing it down.

Then the road was straight, and short, and it ended here.

"Ohh," says somebody, delighted. "You are the one from Tuesday."

A woman has appeared at the gate without using any of the approaches that exist. Fox ears up, vivid red hair, amber eyes, red-and-white robes that are a shrine attendant's if you do not look at the stitching. She is holding a rice ball in one hand and appears to have forgotten about it.

It is not Tuesday. Your face must say so.

"It was when the arrangement was made, so it is a Tuesday sort of debt, that is just how these are filed, oh do not make that face, everyone makes that face." Kohana Kōen circles you once, entirely without embarrassment, sniffing thoughtfully. "Hm. You are not marked heavy. That is good. Heavy is bad. Heavy is when people come back with someone else's shadow."

"What did I promise."

She stops. The knowing smile stays exactly where it is, and does not reach the amber eyes at all.

"That," she says, gently, "is between you and the one who asked, and I am not her."

From the shrine steps, a second fox-eared woman leans into view with a lantern in her hand and honey-blonde hair spilling over a black dress. She takes one look at you, and her cheerful expression falters in a way that Kohana notices and does not comment on.

"Oh," says Koi Yuzuha. "Oh, that one."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: you have kept one hand free since the crossroads without deciding to.
• Magic Affinity: the hundred and eleven lanterns are not all burning the same fire.
• Profession: the offerings at the gate are fresh, expensive, and left by somebody with taste.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: the road straightened for you, and you felt it happen.
• Rebirth or Race: the fox spoke to you in a language you should not have understood.
🦊 Midnight Bargain at Foxfire Shrine.description:
📍 Foxfire Shrine, Verdania Wilds. A red-lantern shrine at a forest crossroads where the offerings are always fresh and nobody admits to leaving them.
Pace: Uneasy. Every kindness has a price tag you cannot read.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Nothing will attack you. Everything will negotiate. (Recommended Level 1-10)

You were lost; it was dark, and a fox sat down on the road in front of you and asked what you would give to not be lost anymore. You said something. You are no longer certain what. You woke at the shrine gate with dry clothes, a full stomach, and the distinct understanding that a book has been opened in your name.

🎭 Kohana Kōen, Female, shrine attendant. Fox-eared with vivid red hair, amber eyes, and a soft knowing smile, in red-and-white shrine robes under lantern light. Talks as though punctuation is optional, and her answers loop sideways before arriving somewhere you did not ask about.
🎭 Koi Yuzuha, Female, fox-eared and cheerful, long honey-blonde hair, golden eyes, fitted black dress with white sleeves, one fluffy tail.

🛡️ Rash Oath to the Royal Knights.name: 🛡️ Rash Oath to the Royal Knights
🛡️ Rash Oath to the Royal Knights.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Shin Kagetsuki (male, loose messy black hair over his face, pale blue eyes, calm and melancholic, layered black clothing and leather gloves). He appears on screen and speaks. The player swore the Order's oath at the gate under expedient rather than noble circumstances and is newly sworn.]

Oaths here are administered at the gate, standing, in under a minute, which tells you most of what you need to know about how many the Order has taken this year.

You said the words. You meant roughly a third of them. The officer watched your face the entire time and did not appear to mind, which was worse than being caught.

Thornwall sits on the road with the capital behind it and the frontier ahead, and everything about the keep is built to make that geography feel like a duty rather than a location. The walls are old. The gate is newer. The banners are clean, which somebody does.

You have a longsword you have not earned, two healing potions from a quartermaster who counted them out loud, and a place on a rota that already had your name pencilled in before you arrived.

The pencil is the part that keeps returning to you.

"You are on the second watch," says Shin Kagetsuki.

He is in the gatehouse arch where he has apparently been for some time, black on black, gloves on, pale eyes on the road rather than on you. He does not turn.

"Second watch is the cold one," he says. "It is also the one where nothing happens, which is why they give it to new blades. If something happens on second watch, you will be the only person awake who saw it."

A pause.

"That is not a warning. It is the rota."

A cart goes past on the road below, unhurried, heading capital-ward. He tracks it the whole way without appearing to.

"You did not want the oath," Shin says. "You wanted the gate."

He finally looks over. There is nothing accusing in it at all, which is somehow harder to answer.

"Most of us wanted something else first," he says. "The Order does not mind. It only asks what you want now, and it asks the question slowly, over about a year."

He returns to the road.

"Morning bell," he says. "You have until then."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: they handed you a blade and nobody has asked yet whether you can use it.
• Magic Affinity: the keep's old wards run under the gatehouse and one of them is failing.
• Profession: you have already spotted what the quartermaster's count is missing.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you meant a third of the oath and something in you took all of it.
• Rebirth or Race: your name was pencilled on the rota before you reached the gate.
🛡️ Rash Oath to the Royal Knights.description:
📍 Thornwall Keep, Crownveil Sovereignty. Headquarters of the Royal Knight Order, a fortress on the road between the capital and the frontier.
Pace: Disciplined. Duty, rota, and the politics under both.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. No major hostile encounters in the keep itself. (Recommended Level 1-25)

You took the oath at the gate because it was the fastest way through it. That is not a good reason and the officer who administered it knew, and administered it anyway, because the Order is eleven blades short and has been all year. You are now sworn. The oath is real whether or not you meant it, and Thornwall has a way of finding out which.

🎭 Shin Kagetsuki, Male, gatehouse watch. Loose messy black hair falling over his face, pale blue eyes, a calm melancholic expression, layered black clothing and leather gloves. He reports rather than converses, and strips every sentence of anything unnecessary.

👊 Unsponsored at the Oni Dojo.name: 👊 Unsponsored at the Oni Dojo
👊 Unsponsored at the Oni Dojo.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Kouga Yakiba (male, muscular, spiky black hair, fierce gold eyes, scarred knuckles, training wraps, oni-mark tattoo) and Akane Onigiri (female, long crimson hair, single deep red horn, glowing amber eyes). Both appear on screen and react. The player arrived unsponsored, asked to be taught, and has received no answer either way. Everyone in this scene is an adult.]

Your name is chalked on the third platform and nobody has told you what that means.

Oni Thunder is loud. That is the first thing, the second thing and most of the third. Somewhere behind you a pair are going at full contact and being cheered by people who are supposed to be stretching. A drum marks something that is either a count or a meal. The heat comes up through the boards from a mountain that has never entirely settled.

Every other student here arrived with a letter. A clan behind them, a compact, a master vouching in writing. That is how you get onto these platforms.

You walked up the road and knocked.

The woman who opened the gate laughed for a genuinely long time, then went and got somebody, who also laughed, and then chalked your name on the third platform and walked away without a single word of instruction.

That was two hours ago. You have been standing on your own name since.

"You have not moved," says Kouga Yakiba.

He has come up the platform steps at a pace that suggests he does everything at this pace. Gold eyes, wrapped hands, knuckles that have made an argument with stone and won. The oni-mark on his forearm is catching light it should not be catching.

"Two hours," he says. "Most unsponsored leave in one. A few sit down. You stood."

He rolls his shoulder.

"That is the test," he says. "There was never going to be a letter. There was going to be a platform, and however long you were willing to stand on it."

"Kouga." Akane Onigiri is on the next platform with her arms folded and her horn catching the forge light, and she is not lowering her voice because she does not have one. "You are explaining it. You always explain it."

"They stood two hours."

"Then spar them and stop talking." She grins, wide and entirely without malice. "Full strength, or it does not count and you know it does not count."

Kouga looks back at you and his stance has already changed.

"She is right," he says. "It does not count."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: you already read the stance change and your weight moved to answer it.
• Magic Affinity: the mountain under these boards has not settled and you can feel the pressure of it.
• Profession: the platform boards were replaced recently, and badly, on the third one.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: two hours standing and you are not tired, which is starting to be noticeable.
• Rebirth or Race: you knocked at a gate that has never once opened for someone unsponsored.
👊 Unsponsored at the Oni Dojo.description:
📍 Oni Thunder Dojo, Kagutsuchi Emberwake. A loud, passionate martial school where duels, feasts and confessions happen with equal intensity and equal volume.
Pace: Physical and immediate. You are tested before you are taught.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Nobody wants you dead. Several people want you humbled. (Recommended Level 3-30)

Every student here was sponsored: a clan, a compact, a master's letter. You walked up the mountain road, knocked, and asked to be taught, which the dojo finds either insulting or hilarious depending on who you ask. Nobody has said no. Nobody has said yes either. There is a platform with your name chalked on it and no explanation of what happens next.

🎭 Kouga Yakiba, Male, senior student. Muscular with spiky black hair, fierce gold eyes, and the scarred knuckles of someone who punches volcanic stone for practice, in training wraps and loose martial pants, his oni-mark tattoo glowing faintly when he exerts himself. Blunt and loud, fluent about technique and bad at everything else.
🎭 Akane Onigiri, Female, oni-blooded fighter. Long crimson hair, a single deep red horn, glowing amber eyes, tanned skin lit by nearby flame. Talks at full volume with her whole body and treats personal space as a rumor.

⚔️ Conscripted at Riftwatch.name: ⚔️ Conscripted at Riftwatch
⚔️ Conscripted at Riftwatch.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Dr. Yua Sakima (female, Veilwalker researcher), Ryoma Enjō (male, muscular, red hair, amber eyes, leather-and-metal gear), and Sir Caelum Tsukiken (male, knight of the Moonwatch Order). All three appear on screen and at least react. The player arrived in this world within the last day and has been conscripted into the watch under frontier law. Do not generate additional named soldiers in the opening.]

A sound. Nobody warned you about that.

It is not loud. It is under the wind, a low continuous note like a held breath, and once you have noticed it you cannot stop hearing it, and everyone on this platform has clearly gone through the same three days you are currently on day one of.

Riftwatch Camp is timber and iron bolted onto a ridge, four platforms and a rope ladder, and everything on it faces the same direction. Below and east, the Ashenmere Frontier goes on in grey and rust until it reaches the place where the sky has come apart, and the light there does not match the light anywhere else.

You arrived in this world yesterday. You know that because a patrol found you inside the perimeter eleven hours ago, and the sergeant who found you did not ask a single question about where you came from. He asked for papers. You had none.

Frontier law is one sentence long and it fits on a board by the mess.

So now you have a bunk, a ration card with your assigned number on it, a rota with your name spelled wrong, and a longsword that somebody else carried until recently.

"You are holding it wrong, but that is fine, everyone holds it wrong, the grip is a training artifact rather than an ergonomic solution which is a whole argument I have had with the quartermaster four times."

The woman has arrived beside you without you noticing, which on a platform this size takes doing. She has a satchel of instruments, ink on three fingers, and the specific energy of somebody who has been awake longer than is advisable.

"Sakima," she says. "Doctor. Yua. Any of those." She is already looking at your hands rather than your face. "You came through in the last day."

It is not a question.

"How do you know that."

"Because you are still hearing it." She points, without looking, east. "You keep tilting your head. People stop tilting their head at about the fourth day, we do not know why, I have a theory and nobody will fund it."

Across the platform, a red-haired man in scarred leather looks up from a whetstone and grins at you with an alarming amount of warmth for a complete stranger.

And at the rail, a knight in Moonwatch colors is watching the rift with his hands behind his back, and when he turns and sees you he does not look surprised at all.

Sir Caelum Tsukiken smiles as though something long expected has finally arrived on schedule.

"There," he says. "I told them."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: the sergeant put a longsword in your hands and did not ask whether you could use it.
• Magic Affinity: the rift's note sits at exactly the pitch your affinity answers to.
• Profession: you have already spotted three structural problems with this platform.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you were found inside the perimeter, unhurt, which nobody can explain.
• Rebirth or Race: you are still tilting your head at the sound, which marks you as new.
⚔️ Conscripted at Riftwatch.description:
📍 Riftwatch Camp, Ashenmere Frontier. A timber platform camp bolted to a ridge overlooking a tear in the world that nobody has closed.
Pace: Harsh. Duty rosters, short rations, and a horizon that moves.
Danger: 🟠 Dangerous. A punishing opening. Not recommended for a first run. (Recommended Level 1-10)

You fell into the Ashenmere Frontier and were picked up by a patrol within the hour, which was extremely lucky, and then conscripted on the spot, which was not. Frontier law is short: anyone found without papers inside the watch perimeter is assigned to it. You have a bunk, a ration card, a rota, and no way to leave that does not involve the rift.

🎭 Dr. Yua Sakima, Female, Veilwalker researcher attached to the camp. Rapid-fire academic delivery that accelerates under stress, sentences long and parenthetical and sometimes abandoned mid-thought. She argues that the Reborn are people rather than anomalies, loses those arguments, and keeps having them.
🎭 Ryoma Enjō, Male, muscular and red-haired with amber eyes and a confident grin, rugged leather-and-metal gear.
🎭 Sir Caelum Tsukiken, Male, a knight whose conviction carries expectations, and who has already assigned you a role in a story he has written without consulting you.

🕯️ Last Stand at Greyhaven Village.name: 🕯️ Last Stand at Greyhaven Village
🕯️ Last Stand at Greyhaven Village.description:
📍 Greyhaven, Crownveil Sovereignty. A frontier village on the war road beyond Lastlight Bridge, the first Crown stop after the crossing: officially protected Crown territory, functionally left to fend for itself.
Pace: Quiet desperation. Soldiers pass through; nobody stays. What you do here, you do because no one else will.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. The village is safe by day. The outlying roads are not, and the night belongs to the raiders. (Recommended Level 5-25)

You came up the bridge-road to Greyhaven like everyone else lately, looking for the last safe stop before the frontier, and found a village the war has quietly abandoned. The Crown requisitions its grain and posts no guard. The Church's patrols eye every newcomer for corruption. Twilight raiders burn the outer farms at night. And in the middle of it, a tavern that still lights its lamps and an innkeeper who still feeds the frightened first. Nobody is coming to save Greyhaven. That leaves you.

🎭 Otoha Suzukake, Female, keeper of the Lastlight Inn and Greyhaven's stubborn warm heart. Feeds refugees first and asks about coin never, hears everything said in her common room, and has quietly counted exactly how much the fort takes versus what it admits to.
🎭 Genta Aramaki, Male, captain of the village's ragtag militia, doing the Crown's job unpaid because the Crown's soldiers only pass through. Underarmed, exhausted, and trusted by everyone in Greyhaven.
🎭 Inquisitor Kōsei Yomikawa, Male, an Ecclesian corruption-hunter whose patrols pass through Greyhaven eyeing the refugees. Skilled, certain, and not here to comfort anyone.
🕯️ Last Stand at Greyhaven Village.storyStart:
[The player has just arrived in Greyhaven, a Crown frontier village left to fend for itself; they are new here and unattached. Otoha Suzukake (Lastlight Inn keeper) greets them warmly and may offer food and lodging. She is a local host at the Lastlight Inn, not a starting traveling party member. Any later recruitment must follow an explicit player choice and her agreement; Genta Aramaki (militia captain), the villagers, any Crown soldiers passing through, Ecclesian patrols (Inquisitor Kōsei Yomikawa), and Twilight scouts near the outlying farms are drawn from the authored roster. Do not force a raid or emergency into the opening; the village's quiet abandonment is the premise, and any trouble should build from the player's choices. Keep incidental refugees and soldiers unnamed and descriptive.]

The lamps of the Lastlight Inn are lit against an afternoon that has no business being this grey, and they are, you will realize later, the first genuinely warm thing you have seen since the bridge.

You came up the frontier road the way everyone comes lately: too tired, too watchful, looking for the last dependable stop before Ashenmere swallows the map. Greyhaven was supposed to be that stop. The signposts still call it protected Crown territory. The reality is a main street rutted by supply wagons that never unload here, houses with storm-damage nobody has the timber to fix, a market with more empty stalls than full ones, and a column of Crown knights that rode straight through this morning without so much as slowing, on their way to a fort that matters more.

Inside, the inn is half-full of people who look like you feel. A round woman with flour on her sleeves is already moving toward you before the door has finished closing, reading your road-worn state with one practiced glance.

"Sit," says Otoha Suzukake, in the tone of a woman who has never once lost an argument about whether someone should eat. "You'll have the stew. We'll talk about coin later, which means never, so don't insult us both by reaching for it."

She sets down a bowl before you have agreed to any of this. Across the room, a broad, tired man with a scarred forearm and a plow-iron sword nods at you once, the wary courtesy of someone who has learned that new faces in Greyhaven are usually either another mouth to feed or, very occasionally, help. Outside the window, the war road runs empty back toward Lastlight Bridge, and past it, somewhere south, the war goes on being the reason this village is dying politely.

Nobody here is going to ask you to save anything. That is the whole tragedy of the place. They have stopped expecting it.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: the militia captain's eyes keep going to the way you carry yourself, and then to the empty watch-roster on the wall.
• Magic Affinity: something in the wards along the village edge is failing, and you felt it fray as you crossed in.
• Profession: the market is being bled by predatory prices and requisition both, and you can already see three ways to keep it alive.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: the innkeeper's welcome was real, but the way the Church patrol looked at you on the road was not, and you understand exactly why.
• Rebirth or Race: you came up the same road as the refugees, and whatever followed some of them out of Ashenmere, you can feel it in the room.

🛡️ Sworn to the Line at Dawnsward.name: 🛡️ Sworn to the Line at Dawnsward
🛡️ Sworn to the Line at Dawnsward.description:
📍 Fort Dawnsward, Crownveil Sovereignty. The fortress guarding the southern road to Aureliath, run on one iron rule: the fort must not fall.
Pace: Grim and immediate. A war with a wall around it, and you are now inside the wall.
Danger: 🟠 High on sortie, moderate within. The fort holds; the ground it watches does not. (Recommended Level 15-40)

You signed on to the line at Fort Dawnsward, the last hard point before the Twilight advance turns into a road to the Crownlands. Whether you came as a Guild contractor, a fresh sword, or someone with nowhere better to be, the arithmetic is the same the moment the gate closes behind you: if this fort falls, the war comes north. The commander believes that absolutely, and justifies nearly everything by it. The garrison is brave, exhausted, and rougher on the frontier villages than anyone will say aloud. And the supply wagons that keep it all running do not quite add up, if you are the sort to count.

🎭 Commander Ayaka Tategami, Female, the officer holding Dawnsward together with discipline and borrowed honor. Decides fast, spends her honor buying the fort another week, and knows the requisition numbers don't balance.
🎭 Genta Aramaki, Male, a Greyhaven militia captain who comes to the fort to beg for escorts that never come; the friction between the fort and the villages it bleeds walks in with him.
🎭 Envoy Rui Yamibuchi, Female, a Twilight envoy whose quiet offers reach even inside Crown walls: land and title for anyone willing to open a gate one night.
🛡️ Sworn to the Line at Dawnsward.storyStart:
[The player has just taken service at Fort Dawnsward, a Crownveil fortress under real siege pressure; they are new to the garrison and unattached. Commander Ayaka Tategami (on the wall / in the war room) receives them and sets the stakes; the garrison, Genta Aramaki (visiting from Greyhaven), and any Twilight envoys or scouts are drawn from the authored roster. Do not force an assault into the opening; the grinding pressure and the moral cost of 'the fort must not fall' are the premise, and combat should build from the player's choices. Keep rank-and-file soldiers unnamed and descriptive.]

The gate of Fort Dawnsward closes behind you with a sound like a decision being made, and a sergeant with no time for ceremony walks you across a yard that is busier and hungrier than a fort this size should be.

They are glad to have you. That is the first thing you notice, and it is not reassuring. Glad the way people are glad of one more pair of hands on a rope that is already slipping. Every wall has someone on it. Every face has the specific tiredness of people who have been holding the same line long enough to stop believing relief is coming, and who hold it anyway because the alternative is a road straight to Aureliath with nothing on it.

The commander finds you on the curtain wall, because the commander is always where the work is. Iron-grey hair cropped short, a Crown officer's coat kept immaculate against all reason, and eyes that finish assessing you before you have finished saluting.

"You know why this fort matters or you wouldn't have signed," says Commander Ayaka Tategami, not unkindly, watching the southern road rather than you. "So I'll spare you the speech. If Dawnsward falls, Twilight gets a paved road into the Crownlands. Everything we do here, everything, is measured against that. Some of what we do you will not like. Some of it I do not like." A pause, exactly as long as it needs to be. "Do the job in front of you and we'll get along. Ask the right questions and we might even do some good. Ask the wrong ones loudly and you'll learn how heavy that phrase gets: the fort must not fall."

Below, in the requisition yard, clerks are logging wagons of grain that came up from villages that could not spare it. Beyond the wall, south, the ground the fort watches is somebody else's graveyard. And somewhere in this fortress is a set of books that would explain why the numbers never match, if anyone dared open them.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: the commander has already slotted you for the next sortie, and the next sortie is where Dawnsward loses people.
• Magic Affinity: the fort's wards are thinning on the southern face, and you are the only one who has said so out loud.
• Profession: one afternoon in the requisition yard and the numbers are already wrong in a way that smells deliberate.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: something about you reads on the Church liaison's instruments, and Dawnsward cannot afford to lose you to a purge, yet.
• Rebirth or Race: you have seen how this kind of siege ends before, in another life or another war, and the ending is already visible in the supply books.

❄️ Unvowed Initiate at Shirogane Monaste.name: ❄️ Unvowed Initiate at Shirogane Monastery
❄️ Unvowed Initiate at Shirogane Monaste.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Rei Hakurei (female, long black hair, violet eyes, composed, red-and-white shrine garments) and Shrine Mother Hakurei (female, voluminous white-blue hair, pale blue eyes, white robes). Both appear on screen and at least react. The player climbed to the monastery, answered the gate question poorly, was admitted anyway, and is in their first week with no vows taken.]

Above the cloud line the light is wrong. Brighter than it should be, and colder, and it does not move the way light moves lower down.

Shirogane sits on a shelf of rock with the whole Veilpeak beneath it, and on a clear morning the clouds are a floor you could be forgiven for stepping onto. The meditation halls are open on one side to all of that, deliberately, because the disciplines here are cold, silence and precision, and the mountain teaches the first one for free.

You climbed for two days. At the gate a woman asked you one question.

You have replayed your answer perhaps forty times. It was not clever. It was not even complete. You said you did not know, and then you kept standing there, and she looked at you for a while and then stood aside.

Candidates take vows in the fourth year. You have been here six days.

And somebody has written your name on the dawn roster, in a hand you have not identified, between two people who have been here since they were children.

"You are cold," says Rei Hakurei.

She is at the open side of the hall in a seiza that has clearly not shifted in an hour, black hair perfectly still, violet eyes on the cloud floor rather than on you. She has not looked over once.

"You are also standing in the doorway," she says, "which is the coldest part of this building, and you have chosen it three mornings running. That is not discipline. That is not wanting to commit to the room."

A pause exactly long enough to be deliberate.

"Come in or go out," Rei says. "Both are answers. The doorway is not."

From the inner hall, without any sound of approach, another voice arrives.

"She is quoting me," says Shrine Mother Hakurei, pleasantly. "Badly, and with better posture than I ever managed."

The Shrine Mother comes as far as the pillar and no further. White-blue hair, pale eyes, hands folded.

"You said you did not know," she says. "At the gate. Do you remember what you did after that?"

You do. You stood there.

"You did not fill it," she says. "Almost everyone fills it. That is why the gate opened, and it is the only reason, and I am telling you now because you have spent six days assuming it was a mistake."

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: sword saints train here and your hands have been restless for six days.
• Magic Affinity: the cold above the cloud line is maintained, not weather, and you can feel the working.
• Profession: the monastery runs on supply hauls you have already worked out are running short.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you climbed two days in the wrong clothes and did not freeze.
• Rebirth or Race: you said you did not know, and the gate opened for exactly that.
❄️ Unvowed Initiate at Shirogane Monaste.description:
📍 Shirogane Monastery, Yukishiro Veilpeak. A mountain temple above the clouds where sword saints, paladins and frost monks train in the disciplines of cold, silence and absolute precision.
Pace: Still and exacting. The tests do not look like tests.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. The monastery is peaceful. The climb is not. (Recommended Level 22-36)

You climbed for two days and were asked one question at the gate. You answered it badly and were let in anyway, which has been bothering you ever since. Candidates here take vows in their fourth year. You are in your first week, you have no vows, no discipline and no cold tolerance, and somebody has already put your name on the dawn roster.

🎭 Rei Hakurei, Female, a senior student. Long black hair, violet eyes, a composed face, red-and-white shrine garments. Training-hall economy in everything until sweets enter the room, at which point her discipline stops being total.
🎭 Shrine Mother Hakurei, Female, who leads here. Voluminous white-blue hair, pale blue eyes, a calm solemn face, white robes. She teaches in koans that each have exactly one honest exit.

♨️ Indentured at the Volcanic Bathhouse.name: ♨️ Indentured at the Volcanic Bathhouse
♨️ Indentured at the Volcanic Bathhouse.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Michiru Kemuritsuki (female, long dark hair loosely pinned up, soft grey-blue eyes, light linen wrap over a simple bathing outfit) and Haruto Kaise (male, tousled dark hair, golden amber eyes, black shirt under a white coat with a cross emblem on the sleeve). Both appear on screen and react. The player was handed over as settlement for a stranger's debt and is working an unspecified term. Do not generate additional named attendants in the opening.]

Nobody here adjusts the water. It comes up out of the mountain at exactly the heat you would have chosen, which is the whole reason the Ashen Silk stands where it does.

You have learned a lot in eleven days. You have learned the order of the pools, which one the old men want and which one they say they want. You have learned to carry four things. You have learned that the timber in this building is two hundred years old and has never rotted because of what is in the steam.

You have not learned how long you are here for.

Eleven days ago a man you had met twice ran up a tab at this house that would buy a small farm, and when the house came for it he did not have it, and what he had instead was you, standing behind him, holding his coat.

He had no right to do that. Everyone agrees. The proprietor said so out loud, at the time, in front of witnesses, and then accepted it anyway, because the alternative was writing off the money.

The house has been decent. That is the confusing part. You have a bed, a wage on paper, and nobody has been unkind to you for a moment.

And yesterday you asked Sen, who has worked here nine years, how she came to the Ashen Silk.

She said her brother's debt, and she said it easily, the way you would name a hometown.

"Your shoulders are up around your ears," says Michiru Kemuritsuki.

She is refilling the cedar buckets along the wall with her eyes on the work, which is how she does most of her observing.

"You are carrying like the left side hurts, which it does, because you have been lifting one-handed for four days to protect a wrist you have not mentioned to anyone." She sets the last bucket down. Grey-blue eyes come up, calm and unhurried. "Show me after the morning bell and I will strap it. That is not a favor; it is that you are no good to the floor with one hand."

She says it lightly. It is still the kindest sentence anyone has said to you in eleven days.

Her hands do not stop. "You asked Sen how she came here," she says, without looking up. "People ask me too, sooner or later." A beat, a real one.

"That is a question with a long answer," she says, "and the morning bell has gone."

Across the soaking hall, a white-coated young man with a cross stitched at the sleeve is crouched beside the far pool, treating a burn on an old woman's forearm with a great deal more care than the burn warrants. He has been here every day. He is not staff.

Haruto Kaise glances up, catches you looking, and does not look away.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: you have been protecting a wrist for four days and nobody has asked why.
• Magic Affinity: the water comes up carrying something the mountain put in it.
• Profession: you have learned the order of the pools and which one the old men actually want.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you knew the tab was impossible before the proprietor finished the number.
• Rebirth or Race: nobody who works here seems to have arrived by any other route.
♨️ Indentured at the Volcanic Bathhouse.description:
📍 Ashen Silk Bathhouse, Kagutsuchi Emberwake. A volcanic bathhouse of mineral pools and dark timber where the water comes up hot from the mountain itself.
Pace: Warm and close. Service work, gossip, and complications.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. Nothing here is dangerous. Several things here are entangling. (Recommended Level 1-10)

A stranger ran up an enormous tab at the Ashen Silk and then produced you as settlement, which he had no legal right to do and which the house accepted anyway because the alternative was losing the money. You are now working it off. The house has been decent about it. The house has also not told you how long the term is, and you have started to notice that nobody who works here seems to have arrived by any other route.

🎭 Michiru Kemuritsuki, Female, senior attendant. Long dark hair loosely pinned up, soft grey-blue eyes, and the healthy glow of someone who spends hours in mineral baths, in a light linen wrap over a simple bathing outfit. Calm and lightly teasing, reading aches and moods in the same glance.
🎭 Haruto Kaise, Male, serious with tousled dark hair, golden amber eyes, and a lean focused face, in a black shirt under a white coat with a cross emblem on the sleeve.

💸 Bought Out by a Portmaris Heiress.name: 💸 Bought Out by a Portmaris Heiress
💸 Bought Out by a Portmaris Heiress.storyStart:
[Present in this scene, all authored world characters. Use their records and do not invent replacements: Harbormaster Umika Hyōchō (Female, Harbormaster of Portmaris and de facto manager of the Guild Central Branch), Hazuki Kanemori (Female, heir of House Kanemori and a Cerulean merchant dynasty in a quiet succession war. She speaks in offers, her small talk has terms). All of them appear on screen and at least react. The player is written in second person only and is never assigned a gender, race, or class; their build decides how they enter the scene. Do not generate additional bystanders, functionaries, guards, or numbered placeholders as named characters. Everyone in this scene is an adult.]

Paper, in Portmaris, is heavier than rope.

You learned that at the third house, when a clerk turned a page toward you and pointed at a signature that was not yours in a hand that was, and explained with real sympathy that the distinction had no standing anywhere on this coast.

The harbor district is loud and enormous and entirely uninterested in your situation. Cranes work. Tonnage moves. The Guild Central Branch takes up one whole side of the customs square and there is a queue outside it that has been the same length all morning. Salt, tar, fish, hot iron, and under all of it the flat industrial rhythm of a port that does not stop for anybody's bad week.

Three houses held the debt. As of this morning, one does.

The office they sent you to is small, glassed, and above the weighing floor, so that the person sitting in it can watch the port work while she talks to you.

"Sit, please. This will be short and I would rather you were not standing for it."

The woman behind the desk is younger than the room and entirely comfortable in it. She has the file already open, squared to the edge of the blotter.

"Hazuki Kanemori. As of nine this morning I hold your position in full." She turns the file so you can read it upside down, which is a courtesy and also a demonstration. "All three houses. Bought at a discount, because a debt attached to a dead borrower and a living face is worth less than a clean one, and because I paid immediately."

"Why."

"That is the question I decline." Not coldly. Almost warmly. "You may ask it as often as you like. I will decline it consistently, and you will eventually decide that is either a threat or a kindness, and I would rather you took your time about which."

Below the glass, the weighing floor clatters. Somebody outside says a number and somebody else disagrees with it.

"Terms," Hazuki says. "The balance stands. The interest stops as of this morning, which is not generosity, it is bookkeeping. Repayment is by contract work, assigned through the Guild under my direction, and the assignments will serve my interests as well as clear your balance. I am telling you that part rather than letting you discover it."

The office door opens without a knock, which tells you something about who is allowed to do that.

"Is this the face without a name," says the Harbormaster, not really a question, and comes in far enough to look at you properly. Weathered, unhurried, entirely in charge of the district outside the window.

"It is," Hazuki says.

Harbormaster Umika Hyōchō studies you for a moment with the flat assessment of somebody who has decided a thousand careers.

"You are seaworthy," she says at last. "Barely, and with a hole in you." To Hazuki, without changing tone: "Whatever you are doing, do it where I can see it."

She leaves. The file is still turned toward you. The balance at the bottom of the page is a number you would need a career to clear.

Hazuki folds her hands.

What now?

[Opening hooks. Use the one that fits this character as a detail where it belongs. The scene still starts at its first line.]
• Combat Class: the Guild queue outside is full of contract work and you have already priced what your hands are worth.
• Magic Affinity: the signature that is not yours was written with something in the ink, and you can feel it on the page.
• Profession: you found the discrepancy between the three houses' figures before Hazuki turned the file around.
• Blessing or Cheat Skill: you knew she was going to decline the question before she declined it.
• Rebirth or Race: somebody wore this face before you did, borrowed on it, and stopped existing, and nobody will say how.
💸 Bought Out by a Portmaris Heiress.description:
📍 Portmaris, Cerulean Coast. The coast's busiest port and the seat of the Adventurer's Guild Central Branch, where the harbor district runs on tonnage, contracts and who owes whom.
Pace: Brisk and transactional. A conversation you cannot leave.
Danger: 🟢 Safe. Nobody in Portmaris settles anything with violence. They settle it with paper. (Recommended Level 1-20)

The name on the debt is not yours. The face the collectors were given is. Somebody who wore this face before you did borrowed heavily across three houses and then stopped existing, and the interest did not stop with them. This morning the paper changed hands: a Kanemori factor bought the whole position, legally and elegantly, and you have been invited to the harbor office to discuss terms with an heir who declines to explain why she wanted it.

🎭 Hazuki Kanemori, Female, heir of House Kanemori and a Cerulean merchant dynasty in a quiet succession war. She speaks in offers, her small talk has terms, and her kindness arrives with plausible deniability.
🎭 Harbormaster Umika Hyōchō, Female, Harbormaster of Portmaris and de facto manager of the Guild Central Branch, delivering verdicts in shipping terms and deciding whose career floats.

⛓️ Auction Day at Starfall Bazaar.name: ⛓️ Auction Day at Starfall Bazaar
⛓️ Auction Day at Starfall Bazaar.storyStart:
[Present in this scene: use the authored world characters the roster places in this area, and use their records for name, appearance and manner. Do not invent named characters for roles the roster already fills. The player was born into slavery and has never known freedom. This start can suit solo or group play.]
