Crown Shard of the Sunken King.name: Crown Shard of the Sunken King
Crown Shard of the Sunken King.description: A fragment of a drowned crown that still commands the deep. The sea remembers its name. [Endgame | Legendary | Tidelace]

Everlit Ember of Creation.name: Everlit Ember of Creation
Everlit Ember of Creation.description: A coal from the first forge-fire, warming the resolve and the spellwork of whoever bears it. [Endgame | Legendary | Emberwake]

Astral Compass of Fated Paths.name: Astral Compass of Fated Paths
Astral Compass of Fated Paths.description: A relic-compass that points not north but toward destiny. Those who follow it rarely lose. [Endgame | Legendary | Starfall]

Soulforge Grand Contract.name: Soulforge Grand Contract
Soulforge Grand Contract.description: The ultimate binding pact, its terms written in a summoner's own resolve. What it calls, comes. [Endgame | Legendary | Academy]

Warbanner of the Last Stand.name: Warbanner of the Last Stand
Warbanner of the Last Stand.description: A banner that has never fallen, stiffening the spine of everyone who fights beneath it. [Endgame | Legendary | Thornblood]

Timeless Sands of the Endless Hour.name: Timeless Sands of the Endless Hour
Timeless Sands of the Endless Hour.description: An hourglass whose sand never empties, gifting its keeper moments no one else is granted. [Endgame | Mythic | Academy]

Reliquary Staff of the Highest Choir.name: Reliquary Staff of the Highest Choir
Reliquary Staff of the Highest Choir.description: A sacred staff bearing the relics of a hundred saints, through which the divine answers as if the wielder were owed. Miracles come easily to its bearer. [Endgame | Legendary | Ecclesia]

Cultivator's Breathing Beads.name: Cultivator's Breathing Beads
Cultivator's Breathing Beads.description: A loop of worn wooden beads counted through during breathing forms, each one polished by a decade of the same patient practice. [Start | Signature | Veilpeak]

Weighted Marching Harness.name: Weighted Marching Harness
Weighted Marching Harness.description: A body harness hung with iron plates, worn during training until the weight stopped registering. It never comes off now. [Start | Signature | Ashenmere]

Chalked Grip Wraps.name: Chalked Grip Wraps
Chalked Grip Wraps.description: Cloth wraps dusted with grip chalk, rewound before every match. What they hold, they keep. [Start | Signature | Ashenmere]

Conditioning Forearm Bands.name: Conditioning Forearm Bands
Conditioning Forearm Bands.description: Hardened bands worn during years of arm conditioning, dented in a pattern that maps every block they ever took. [Start | Signature | Veilpeak]

Sentinel's Mending Talisman.name: Sentinel's Mending Talisman
Sentinel's Mending Talisman.description: A warm iron talisman that quickens the body's own repair, worn by those who hold a line and expect to be hit doing it. [Start | Signature | Crownveil]

Breacher's Iron Collar.name: Breacher's Iron Collar
Breacher's Iron Collar.description: A reinforced collar and shoulder guard for absorbing the volley on the approach. Scored, dented, and never replaced. [Start | Signature | Ashenmere]

Sealed Contagion Phial.name: Sealed Contagion Phial
Sealed Contagion Phial.description: A stoppered phial of the illness its bearer survived, carried as proof, warning, and working material. [Start | Signature | Wilds]

Notched Endurance Tally.name: Notched Endurance Tally
Notched Endurance Tally.description: A strip of leather notched once for every fight that should have ended them. It is running out of room. [Start | Signature | Frontier]

Beastblood Fang Cord.name: Beastblood Fang Cord
Beastblood Fang Cord.description: A cord strung with a fang from whatever first woke the blood. It warms when the temper rises. [Start | Signature | Verdania]

Iron Ore.name: Iron Ore
Iron Ore.description: Common ore streaked with rust-red. The backbone of every frontier forge and the first thing an apprentice learns to smelt. [T1 | Common | Mining]

Copper Ore.name: Copper Ore
Copper Ore.description: Soft green-veined ore, easy to work and easier to ruin. Favored for wiring, fittings, and a smith's first honest mistake. [T1 | Common | Mining]

Silver Ore.name: Silver Ore
Silver Ore.description: Pale ore that takes an edge poorly and an enchantment beautifully. Anything meant to harm the unclean starts here. [T2 | Uncommon | Mining]

Coldiron Ore.name: Coldiron Ore
Coldiron Ore.description: Ore quenched in a vein of underground meltwater, permanently cool to the touch. Fae and spirits will not willingly grip it. [T2 | Uncommon | Deephollow]

Rift-Touched Ore.name: Rift-Touched Ore
Rift-Touched Ore.description: Ore that lay too long beside a rift, veined with pale blue that brightens near Riftlight. Forged into a blade it leaves a faint Riftlight shimmer in the steel. [T2 | Uncommon | Riftmaw]

Kurogane Ore.name: Kurogane Ore
Kurogane Ore.description: The black iron the Deephollow is named for, drawn from below the crystal line. Dense, dark and slow to heat; folded with patience it becomes Deepvein Steel. [T3 | Rare | Deephollow]

Emberforge Ingot.name: Emberforge Ingot
Emberforge Ingot.description: An ingot that holds forge-heat for days after quenching. Working it requires gloves, patience, and a shop that does not mind the smell. [T3 | Rare | Emberwake]

Deepvein Steel.name: Deepvein Steel
Deepvein Steel.description: Steel folded with ore drawn from below the crystal line. Holds an edge through a campaign and rings when struck. [T3 | Rare | Deephollow]

Mythril Ingot.name: Mythril Ingot
Mythril Ingot.description: Impossibly light silver-blue metal that resists heat, rust, and reason. A single ingot is a smith's whole reputation. [T4 | Epic | Deephollow]

Adamantine Shard.name: Adamantine Shard
Adamantine Shard.description: A fragment of the hardest known substance, workable only in a magically stoked forge. Chips diamond. Does not chip back. [T4 | Epic | Deephollow]

Starmetal Fragment.name: Starmetal Fragment
Starmetal Fragment.description: Metal from a fallen star, faintly warm and faintly humming. Must be worked under open sky during the right alignment. [T5 | Legendary | Starfall]

Dragonsteel Billet.name: Dragonsteel Billet
Dragonsteel Billet.description: Steel quenched in dragonfire and cooled in dragon breath. It remembers the wyrm and behaves accordingly. [T5 | Legendary | Emberwake]

Tanned Hide.name: Tanned Hide
Tanned Hide.description: Serviceable cured leather, the standard bolt of every frontier workshop. Unglamorous and endlessly useful. [T1 | Common | Leatherworking]

Direwolf Pelt.name: Direwolf Pelt
Direwolf Pelt.description: Thick grey pelt from a beast that hunted in the deep wilds. Warm enough for Veilpeak, heavy enough to turn a blade. [T2 | Uncommon | Verdania]

Basilisk Leather.name: Basilisk Leather
Basilisk Leather.description: Scaled hide with a faint mineral sheen, prized for armor that resists petrifying magic. Cutting it dulls three knives. [T3 | Rare | Wilds]

Drakescale Plating.name: Drakescale Plating
Drakescale Plating.description: Overlapping scales shed by a young drake, light and fire-resistant. Every armorer wants it and few can source it. [T4 | Epic | Emberwake]

Common Bolt Cloth.name: Common Bolt Cloth
Common Bolt Cloth.description: Honest woven cloth by the bolt. The starting point for every uniform, apron, and first commission. [T1 | Common | Tailoring]

Moonspun Thread.name: Moonspun Thread
Moonspun Thread.description: Thread spun under a full moon that holds a faint silver shimmer in low light. Enchantments bind to it eagerly. [T3 | Rare | Tidelace]

Spider-Silk Skein.name: Spider-Silk Skein
Spider-Silk Skein.description: Silk from deep-cave arachnids, stronger than steel wire at a fraction of the weight. Handled with tongs. [T3 | Rare | Deephollow]

Phoenixdown Tuft.name: Phoenixdown Tuft
Phoenixdown Tuft.description: A tuft of down that is faintly warm and never gets wet. Garments lined with it laugh at winter. [T5 | Legendary | Emberwake]

Seasoned Hardwood.name: Seasoned Hardwood
Seasoned Hardwood.description: Properly dried stave-wood with straight grain. The difference between a bow that lasts and one that does not. [T1 | Common | Woodworking]

Ironbark Stave.name: Ironbark Stave
Ironbark Stave.description: Wood so dense it turns an axe, harvested from trees that grew where the soil ran with ore. [T2 | Uncommon | Verdania]

Spiritwood Branch.name: Spiritwood Branch
Spiritwood Branch.description: Wood cut from a tree grown in high ambient mana, still faintly warm. Standard tools bounce off it. [T3 | Rare | Verdania]

Elderheart Timber.name: Elderheart Timber
Elderheart Timber.description: Heartwood from a tree that stood five centuries. Working it feels less like carving and more like negotiating. [T4 | Epic | Verdania]

Worldroot Fiber.name: Worldroot Fiber
Worldroot Fiber.description: Fiber drawn from the deep root network that connects distant ecosystems. It is still, faintly, alive. [T5 | Legendary | Verdania]

Rough Quartz.name: Rough Quartz
Rough Quartz.description: Cloudy uncut quartz, the stone every apprentice jeweler ruins a dozen of before the first clean facet. [T1 | Common | Crystal Prospecting]

Mana Crystal.name: Mana Crystal
Mana Crystal.description: A crystal that holds a charge of ambient mana. The universal currency of enchanting workshops. [T2 | Uncommon | Deephollow]

Riftlight Shard.name: Riftlight Shard
Riftlight Shard.description: A condensed fragment of the blue-white light that dungeon monsters dissolve into. Warm, and faintly humming. [T2 | Uncommon | Riftmaw]

Resonance Stone.name: Resonance Stone
Resonance Stone.description: A stone that rings at a specific pitch and holds that note indefinitely. Crystalsingers pay absurdly for matched pairs. [T3 | Rare | Deephollow]

Starfall Gem.name: Starfall Gem
Starfall Gem.description: A gem that fell already cut, its facets forming no pattern any lapidary can reproduce. [T4 | Epic | Starfall]

Heartcrystal Core.name: Heartcrystal Core
Heartcrystal Core.description: The intact core of a crystal formation, humming with the resonance of the mountain that grew it. [T5 | Legendary | Deephollow]

Slime Residue.name: Slime Residue
Slime Residue.description: Faintly luminous gel recovered from a dissolved slime. Adhesive, mildly reactive, and everywhere. [T1 | Common | Monster Harvesting]

Goblin Fang.name: Goblin Fang
Goblin Fang.description: A cracked yellow fang. Worth little individually, which is why harvesters take them by the handful. [T1 | Common | Monster Harvesting]

Beast Sinew.name: Beast Sinew
Beast Sinew.description: Tough tendon recovered intact from a large beast. Bowstrings made from it outlast their bows. [T2 | Uncommon | Monster Harvesting]

Wyvern Talon.name: Wyvern Talon
Wyvern Talon.description: A curved talon, still wickedly sharp. Ground into weapon coatings or set whole into gauntlets. [T3 | Rare | Duskfields]

Basilisk Eye.name: Basilisk Eye
Basilisk Eye.description: A preserved eye that still faintly tracks movement in the jar. Used in petrification wards and in nothing pleasant. [T4 | Epic | Wilds]

Demonheart Ember.name: Demonheart Ember
Demonheart Ember.description: A still-burning coal recovered from a demon's chest cavity. It does not cool and it does not forgive. [T5 | Legendary | Twilight]

Sunleaf Herb.name: Sunleaf Herb
Sunleaf Herb.description: Bright yellow leaves that keep their color when dried. The base of nearly every low-tier healing draught. [T1 | Common | Herbalism]

Bitterroot.name: Bitterroot
Bitterroot.description: A gnarled root that tastes exactly as advertised. Neutralizes toxins and ruins tea. [T1 | Common | Foraging]

Nightbloom Petal.name: Nightbloom Petal
Nightbloom Petal.description: A petal that opens only after dark and closes at the first touch of light. Sedatives and poisons both start here. [T2 | Uncommon | Rosethorn]

Mana Lotus.name: Mana Lotus
Mana Lotus.description: A flower grown in mana-saturated water, its petals faintly translucent. Alchemists ration them by the petal. [T3 | Rare | Tidelace]

Ghostcap Mushroom.name: Ghostcap Mushroom
Ghostcap Mushroom.description: A pale mushroom that grows only where a spirit lingered. Handled with reverence and gloves. [T3 | Rare | Spiritfen]

Dreamspore Cluster.name: Dreamspore Cluster
Dreamspore Cluster.description: Spores that induce vivid sleep. Essential for dream magic and strictly controlled by the Church. [T4 | Epic | Spiritfen]

Worldbloom Nectar.name: Worldbloom Nectar
Worldbloom Nectar.description: Nectar from a flower that blooms once a century. A single vial can anchor a legendary enchantment. [T5 | Legendary | Verdania]

Field Grain Sack.name: Field Grain Sack
Field Grain Sack.description: A sack of honest grain. Bread, ale, and half the frontier's calories start here. [T1 | Common | Farming]

River Catch.name: River Catch
River Catch.description: A fresh haul of river fish packed in reeds. Perishable, plentiful, and the backbone of coastal cooking. [T1 | Common | Fishing]

Spice Trader's Pouch.name: Spice Trader's Pouch
Spice Trader's Pouch.description: A pouch of caravan spices from the Mirage Sea. Transforms a competent dish into a memorable one. [T2 | Uncommon | Renka]

Monster Meat Cut.name: Monster Meat Cut
Monster Meat Cut.description: A prime cut harvested from a defeated beast. Battle Chefs swear the mana content is the entire point. [T2 | Uncommon | Battle Cooking]

Emberfruit.name: Emberfruit
Emberfruit.description: A fruit that stays warm to the touch and adds a slow heat to anything it is cooked into. [T3 | Rare | Emberwake]

Frostberry Cluster.name: Frostberry Cluster
Frostberry Cluster.description: Berries that stay frozen at room temperature. Prized for preserving and for very good desserts. [T3 | Rare | Veilpeak]

Blank Rune Blank.name: Blank Rune Blank
Blank Rune Blank.description: An unmarked stone disc prepared for carving. The carver's canvas, sold in bundles and ruined in bundles. [T1 | Common | Rune Carving]

Enchanter's Chalk.name: Enchanter's Chalk
Enchanter's Chalk.description: Chalk ground with powdered mana crystal. Draws sigils that hold a charge long enough to set. [T2 | Uncommon | Enchanting]

Binding Ink.name: Binding Ink
Binding Ink.description: Ink brewed to hold magical intent. Contracts written in it are noticeably harder to weasel out of. [T3 | Rare | Scribal Arts]

Ley-Touched Filament.name: Ley-Touched Filament
Ley-Touched Filament.description: A thread of metal drawn along a ley line, permanently conductive to mana. Woven into the finest enchanted gear. [T4 | Epic | Aetherglass]

Sealwright's Wax.name: Sealwright's Wax
Sealwright's Wax.description: Wax that hardens into something closer to stone, used to close a Grand Seal. One tin, one seal. [T5 | Legendary | Ecclesia]

Guild Scout's Hood.name: Guild Scout's Hood
Guild Scout's Hood.description: A practical hood with a stiffened brim, standard issue for anyone who works outside the walls. [Low | Common | Guild]

Ironvein Mining Helm.name: Ironvein Mining Helm
Ironvein Mining Helm.description: A dented helm with a lamp bracket, built to survive a collapse and usually does. [Mid | Uncommon | Deephollow]

Cinderguard Faceplate.name: Cinderguard Faceplate
Cinderguard Faceplate.description: A soot-blackened faceplate that filters ash and turns heat. Standard in the forge districts. [Mid | Rare | Emberwake]

Nocturne Half-Mask.name: Nocturne Half-Mask
Nocturne Half-Mask.description: A lacquered half-mask worn to the nocturne, concealing identity and a great deal else. [Mid | Rare | Rosethorn]

Spiritfen Ward-Circlet.name: Spiritfen Ward-Circlet
Spiritfen Ward-Circlet.description: A circlet hung with paper charms that still when spirits are near and rattle when they are not. [Mid | Rare | Spiritfen]

Tidecaller's Coral Crown.name: Tidecaller's Coral Crown
Tidecaller's Coral Crown.description: A crown of living coral that keeps its wearer breathing easy underwater. [Late | Epic | Tidelace]

Archmagus Study Circlet.name: Archmagus Study Circlet
Archmagus Study Circlet.description: A thin silver circlet that steadies concentration through long castings. [Late | Epic | Academy]

Apprentice's Work Gloves.name: Apprentice's Work Gloves
Apprentice's Work Gloves.description: Stiff leather gloves worn through at the fingertips. Everyone starts with a pair like these. [Low | Common | Guild]

Bowyer's Draw Gloves.name: Bowyer's Draw Gloves
Bowyer's Draw Gloves.description: Reinforced at the draw fingers, worn smooth everywhere else. [Mid | Uncommon | Verdania]

Duelist's Dress Gauntlets.name: Duelist's Dress Gauntlets
Duelist's Dress Gauntlets.description: Slim court gauntlets built for a rapier grip and an evening's worth of insults. [Mid | Rare | Crownveil]

Frostbite Wraps.name: Frostbite Wraps
Frostbite Wraps.description: Layered wraps that keep the fingers working in Veilpeak cold. Fumbling is fatal up there. [Mid | Rare | Veilpeak]

Emberforge Smithing Mitts.name: Emberforge Smithing Mitts
Emberforge Smithing Mitts.description: Heavy mitts that let a smith hold something glowing without flinching. [Mid | Rare | Emberwake]

Mythril Articulated Gauntlets.name: Mythril Articulated Gauntlets
Mythril Articulated Gauntlets.description: Gauntlets of such fine articulation the wearer forgets they are armored. [Late | Epic | Deephollow]

Voidtouched Grasp.name: Voidtouched Grasp
Voidtouched Grasp.description: Gauntlets that drink a little of whatever they close around. Unsettling to shake hands with. [Late | Epic | Twilight]

Traveler's Worn Boots.name: Traveler's Worn Boots
Traveler's Worn Boots.description: Boots that have already walked a long way and intend to walk further. [Low | Common | Wandering]

Marsh-Strider Waders.name: Marsh-Strider Waders
Marsh-Strider Waders.description: Tall waders that keep the Spiritfen's water and its residents out. [Mid | Uncommon | Spiritfen]

Silent-Sole Slippers.name: Silent-Sole Slippers
Silent-Sole Slippers.description: Soft-soled slippers that make no sound on stone, tile, or a creaking floorboard. [Mid | Rare | Underground]

Duskfields Riding Spurs.name: Duskfields Riding Spurs
Duskfields Riding Spurs.description: Spurred riding boots cut for the plains, worn by people who consider walking a failure. [Mid | Rare | Windrunner]

Ashwalker Sabatons.name: Ashwalker Sabatons
Ashwalker Sabatons.description: Thick-soled boots that let their wearer cross fresh volcanic ground without regretting it. [Mid | Rare | Emberwake]

Skystep Greaves.name: Skystep Greaves
Skystep Greaves.description: Greaves that lighten the wearer at the apex of a jump. Aetherglass artificers still argue about how. [Late | Epic | Aetherglass]

Worldroot Treads.name: Worldroot Treads
Worldroot Treads.description: Boots grown rather than stitched, which grip any natural surface as though invited. [Late | Epic | Verdania]

Padded Travel Trousers.name: Padded Travel Trousers
Padded Travel Trousers.description: Reinforced at the knee and seat, because the road is mostly falling and sitting. [Low | Common | Guild]

Guild Skirmisher's Tassets.name: Guild Skirmisher's Tassets
Guild Skirmisher's Tassets.description: Overlapping thigh plates that do not restrict a low stance. Frontier standard issue. [Mid | Uncommon | Ashenmere]

Nocturne Layered Skirt.name: Nocturne Layered Skirt
Nocturne Layered Skirt.description: A ballroom skirt with steel boning sewn into the panels. Dances beautifully. Stops a knife. [Mid | Rare | Rosethorn]

Shrine Hakama of Warding.name: Shrine Hakama of Warding
Shrine Hakama of Warding.description: Formal hakama stitched with warding thread, worn by shrine maidens who expect trouble. [Mid | Rare | Tidelace]

Deepdelve Reinforced Legguards.name: Deepdelve Reinforced Legguards
Deepdelve Reinforced Legguards.description: Legguards built for the crawl, the climb, and the long walk back out. [Mid | Rare | Deephollow]

Dragonscale Cuisses.name: Dragonscale Cuisses
Dragonscale Cuisses.description: Thigh plates of true dragonscale, light enough to run in and hot to the touch. [Late | Epic | Emberwake]

Archmagus Layered Robes (Lower).name: Archmagus Layered Robes (Lower)
Archmagus Layered Robes (Lower).description: The lower half of a master's regalia, every layer a small mana reservoir. [Late | Epic | Academy]

Guild Initiate's Gambeson.name: Guild Initiate's Gambeson
Guild Initiate's Gambeson.description: Quilted padding issued to every new registrant. It has saved more lives than it gets credit for. [Low | Common | Guild]

Foraging Vest.name: Foraging Vest
Foraging Vest.description: A vest of many pockets, each already full of something the wearer swears is useful. [Low | Common | Foraging]

Frontier Six-Shooter.name: Frontier Six-Shooter
Frontier Six-Shooter.description: An honest black-powder revolver of frontier iron and worn walnut, six chambers and no apologies. It smells of oil and cordite, kicks like a mule, and clears leather faster than most people clear their throats. No runes, no mana, just powder, lead, and nerve. [Early | Uncommon | Ashenmere]

Lever-Action Repeater.name: Lever-Action Repeater
Lever-Action Repeater.description: A long black-powder rifle worked by a lever loop under the stock, chambering the next round with a sound every frontier bandit learns to dread. Slower than a revolver up close, murder at range, and reliable in mud, snow, and salt where finer weapons sulk. Powder and iron, nothing arcane. [Early | Uncommon | Ashenmere]

Ironpoint Cavalry Lance.name: Ironpoint Cavalry Lance
Ironpoint Cavalry Lance.description: A long couched lance of ash and iron, balanced to brace under one arm and aim with the whole body. On foot it keeps trouble at spear length; from a saddle it becomes an argument nobody wins twice.

Guardsman's Halberd.name: Guardsman's Halberd
Guardsman's Halberd.description: A guardsman's halberd: axe-blade, back-hook, and a spike on a long haft. Three weapons that could not agree on one job, so they took all of them. Reliable at a wall, at a gate, or in front of someone important.

Sweeping War Glaive.name: Sweeping War Glaive
Sweeping War Glaive.description: A single broad blade set on a long war-haft, honed for the sweep as much as the point. It carves wide, keeps a circle clear, and looks unfairly good doing it.

Three-Prong War Trident.name: Three-Prong War Trident
Three-Prong War Trident.description: A three-pronged war trident with barbed tines meant to catch a blade as easily as a body. Favored by coast guards, pit fighters, and anyone who likes a weapon that traps as well as it stabs.

Knight's Poleaxe.name: Knight's Poleaxe
Knight's Poleaxe.description: A knight's poleaxe of hammer, spike, and axe on a steel-cheeked haft, built for the ugly work of fighting armored men. Short enough to swing in a press, heavy enough to make plate a formality.

Crescent Guandao.name: Crescent Guandao
Crescent Guandao.description: A heavy crescent blade on a red-tasseled pole, weighted at the butt for balance and drama in equal measure. Traditionally the weapon of a general, and it carries itself like one.

Corsair's Cutlass.name: Corsair's Cutlass
Corsair's Cutlass.description: A corsair's cutlass with a broad curved blade and a knuckle-guard that doubles as a fist. Built for tight quarters, wet decks, and arguments that end quickly.

Curved Desert Scimitar.name: Curved Desert Scimitar
Curved Desert Scimitar.description: A curved desert saber of pattern-forged steel, light in the hand and hungry for motion. It cuts best when you are already moving, which is most of the time.

Heavy Falchion.name: Heavy Falchion
Heavy Falchion.description: A heavy single-edged falchion, thick at the tip where the weight does its arguing. Cheap to make, brutal to meet, and honest about what it is.

Needlepoint Estoc.name: Needlepoint Estoc
Needlepoint Estoc.description: A long, edgeless thrusting blade, stiff as a rod and ground to a needle point. Useless for slashing, unmatched for finding the one gap a suit of armor forgot about.

Twin-Grip Zweihander.name: Twin-Grip Zweihander
Twin-Grip Zweihander.description: An enormous two-hander with a second grip past the crossguard and blunt parrying lugs on the blade. Long enough to keep a whole line of spears at bay, heavy enough to end the argument once it is close.

Hooked Khopesh.name: Hooked Khopesh
Hooked Khopesh.description: A bronze-dark khopesh curved into a sickle hook, edge riding the outside of the crescent. Ancient, ceremonial, and very good at pulling a shield out of the way before the real cut lands.

Cavalry Sabre.name: Cavalry Sabre
Cavalry Sabre.description: A slim cavalry sabre with a swept basket guard, light enough for the wrist to do the talking. Made for quick clean cuts and getting out again before anyone answers.

Long-Haft Dane Axe.name: Long-Haft Dane Axe
Long-Haft Dane Axe.description: A long-hafted broad-bearded axe meant for two hands and open ground. The beard hooks shields down; the edge handles whatever was hiding behind them.

Spiked Morning Star.name: Spiked Morning Star
Spiked Morning Star.description: A stout haft topped with a spiked iron ball, subtle as a thunderclap. It does not parry, it does not finesse, it simply arrives.

Ball-and-Chain Flail.name: Ball-and-Chain Flail
Ball-and-Chain Flail.description: A spiked head on a short chain, as dangerous to learn as it is to face. It ignores shields by simply swinging around them, and it does not care whose timing it ruins.

Ironhead War Maul.name: Ironhead War Maul
Ironhead War Maul.description: A two-handed sledge with an iron head the size of a bad decision. Slow to raise, impossible to argue with, and murder on anything that trusted its armor.

Bandit's Greatclub.name: Bandit's Greatclub
Bandit's Greatclub.description: A crude tree-trunk of a club, banded with scrap iron and studded where the wood split. Zero craftsmanship, alarming results.

Punching Katar.name: Punching Katar
Punching Katar.description: A push-dagger with an H-grip that sits in the fist, so the blade points straight out from the knuckles. Every punch becomes a thrust, which is the entire idea.

Twin Iron Sai.name: Twin Iron Sai
Twin Iron Sai.description: A matched pair of iron sai, prong-guarded and blunt-pointed, made to trap a blade and snap a wrist. They flip, reverse, and catch, which is most of a conversation.

Knuckle Trench Knife.name: Knuckle Trench Knife
Knuckle Trench Knife.description: A short brutal blade with a cast knuckle-guard for a grip, so the off-hand option is always 'hit them with the handle.' Made for the ugly range where nothing else fits.

Returning War Boomerang.name: Returning War Boomerang
Returning War Boomerang.description: A hardwood war boomerang carved with a wicked leading edge, weighted so a clean throw comes home. Miss and it forgives you; hit and it comes back for seconds.

Star Shuriken Set.name: Star Shuriken Set
Star Shuriken Set.description: A pouch of balanced star-blades, thin, dark, and quiet. Individually a nuisance, in a fast hand a storm that arrives before the sound does.

Balanced Throwing Knives.name: Balanced Throwing Knives
Balanced Throwing Knives.description: A bandolier of balanced throwing knives, each one the same weight so the wrist never has to think. Drawn, thrown, and drawn again in one motion that looks like sleight of hand.

Weighted Kunai Set.name: Weighted Kunai Set
Weighted Kunai Set.description: A set of heavy iron kunai, part throwing blade, part pry-bar, part climbing spike. Honest tools that moonlight as weapons, which is the most ninja thing about them.

Bundled War Javelins.name: Bundled War Javelins
Bundled War Javelins.description: A bundle of short war javelins with soft iron necks that bend on impact, so nobody throws them back. Simple, ancient, and rude to shields.

Paired Francisca Axes.name: Paired Francisca Axes
Paired Francisca Axes.description: A pair of short francisca throwing axes with wicked drop-shaped heads, meant to be hurled in a bounce that nobody can read. Also perfectly happy to be used up close.

Weighted Hunting Bolas.name: Weighted Hunting Bolas
Weighted Hunting Bolas.description: Three weighted stones on braided cords, spun up and let fly to wrap a runner's legs mid-stride. A hunter's tool that works just as well on things that fight back.

Steel-Prod Crossbow.name: Steel-Prod Crossbow
Steel-Prod Crossbow.description: A compact steel-prod crossbow with a stirrup for the foot and a bolt clip on the stock. Point, hold, release: it asks almost nothing of the arm and delivers rather a lot.

Windlass Heavy Crossbow.name: Windlass Heavy Crossbow
Windlass Heavy Crossbow.description: A siege-weight crossbow spanned by a windlass crank, slow as a grudge and twice as final. One bolt, but that bolt has opinions about walls.

Repeating Chu-Ko-Nu.name: Repeating Chu-Ko-Nu
Repeating Chu-Ko-Nu.description: A lever-worked repeating crossbow with a top-mounted bolt magazine, trading power for a rain of little bolts. Each one is minor; the volume is the argument.

Leather Shepherd's Sling.name: Leather Shepherd's Sling
Leather Shepherd's Sling.description: A simple braided leather sling and a pouch of smooth shot, the cheapest deadly thing on any road. Looks like a toy right up until the stone arrives.

Long-Barrel Musket.name: Long-Barrel Musket
Long-Barrel Musket.description: A long-barreled black-powder musket with a bayonet lug at the muzzle, powder and lead and patience. Slow to load, loud enough to end a conversation, and a spear once it is empty.

Scattershot Blunderbuss.name: Scattershot Blunderbuss
Scattershot Blunderbuss.description: A short flared-muzzle blunderbuss that swallows a fistful of shot and hands it back to a whole doorway at once. Aiming is more of a suggestion than a requirement.

Iron Hand Cannon.name: Iron Hand Cannon
Iron Hand Cannon.description: A brutal short iron hand cannon, more pipe than pistol, touched off by hand and felt in the shoulder. One shot, enormous, and not remotely subtle.

Hardwood Bo Staff.name: Hardwood Bo Staff
Hardwood Bo Staff.description: A plain hardwood bo, waxed smooth and weighted even end to end. No blade, no edge, no excuses, just reach, rhythm, and a great many bruises for whoever underestimates it.

Oak Quarterstaff.name: Oak Quarterstaff
Oak Quarterstaff.description: A stout iron-shod oak quarterstaff, tall as its owner and twice as stubborn. The most respectable weapon a traveler can lean on and still swing when the road gets rude.

Paired Hardwood Tonfa.name: Paired Hardwood Tonfa
Paired Hardwood Tonfa.description: A matched pair of side-handled hardwood tonfa that spin out to strike and tuck back along the forearm to guard. An extension of the arms, which is exactly how they are meant to feel.

Segmented Three-Section Staff.name: Segmented Three-Section Staff
Segmented Three-Section Staff.description: Three hardwood rods joined by short chains, folding from a staff into a flail and back mid-swing. As dangerous to the beginner as to the target, and twice as impressive once mastered.

Tiger Hook Swords.name: Tiger Hook Swords
Tiger Hook Swords.description: A matched pair of hook swords with crescent guards and pommel spikes, able to link hook-to-hook into a single long weapon. Three edges per blade, and all of them busy.

Coiling Urumi.name: Coiling Urumi
Coiling Urumi.description: A flexible whip-sword of long flat steel that coils like a belt at rest and lashes like a living edge in motion. Fatal to the untrained wielder, which is most of its reputation.

Focused Spellwand.name: Focused Spellwand
Focused Spellwand.description: A short focused spellwand of rune-inlaid wood, tuned for fast precise casting over raw power. It fits the sleeve, the boot, or the hand of someone who prefers not to look armed.

Channeling Crystal Orb.name: Channeling Crystal Orb
Channeling Crystal Orb.description: A palm-sized channeling orb of clouded crystal that hovers a hand's breadth above the glove and answers to a thought. Beautiful, expensive, and quietly overqualified.

Blessed Prayer Beads.name: Blessed Prayer Beads
Blessed Prayer Beads.description: A long loop of blessed prayer beads that warm at each spoken sutra and can be snapped taut as a strand or hurled as a ring of light. Devotion you can wear, and swing.

Warding Talisman Slips.name: Warding Talisman Slips
Warding Talisman Slips.description: A fan of inked paper talisman slips that snap rigid and blaze with sigils when charged, then burn away as they spend themselves. One-use, exquisitely styled, and unnervingly effective.

Round Steel Buckler.name: Round Steel Buckler
Round Steel Buckler.description: A small round steel buckler gripped in the fist, all deflection and no weight. It hides the hand, punches like a boss, and keeps the sword hand free for the real work.

Kite Wall Shield.name: Kite Wall Shield
Kite Wall Shield.description: A tall teardrop kite shield that covers shoulder to shin, strapped to the arm for the long haul. A mobile wall that still lets you run, which is the whole appeal.

Cast-Iron Frying Pan.name: Cast-Iron Frying Pan
Cast-Iron Frying Pan.description: A heavy cast-iron frying pan, seasoned black and dense enough to double as a small anvil. Cooks a fine breakfast; rings like a bell off a bandit's helmet.

Reinforced Grappling Gauntlets.name: Reinforced Grappling Gauntlets
Reinforced Grappling Gauntlets.description: Fingerless gauntlets reinforced across the palm and wrist, textured for grip rather than impact. Built to turn a hold into a decision the other person does not get a vote on.

Bulwark Siege Shield.name: Bulwark Siege Shield
Bulwark Siege Shield.description: An oversized advancing shield, heavy enough to brace a doorway and wide enough for an ally to live behind. Made for walking into fire, not hiding from it.

Roadsong Lute.name: Roadsong Lute
Roadsong Lute.description: A sturdy traveling lute with a reinforced neck and a warm wooden soundboard. Built for performances on the road and for channeling bard abilities the player has learned. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Rosewood Bard Violin.name: Rosewood Bard Violin
Rosewood Bard Violin.description: A rosewood violin with a fitted bow and a road-safe case. A responsive performance instrument and focus for learned bard abilities; the bow is for playing, not a disguised sword. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Silverwind Traveling Flute.name: Silverwind Traveling Flute
Silverwind Traveling Flute.description: A compact metal flute wrapped for travel. Its clear voice carries across an inn yard or a battle line, and it can focus bard abilities the player has learned. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Moonstring Hand Harp.name: Moonstring Hand Harp
Moonstring Hand Harp.description: A small, portable harp with a curved wooden frame and a protective travel cover. Sized for an adventurer to carry and play; a focus for learned bard abilities, not a full-sized concert harp. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Marchbeat War Drum.name: Marchbeat War Drum
Marchbeat War Drum.description: A compact, strap-mounted drum with a pair of beaters. Keeps marching time and channels learned bard abilities through rhythm. Its beat does not grant free attacks, automatic haste, or unlimited buffs. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Tidelace Road Shamisen.name: Tidelace Road Shamisen
Tidelace Road Shamisen.description: A three-stringed traveling shamisen associated with Tsukihana Tidelace festival performers. Includes a plectrum and protective wrap; usable as a focus for learned bard abilities. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Otherworld Smartphone.name: Otherworld Smartphone
Otherworld Smartphone.description: A personal smartphone carried across worlds, kept charged by its owner's Otherworld Smartphone cheat. Its ordinary offline tools work; connected or magical features follow the capabilities agreed by player and narrator. Stores actual notes, photos, recordings, and saved files. No automatic quest acceptance, money creation, or access to hidden facts.

Guild Roadcloak.name: Guild Roadcloak
Guild Roadcloak.description: Waxed canvas, a sturdy clasp, and a hem cut clear of muddy boots. Sheds ordinary rain and wind without restricting a sword arm. No magical ward or stat bonus. Sold by guild outfitters and general clothiers; a beginner Tailoring project with canvas and wax. [Early | Common | Crownveil]

Frostbell Fur Cape.name: Frostbell Fur Cape
Frostbell Fur Cape.description: A short wool cape with a deep fur collar, made for cold mountain roads. Retains warmth and lends confidence to outdoor travel; it cannot prevent frostbite in extreme conditions or stop magical ice. Sold by Frostbell outfitters or sewn from wool and ethically sourced fur. [Early | Uncommon | Yukishiro]

Lanternstage Half-Cape.name: Lanternstage Half-Cape
Lanternstage Half-Cape.description: A reversible half-cape with weighted corners that follow a performer's turn without tangling an instrument. Warm gold for festival songs, midnight blue for intimate ballads. Supports practiced performance; it neither compels an audience nor casts spells. Sold by festival costumers and made through Tailoring. [Early | Uncommon | Festival Circuit]

Rosethorn Evening Shawl.name: Rosethorn Evening Shawl
Rosethorn Evening Shawl.description: Black lace over wine-red silk, fastened with a rose-shaped clasp. Its cut and discreet house-neutral embroidery help the wearer dress appropriately for formal company. It grants no noble title, invitation, attraction or consent. Commissioned from Rosethorn tailors with silk and lace. [Mid | Uncommon | Rosethorn]

Emberglass Ashcloak.name: Emberglass Ashcloak
Emberglass Ashcloak.description: Tight ash-grey weave edged with heat-resistant glass thread, for drifting ash, stray sparks and volcanic weather. Face and breath still need protection; lava and direct flame still burn. Made by Emberwake outfitters with Tailoring and glass thread; sometimes found in expedition caches. [Mid | Rare | Emberwake]

Moonlit Promise Mantle.name: Moonlit Promise Mantle
Moonlit Promise Mantle.description: Soft dusk-blue cloth hand-embroidered with a small symbol chosen together. Helps its wearer notice subtle moods. Between a consenting maker and wearer who trust each other, the symbol warms faintly within arm's reach; the warmth is narrative only, grants no stats, and senses nothing distant or hidden. A deliberate Tailoring or Gift Crafting commission, given on-screen; wearing it never changes a relationship by itself. [Mid | Rare | Companion Craft]

Rending Claw Gauntlets.name: Rending Claw Gauntlets
Rending Claw Gauntlets.description: Steel-backed gauntlets with three curved blades over each set of knuckles, honed for raking cuts and driven thrusts. Your fists are still the weapon; now they cut.

Company Crest Pin.name: Company Crest Pin
Company Crest Pin.description: A small enameled pin bearing your Company's crest. Guild clerks and other adventurers read your banner from it at a glance.

Blank Company Charter.name: Blank Company Charter
Blank Company Charter.description: An Adventurer's Guild charter form with the fee already stamped paid. Fill in a name, a crest, two partners' signatures and an address, then file it at any guild hall to found your own Company.

Wayfarer's Guitar.name: Wayfarer's Guitar
Wayfarer's Guitar.description: A six-string traveling guitar with a sun-faded top and a strap worn to the shape of one shoulder. Loud enough for a tavern, light enough for the road. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Thunderhead Stormstring.name: Thunderhead Stormstring
Thunderhead Stormstring.description: A solid-bodied guitar strung with lightning-treated wire, cabled to a mana crystal amplifier that hums when it is switched on. It carries across a festival ground. It does not shock anyone or cast anything. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Shrine-Tuned Lyre.name: Shrine-Tuned Lyre
Shrine-Tuned Lyre.description: A small hand lyre with a curved wooden frame and gut strings, tuned the old shrine way. It sits in the crook of one arm. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Moonbridge Zither.name: Moonbridge Zither
Moonbridge Zither.description: A long floor zither of pale wood with silk strings and ivory-colored movable bridges, carried in a brocade case. Played kneeling, with finger picks. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Festival Tambourine.name: Festival Tambourine
Festival Tambourine.description: A hand tambourine with a painted skin and two rows of brass jingles, ribbons tied to the frame. Built to be heard over a crowd. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Seedshell Maracas.name: Seedshell Maracas
Seedshell Maracas.description: A matched pair of dried gourd maracas filled with reef seeds and painted in harbor colors. They keep time and nothing else. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Kagura Suzu Bells.name: Kagura Suzu Bells
Kagura Suzu Bells.description: A handheld tree of small brass bells in three tiers, with five long colored ribbons tied below the grip. Used in shrine dance and festival blessings. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Folding Road Piano.name: Folding Road Piano
Folding Road Piano.description: A four-octave folding piano in a hard case, with trestle legs that lock and a sustain pedal on a cord. Heavy, but one person can carry it. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Festival Taiko.name: Festival Taiko
Festival Taiko.description: A barrel-bodied festival drum on a folding stand, with two thick sticks. Heard across a harbor. Its beat grants no free attacks and no automatic buffs. [Start | Signature | Bard]

Knightly Plate Armor.name: Knightly Plate Armor
Knightly Plate Armor.description: A full harness of plate with a surcoat or cape, finished in its wearer's colors. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Blackened Plate Armor.name: Blackened Plate Armor
Blackened Plate Armor.description: A full harness of dark plate, scarred or ember-seamed, made to be remembered. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Lacquered Lamellar Armor.name: Lacquered Lamellar Armor
Lacquered Lamellar Armor.description: Lacquered lamellar plates laced over silk, with a crested helmet. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Scale Battle Armor.name: Scale Battle Armor
Scale Battle Armor.description: Fitted scale over leather, with a high collar and reinforced gloves. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Breastplate and Leathers.name: Breastplate and Leathers
Breastplate and Leathers.description: A chest plate over leather or cloth layers, with an armored piece or two to match. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Armored Battle Gown.name: Armored Battle Gown
Armored Battle Gown.description: A gown split for movement over armored corsetry and plated shoulders. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Adventurer's Leathers.name: Adventurer's Leathers
Adventurer's Leathers.description: A fitted set of working leathers with good boots and a broad belt. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Reinforced Long Coat.name: Reinforced Long Coat
Reinforced Long Coat.description: A long leather or padded coat with reinforced seams, made for the road and the duel. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Furs and Hides.name: Furs and Hides
Furs and Hides.description: Heavy furs and worked hide, hung with charms, bone and clan markers. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Reinforced Battle Dress.name: Reinforced Battle Dress
Reinforced Battle Dress.description: A dress or uniform cut for fighting, with a boned bodice and hidden panels. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Creature Harness.name: Creature Harness
Creature Harness.description: A fitted leather harness with a satchel or saddlebags, sized for a body on four legs, wings or coils. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Everyday Clothes.name: Everyday Clothes
Everyday Clothes.description: Comfortable clothes for an ordinary day: no armor and no pretense. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Otherworld Clothes.name: Otherworld Clothes
Otherworld Clothes.description: Clothes from another world. Nothing in Luxcellia is cut or stitched like them. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Traveling Cloak and Clothes.name: Traveling Cloak and Clothes
Traveling Cloak and Clothes.description: Practical layers under a long cloak or coat, made for weather and distance. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Academy Uniform.name: Academy Uniform
Academy Uniform.description: A neatly kept academy uniform in school colors. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Kimono and Sash.name: Kimono and Sash
Kimono and Sash.description: A kimono, yukata or hakama set with its sash and sandals. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Shrine Vestments.name: Shrine Vestments
Shrine Vestments.description: The layered robes of a shrine, in white, red or violet, with ribbons or paper charms. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Holy Vestments.name: Holy Vestments
Holy Vestments.description: White and gold vestments with a stole and a holy or healer's insignia. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Mage's Robes.name: Mage's Robes
Mage's Robes.description: A caster's robes, gown or working coat, in the cut and colors of its wearer's craft. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Occult Vestments.name: Occult Vestments
Occult Vestments.description: Dark layered vestments sewn with seals and sigils. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Shadow Garb.name: Shadow Garb
Shadow Garb.description: A close, dark, quiet outfit with a hood or half-mask. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Fine Dress.name: Fine Dress
Fine Dress.description: A well-made dress or gown in lace, silk or embroidery, cut to be looked at. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Court Regalia.name: Court Regalia
Court Regalia.description: Rich court regalia: heavy fabric, rank worked into the trim, a mantle or cape. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Tailored Formalwear.name: Tailored Formalwear
Tailored Formalwear.description: A sharply tailored suit or coat with gloves, cut with room to move. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Seafarer's Coat.name: Seafarer's Coat
Seafarer's Coat.description: A weathered long coat over a loose shirt, with boots that know a deck. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Wedding Attire.name: Wedding Attire
Wedding Attire.description: A ceremonial wedding dress with a veil and a long train. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Stage Costume.name: Stage Costume
Stage Costume.description: A bright costume built for a stage: bold color, ribbons or a cape, made to move in. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Servant's Uniform.name: Servant's Uniform
Servant's Uniform.description: A crisp uniform of service, with an apron or tailored cuffs. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Training Gi.name: Training Gi
Training Gi.description: A plain training gi or sleeveless wraps, with a belt and hand wraps. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Swimwear.name: Swimwear
Swimwear.description: Swimwear with a light wrap. It keeps the sun off and nothing else. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Sleepwear.name: Sleepwear
Sleepwear.description: Soft, rumpled sleepwear. Comfortable, and no protection at all. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Bunny Suit.name: Bunny Suit
Bunny Suit.description: A sleek bunny suit with cuffs, ears and a tail. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Training Wraps.name: Training Wraps
Training Wraps.description: Bandage wraps on the hands, forearms and torso, and loose trousers. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Collar and Name Tag.name: Collar and Name Tag
Collar and Name Tag.description: A well-made collar with a small bell or tag. [Starter | Common | Outfit]

Crescent Reaper Scythe.name: Crescent Reaper Scythe
Crescent Reaper Scythe.description: Crescent-bladed reaper's scythe. Devastating sweep, absolutely no subtlety.

Iron-Crowned Basalt Idol.name: Iron-Crowned Basalt Idol
Iron-Crowned Basalt Idol.description: A palm-sized basalt effigy crowned with jagged iron, warm to the thumb. It listens only when held without an apology. [Start | Signature | Dark Gods]

Levyman's War Scythe.name: Levyman's War Scythe
Levyman's War Scythe.description: A scythe blade straightened and riveted in line on a long ash pole. Plain, heavy and long, and it holds a line against riders.

Witch's Hex.name: Witch's Hex
Witch's Hex.description:
The witch marks the target with a debilitating hex: accuracy curdling, damage output sagging, every action arriving slightly wrong in ways the victim can feel but not fix. The hex manifests as a visible mark (a smudge of dark script on the skin that everyone can see and nobody can scrub) fading only when the curse ends. The mark is the mercy and the cruelty at once: the victim knows exactly what is wrong with them, and exactly who did it.
[Dark Magic: 2]

Radiant Aegis.name: Radiant Aegis
Radiant Aegis.description:
Raise a barrier of radiant golden light around yourself or an ally. The shield takes the force of incoming blows and pulses with healing energy for those it protects; the stronger your conviction, the harder it is to break, and a shield raised for someone you love shines brightest of all. It guards you or one ally on the turn you raise it; keeping it up takes your action again each turn.
[Light Magic: 5]

Parry.name: Parry
Parry.description:
The duelist's foundation: an incoming attack met with precise blade movement: force redirected rather than absorbed, the enemy's momentum spent into empty air. A perfect parry creates the opening for a devastating counter: the parry is never the sentence; it is the comma before it. Masters fight whole duels appearing merely to decline.
[Dueling: 2]

Devour.name: Devour
Devour.description:
Open a small void pocket that swallows incoming force, consuming the kinetic or magical energy of a blow before it reaches you. The void grows heavier with every strike it eats, and sooner or later it has to release. It guards you on the turn you open it; keeping it open takes your action again each turn.
[Void Magic: 4]

Sage's Dispel.name: Sage's Dispel
Sage's Dispel.description:
The sage's editing pass: one active magical effect, blessing, affliction, enchantment, or running spell, unraveled into harmless sparks with a librarian's efficiency. Essential against enemy spellcasters; devastating against enemy confidence. The drifting sparks of someone's dismantled preparation are the school's favorite rhetorical device.
[Arcane Magic: 2]

Vanish.name: Vanish
Vanish.description:
A smoke pellet cracks against the ground and the assassin is a rumor: invisible until they attack: repositioning, escaping, or arranging the perfect backstab from the audience's blind spot. The strike spends the silence, always. Enemies who watch the smoke bloom learn the correct response, moving, exactly one experience too late.
[Dagger Fighting: 2]

Weaken.name: Weaken
Weaken.description:
The enchanter's inverse art, applied with a critic's eye: the target's equipment turning brittle and unreliable: weapon damage sagging, armor effectiveness fraying, straps and rivets developing sudden doubts. The warrior is untouched; their confidence in everything they're holding is not. The weakening afflicts gear for the duration rather than breaking it outright, enchanted equipment resists with the indignation of good workmanship, and fighters who hear their own armor creak mid-parry fight differently forever after.
[Enchanting: 3]

Mana Barrier.name: Mana Barrier
Mana Barrier.description:
A large plane of compressed mana raised where the caster insists: shimmering, visible, and shaped to purpose: flat before a doorway, curved around three allies, angled to shed the dragon's breath sideways. Both physical and magical assault meet the same patient refusal. Its shapeability is the technique's whole promotion above lesser wards, concentrated assault visibly drains its shimmer, and sages grade one another by how casually they can wall a corridor mid-sentence. It guards those behind it on the turn you raise it; holding it takes your action again each turn.
[Arcane Magic: 4]

Beguile.name: Beguile
Beguile.description:
Weave dark charisma and pact-enhanced charm to temporarily dominate a weak-willed target, turning them against their allies. The target's eyes glaze with violet light and they fight for you until the spell breaks.
[Charm Magic: 6 · persuasion: 5]

Empower.name: Empower
Empower.description:
The enchanter lends their own gear, or an ally's (never a foe's), a quick promotion: weapons biting harder, armor turning blows aside, the whole kit glowing with arcane light like equipment that just got good news. Craftsmanship, tipped. The visible glow announces exactly who carries the blessing (enemies read enchantment-light fluently and prioritize accordingly), and enchanters ration the art nightly: who glows tomorrow is the party's quietest politics. It empowers one set of gear on the turn you cast it; renewing it takes your action again each turn.
[Enchanting: 2]

Gem Cut.name: Gem Cut
Gem Cut.description:
Cut a rough gem into a perfect facet that maximizes its brilliance and magical conductivity. A well-cut gem is worth several times its uncut form and channels mana more efficiently for enchanting purposes.
[Jewelcrafting: 2]

War Cry.name: War Cry
War Cry.description:
Release a thunderous battle cry that shakes the ground, rattles weapons in their sheaths, and floods your allies with adrenaline. Enemies caught in the shout are momentarily staggered and their morale wavers. Allies gain a surge of courage and fighting spirit. The cry carries orc ancestral magic; it is not just sound, it is intent made audible. Walls crack. Torches flicker. And everyone in earshot knows exactly who is in charge of this fight.
[intimidation: 1]

Backstab.name: Backstab
Backstab.description:
The assassin's oldest theorem: an attack from behind or from stealth landing with massively increased damage: the blade finding the gap between armor plates. Face to face, it is merely a knife and an apology; reaching the position is the actual profession. The fight was won during the approach. The blade just files the conclusion.
[Dagger Fighting: 2]

Hex Bolt.name: Hex Bolt
Hex Bolt.description:
Fire a bolt of cursed energy that homes in on a target. On impact, it deals dark damage and applies a minor hex that reduces the target's accuracy for a short duration. The bolt trails violet smoke and whispers on impact.
[Dark Magic: 2]

Jury-Rig.name: Jury-Rig
Jury-Rig.description:
Temporarily repair a broken weapon, device, or piece of equipment using improvised materials and sheer mechanical stubbornness. The repair holds for the current encounter before falling apart, but by then, you needed it to work.
[Artifice: 2]

Luckstep.name: Luckstep
Luckstep.description: Twist fate through movement: a near miss, a lucky opening, an improbable escape when agility and luck align. Tilt probability for one crucial moment, but only when already moving. Standing still and hoping is not how luck works.

Phantasm.name: Phantasm
Phantasm.description:
A whispered weave slips behind the target's eyes and builds something that isn't there: a blade at the throat, a floor giving way, a face they hoped never to see again. The body believes before the mind can argue: flinching, stumbling, guarding against nothing. Strong wills tear it apart in moments, holding the image taxes the caster's concentration, and a mind that shatters one phantasm is braced against the next for a good while.
[Illusion Magic: 2]

Star Map.name: Star Map
Star Map.description:
Project a celestial map that reveals the positions, movements, and intentions of every entity within a vast radius. The constellation pattern on your skin blazes to life, and for a transcendent moment you perceive the battlefield as the stars see it: from above, from all angles, with perfect clarity. Hidden enemies are exposed. Ambushes are revealed. Optimal strategies crystallize.
[Star Magic: 12]

Web Spin.name: Web Spin
Web Spin.description: Silk leaves the Arachne-Kin's hands in a hissing spray: enemies slow, stick, and stumble as the strands cinch; the clever ones stop moving entirely, which is also a victory. Off the battlefield the same silk becomes climbing lines, trip-snares, bridges, and the world's most passive-aggressive door lock. The glands need time to replenish after a heavy spray, fire makes the strands ash, and rain makes everything regrettable.

Deathgrip.name: Deathgrip
Deathgrip.description:
A skeletal hand of condensed dark magic closes around the target and hauls them across the ground to the knight's feet: living victims arrive stunned by the grave-cold of it; the undead arrive obedient, compelled by something older than fear. Nothing improves a formation like deleting the enemy's backline. The grip needs a clear line and a committed pull, and the dark takes a few breaths to gather that much hunger again.
[Dark Magic: 2]

Deep Cast.name: Deep Cast
Deep Cast.description:
Cast your line into deep or hidden waters to hook something unexpectedly valuable: a mana-eel, a pearl clam, a spirit fish, or the kind of catch that makes other fishermen stare. The deeper you go, the stranger the reward.
[Fishing: 2]

Evil Ward.name: Evil Ward
Evil Ward.description:
The exorcist inscribes a ward that keeps watch so nobody else has to: it pulses with quiet light when evil approaches, and it cannot be fooled by mundane disguise: the possessed merchant, the polite thing wearing a face, all register honestly. A smoke alarm for the unholy. Truly ancient evils sometimes register as a pulse so steady it reads as calm. It is not calm.
[intimidation: 2]

Hex Armor.name: Hex Armor
Hex Armor.description:
Faint violet script crawls across the knight's armor, waiting. Every fist, fang, and blade that lands wakes a curse in answer: fingers that stiffen, luck that sours, a sword arm that suddenly weighs double. Attackers learn quickly that hitting a Hex Knight is a negotiation. The script must be rewoven once spent, and clever enemies simply stop touching the armor, which is, of course, also the point.
[Dark Magic: 3]

Hide Cure.name: Hide Cure
Hide Cure.description:
Quickly tan and cure a fresh monster hide into workable leather, preserving its natural properties: fire resistance from a drake, flexibility from a slime, durability from a basilisk. The cured hide retains the monster's essence and is ready for crafting.
[Leatherworking: 2]

Iron Skin.name: Iron Skin
Iron Skin.description:
The Ironclad's blessing, worn openly: mana hardening the body itself: damage resistance rising beyond what armor provides, skin taking on a faint metallic sheen, the fighter becoming more statue than person and fighting like a statue with opinions. The hardening layers over armor rather than replacing it, the sheen announces the state to everyone with eyes, and blades that skip off bare forearms produce the technique's signature sound: steel's confusion, audible. It guards you on the turn you harden; staying hardened takes your action again each turn.
[athletics: 5]

Mana Bolt.name: Mana Bolt
Mana Bolt.description:
A concentrated bolt of pure mana, fired from the palm with a sound like a plucked string: basic, reliable, and the first spell every Mage learns: arcane damage in its simplest grammar, and it never runs out of style. The bolt is honest about what it is: quick to cast, modest in appetite, and unspectacular by design. Archmages still throw them, because the fundamentals never stopped working; they just stopped being noticed.
[Elemental Magic: 1]

Ore Sense.name: Ore Sense
Ore Sense.description:
Detect valuable ore deposits and mineral veins through stone and earth by reading subtle signs: color patterns, resonance, moisture, and the particular silence that only occurs near dense metal. You know where to dig before you swing the pick.
[Mining: 2]

Pact Bolt.name: Pact Bolt
Pact Bolt.description:
A bolt of pact energy (the summoner's contract given projectile form) striking with arcane damage that honors both signatures: if a summon is active, a portion of the harm flows to the creature as healing, the pact feeding its own. Offense with a benefits package. Creatures maintained by their summoner's marksmanship develop strong opinions about accuracy.
[persuasion: 2]

Quick Map.name: Quick Map
Quick Map.description:
Sketch a functional dungeon map on the fly, marking paths, hazards, points of interest, and the route back to safety. Your map is clear enough that any party member can follow it and accurate enough to trust with their life.
[Dungeon Surveying: 2]

Reinforce.name: Reinforce
Reinforce.description:
Reinforce a piece of armor in the moment it matters, making it significantly harder: metal plates thicken, leather stiffens, and enchantments bind tighter. The effect is dramatic but brief: the armor returns to normal once the magic fades. It guards one set of armor on the turn you cast it; renewing it takes your action again each turn.
[Armorsmithing: 3]

Soul Mend.name: Soul Mend
Soul Mend.description:
Reach into a target's soul and mend the damage that physical healing cannot touch: spiritual wounds, emotional trauma, curse scars, and the invisible marks left by Blessing corruption. Your touch is warm, your light is gentle, and the relief it brings makes people cry. You heal what the world forgot was broken.
[Soul Magic: 5]

Soul Reap.name: Soul Reap
Soul Reap.description:
The scythe swings wreathed in soul-light, and the cut takes twice: flesh parting to the physical edge, and something thinner peeling away with it: a portion of the target's life force flowing back along the haft to close the reaper's own wounds. Harvest, in the professional sense. The drain is a sip, not a feast (the healing is real but modest), and souls notice being skimmed: the reaped fight the reaper afterward with a very particular urgency.
[Dark Magic: 3]

Stormwall.name: Stormwall
Stormwall.description:
The caller drags a hand across the sky and a wall of shrieking wind and stitched lightning stands up between their allies and everything else. Arrows tumble away like leaves; bolts ground themselves harmlessly; anything that wades in melee-close takes the storm's opinion directly. Holding the wall is a sustained argument with the weather; it collapses if the caller's concentration breaks, and the sky sulks a while before agreeing to stand up again.
[Storm Magic: 3]

Time Slip.name: Time Slip
Time Slip.description:
Slip through the timestream, briefly accelerating yourself while everything else crawls. For a few seconds you move at impossible speed: dodging attacks that haven't arrived yet, striking enemies before they react, and repositioning while the world stands still. When you resynchronize, the displaced time gives you a headache.
[Time Magic: 7]

Void Step.name: Void Step
Void Step.description:
Step into the void between dimensions and emerge from a different point in space. The transit is instantaneous and you pass through a place that is dark, cold, and not entirely empty. You can carry willing allies through the void and store small objects in dimensional pockets. Things in the void have noticed you.
[Space Magic: 5]

Wild Call.name: Wild Call
Wild Call.description:
The tamer calls and the land answers with whoever's home: wolves in forests, hawks in open fields, bears in mountains: a wild creature fighting alongside them for the duration, then going home unbonded. Barren places answer thinly; the technique is a conversation with the terrain. The land lends, and lending has manners.
[Beast Keeping: 2]

Windborne.name: Windborne
Windborne.description: Wings spread (or the wind simply agrees) and the Avian-Kin leaves the ground: a short true flight or a long graceful glide, over the pit trap, above the sword swing, onto the balcony everyone else needs stairs for. Height changes every fight it touches. The air asks for open space and honest effort; cramped corridors clip wings, storms argue back, and each flight earns a rest before the next.

Aegis Wall.name: Aegis Wall
Aegis Wall.description:
Raise a translucent wall of compressed mana in front of you or an ally. The wall blocks physical and magical attacks, taking their force until it shatters, and walls raised turn after turn can shape corridors, rooms, or defensive positions. It shimmers with the caster's mana color and is beautiful enough that enemies sometimes hesitate to break it. It guards you or one ally on the turn you raise it; keeping it standing takes your action again each turn.
[Arcane Magic: 2]

Aimed Shot.name: Aimed Shot
Aimed Shot.description:
The ranger stops, breathes, and lets the world narrow to a line: bonus damage scaling with every heartbeat spent aiming, until a perfectly held shot finds the gap the anatomy tried to hide. Patience, weaponized. Those heartbeats are spent standing still in a fight that is not: the style belongs to rangers with cover, discipline, and a party willing to buy them the quiet.
[Archery: 2]

Battle Cry.name: Battle Cry
Battle Cry.description:
The berserker's lungs open and the fight changes temperature: a primal roar that makes nearby enemies flinch mid-swing and floods allies with adrenaline they will later describe as 'inexplicable' and 'excellent.' The flinch is a window, not a wound, and a throat can only summon that much conviction so often before it needs the quiet back.
[intimidation: 2]

Calm Beast.name: Calm Beast
Calm Beast.description:
Soothe an agitated animal or monster through calm presence, scent, and body language. The creature's hostility drops, its panic subsides, and for a brief window it regards you as something other than a threat. Works best before the biting starts.
[Beast Keeping: 2]

Carve Wand.name: Carve Wand
Carve Wand.description:
Shape a temporary magic wand from available wood, bone, or organic material, channeling a spell through it for enhanced effect. The wand lasts for one encounter before its crude structure fails, but a wand is a wand when you need one.
[Woodworking: 2]

Cover Ally.name: Cover Ally
Cover Ally.description:
The intercept: an attack meant for a nearby ally taken instead on the War Priest's shield: thrown into the path with the geometry of sacrifice drilled until it's reflex. The intercepted blow lands with its full honest force on the volunteer. Allies who have been covered once fight afterward with the technique's true product: the certainty of being worth standing in front of.
[Shield Combat: 3]

Crowd Roar.name: Crowd Roar
Crowd Roar.description:
The gladiator plants their feet and roars (the sound of ten thousand arena nights compressed into one throat) and allies feel it land in their chests like a war drum. Blades swing harder. Doubt dies. The roar feeds on drama: the bigger the moment, the bigger the surge, which is why gladiators save it for when the crowd (real or imagined) is on its feet. A voice can only give that much so often before it needs the quiet back.
[intimidation: 1]

Dark Pulse.name: Dark Pulse
Dark Pulse.description:
Darkness detonates outward from the knight's body like a heartbeat made hostile: everything nearby takes the pulse and staggers back, shoved by a pressure that feels less like force and more like the night declining company. Crowds stop being a problem. The pulse radiates from the knight's own position (it clears the room around them, nothing more distant) and the darkness must pool again in the blood before the heart can beat that loudly twice.
[Dark Magic: 2]

Death Mark.name: Death Mark
Death Mark.description:
A soul brand settled onto the target, glowing pale in a spectrum of one; while branded, they take bonus damage from the marker's attacks and cannot hide from the marker's senses; not behind walls, not in crowds, not in the dark that usually loves them. Visible only to the one who needs it. The mark rides one soul at a time and burns for its duration, it guides and sharpens the marker's work alone (the party sees nothing; the intimacy is the point), and prey who somehow learn of the brand acquire its secondary effect: sleeplessness, at range.
[Stealth: 3]

Double Tap.name: Double Tap
Double Tap.description:
Two shots, one breath: the first breaks the guard, the second is already through the gap it made. Speed kills, and the marksman is very fast. The pairing works its magic on defenses that could have stopped one shot (against nothing, it is simply two hits; against a wall, two disappointments) and the double rhythm is a signature that survivors describe accurately, which is how counter-shooters eventually learn to charge for the second shot.
[Firearms: 3]

Earthshift.name: Earthshift
Earthshift.description:
The geomancer reads the ground like clay on a wheel and reshapes it: a wall where there was open field, a pitfall where there was confident footing, a tilted slope that turns a charge into a tumble. Terrain is the oldest weapon and it never misses. The shift works only on honest earth and stone, timber floors and enchanted masonry refuse, and the land holds its new shape but not the caster's stamina, which needs a few breaths between arguments.
[Earth Magic: 1]

Flow State.name: Flow State
Flow State.description:
The Monk's baseline miracle: the body moving on pure instinct, incoming attacks seeming slower and strikes flowing without the drag of conscious thought. Not power. Clarity. A monk who notices they are flowing has stopped. Opponents describe it with the school's favorite complaint: like fencing water that had read your diary.
[acrobatics: 2]

Frost Veil.name: Frost Veil
Frost Veil.description: Surround yourself with drifting snow and cold mist, making you harder to target and reducing incoming fire or heat-based effects. Obscures your form and chills the air enough to slow projectiles and dull flame magic.

Haste Step.name: Haste Step
Haste Step.description:
The chronomancer leans slightly out of the shared second: their personal timeline accelerates, movement and reaction doubling while the world congeals into generous slow motion around them. Blades drift. Openings yawn. Everything else seems to stand politely still. The step is brief by cosmic necessity, and time keeps books: when the acceleration ends, the borrowed moments settle back onto the chronomancer as a wave of visceral, clock-deep fatigue.
[Time Magic: 2]

Iaido Draw.name: Iaido Draw
Iaido Draw.description:
The blade is sheathed. Then the enemy is cut. The steps between happened faster than the eye agreed to witness: iaido's foundational technique, the sword's whole argument compressed into a single fluid motion. Stillness, punctuated. A rattled hand draws merely fast, and merely fast is visible.
[Swordsmanship: 1]

Jinx Field.name: Jinx Field
Jinx Field.description:
Create an area of cursed ground where luck itself turns hostile. Enemies inside the Jinx Field suffer constant minor misfortunes: attacks miss more often, critical hits become critical failures, footing becomes unreliable, and anything that can go wrong does. The field doesn't deal damage directly, but the accumulated bad luck makes enemies hesitate, stumble, and make mistakes that your party can exploit.
[Dark Magic: 1]

Lunar Leap.name: Lunar Leap
Lunar Leap.description: Perform an impossibly graceful leap, crossing distance, dodging danger, or reaching high places as if gravity briefly forgot to apply. Moon Rabbits call this riding the moonbeam. Everyone else calls it deeply unfair.

Mana Blade.name: Mana Blade
Mana Blade.description:
Compressed mana sheathes the sword and extends it: reach doubled for a single thrust, the extension shimmering like an afterimage of the blade that hasn't happened yet. Enemies who measured the distance measured wrong. Duelists who face a spellblade twice learn to add a blade's length to everything: exactly the respect the technique was designed to extort.
[Elemental Magic: 2]

Mana Bloom.name: Mana Bloom
Mana Bloom.description:
Grow a quick plant from available seed and mana-infused soil, producing a useful harvest in minutes rather than weeks. The bloom is temporary and the yield is small, but a single herb or fruit at the right moment can save a life.
[Farming: 3]

Mana Surge.name: Mana Surge
Mana Surge.description:
The caster's body crackles with visible excess: mana regeneration doubling, recovery between spells compressing, the whole casting rhythm shifting up a tempo. Cast faster, cast harder, cast more: for a while, the mage is their own reinforcements. The surge runs its duration and ends without negotiating, the visible crackle marks the caster as the priority target they have honestly become, and the accelerated pace is a loan against the body's calm: post-surge hands shake like they know what they did.
[Elemental Magic: 16]

Mass Charm.name: Mass Charm
Mass Charm.description:
Extend your magical charisma outward in a wave of charm energy, making all hostile humanoids in range momentarily regard you as an ally. The effect is brief but powerful: long enough to stop a fight or redirect a mob.
[performance: 68 · persuasion: 7]

Mind's Eye.name: Mind's Eye
Mind's Eye.description:
The senses attune to combat's undercurrent: enemy movements perceived at the moment of commitment rather than execution (the shoulder before the swing, the weight-shift before the lunge) reaction arriving with supernatural timing for the duration. Fighting people who have already told you their plans. The eye reads bodies rather than minds (feints from masters are forged in the same handwriting; the technique narrows the gap, never closes it), and holding that depth of attention is its own labor: the eye closes when focus frays.
[survival: 5]

Oath Blade.name: Oath Blade
Oath Blade.description:
Swear an oath upon your blade against a specific enemy. Until the oath is fulfilled or broken, all your abilities deal increased damage to that target and you can sense their location. Breaking the oath has divine consequences.
[Swordsmanship: 43]

Overgrowth.name: Overgrowth
Overgrowth.description:
Command nearby plant life to explode into aggressive growth, creating a thicket of grasping vines, thorny barriers, and choking foliage. Enemies are entangled, movement becomes impossible, and thorns tear at anyone who struggles. The forest does not ask permission.
[Nature Magic: 5]

Quick Brew.name: Quick Brew
Quick Brew.description:
The alchemist's answer to poor planning: a combat potion mixed during the battle: reagents from belt pouches, a flask shaken between dodges, drunk or thrown while still fizzing. A real potion's understudy, and gloriously available. Parties learn the sound of desperate rummaging as either salvation or an alchemist about to be interesting.
[Alchemy: 2]

Quick Draw.name: Quick Draw
Quick Draw.description:
The hand was empty; the shot has fired: draw and discharge in one motion faster than most people blink: the opening move that catches the most people off guard, permanently in some cases. It wins the first beat of a fight rather than the fight itself. Everyone who has watched one keeps their hands visible around gunslingers forever after.
[Firearms: 2]

Quick Rune.name: Quick Rune
Quick Rune.description:
Sketch a temporary rune on a nearby surface for an immediate effect: a flash rune to blind, a flame rune to ignite, a ward rune to block. The rune burns out after one activation, but speed is the point.
[Rune Carving: 2]

Raise Dead.name: Raise Dead
Raise Dead.description:
Reanimate a fallen creature as a skeleton minion under your command. The skeleton retains basic combat instincts and follows simple orders; it does not think or speak. What the corpse was decides its skills and manner, never its level, which is yours: a fallen knight makes a better-trained skeleton than a fallen rat, not a stronger one than you.
[Dark Magic: 2]

Rapid Fire.name: Rapid Fire
Rapid Fire.description:
Three arrows, one breath: fired in rapid succession at a single target or spread across several: each slightly less accurate than an aimed shot, the volume of fire more than compensating, probability recruited as a fourth arrow. The rapid trades precision for pressure per volley (suppression is a legitimate school of archery and this is its handshake), three arrows are three arrows of real inventory, and enemies pinned under the rhythm face its designed dilemma: moving into one, or waiting for all three.
[Archery: 3]

Refraction.name: Refraction
Refraction.description:
Redirect an incoming spell through a crystal prism, splitting it into multiple weaker beams that strike different targets or reflecting it back toward the caster. The more complex the spell, the more dangerous the refraction.
[Light Magic: 4]

Rift Slash.name: Rift Slash
Rift Slash.description:
The cross-shaped slash tears open more than air: a rift in space itself, hanging where the blade crossed: raw arcane damage pouring into anything touching it. Swordsmanship graduating into vandalism against geometry. Cutting space leaves the sword-arm briefly unconvinced of distances: the school's veterans call it the fee.
[Rift Magic: 25]

Rune Burst.name: Rune Burst
Rune Burst.description:
Trigger a carved rune from a distance, activating its stored effect remotely. The rune could be an ally's weapon blessing, a dungeon wall trap you carved earlier, or the surprise you left on the door frame for whoever follows you.
[Rune Carving: 4]

Shapeshift.name: Shapeshift
Shapeshift.description:
Bones shift, features flow, and the changeling is wearing someone else's face; not an illusion but honest flesh, warm to the touch and true to a mirror. Voices, mannerisms, and memories are the changeling's own problem: the body is perfect and the performance is not, which is where Deception earns its keep. Each change takes real effort and a private moment; shifting under scrutiny is how changelings get caught, and how legends about them start.
[Deception: 1]

Siren Song.name: Siren Song
Siren Song.description:
A song that reaches past the ears and into the soul: enemies entranced (aggression fading, weapons lowering, forgetting for a few beautiful seconds why they were fighting) while allies feel wounds ache less and resolve harden. It doesn't control minds; it overwhelms hearts. The effect breaks if targets are attacked, but those seconds of stunned vulnerability are often all your party needs.
[performance: 2]

Skill Copy.name: Skill Copy
Skill Copy.description:
Observe a technique and replicate it perfectly with your own body. After witnessing a physical skill, combat style, or ability, you can echo it back: matching the original's speed, power, and precision. Copied techniques fade over time unless reinforced. Your fighting style is everyone's fighting style.
[acrobatics: 5]

Smoke Bomb.name: Smoke Bomb
Smoke Bomb.description:
The bomb lands and the room vanishes in a cloud of choking, blinding smoke: enemies sightless and coughing poison, the fight reorganized around who can see. Which is exactly one person: the alchemist reads the cloud perfectly, having written the formula. The smoke holds for the cloud's lifespan (wind scatters it; open sky shortens it), the poison is a steady toll on everyone inside without the antidote, and fighting a silhouette that navigates your blindness like noon is the experience that retires henchmen.
[Alchemy: 5]

Soul Drain.name: Soul Drain
Soul Drain.description:
Reach toward a target and pull at their life force. Dark energy streams from the target to your hand, dealing necrotic damage and restoring a portion of your health. The target feels a bone-deep cold and existential dread.
[Soul Magic: 2]

Speed Copy.name: Speed Copy
Speed Copy.description:
Rapidly duplicate a scroll, document, or map with perfect accuracy and speed that would make a printing press jealous. The copy is temporary (the ink fades after a day) but sometimes you need the information now, not later.
[Scribal Arts: 2]

Star Arrow.name: Star Arrow
Star Arrow.description:
The archer's magnum opus in one shaft: an arrow infused with so much mana it becomes a streak of light: extreme speed, explosive force, the battlefield illuminated by its passage like a comet taking sides. Your most powerful single shot, and the sky briefly agrees.
