The star spends a deep channel per firing (the glow while drawing is the world's warning and the archer's declaration together), its explosive arrival is a single target's catastrophe with a radius of commentary, and every witness tracks the streak the same way: upward in memory, forever.
[Archery: 37]

Star Chart.name: Star Chart
Star Chart.description:
The astrologer draws a hand across the air and the night sky answers indoors: a slowly turning chart of silver constellations that maps the battlefield onto the heavens. Enemy weaknesses glimmer as dark stars; allied strikes find their marks as if guided by orbit. The chart demands the astrologer's ongoing attention to keep true, fades if they take a hard hit, and the stars prefer not to be consulted twice in quick succession.
[Star Magic: 1]

Storm Cage.name: Storm Cage
Storm Cage.description:
The prison with live wiring: an enemy trapped in a cage whose bars are continuous lightning: shocking on contact, the interior filled with interference that disrupts magic. Caging a champion is a duel of reserves, and escape attempts are billed in real time. Captured mages face its special insult: the interference garbles even their complaints.
[Lightning Magic: 30]

Storm Dive.name: Storm Dive
Storm Dive.description:
Airborne, the dragoon becomes a drill: spinning with spear extended, the rotation generating a wind tunnel that accelerates the descent: a falling auger with a person's judgment attached. Armor means nothing; armor was designed for attacks that arrive politely. Craters left by storm dives have a signature twist the school recognizes with pride.
[acrobatics: 65]

Storm Rune.name: Storm Rune
Storm Rune.description:
A lightning rune bites into the weapon and stays: every contact discharges into the target: bonus voltage, seized muscles, a brief stun that turns exchanges into free hits. The blade hums like a held breath. The rune's charge is finite, spent strike by strike, and carving a fresh one demands a steady hand and a pause the battle may charge admission for.
[Rune Carving: 5]

Style Aura.name: Style Aura
Style Aura.description:
Project an aura of immaculate style that inspires confidence in allies and makes enemies hesitate before attacking someone who clearly has their life together. The effect is purely social, but in Luxcellia, social power is real power.
[Fashion Styling: 3]

Sweet Deal.name: Sweet Deal
Sweet Deal.description:
Negotiate a dramatically favorable trade: buying at a discount, selling at a premium, or structuring a deal so good the other party suspects they have been enchanted. They have not. You are simply very good.
[Merchant Trade: 3]

Sword Draw.name: Sword Draw
Sword Draw.description:
The sheath whispers and the cut has happened: a lightning draw-and-slash, the blade home again before the enemy's understanding arrives. The duel's first word, spoken before hello. The school's philosophy in one motion: the fight's most important strike is the one before the fight.
[Swordsmanship: 1]

Throw Bomb.name: Throw Bomb
Throw Bomb.description:
The alchemist's oldest argument: a hurled sphere that detonates on impact in fire and hissing acid, damaging everything in the blast and leaving a scorch mark shaped like a lesson. The explosion is satisfyingly loud, which the alchemist insists is a safety feature. Each bomb is real inventory (brewed, stoppered, and carried at the alchemist's own risk) and throwing accuracy is a separate skill from brewing brilliance, a distinction parties learn in one memorable afternoon.
[Alchemy: 2]

Titan Blow.name: Titan Blow
Titan Blow.description:
Deliver a single devastating strike with the force of a landslide. The impact generates a shockwave that damages everything nearby, shatters armor, and sends lighter enemies flying. When you connect, the ground cracks. When you miss, the air cracks. There is no subtle version of this attack.
[athletics: 5]

Titan Grip.name: Titan Grip
Titan Grip.description:
Your rage-enhanced strength lets you wield two-handed weapons in one hand, dual-wield heavy weapons, or use improvised weapons that no sane person would pick up. Furniture, boulders, and other enemies are all valid options.
[Unarmed Combat: 4]

Totem Ward.name: Totem Ward
Totem Ward.description:
The shaman plants a spirit totem and the ground around it becomes defended: allies within taking reduced damage and shrugging off fear as the carved faces glare outward on their behalf. A checkpoint with opinions, and a totem cannot follow a retreat it disapproves of. It guards allies near the totem on the turn you plant or wake it; waking it again takes your action again each turn.
[Nature Magic: 2]

Trick Shot.name: Trick Shot
Trick Shot.description:
The gunslinger reads the room's geometry in an instant and fires at the wall: the shot ricocheting off a calculated surface to strike the target crouched safely behind cover. They didn't think cover mattered. They were nearly right. Enemies who watch a bullet turn a corner develop a haunted relationship with architecture that outlasts the fight.
[Firearms: 2]

Antler Ward.name: Antler Ward
Antler Ward.description:
Manifest a soft woodland ward shaped like branching antlers. The ward steadies nearby allies, warns of approaching danger, and briefly deflects hostile intent, curses, or fear effects with calm natural magic.
[Nature Magic: 2]

Arcane Rain.name: Arcane Rain
Arcane Rain.description:
The volley goes up, and the sky takes over: arrows arcing high and falling across a great swath of ground, each one detonating in elemental fire on arrival. Formations dissolve. Charges reconsider. The sky itself becomes the weapon, briefly and gorgeously. The rain asks for open air overhead and a full quiver's commitment, and after the storm the archer's arms and the archer's ammunition both need serious replenishing.
[Archery: 25]

Assassinate.name: Assassinate
Assassinate.description:
The signature killing technique, named without euphemism: a single, perfectly executed strike designed to end a fight in one blow. When conditions align, nothing survives this. The strike is the receipt; the stalk, the angle, and the patience are the purchase. Its existence reshapes every room the profession enters: somewhere between setup and stillness, someone is already dead and doesn't know it.
[Stealth: 72]

Astral Step.name: Astral Step
Astral Step.description:
Movement fast enough to leave the truth behind: a glowing afterimage stands where the fighter was, patient and convincing, while attacks aimed with perfect timing hit perfect nothing. You're already behind them. The step spends explosive effort for one relocation (it is an escape and an ambush wearing the same motion) and enemies who fall for the afterimage twice start attacking the empty spaces on principle, which is its own kind of victory.
[acrobatics: 54]

Battle Brew.name: Battle Brew
Battle Brew.description:
Concoct a quick combat stimulant that boosts an ally's physical or magical output for a short burst. The effects are potent, the side effects are manageable, and the taste is what you would expect from something mixed in a flask during combat.
[Brewing: 2]

Beast Merge.name: Beast Merge
Beast Merge.description:
The tamer and the beast briefly stop being two: a merging that lends the tamer the creature's physical gifts, claws, wings, gills, or speed, the bond made literal, flesh cooperating across species out of pure trust. The fusion transforms the tamer's combat capability for its window and then separates cleanly, it borrows traits rather than mass (merging with a bear lends the claws, not the tonnage), and the intimacy is real: beasts remember being worn, and only deep bonds survive the strangeness twice.
[Beast Keeping: 11]

Beast Sense.name: Beast Sense
Beast Sense.description: Your animal heritage grants senses far beyond human capability. You can hear heartbeats through walls, smell emotions on the wind, see clearly in near-total darkness, and track a target across miles of wilderness. Your instincts are primal and reliable; you know when you're being watched, when someone is lying, and when a fight is about to start. The downside is that strong smells, loud noises, and someone scratching behind your ears all hit harder too.

Benediction.name: Benediction
Benediction.description:
The priest speaks prevention over an ally: divine protection settling in quiet reserve, waiting to catch the next status effect that would land: poison declined, paralysis refused, fear returned to sender, charm and curse alike bounced at the threshold. Prevention is the best medicine, and this is prevention with a signature. The benediction absorbs one affliction and spends itself (choosing who carries it into which fight is the priest's nightly chess), and allies who feel a curse simply not arrive develop the correct theology: gratitude, in advance.
[Divinity: 5]

Blade Dance.name: Blade Dance
Blade Dance.description:
The swordwork stops being separate decisions: a flowing state where each attack chains into the next: faster, harder, and looking, to any witness, like choreography that happens to be lethal. Its rhythm punishes crowds that expected pauses between deaths. The form's oldest compliment: it looked rehearsed. It wasn't. That's the discipline.
[Swordsmanship: 4]

Blade Storm.name: Blade Storm
Blade Storm.description:
The fan of hidden edges: knives, needles, and shuriken thrown in one wide arc: each projectile coated in a different substance, the enemy's healer left triaging a chemistry exam. Mixed coatings defeat any single antidote by design. Survivors describe the special despair: knowing something is in the wounds, and not knowing which.
[Dagger Fighting: 6]

Blade Waltz.name: Blade Waltz
Blade Waltz.description:
The rhythm where categories dissolve: every dodge transitioning into a strike, every strike into a dodge: offense and defense the same continuous movement, a duel in three-four time. You are dancing. They are losing. Enemies describe it with the school's favorite testimony: there was never a moment to attack. There were only movements, and all of them were hers.
[Swordsmanship: 25]

Blood Armor.name: Blood Armor
Blood Armor.description:
The mage's own blood rises through the skin and hardens: a crimson, semi-solid carapace: life force made manifest as armor, catching blows that should have reached the life itself. It is beautiful in the way that makes bystanders step back. The armor is drawn from the mage's actual vitality (raising it costs health up front), and blood-armored mages bleed style: every crack in the carapace is a very literal expense report. It guards you on the turn you raise it; keeping it hardened takes your action again each turn.
[Blood Magic: 4]

Blood Curse.name: Blood Curse
Blood Curse.description:
The curse closes the door healing uses so the target's wounds simply will not shut: existing injuries weeping steadily, healing magic arriving muffled and partial, every cut an ongoing toll instead of a finished blow. Attrition, weaponized. The curse worsens what exists rather than creating new harm (an unwounded target merely carries a threat), it can be cleansed by sufficient light or outlasted by sufficient stubbornness, and healers hate it with a specific professional fury the mage finds flattering.
[Blood Magic: 5]

Blood Drain.name: Blood Drain
Blood Drain.description:
The mage opens a channel and the target's vitality answers the pull: life force flowing out as visible crimson threads, their strength becoming the mage's mending in real time. Vampirism with a scholar's precision. The threads are gorgeous and utterly incriminating, and stolen vitality sits slightly wrong in the veins: borrowed blood always knows.
[Blood Magic: 2]

Broken Halo.name: Broken Halo
Broken Halo.description: Manifest a cracked halo of dim gold and shadow. Increases resistance to fear, charm, and divine pressure. Nearby enemies feel the weight of judgment: an unsettling pressure that makes aggression harder to sustain.

Countersong.name: Countersong
Countersong.description:
Play a counter-melody that disrupts magical effects. Hostile enchantments, illusions, and charm effects targeting your allies unravel against the dissonant interference. The musical equivalent of jamming a signal.
[performance: 41 · persuasion: 6]

Cross Slash.name: Cross Slash
Cross Slash.description:
Two diagonal cuts arriving as one thought: an X carved across the target so quickly the second slash finishes before the first wound has announced itself: the pain arriving after the geometry. Break the flow and it is merely two swings. Its distinctive scar is a calling card that veterans of the style recognize, sometimes fondly.
[Swordsmanship: 2]

Cryo Prison.name: Cryo Prison
Cryo Prison.description:
The prison built by subtraction: an enemy encased in layered enchanted ice: the prison absorbing heat, the interior growing progressively colder, a cell that punishes its occupant for the crime of having a temperature. Fire magic can crack it. Anything else just slides off. Freed prisoners emerge with the parting gift: frostbite, and a lasting flinch at the sound of settling ice.
[Ice Magic: 7]

Curse Blade.name: Curse Blade
Curse Blade.description:
Hexes coil down the blade like ivy, and every wound plants one: attack sours, then defense, then speed, then aim, the curses cycling with each hit until the target is fighting themselves as much as the knight. Long fights tilt one strike at a time. The blade holds only so much malice per weaving (spent curses must be re-etched) and cleansing magic can strip a stack, which frustrates Hex Knights immensely and audibly.
[Dark Magic: 2]

Dragon Claw.name: Dragon Claw
Dragon Claw.description:
Dragon fire gloves the knight's hands and the technique goes feral: claw-like sweeps at melee's most personal range, flames hot enough to melt steel, every swipe leaving burning gashes. Elegant swordwork this is not; effective it extremely is. Armored veterans who watch steel run like wax reorganize their entire understanding of the fight.
[intimidation: 2]

Dragon Dive.name: Dragon Dive
Dragon Dive.description:
The swordsman goes up, an honest leap with theatrical hang-time, and comes down like a dragon deciding the ground owed it money: massive impact on the target, a shockwave that scatters everyone adjacent, a crater as a signature. The dive commits everything to the descent; while airborne the swordsman is a declared intention with no steering, and a target that reads the leap has exactly the shadow's width of warning to be elsewhere.
[acrobatics: 4]

Dragon Fang.name: Dragon Fang
Dragon Fang.description:
The two-hit signature, named for the bite: an upward slash that launches the enemy skyward, and the midair thrust that spikes them back down: the pattern of a dragon's jaws closing, performed in steel and altitude. Stylish and devastating, in the school's preferred order. The fang commits to both beats (the launch without the spike is a gift of repositioning to the enemy), the midair thrust demands acrobatic conviction, and the crater-and-bounce conclusion is the technique's calling card: veterans identify the school from the sound.
[acrobatics: 4]

Dragon Fist.name: Dragon Fist
Dragon Fist.description:
Concentrate overwhelming ki into a single fist until the energy becomes visible as a draconic aura around your arm. The punch delivers force equivalent to a siege weapon. Use sparingly: your arm needs time to recover.
[Unarmed Combat: 8]

Dragon Form.name: Dragon Form
Dragon Form.description:
The knight stops borrowing from the vein and moves in: full draconic hybrid transformation: scales armoring, wings unfolding, a breath weapon arriving like an heirloom. Partial, the scholars insist. Devastating, the witnesses correct. There is no incognito after wings, and returning to human shape always takes one moment longer than the knight expects. They stop mentioning it. They never stop noticing.
[Fire Magic: 19]

Dragon Rage.name: Dragon Rage
Dragon Rage.description:
The dragon's fury moves in: every attribute surging, pain shrinking to gossip, strikes landing with hoard-guarding conviction, and the eyes going slit-pupiled and unselective. The fury is not on anyone's side but the dragon's. Allies learn to give the rage room; the smart ones announce themselves loudly and from behind cover. When it burns out, the borrowed wrath leaves like a tide, and the fighter stands in the wreckage doing arithmetic about who is still standing.
[intimidation: 24]

Dragon Roar.name: Dragon Roar
Dragon Roar.description:
The roar arrives before the sound does: a draconic pressure that stuns everything hostile in reach, rattles the ground, carries for miles, and reminds allies at a cellular level whose side they are lucky to be on. Battles pause to acknowledge it. The roar spends the throat and the presence both; it cannot be whispered, cannot be repeated quickly, and cannot be taken back: everything for miles now knows exactly where the dragon-voiced stands.
[intimidation: 9]

Dragon Wing.name: Dragon Wing
Dragon Wing.description:
Spectral wings unfold from the back in translucent draconic glory: true flight for a short, glorious window, plus a wingspan that buffets enemies sideways and swats projectiles out of their convictions. Ground tactics stop applying to exactly one person. The wings hold for a brief duration and vanish without negotiating, so altitude should be chosen with the landing in mind, and their unmistakable silhouette announces the flier to everything with eyes.
[acrobatics: 14]

Field Patch.name: Field Patch
Field Patch.description:
Perform a rapid field repair on damaged armor: hammering out dents, replacing rivets, and patching gaps with whatever metal is available. The repair restores protection and keeps the tank standing for one more fight.
[Armorsmithing: 2]

Flame Lance.name: Flame Lance
Flame Lance.description:
Precision pyromancy: a concentrated jet of fire projected in one straight line: piercing through lighter obstacles, delivering heavy flame to everything along its length, a surgeon's answer in an arsonist's discipline. The lance burns its line and only its line (aim is the entire spell; enemies beside the beam watch it pass with gratitude), lighter cover yields and heavy stone ends the argument, and pyromancers who master the lance are trusted indoors, which in their profession is the highest compliment available.
[Fire Magic: 3]

Gale Thrust.name: Gale Thrust
Gale Thrust.description:
The spear thrusts and the air goes with it: a lance of compressed wind pressure extending the strike to medium range, hitting like a physical blow delivered by weather with excellent manners. Reach, without the courtesy of warning. The gale carries a single thrust's force and softens with distance (at the far edge it shoves rather than skewers), the compression demands full committed form, half-hearted thrusts produce breeze and commentary, and dragoons use it to teach archers that distance was always negotiable.
[athletics: 12]

Gentle Step.name: Gentle Step
Gentle Step.description:
Move with quiet, graceful precision through forests, crowds, snow, loose leaves, or sacred ground without disturbing the scene. Deerkin are difficult to startle and harder to track when they choose gentleness over speed.
[survival: 1]

Ground Slam.name: Ground Slam
Ground Slam.description:
The weapon comes down into the earth with force the earth takes personally: stone cracking, a shockwave rolling outward, every enemy in the ring staggered and knocked from their footing as the stone heaves beneath them. Formation-breaking, written in bedrock. The slam spends its fury on balance rather than bodies (the damage is real, but the stagger is the prize), it wants solid ground to argue with, and the swing's full commitment leaves the warrior planted for one honest beat afterward.
[athletics: 3]

Hearty Meal.name: Hearty Meal
Hearty Meal.description:
Prepare a substantial meal that restores significant health and stamina to everyone who eats it. The food is simple, filling, and made with the kind of love that makes wounds close faster. Works best when served hot.
[Cooking: 2]

Heavensfall.name: Heavensfall
Heavensfall.description:
Ascend beyond normal jump height using pure mana propulsion, then descend at terminal velocity with your spear blazing. The impact is cataclysmic: crater, shockwave, dust cloud, everything. Boss-fight finisher energy.
[Archery: 7]

Holy Strike.name: Holy Strike
Holy Strike.description:
The Paladin's fundamental: divine light infused into the weapon, one strike delivering bonus light damage: extra effective against undead and demons, the sword glowing golden at the exact moment of impact. Judgment, notarized, at swing speed.
[Divinity: 3]

Ignore Pain.name: Ignore Pain
Ignore Pain.description:
Rage files the pain for later: incoming damage reduced, injuries that should slow the berserker simply declining to: the body's complaints stamped, sorted, and archived while the fight remains in session. You'll feel it all later. That's a problem for future you. The suppression runs its duration and mutes signal rather than damage (the wounds are real and patient; the book is exact), it demands genuine rage as fuel, and future you (the technique's designated creditor) is famously eloquent on the subject, from the floor, the next morning.
[athletics: 5]

Inner Peace.name: Inner Peace
Inner Peace.description:
The monk sits down in the middle of everything and means it: meditation so deep that health and ki regenerate rapidly, the battlefield quieting around them out of respect or confusion. Recovery, achieved by stopping. Interruption ends it instantly. Enemies who watch a wounded monk breathe and rise refreshed learn the school's most alarming lesson: the monk was never in a hurry.
[athletics: 15]

Jump Strike.name: Jump Strike
Jump Strike.description:
The dragoon leaves the ground like the ground was a suggestion: a towering leap, a heartbeat of silhouette against the sky, and a descending spear-point that converts fall height directly into damage. Low ceilings are the school's ancestral enemy. Every dragoon eventually learns the discipline's one commandment: the landing is also your problem.
[Polearm Combat: 2]

Living Rune.name: Living Rune
Living Rune.description:
The rune settles onto an ally's skin like a sleeping guardian that wakes the instant you draw it: a shield blooming, a warding flash, and then it fades, duty done. It cannot be left waiting for danger that has not arrived; it answers the peril in front of you now. It guards one ally on the turn you draw it; guarding them again takes your action again the next turn.
[Enchanting: 50]

Magnum Opus.name: Magnum Opus
Magnum Opus.description:
The ultimate Bard ability. Perform your masterpiece: a composition that channels every ounce of your magical talent, charisma, and emotion into a single piece of music that warps reality around it. Allies are healed, empowered, and shielded. Enemies are damaged, weakened, and disoriented. The battlefield transforms into a concert stage with you at the center.
[performance: 12]

Mana Rapier.name: Mana Rapier
Mana Rapier.description:
Compressed mana sheathes the rapier and commits: reach doubled for the duration, arcane damage riding every thrust, the extended blade shimmering like a heat mirage that keeps drawing blood. Fencing at a distance the opponent's footwork was never taught. The extension holds while fed (a steady mana bleed the duelist budgets like breath), the mirage-blade is visible to anyone watching carefully (which in a duel is everyone) and its answer is simple and cruel: fence the air where the blade might be.
[Arcane Magic: 26]

Overchannel.name: Overchannel
Overchannel.description:
The mage pushes past the spell's safe limits on purpose: mana forced in beyond capacity, power multiplying while control frays at the seams, the spell visibly distorting into something bigger, hungrier, and less polite. Overchanneled spells drift, splash, and improvise at the edges. Habitual users develop the known signature: spectacular results, and eyebrows that grew back differently.
[Elemental Magic: 7]

Pack Strike.name: Pack Strike
Pack Strike.description:
The tamer speaks one word and the pack becomes a single decision: every bonded creature striking the same target at once: fangs low, talons high, something heavy through the middle. Coordination as a weapon. Asking the whole family to commit means the whole family committed: praise, and possibly a shared kill's worth of dinner, is contractually implied.
[Beast Keeping: 2]

Palm Strike.name: Palm Strike
Palm Strike.description:
The monk's open palm arrives quiet and leaves loud: ki channeled into the point of impact, force transferring through armor to argue with the structures inside: ribs, resolve, internal certainty. The armor is fine, and that is the joke. Veterans who take one well-placed palm stop trusting their breastplate in a way that never fully heals.
[Unarmed Combat: 2]

Perfect Fit.name: Perfect Fit
Perfect Fit.description:
Adjust or create clothing that fits its wearer so perfectly it provides a social advantage: confidence, presence, the unshakeable feeling that you belong wherever you are standing. In Luxcellia, the right fit is the difference between an entrance and an entrance.
[Tailoring: 2]

Phase Shift.name: Phase Shift
Phase Shift.description:
Phase briefly through solid matter, becoming intangible for a few heartbeats. Attacks pass through you and you can move through walls, locked doors, and enemy formations untouched. The world blurs at the edges when you phase, and for a moment you exist everywhere and nowhere at once.
[Stealth: 5]

Primal Roar.name: Primal Roar
Primal Roar.description:
The roar crosses the line from sound to physics: a shockwave rolling out in a cone: enemies shoved backward and deafened, glass shattering, the world in front of the fighter comprehensively informed. Allies stand behind the noise or become percussion. Everything within a mile now knows two facts: where the fighter is, and that they are unhappy.
[intimidation: 34]

Prize Catch.name: Prize Catch
Prize Catch.description:
The Fisher's masterpiece, performed against an uncooperative co-author: a difficult catch landed: the fish fighting back, the water arguing, the payoff an ingredient that makes an alchemist weep with envy, rare cooking and crafting materials pulled from water that did not want to give them. The catch demands water worth fishing and patience worth the name (the prize scales with the venue; legendary waters hold legendary arguments), each attempt is a genuine contest, and kitchens supplied by a prize-fisher develop reputations that travel farther than the fisher does.
[Fishing: 3]

Realm Merge.name: Realm Merge
Realm Merge.description:
The ultimate Spirit Walker technique. Merge the spirit realm and the material world into a single overlapping reality. The dead walk beside the living, spiritual barriers dissolve, and you stand at the threshold between worlds as its master. Every spirit answers your call, every shadow reveals its secrets.
[Spirit Channeling: 95]

Rescue Pull.name: Rescue Pull
Rescue Pull.description:
The shieldbearer sees an ally falling and simply arrives: a full charge through whatever is in the way, one fist in their collar, and a rough, fast drag behind the shield's shadow. It is not gentle. It is not optional. It works. The pull demands a clear enough line to charge and everything the legs have, and the rescued party is deposited safe, winded, and (tradition holds) briefly furious about the collar.
[athletics: 34]

Restoration.name: Restoration
Restoration.description:
Channel a surge of golden healing light that closes wounds, neutralizes poisons, cures diseases, and regenerates damage that other healers consider permanent. The light is warm, comforting, and feels like being held. At its peak, you can heal multiple allies simultaneously.
[Light Magic: 7]

Reveal Evil.name: Reveal Evil
Reveal Evil.description:
The exorcist's floodlight: every evil entity across a wide area forced into the open: disguises peeling, invisibility collapsing, possessions dragged into visibility with the host's own shadow pointing at the tenant. No shadow can hide from the Exorcist's judgment. The reveal exposes rather than destroys (what stands revealed must still be fought, and it is now both visible and furious), the great unveiling spends deep grace in one pulse, and entities that felt the light find the exorcist's face very memorable, mutually.
[Insight: 8]

Rune Circle.name: Rune Circle
Rune Circle.description:
A wide circle of runic script blooms across the ground and begins taxing magic itself: spellcasting inside costs dramatically more mana, turning enemy mages into misers mid-battle and grand incantations into ruinous gambles. Counter-magic as territory. The circle suppresses within its drawn bounds only (mages who step out resume their lifestyle), holds while its script stays unbroken, and it is gloriously impartial: allied casters inside pay the same tariff, so placement is the entire art.
[Rune Carving: 12]

Rune Strike.name: Rune Strike
Rune Strike.description:
The rune knight's alphabet, spoken with a sword: a strike from a rune-inscribed weapon, the script activating on impact: elemental damage detonating in the wound. Knights carve during lulls the way archers fletch. Rune knights duel each other in a language civilians only see as light.
[Arcane Magic: 3]

Sacred Ward.name: Sacred Ward
Sacred Ward.description:
The priest touches an ally's shoulder and leaves protection there: a divine ward, invisible until struck, that takes the force of the blows aimed at them and shatters in a burst of light with a temper, capable of dazzling the attacker who spent their blow on it. Mercy with a counterpunch, and choosing who to guard is the priest's constant arithmetic. It guards one ally on the turn you place it; guarding them again takes your action again the next turn.
[Divinity: 2]

Second Life.name: Second Life
Second Life.description: When you would die, you don't. Instead, you revive with a burst of power proportional to how unfair the death was. Each revival leaves a permanent mark, a white streak of hair, a changed eye, a scar that doesn't fade, and the cost escalates. Dying is never free, even for the Undying.

Second Wind.name: Second Wind
Second Wind.description:
At rage's peak, the berserker's body does the impossible bookkeeping: heart rate steadying inside the storm, wounds closing slightly, stamina flowing partially back: a recovery state stolen from the middle of fury. The calm before the next storm, hosted inside the current one. The wind rises only when rage genuinely peaks (it cannot be invoked from calm; the fury is the fuel line), its mending is a patch rather than a cure, and enemies who watch a bleeding berserker breathe and straighten experience the fight's most honest omen.
[athletics: 38]

Seeker Shot.name: Seeker Shot
Seeker Shot.description:
The arrow leaves the string already interested: enchanted to track its target, it banks around pillars, curves past cover, and adjusts mid-flight with the patience of a professional grudge. Hiding becomes a delay tactic. It can chase what it knows, not what it guesses: the enchantment needs a clean look at the mark before loosing.
[Archery: 3]

Self-Repair.name: Self-Repair
Self-Repair.description:
The automaton's mana core brightens through the seams as inner filaments crawl across cracked plating like glowing solder, knitting bent frames back into true: the body rebuilding itself with the patience of a workshop. Deep structural wounds leave faint weld-lines that a sharp-eyed engineer can read like a history.
[Engineering: 1]

Shadow Army.name: Shadow Army
Shadow Army.description:
Every shadow present, allies', enemies', furniture's, rises as dark constructs that fight for the caster, each clone mimicking its source's combat style with dark damage. The enemy champion's own shadow, using the champion's own technique, on the other side. A crowded battle is an armory; an empty plain at noon is a disappointment.
[Shadow Magic: 36]

Shadow Bind.name: Shadow Bind
Shadow Bind.description:
The target's shadow is nailed to the ground, and the target discovers they are attached to it: feet rooted mid-stride, position locked, while hands and voice remain insultingly free. Archers love it. Duelists build entire finishes on it. The bind needs a shadow to seize (flat noon light and true darkness both starve it) and holding a struggling person by their silhouette takes focus that must be regathered once the shadow tears loose.
[Shadow Magic: 6]

Shadow Bolt.name: Shadow Bolt
Shadow Bolt.description:
Fire a bolt of condensed shadow that deals dark damage and briefly dims the area around the impact point. The bolt is nearly invisible in low light, making it difficult to dodge when fighting in darkness.
[Shadow Magic: 2]

Shadow Rise.name: Shadow Rise
Shadow Rise.description:
The monarch gestures at a fallen enemy, and their shadow peels off the corpse and stands up: a soldier of darkness wearing the shape and skills of what it was, loyal now to the one who called it. Every battlefield is a recruitment drive. The rising asks for an intact shadow and a fresh fall; the long-dead and the burned-away yield nothing, daylight makes new soldiers thin and reluctant, and each raising takes a real measure of the monarch's will.
[Shadow Magic: 2]

Shadow Step.name: Shadow Step
Shadow Step.description:
The mage melts into shadow here and stands up in shadow there: directly behind the target, deposited by the darkness itself into a perfect striking position. Stylish and lethal, in the school's mandatory order. The step wants shadows at both doors (bright open ground starves it), its range is honest and its arrival is committed (behind the enemy is also within the enemy's reach, one turn later) and duelists who face shadow-steppers develop the profession's signature spin-flinch, which the mages consider applause.
[Shadow Magic: 13]

Shadow Swap.name: Shadow Swap
Shadow Swap.description:
One blink and the mage has traded places with a shadow: their own, or the shadow of anyone standing carelessly nearby. To observers it reads as teleportation with a grudge: the mage is suddenly there, and possibly someone else is suddenly here, mid-swing, facing the wrong way. The swap needs a shadow to trade with (bright noon and pitch dark both refuse), and swapping with another creature's shadow drags no one but repositions everything: geometry as a weapon.
[Shadow Magic: 17]

Shadow Walk.name: Shadow Walk
Shadow Walk.description:
Shadows become doorways: the walker sliding from one patch of darkness into another nearby, bypassing the obstacles, enemies, and awkward conversations in between. Silent. Instant. Terrifying: mostly in retrospect, when the guards compare notes. The walk connects existing shadows at short range (no darkness at the destination, no door), each crossing is quick but not free, and rooms lit deliberately bright are the countermeasure everyone eventually pays for, which shadow-walkers take as a compliment.
[Stealth: 8]

Knight's Shield Bash.name: Knight's Shield Bash
Knight's Shield Bash.description:
The knight's shield stops being defensive for exactly one motion: rammed into face or center mass, staggering the enemy backward. Simple, brutal, effective: the sound alone is a percussion note that means the knight disagrees. Works best on targets with faces at shield height: giants require creativity or a box.
[Shield Combat: 1]

Shield Wall.name: Shield Wall
Shield Wall.description:
The vanguard raises the shield, braces, and becomes immovable law: incoming damage dramatically reduced, a person deciding to be a wall and proving it. A wall does not counterattack; it outlasts. Its true product is time: every second the vanguard refuses to fall is a second the party spends winning. The stance protects on the turn you take it; holding it takes your action again each turn.
[Shield Combat: 2]

Silent Kill.name: Silent Kill
Silent Kill.description:
The professional grade: a target eliminated so quickly and quietly that the room continues its conversation: the body doesn't fall, you catch it. No sound. No alarm. Just one fewer voice, unnoticed. The kill demands true stealth, a clean approach, and a target genuinely unaware (alerted prey converts the technique into an ordinary and much louder fight), lowering a body silently is its own trained art, and the signature absence, no scream, no thud, no anything, is how survivors eventually realize, too late to matter, what walked among them.
[Stealth: 57]

Singularity.name: Singularity
Singularity.description:
Create a localized gravity singularity: a point of such immense gravitational force that everything nearby is dragged toward it irresistibly. Enemies, projectiles, debris, even light bends toward the crushing point. The singularity is brief but devastating: what it catches, it compresses. What it releases, it scatters. The ground around it is permanently cratered.
[Gravity Magic: 20]

Solar Flare.name: Solar Flare
Solar Flare.description:
The ultimate fire spell, meaning the discipline stopped iterating: the heat of the sun channeled into a single blast: blindingly bright, vaporizing nearly anything in its path, the word 'nearly' doing load-bearing work. The channel is long and unmistakable: the world's mercy is that you can see the sun being borrowed. Afterward the path is simply gone, and the air above it wavers for an hour.
[Fire Magic: 57]

Sonic Blast.name: Sonic Blast
Sonic Blast.description:
Performance magic, concentrated past politeness: a blast of amplified sound: the shockwave dealing physical damage, shattering glass, sending lighter enemies tumbling like criticism. Your instrument becomes a cannon, a sentence the bard delivers with unseemly delight. The blast fires in the direction the performance aims (the instrument's voice, weaponized whole), each release spends breath, strings, and dignity together, and venues that have hosted one maintain the profession's oldest ban: no bards near the good windows.
[performance: 27]

Soul Siphon.name: Soul Siphon
Soul Siphon.description:
Latch an invisible tether onto a target's life force and drain it over several seconds, healing yourself as their vitality transfers. The target feels a creeping chill and growing exhaustion. Cruel, effective, and sustainable.
[Soul Magic: 5]

Spell Dance.name: Spell Dance
Spell Dance.description:
The spellblade stops choosing between arts: a combat trance where every sword swing automatically channels its matching spell: the rising cut carrying flame, the parry ringing with ward-light, offense and casting merged into one fluid grammar. Watching it is watching an argument won in cursive. The dance runs while the trance holds and demands both disciplines already mastered (the trance merges skills, it does not supply them), and when it ends the spellblade lands hard on both bills at once: sword-arm and mana, paid together.
[Arcane Magic: 31]

Spell Store.name: Spell Store
Spell Store.description:
The Spellblade's defining trick: a spell cast into the weapon and banked: riding silent in the steel until the next melee strike releases it on impact, blade damage and magical effect arriving as one sentence. Casting time, prepaid. The store holds one spell until spent (the weapon carries a single loaded argument; choosing it is the art), the charge waits patiently through parries and footwork for genuine contact, and duelists who trade blows with a spellblade learn the school's anxiety: any given swing might be the loaded one.
[Enchanting: 9]

Spell Weave.name: Spell Weave
Spell Weave.description:
The sage stops casting spells one at a time: two workings merged into a single enhanced cast: a barrier woven with gravity that drags what it blocks, a bolt braided with time-slow, chains carrying spatial rend in every link. Creativity is your strongest stat, and the weave is its examination. The weave merges two spells the sage genuinely commands (fusion amplifies mastery; it does not substitute for it), holding two structures in one cast is the discipline's famous strain, and enemies who prepared for either component meet, instead, the conversation between them.
[Arcane Magic: 36]

Spike Field.name: Spike Field
Spike Field.description:
The geomancer speaks one sharp word downward and the ground answers in dozens: stone spikes erupting across the target area, impaling the slow and converting the terrain into a jagged zone nothing sensible crosses. Area denial, written in exclamation points. The field claims its area and holds its shape after the eruption (the spikes are honest stone: climbable by the patient, cover for the clever), it wants true ground beneath it, and raising a hedge of geology leaves the caster's connection to the earth briefly spent.
[Earth Magic: 6]

Spirit Bond.name: Spirit Bond
Spirit Bond.description:
The shaman befriends rather than binds: a friendly spirit settling into companionship: a hawk-spirit sharpening perception, a hearth-spirit mending slowly and constantly, a stone-spirit shrugging off an element. It endures as long as the friendship is honored. Neglect the relationship and the gift quietly, politely, goes home.
[Spirit Channeling: 2]

Spirit Gaze.name: Spirit Gaze
Spirit Gaze.description:
The eyes open onto the other layer: hidden entities outlined in cold light, magical effects visible as weather, illusions rendered with their seams showing and their stagehands exposed. Nothing spiritual can hide from the gaze. It reveals; it does not resolve (the wraith seen is still a wraith to be dealt with) and looking into the spirit realm is a two-way courtesy: what the walker sees clearly can, occasionally, see them clearly back.
[Occult Lore: 4]

Spirit Heal.name: Spirit Heal
Spirit Heal.description:
Warmth from the other side of the veil, borrowed with permission: the spirit walker channels gentle energy into an ally's wounds, flesh mending under a touch that feels like being remembered fondly. The healing is soft-spoken but real. It draws on the goodwill of spirits present (places scoured of the dead offer thin help) and each channeling asks the walker to hold the door open a while, which is never entirely free.
[Spirit Channeling: 3]

Spirit Lash.name: Spirit Lash
Spirit Lash.description:
The shaman calls and an elemental spirit lashes down the line (flame, frost, or storm by the shaman's attunement) striking everything in its path and lingering briefly afterward as a hazard with the spirit's temper. A whip made of borrowed weather. The lash runs its line and no wider (aim is negotiation), the lingering element claims the ground it crossed, and spirits lent for violence expect the shaman's courtesy afterward: attunement is a relationship, and relationships keep accounts.
[Spirit Channeling: 4]

Spirit Link.name: Spirit Link
Spirit Link.description:
The priest binds the party into one divine circuit: damage distributed evenly among all linked allies: no single member taking a killing blow while the link holds, every wound socialized across willing shoulders. The party suffers together, which is the point and the prayer. The link shares harm rather than reducing it (the total is honest; only the addressing changes), it holds while the priest's grace sustains the circuit, and its theology is exact: a party that trusts the link fights fearlessly, and a party that doesn't shouldn't be linked.
[Spirit Channeling: 35]

Spirit Rift.name: Spirit Rift
Spirit Rift.description:
The walker tears a seam between worlds and the seam inhales: enemies dragged toward the rift, their connection to the material world fraying at the edges: strength dimming, footing failing, the veil's cold pouring through their certainty. Standing near an open door to elsewhere is bad for the living. The rift pulls while the walker holds it open and weakens rather than swallows (it is pressure, not a portal to fall through), and doors between worlds open both ways: something occasionally looks out.
[Rift Magic: 8]

Spirit Trap.name: Spirit Trap
Spirit Trap.description:
The shaman seeds the ground with a bargain: a spirit trap, invisible and patient, waking when an enemy steps on it: slowing, damaging, terrifying, or binding, depending on which spirit agreed to wait there. Spirits who serve in traps expect gratitude in proportion to how long they crouched in the dirt.
[survival: 4]

Spirit Walk.name: Spirit Walk
Spirit Walk.description:
The walker steps sideways into the spirit realm, crosses on paths of memory and moonlight, and steps back out somewhere better: past the wall, beyond the chasm, behind the door with the excellent lock. To material eyes, they simply stopped being here and started being there. The walk covers modest distances along the veil's own geography (the spirit realm does not run in straight lines) and its roads have residents, some of whom take an interest in commuters.
[Stealth: 18]

Steal Skill.name: Steal Skill
Steal Skill.description:
Quick fingers in the magical sense: the thief brushes past and lifts an enemy's active blessing clean off them (the glowing edge, the stone skin, the borrowed speed) wearing it while the original owner discovers, mid-swing, that they are suddenly ordinary. Twice on the same mark never works; people guard what they've lost.
[Dagger Fighting: 2]

Stone Lance.name: Stone Lance
Stone Lance.description:
The caster stamps once, and the earth answers: a spear of raw stone erupts beneath the target, launching them skyward in a burst of soil and shattered cobbles. Airborne enemies lose their footing, their formation, and usually their dignity. The lance needs true ground to draw from (ship decks, rooftops, and worked marble resist the call) and the earth must rest a few breaths before it will answer again.
[Earth Magic: 2]

Summon Gate.name: Summon Gate
Summon Gate.description:
The summoner opens a gate that arrives hungry: a dimensional aperture at the target location, dragging enemies toward it with tidal insistence, arcane damage riding the pull while proximity to elsewhere disorients everything caught in the current. A drain in the battlefield's floor. The gate pulls while the summoner sustains it and drags rather than devours (it herds enemies into arm's reach of consequences, usually prepared ones), and standing near an open door to elsewhere does things to inner ears and outer courage alike.
[Space Magic: 40]

Thunderbolt.name: Thunderbolt
Thunderbolt.description:
The bolt at full ceremony: massive lightning called from the sky (or conjured indoors, the discipline having solved its own architectural complaint) striking one point with catastrophic force. The gathering static is the target's honest warning, frequently wasted. This spell does not damage areas. It ends addresses.
[Lightning Magic: 22]

Tidal Surge.name: Tidal Surge
Tidal Surge.description:
The caster calls and the sea answers out of nowhere: a massive wave crashing through the battlefield, sweeping enemies off their feet, off their positions, and occasionally off the map, with devastating water damage riding the crest. Terrain becomes temporarily nautical. The surge is gloriously indiscriminate about footing (allies should be behind or above it) and summoning that much ocean inland leaves the caster wrung out like the landscape: soaked, spent, and briefly beloved by frogs.
[Water Magic: 9]

Time Freeze.name: Time Freeze
Time Freeze.description:
The target is removed from the schedule: frozen in time completely, unmoving, unhurt, unreachable, a statue of themselves while the world continues without them. When time resumes, they experience the gap as a missing breath: the fight has moved, and nobody consulted them. The freeze holds for seconds and protects as absolutely as it imprisons (a frozen enemy cannot be harmed either: the spell buys position, not damage), and time bills the caster coldly for every second borrowed.
[Time Magic: 12]

Trap Bypass.name: Trap Bypass
Trap Bypass.description:
Identify and safely bypass a trap protecting a treasure without triggering it. You see the mechanism, understand the logic, and know exactly where to step, what to pull, and what absolutely not to touch.
[Treasure Seeking: 3]

Trap Disarm.name: Trap Disarm
Trap Disarm.description:
Analyze and disarm a mechanical or magical trap by understanding its engineering principles. You see the mechanism's logic, identify the safest bypass, and disable it without triggering the payload. Works on dungeon traps, ward triggers, and the kind of door mechanisms that the Aetherglass Reaches left behind as practical jokes.
[Engineering: 12]

Turn Undead.name: Turn Undead
Turn Undead.description:
Sacred light in one commanding pulse: undead creatures breaking and fleeing in supernatural terror, the weakest simply unmade mid-retreat, the strong holding their ground while smoking and reconsidering. Authority exercised over the restless grave. The turning routs rather than destroys the sturdy (a fleeing horde regroups; the pulse buys space and time), its reach is the priest's conviction made radius, and necromancers whose armies scatter at one word develop an urgent professional interest in the priest's schedule.
[Divinity: 19]

Wall Runner.name: Wall Runner
Wall Runner.description:
Ki-enhanced grip and a monk's disregard for architecture's intent: running along vertical surfaces and ceilings, repositioning to any point in an enclosed space regardless of gravity's editorial opinion. Dungeons become three-dimensional playgrounds; ambushes acquire a Z-axis. The run lasts as long as momentum and ki cooperate (stopping mid-wall returns the monk to gravity's keeping immediately and educationally), and enemies who fight wall-runners develop the school's favorite gift: checking the ceiling first, forever.
[acrobatics: 9]

Wild Taming.name: Wild Taming
Wild Taming.description:
Mid-battle, the tamer walks toward the hostile creature instead of away: meeting its eyes, matching its posture, establishing a dominance bond through proximity and pure nerve. If it takes, the creature turns and fights for them for the rest of the combat. Recruitment at claw's length. The taming needs closeness, composure, and a creature capable of respecting hierarchy (the mindless and the enraged do not negotiate), and a bond forged in one fight lasts one fight: keeping it afterward is a courtship, not a command.
[Beast Keeping: 29]

Wind Cutter.name: Wind Cutter
Wind Cutter.description:
The slash moves fast enough that the air gives up and becomes the weapon: a compressed cutting wave extending the blade's reach by several meters, arriving with a sound like cloth tearing at scale. Swordsmanship, mailed. The cutter carries a single slash's force and thins with distance (at the edge of its reach it insults rather than injures) and the compression takes a drawn breath and clean form; sloppy swings produce only wind and embarrassment.
[Swordsmanship: 11]

Wooden Ward.name: Wooden Ward
Wooden Ward.description:
Carve a protective totem from available wood that generates a small ward around the area. The totem is humble but effective: a carved spirit face that watches over the camp and pushes back the darkness.
[Woodworking: 3]

Apex Channel.name: Apex Channel
Apex Channel.description:
The tamer opens themselves and an apex predator's spirit pours through: the strength, the speed, the terrible clean instincts of the thing at the top of some wild food chain: the beast master becoming, briefly, the beast. Movements simplify. Hesitation dies. The channel runs while the tamer's body can host that much wildness and then closes, leaving them shaking and clear-eyed; the borrowed instincts are magnificent and amoral, and tamers learn to choose their predator to suit the room.
[persuasion: 49]

Arcane Arrow.name: Arcane Arrow
Arcane Arrow.description:
Mana climbs the shaft and settles into the arrowhead as visible light: the shot flies true and lands twice: honest impact plus a bite of arcane damage that treats minor magical barriers as decorative. The archer's answer to 'my ward will stop it.' The imbuing is quick but real (each arrow is enchanted at the draw, not in advance), and the glow that makes the arrow lethal also makes it legible: night ambushes require either darker magic or better positioning.
[Archery: 2]

Arcane Sigil.name: Arcane Sigil
Arcane Sigil.description:
A circle of quiet light sinks into the ground and waits with a scholar's patience. The first hostile foot to cross it receives the thesis: an arcane detonation plus one affliction drawn at random from the sigil's mean little library: slowed, dazzled, hexed, or worse. The sigil is invisible to the careless and legible to the trained, holds until triggered or dispelled, and the caster can maintain only so many lessons in the ground at once.
[Arcane Magic: 5]

Arcane Slash.name: Arcane Slash
Arcane Slash.description:
The Sword Saint's opening argument: a slash of magical force releasing a wave of cutting energy at range: the sword's reach extended from arm's length to across-the-room. The wave thins with distance; at the far edge it insults rather than injures. Veterans read one another's waves like handwriting: the arc's color, curve, and temper naming the sender before the damage does.
[Swordsmanship: 3]

Astral Sight.name: Astral Sight
Astral Sight.description:
The stars annotate everything, for eyes taught to read them: illusions unravel at their celestial seams, magical darkness thins to gauze, disguises reveal the signatures all things carry whether they consent or not. It reads what is concealed, not what is distant. Things that realize they've been seen through respond with the full range: relief, fury, or immediate scheduling changes.
[Star Magic: 3]

Beast Tongue.name: Beast Tongue
Beast Tongue.description:
Open a temporary channel of communication with a nearby animal. You understand its emotions, intentions, and basic thoughts, and it understands your requests. Doesn't guarantee cooperation: animals have opinions.
[Nature Magic: 2]

Blink Strike.name: Blink Strike
Blink Strike.description:
The swordsman is in front of the target; the wound is behind them: an instantaneous blink through space, a point-blank strike arriving before the enemy finishes turning. Distance, deleted rather than crossed. Blind teleportation is how swordsmen become masonry. Enemies develop the school's signature gift: flinching at empty air.
[Unarmed Combat: 4]

Blood Frenzy.name: Blood Frenzy
Blood Frenzy.description:
The vampire blood answers when called: eyes darkening, canines extending, speed and strength spiking to true-vampire register: attacks faster, wounds sipping closed with every hit landed. The frenzy runs until the blood calms, leaving its wielder drained; the collapse afterward is scheduled. And the cost: using it reveals the heritage to everyone present, permanently. Certain older things take note that a bloodline is awake.
[athletics: 2]

Blood Strike.name: Blood Strike
Blood Strike.description:
The mage pays first and casts second: a measured portion of their own health opened and offered, converted into dark magic that lands with devastating, personal weight. Token cuts buy token results. Blood magic keeps perfect books: a mage who overdraws mid-fight discovers that the spell was strong and the caster, suddenly, is not.
[Blood Magic: 3]

Bulwark Aura.name: Bulwark Aura
Bulwark Aura.description:
Radiate a protective field that hardens the defenses of everyone nearby. Allies' armor becomes tougher, their shields hold firmer, and their bodies turn aside harm more easily. The aura pulses with each of your heartbeats, and the closer an ally stands to you, the safer they are: the center of a living fortress that walks. It guards allies near you on the turn you raise it; sustaining it takes your action again each turn.
[athletics: 10]

Charm Person.name: Charm Person
Charm Person.description:
The bard's oldest and most argued-about spell: subtle persuasion woven into words and melody: a humanoid target coming to regard the caster as a trusted friend. Not control: just trust and a willingness to listen. The charm frays under hostile acts, and strong wills resist. The true controversy is the aftermath: some charms end, and the friendship, awkwardly, doesn't.
[performance: 4 · persuasion: 4]

Comfort Food.name: Comfort Food
Comfort Food.description:
Cook something that soothes emotional distress, calms fear, and restores morale. It is the dish someone makes when they want to say they care without saying it. The effect is gentle but deeply felt: a warm bowl of soup that makes the dungeon feel slightly less terrible.
[Cooking: 3]

Counter Flow.name: Counter Flow
Counter Flow.description:
The incoming attack is accepted, redirected, and returned to sender with its own postage: momentum guided past its target and into the floor, the wall, or their own colleague. The harder they swing, the harder they fall. It needs the attacker's commitment to work with: cautious opponents starve it, which is itself a victory.
[Dueling: 4]

Counterspell.name: Counterspell
Counterspell.description:
The mage reads the enemy incantation mid-cast and reaches into its plumbing: mana structure disrupted, the spell fizzling into embarrassed sparks, the invested mana simply gone from the caster's book. Denied, with fees. The counter demands timing and magical perception both (the window is the length of a syllable) it answers one spell per interruption, and enemy casters who have been counterspelled twice develop the profession's signature paranoia: casting faster, sloppier, and angrier, which is its own victory.
[Arcane Magic: 3]

Crimson Rain.name: Crimson Rain
Crimson Rain.description:
The mage opens a withdrawal from every nearby enemy at once: health draining upward in a rain of crimson energy, arcing home, each affected target paying into the caster's mending. The battlefield becomes your chalice. The rain sips from all in range rather than gorging on one (crowds are the spell's whole economy: against a lone enemy it is merely rude), the crimson arcs are visible across a battlefield and unmistakable in testimony, and drinking a crowd's vitality at once carries the profession's usual aftertaste: borrowed blood, restless in the veins.
[Blood Magic: 11]

Crimson Tide.name: Crimson Tide
Crimson Tide.description:
Weaponize your own vitality into a wave of crystallized blood that sweeps across the battlefield. The crimson tide cuts, binds, and drains: each enemy struck feeds a portion of their life force back to you. The cost is paid in blood. Yours, specifically.
[Blood Magic: 5]

Danger Sense.name: Danger Sense
Danger Sense.description: A cold certainty arrives seconds ahead of the harm: the ambush breathing in the tall grass, the flagstone that is a trap, the arrow already loosed. The body is moving before the mind finishes asking why. The sense warns of imminent, physical threats (slow schemes and gentle poisons slip beneath it) and companions learn to treat the bearer's sudden stillness as a command performance: when they freeze, everyone freezes.

Dawn's Grace.name: Dawn's Grace
Dawn's Grace.description: Restore a small amount of health or cleanse a minor harmful condition with warm celestial light. Gentle healing: the steady comfort of sunrise after a cold night. Leaves a faint warmth on the healed area.

Demonic Gate.name: Demonic Gate
Demonic Gate.description:
Open a small rift to the demon realm that pulls in nearby enemies with gravitational force while dealing continuous dark damage. The rift screams faintly. It stays open for several seconds before collapsing.
[Void Magic: 8]

Dispel Magic.name: Dispel Magic
Dispel Magic.description:
The sage's clean slate: every enchantment and magical effect stripped from a target at once: beneficial, harmful, all of it dissolving into drifting sparks. Sometimes the most powerful magic is taking someone else's away. The dispel is comprehensive rather than selective (the target's own blessings go with the curses: aim it with that arithmetic done), it unravels active magic rather than innate nature, and enemy champions who watch a battle's worth of preparation sparkle away in one gesture produce the spell's true product: despair with witnesses.
[Arcane Magic: 9]

Divine Smite.name: Divine Smite
Divine Smite.description:
Even Priests need to fight sometimes. Call down a bolt of divine judgment on an enemy, dealing light damage. Extra effective against undead and demons. The Church says violence is a last resort. The last resort is effective.
[Divinity: 4]

Dragon Scale.name: Dragon Scale
Dragon Scale.description:
Draconic energy rises through the skin and answers with armor: shimmering scales in the vein's elemental color, dulling incoming blows with the smug durability of an older species. A dragon-scaled knight is tough, not untouchable, and glittering visibly with draconic heritage ends all pretense of traveling incognito.
[intimidation: 2]

Earthshatter.name: Earthshatter
Earthshatter.description:
Bring your fist or weapon down with the force of a falling mountain. The impact point craaters. Shockwaves radiate outward, staggering everything within range. The ground splits in radiating fractures. Buildings tremble. Enemies caught in the impact zone are launched, crushed, or buried. You hit the world and the world blinked.
[athletics: 18]

Fallen Grace.name: Fallen Grace
Fallen Grace.description: Use damaged celestial wings to slow a fall, glide, leap dramatically, or reposition in combat with eerie grace. Not true flight: fragments of what once was. Scattered feathers dissolve into motes of gold and ash.

Field Remedy.name: Field Remedy
Field Remedy.description:
Quickly identify medicinal plants in the immediate environment and prepare a basic herbal remedy: a poultice that stops bleeding, a chewed root that eases pain, or a leaf compress that draws venom. The remedy is simple but effective, and it works when the healer is the patient.
[Divinity: 2]

Fire Inferno.name: Fire Inferno
Fire Inferno.description:
The firestorm without punctuation: a large area engulfed: flames spiraling from the ground, raining from above, sustained fire damage to everything within, heat sufficient to melt steel and every argument for staying. Territory, converted to furnace. The inferno claims its area for its duration with total impartiality (the caster sculpts the border, not the temperament; allies respect the line or improvise regrets), sustaining a district of fire draws deep and continuously, and the ground afterward is glazed and honest: something unreasonable was here.
[Fire Magic: 29]

Flame Weapon.name: Flame Weapon
Flame Weapon.description:
Fire takes the blade like a rumor takes a tavern: roaring, immediate, and impossible to ignore. Every strike lands burning, and the flame persists for several seconds of follow-up hits: pressure becomes arson. The fire respects its schedule and gutters on time, water and smothering end it early, and a burning weapon is a burning beacon: every enemy in the dark now knows precisely where the swordsman stands, which aggressive swordsmen consider an invitation.
[Fire Magic: 3]

Flash Freeze.name: Flash Freeze
Flash Freeze.description:
Winter, delivered in one syllable: a target frozen solid in a block of ice: immobilized, taking continuous cold damage until the block breaks, a person converted to sculpture with a pulse. Strong targets shatter free early; weaker ones remain, patiently, exactly where they were caught. The freeze claims one target per casting (the block is honest ice: fire ends it, force cracks it, time thins it), and the frozen report the same detail with lasting resentment: being able to see the fight continue, attendance not optional, participation denied.
[Ice Magic: 13]

Forge Strike.name: Forge Strike
Forge Strike.description:
The smith's argument, delivered with the smith's eye: a hammer blow aimed at where metal is weakest, catching the gap the armorer compromised on and the rivet line where corners were cut. Damage lands, and armor effectiveness follows it down. Warriors who hear their own breastplate addressed by its weak points develop a sudden, expensive interest in commissioning better.
[Blacksmithing: 2]

Frost Weapon.name: Frost Weapon
Frost Weapon.description:
Ice sheathes the blade and travels with every cut: wounds that frost over, footwork that drags, armor gone brittle enough to complain on the next hit. The cold lingers after the cut, doing quiet work. The coating melts against fire-wreathed foes and thaws on its own schedule, and the wielder's own hand goes half-numb around the grip: a quiet toll the frost never mentions until the third fight of the day.
[Ice Magic: 4]

Golem Puppet.name: Golem Puppet
Golem Puppet.description:
The puppeteer looks at the available materials, rubble, timber, an unfortunate statue, and assembles a golem on the spot: massive, slow, and immensely durable, obeying simple commands with the patience of furniture. A siege engine improvised from the scenery. The golem is only as good as its ingredients (a mud golem has mud opinions), it holds together until destroyed or dismissed, and building one mid-battle takes the puppeteer's full concentration for a window enemies are welcome to interrupt. They rarely reach the puppeteer through the construction site.
[Artifice: 38]

Guard Stance.name: Guard Stance
Guard Stance.description:
The knight plants, raises the shield, and becomes an iron decree: incoming damage dramatically reduced, the wall the enemy breaks against on purpose, repeatedly. A planted knight advances nowhere; holding ground is the plan. Every heartbeat the wall holds is a heartbeat the party spends winning somewhere else. The stance protects on the turn you take it; holding it takes your action again each turn.
[athletics: 2]

Healing Hymn.name: Healing Hymn
Healing Hymn.description:
Sing a gentle restorative hymn that heals allies over time. The melody weaves through the air like warm light, mending minor wounds and easing pain. Not as potent as divine healing, but it doesn't require prayer.
[performance: 3]

Healing Rain.name: Healing Rain
Healing Rain.description:
The caster asks the sky for kindness and the sky agrees: gentle rain, each drop infused with restorative magic: health returning to every ally within like a warm spring shower with a medical license. Emergencies want sharper tools; this is recovery, not rescue. Fighting while being healed by warm rain does something to morale nobody has bothered to explain, because it's raining and everyone feels fine.
[Water Magic: 4]

Heart's Read.name: Heart's Read
Heart's Read.description: The succubus glances, and the nearby heart opens like a book with poor security: fears in the margins, desires underlined. Not mind reading: hearts, which are less precise and more damning. A calm liar with a quiet heart reads as calm. People who learn they were read respond with fascinating new emotions. Which she also reads.

Hex Analysis.name: Hex Analysis
Hex Analysis.description:
Identify and deconstruct enemy magical effects, curses, and enchantments in real time. The analysis unfolds like an academy disputation while the enemy's protective magic falls apart. Reveals hidden blessings, curse structures, and magical weak points. Knowledge is the deadliest weapon.
[Occult Lore: 5]

Hex Cauldron.name: Hex Cauldron
Hex Cauldron.description:
The witch conjures the spectral cauldron and lets it work: bubbling over with malice, continuously spewing curses at every nearby enemy: attributes randomly sagging, damage ticking, spellcasters finding their voices suddenly on loan. Area denial, brewed. The cauldron curses whoever remains in its reach (its randomness is genuine; the witch aims the pot, not the pours), it stands and stews until dispelled or expired, and its burbling is audible across a battlefield: a sound veteran enemies have learned to take personally.
[Dark Magic: 18]

Holy Avenger.name: Holy Avenger
Holy Avenger.description:
The weapon, temporarily promoted to relic: blazing golden, dealing holy damage on every strike, and the clause of consequence: undead enemies cannot regenerate while wounded by it, their oldest trick suspended by injunction. Wounds that stay are wounds the horde has never budgeted for. For these minutes, the divine is holding this exact sword.
[Swordsmanship: 9]

Holy Barrier.name: Holy Barrier
Holy Barrier.description:
A wall of divine light with a selective threshold: undead, demons, and dark spirits repelled at the border (pressing against it like weather against glass) while the faithful pass through untouched, barely noticing the warmth. Sanctuary that knows its guests. The barrier bars the unholy rather than harming them (it is a refusal, not a sword), and truly powerful entities test it constantly: the barrier holds by the priest's conviction, and conviction under siege is the actual spell. It bars the unholy on the turn you raise it; sustaining it takes your action again each turn.
[Light Magic: 11]

Ice Blizzard.name: Ice Blizzard
Ice Blizzard.description:
A localized blizzard, summoned with a grudge: ice shards and sleet, visibility dropping to zero, movement to a crawl, the cold climbing toward life-threatening. Winter, delivered by appointment. The deepening cold does patient work that spikes and swords cannot, and enemies who retreat learn the storm's small print: the caster chose where it ends.
[Ice Magic: 21]

Inferno Bomb.name: Inferno Bomb
Inferno Bomb.description:
The alchemist's magnum opus in a heavy sphere: a massive bomb birthing a sustained conflagration: continuous fire damage across the whole area, flame that burns until the reagent is spent and not one heartbeat less. Area denial, published in first-degree. The inferno holds its territory with chemical patience (retreating from it is wisdom; fighting in it is billing), the reagent burns on its schedule regardless of second thoughts, and each bomb is serious brewing: the alchemist carries very few, and throws them like signatures.
[Alchemy: 24]

Lance Charge.name: Lance Charge
Lance Charge.description:
The spear braced, the run begun, and physics recruited: momentum building until the impact arrives as arithmetic: force enough to impale through monster hide and shield alike. A cramped charge is a jog with a spear. The oldest teaching survives every generation: the dragoon who hesitates mid-charge delivers a hesitation, at speed, to someone braced.
[athletics: 7]

Lay on Hands.name: Lay on Hands
Lay on Hands.description:
The paladin's simplest miracle and the order's whole thesis: hands on a wounded ally, divine healing channeled directly: faster than a potion, warmer than bandages, fueled by genuine compassion, which is not a flourish but the actual fuel. Veterans of many wars report the warmth is the part they remember, decades after forgetting the wound.
[Divinity: 2]

Mana Setting.name: Mana Setting
Mana Setting.description:
Set a gem into a ring, pendant, or accessory in a way that creates a mana-conducting circuit. The resulting piece can store a small spell, amplify an enchantment, or provide a passive magical benefit. The craft requires steady hands and an understanding of magical flow.
[Jewelcrafting: 4]

Meteor Slash.name: Meteor Slash
Meteor Slash.description:
Launch yourself skyward and descend with a vertical slash that channels your entire falling momentum into the blade. The impact creates a shockwave. Visually identical to a falling star, and just as destructive.
[Swordsmanship: 9]

Meteor Storm.name: Meteor Storm
Meteor Storm.description:
S-rank spell material, meaning exactly what it says: flaming meteors called down from the sky, each leaving a crater, the devastation apocalyptic in the technical sense that survivors reorganize their theology. Allies evacuate or become geology. The cratered field afterward is a monument: magic of this rank leaves addresses.
[Elemental Magic: 34]

Mirror Clone.name: Mirror Clone
Mirror Clone.description:
Create a perfect duplicate of yourself from reflected light and fractured perception. The clone can fight, cast spells, and interact with the world, but it deals reduced damage and shatters into blinding shards when destroyed. Enemies can never tell which of you is real. Sometimes neither can you.
[Illusion Magic: 5]

Mirror Image.name: Mirror Image
Mirror Image.description:
The illusionist splits like light through a prism: three copies fan out, each moving with independent purpose, each convincingly them. Every image holds together for exactly one hit before shattering into glittering nothing, which makes enemies pay in attacks for the privilege of finding the real one. Bright truth-light and keen senses thin the trick, and the shards must be regathered before the mirror can break again.
[Illusion Magic: 1]

Misdirection.name: Misdirection
Misdirection.description:
A sound where nobody is, a decoy, a thrown coin, a lie told by the environment itself. Enemies attack the wrong target or spend their finest attack on a rumor. The window is short; one clean beat for the reposition, the strike, or something far worse. Works on attention, not minds: the vigilant burn slower, the paranoid burn twice.
[Deception: 1]

Phantom Rush.name: Phantom Rush
Phantom Rush.description:
Pure speed as a skeleton key: a dash through the enemy's guard, multiple strikes landing before reaction has finished forming. There is no steering mid-phantom; the whole sequence lands or whiffs together. Defenders describe it afterward the same way: the blur, then the count of wounds, then the recount.
[Illusion Magic: 4]

Pinning Shot.name: Pinning Shot
Pinning Shot.description:
The arrow that argues with movement: a limb, a cloak, or (the eerie masterpiece) a shadow pinned to the ground, the target rooted mid-stride. The pin holds until torn free at a cost in flesh, fabric, or unsettling shadow-pain. Enemies pinned by their own shadow spend the fight's remainder in a philosophical crisis the archer finds productive.
[Archery: 5]

Plague Touch.name: Plague Touch
Plague Touch.description:
The hand goes necrotic and the touch delivers a career: infection dealing damage over time, healing arriving muffled, and the signature clause: it spreads on contact, formation cohesion becoming a vector. One touch, many patients. Dragging your infected friend to safety has terms. Healers triage with the intended despair: treating symptoms while the mage makes more.
[Poison Magic: 9]

Puppet Dance.name: Puppet Dance
Puppet Dance.description:
The puppeteer's opening number: a small, swift puppet animated into the fight, bladed limbs flickering, executing commands with clockwork enthusiasm and collapsing, when destroyed, into parts that will fight again tomorrow. It harasses, flanks, and finishes rather than duels. Parties that travel with one long enough begin, against all reason, to greet it by name.
[Thread Arts: 2]

Quaking Palm.name: Quaking Palm
Quaking Palm.description:
The strike with a delivery date: a palm implanting delayed ki inside the target: the energy detonating seconds later as devastating internal damage that armor cannot prevent, having been, technically, invited inside. Walk away. Count to three. The palm demands clean contact to implant (the delay is the art and the theater both), the detonation cannot be blocked by anything the target owns, and the school's signature image has ended negotiations across the continent: the monk, already leaving, and the count everyone present is silently keeping.
[acrobatics: 82]

Quick Scribe.name: Quick Scribe
Quick Scribe.description:
Scribe a combat scroll at speed, producing a single-use spell scroll that anyone in the party can activate. The scroll is crude, temporary, and the ink fades after one use, but a healing scroll in the right hands at the right moment has saved more lives than careful penmanship ever did.
[Inscription: 2]

Radiant Aura.name: Radiant Aura
Radiant Aura.description:
The priest becomes a place worth standing: healing light radiating steadily: small amounts of health flowing continuously to all nearby allies. Triage, ambient. Emergencies still want the focused beam; this is the tide, not the rescue. People fight measurably braver inside warmth, a fact priests exploit with clear consciences.
[Divinity: 36]

Rallying Cry.name: Rallying Cry
Rallying Cry.description:
The knight's voice, deployed: a battle cry that steadies allied nerves and burns fear away mid-flinch: nearby allies steeled against the blows coming for them, courage arriving as armor. It cures fear rather than wounds; the priest handles the rest. A rallying cry only works from someone the party believes, which must be earned before it can be shouted. It steadies allies near you on the turn you shout it; rallying them again takes your action again each turn.
[Command: 4]

Rejuvenation.name: Rejuvenation
Rejuvenation.description:
Channel nature's regenerative power into a target, accelerating their natural healing dramatically. Wounds close as if days pass in seconds, and the target feels the warm vitality of a spring morning.
[Nature Magic: 7]

Resurrection.name: Resurrection
Resurrection.description:
The most powerful prayer a Priest can offer: hands pressed over the stilled heart, refusing: out loud, in words the divine cannot ignore. Death is asked, not commanded, to give this one back. Success depends on how recently they fell and how fiercely the caster will not let go. A soul called back remembers, faintly, who did the calling, and the caster carries the emptiness of the prayer for days.
[Divinity: 46]

Runic Shield.name: Runic Shield
Runic Shield.description:
The runes etched into armor wake at a word: script flaring to life, a magical barrier drinking the force of incoming blows: a fuel gauge written in ancient letters. Spent runes must be re-inscribed in genuine downtime, which is why rune knights treat quiet evenings as ammunition. It guards you on the turn you wake it; keeping it lit takes your action again each turn.
[Arcane Magic: 3]

Runic Weapon.name: Runic Weapon
Runic Weapon.description:
The full inscription: the entire weapon infused with runic power: cutting through magical barriers as through argument, dealing multiple damage types as the script cycles along the blade. The multi-typed edge defeats defenses built for any single answer. Every rune-reader present knows exactly what school, what mastery, and what is about to be proven.
[Rune Carving: 34]

Scent Memory.name: Scent Memory
Scent Memory.description:
Create a fragrance tied to a specific person or memory: the smell of a shared afternoon, a childhood home, a confession at a festival. The scent triggers vivid emotional recall in whoever wears it or encounters it, making the moment impossible to forget.
[Perfumery: 3]

Shadow Blink.name: Shadow Blink
Shadow Blink.description:
Blink between shadows instantaneously, crossing vast distances in the time between heartbeats. You dissolve into one shadow and materialize from another: behind an enemy, above them, beside an ally who needs saving. The rapid repositioning makes you nearly impossible to pin down, and each blink leaves a ghostly afterimage that lingers for a disorienting moment.
[Stealth: 12]

Shadow Cloak.name: Shadow Cloak
Shadow Cloak.description:
Wrap yourself in living shadow, becoming nearly invisible in dim light and completely invisible in darkness. The cloak muffles sound and scent. Moving breaks the effect partially, but standing still makes you virtually undetectable.
[Shadow Magic: 3]

Shadow Clone.name: Shadow Clone
Shadow Clone.description:
