A duplicate steps out of the ninja's shadow and gets to work, attacking, dodging, and drawing the guard's eye as a full combatant with one fatal flaw: a single hit dissolves it. The enemy's true mistake comes after the dissolve: from then on, every version of the ninja gets attacked with hesitation.
[Dagger Fighting: 2]

Shadow Dance.name: Shadow Dance
Shadow Dance.description:
The rhythm of vanish-strike-vanish: each attack transitioning into invisibility, each reappearance a strike from a different angle: fluid shadow movement where the enemy fights a pattern instead of a person, bleeding on the beats between. The dance sustains while focus and shadow cooperate (each vanish is brief; the strikes mark the tempo the enemy can learn, which masters therefore syncopate), bright light shortens every disappearance, and survivors describe the losing experience in the school's favorite review: they were only ever there when it hurt.
[Stealth: 53]

Shock Weapon.name: Shock Weapon
Shock Weapon.description:
Lightning takes residence in the weapon and pays rent on every hit: struck enemies seizing briefly as the current locks their muscles, bonus voltage riding each blow for the duration. Pressure becomes paralysis becomes more pressure. The charge holds for its window and then grounds out, water improves it in ways the wielder must also respect (a shocking weapon in the rain has no friends), and the constant crackle makes stealth an abandoned career.
[Lightning Magic: 10]

Siege Deploy.name: Siege Deploy
Siege Deploy.description:
Deploy a portable siege mechanism or structural tool: a portable ram, a scaling ladder, a brace, or a temporary barricade assembled from available materials and engineering know-how. The construct is functional, ugly, and exactly what the situation requires.
[Engineering: 34]

Sniper's Eye.name: Sniper's Eye
Sniper's Eye.description:
One shot, placed rather than fired: armor ignored, critical damage delivered, the projectile finding the gap, the joint, the weak point: precision at its most lethal, arriving like a professional opinion. The eye demands stillness, sightline, and a held breath's worth of focus per shot (this is marksmanship as meditation, not volume), and its perfection is specific: one target, one truth, and a report that tells everyone with ears exactly which direction genius came from.
[Firearms: 16]

Space Portal.name: Space Portal
Space Portal.description:
Open a pair of connected portals between two points you can see. Anything entering one exits the other: including allies, projectiles, and redirected enemy attacks. The portals shimmer with geometric fractals.
[Space Magic: 8]

Spatial Lock.name: Spatial Lock
Spatial Lock.description:
The target is frozen in space; not time, position: conscious, aware, furious, and physically unable to depart their exact coordinates. Teleportation fails, arriving nowhere. Locked is not helpless: the technique parks them; the party handles the rest. Teleporters who slam into their own failed escape develop the intended condition: claustrophobia, in open fields.
[Space Magic: 34]

Speed Reload.name: Speed Reload
Speed Reload.description:
Hands blur, and the weapon is simply never empty: reload motions compressed to supernatural flickers, fire rate doubling, every shot arriving with no time bought for the enemy to breathe between them. Sustained fire becomes a wall. The blessing accelerates the hands, not the ammunition pouch, bullets still run honest math, and when the seraph's grace lifts, the fingers sting like they borrowed the speed from somewhere with interest.
[Firearms: 4]

Spirit Blade.name: Spirit Blade
Spirit Blade.description:
Ki channeled through steel until the steel exceeds itself, a visible spiritual extension flowing past the physical edge for additional force damage on every cut, and the technique's true purpose: the spirit blade strikes the ethereal and incorporeal, wraiths discovering that something in this world can still reach them. The extension glows while ki sustains it, against ordinary flesh it is a fine bonus and against ghosts it is the whole conversation, and spirits who assumed immunity to swordsmanship revise the assumption with memorable urgency.
[survival: 14]

Spirit Phase.name: Spirit Phase
Spirit Phase.description:
For one held breath, the walker steps halfway out of the world: body gone translucent, incoming attacks passing through empty suggestion, thin walls becoming doorways of opinion. Timing it against a killing blow is the signature of the style. The phase is brief by the veil's own rules (the spirit realm charges rent) and while intangible, the walker's own attacks are equally hypothetical: you cannot hit the world you have politely left.
[Spirit Channeling: 3]

Swordbreaker.name: Swordbreaker
Swordbreaker.description:
A precision strike targeting the opponent's weapon. On success, damages or destroys the enemy's weapon, disarming them. Against monsters, targets a limb or natural weapon instead. The ultimate 'I'm better than you' move.
[Swordsmanship: 65]

Thread World.name: Thread World
Thread World.description:
The puppeteer's masterwork spreads invisible across the entire battlefield: a web of threads spanning every lane and doorway, every vibration reporting home: footsteps, drawn blades, the held breath before an ambush. Nothing happens without your knowledge. Omniscience, woven. The web senses rather than strikes (it is intelligence, and intelligence is enough), laying it takes the profession's deepest focus and holding the whole world's trembling in one mind is the technique's true cost: puppeteers describe it as 'listening to everything, forever, for ten minutes.'
[Artifice: 66]

Thunder Clap.name: Thunder Clap
Thunder Clap.description:
Clap your hands and release a concussive blast of thunder and lightning in all directions. Enemies are shocked, deafened, and staggered. The sound alone can shatter glass and stun anyone within arm's reach.
[Lightning Magic: 4]

Tidal Reload.name: Tidal Reload
Tidal Reload.description:
Draw ambient moisture to clean, cool, and reload weapons instantly. Near water, this also generates a burst of pressurized spray that blinds melee attackers and creates distance. The ocean is always an ally. Far from the coast, the ability still works: just less dramatically.
[Water Magic: 3]

Trap Setting.name: Trap Setting
Trap Setting.description:
Quickly set a concealed trap at your location: snare, spike trap, alarm, or explosive depending on materials. Rangers always carry trap components. The best fights are the ones decided before the enemy arrives.
[Dungeon Surveying: 3]

Undying Fury.name: Undying Fury
Undying Fury.description:
The death that rage declines: when a lethal blow lands, the berserker survives at 1 HP: entering a berserk state where damage doubles for a short window. It cannot be invoked in advance; death must swing first and be refused. Enemies who watch their finishing blow anger someone experience combat's most honest omen.
[athletics: 75]

Unholy Surge.name: Unholy Surge
Unholy Surge.description:
Black-green fire sheathes the blade, and the strike lands with a butcher's certainty: necrotic power that bites deepest into living flesh and lingers in the wound, souring healing that tries to close it. The living fear it correctly. The surge draws from the knight's own vitality to fuel itself, a small cold withdrawal each time, and holy ground makes the fire gutter like a candle in a doorway.
[Dark Magic: 2]

Vacuum Blade.name: Vacuum Blade
Vacuum Blade.description:
Create a blade of compressed vacuum: the absence of air shaped into a cutting edge. The blade ignores conventional armor because it cuts at the molecular level. No sound, no flash, just a line of nothingness that severs what it touches.
[Wind Magic: 6]

Wild Harvest.name: Wild Harvest
Wild Harvest.description:
Find useful plants, mushrooms, and natural materials in any terrain within minutes. You know what is edible, what is medicinal, and what will keep the party alive when the rations run out and the nearest shop is three dungeons away.
[Foraging: 2]

Wind Barrier.name: Wind Barrier
Wind Barrier.description:
High-speed winds stand up in a howling wall: arrows tumbling away, projectiles shredded, light magic scattered into harmless glitter: anything lightweight that enters is redistributed as confetti. Defense you can hear three rooms away. It answers ranged insult and thin magic (heavy blows and committed bodies wade through the howl), and its constant announcement is the tradeoff nobody negotiates around: a wind wall keeps you safe and keeps you found. It guards those behind it on the turn you raise it; keeping it spinning takes your action again each turn.
[Wind Magic: 4]

Absolute Zero.name: Absolute Zero
Absolute Zero.description:
The Frozen Throne's signature verdict: a target or area flash-frozen toward temperatures that make winter look indecisive: enemies immobilized in absolute ice, rendered so brittle that the follow-up strike shatters them with dramatic effect, which the blessing considers the entire point. The freeze claims its target in one catastrophic drop (the brittleness is the gift; the party's heavy hitter is the delivery), cold at theoretical limits draws the throne's deepest reserves, and the silence after an absolute freeze is famous: even the battlefield declines to comment.
[Ice Magic: 9]

Anthem of War.name: Anthem of War
Anthem of War.description:
The bard abandons subtlety and belts it: a thunderous war anthem driving every ally into controlled battle frenzy: attack power surging, pain filed under later. The music is the magic; silencing the singer is the counter every enemy eventually attempts. The bard finishes hoarse, beloved, and completely unable to whisper.
[Sound Magic: 6]

Arcane Chains.name: Arcane Chains
Arcane Chains.description:
Shackles of pure mana snap around the target: bound in place, magic suppressed, and the chains tighten when the target uses magic, punishing the exact struggle a mage attempts first. Brute strength eventually argues through what magic cannot. The binding's true lesson: sometimes the correct response to magic is patience, which mages famously lack.
[Arcane Magic: 17]

Arcane Shield.name: Arcane Shield
Arcane Shield.description:
Raw mana pressed into a shimmering plane: incoming damage sinks into it and dims, spells especially arriving like stones into deep water. Against magic it is a wall; against a warhammer it is a strongly worded suggestion. Projecting it costs the brawler focus better spent on the fist behind it, which is the whole balancing act of the style. It guards you on the turn you raise it; holding it takes your action again each turn.
[Arcane Magic: 3]

Barrier Arrow.name: Barrier Arrow
Barrier Arrow.description:
The arrow lands and becomes architecture: a shimmering barrier blooming at the impact point: enemies and projectiles refused, allies waved through like regulars. Cover, delivered at range, exactly where the line needed it. The archer carries only so many barrier-heads in a quiver: walls this convenient are fletched, not free. It guards the spot you shoot on the turn you loose it; holding the line takes another shot each turn.
[Archery: 4]

Beast Command.name: Beast Command
Beast Command.description:
Direct a trained companion creature in combat: positioning, flanking, attacking, or defending. The beast responds to your bond and training with coordination that surprises enemies expecting an uncontrolled animal.
[Beast Keeping: 3]

Beast Mending.name: Beast Mending
Beast Mending.description:
The tamer lays both hands on the wounded creature and simply gives: their own vitality flowing across the bond, torn flesh knitting under fingers that shake slightly with the cost. The bond makes the transfer direct and honest: the beast's pain arrives as the tamer's fatigue. Mending flows along true bonds only, and every serious healing is a withdrawal from the tamer's own body that no gratitude, however furry, refunds.
[Beast Keeping: 4]

Blazing Cloak.name: Blazing Cloak
Blazing Cloak.description:
Surround yourself in a cloak of controlled fire. Melee attackers take fire damage on contact, and your fire spells are amplified while the cloak burns. Your clothes are magically protected. Your eyebrows are not guaranteed.
[Fire Magic: 12]

Bone Colossus.name: Bone Colossus
Bone Colossus.description:
Gather bones from multiple sources and assemble them into a towering skeletal construct: a bone colossus that fights as your champion. It's massive, slow, and hits like a building falling on someone.
[Spirit Channeling: 60 · Arcane Magic: 6]

Brutal Strike.name: Brutal Strike
Brutal Strike.description:
No feint, no artistry: the gladiator simply hits the target the way a falling gate hits a cart: a staggering, bone-jarring blow that knocks the wind out of the armored and knocks the unarmored down entirely. It is honest violence, and honesty travels. The strike telegraphs by nature (that is the price of that much force), asks everything of the swing, and needs a beat of recovered footing before it can be thrown again.
[Heavy Weapons: 2]

Call the Pack.name: Call the Pack
Call the Pack.description:
One call, a whistle, a roar, a name only beasts know, and every creature the tamer has ever truly bonded answers: wings from the treeline, paws from the ridge, something enormous surfacing from the river, all of it loyal and all of it arriving. A small army with one heart. The call reaches only genuine bonds, takes the pack real travel time across real distance, and asking everyone to come means everyone came: the tamer now owes the whole family dinner.
[Beast Keeping: 41]

Calming Scent.name: Calming Scent
Calming Scent.description:
Release a fragrance that calms aggression and soothes anxiety in an area. Hostile creatures become less inclined to fight, anxious allies regain their composure, and the air itself seems to breathe easier. The scent lingers long after you have moved on.
[Perfumery: 2]

Chronos Reign.name: Chronos Reign
Chronos Reign.description:
The ultimate Chronomancer technique. Stop time itself across the entire battlefield. For several seconds, only you and your allies can move. Every enemy is frozen, every spell is paused, and you have all the time in the world to set up the perfect sequence of actions. When time resumes, the results are devastating and instantaneous. The universe blinks and misses everything.
[Time Magic: 48]

Combat Puppet.name: Combat Puppet
Combat Puppet.description:
The puppeteer deploys the big one: a combat puppet armed with real weapons, stronger and more durable than the basic troupe, capable of holding a front line while its owner conducts from safety. A bodyguard built in a workshop. The puppet fights at the length of its threads and the quality of its construction, holding its own but not improvising (puppets execute; they do not adapt), and losing one mid-fight is losing weeks of workmanship: puppeteers grieve in repair bills.
[Artifice: 4]

Command Voice.name: Command Voice
Command Voice.description:
Speak with divine authority, issuing a single command that resonates in the listener's very soul. The command cannot compel self-destruction, but it carries supernatural weight: enemies hesitate, guards stand aside, and the arrogant reconsider their life choices. The Blessing punishes lies with silence.
[persuasion: 5]

Contract Seal.name: Contract Seal
Contract Seal.description:
Seal a written agreement with magical binding ink that penalizes any signer who breaks the terms. The penalty is agreed upon at signing: pain, misfortune, mana drain, or the sudden inability to lie about the contract's contents. The Twilight Dominion considers these sacred; the Crownveil courts consider them legally binding.
[Inscription: 24]

Corpse Puppet.name: Corpse Puppet
Corpse Puppet.description:
The defeated enemy stands back up on threads: converted permanently into a puppet that fights for the puppeteer: same shape, familiar moves, a shadow of its former ability and none of its former opinions or its voice. Every battlefield doubles as recruitment. The conversion requires a reasonably intact defeated enemy and real ritual attention, the puppet retains skill's outline but not its edge, and marching your enemies' dead colleagues into the next fight has a documented effect on enemy morale and on how the Church addresses you.
[Artifice: 47]

Crescent Draw.name: Crescent Draw
Crescent Draw.description:
The iaido philosophy, widened: a single arcing draw that cuts through multiple enemies in one sweep, the arc so clean it parts the air itself and leaves a visible crescent hanging in the blade's wake like a signature in light. Space-clearing, calligraphed. The crescent trades the straight draw's speed for breadth (surrounded is the technique's home; single duels want its sibling), the wide arc demands room to write in, and the lingering crescent is pure theater with a function: everything still standing has been shown, precisely, the blade's reach.
[Swordsmanship: 5]

Crystal Bloom.name: Crystal Bloom
Crystal Bloom.description:
Grow a bed of jagged crystals from any surface, floor, wall, or ceiling, that traps enemies in place and damages anything that moves through the field. The crystals persist until shattered or the mana fades.
[Crystal Magic: 5]

Crystal Sense.name: Crystal Sense
Crystal Sense.description:
Detect nearby mana crystals and mineral deposits through the subtle resonance they emit. You feel the hum before you see the glow, and you know whether the find is worth the climb, the dig, or the risk of whatever is nesting on top of it.
[Crystal Prospecting: 2]

Curse Removal.name: Curse Removal
Curse Removal.description:
The exorcist takes the curse apart strand by strand: naming its anchor, unhooking its teeth, drawing the whole affliction out and burning it to nothing in a closed fist. The purification is complete: no remnant, no relapse, no seed left to regrow. It is also expensive: unmaking someone else's malice drains the exorcist badly, and the older and angrier the curse, the longer they sway on their feet afterward.
[Occult Lore: 7]

Cursed Ground.name: Cursed Ground
Cursed Ground.description:
The witch curses the ground itself, and the ground develops a sense of humor: enemies crossing it trip on nothing, drop weapons that were firmly held, and trigger small magical accidents with impeccable comedic timing. Misfortune, zoned. The curse afflicts the marked area only and expresses itself in minor chaos rather than raw damage (it wins fights by ruining choreography) and its randomness is genuine: the witch controls where the bad luck lives, never which pratfall it chooses.
[Charm Magic: 12]

Dark Affinity.name: Dark Affinity
Dark Affinity.description:
Your demon blood gives you a natural connection to shadow and dark magic. Darkness feels comfortable rather than threatening. You can manipulate shadows, see in pitch blackness, and sense demonic energy. Dark-type spells come easier to you, and demons instinctively recognize you as kin. The church finds this concerning. You find it useful.
[Occult Lore: 3]

Death Blossom.name: Death Blossom
Death Blossom.description:
The spin through the crowd: blades extended, every enemy within reach struck with lethal precision: each cut targeting a different vital point, the rotation solving the room in one revolution. You stop in the center of the carnage, which is the technique's signature and its portrait. The blossom includes everything in reach without appeal (allies clear the radius; the flower does not check invitations), its full rotation commits utterly, and the final stillness (the killer motionless amid the falling) is the school's calling card, left deliberately.
[Stealth: 32]

Death's Chill.name: Death's Chill
Death's Chill.description:
Release a wave of necrotic cold that slows and damages all enemies in a cone. The cold isn't natural: it's the temperature of the grave, and it seeps through armor to freeze muscles and dull reactions.
[Poison Magic: 3 · Arcane Magic: 2]

Divine Shield.name: Divine Shield
Divine Shield.description:
Holy light settles over the caster in a barrier that treats assault as testimony: the shield glowing brighter with every blow it drinks, a lighthouse being argued with. When it breaks, it shatters dramatically: a burst of radiance that announces exactly how much was endured, and its swelling glow is honest with everyone: enemies can read how close it is to breaking, which becomes its own psychological duel. It guards you on the turn you raise it; keeping it up takes your action again each turn.
[Light Magic: 4]

Divine Vessel.name: Divine Vessel
Divine Vessel.description:
The ultimate Priest ability. Become a vessel for divine power: your eyes glow gold, your voice echoes with celestial resonance, and every spell you cast is amplified to miraculous levels. Healing becomes regeneration. Barriers become absolute. Your very presence purges corruption. Brief, overwhelming, and sacred.
[Divinity: 56]

Dragon Breath.name: Dragon Breath
Dragon Breath.description:
The blessing opens the oldest channel in your blood: a roaring short-range cone of true dragonfire loosed from mouth or open palms. It burns far hotter than any common firebolt, engulfing the whole front rank in searing heat and leaving a clinging slag-fire that keeps scorching armor and flesh after the exhale ends. This is a furnace door blown wide rather than long-range artillery: each breath taxes lungs and vein together, and loosing it in public ends any disguise on the spot.
[Fire Magic: 3]

Dream Walking.name: Dream Walking
Dream Walking.description:
The familiar slips into a sleeper's dream like a letter under a door: gathering what the dreaming mind guards poorly (names, fears, the location of the thing they think about before sleep) or planting one soft suggestion where morning will find it. The target wakes unsettled, certain of nothing, unable to name the source. The walking needs a sleeping target and a patient familiar, dreams defend themselves in strange ways, and minds visited too often start sleeping badly on purpose.
[Dream Magic: 9]

Dream Whisper.name: Dream Whisper
Dream Whisper.description:
Send a faint message, image, or emotional impression into a sleeping target's dream. Useful for warnings, clues, comfort, or unsettling enemies. The dreamer may not remember clearly, but the impression lingers.
[Dream Magic: 2]

Dueling Focus.name: Dueling Focus
Dueling Focus.description:
The world narrows to one opponent: absolute concentration: attacks against them sharper, their tells arriving like subtitles. Everything else fades to background noise, which is precisely the price: flankers love a focused duelist. Its masters treat it as a formal declaration: locking eyes and going quiet is, in dueling circles, a complete sentence.
[Dueling: 5]

Earthen Golem.name: Earthen Golem
Earthen Golem.description:
Shape stone and earth into a humanoid construct that fights on your behalf. The golem is slow but immensely strong and durable. It follows simple commands and can take hits that would destroy living fighters.
[Earth Magic: 7]

Eclipse Slash.name: Eclipse Slash
Eclipse Slash.description:
The crescent of pure darkness, swung at battlefield scale: temporary night falling across the field, every enemy in the arc taking devastating dark damage and losing their sight to a blackness that lingers past the blade. One slash, one eclipse. The eclipse claims its arc in a single release (the lingering dark hampers enemies while the caster's allies were warned, which is the whole choreography), summoning night on command spends the mage's reserves like a festival spends candles, and witnesses date fights by it afterward: before the eclipse, and after.
[Shadow Magic: 42]

Ember Rebirth.name: Ember Rebirth
Ember Rebirth.description: Use it as the killing blow comes or lands, and the Phoenixborn answers that same turn with dawn: fire erupts outward in a ring that scours everything nearby, and from the center they rise with much of their health returned: wounds cauterized, heart restarted, eyes briefly gold. It is the single most beautiful thing most enemies never live to describe. The flame answers only once per day, and rising costs something each time: exhaustion that no potion touches, and ash where their footprints were.

Enchant Armor.name: Enchant Armor
Enchant Armor.description:
The enchanter lays hands on their own armor or an ally's and pours protection into the plates: incoming physical and magical damage alike arriving dulled, the metal humming softly with stored power like a kettle deciding against boiling. Insurance, audible. An enchanter can armor the party, but one coat at a time, which makes the order of operations a small nightly politics. It guards one wearer on the turn you cast it; renewing it takes your action again each turn.
[Enchanting: 4]

Escape Artist.name: Escape Artist
Escape Artist.description:
The refusal to stay caught, professionalized: ropes shed, chains slipped, locks picked by feel, magical bindings discovering loopholes: including, the technique notes, social obligations. Each binding is its own puzzle solved at speed. Captors discover the profession's motto: 'thoroughly' is a challenge rating, not a guarantee.
[acrobatics: 32]

Event Horizon.name: Event Horizon
Event Horizon.description:
The ultimate shadow spell. Open a rift to the Void: the space between spaces where shadow originates. The rift generates crushing gravitational pull that drags everything toward it while dealing continuous dark damage. Light bends, sound warps, and the fabric of reality stretches toward the point of no return.
[Shadow Magic: 55]

Evil Analysis.name: Evil Analysis
Evil Analysis.description:
The exorcist studies the entity the way a locksmith studies a vault: true nature identified, hidden vulnerabilities mapped, secret names surfaced, and (the profession's real currency) the specific rituals that can destroy it. Knowledge as a killing blow's blueprint. The analysis demands focused observation of the entity itself (time spent studying is time spent in its company, which is the fee), it reveals the path rather than walking it, and entities that feel themselves being read respond with the urgency of the correctly frightened.
[Occult Lore: 39]

Falling Petal.name: Falling Petal
Falling Petal.description:
The dodge that ends fights: a graceful evasion flowing directly into a lethal counter: the petal falling away from the stem, untouched by the wind that came for it, and the wind paying for the attempt. A cautious opponent starves the flower. Duelists describe losing to it bitterly, in the technique's own poetry: they missed, and then they were finished.
[acrobatics: 5]

Final Descent.name: Final Descent
Final Descent.description:
The ultimate Dragoon technique. Ascend until you become a speck in the sky, then dive with your spear wrapped in a column of elemental fury: fire, lightning, and wind spiraling together. The descent takes seconds. The impact reshapes the battlefield. Nothing survives ground zero. The crater is your signature.
[athletics: 69]

Fire Eruption.name: Fire Eruption
Fire Eruption.description:
The caster marks the ground and the ground becomes a volcano's opinion: flame blasting upward from below across the target area, enemies launched skyward on pillars of fire, everything in the radius scorched by geology's least patient element. Attacks from underneath are the ones nobody guards. The eruption claims its marked area and no more (aim is everything; allies read the marking or learn), it needs a beat of channeling that watchful enemies can spot in the glowing seams, and the scorched ground afterward is a signature the Emberwake would recognize.
[Fire Magic: 6]

Flowing Blade.name: Flowing Blade
Flowing Blade.description:
The strike fails, parried, dodged, denied, and the swordsman's answer is already flowing: the blocked momentum redirected into a follow-up from an angle the defense never scheduled. A failed strike becomes a second chance; a parried swordsman becomes more dangerous. Fluid swordsmanship at its finest. The flow feeds on the swordsman's own redirected motion (it needs a genuine attempt to convert; you cannot flow from nothing), and duelists who parry the style correctly once learn the school's motto the hard way: the first swing was the question.
[Swordsmanship: 7]

Foxfire Feint.name: Foxfire Feint
Foxfire Feint.description: A bloom of blue-white foxfire dances exactly where the Kitsune-Blessed is not: eyes follow it, blades follow the eyes, and social disasters dissolve into 'did anyone else see that?' while the fox is already three graceful steps gone. The fire is playful misdirection, not force (it draws attention and spends it) and each flame owes a little mischief back to the shrine, which keeps the accounting in ways foxes decline to explain.

Frozen Ground.name: Frozen Ground
Frozen Ground.description:
The floor becomes an opinion: flash-frozen into a treacherous mirror where enemies slip, sprawl, and lose every plan that involved footing, while the caster glides across it with a skater's insulting grace. Terrain control with a sense of theater. The ice claims the frozen area only, melts on its own schedule (faster near fire, slower in Yukishiro, obviously), and it is loyal to physics rather than friendship: allies without ice-sense should route around, or provide the comedy.
[Ice Magic: 3]

Gadget Deploy.name: Gadget Deploy
Gadget Deploy.description:
Activate a prepared gadget for a tactical effect: smoke screen, flash charge, trip wire, or whatever you built into today's loadout. The device does exactly what it was designed to do, assuming you remember which pocket you put it in.
[Artifice: 3]

Healing Light.name: Healing Light
Healing Light.description:
The Priest's first spell and the one nobody outgrows: warm divine light onto a wounded ally: flesh closing, warmth spreading like being remembered by someone who matters. More effective when cast with genuine concern; that is the mechanism, not a flourish. Every veteran on the continent knows the exact temperature of it: the warmth is the first thing anyone remembers about being saved.
[Divinity: 2]

Healing Totem.name: Healing Totem
Healing Totem.description:
The totem drinks a healing spirit's patience and pours it back out as an area of quiet restoration: allies near it feel wounds close by degrees, warm and unhurried, like sitting near a hearth that likes them. It anchors a battle line beautifully. The mending flows only within the totem's reach and only while it stands (enemies learn quickly to aim at the post instead of the people) and the spirit expects the warden's thanks afterward.
[Nature Magic: 3]

Heaven's Gale.name: Heaven's Gale
Heaven's Gale.description:
The ultimate wind spell. Call down the winds of the upper atmosphere: a vertical column of air moving at speeds that make hurricanes look gentle. The gale flattens structures, scatters armies, and reshapes terrain.
[Wind Magic: 18]

Hellfire Bolt.name: Hellfire Bolt
Hellfire Bolt.description:
Hurl a bolt of demonic fire that burns with dark energy rather than natural heat. The flames are violet-black and cannot be extinguished by water: only by magic or time. Deals fire and dark damage simultaneously.
[Fire Magic: 9]

Hidden Needle.name: Hidden Needle
Hidden Needle.description:
The trap inside the ordinary: a step that arms something, a gesture that releases it, a thrown object that was never the attack: a deadly mechanism concealed within innocuous motion, activating when conditions are met, catching even vigilant enemies precisely because they were watching the obvious. The needle rewards preparation and patience (the setup is the skill; the activation is just punctuation), one trap rides one concealing action, and enemies who survive it are permanently ruined for watching anyone do anything casual.
[Stealth: 36]

Holy Radiance.name: Holy Radiance
Holy Radiance.description:
One pulse, two congregations: blinding divine light bursting outward: enemies seared, allies healed, the light sorting the room by allegiance at the speed of judgment. The after-image is famous on both sides: the healed remember gold; the seared remember nothing, which they report as worse.
[Light Magic: 27]

Hundred Fists.name: Hundred Fists
Hundred Fists.description:
The Arcane Brawler's ultimate: a barrage so fast each punch trails afterimages: the target struck by what appears to be, and functionally is, a hundred fists at once. The stillness afterward is scheduled; allies cover it or the technique covers a defeat. Witnesses uniformly fail the same way describing it: the counting.
[Unarmed Combat: 8]

Hunter's Mark.name: Hunter's Mark
Hunter's Mark.description:
The ranger designates the quarry, and the world narrows: the target's location sensed like a compass heading, attacks against them landing with bonus intent, the trail impossible to lose across wilderness, crowd, or excuse. Being hunted becomes a condition rather than an event. The mark rides one quarry for its duration (choosing who is the hunter's whole tactical statement), it aids pursuit and punishment rather than dealing its own harm, and marked prey who somehow learn of it experience a very specific quality of sleep.
[Archery: 7]

Inferno Burst.name: Inferno Burst
Inferno Burst.description:
Unleash a devastating eruption of flame fueled by raw emotion. The angrier you are, the wider and hotter the burst. Allies near the edge feel warmth. Enemies in the center are incinerated. The fire crackles with a sound suspiciously like laughter.
[Fire Magic: 5]

Infinite Edge.name: Infinite Edge
Infinite Edge.description:
Enter a flowing combat state where every strike leads seamlessly into the next. Your attacks accelerate, each sword swing faster than the last, until you generate phantom slashes: cuts that arrive from angles your blade never physically traveled. The dance doesn't stop until everything in range is cut down.
[Swordsmanship: 5]

Iron Fortress.name: Iron Fortress
Iron Fortress.description:
The body decides to be architecture: mass settling, stance rooting, vitality swelling to a titan's reserve that turns killing blows into line items. The fortress simply refuses to fall, and wise fortresses arrange to be winning before the walls come down. It guards you on the turn you take it; holding it takes your action again each turn.
[athletics: 53]

Iron Will Cut.name: Iron Will Cut
Iron Will Cut.description:
One cut, carried by conviction instead of muscle: the blade goes where the resolve points and declines to be turned; not by parry, not by armor's argument, not by the wielder's own doubt, which is the real opponent. Willpower made steel. The cut demands a settled heart to swing; hesitation dulls it to ordinary metal, and a swordsman's worst day is discovering mid-arc exactly how sure they weren't.
[Swordsmanship: 3]

Judgment Mark.name: Judgment Mark
Judgment Mark.description:
The inquisitor speaks the charge aloud, and a sigil of pale fire brands itself above the target's heart: visible through walls, smoke, shadow, and lies. There is no hiding from judgment, and holy power finds the mark like water finds a low place. The brand demands a spoken accusation with belief behind it; mark someone the inquisitor doubts is guilty and the sigil burns the accuser's tongue instead.
[Divinity: 1]

Keepsake Ward.name: Keepsake Ward
Keepsake Ward.description:
Create a keepsake item that carries a faint protective ward for its bearer: a quiet warning of harm, a steadying warmth, the feeling that someone cares whether you come home. The keepsake warns and comforts; in a fight, it cannot stop a blow on its own.
[Gift Crafting: 3]

Kunai Barrage.name: Kunai Barrage
Kunai Barrage.description:
A spread of kunai leaves the ninja's hands in one fan: multiple targets struck, each blade wearing a mild toxin that drags footwork into syrup. Each blade stings rather than fells; the slow is the product. The toxin's mildness is a professional courtesy nobody believes until the antidote proves unnecessary.
[Dagger Fighting: 2]

Layered Curse.name: Layered Curse
Layered Curse.description:
Apply a debilitating curse that stacks with other active curses on the target. Each Layered Curse reduces a different aspect of the target's capabilities: speed, accuracy, damage, defense, or resistance. Multiple layers compound geometrically: one curse is annoying, two are concerning, three are crippling, and four mean the target is fighting at half capacity. Removing the curses requires dispelling each layer individually.
[Dark Magic: 2]

Light Sanctum.name: Light Sanctum
Light Sanctum.description:
The dome of pure light, raised as sacred law: everyone inside protected from external attack while continuous healing washes through, and dark magic cannot even exist within, the sanctum treating darkness as a trespass and unmaking it at the border. Shadow-wielders regard a standing sanctum the way arsonists regard rain.
[Light Magic: 41]

Mana Fortress.name: Mana Fortress
Mana Fortress.description:
The sage's cathedral: a massive dome of layered arcane barriers: spells breaking on the outer shell, projectiles dying in the middle, physical entry refused at the innermost. Layered protection is layered upkeep; the sage inside is both architect and generator, and enemies settle into the siege the fortress was built to win: patience versus mana, and the sage brought more. It guards everyone inside on the turn you raise it; sustaining it takes your action again each turn.
[Focus: 34]

Meteor Strike.name: Meteor Strike
Meteor Strike.description:
Call down a concentrated bolt of celestial energy from above: a miniature star that crashes into the target area with devastating force. The impact leaves a smoldering crater and everything nearby is bathed in blinding starlight. The Church calls it divine judgment. The crater calls it Tuesday.
[Light Magic: 7]

Mutagen Spray.name: Mutagen Spray
Mutagen Spray.description:
The alchemist mists the party with progress: a cloud of alchemical mutagen enhancing physical capabilities across everyone breathing it: stronger, faster, briefly improved beyond warranty. The power is real. The side effects are temporary. Probably. The spray lifts allies within the cloud for its duration (side effects draw from a rotating menu the alchemist describes as 'cosmetic, mostly': the itching, the night vision, the brief tail), and parties learn the ritual response: inhale, improve, and file complaints later through chattering, temporarily perfect teeth.
[Alchemy: 30]

Nature's Ally.name: Nature's Ally
Nature's Ally.description:
The wilderness takes a side, and it's yours: vines entangling pursuers, roots tripping at exactly the wrong step, wind shifting to swallow your scent, birds crying warning before the ambush closes. Nature recognizes you as one of its own, and family helps. The aid arrives suited to the surroundings (stone halls and salted fields have little to offer; the technique reads the terrain's inventory), each calling is one favor honestly given, and rangers honor the account's terms: those the wild assists leave the wild better, or find it suddenly neutral.
[survival: 31]

Necrotic Nova.name: Necrotic Nova
Necrotic Nova.description:
The mage becomes the epicenter on purpose: an expanding sphere of pure necrotic energy rolling outward from their own body: living creatures within taking massive dark damage while undead allies are healed and empowered by the same wave, the nova reading allegiance by pulse. One blast, two congregations. The sphere expands once per release with the caster at its heart (positioning is the entire tactical text: living allies clear the radius or contribute), and detonating necrosis from one's own chest marks the mage in every witness's permanent record.
[Dark Magic: 34]

Nimble Escape.name: Nimble Escape
Nimble Escape.description:
The Mousekin art of simply not being caught: grapples shed, bindings slipped, tight spaces navigated with desperate, wriggling agility that larger creatures find genuinely offensive. Its reach is gloriously broad: magical bindings, nets, webs, and social situations where you really need to not be in the room anymore. Captors who plan for a Mousekin plan for water: containers, not grips.
[acrobatics: 1]

Phoenix Flame.name: Phoenix Flame
Phoenix Flame.description:
Channel the legendary phoenix fire: flames that burn away corruption, purify curses, and can reignite the spark of life in a recently fallen ally. The fire is golden-white instead of orange and feels warm rather than painful to allies.
[Fire Magic: 45]

Puppet Double.name: Puppet Double
Puppet Double.description:
A puppet wearing the puppeteer's face steps into the light and mimics their movements with unsettling fidelity: enemies committing attacks, plans, and pride against a duplicate while the original conducts from a different angle entirely. Misdirection with joints. The double mimics rather than improvises (close inspection or a solid hit reveals the wood beneath the performance), splitting attention between self and double is the technique's true cost, and enemies fooled once develop a career-long distrust of everyone's face.
[Artifice: 16]

Purify Spirit.name: Purify Spirit
Purify Spirit.description:
Divine energy in one targeted burst, aimed not at the host but at the tenant: the possessing spirit forced out, immediately, violently, and with prejudice, the exorcism landing on the entity like an eviction served at dawn. The host collapses free; the spirit arrives in the open air with grievances. The purge expels rather than destroys (what comes out must still be dealt with, and it is never in a good mood), and the burst spends real grace: exorcists learn to have a plan for the sixty seconds after success.
[Divinity: 3]

Radiant Burst.name: Radiant Burst
Radiant Burst.description:
Purifying light in one expanding wave: enemies in range scorched by radiance, allies it washes over feeling curses and afflictions burn away mid-stride: harm and hygiene in a single pulse, undead and demons receiving the light's special attention. The burst expands once per release and treats the room impartially by nature (enemies pay, allies are laundered, the unholy pay double), and releasing that much stored radiance leaves the caster briefly dim in the spirit's book: light given is light gathered again slowly.
[Light Magic: 4]

Ricochet Shot.name: Ricochet Shot
Ricochet Shot.description:
Fire a bullet enchanted to bounce between surfaces, hitting targets around cover or striking multiple enemies in enclosed spaces. Perfected during shipboard combat in tight corridors. The trajectories are calculated by instinct, not math, and the instinct has never been wrong.
[Firearms: 8]

Royal Command.name: Royal Command
Royal Command.description:
The sovereign's voice drops into a register that armies remember: a single ally is named, and power settles over them like a mantle: steadier hands, brighter nerve, strength borrowed from the authority itself. The command cannot turn inward; a ruler empowers the people who fight for them, never themselves. Each decree takes true conviction to issue, and even a sovereign's voice needs a few beats to gather that weight again.
[Command: 2]

Sacred Ground.name: Sacred Ground
Sacred Ground.description:
The exorcist consecrates the field itself: sanctified ground hostile to evil (undead burning by the step, dark magic arriving muffled) while allies feel the resistance settle into them like borrowed conviction. The border is exact, and the clever unholy respect it to the inch: fights develop a very literal line.
[Light Magic: 4]

Sacred Strike.name: Sacred Strike
Sacred Strike.description:
Sanctified energy pours down the exorcist's arm and the strike lands twice-blessed: honest impact plus a searing rebuke that undead, demons, and the possessed experience as personal correspondence: light going through them like a judgment. Against ordinary flesh it is merely a good hit wearing vestments.
[Divinity: 2]

Shadow Cleave.name: Shadow Cleave
Shadow Cleave.description:
Shadow pours down the blade and the slash arrives trailing night: dark damage in the cut, and a smear of darkness left across the target's eyes that dims the world for them at the worst professional moment. Duelists hate it with specificity. The dimming is brief, a stolen second of blindness, not a stolen fight, and the shadow must be re-fed between cleaves; the dark lends its edge on a strict schedule.
[Dark Magic: 3]

Shadow Clones.name: Shadow Clones
Shadow Clones.description:
Two duplicates of dark-stuff step out and take the field: flanking, distracting, absorbing hits meant for the original: reduced damage but real presence, three problems wearing one face. Destroyed, they dissolve into dark mist with theatrical dignity. The clones fight at a fraction of the caster's force (they are pressure and confusion, not a doubled army), splitting attention three ways is the technique's true discipline, and enemies who guess wrong about which one is real fund the school's entire reputation.
[Shadow Magic: 21]

Shatter Guard.name: Shatter Guard
Shatter Guard.description:
Rage focused into a single structural argument: an overhead blow engineered to break blocks, split shields, and collapse defensive stances: the target's guard destroyed outright and their whole posture left open like a door off its hinges. The answer to turtles. The blow spends its fury on the defense rather than the defender (the follow-up is the party's job, and the party should be ready), and its huge commitment telegraphs honestly: read early, it shatters nothing but the swordsman's positioning.
[Heavy Weapons: 6]

Silver Tongue.name: Silver Tongue
Silver Tongue.description:
The next statement leaves the mouth supernaturally convincing: lies wearing truth's posture, requests arriving as foregone conclusions, the sentence landing with a weight the words alone never earned. Rhetoric, enchanted. The tongue silvers one statement per gathering: choosing the sentence is the entire art (masters spend it on nine words or fewer), and while it works best when the target is already inclined to agree, it tips scales rather than replacing them, and outright absurdities still fail, merely more charmingly than usual, which has its own uses.
[persuasion: 4]

Sniper's Nest.name: Sniper's Nest
Sniper's Nest.description:
Find an elevated position and enter a focused sniping stance. While in position, your range doubles, your accuracy increases dramatically, and you gain the ability to spot enemies through partial cover.
[Firearms: 22]

Song of Haste.name: Song of Haste
Song of Haste.description:
Play an accelerating rhythm that quickens allies' movements and reactions. The tempo speeds up gradually, and everyone in range finds their footwork faster, their swings quicker, and their dodges sharper.
[performance: 9]

Spell Reflect.name: Spell Reflect
Spell Reflect.description:
The mirror with a timing window: a reflective barrier that bounces incoming spells back at their caster: the window narrow, the results spectacular, the technique's entire tuition paid in reflexes. Nothing demoralizes a Mage faster than their own Fireball, a fact the ability's documentation states as its design goal. The reflect answers spells caught in its brief activation (curved, delayed, and area magic decline the mirror's invitation), each raising spends real focus, and mages who have eaten their own signature spell change disciplines with documented frequency.
[Arcane Magic: 13]

Spell Trigger.name: Spell Trigger
Spell Trigger.description:
The mage stores a spell in a surface and teaches it patience: a trigger keyed to conditions of the caster's choosing: the third footstep, the opened door, the specific face. When the terms are met, the stored spell casts itself. Vague terms produce lawyer problems. Trained eyes can spot the shimmer of stored intent: placement is the art.
[Firearms: 6]

Spirit Beacon.name: Spirit Beacon
Spirit Beacon.description:
Ignite your soul flame to maximum luminance, creating a beacon that burns away spiritual corruption, dispels possessions, banishes wraiths, and illuminates hidden truths. Lies spoken within the beacon's radius become visible as dark smoke. Hidden enemies are outlined in soul-light. The dead within range are soothed. The living within range feel a profound, bone-deep sense of safety.
[Soul Magic: 15]

Spirit Prison.name: Spirit Prison
Spirit Prison.description:
Bars of woven light rise around the evil entity and close: no escape, no attack, no abilities: just a furious presence in a bright cage, finally available for conversation, judgment, or transport. The prison holds absolutely while it holds at all: maintaining it against a strong entity is a continuous act of will, and the light dims the moment the exorcist's attention genuinely breaks. One prisoner at a time. Choose well.
[Occult Lore: 21]

Spirit Shield.name: Spirit Shield
Spirit Shield.description:
Call upon a protective spirit to shield yourself or an ally from harm. The spirit manifests as a faint, luminous presence that intercepts blows and whispers warnings of approaching danger. The bond is brief but the gratitude is lasting. It guards you or one ally on the turn you call it; calling it again takes your action again each turn.
[Spirit Channeling: 4]

Steel Blossom.name: Steel Blossom
Steel Blossom.description:
The samurai's flowering pattern: multiple shallow cuts opening in sequence, each following the last like petals leaving a branch: no single wound decisive, the accumulation undeniable. Armor interrupts petals; the pattern prefers cloth and confidence. Duelists who watch their own blood describe a flower develop the intended condition: distraction, fatal.
[Swordsmanship: 2]

Summon Legend.name: Summon Legend
Summon Legend.description:
The ultimate Summoner technique. Tear open the boundary between worlds and call forth a legendary entity: a being of mythic power that exists in no single realm. The summon obeys because it chooses to, and its power reshapes the battlefield. It joins your party the moment it answers and stays until it is dismissed or falls: an aspect of the legend, no stronger than its summoner. While it stays, you stand beside something that gods would hesitate to fight.
[Spirit Channeling: 100]

Thousand Cuts.name: Thousand Cuts
Thousand Cuts.description:
Your blade becomes a blur of phantom strikes. You attack so fast that the air itself splits into cutting edges, delivering dozens of slashes in a single motion. The cuts arrive from impossible angles: from your sword, from its afterimages, from the very space your blade traveled through moments ago. The enemy doesn't see a swordsman. They see a storm with a handle.
[Swordsmanship: 18]

Thunder Lance.name: Thunder Lance
Thunder Lance.description:
The jump strike, electrified: lightning channeled through the spear during descent, the charge detonating on impact: lightning damage blooming in a radius around the landing point, the thunderclap echoing off everything with an opinion. Altitude plus voltage equals arithmetic nobody survives casually. The lance spends its charge on one landing (the radius punishes enemies who gathered to catch the dragoon: a decision they revise in the air), and the technique's announcement is total: thunder, from a person, arriving. Subtlety filed for a different school.
[athletics: 25]

Thunderstrike.name: Thunderstrike
Thunderstrike.description:
Call down a thunderbolt from the sky to strike a target with devastating precision. The bolt tracks your intent; it can arc between multiple enemies or focus on a single target for maximum damage. The thunderclap that follows shakes the battlefield.
[Storm Magic: 10]

Time Dilation.name: Time Dilation
Time Dilation.description:
A pocket of the battlefield thickens: inside the faint shimmer, enemies wade at half speed while the chronomancer moves at the world's honest pace: dodging becomes strolling, aiming becomes choosing. The distortion is small, visible, and rude. It slows everything inside impartially (allies should mind the edges), holds only briefly before time reasserts its dignity, and repeat castings come slower: time notices being handled.
[Time Magic: 2]

Trap Analysis.name: Trap Analysis
Trap Analysis.description:
Identify a trap's trigger mechanism, damage potential, and reset condition by analyzing its architectural and magical structure. You know what it does before it does it, and you know how to tell the party without everyone panicking.
[Dungeon Surveying: 3]

Truth Overlay.name: Truth Overlay
Truth Overlay.description: The world annotates itself: stats hover over strangers, conditions glow on the wounded, hidden qualities shine through shop-counter glass, monster weaknesses print themselves in the air; and, most dangerously, where something is being kept from you (the gap in a story, the clause missing from a contract, the pocket sewn shut) the overlay marks the spot and tells you what it can read of what fills it. It reads past the limits of ordinary appraisal, in plain words; only the world's truly unreadable beings turn it aside. Always on. Impossible to unsee. The overlay reads what is, not what will be, and people who realize they are being read this thoroughly respond with awe, recruitment offers, or knives.

Umbral Throne.name: Umbral Throne
Umbral Throne.description:
The night-throne miracle: darkness rising around the sovereign in towering architecture, enemy radiance smothered like candles in a fist and hostile morale cracking as every shadow acquires the weight of judgment. For the throne's duration, the dark is a court and the sovereign presides. Raising it in witnesses' view ends every rumor's subtlety: the dark has a monarch, and now they know its face.
[Shadow Magic: 18]

Undead Legion.name: Undead Legion
Undead Legion.description:
Mass necromancy with a supply sergeant's philosophy: multiple corpses raised simultaneously: an instant squad of skeleton soldiers standing up in ragged unison. Quantity over quality, but when you raise ten skeletons at once, quality becomes academic. The legion requires corpses in inventory (battlefields provide; gardens do not), the squad fights with a skeleton's honest limitations multiplied into genuine tactics, sustaining many draws steadily on the necromancer, and the visual of a graveyard standing up has ended more sieges than the skeletons themselves.
[Dark Magic: 84]

Vanishing Act.name: Vanishing Act
Vanishing Act.description:
A bow, a flourish, a burst of stage-smoke, and the thief is simply somewhere else, up to twenty feet away, usually behind the person who was aiming at them. The theatrics are not vanity; the misdirection is what breaks the targeting. It works best on eyes that were watching closely, which is why it must be earned fresh each time: an audience shown the same trick twice starts watching the smoke instead of the bow.
[Deception: 1]

Ward Inscribe.name: Ward Inscribe
Ward Inscribe.description:
Inscribe a protective ward onto a surface, door, shield, armor, or floor, that triggers when a specific condition is met. The ward can repel enemies, block spells, sound an alarm, or turn the inscribed surface into a barrier that holds for minutes. The ward lasts until triggered or the ink fades at dawn.
[Inscription: 9]

Wardrobe Swap.name: Wardrobe Swap
Wardrobe Swap.description:
Instantly change into a prepared outfit, gaining a social advantage appropriate to the occasion: armor for a duel, formalwear for a gala, or something devastating for a confession. Appearance is power in Luxcellia, and you never waste a moment.
[Fashion Styling: 2]

Weakness Scan.name: Weakness Scan
Weakness Scan.description:
Analyze a target with supernatural precision, revealing weak points, vulnerabilities, and the optimal attack vector. After scanning, your next attack against that target gains bonus damage and ignores a portion of their defenses. The War God sees every crack in every wall.
[Insight: 3]

requirements.variable: Blessing of the War God's Eye

Abyssal Deluge.name: Abyssal Deluge
Abyssal Deluge.description:
The ultimate water spell. Open the heavens and drown the battlefield in an apocalyptic flood. A vertical column of water descends from above with the force of the open ocean, crushing enemies beneath thousands of tons of conjured seawater.
[Water Magic: 24]

Aerial Evasion.name: Aerial Evasion
Aerial Evasion.description:
The legs answer before the mind finishes asking: an explosive launch out of danger, the attack closing on empty air while the dragoon is already above it, reading the fight from altitude. Escape as reflex, altitude as answer. The evasion buys one clean exit per spring (the legs deliver what training banked), it transitions directly into a Jump Strike on landing (the school's signature cruelty: the dodge is the windup) and dragoons who evade upward indoors contribute to the profession's ceiling-repair fund.
[acrobatics: 3]

Alpha Presence.name: Alpha Presence
Alpha Presence.description:
Project an aura of absolute predatory authority that causes lesser creatures to submit and even sapient enemies to feel the primal urge to kneel. Monsters hesitate. Beastkin acknowledge your dominance. The weak-willed simply obey. You carry the weight of an apex predator's gaze.
[intimidation: 5]

Amorphous Body.name: Amorphous Body
Amorphous Body.description: The Slime-Born exhales and lets their edges go soft: flesh shifts toward translucent gel, blades pass through with a wet, unsatisfying sound, and gaps under doors become doorways. Blunt trauma still ripples through unpleasantly, and holding the softened state takes focus: mind wandering, body firming. Reforming crisp edges afterward takes a moment of concentration, and anything worn or carried remains stubbornly solid the whole time.

Appraise Value.name: Appraise Value
Appraise Value.description:
One look, and the item confesses its finances: true value, rarity, demand, and the profitable layer: the forgery's tells, the seller's desperation, the exact number that makes everyone wince in the right direction. It prices the market, not the meaning; a mother's locket appraises at silver-weight. A merchant who already knows the player appraises opens closer to honest; the reading itself is silent, and a deal struck stands.
[Merchant Trade: 2]

Blood Dominion.name: Blood Dominion
Blood Dominion.description:
The mage stops attacking the body and administers it: absolute control over the blood inside a single target: paralysis by decree, limbs moved against their owner's screaming preference, or the vital current simply instructed to boil. Total dominion over life itself, exercised retail. The dominion claims one target and costs the mage a war of concentration against a resisting will (strong hearts fight for their own blood, and win ground), its use is unmistakable and unforgivable in every witness's memory, and the Church's file on blood dominion has no thin entries.
[Blood Magic: 37]

Bulwark Charge.name: Bulwark Charge
Bulwark Charge.description:
The shield goes up and the saint becomes traffic: a full charge that bowls through the enemy line, bodies knocked aside with impact damage and the deep moral injury of being run over by someone defensive. Formations open like curtains. The charge needs a running start and a straight conviction (it does not corner) and whatever stands at the end of the line receives the accumulated opinion of every step, which is the entire point.
[Shield Combat: 4]

Celestial Bolt.name: Celestial Bolt
Celestial Bolt.description:
A thin beam of starlight falls from nowhere at all (through the ceiling, through the smoke, through the raised shield) and lands exactly where the astrologer is looking. Cover means nothing to something that has already traveled forever. Undead and demons burn under it like paper under a lens. The stars are precise but not hurried: each bolt must be sighted with care, and the sky considers each request before granting the next.
[Star Magic: 2]

Combat Cuisine.name: Combat Cuisine
Combat Cuisine.description:
Prepare a quick fortifying meal mid-battle using whatever ingredients are available: monster meat, dungeon mushrooms, herbs from your pack. The dish grants temporary combat enhancements and the morale boost of hot food in a desperate moment.
[Battle Cooking: 3]

Counter Stance.name: Counter Stance
Counter Stance.description:
The low stance, sword angled behind: an invitation written in posture. The next incoming attack is deflected and answered in the same motion: an immediate counter-slash through the opening the enemy generously created by attacking at all. The stance converts one committed attack per adoption (cautious enemies who refuse to swing starve it, which is a duel of patience the stance is built to win), and its readable invitation is genuine bait: veterans recognize the posture, and attack anyway, and are counted upon to.
[Swordsmanship: 3]

Dawn's Embrace.name: Dawn's Embrace
Dawn's Embrace.description:
Bathe an entire area in healing dawn light. Every ally within the radiance is healed simultaneously: wounds close, poisons neutralize, diseases purge, exhaustion lifts. The light is warm, golden, and feels like being held by someone who loves you unconditionally. Even allies who were on death's edge are pulled back. The cost to you is proportional to how many you save.
[Light Magic: 18]

Devour Mastery.name: Devour Mastery
Devour Mastery.description: Every defeated or deeply studied opponent becomes a textbook: one of their signature techniques starts making sense, mastery accumulating in days that should take seasons. The predator's education is other people's life work. It demands genuine victory or genuine study, glancing blows teach nothing, and masters whose techniques start appearing in the bearer's hands tend to take that very, very personally.

Dread Presence.name: Dread Presence
Dread Presence.description:
The temperature of the room drops by a story: the Dullahan heritage surfaces, and everyone present remembers, all at once, that death is a person who keeps appointments. Weak enemies break and run. Strong ones stand their ground with shaking hands and slipping aim. The dread is honest supernatural weight, not theater; it spends itself in the unleashing, needs time to pool again, and the truly fearless (and the truly stupid) walk through it untouched.
[intimidation: 1]

Elaborate Trap.name: Elaborate Trap
Elaborate Trap.description:
Quickly set up a hidden trap using available materials and a generous application of creative thinking. The trap can be a tripwire, a snare, a rigged object, a collapsing floor section, or anything else the environment supports. Enemies who trigger it suffer damage, immobilization, or a humiliating combination of both. The best traps are the ones the enemy walks into while feeling clever.
[Stealth: 3]

Eldritch Chain.name: Eldritch Chain
Eldritch Chain.description:
Conjure spectral chains from a pact sigil that bind a target's limbs. The chains tighten when the target struggles and deal dark damage over time. Breaking free requires significant strength or magical dispelling.
[Flexible Weapons: 3]

Elemental Aura.name: Elemental Aura
Elemental Aura.description:
The attuned element rises and orbits: a whirlwind of fire, frost, stone-shard, or lightning wrapping the caster in weather with loyalty: nearby enemies pay for proximity, and projectiles get batted from the air like opinions nobody asked for. Walking arsenal, walking wall. The aura matches the caster's attunement (variety is a different mage's problem), holds for a sustained burn of mana and focus, and makes stealth a fond, funny memory.
[Elemental Magic: 6]

Elemental Body.name: Elemental Body
Elemental Body.description:
The mage stops wearing a body and wears an element: living flame, flowing water, howling wind, or walking stone: physical attacks passing through, the mage's touch carrying the element's damage. Immunity to the physical is paid in the element's own vulnerabilities: flame meets water; stone meets patience. Returning to flesh is always described the same way: heavier, slower, and strangely like an apology.
[Elemental Magic: 22]

Enchant Weapon.name: Enchant Weapon
Enchant Weapon.description:
The enchanter primes their own weapon, or an ally's (never a foe's), with one held breath of element: fire, ice, or lightning by attunement, stored silent in the steel until the next hit releases it, and the effect is dramatic, a strike that lands twice in two languages. One blow, footnoted. The enchantment spends itself on the next hit entirely (a whiff wastes nothing; the charge waits for contact), priming takes a calm beat per weapon, and fighters who feel the stored element humming in their grip describe it as carrying a lit match politely.
[Enchanting: 3]

Familiar's Aid.name: Familiar's Aid
Familiar's Aid.description:
The witch murmurs and the familiar is already moving: scouting the ridge, carrying a minor spell in its mouth like a retrieved stick, fetching the crucial item from the unreachable shelf. Loyal, unnaturally clever, and smug about both. It keeps score of errands in a currency of treats, warmth, and being told it did well. It did.
[Nature Magic: 3]

Flawless Craft.name: Flawless Craft
Flawless Craft.description: The crafter clears the bench, breathes, and commits everything to one attempt: extraordinary focus poured into a single working: the odds of an exceptional or masterwork result climbing dramatically as hands, judgment, and intent align for one sustained act of care. Excellence, on purpose. The focus can be summoned once per crafting session (that total commitment is precisely what makes it unrepeatable: a second attempt would be technique without the fire), and crafters describe the state afterward the same way: emptied, satisfied, and unfit for anything but tea.

Gem Extraction.name: Gem Extraction
Gem Extraction.description:
Carefully extract a gem from its surrounding rock without cracking, scratching, or destabilizing the deposit. The gem retains maximum clarity and value, where a careless miner would produce a handful of expensive gravel.
[Mining: 3]

Graviton Crush.name: Graviton Crush
Graviton Crush.description:
Generate a localized gravity well that crushes everything within its radius under immense gravitational pressure. Enemies are pinned to the ground, projectiles are pulled off course, and the ground itself cracks under the strain. The well collapses after several seconds with a thunderous implosion.
[Gravity Magic: 5]

Ground Breaker.name: Ground Breaker
Ground Breaker.description:
The enchanted weapon comes down on the earth like a verdict: a line of magical energy erupting forward through the ground: fire splitting stone or frost heaving it in glittering plates. Ranged devastation, delivered by geology. Swinging that hard at the floor announces the dungeon breaker to every level above and below.
[Dungeon Surveying: 6]

Guardian Angel.name: Guardian Angel
Guardian Angel.description:
The priest speaks an ally's name upward and something listens: a brief manifestation of divine protection taking station above them, and when the lethal blow comes, the guardian takes it, heals the target in the same radiant instant, and dissipates, duty complete. One miracle, one save. The angel guards against exactly one death and cannot be stockpiled (grace attends emergencies, not inventories), the summons spends deep divinity on faith that the blow is coming, and allies who feel it catch what should have killed them fight the rest of the day differently.
[Divinity: 41]

Identify Relic.name: Identify Relic
Identify Relic.description:
Examine a mysterious object and determine its properties, origin, and potential dangers. You can identify a relic's era, assess its magical potency, and estimate what it might do before you accidentally activate it.
[Relic Appraisal: 2]

Legendary Shot.name: Legendary Shot
Legendary Shot.description:
The ultimate Ranger technique. One perfect arrow, charged with everything you have: mana, skill, intent, and the wind itself. It curves around obstacles, punches through barriers, and hits with the force of a ballista bolt. One arrow. One kill. No exceptions.
[Archery: 50]

Light of Truth.name: Light of Truth
Light of Truth.description:
Bathe an area in revealing light that strips away all illusions, invisibility, and magical disguises. Hidden enemies are exposed, shapeshifters revert, and lies become physically uncomfortable to speak.
[Light Magic: 22]

Liquid Courage.name: Liquid Courage
Liquid Courage.description:
Serve a drink that fills an ally with warmth, courage, and the conviction that things are going to be fine. Fear effects are suppressed, morale is restored, and the next fight feels winnable. The hangover is tomorrow's problem.
[Brewing: 3]

Lucky Disguise.name: Lucky Disguise
Lucky Disguise.description: A leaf on the head, a shimmer of trickster magic, and the Tanuki-Blooded is somebody harmless: a forgettable merchant, a dozing pilgrim, whoever the scene most conveniently needed. Eyes slide past; memories stay vague. The disguise is luck and suggestion, not true transformation (close scrutiny, true-sight, and dogs are all rude about it) and each borrowed face must be given back to the shrine's luck before another can be worn.

Magnetic Pulse.name: Magnetic Pulse
Magnetic Pulse.description:
Electromagnetism, weaponized with a sense of humor: a pulse that rips metal weapons from enemy hands, drags armored targets stumbling toward the caster, or repels them violently the other way. Knights in full plate become projectiles: the technique's documentation says this, approvingly. The pulse works metal and only metal (the unarmored and the wooden-armed shrug; the fully-plated orbit), each emission spends a serious charge, and veteran enemies facing lightning-mages develop the discipline's intended paranoia: leather straps, and lots of them.
[Lightning Magic: 16]

Mana Construct.name: Mana Construct
Mana Construct.description:
Raw mana, shaped by intention: barriers, platforms, weapons, tools: assembled at thought-speed, limited only by reserves and imagination, a phrase students learn is mostly a warning about imagination. Complexity costs more than size: a glowing wall is cheap; a working lock is a thesis. Veterans are identified by the bridge already forming before anyone asked.
[Arcane Magic: 2]

Mana Severance.name: Mana Severance
Mana Severance.description:
Cut an enemy's connection to their mana supply entirely. Their spells collapse. Their enchantments fail. Their magical defenses evaporate. For a devastating window, they are rendered completely mundane in a world that runs on magic. The severed mana bleeds visibly from them like luminous smoke, and the silence where their power used to be is deafening.
[Arcane Magic: 15]

Master Reforge.name: Master Reforge
Master Reforge.description:
Permanently upgrade a weapon or piece of armor during downtime, improving its quality by one tier. The reforged item retains its enchantments and gains enhanced durability. This is the craft that separates a smith from a legend.
[Blacksmithing: 5]

Mirror Enchant.name: Mirror Enchant
Mirror Enchant.description:
The enchanter links two fates with opposite terms: one enchantment on an ally, its mirror on an enemy: damage taken by the ally partially reflected into the linked foe, every blow against the protected arriving as an invoice to the marked. What goes around comes around, with routing. The mirror binds one pair for its duration (choosing the enemy half is the tactics: link the archer's target, punish the archer's enthusiasm), the reflection is partial rather than total, and enemies who realize they are hurting themselves undergo combat's most satisfying hesitation.
[Enchanting: 20]

Moonlit Remedy.name: Moonlit Remedy
Moonlit Remedy.description: The Moon Rabbit's gentle pharmacy: a lunar remedy channeled soft and silver: minor health restored, panic calmed, poison eased, the whole kit of small mercies in one moonlit touch. Crises want the priest; the long road wants this. Recipients report the true effect beneath the mechanical one: for a moment, everything felt survivable, which turned out to be what they needed.

Nature's Grasp.name: Nature's Grasp
Nature's Grasp.description:
The caster's fingers curl, and the ground remembers it is alive: roots burst upward and lace around the target's legs, cinching tight with the slow certainty of a forest claiming a fence post. Bound targets can fight, but they fight planted. The grasp needs living earth beneath it, stone floors and salted ground stay silent, and torn roots take a few breaths to regrow their patience.
[Nature Magic: 1]

Object Barrage.name: Object Barrage
Object Barrage.description:
Threads snap taut across the battlefield and the room itself attacks: dropped weapons, loose stone, a table, somebody's unattended lunch: all of it airborne at once in a coordinated barrage from six directions. Cluttered spaces become armories. The barrage needs objects to throw (bare arenas offer nothing) and a puppeteer's full attention to conduct, and after the performance the threads must be gathered and rewound before the room can fly again.
[Artifice: 56]

Patron's Favor.name: Patron's Favor
Patron's Favor.description:
Invoke your patron demon's direct attention. For a brief duration, your dark magic costs no mana, your curses apply instantly, and a faint demonic silhouette looms behind you. The patron is watching. Make it entertaining.
[Occult Lore: 49]

Peerless Blade.name: Peerless Blade
Peerless Blade.description:
The ultimate Duelist technique. Your swordsmanship reaches a level where every movement is optimal, every strike is a masterpiece, and no opponent can match your blade. For the duration, you cannot miss, every attack is a critical hit, and your parry is absolute. The Academy calls this theoretical perfection. You call it Tuesday.
[Dueling: 18]

Phantom Strike.name: Phantom Strike
Phantom Strike.description:
The ultimate Assassin technique. Move so fast you become genuinely invisible; not hidden, but moving between moments. You strike multiple enemies in what appears to be a single instant. When you stop, the cuts appear all at once. No one saw you move. No one ever will.
[Stealth: 78]

Phantom Weapon.name: Phantom Weapon
Phantom Weapon.description:
The weapon stops committing to a element: transformed into a shifting construct of pure elemental force, cycling with each strike: fire, then frost, then storm, every hit a different magical language. Resistances become a guessing game the defender loses by definition. The phantom form holds for its duration on a serious elemental draw, the cycling is sequential rather than chosen (masters learn to count, timing the right element to the right moment), and blades that change color mid-combo are remembered by everyone who survives the rainbow.
[Elemental Magic: 27]

Line-Breaker Round.name: Line-Breaker Round
Line-Breaker Round.description:
The shot declines to stop: through the first target, still lethal into the second, discourteous to a third if they insisted on lining up. Overpenetration is a feature, not a bug, and enemy formations are a menu. The round wants targets in a line and loses conviction with each body it educates, and firing it into a melee containing friends is the fastest way a marksman ever lost their dinner invitations.
[Firearms: 4]

Pressure Crush.name: Pressure Crush
Pressure Crush.description:
The target is encased in a sphere of water given one instruction: compress. Hydraulic pressure from all sides: armor cracking, barriers shattering, the ocean floor's opinion delivered at street level. Survivors describe the horror precisely: there was nothing to fight. It was everywhere, and it was patient.
[Water Magic: 6]

Pressure Point.name: Pressure Point
Pressure Point.description:
Two fingers, one address: a strike to a specific pressure point delivering the monk's choice of consequences: paralysis, numbness, blooming pain, or mana flow disrupted mid-channel. Anatomy as a control panel. The point demands anatomical knowledge and precision timing both (the technique is a library, not a punch), unfamiliar physiologies must be read before they can be pressed (the first strike on a new monster species is always a hypothesis) and casters who feel their mana stutter under a fingertip develop lifelong opinions about letting monks close.
[acrobatics: 20]

Reckless Swing.name: Reckless Swing
Reckless Swing.description:
Everything the berserker has, spent in one arc: no guard, no plan, no tomorrow: just a swing with the whole body's conviction behind it and a sound like a gate coming off its hinges. The damage is tremendous. The opening left behind is also tremendous; anyone still standing gets a free and generous reply. Worth it, the berserker will insist, from the ground if necessary.
[Heavy Weapons: 1]

Runic Fortress.name: Runic Fortress
Runic Fortress.description:
The rune knight's masterwork in coverage: an area laced with interconnected runes, traps waiting, wards standing, blessings humming for allies, hexes coiled for intruders, a matrix of simultaneous magical effects operating like a garrison written in script. Territory, annotated into a weapon. The fortress claims the inscribed area and takes real time to lay (this is preparation's triumph, not improvisation's), the matrix runs until its runes are found and broken one by one, and enemies who enter uninformed provide the fortress's favorite kind of demonstration.
[Rune Carving: 48]

Runic Overload.name: Runic Overload
Runic Overload.description:
The rune knight carves greedily: multiple runes inscribed simultaneously: fire, ice, and lightning converging through runic fusion into a single devastating release, three grammars shouting one word. The overload spends every carved rune at once in a strike that argues in three elements, fusion demands flawless simultaneous inscription (a botched rune in the chord sours the whole release), and the technique's name is honest: pushing that much through one blade at once leaves the runes scorched and the knight's arms humming for a long beat.
[Rune Carving: 22]

Sacred Barrier.name: Sacred Barrier
Sacred Barrier.description:
Summon a massive barrier of consecrated light across the battlefield. It mends allies who pass through it, sears enemies who touch it, and only legendary magic can hope to dispel it. It blooms like golden wings unfurling: divine intervention given visible, beautiful, terrifyingly powerful form. It guards your allies on the turn you raise it; sustaining it takes your action again each turn.
[Light Magic: 15]

Serpent's Gaze.name: Serpent's Gaze
Serpent's Gaze.description:
The Lamia-Blooded catches a target's eyes and holds them: pupils narrowing to slits, the world going slow and warm and agreeable for the one caught looking. Movements drag; suggestions start sounding like their own good ideas. The gaze is a thread, not a chain: any real pain snaps it instantly, it needs willing (or careless) eye contact to begin, and minds that have been caught once flinch away from a second helping.
[Charm: 1]

Shadow Bargain.name: Shadow Bargain
Shadow Bargain.description:
Offer your shadow as temporary collateral to your patron in exchange for a burst of overwhelming dark power. Your next three spells are massively enhanced, but you cast no shadow until the bargain completes.
[Occult Lore: 13]

Shadow Command.name: Shadow Command
Shadow Command.description:
