Blood Crown Manifestation.name: Blood Crown Manifestation
Blood Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign blood settles and the crimson acquires vows: wounds sealed like promises kept, targets marked in a register that does not smudge, crimson weapons shaped with a signature's exactness. Blood, notarized. The crowned carry the tell: they always know, without looking, exactly who in the room is bleeding.
[Blood Magic: 5]

Charm Crown Manifestation.name: Charm Crown Manifestation
Charm Crown Manifestation.description:
Manifest a crown of sovereign charm. Charm spells gain emotional clarity, strengthening morale, calming panic, shaping glamour, drawing attention, and exposing contradictions without overriding free will.
[Charm Magic: 5]

Dream Crown Manifestation.name: Dream Crown Manifestation
Dream Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign dream settles and the subconscious acquires an interpreter: nightmares soothed by being correctly read, dream-mist constructs shaped from meaning rather than matter, rest induced like a gift, ritual dream paths opened to places no map admits exist. Sleep, curated. The crowned carry the blessing's tell: people near them remember their dreams, all of them, kindly.
[Dream Magic: 5]

Earth Crown Manifestation.name: Earth Crown Manifestation
Earth Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign earth settles and stone acquires draftsmanship: walls raised plumb and true, ramps and pillars placed like arguments, anchors that hold what must hold. Engineering, at gesture speed. The crowned develop the quiet tell: the ground is always, subtly, more convenient wherever they happen to be standing.
[Earth Magic: 5]

Illusion Miracle Dominion.name: Illusion Miracle Dominion
Illusion Miracle Dominion.description:
Mirage at sovereign scale: enemies spending their finest attacks on false armies that die convincingly, allied movement hidden so completely the dust forgets to rise, a boss phase converted into a theater of wrong assumptions. Reality's understudy, given the lead. One great staging per miracle. Enemies who learn they fought scenery doubt every battlefield forever after.
[Illusion Magic: 15]

Last Stand of the Retired.name: Last Stand of the Retired
Last Stand of the Retired.description:
Draw a hidden weapon and fight with the lethal precision of someone who used to be much more than they appear. Combat instincts are rusty but the muscle memory is intact. When the decision to fight is made, the professional exterior disappears and something older, sharper, and far more dangerous takes its place. Everyone who witnesses it understands what this person used to be.
[survival: 27]

Light Crown Manifestation.name: Light Crown Manifestation
Light Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign light settles and radiance gains its administration: hidden threats revealed as a standing courtesy, corruption purified on contact, the cursed and the undead burned with jurisdictional confidence, and beneath it, allied resolve quietly strengthening, because light with a sovereign is light with a plan. The crowned do not enter rooms unannounced ever again.
[Light Magic: 5]

Route Optimization Thread.name: Route Optimization Thread
Route Optimization Thread.description: A faint golden thread only the bearer sees unspools toward the chosen goal: the safe way, the fast way, the rich way, or the dramatic way, depending on what was asked. Patrols are avoided before they are heard; shortcuts exist that maps deny. The thread answers one objective at a time and shows a route, not a guarantee: it cannot see choices other people have not made yet, and companions eventually notice that this party never, ever gets lost, which is its own kind of tell.

Sound Crown Manifestation.name: Sound Crown Manifestation
Sound Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign sound settles and acoustics acquire a conductor: sonic impacts placed like drumbeats, silence fields dropped over enemy casters like velvet, echo mapping that reads architecture aloud, morale rhythms allies march to without noticing. The crowned are never, ever surprised by footsteps: a fact that unsettles everyone who tries.
[Sound Magic: 5]

Space Crown Manifestation.name: Space Crown Manifestation
Space Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign space settles and geometry acquires a manager: short gates opened like doors that were always there, movement folded to skip the boring middle, pocket storage that balances its books. Distance, administered. The crowned develop the tell: they are never quite where you watched them stand.
[Space Magic: 5]

Storm Crown Manifestation.name: Storm Crown Manifestation
Storm Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign storm settles and the weather acknowledges its sovereign: rain, pressure, thunderclap timing, windshear, and at the crown's height, battlefield-scale atmospheric rhythm, the tempo of the entire fight conducted from above. The crowned are announced by their own thunder, which they pretend to find inconvenient.
[Storm Magic: 5]

Water Crown Manifestation.name: Water Crown Manifestation
Water Crown Manifestation.description:
Manifest a crown of sovereign water. Water spells gain extreme fluid precision, allowing pressure currents, cleansing streams, impact-cushioning veils, binding ribbons, and mirrorlike sensing ripples.
[Water Magic: 5]

All-Element Sovereign Mode.name: All-Element Sovereign Mode
All-Element Sovereign Mode.description: Every affinity at once, in perfect balance: fire braided with frost, stone lifted on wind, light and shadow cast from the same hand: hybrid spells that textbooks call impossible written casually in the air. It is what mastery looks like from the far side. The mode demands sovereign-level concentration to keep eight elements from arguing, and the sight of it ends the bearer's anonymity in any room containing a single trained mage.

Contract Loophole Override.name: Contract Loophole Override
Contract Loophole Override.description: Every unfair bargain has one thread loose, and the bearer's fingers find it: the clause with two readings, the oath's unstated assumption, the rule that binds the letter and frees the spirit. Escape arrives dressed as compliance. The override needs an actual flaw to exploit, an airtight bargain stays airtight, and beings who trade in binding words treat a known loophole-walker as either a treasure to recruit or a problem to make airtight examples of.

Convenient Miracle Trigger.name: Convenient Miracle Trigger
Convenient Miracle Trigger.description: At the exact peak of the drama, the world blinks: the rope holds, the guard is called away, the old friend happens to be in this exact town, the rain starts precisely when a fire needed drowning. One coincidence, wildly convenient, entirely genre-appropriate. The trigger answers maximum drama only (it ignores mundane wishes entirely) and each miracle is the sort of story people retell until someone starts keeping a list.

Lightning Miracle Dominion.name: Lightning Miracle Dominion
Lightning Miracle Dominion.description:
The judgment miracle: divine bolts chained through chosen targets (chosen being the operative sovereignty), a battlefield stunned into one decisive opening, or a single boss struck with authority that reads less like damage and more like sentencing. One great working per miracle. Lightning that chooses is lightning with a monarch, and battlefields it has judged smell of ozone and reconsideration for days.
[Lightning Magic: 15]

Nature Crown Manifestation.name: Nature Crown Manifestation
Nature Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign nature settles and the green acquires precision: roots that grip like decisions, vines placed like punctuation, thorns with addresses, spirit-green sanctuaries growing around allies like the forest taking a personal interest. Growth, curated. The crowned are followed everywhere by the tell: things bloom near them, out of season, on purpose.
[Nature Magic: 5]

Poison Crown Manifestation.name: Poison Crown Manifestation
Poison Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign poison settles and toxicity acquires a pharmacist: venom shaped to purpose, antidotes refined at bedside speed, miasma veils with guest lists, exposure lines drawn so allies walk through gardens the enemy experiences as minefields. Toxicity, prescribed. The crowned taste everything first, always, and are never once wrong.
[Poison Magic: 5]

Shadow Crown Manifestation.name: Shadow Crown Manifestation
Shadow Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign shadow settles and the dark acquires discretion: allies concealed with tailored dimness, shadow decoys standing convincing watch, silhouette binds holding enemies by their own outlines, short slips through dim space like stepping through a curtain. Darkness, at a whisper. The crowned's shadow occasionally moves a half-beat early, and pretends it didn't.
[Shadow Magic: 5]

True Dragon Transformation.name: True Dragon Transformation
True Dragon Transformation.description:
Not the hybrid. The dragon: full transformation into flight, breath weapon, and physical power at the scale where architecture becomes a tactical consideration. Brief, exhausting, and utterly devastating; the vein's deepest inheritance, spent whole. The true form holds for a handful of glorious moments before the human frame reclaims itself shaking and hollowed (the exhaustion afterward is a certainty allies plan around), and there is no hiding the witnesses: everyone within a mile now has the same story, and it is true.
[Fire Magic: 39]

Assassin's Cloak of Shadows.name: Assassin's Cloak of Shadows
Assassin's Cloak of Shadows.description:
Living shadow settles over the assassin like a second profession: harder to detect, harder to hit, and (the cloak's premium feature) immune to tracking magic entirely, presence muffled from every sense, magical and mundane alike. Scrying returns static; hounds return confused. The cloak conceals while it lasts (it dims the wearer rather than deleting them: sharp eyes at close range still argue), and its true product is strategic: an assassin who cannot be tracked must be predicted, and predicting assassins is a famously brief career.
[Stealth: 25]

Crystal Crown Manifestation.name: Crystal Crown Manifestation
Crystal Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign crystal settles and the facets acquire intent: crystal spells gaining cut precision: prism shields angled to scatter exactly what threatens, crystal cages grown to measure, refracting planes placed like arguments, resonance lattices that hum warnings, and mana-storing gem structures banking power against later need. Geometry, gem-grade. The crown elevates the wearer's crystal magic while manifested, sustaining worn lattice is constant faceting work, and the crowned glitter faintly at all times: subtlety, the blessing concedes, was never on offer.
[Crystal Magic: 5]

Gravity Crown Manifestation.name: Gravity Crown Manifestation
Gravity Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign gravity settles and weight acquires a throne: enemies pinned under localized emphasis, allies lightened for leaps their knees will deny later, strikes landing heavy as verdicts, stones taken into obedient orbit. Down, curated. The crowned develop the blessing's tell: nothing they carry ever looks heavy, and everything they dislike does.
[Gravity Magic: 5]

Universal Translation Field.name: Universal Translation Field
Universal Translation Field.description: Every voice arrives in meaning: spoken tongues, dead scripts, monster-speech, coded guild slang, the layered dialects of magical inscription: all of it, understood and answerable. Language stops being a wall anywhere in the world. The field carries words, not intent: lies translate perfectly, and sarcasm survives the journey intact. Scholars would kill for it, spymasters have probably considered it, and the Omniglot learns quickly to pretend confusion strategically.

Illusion Crown Manifestation.name: Illusion Crown Manifestation
Illusion Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign illusion settles and the lies acquire craftsmanship: doubles with correct shadows, false terrain that survives a second look, aim distortions of a hand's width that decide duels, scene-level misdirection that reorganizes what a battlefield believes about itself. Deception, at production quality. Nobody who knows the crowned ever fully trusts a hallway again.
[Illusion Magic: 5]

Lightning Crown Manifestation.name: Lightning Crown Manifestation
Lightning Crown Manifestation.description:
The crown of sovereign lightning settles and the voltage acquires manners: flash-step bursts that end arguments mid-syllable, nerve stuns placed like acupuncture, chain arcs that choose their circuit, reflexes sharpened to storm-speed. Precision, at the speed of light's rude cousin. The crowned acquire the signature tell: hair with sovereign opinions.
[Lightning Magic: 5]

Miracle Restoration.name: Miracle Restoration
Miracle Restoration.description: Channel an overwhelming surge of sacred energy through your hands into a wounded target, mending injuries that conventional healing cannot touch: severed tendons reknit, shattered bones fuse, and cursed wounds unravel as raw vitality floods the affected area. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next healing action and can reverse conditions normally considered permanent.

Death's Door Reversal.name: Death's Door Reversal
Death's Door Reversal.description: When an ally has fallen to the threshold of death, pour your entire healing focus into a single desperate restoration that drags them back from the edge: the technique stabilizes lethal damage, purges death-state debuffs, and restores enough vitality to return the target to combat readiness. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next emergency healing action on a critically wounded or dying target.

Sovereign Summon.name: Sovereign Summon
Sovereign Summon.description: Reach across dimensional boundaries and call forth an entity of extraordinary power; not a bound servant but a willing ally drawn by the authority of your summoning presence. The entity manifests fully formed, combat-ready, in your party from the moment it arrives, and acting with independent intelligence far beyond what normal summoning produces. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next summoning action and bypasses normal restrictions on summon tier.

Bond Beyond Worlds.name: Bond Beyond Worlds
Bond Beyond Worlds.description: Strengthen the link between yourself and an already-summoned entity, reinforcing its presence in the material world and amplifying its combat parameters through shared resonance. The bonded entity fights harder, lasts longer, and can execute coordinated attacks as though it shares your tactical awareness. Massively increases the effectiveness of your summoned entity's next action and extends its duration.

Taboo Skill Unlock.name: Taboo Skill Unlock
Taboo Skill Unlock.description: Your soul resonates with forbidden knowledge, allowing you to instinctively access sealed or banned magical techniques that your conscious mind has never studied. The unlocked technique integrates with your existing abilities and can be combined with conventional magic in ways that make magical theorists deeply uncomfortable. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next action using forbidden, sealed, or restricted magic.

Sealed Knowledge Resonance.name: Sealed Knowledge Resonance
Sealed Knowledge Resonance.description: Extend your forbidden affinity outward to sense and unravel magical seals, wards, and restrictions in your vicinity: locked grimoires open, sealed doors crack, and protective enchantments waver as your presence disrupts whatever authority originally bound them. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next action to dispel, bypass, or break a magical seal or ward.

Evolutionary Bond.name: Evolutionary Bond
Evolutionary Bond.description: Forge a deep connection with a bonded creature that accelerates its natural growth, triggering permanent evolutionary advancement far beyond what the species normally achieves. The bonded creature gains enhanced combat capability, increased intelligence, and may develop abilities unique to your shared bond. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next beast-bonding or creature-command action and can trigger permanent evolution in bonded creatures.

Shadow Multiplier.name: Shadow Multiplier
Shadow Multiplier.description: Activate your hidden stat set while concealed in darkness or stealth, multiplying your combat parameters to levels that turn a competent fighter into a lethal ambush predator. Movement speed, strike power, and reaction time all surge beyond their normal ceilings for the duration of the concealed state. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next attack or combat action performed from stealth or darkness.

Ambush Supremacy.name: Ambush Supremacy
Ambush Supremacy.description: Execute a devastating opening strike from concealment that carries the full weight of your shadow-state multiplied parameters: the attack lands before the target registers your presence and carries secondary effects that prevent immediate counterattack. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next ambush or surprise attack and applies a brief stagger to the target.

Perfect Replay.name: Perfect Replay
Perfect Replay.description: Call on your body's archive of peak moments to reproduce a previously executed perfect technique with flawless fidelity: the same speed, the same angle, the same impossible timing that made it work the first time. The replayed technique carries the full effectiveness of the original moment regardless of your current condition. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next combat or physical action by reproducing a recorded peak performance.

Highlight Reel Override.name: Highlight Reel Override
Highlight Reel Override.description: Stack multiple recorded peak performances into a single impossible combination attack: a sequence of techniques from different fights, different moments, and different emotional states executed in rapid succession as one continuous action. The combined replay exceeds what any single performance could achieve. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next action by chaining multiple recorded peak techniques into one devastating sequence.

Immovable Stance.name: Immovable Stance
Immovable Stance.description: The cheat skill that argues with physics and wins: planted, the character becomes conceptually absolute: knockback fails, grapples bounce, displacement magic fizzles against a position that declined. The next defensive action lands massively stronger from the anchored base. Word of the one who cannot be moved travels to exactly the tacticians who plan around such things.

Absolute Guardian Line.name: Absolute Guardian Line
Absolute Guardian Line.description: Extend your immovable presence outward to create a defensive zone around nearby allies: anything standing behind your line benefits from your absolute defensive aura, making them harder to hit, harder to displace, and harder to target while you hold position. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next defensive action and extends damage reduction and displacement immunity to allies within your protective zone.

Anthem of the Unbreakable.name: Anthem of the Unbreakable
Anthem of the Unbreakable.description: Perform a battle anthem whose supernatural resonance amplifies the combat performance of every ally who hears it: morale surges, pain dulls, movements sharpen, and each listener fights beyond their usual limits as the music rewrites their emotional and physical state. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next support or bolstering action and applies enhanced combat bonuses to all allies within hearing range.

Requiem of Surrender.name: Requiem of Surrender
Requiem of Surrender.description: Perform a dirge that saps the will to fight from every enemy who hears it: conviction wavers, aggression drains, movements slow, and the emotional weight of the music makes continued resistance feel pointless. The effect is not mind control but an overwhelming emotional resonance that makes the case for surrender more compelling than the case for fighting. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next weakening or binding action against all enemies within hearing range.

Horizon Shot.name: Horizon Shot
Horizon Shot.description:
Loose an arrow imbued with divine intent that curves around obstacles, accelerates through wind resistance, and strikes a target at extreme range with supernatural accuracy: the arrow knows where it needs to go and adjusts course mid-flight. Greatly increases the effectiveness of your next ranged attack action and ignores cover, distance penalties, and line-of-sight requirements.
[Archery: 5]

Arrow Storm Sovereignty.name: Arrow Storm Sovereignty
Arrow Storm Sovereignty.description:
Fire a divine volley where each arrow independently seeks its own target across the battlefield: a single draw of the bow produces a storm of projectiles that find individual enemies with unerring precision, striking weak points and ignoring shields. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next ranged attack action against all visible targets in the area.
[Archery: 15]

Greater Summoning.name: Greater Summoning
Greater Summoning.description:
Call upon your covenant bond to summon a powerful spirit ally from beyond the material plane; not a bound servant but a willing companion who manifests with independent intelligence, full combat capability, and genuine loyalty. The spirit's strength reflects the depth of your bond rather than your raw magical power. Greatly increases the effectiveness of your next summoning action and produces a spirit ally of exceptional power and duration.
[Spirit Channeling: 5]

Soul Link Resonance.name: Soul Link Resonance
Soul Link Resonance.description:
Temporarily fuse your soul with a bonded spirit, merging its abilities with your own for a brief period of amplified power: your physical and magical capabilities surge as the spirit's essence reinforces your own, granting access to abilities neither of you could use alone. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next action by channeling a bonded spirit's power directly through your body.
[Spirit Channeling: 15]

Thousand Palms.name: Thousand Palms
Thousand Palms.description:
Execute a divine martial sequence that delivers dozens of precisely targeted strikes in the span of a heartbeat: each blow finds a pressure point, nerve cluster, or structural weakness with supernatural accuracy, and the cumulative damage far exceeds what the individual strikes should produce. Greatly increases the effectiveness of your next unarmed combat action and strikes all targets within melee range.
[Unarmed Combat: 5]

Flow State Transcendence.name: Flow State Transcendence
Flow State Transcendence.description:
Enter a state of perfect martial flow where your body moves faster than conscious thought: every attack, dodge, and counter happens with divine precision as muscle memory, combat instinct, and supernatural awareness merge into a single continuous motion. Massively increases the effectiveness of all combat actions for a short duration and allows perfect real-time adaptation to any fighting style.
[Unarmed Combat: 15]

Harmonic Resonance.name: Harmonic Resonance
Harmonic Resonance.description:
Sing a melody that resonates with the emotional truth of the moment, producing a supernatural effect that heals wounds, breaks minor enchantments, or bolsters allies depending on the emotional content of the song. The effect is not enchantment magic; it works through beauty and emotional authenticity rather than mana manipulation. Greatly increases the effectiveness of your next support, healing, or dispel action through musical performance.
[Sound Magic: 5]

Requiem of the Fallen.name: Requiem of the Fallen
Requiem of the Fallen.description:
Perform a requiem of such devastating emotional power that it reshapes the battlefield: enemies lose the will to fight, allies surge with renewed purpose, and the boundary between inspiration and devastation blurs into a single overwhelming emotional experience. Massively increases the effectiveness of your next action that affects morale, and simultaneously bolsters all allies and weakens all enemies within hearing range.
[Sound Magic: 15]

Shadow Extraction.name: Shadow Extraction
Shadow Extraction.description:
Call to the lingering battle-echo of a defeated monster, dungeon-born foe, or magically marked enemy and pull its shadow into service. A successful extraction creates a loyal shadow soldier shaped from residual mana and will, not flesh. Stronger targets resist, named enemies require story permission, and the first successful extraction should feel like the world just realized a king entered the room.
[Shadow Magic: 5 · Soul Magic: 3]

Shadow Soldier Legion.name: Shadow Soldier Legion
Shadow Soldier Legion.description:
Store loyal shadow soldiers inside your own shadow and summon them as a coordinated fighting force. The legion can guard allies, swarm enemies, scout dark passages, hold formations, and return to your shadow when dismissed or destroyed. Individual soldiers are weaker than they were in life, but discipline, numbers, and perfect loyalty make the army terrifying.
[Shadow Magic: 10 · Spirit Channeling: 8]

Monarch's Command.name: Monarch's Command
Monarch's Command.description:
Issue a sovereign order through your shadow army. Loyal shadows obey instantly, allies feel the pressure of your command steady their nerves, and lesser enemies hesitate as if their own shadows are waiting for permission to move. This does not override free will; it turns authority, fear, and battlefield discipline into raw tactical force.
[intimidation: 8 · Shadow Magic: 6]

Shadow Exchange.name: Shadow Exchange
Shadow Exchange.description:
Swap places with one of your marked shadows, a summoned shadow soldier, or a shadow you have personally anchored. The exchange can rescue an ally, reposition behind an enemy, escape a lethal strike, or turn any dark corner into a royal passage. Long distances, bright sanctified ground, and unstable Riftmaw space increase the strain.
[Shadow Magic: 12 · Space Magic: 5]

Ebon Throne Dominion.name: Ebon Throne Dominion
Ebon Throne Dominion.description:
Unfurl a battlefield domain where every shadow kneels toward you. Your shadow soldiers become sharper and harder to destroy, enemy movement is dragged by their own silhouettes, and defeated foes become easier to extract while the domain holds. The area feels like a throne room made of midnight: beautiful, quiet, and absolutely not democratic.
[Shadow Magic: 16 · Soul Magic: 12 · Spirit Channeling: 10]

Saintess's Grace.name: Saintess's Grace
Saintess's Grace.description:
The Saintess reaches out, and the divine reaches with her: one touch that closes wounds and burns away a lingering affliction in the same warmth: healing that arrives less like magic and more like being forgiven. Those touched report the same detail: for a heartbeat, they felt worth saving, which is half the cure.
[Divinity: 2]

Center Stage.name: Center Stage
Center Stage.description:
The Idol claims the spotlight and the spotlight claims the room: a radiant aura strengthening every ally who can see her, its power scaling with the audience: the more eyes on her, the brighter everyone burns. Hiding an Idol wastes the entire class; the front line is the venue. Looking at her powers her, and not looking at her is how you get hit by everyone she's empowering.
[performance: 2]

Warden's Hook.name: Warden's Hook
Warden's Hook.description:
The chain goes out, the enemy comes back: a hooked throw that bites into armor, cloth, or pride and drags the target to the Warden's feet: casters ripped from their backline, escapes converted into arrivals. The battlefield's leash, thrown. Enemies who feel the bite learn the class's first law: your position was a suggestion.
[Flexible Weapons: 2]

All In.name: All In
All In.description:
The Gambler's signature wager: a strike bet double-or-nothing: the coin flips, and the blow lands either devastatingly doubled or embarrassingly whiffed, no middle outcome permitted by house rules. The Gambler always knows the odds. The Gambler bets anyway. That's the class. When the Gambler flips the coin first and swings second, the odds were never fair.
[Deception: 2]

Wanderer's Draw.name: Wanderer's Draw
Wanderer's Draw.description:
Iaido with road dust on it: the Ronin's counter-draw, honed across a hundred roadside disagreements: the blade clearing its sheath in answer to an attack, cutting along the line the enemy's own commitment opened. No ceremony. Just the table, the cup, and suddenly the sword. Survivors describe the same detail: they never saw the draw. They saw the sheathing after, which was worse.
[Swordsmanship: 2]

Ofuda Seal.name: Ofuda Seal
Ofuda Seal.description:
The talisman leaves the Onmyoji's fingers already knowing its address: paper striking the target and sticking: spirits dampened, magic muffled, cursed limbs arguing with calligraphy and losing. Tearing it off is possible, painful, and considered extremely rude by everything watching. Enemies who fight Onmyoji develop the profession's intended flinch: from paper.
[Occult Lore: 3]

Winter's Grasp.name: Winter's Grasp
Winter's Grasp.description:
The cold reaches out and takes hold: frost climbing the target from the ground up: movement slowing, joints stiffening. Not an attack. A claim. Everything the Cryomancer fights ends up moving at the Cryomancer's preferred speed, which is to say, slower, and then not at all.
[Ice Magic: 2]

Oni Crush.name: Oni Crush
Oni Crush.description:
The overhead blow that folklore warned about: fist or kanabo brought down with oni-strength, the impact staggering the target. Doors have been used to demonstrate. Doors are no longer consulted. The wind-up is visible, dodgeable, and somehow lands anyway, and everything the Oni Brawler does next happens to someone still ringing.
[Unarmed Combat: 2]

Kagura Purification.name: Kagura Purification
Kagura Purification.description:
The sacred dance, performed under battlefield conditions: kagura steps tracing a ward into the air: corruption cleansed from allies within the circle, hostile spirits pushed to the perimeter, the ground briefly remembering it belongs to a shrine. Everything unclean caught inside the pattern receives the shrine's oldest message: not here.
[Divinity: 4]

Temple Gate Stance.name: Temple Gate Stance
Temple Gate Stance.description:
The Sohei plants the naginata and becomes doctrine: a defensive stance covering the ground a temple gate would: sweeping arcs that own the corridor, footwork that surrenders nothing. The naginata's reach makes the corridor a toll road; the Sohei sets the rate. Enemies who charge a held gate discover why the temples stopped worrying about the front door.
[Polearm Combat: 2]

Yokai Snare.name: Yokai Snare
Yokai Snare.description:
The hunter's wire, strung for things that don't respect walls: blessed cord, salt-line geometry, and grudge-lore placed exactly where the quarry's nature forces it to step: spirits caught mid-slip, shapeshifters held mid-shift. Folklore, load-bearing. Everything ever caught in one files the same complaint: that's cheating. It isn't. It's homework.
[survival: 2]

Fan Snap Riposte.name: Fan Snap Riposte
Fan Snap Riposte.description:
The fan closes, the argument opens: a deflection performed with the iron tessen's snap, turning the incoming strike aside in the same motion that delivers the answer. Violence at tea-ceremony precision. Opponents who hear the click have already been answered, and are merely waiting for their body to receive the news.
[Dueling: 2]

Thunderstep.name: Thunderstep
Thunderstep.description:
The flash before the sound: a lightning-charged step that closes distance faster than the warning can travel: the Storm Fist arriving palm-first, the thunder catching up a heartbeat later like punctuation. Enemies describe the sequence in the school's preferred order: hit first, then the flash, then the sound, then the falling.
[Unarmed Combat: 2]

Impeccable Service.name: Impeccable Service
Impeccable Service.description:
The Battle Maid's first duty, performed under fire: an ally shielded behind flawless positioning while an affliction is tidied off them like a stain from good linen, delivered with a small bow that somehow makes it more intimidating. Recipients report the strange dual comfort: safe, cared for, and absolutely certain they should not track mud.
[Dagger Fighting: 2]

Punchline.name: Punchline
Punchline.description:
The setup walks in wearing motley; the punchline arrives from wherever the audience wasn't looking. A taunt, a pratfall, a juggled something that holds attention exactly one beat too long, and the strike that lands while they're still deciding whether to laugh. Victims universally report the same final indignity: they saw the setup. They knew. It landed anyway. Ta-dah.
[performance: 2]

Lullaby Veil.name: Lullaby Veil
Lullaby Veil.description:
The Dreamweaver hums, and the battlefield gets heavy-lidded: drowsy dream-mist settling over enemies: limbs slowing, focus swimming. Not sleep. The suburbs of sleep. Strong wills wade through it scowling; the weak-willed begin negotiating with gravity. Its true cruelty is comfort: resisting felt, the entire time, like a terrible idea.
[Dream Magic: 4]

Boarding Action.name: Boarding Action
Boarding Action.description:
The Corsair's answer to distance: a hooked line thrown, a swing that ignores the terrain's opinion, an arrival blade-first into the enemy's comfortable formation. Rigging, rafters, and chandeliers all count as rigging if the Corsair believes hard enough. The fight is now happening at cutlass range, on the Corsair's deck, by definition.
[Swordsmanship: 2]

Quarry Lock.name: Quarry Lock
Quarry Lock.description:
The mark goes in the book and the book does not forget: one target locked as quarry: their trail brightening, their hiding places downgraded to delays. The Hunter's files open slowly and close permanently. Marked targets report the sensation with remarkable consistency: being late on a debt they don't remember taking.
[investigation: 3]

Parasol Guard.name: Parasol Guard
Parasol Guard.description:
The canopy opens and becomes doctrine: the bladed parasol angled as a buckler: arrows shed like rain, spells scattered off waxed silk that has no business being that effective. It defends the direction it faces, which is why Parasol Duelists never stop strolling in circles. Nothing is more quietly demoralizing than an opponent deflecting your best attack while appearing to check the weather.
[Dueling: 2]

Trigger Parry.name: Trigger Parry
Trigger Parry.description:
The gunblade's founding heresy: a parry that pulls the trigger: the enemy's blade caught on the flat while the barrel, now conveniently pointed somewhere upsetting, delivers the rebuttal at zero range. Duelists who cross a gunblade for the first time universally describe the same education: the parry felt normal. Then it went off.
[Firearms: 2]

Riptide Sweep.name: Riptide Sweep
Riptide Sweep.description:
The spear sweeps and the sea comes with it: a low polearm arc riding a summoned current: enemies' footing dragged sideways by water that arrived from nowhere and left with their balance. Three sweeps in, the ground is wet, the footing is theirs, and the enemy is fighting at sea without ever boarding anything.
[Polearm Combat: 2]

Heat Haze Feint.name: Heat Haze Feint
Heat Haze Feint.description:
The shimmer that sells the lie: the Mirage Blade wrapped in desert-heat distortion: their outline swimming, the enemy's parry meeting air that was wearing a very convincing sword. After the third feint, enemies begin parrying things that aren't there preemptively, which the school scores as a win.
[Illusion Magic: 2]

Aurora Ward.name: Aurora Ward
Aurora Ward.description:
Dawn, rendered load-bearing: a prismatic barrier in the Sentinel's colors: incoming force scattered across the spectrum before it reaches anyone behind them. The colors thin as the charge spends. Its beauty is doctrine: enemies aim worse at something gorgeous, a fact the Sentinels know, exploit, and refuse to apologize for.
[Light Magic: 2]

Silver Stake.name: Silver Stake
Silver Stake.description:
The profession's oldest sentence, delivered in silver: a driving thrust that pins what it pierces: undead staggering, regeneration hiccupping around the wound. Against the living, merely an excellent thrust with expensive taste; against the deathless, doctrine. The monsters heal from everything. That is why we brought the thing they don't.
[Swordsmanship: 2]

Triage Protocol.name: Triage Protocol
Triage Protocol.description:
Battlefield medicine at the Plague Doctor's tempo: one ally assessed, stabilized, and returned to service in a held breath: bleeding staunched, shock interrupted, the mask's calm settling like an official ruling that they are not allowed to die yet. Patients report it identically: terrifying, efficient, and weirdly reassuring, in that order.
[Herbalism: 3]

Devour Hex.name: Devour Hex
Devour Hex.description:
The class's namesake, performed tableside: a curse pulled off an ally in one practiced motion and eaten: swallowed whole, held down by trained will. The eaten curse is carried, not destroyed, and 'back at the sender' is traditional. Allies learn to read the aftermath: the grimace, the swallow, and the quiet, unsettling 'hm. Bitter.'
[Dark Magic: 3]

Seamstep Cut.name: Seamstep Cut
Seamstep Cut.description:
The Riftmaw's first lesson, weaponized: a step through a seam in space that isn't there for anyone else: the Riftblade exiting the enemy's blind side mid-cut, the slash arriving from an angle the room's geometry formally disputes. The parry was correct. The direction was correct. The Riftblade was simply elsewhere, and armed, and behind them.
[Rift Magic: 2]

Moonlit Omen.name: Moonlit Omen
Moonlit Omen.description:
The moon has already seen tomorrow night; the Oracle merely reads the minutes. The enemy's next intention arrives a heartbeat early: the feint flagged, the killing blow marked in silver before its owner finishes deciding on it. Enemies lodge the same complaint: it wasn't that she was fast. It's that she was already finished dodging.
[Star Magic: 3]

Awaken Relic.name: Awaken Relic
Awaken Relic.description:
The knight speaks the weapon's old name, and the weapon remembers: edge brightening with borrowed centuries, techniques of previous wielders stirring in the grip. A relic awakened too often grows opinionated about scheduling; the bond is a relationship, not an ignition switch. Witnesses describe it the same way: the sword woke up, and the fight became outnumbered.
[Enchanting: 2]

Duel of Roses.name: Duel of Roses
Duel of Roses.description:
The formal challenge, delivered as a weapon: a rose marked to one opponent: the duel declared, blade-work sharpening against that enemy alone. Strikes against the declared duelist bite deeper; strikes against anyone else are, frankly, gauche. Enemies who ignore a declared duel find that witnesses remember, and Luxcellia's courts keep score in ways armor doesn't cover.
[Dueling: 2]

Starshot.name: Starshot
Starshot.description:
An arrow loosed like a falling star: a comet-trail of light across the field, the hit arriving with a flare that marks the target in starlight, visible to every ally. A marked target is a coordinated target, and the light takes its time fading. Starfall Archers do not loose invisible arrows, on principle, and the principle has never once cost them a fight they'd admit to.
[Archery: 2]

Resonant Aria.name: Resonant Aria
Resonant Aria.description:
The Crystalsinger holds a note, and the note holds the line: crystal hummed into existence mid-melody: a singing barrier grown facet by facet, its lattice chiming as attacks refract. Silencing the singer is the counter, and the crystal takes it personally. Everywhere the aria has been sung glitters faintly at dusk, on pitch, for years. It guards those behind it on the turn you sing it; holding the note takes your action again each turn.
[Crystal Magic: 2]

Cinder Brand.name: Cinder Brand
Cinder Brand.description:
The banked ember, paid out one cut at a time: a slash that leaves burning coals in the wound: damage that smolders on after the blade withdraws, patient as a hearth. Dousing it takes water, time, or dignity, and rarely all three survive. The Cinder Knight's fire never spends itself. It invests.
[Swordsmanship: 2]

Golem Command.name: Golem Command
Golem Command.description:
One directive, spoken to stone that trusts you: hold hardening it into architecture, advance lending it a landslide's momentum, guard snapping it between an ally and the incoming worst. Golems obey the spirit of an order with mineral literalism: Golemancers learn to phrase carefully, usually once. Veterans thank the golem afterward, out loud, because the stone remembers being appreciated.
[Earth Magic: 3]

Opening Refrain.name: Opening Refrain
Opening Refrain.description:
The duel's first bar, composed in advance: a parry-strike delivered on the beat: the enemy's opening caught in rhythm, answered in tempo, the Songblade's edge ringing a note that announces which of them is conducting. Three refrains in, the enemy is fighting on the Songblade's tempo without noticing, and the composition has reached the movement titled 'inevitable.'
[Sound Magic: 2]

Hero's Challenge.name: Hero's Challenge
Hero's Challenge.description:
The Hero plants their feet and makes it everyone's business: a challenge loud enough to reorganize the battlefield: enemy attention dragged onto the one person built to carry it, allies rallying in the shadow of someone who just volunteered, on purpose, again. Courage is contagious and the Hero is patient zero. Enemies who take the bait discover the oldest trap: the Hero wanted their attention. The party wanted it more.
[persuasion: 2]

Overlord's Decree.name: Overlord's Decree
Overlord's Decree.description:
The Demon Lord speaks, and the room's spine reconsiders: dread pressure rolling outward: enemy resolve buckling, weapons dipping, formations remembering appointments elsewhere. The strong-willed resist and are noticed resisting, which is its own problem. The Demon Lord never raises their voice. The room simply gets heavier, and everyone in it knows whose.
[intimidation: 2]

Claim Domain.name: Claim Domain
Claim Domain.description:
The Dungeon Lord surveys the room, and the room changes allegiance: territory claimed mid-combat, traps arming easier, minions fighting harder, the enemy realizing the battlefield has an owner and it isn't them. Delvers who breach a claimed room report the sensation exactly: the dungeon didn't get harder. It got personal.
[Dungeon Surveying: 2]

Timber Strike.name: Timber Strike
Timber Strike.description:
A forceful overhead chop that uses the full weight of the axe head to punch through light defenses. Deals bonus damage against shields and wooden barriers. The wind-up is slow enough that agile opponents can sidestep, and the committed downswing roots the user in place for a beat afterward. Best used on targets that are engaged with an ally or caught flat-footed.
[Axe Fighting: 1]

Hewing Sweep.name: Hewing Sweep
Hewing Sweep.description:
A wide horizontal arc that trades precision for area. The sweep catches multiple enemies in close formation and can stagger lighter opponents, but the recovery window is long enough for flanking attackers to punish. The arc's reach scales with weapon length. Less effective against single, well-positioned foes who can simply back out of range.
[Axe Fighting: 5]

Splitting Maul.name: Splitting Maul
Splitting Maul.description:
A two-handed overhead slam that channels full body weight through the axe head into a single crushing point. High chance of breaking through active guards and shattering brittle equipment. The committed downswing roots the user in place, making it dangerous when surrounded. Deals bonus damage to stationary targets and constructs. Ineffective against flying enemies or anything that can simply move aside.
[Axe Fighting: 14]

Rending Cleave.name: Rending Cleave
Rending Cleave.description:
A brutal diagonal slash designed to open deep wounds along natural weak points in armor joins and exposed flesh. Targets struck take residual bleeding damage over the following turns. The technique requires reading the target's stance to find the seam, so it loses effectiveness against amorphous or heavily-plated creatures with no obvious gaps. Bleeding can be stopped by healing magic or first aid.
[Axe Fighting: 25]

Berserker Rush.name: Berserker Rush
Berserker Rush.description:
A charging chain of three rapid axe swings delivered while closing distance. Each successive hit builds momentum, with the final strike dealing significantly more damage than the first. The user's defense drops sharply during the rush, and the trajectory cannot be redirected once committed. Devastating against backline targets and spellcasters who rely on distance. Walls, tight corners, and grapple-type counters shut it down hard.
[Axe Fighting: 40]

Executioner Arc.name: Executioner Arc
Executioner Arc.description:
A devastating overhead strike empowered by focused killing intent that can cleave through magical barriers and high-tier armor. The sheer kinetic force sends a shockwave through the target, disrupting concentration and breaking active spellcasting. Requires firm footing and a full breath of focused intent before release. Targets with evasion abilities or teleportation can escape during the charge-up. Deals massively increased damage to targets below half health.
[Axe Fighting: 56]

Mountain Splitter.name: Mountain Splitter
Mountain Splitter.description:
A legendary technique that channels raw strength into a single blow capable of splitting stone and shattering enchanted defenses. The axe head trails visible force lines as it descends. Deals massive single-target damage and can destroy terrain features, creating new cover or hazards in the environment. The user cannot act defensively for one turn after the strike. Only veteran axe fighters can maintain the bodily control required to land it consistently.
[Axe Fighting: 75]

World Cleaver.name: World Cleaver
World Cleaver.description:
The pinnacle of axe mastery. The wielder raises the axe to its apex, and for a single breath, gravity warps toward the blade. The resulting downstroke sunders everything in its path, bypassing conventional defenses and elemental resistances alike. The spiritual and physical toll is immense: the user is weakened for several turns afterward and cannot use axe techniques during recovery. Usable only once per major engagement. Against truly mythic-tier opponents, even this strike may be endured rather than fatal.
[Axe Fighting: 96]

Skull Crack.name: Skull Crack
Skull Crack.description:
A straightforward overhead strike with a mace, hammer, or staff aimed at the crown of the target's head. Deals bonus damage against unarmored or lightly-armored targets and has a chance to daze the opponent, reducing their accuracy on the following turn. Heavily-armored opponents absorb most of the concussive force through their helm. Simple to execute, reliable, and easy to follow up with a second swing.
[Blunt Weapons: 1]

Crushing Blow.name: Crushing Blow
Crushing Blow.description:
A heavy two-handed swing that prioritizes raw impact over speed. The force is concentrated through the striking head to maximize trauma against rigid targets like armor, bone, shields, and stone. Effective at denting plate armor and reducing its protective value for the rest of the fight. The slow telegraph makes it easy to parry for trained duelists, but the weight behind it can overpower lighter blocks entirely.
[Blunt Weapons: 5]

Shieldbreaker.name: Shieldbreaker
Shieldbreaker.description:
A targeted strike aimed specifically at an opponent's shield or blocking arm. Repeated use degrades shield integrity rapidly, and even a single clean hit can numb the blocking limb. Against shielded enemies this technique removes their primary defense; against unshielded opponents, it functions as a standard power attack with no special bonus. The focused aim means the attack is slower than a regular swing and punishable on a miss.
[Blunt Weapons: 14]

Tremor Slam.name: Tremor Slam
Tremor Slam.description:
A ground-pounding strike that channels force through the floor or terrain, sending a shockwave outward from the point of impact. Enemies standing on the same surface within close range are staggered and may lose their footing. Flying enemies, those braced against walls, and opponents on different elevation are unaffected. Destructible flooring may collapse. Requires a solid surface beneath the user and a weapon heavy enough to transmit the force.
[Blunt Weapons: 25]

Iron Maelstrom.name: Iron Maelstrom
Iron Maelstrom.description:
A spinning attack where the user whirls their blunt weapon in a continuous arc, striking everything within reach multiple times. Each rotation builds speed and force. The attack deals sustained area damage over several seconds but leaves the user dizzy and unable to guard during or immediately after. Countered by ranged attacks from outside the spin radius, grapples that interrupt the rotation, or simply backing away and waiting it out.
[Blunt Weapons: 40]

Bonecrusher.name: Bonecrusher
Bonecrusher.description:
An expertly placed strike targeting skeletal structure and load-bearing joints. On a clean hit, the target suffers a crippling injury that reduces movement speed and physical attack power for the remainder of the encounter. Undead and skeletal enemies take massively increased damage. Armored targets require precise aim at joint gaps, increasing the difficulty. Healing magic can mend the injury over time but not instantly in combat.
[Blunt Weapons: 56]

Earthrend.name: Earthrend
Earthrend.description:
A catastrophic downward strike that fractures the ground itself in a cone ahead of the user. The ruptured terrain launches debris, opens fissures, and creates difficult ground that persists after the fight. All grounded enemies in the cone take heavy blunt damage and are knocked prone. The user needs at least two seconds of wind-up and must be standing on destructible terrain. Stone, packed earth, and ice work well; water, sand, and magical barriers do not transmit the force.
[Blunt Weapons: 75]

Titan Hammer.name: Titan Hammer
Titan Hammer.description:
The ultimate expression of blunt-force mastery. The user gathers an impossible concentration of physical power into a single overhead blow that distorts the air around the weapon head. On contact, the force ignores conventional armor, magical shielding, and damage resistance entirely, delivering pure concussive trauma directly to the target's body. The physical toll on the user is severe: muscles tear, joints ache, and follow-up attacks are significantly weakened for several turns. Legendary-tier targets may endure the hit through sheer vitality.
[Blunt Weapons: 96]

Quick Slash.name: Quick Slash
Quick Slash.description:
A rapid flick of the wrist that draws a shallow cut across exposed skin or light armor gaps. Deals modest damage but executes faster than almost any other melee attack, making it ideal for interrupting enemy actions or landing the first strike in an exchange. The shallow cut rarely threatens armored opponents and cannot penetrate plate or thick hide. Best chained with follow-up techniques or used to create openings.
[Dagger Fighting: 1]

Fan of Blades.name: Fan of Blades
Fan of Blades.description:
A rapid sequence of slashes delivered in an expanding fan pattern at close range, targeting face, throat, wrists, and any other exposed area in quick succession. Each cut is shallow but the accumulated blood loss and pain add up fast. Opponents with full-body armor or magical shielding take minimal damage. The technique burns through the user's stamina quickly and cannot be sustained for more than a few seconds.
[Dagger Fighting: 10]

Arterial Strike.name: Arterial Strike
Arterial Strike.description:
A surgically precise cut targeting a major blood vessel in the neck, inner thigh, or wrist. Requires intimate knowledge of anatomy and a clear line to the target area. On a clean hit, the target begins hemorrhaging rapidly, losing health every turn until treated. The wound resists natural clotting and requires active healing magic or skilled first aid to close. Constructs, undead, and slime-type creatures are immune. Heavily armored targets must have their armor compromised first.
[Dagger Fighting: 16]

Death of a Thousand Cuts.name: Death of a Thousand Cuts
Death of a Thousand Cuts.description:
An extended assault where the user darts in and out of the opponent's range, landing dozens of precise cuts in rapid succession. Each individual wound is minor, but the cumulative trauma degrades the target's combat effectiveness turn by turn: accuracy drops, reaction time slows, and eventually the blood loss becomes critical. The user must maintain close range throughout, making them vulnerable to area attacks and grapples. Interrupted if pinned, stunned, or immobilized.
[Dagger Fighting: 22]

Phantom Edge.name: Phantom Edge
Phantom Edge.description:
A knife technique so fast the blade appears to pass through the target without resistance. The user strikes at a frequency that bypasses conventional parry timing, and the cuts register a fraction of a second after the blade has already withdrawn. Ignores most forms of active defense including magical barriers that react to incoming force. The strain on the user's muscles and tendons is extreme, disabling fine motor control in the weapon hand for several turns. Requires a blade in perfect condition; a chipped or dull edge cannot achieve the necessary speed.
[Dagger Fighting: 30]

Heartseeking Fang.name: Heartseeking Fang
Heartseeking Fang.description:
The ultimate assassination technique. The user reads the target's breathing pattern, heartbeat rhythm, and muscle tension, then delivers a single thrust timed to slip between ribs and pierce the heart directly. Against targets with a biological heart, this strike deals critical damage that can end fights instantly. The setup requires three full seconds of uninterrupted observation at close range, during which the user is completely vulnerable. Targets without hearts, with displaced organs, or under transformation effects are immune to the instant-kill component but still take heavy piercing damage.
[Dagger Fighting: 47]

Reaping Arc.name: Reaping Arc
Reaping Arc.description:
A wide sweeping cut with the scythe blade that exploits the weapon's natural reach advantage. The curved edge hooks around shields and catches opponents who think they are outside melee range. Deals modest damage but covers a large area, making it effective against groups of weaker enemies. The extended swing arc leaves a gap on the user's weapon-side that experienced fighters can exploit by stepping inside the reach.
[Scythe Combat: 1]

Harvest Pull.name: Harvest Pull
Harvest Pull.description:
A hooking technique that uses the scythe's curved blade to catch an opponent's limb, weapon, or armor and yank them off-balance or pull them into close range. Effective for dragging ranged attackers into melee or pulling mounted enemies from their mounts. The pull force depends on the user's strength versus the target's weight and footing. Targets braced against solid objects or significantly larger than the user resist the pull entirely.
[Scythe Combat: 5]

Grim Flourish.name: Grim Flourish
Grim Flourish.description:
A spinning scythe technique that uses centrifugal force to accelerate the blade through a full rotation, striking twice in rapid succession. The first cut forces a defensive reaction, and the second arrives from an unexpected angle as the blade completes its circuit. Requires open space to execute; cramped quarters or low ceilings make the spin impossible. The technique's intimidation factor often rattles inexperienced opponents into making mistakes.
[Scythe Combat: 14]

Soul Scythe.name: Soul Scythe
Soul Scythe.description:
A technique that channels the user's fighting spirit through the scythe blade, creating a crescent-shaped energy projection that extends the weapon's effective range by several meters. The energy arc deals damage to everything in its path and can cut through light magical barriers. The spiritual cost manifests as fatigue proportional to the projection's size. Maintaining the projection drains mana if available. Purely physical opponents cannot replicate or counter the energy extension but can dodge it.
[Scythe Combat: 25]

Death's Waltz.name: Death's Waltz
Death's Waltz.description:
A flowing combat pattern where the user moves in sweeping circular steps, treating the scythe as an extension of continuous rotational motion. Every step generates another cutting arc, creating a persistent zone of danger around the user that lasts for several turns. Enemies entering the zone take automatic slashing damage. The user cannot stop mid-waltz without stumbling, and ranged attacks from outside the zone are the most reliable counter. Movement speed is locked to the waltz rhythm.
[Scythe Combat: 40]

Harvest Moon.name: Harvest Moon
Harvest Moon.description:
A massive scythe swing that traces a full crescent in the air, launching a blade of compressed air and spiritual energy toward distant targets. The crescent travels up to twenty meters and cuts through obstacles in its path. The technique requires a full wind-up rotation and leaves the user stationary and exhausted for a moment afterward. Multiple targets caught in the crescent's path each take full damage. Dissipated by strong wind magic or spatial distortion effects.
[Scythe Combat: 56]

Quietus.name: Quietus
Quietus.description:
A single, perfect reaping stroke delivered with absolute focus. The blade passes through the target with minimal resistance, as though cutting air rather than flesh. The wound does not appear for a full second after the cut, then opens all at once. Deals catastrophic damage and suppresses natural regeneration and healing magic on the wound for several turns. The technique demands complete stillness before the strike, making it unusable while being actively pressured. Against regenerating or undying targets, the healing suppression is its true value.
[Scythe Combat: 75]

Final Harvest.name: Final Harvest
Final Harvest.description:
The apex of scythe mastery, a technique whispered about in the academies as the closest a mortal weapon can come to true death magic. The user enters a trance-like state where their movements become perfectly fluid, and the scythe moves in patterns that seem to anticipate the target's evasion before it happens. For three turns, every attack is a killing stroke. The trance leaves the user physically collapsed afterward, unable to fight until they recover. Targets with death immunity or divine protection resist the worst of the effect but still take severe damage.
[Scythe Combat: 96]

Iron Fan Strike.name: Iron Fan Strike
Iron Fan Strike.description:
A sharp snap of a combat fan that sends a blade of compressed air toward the target at close range. The attack is fast, elegant, and nearly silent, making it excellent for surprise strikes in social settings where drawing a conventional weapon would cause alarm. Damage is modest and falls off rapidly beyond five meters. The fan must be constructed for combat; a decorative fan shatters on the first serious strike.
[Fan Combat: 1]

Flutter Guard.name: Flutter Guard
Flutter Guard.description:
A defensive technique that uses rapid opening and closing of the fan to create unpredictable air currents that deflect incoming projectiles and disrupt the aim of ranged attackers. Works against arrows, thrown weapons, and small magical projectiles. Larger projectiles, area spells, and melee attacks are unaffected. The technique requires continuous hand motion and cannot be maintained while attacking. Provides a significant evasion bonus for as long as the user sustains it.
[Fan Combat: 5]

Petal Storm.name: Petal Storm
Petal Storm.description:
A rapid series of slashing motions with the fan's sharpened edges, delivered in a pattern that resembles falling petals. Each cut targets a different exposed area in quick succession. The visual beauty of the technique often distracts opponents, providing a subtle accuracy bonus. Effective against lightly-armored targets; heavy armor reduces the damage significantly since the fan edges lack the mass to penetrate plate. Can be performed with one hand, leaving the other free.
[Fan Combat: 14]

Silken Gale.name: Silken Gale
Silken Gale.description:
A sweeping fan motion that generates a focused gust of wind strong enough to knock lighter opponents off their feet or push back advancing enemies. The wind disrupts loose footing, scatters paper and light objects, and can extinguish non-magical flames in the area. Heavier opponents are staggered but not toppled. The technique channels charisma and fighting spirit rather than raw physical strength, making it one of the few combat arts that scales with force of personality. Useless in enclosed spaces without air circulation.
[Fan Combat: 25]

Dance of Veils.name: Dance of Veils
Dance of Veils.description:
An elegant evasion and counter technique where the user moves in flowing dance-like patterns, using the fan to redirect incoming attacks rather than block them. For several turns, the user gains dramatically increased evasion against melee attacks and can riposte with a cutting fan strike each time they successfully dodge. The technique requires concentration and breaks if the user takes a direct hit. Particularly effective against single powerful attackers; less useful against swarms or area effects.
[Fan Combat: 40]

Tempest Fan.name: Tempest Fan
Tempest Fan.description:
A technique that channels immense force through the fan to generate a localized windstorm in a cone ahead of the user. The storm shreds everything in its path with razor-sharp air currents, dealing heavy slashing damage to all targets within range. Environmental objects become projectiles caught in the wind. The user must plant their feet and brace against the backlash, making them immobile during the technique. Dispelled by wind-nullification magic or barriers that seal air movement.
[Fan Combat: 56]

Thousand Paper Cranes.name: Thousand Paper Cranes
Thousand Paper Cranes.description:
An advanced technique that channels spiritual energy through the fan to create dozens of razor-sharp wind constructs shaped like origami cranes. The constructs swarm the target independently, attacking from every angle simultaneously. Each crane deals modest individual damage, but the swarm overwhelms defensive reactions and conventional blocking. The technique drains significant stamina and spiritual energy. Targets with area-of-effect defenses or elemental wind absorption can neutralize the swarm. The constructs persist for two turns before dissipating.
[Fan Combat: 75]

Divine Wind.name: Divine Wind
Divine Wind.description:
The supreme art of fan combat, a technique recorded in only a handful of ancient scrolls. The user becomes the eye of a spiraling vortex of cutting wind that expands outward in all directions. Everything within the vortex radius takes continuous slashing damage that ignores physical armor. Allies and the user are shielded in the calm center. The vortex persists for up to four turns but drains the user's vitality directly; sustaining it too long can be fatal. Ended prematurely by spatial magic, extreme cold that freezes the air, or disrupting the user's concentration.
[Fan Combat: 96]

Lash Snap.name: Lash Snap
Lash Snap.description:
A quick crack of a whip, chain, or flexible weapon that strikes a single target at medium range. The attack is faster than most melee approaches and can reach opponents who believe they are safely outside sword distance. Damage is modest but the sharp crack can startle mounts and untrained combatants. Less effective against heavily-armored targets since the strike disperses force across the impact surface rather than concentrating it.
[Flexible Weapons: 1]

Coiling Snare.name: Coiling Snare
Coiling Snare.description:
A wrapping strike that winds the flexible weapon around a target's limb, weapon, or neck, briefly immobilizing the caught body part. The bind lasts only a moment against strong opponents who can tear free, but that moment is enough for an ally to land an uncontested strike or for the user to yank the target off-balance. Fails against targets with bladed armor, extreme heat auras, or bodies too large for the weapon to wrap. The user's weapon is occupied for the duration of the bind.
[Flexible Weapons: 3]

Serpent Flurry.name: Serpent Flurry
Serpent Flurry.description:
A rapid sequence of strikes where the flexible weapon moves in unpredictable serpentine patterns, lashing from different angles in quick succession. The irregular timing makes the attacks extremely difficult to parry or predict. Each individual hit deals light damage, but four to six connect in the span of a single action. Armored targets shrug off the individual hits; the technique excels against exposed flesh and light armor. Sustained use fatigues the user's wrist and forearm.
[Flexible Weapons: 10]

Ricochet Lash.name: Ricochet Lash
Ricochet Lash.description:
A technique that bounces the weighted tip of a chain or flail off a hard surface to strike a target from an unexpected angle, bypassing their guard entirely. The user reads the environment for usable ricochet surfaces: walls, pillars, floors, shields, even other enemies. Requires a rigid surface nearby and precise spatial awareness. Open fields with no bounce surfaces make the technique impossible. The redirected strike carries less force than a direct hit but almost always connects against opponents focused on the user's facing.
[Flexible Weapons: 16]

Iron Tempest.name: Iron Tempest
Iron Tempest.description:
The user spins their flexible weapon in an accelerating orbit around their body, creating a persistent zone of whirling metal that damages anything that enters and deflects incoming projectiles. The orbit can be sustained for several turns but demands constant motion and concentration. The user cannot attack specific targets while maintaining the tempest and moves at half speed. Interrupted by grapples, entanglement effects, or anything that stops the weapon mid-spin. The zone radius scales with weapon length.
[Flexible Weapons: 38]

Binding Chains.name: Binding Chains
Binding Chains.description:
An advanced restraint technique that wraps the target in multiple loops of chain or weighted cord, progressively restricting their movement until they are fully immobilized. The binding tightens with each turn the target struggles, rewarding patience over brute escape attempts. Targets with exceptional strength can break free, but doing so costs them multiple turns of focused effort. Bladed limbs, fire auras, or acid secretions sever the binding quickly. While sustaining the bind, the user cannot attack others.
[Flexible Weapons: 47]

Dragon's Tail.name: Dragon's Tail
Dragon's Tail.description:
A master-level technique where the user whips their weapon so fast it breaks the sound barrier, creating a shockwave along its path. The sonic crack deals concussive damage in a line that passes through physical barriers and armor, reaching targets that conventional attacks cannot touch. The force required tears at the user's shoulder and elbow joints, limiting usage and degrading accuracy on follow-up attacks. Against sound-sensitive creatures the technique deals bonus damage and can cause disorientation.
[Flexible Weapons: 66]

Leviathan Coil.name: Leviathan Coil
Leviathan Coil.description:
The pinnacle of flexible weapon mastery. The user channels their full fighting spirit through the weapon, which moves with seemingly independent intelligence, striking, binding, and deflecting simultaneously as though wielded by multiple fighters. For three turns the weapon acts as both offense and defense, attacking up to three targets per turn while maintaining a defensive perimeter. The spiritual drain is catastrophic: afterward the user collapses into exhaustion and cannot fight effectively for an extended recovery period. The weapon must have personal significance to the user; borrowed or generic weapons cannot sustain the spiritual load.
[Flexible Weapons: 88]

Quick Toss.name: Quick Toss
Quick Toss.description:
A fast, accurate throw of a small weapon at a single target within short range. Throwing knives, darts, small axes, and shuriken all qualify. The throw executes faster than drawing a bow and can interrupt enemy actions or finish off wounded targets at range. Damage drops significantly beyond ten meters and the projectile is lost unless retrieved. Armored targets deflect most thrown weapons unless the throw targets exposed areas.
[Thrown Weapons: 1]

Scatter Throw.name: Scatter Throw
Scatter Throw.description:
A technique where the user hurls three to five small projectiles in a spread pattern, covering a wide area. Individual accuracy drops compared to a focused throw, but the spread makes dodging difficult and at least one projectile usually connects. Effective for suppressing groups of enemies or tagging fast-moving targets. Consumes multiple pieces of ammunition per use. Useless at long range where the spread becomes too wide to threaten anyone.
[Thrown Weapons: 5]

Ricochet Blade.name: Ricochet Blade
Ricochet Blade.description:
A calculated throw that bounces a bladed projectile off one or more hard surfaces to strike a target behind cover or around corners. The user must visualize the bounce path before throwing, and each ricochet reduces the projectile's remaining force. Maximum of two bounces under normal conditions; a third is theoretically possible but requires exceptional spatial awareness and a perfectly weighted weapon. Useless in open terrain with no surfaces to bounce from. The technique's true value is bypassing shields and cover.
[Thrown Weapons: 25]

Storm of Steel.name: Storm of Steel
Storm of Steel.description:
A sustained barrage where the user draws and throws projectiles in continuous rapid succession, maintaining suppressive fire for several turns. The sheer volume of incoming steel forces opponents to stay in cover and prevents spellcasters from completing incantations. Accuracy per throw is lower than a careful aimed shot, but the aggregate damage adds up fast against exposed targets. Drains the user's entire supply of throwable ammunition. Once empty, the technique ends and the user must retrieve or resupply.
[Thrown Weapons: 40]

Phantom Javelin.name: Phantom Javelin
Phantom Javelin.description:
A throw infused with the user's fighting spirit that creates a brief afterimage trail behind the projectile, making it appear to split into two or three copies in flight. Only the real projectile deals damage, but the target must guess which one to dodge. Even experienced fighters are caught by the deception roughly half the time. Spiritual sensitivity or true-sight abilities negate the illusion. The technique works with any thrown weapon but is most convincing with javelins and spears whose longer profiles create more convincing duplicates.
[Thrown Weapons: 56]

Heaven Piercer.name: Heaven Piercer
Heaven Piercer.description:
A throw of such force and precision that the projectile breaks the speed of sound, arriving before the target can react to the throw motion. The projectile penetrates magical barriers, conventional shields, and all but the heaviest armor. The sonic boom along its flight path can stagger nearby bystanders. The technique requires a specially reinforced throwing weapon; ordinary projectiles shatter from the launch force. Only one throw per engagement at this intensity before the user's throwing arm needs recovery time.
[Thrown Weapons: 75]

Godspear.name: Godspear
Godspear.description:
The legendary apex of thrown weapon mastery. The user concentrates every ounce of physical power, spatial awareness, and fighting spirit into a single throw that crosses impossible distances with unerring accuracy. The projectile ignores wind, gravity, intervening obstacles, and defensive magic, traveling in a perfectly straight line to its target as though reality itself bends to accommodate it. The physical toll is devastating: the user's throwing arm is completely disabled for the rest of the engagement, and the spiritual exhaustion leaves them weakened for hours afterward. Against divine-tier targets, the throw connects but may not penetrate their innate protections.
[Thrown Weapons: 96]

Unorthodox Strike.name: Unorthodox Strike
Unorthodox Strike.description:
An attack using an unconventional or improvised weapon in a way no formal style would teach. Furniture legs, farming tools, musical instruments, bottles, or any weapon too strange for standard classification. The attack is unpredictable precisely because no one trains to defend against it. Deals modest damage but opponents trained exclusively in formal combat styles take a slight accuracy penalty when defending, as their muscle memory has no template for the incoming angle.
[Exotic Weapons: 1]

Adaptive Grip.name: Adaptive Grip
Adaptive Grip.description:
The user rapidly adjusts their grip, stance, and striking angle to exploit an exotic weapon's unique properties rather than fighting against them. A kusarigama's chain becomes a grapple line, a war fan's edge becomes a cutter, a tonfa's handle becomes a joint lock. Provides a passive accuracy bonus when wielding any weapon outside the standard sword/axe/bow categories. The bonus reflects genuine mastery of the weapon's design rather than brute-forcing a conventional technique onto an unconventional tool.
[Exotic Weapons: 5]

Bewildering Form.name: Bewildering Form
Bewildering Form.description:
A fighting style that deliberately uses confusing weapon movements to disorient the opponent. The user swings, spins, and repositions their exotic weapon in patterns designed to obscure the actual attack within a flurry of feints. Opponents without experience fighting exotic weapons suffer an accuracy and evasion penalty for the duration. Trained exotic weapon users are immune to the confusion. The technique sacrifices some offensive power for its disorienting effect.
[Exotic Weapons: 14]

Weapon Mimic.name: Weapon Mimic
Weapon Mimic.description:
After observing an opponent's fighting style for at least one turn, the user adapts their exotic weapon to counter it specifically. The exotic weapon's versatile handling allows it to simulate the defensive responses of whatever weapon type the opponent uses, neutralizing their trained advantages. Provides a scaling defensive bonus against the studied opponent that increases each turn of continued observation. Resets if the opponent switches styles or weapons. Cannot mimic magical combat techniques, only physical weapon patterns.
[Exotic Weapons: 25]

Chimera Style.name: Chimera Style
Chimera Style.description:
An advanced technique that chains attacks from multiple weapon disciplines into a single fluid combination using the exotic weapon's unusual properties. A bladed staff might transition from spear thrusts to staff sweeps to short-range cuts in a single sequence. Each transition catches defenders who adjusted to the previous attack pattern. The number of style transitions possible in one sequence scales with skill level. Requires deep understanding of at least two conventional weapon styles in addition to the exotic weapon itself.
[Exotic Weapons: 40]

Impossible Angle.name: Impossible Angle
Impossible Angle.description:
A strike delivered from an angle that conventional weapon geometry cannot achieve. The exotic weapon's unique shape, balance, or articulation allows the attack to curve, hook, or redirect in ways that bypass standard parry positions entirely. Experienced fighters describe the incoming angle as simply wrong, as though the weapon bent mid-swing. Ignores parry and block bonuses from conventional defensive techniques. Magical barriers and pure evasion still apply. The technique requires a weapon with genuine mechanical articulation; rigid exotic weapons cannot achieve the necessary angle deviation.
[Exotic Weapons: 56]

Arsenal Incarnate.name: Arsenal Incarnate
Arsenal Incarnate.description:
The user enters a heightened state where every object within reach becomes a lethal weapon in their hands. Chairs, branches, loose stones, enemy weapons knocked to the ground, even articles of clothing are wielded with the same lethality as a forged blade. For several turns, the user fights with whatever is available, seamlessly transitioning between improvised weapons as each is spent or broken. Each improvised weapon strikes once at full power before being discarded. The state ends when the user runs out of available objects or the duration expires. Rooms full of furniture and debris favor this technique; empty spaces limit it.
[Exotic Weapons: 75]

Formless Blade.name: Formless Blade
Formless Blade.description:
The ultimate expression of exotic weapon mastery: the user transcends the concept of a fixed weapon style entirely. Their movements cannot be categorized, predicted, or studied because they follow no pattern at all. Every strike is unique, generated in the moment from pure combat intuition. Provides massive bonuses to accuracy and evasion for the duration because no defensive system can model the incoming attacks. The state requires absolute mental clarity; any emotional disruption, pain, or distraction breaks it immediately. While active, the user cannot execute any named technique from any weapon style, including exotic weapon abilities. The formlessness is the technique.
[Exotic Weapons: 96]

Tripwire.name: Tripwire
Tripwire.description:
The user stretches a near-invisible thread across a pathway or combat area at ankle height. Enemies moving through the area without detecting the thread are tripped, falling prone and losing their next action. The thread is extremely difficult to spot without active searching or enhanced perception. Detectable by tremor-sense, magical detection, or any ability that reveals hidden objects. The thread breaks after one use and must be reset. Requires a moment of preparation and two anchor points, so it cannot be deployed mid-combat in open ground.
[Thread Arts: 1]

Razor Line.name: Razor Line
Razor Line.description:
A cutting technique using a single taut thread held between both hands or anchored to a finger ring. The user draws the thread across exposed flesh at high speed, inflicting a deep, clean cut that bleeds freely. The thread must be specially treated or made from monster silk to hold an edge. Effective at very close range only. Armored targets, thick-skinned creatures, and anything wearing layered cloth resist the cut. The technique is nearly invisible in execution, making it a favored tool of assassins and court intrigue specialists.
[Thread Arts: 5]

Web Weave.name: Web Weave
Web Weave.description:
The user deploys multiple threads across an area, creating a nearly invisible web that restricts movement and entangles anyone who walks into it.
