Runeforged Blade.description:
The smith works runes directly into the structure of the metal during forging rather than etching them on the surface afterward. Runeforged weapons carry powerful, stable enchantments that cannot be dispelled without destroying the weapon itself. The runes activate in response to the wielder's intent, providing effects tuned to the weapon's purpose. The technique requires both master smithing and knowledge of runic inscription, and the runes must be struck into the metal at exactly the right heat or they lose potency. Each runeforged weapon is a significant undertaking.
[Blacksmithing: 51]

Soulbound Masterwork.name: Soulbound Masterwork
Soulbound Masterwork.description:
The pinnacle of the forge. The smith creates a weapon so perfectly crafted that it develops a bond with its wielder, growing in power as they grow and eventually manifesting unique properties shaped by the deeds accomplished with it. A soulbound masterwork begins as an exceptional weapon and becomes a legendary artifact over the course of its wielder's career, remembering every battle. Creating one requires the finest materials, months of dedicated work, and the smith investing a fragment of their own spirit into the forging. Only one can be created at a time, and the smith cannot begin another until the first has found its wielder.
[Blacksmithing: 72]

Thoughtful Token.name: Thoughtful Token
Thoughtful Token.description:
The crafter creates a small personal gift tailored to a specific recipient's tastes and interests. A well-chosen token provides a meaningful boost to the recipient's disposition when given, larger than an equivalent purchased item because it demonstrates genuine attention. The technique requires knowing something real about the recipient; a generic gift crafted with this skill is merely a nice object. Effective for building early rapport with NPCs the crafter wants to befriend or court.
[Gift Crafting: 5]

Keepsake Craft.name: Keepsake Craft
Keepsake Craft.description:
The crafter makes a durable memento designed to be carried and treasured over time: a charm, a pendant, a carved figure, a pressed-flower locket. Keepsakes deepen an existing bond and serve as a lasting reminder of the relationship; recipients often keep them for years. The emotional value scales with the depth of the existing relationship and the personal significance of the materials used. A keepsake made from a shared memory or meaningful location carries far more weight than one made from ordinary materials.
[Gift Crafting: 8]

Sentiment Weaving.name: Sentiment Weaving
Sentiment Weaving.description:
The crafter imbues a gift with a genuine emotional resonance that the recipient can feel when they hold it. The gift carries a faint impression of the crafter's sincere feelings, warmth, gratitude, devotion, or apology, communicated wordlessly through the object. This makes it a powerful tool for expressing feelings that are difficult to say aloud. The resonance is only as strong as the crafter's genuine emotion; a gift crafted with false or manipulative intent carries an unpleasant hollowness that perceptive recipients notice.
[Gift Crafting: 17]

Bond Talisman.name: Bond Talisman
Bond Talisman.description:
The crafter creates a paired set of talismans that maintain a subtle connection between the giver and receiver. Holders of paired talismans can sense each other's general emotional state and rough direction across moderate distances, and each feels a faint warmth when the other thinks of them. The connection is gentle and non-invasive, providing reassurance rather than surveillance. The talismans require materials personally significant to both parties and only function while both willingly carry their half. Breaking the bond requires deliberately discarding the talisman.
[Gift Crafting: 32]

Heartfelt Masterpiece.name: Heartfelt Masterpiece
Heartfelt Masterpiece.description:
The crafter produces a gift of such personal significance and artistic quality that it becomes a defining moment in a relationship. A heartfelt masterpiece is customized down to the smallest detail, incorporating shared history, inside references, and the recipient's deepest values. Receiving one produces a major, lasting improvement to the relationship and often marks a turning point. The crafting requires deep knowledge of the recipient and significant time and materials. Each masterpiece is unique and cannot be replicated; giving two people identical masterpieces cheapens both.
[Gift Crafting: 51]

Gift of a Lifetime.name: Gift of a Lifetime
Gift of a Lifetime.description:
The ultimate expression of gift crafting: a creation so perfectly attuned to its recipient that it becomes their most treasured possession for the rest of their life. The gift addresses something the recipient has longed for without ever voicing: a lost connection restored, a dream made tangible, a wound acknowledged and honored. Receiving it can permanently transform the recipient's relationship with the giver, turning acquaintances into devoted allies and deepening love into unshakeable commitment. Creating one requires profound understanding of the recipient's heart, the rarest materials, and the crafter pouring their entire being into the work. A crafter creates only a handful of these in a lifetime.
[Gift Crafting: 72]

Precise Setting.name: Precise Setting
Precise Setting.description:
The jeweler sets gemstones with enough precision that their natural properties are preserved and enhanced rather than dampened by the mounting. Magical gems set with this technique retain their full potency, and the setting itself is secure against loss during active use. The technique is essential for functional magical jewelry; a poorly-set enchantment gem may fall out, crack, or lose its charge. Requires fine tools and steady hands. Also improves the resale value and visual appeal of any piece.
[Jewelcrafting: 5]

Gem Cutting.name: Gem Cutting
Gem Cutting.description:
The jeweler cuts raw gemstones to maximize their optical and magical properties, revealing facets that focus light and channel magical energy efficiently. A well-cut gem holds more enchantment charge, refracts light more beautifully, and commands a far higher price than an uncut stone. Each gem type has an ideal cut that suits its crystalline structure; cutting against the grain shatters the stone. The technique requires knowledge of each gem's internal structure and considerable patience, as a single miscut wastes a valuable material.
[Jewelcrafting: 8]

Attunement Setting.name: Attunement Setting
Attunement Setting.description:
The jeweler crafts jewelry that attunes to its wearer over time, gradually adapting its magical properties to complement the wearer's abilities and needs. An attunement ring worn by a mage slowly develops mana-conductive properties; the same ring worn by a warrior develops resilience. The attunement takes weeks of continuous wear to fully develop and resets if the jewelry changes owners. The technique produces jewelry that grows more valuable to its specific owner over time while remaining generic to anyone else.
[Jewelcrafting: 17]

Focus Crystal Crafting.name: Focus Crystal Crafting
Focus Crystal Crafting.description:
The jeweler creates crystalline focuses that amplify and refine magical energy channeled through them. A focus crystal set into a staff, wand, or piece of jewelry reduces the mana cost of spells and improves their precision. Different crystal cuts and materials suit different magical disciplines: a fire mage's focus differs from a healer's. The crafting requires flawless raw crystals and precise cutting; internal fractures cause the focus to shatter under magical load. High-quality focuses are prized by every spellcaster who can afford them.
[Jewelcrafting: 32]

Reliquary Craft.name: Reliquary Craft
Reliquary Craft.description:
The jeweler creates ornate containers designed to house and stabilize powerful magical objects, spirits, or essences. A properly crafted reliquary can safely contain items that would otherwise be dangerous to carry: a bound spirit, a volatile enchantment, a fragment of divine or demonic power. The reliquary regulates the contained energy, preventing leakage and protecting the bearer. The crafting requires precious metals, stabilizing gems, and knowledge of containment principles. A flawed reliquary may fail catastrophically, releasing whatever it was meant to hold.
[Jewelcrafting: 51]

Crown of Ages.name: Crown of Ages
Crown of Ages.description:
The supreme achievement of jewelcrafting: a regalia-tier piece that is a legendary artifact in its own right. A crown of ages incorporates multiple perfectly-cut legendary gems, master settings, and a unifying enchantment that binds the whole into something greater than its parts. Such a piece can grant its wearer significant magical power, project authority that bends crowds, or house an ancient power passed down through generations. Creating one requires gems of extraordinary rarity, months of flawless work, and the jeweler operating at the absolute peak of their craft. A single internal flaw ruins the entire piece, and few jewelers ever complete one.
[Jewelcrafting: 72]

Combat Ration.name: Combat Ration
Combat Ration.description:
The cook prepares field rations optimized for consumption during or immediately before combat. A combat ration is compact, quick to eat, and provides a short burst of stamina and focus without the sluggishness of a full meal. Consuming one mid-fight restores a small amount of stamina and steadies the hands. The rations keep for several days and can be prepared in bulk before an expedition. The technique balances immediate energy against digestibility; a ration that sits heavy is worse than none at all in a fight.
[Battle Cooking: 5]

Adrenaline Dish.name: Adrenaline Dish
Adrenaline Dish.description:
The cook prepares a dish using stimulant ingredients that temporarily heighten the eater's reflexes and combat awareness. Consumed before a battle, an adrenaline dish provides a short-duration boost to reaction speed and accuracy. The effect is powerful but comes with a comedown: once it fades, the eater feels a wave of fatigue. The technique must balance potency against the severity of the crash. Overuse builds tolerance, requiring stronger doses for diminishing returns.
[Battle Cooking: 8]

Iron Stomach Feast.name: Iron Stomach Feast
Iron Stomach Feast.description:
The cook prepares a hearty pre-battle meal that fortifies the eater against physical punishment. For the duration of the blessing, the eater's pain tolerance increases, their stamina drains more slowly, and minor wounds trouble them less. The meal takes time to prepare and must be eaten before combat, not during. The fortification is physical resilience, not magical protection; it helps the eater keep fighting through hardship rather than preventing damage. Effective for prolonged engagements and endurance challenges.
[Battle Cooking: 17]

Berserker's Broth.name: Berserker's Broth
Berserker's Broth.description:
The cook brews a potent broth that induces a controlled combat frenzy in those who drink it. The frenzy grants a significant boost to physical strength and aggression while dulling fear and hesitation. The tradeoff is reduced tactical judgment; the drinker fights harder but less carefully. The broth's effects are strong enough that it must be used deliberately, not casually. The frenzy fades after the battle, leaving the drinker exhausted. Individuals with strong self-control retain more tactical awareness during the frenzy than impulsive ones.
[Battle Cooking: 32]

War Banquet.name: War Banquet
War Banquet.description:
The cook prepares a comprehensive pre-battle feast for an entire party or war band, providing coordinated blessings that bolster each eater's role. Frontliners receive fortification, spellcasters receive focus, scouts receive heightened perception. The banquet's blessings last through an extended engagement and significantly improve the group's combat effectiveness. Preparation requires hours and quality ingredients scaled to the group size. The technique is a favorite of adventuring parties and military units preparing for major operations, turning a shared meal into a tactical advantage.
[Battle Cooking: 51]

Feast of Champions.name: Feast of Champions
Feast of Champions.description:
The ultimate battle-cooking creation: a legendary feast that temporarily elevates every eater to the peak of their combat potential. For the duration of a major battle, all eaters gain substantial boosts to their physical capabilities, resistance to fear and pain, and coordination with their allies. The feast draws on the shared bonds of those who eat it together, growing more potent the stronger their camaraderie. Preparing it requires legendary ingredients and a full day of work, and it can be served only rarely due to the intensity of the effect. A party that shares a feast of champions before a decisive battle fights as a single unstoppable force.
[Battle Cooking: 72]

Supple Tanning.name: Supple Tanning
Supple Tanning.description:
The leatherworker tans hides to achieve an ideal balance of flexibility and durability. Supple-tanned leather moves with the wearer without cracking, resists water and wear, and lasts far longer than roughly-processed hide. Armor and gear made from properly tanned leather provides better protection and comfort. The tanning process takes days and requires the right combination of agents for each hide type. Monster hides need specialized tanning techniques to preserve their inherent properties.
[Leatherworking: 5]

Reinforced Bracing.name: Reinforced Bracing
Reinforced Bracing.description:
The leatherworker layers and braces leather armor at key stress points, significantly improving its protective value without adding much weight. Reinforced leather turns aside glancing blows and reduces the impact of direct hits, bridging the gap between cloth and metal armor. The technique places bracing exactly where it is needed based on how the wearer fights and where they are most exposed. The improvement is meaningful for anyone who relies on mobility and cannot wear heavy plate.
[Leatherworking: 8]

Beast Hide Curing.name: Beast Hide Curing
Beast Hide Curing.description:
The leatherworker cures the hides of magical beasts and monsters in a way that preserves their innate properties. A fire drake's hide retains heat resistance; a frost wolf's pelt provides cold protection; a shadow panther's hide grants stealth benefits. The curing process is specific to each creature type and requires knowledge of the properties being preserved. Improperly cured monster hide loses its magical qualities and becomes ordinary leather. Gear made from properly cured beast hide combines physical protection with elemental resistance.
[Leatherworking: 17]

Living Leather.name: Living Leather
Living Leather.description:
The leatherworker treats hide with a process that keeps a portion of its living properties intact, producing armor that slowly repairs minor damage and gradually conforms to the wearer's body over time. Living leather grows more comfortable and better-fitting with wear, and small cuts and scuffs mend themselves over days of rest. The treatment requires fresh hide and specialized reagents. The living quality fades if the leather is exposed to fire, extreme cold, or long periods of disuse, at which point it becomes ordinary cured leather.
[Leatherworking: 32]

Warden's Hide.name: Warden's Hide
Warden's Hide.description:
The leatherworker crafts armor from the hide of an apex predator or guardian beast, imbuing it with the creature's protective instincts. Warden's hide armor provides a warning sense to its wearer, subtly alerting them to nearby danger and hostile intent before an attack lands. The armor also carries an intimidating aura drawn from the source creature, giving lesser beasts pause. The crafting requires the intact hide of a powerful territorial creature and careful preservation of its predatory essence. The protective sense is a genuine survival advantage in dangerous territory.
[Leatherworking: 51]

Dragonhide Regalia.name: Dragonhide Regalia
Dragonhide Regalia.description:
The pinnacle of leatherworking: armor crafted from the hide of a true dragon or comparable legendary creature. Dragonhide regalia provides protection rivaling the finest metal plate while remaining as flexible as cloth, and it carries powerful inherent resistances drawn from the dragon's nature: fire immunity from a flame dragon, spatial resilience from a void dragon. The armor is nearly indestructible and grows subtly more attuned to its wearer over years of use. Crafting it requires an intact section of legendary hide, months of painstaking work, and mastery of every leatherworking technique. Only a handful of such pieces exist in the world.
[Leatherworking: 72]

Sharp Appraisal.name: Sharp Appraisal
Sharp Appraisal.description:
The merchant accurately assesses the true value of goods at a glance, seeing past a seller's inflated claims or a buyer's lowball offers. This prevents the merchant from being cheated and reveals when an item is being sold below its worth: a bargain to snap up. The appraisal covers common trade goods, gear, and materials; exotic or magical items may require specialized knowledge. The skill also lets the merchant estimate an NPC's willingness to pay, providing an edge in every negotiation.
[Merchant Trade: 5]

Silver Negotiation.name: Silver Negotiation
Silver Negotiation.description:
The merchant negotiates prices with skill that consistently produces better deals than an untrained trader could manage: lower prices when buying, higher when selling. The technique reads the counterparty's eagerness, anchors the opening offer strategically, and knows when to walk away to force a concession. The improvement applies to every transaction, compounding over time into significant wealth. NPCs respect a shrewd but fair negotiator; those who feel cheated remember it, so the best merchants leave the other party feeling they got a fair deal too.
[Merchant Trade: 8]

Market Reading.name: Market Reading
Market Reading.description:
The merchant reads market conditions to identify profitable opportunities: which goods are scarce where, which regions pay premiums for which materials, and when prices are about to shift. This knowledge enables arbitrage, buying cheap in one place and selling dear in another, and helps the merchant avoid buying into a collapsing market. The reading requires gathering information from multiple sources and understanding regional economies. A merchant with sharp market reading turns ordinary trade routes into reliable profit engines.
[Merchant Trade: 17]

Supply Network.name: Supply Network
Supply Network.description:
The merchant establishes and maintains a network of suppliers, buyers, and information sources across multiple locations. The network provides access to goods not available on the open market, advance warning of price changes, and reliable buyers for unusual merchandise. Maintaining the network requires cultivating relationships and honoring agreements; a merchant who burns contacts finds the network closing to them. A well-run supply network is a significant asset, granting the merchant options and leverage that a lone trader cannot match.
[Merchant Trade: 32]

Monopoly Play.name: Monopoly Play
Monopoly Play.description:
The merchant corners the market on a specific good or service, controlling its supply and setting its price. Establishing a monopoly requires capital, market knowledge, and often political maneuvering to lock out competitors. Once established, a monopoly generates substantial profit and grants the merchant real influence over the parties who depend on the controlled good. Monopolies attract enemies, however: undercut competitors, resentful buyers, and authorities wary of concentrated economic power. Maintaining one is an ongoing game of leverage and vigilance.
[Merchant Trade: 51]

Merchant Prince.name: Merchant Prince
Merchant Prince.description:
The apex of commercial mastery: the merchant commands a trade empire that rivals noble houses in wealth and influence. A merchant prince moves goods, capital, and information across the entire continent, shapes regional economies through their decisions, and wields political power through the debts and dependencies they hold. Reaching this level requires decades of shrewd trade, an extensive network, and the accumulated wealth to weather any single setback. A merchant prince can fund armies, sway councils, and outlast kings, all without wielding a weapon. Their word moves markets, and their favor is courted by the powerful.
[Merchant Trade: 72]

Flattering Cut.name: Flattering Cut
Flattering Cut.description:
The stylist selects and adjusts clothing to flatter a specific person's build, coloring, and presence, noticeably improving how they are perceived. A well-styled outfit provides a charisma boost in social settings and makes strong first impressions. The technique reads the person's natural features and the impression they want to project, then dresses them accordingly. Effective for preparing oneself or an ally for an important social event, negotiation, or courtship where appearance carries weight.
[Fashion Styling: 5]

Occasion Dressing.name: Occasion Dressing
Occasion Dressing.description:
The stylist dresses a person appropriately for a specific social occasion, reading the unwritten dress codes of courts, guilds, festivals, and ceremonies. Correct occasion dressing signals belonging and respect, opening doors that improper attire would close, while a deliberate departure from convention can make a bold statement. The technique requires knowledge of local customs and the ability to interpret what an event's formality actually demands. Being perfectly dressed for the room is a subtle but real social advantage.
[Fashion Styling: 8]

Signature Look.name: Signature Look
Signature Look.description:
The stylist develops a distinctive personal style for a client that becomes part of their identity and reputation. A signature look makes the wearer instantly recognizable and memorable, reinforcing the image they want to project: dangerous, elegant, approachable, or mysterious. Once established, the look does ongoing work: people recognize and react to it before a word is spoken. The technique requires understanding the client's goals and crafting a coherent aesthetic that supports them. A strong signature look is a form of nonverbal reputation.
[Fashion Styling: 17]

Illusion of Status.name: Illusion of Status
Illusion of Status.description:
The stylist assembles an appearance that projects a social status higher than the wearer actually holds, using cut, quality signals, and carefully chosen accessories to imply wealth, rank, or authority. The illusion opens doors and earns deference that the wearer has not formally earned. It holds up to casual scrutiny but can unravel if a knowledgeable observer examines the details or the wearer's behavior contradicts the projected status. The technique is invaluable for infiltration, negotiation from a position of apparent strength, and moving through circles above one's station.
[Fashion Styling: 32]

Transformative Styling.name: Transformative Styling
Transformative Styling.description:
The stylist completely transforms a person's appearance through clothing, grooming, and presentation, to the point where they become difficult to recognize. A transformative styling can turn a rough adventurer into a refined noble, a noble into an anonymous commoner, or one persona into a wholly different one. The change is achieved entirely through mundane means, no magic, making it undetectable by magical scrying that looks for disguise enchantments. The technique is prized for infiltration, escaping recognition, and dramatic social reinvention. It requires time, materials, and a cooperative subject.
[Fashion Styling: 51]

Icon.name: Icon
Icon.description:
The ultimate expression of fashion mastery: the stylist crafts an appearance so striking and perfectly realized that the wearer becomes a cultural icon, their look imitated and their presence commanding rooms. An icon's appearance carries genuine social power, projecting an aura of authority, desirability, and significance that shapes how everyone responds to them. The styling incorporates every element (clothing, grooming, movement, accessories, and the confidence to carry it all) into a unified whole that transcends mere fashion. Achieving iconic status requires flawless taste, deep understanding of the client, and materials of the finest quality. An icon does not follow trends; they set them.
[Fashion Styling: 72]

Authenticity Check.name: Authenticity Check
Authenticity Check.description:
The appraiser distinguishes genuine ancient relics from forgeries, reproductions, and mislabeled goods. By examining materials, craftsmanship, wear patterns, and telltale signs of age, the appraiser determines whether an item is what it claims to be. This prevents costly mistakes when buying antiquities and reveals when a genuine treasure is being sold as a common trinket. The check covers most historical artifacts; extremely sophisticated forgeries or magically disguised items may require deeper examination. Essential knowledge for anyone dealing in the relic trade.
[Relic Appraisal: 5]

Provenance Tracing.name: Provenance Tracing
Provenance Tracing.description:
The appraiser reconstructs the history and origin of a relic from its physical characteristics, inscriptions, and stylistic markers. Establishing provenance reveals where an item came from, roughly when it was made, and what culture or individual produced it. This dramatically increases a relic's value and can unlock clues about related treasures, lost locations, or historical mysteries. The tracing requires broad historical knowledge and careful observation. A relic with well-documented provenance is worth far more than an identical item of unknown origin.
[Relic Appraisal: 8]

Magical Residue Reading.name: Magical Residue Reading
Magical Residue Reading.description:
The appraiser detects and interprets the traces of magic that linger in enchanted or historically significant relics. The reading reveals whether an item holds active enchantments, dormant power, or the faded imprint of magic used near it long ago. This distinguishes genuinely magical artifacts from ordinary objects and identifies the general nature of any enchantment present. Reading residue requires magical sensitivity and experience interpreting the subtle signatures different types of magic leave behind. It is the first step in safely handling any potentially dangerous relic.
[Relic Appraisal: 17]

Curse Detection.name: Curse Detection
Curse Detection.description:
The appraiser identifies cursed and dangerous relics before they can harm the bearer. Many ancient artifacts carry protective curses, binding enchantments, or malevolent influences that activate when the item is taken or used. Curse detection reveals the presence and general nature of such dangers, allowing the appraiser to warn against handling the item or to prepare appropriate countermeasures. The detection covers most curses; exceptionally subtle or divinely-placed curses may evade a first examination. This skill has saved countless treasure hunters from grim fates.
[Relic Appraisal: 32]

Relic Attunement.name: Relic Attunement
Relic Attunement.description:
The appraiser safely awakens and attunes a dormant magical relic, unlocking its powers for a chosen bearer. Many ancient artifacts arrive inert, their abilities sealed by time, protective measures, or the loss of their activation methods. Relic attunement reads the item deeply enough to determine how to safely awaken it and bind it to a wielder without triggering defensive curses or overloading the bearer. The process requires deep understanding of the relic's nature and considerable care. A botched attunement can destroy the relic or harm the would-be bearer.
[Relic Appraisal: 51]

Legend Reader.name: Legend Reader
Legend Reader.description:
The supreme mastery of relic lore: the appraiser can read the complete history and full potential of any artifact, no matter how ancient or obscure. Holding a legendary relic, the Legend Reader perceives its origin, every hand that held it, the deeds accomplished with it, its true powers, and the conditions required to unlock them fully. This knowledge is invaluable for wielding world-shaping artifacts safely and completely. The reading strains the appraiser's mind, drawing on both scholarship and a near-supernatural sensitivity to the echoes objects carry. Only a few living scholars possess this ability, and their counsel is sought by kings and heroes alike.
[Relic Appraisal: 72]

Trained Eye.name: Trained Eye
Trained Eye.description:
The treasure seeker spots valuables that others overlook: a glint of gold in the mud, an unusual stone among ordinary rocks, a concealed compartment in old furniture. The trained eye reduces the chance of walking past hidden wealth and increases the yield from any location worth searching. The skill applies to ruins, dungeons, markets, and anywhere valuables might be hidden or discarded. It does not detect magically concealed treasure, but it catches everything a sharp, experienced scavenger would notice on careful inspection.
[Treasure Seeking: 5]

Cache Sense.name: Cache Sense
Cache Sense.description:
The treasure seeker develops an instinct for where people hide things. Loose floorboards, false-bottomed drawers, buried strongboxes, hollow walls, and other common hiding spots draw the seeker's attention. The sense is built on understanding how people think when they conceal valuables, letting the seeker check the right places first instead of searching blindly. Particularly effective in dwellings, camps, and any location where an owner might have stashed something. Clever or paranoid hiders who use unconventional spots are harder to predict.
[Treasure Seeking: 8]

Ruin Reading.name: Ruin Reading
Ruin Reading.description:
The treasure seeker reads the layout and history of ruins and dungeons to identify where treasure is most likely to be found. Understanding how a place was used (where the vault would have been, where the wealthy lived, where valuables would have been stored or lost) turns aimless exploration into a directed search. The reading draws on knowledge of architecture, history, and human behavior. In a large ruin, this skill is the difference between finding the treasure vault and wandering empty corridors until supplies run out.
[Treasure Seeking: 17]

Trap Awareness.name: Trap Awareness
Trap Awareness.description:
The treasure seeker detects the traps and defenses that guard valuable caches. Pressure plates, tripwires, magical wards, poison needles, and collapsing floors are spotted before they trigger, allowing the seeker to disarm or avoid them. The awareness comes from experience with how treasure is protected and an eye for the subtle signs of a trap's presence. It covers most mechanical and common magical traps; exotic or unique defenses may still surprise a careless seeker. This skill keeps treasure hunters alive long enough to enjoy their finds.
[Treasure Seeking: 32]

Vault Cracking.name: Vault Cracking
Vault Cracking.description:
The treasure seeker opens sealed vaults, locked chests, and protected caches that resist conventional access. Combining lockpicking, mechanism analysis, and knowledge of how vaults are secured, the seeker works through layered defenses to reach what lies within. Complex vaults may require identifying and defeating multiple locks, wards, and puzzles in the correct sequence. The technique requires patience, tools, and a cool head, as many vaults punish mistakes. A master vault cracker can reach treasure that has defeated every seeker before them.
[Treasure Seeking: 51]

Seeker's Fortune.name: Seeker's Fortune
Seeker's Fortune.description:
The ultimate treasure-seeking mastery, bordering on the supernatural: the seeker develops an uncanny intuition that draws them toward significant treasure. Standing at a crossroads or entering a ruin, the seeker feels a pull toward the direction that holds the greatest reward, as though fortune itself guides their steps. The favor does not reveal exact locations but consistently steers the seeker toward the richest finds and away from empty risk. It cannot be forced and works best when the seeker trusts the instinct. Legendary treasure hunters are said to possess this gift, finding hoards that others searched for lifetimes and never located.
[Treasure Seeking: 72]

Clean Harvest.name: Clean Harvest
Clean Harvest.description:
The harvester extracts materials from a defeated monster without damaging or contaminating them, yielding higher-quality components than rough butchery. Clean-harvested hides, fangs, scales, and organs retain their full value and any inherent properties. The technique requires knowing each creature's anatomy well enough to cut precisely and avoid rupturing valuable glands or staining usable materials. A clean harvest can double the value of what a careless harvester would recover, and it preserves rare components that rough handling destroys.
[Monster Harvesting: 5]

Essence Extraction.name: Essence Extraction
Essence Extraction.description:
The harvester extracts the concentrated magical essence from a monster's body: the mana core, elemental gland, or spirit residue that gives the creature its supernatural properties. Extracted essence is a potent crafting ingredient for alchemy, enchanting, and cooking. The extraction must be performed soon after the creature falls, before the essence dissipates, and requires proper containment vessels. Different monster types yield different essences, each valuable for different applications. Skilled extraction recovers essence that unskilled harvesting loses entirely.
[Monster Harvesting: 8]

Rare Component Recovery.name: Rare Component Recovery
Rare Component Recovery.description:
The harvester recovers the rare and valuable components that most monsters yield only occasionally: a beast's crystallized heart, an intact venom sac, a flawless scale, a dragon's whisker. These components are the difference between an ordinary harvest and a lucrative one, and they are required for high-tier crafting recipes. Recovery requires knowing where these components form, how to identify a specimen worth harvesting, and the delicate technique to extract them intact. Even skilled harvesters do not recover rare components every time, but they recover them far more often than the untrained.
[Monster Harvesting: 17]

Toxin Milking.name: Toxin Milking
Toxin Milking.description:
The harvester safely extracts venom, poison, acid, and other toxic substances from monsters, whether living or freshly slain. Milked toxins are valuable ingredients for poison craft, alchemy, and weapon coating, and some are worth more than the rest of the creature combined. The technique requires precise handling to avoid self-poisoning and proper containment to preserve the toxin's potency. Milking from a living, restrained creature yields renewable supply; milking from a corpse is one-time. Different creatures produce different toxins, each with distinct applications and dangers.
[Monster Harvesting: 32]

Trophy Preservation.name: Trophy Preservation
Trophy Preservation.description:
The harvester preserves impressive monster parts as trophies and functional materials that retain their properties indefinitely. A preserved dragon skull, an intact chimera hide, or a mounted apex-predator head serves as proof of a great hunt, a valuable trade good, and sometimes a functional item retaining the creature's magical qualities. The preservation process halts decay and locks in whatever properties the part held at harvest. The technique requires specialized reagents and considerable skill; a poorly-preserved trophy rots or loses its magical qualities over time.
[Monster Harvesting: 51]

Perfect Specimen.name: Perfect Specimen
Perfect Specimen.description:
The pinnacle of monster harvesting: the harvester recovers a legendary creature's body with such perfection that nearly every component is preserved at maximum quality, including materials that are normally lost or destroyed in any ordinary harvest. From a single perfect specimen, the harvester can supply materials for multiple legendary-tier crafts, dragonhide for armor, dragon bone for weapons, dragon essence for enchantment, dragon blood for alchemy, all recovered intact. Achieving a perfect harvest requires flawless technique, deep anatomical knowledge of even the rarest creatures, and hours of meticulous work on a fresh specimen. A perfectly harvested legendary monster is worth a fortune and enables crafting that lesser materials cannot support.
[Monster Harvesting: 72]

Vein Attunement.name: Vein Attunement
Vein Attunement.description:
The prospector detects crystal formations through subtle environmental cues: faint mana shimmer, temperature variations, the particular way light bends near buried deposits. Crystal sense reveals the presence and rough location of crystal veins that would otherwise require blind digging to find. The sense works best in crystal-rich environments like caverns and ley-line intersections. It does not pinpoint exact locations or reveal crystal quality, but it turns aimless prospecting into a directed search, dramatically improving the odds of a find.
[Crystal Prospecting: 5]

Purity Assessment.name: Purity Assessment
Purity Assessment.description:
The prospector evaluates the purity and quality of raw crystals in the field, distinguishing valuable specimens from flawed or worthless ones before investing effort in extraction. The assessment reads internal clarity, structural integrity, and mana saturation. This prevents wasting time on crystals that will shatter during extraction or prove too impure for crafting use, and it flags the rare high-purity specimens worth extra care. Accurate purity assessment is what separates a profitable prospecting run from a load of useless rock.
[Crystal Prospecting: 8]

Resonance Mapping.name: Resonance Mapping
Resonance Mapping.description:
The prospector maps the resonance patterns of a crystal deposit to understand its full extent and structure before extraction. By tapping the crystals and reading the harmonic response, the prospector determines how deep the vein runs, where the largest and purest specimens lie, and where the formation is unstable. This knowledge maximizes yield and prevents the collapses and shatterings that destroy careless prospectors' finds. Resonance mapping is essential for working the large, valuable deposits that reward systematic extraction over opportunistic chipping.
[Crystal Prospecting: 17]

Charged Crystal Harvest.name: Charged Crystal Harvest
Charged Crystal Harvest.description:
The prospector safely extracts mana-charged crystals that hold volatile magical energy, without triggering the discharge that destroys both crystal and prospector. Mana crystals are prized for enchanting, spellcasting focuses, and magical device construction, but their stored energy makes them dangerous to harvest. The extraction requires reading the crystal's charge state, discharging excess energy safely, and cutting the specimen free without cracking its structure. Properly extracted mana crystals are among the most valuable prospecting yields, and the technique is what makes harvesting them viable at all.
[Crystal Prospecting: 32]

Geode Mastery.name: Geode Mastery
Geode Mastery.description:
The prospector locates and opens geodes and crystal pockets to recover the pristine formations hidden within. Sealed geodes protect their crystals from weathering and contamination, meaning the specimens inside are often of exceptional quality, but opening one without shattering its contents requires precise technique. The prospector reads the geode's structure to find the natural fault line and opens it cleanly. Geode mastery yields some of the finest crystal specimens available, including rare formations that grow only in the sealed environment of a geode's interior.
[Crystal Prospecting: 51]

Heartcrystal Harvest.name: Heartcrystal Harvest
Heartcrystal Harvest.description:
The supreme achievement of crystal prospecting: the prospector locates and extracts heartcrystals, the rare primordial formations that grow at the core of ancient ley-line convergences and hold immense concentrated magical power. A single heartcrystal can power a legendary enchantment, serve as the focus of a world-class magical device, or fuel rituals beyond the reach of ordinary materials. Finding one requires an almost mystical attunement to the deep currents of the world's magic, and extracting it intact demands flawless technique, as the slightest error shatters the crystal or unleashes its stored energy catastrophically. Heartcrystals are so rare that most prospectors never see one in a lifetime of searching.
[Crystal Prospecting: 72]

Void-Cutting Edge.name: Void-Cutting Edge
Void-Cutting Edge.description:
A strike honed to such perfection that it cuts the space between the blade and its target, ignoring distance within a few meters. The cut lands before the swing appears to complete. Bypasses conventional parry timing and shield positioning. The spatial precision required means a single lapse in focus causes the cut to miss entirely, striking empty air.
[Swordsmanship: 79]

Mind's Eye Severance.name: Mind's Eye Severance
Mind's Eye Severance.description:
The swordsman enters a state of total combat clarity where they perceive the ideal cutting line through any defense a fraction of a second before executing it. Attacks flow into openings that have not yet appeared. Provides a large accuracy and critical bonus for several turns, but the mental intensity is exhausting and cannot be sustained back-to-back.
[Swordsmanship: 84]

Heaven-and-Earth Cleave.name: Heaven-and-Earth Cleave
Heaven-and-Earth Cleave.description:
A two-stroke technique that cuts once along the vertical and once along the horizontal in a single fluid motion, forming a cross of severing force that few defenses can cover simultaneously. The strike can cleave through magical barriers and reinforced armor. Committing to both strokes leaves the swordsman fully extended and open on the recovery.
[Swordsmanship: 89]

Formless Blade Sovereignty.name: Formless Blade Sovereignty
Formless Blade Sovereignty.description:
The swordsman transcends technique itself, their blade answering intent directly without the intermediary of a named form. Every cut is generated in the moment, unpredictable and unblockable by pattern-reading defenses. Grants mastery-tier accuracy and evasion while active. The state requires perfect calm; pain, fear, or rage collapses it instantly.
[Swordsmanship: 95]

One Sword, All Things.name: One Sword, All Things
One Sword, All Things.description:
The absolute summit of the blade. For a handful of heartbeats the swordsman and the sword become a single principle of severance, and everything within reach (matter, energy, barrier, even the concept of an obstacle) parts before the edge. A single stroke can end a legend or split a fortress gate. The spiritual and physical cost is annihilating; afterward the swordsman is left hollowed and defenseless, and the technique can be called upon only once in a great while.
[Swordsmanship: 100]

Piercing Volley.name: Piercing Volley
Piercing Volley.description:
The archer looses a rapid succession of shots at overwhelming speed, each drawn and released faster than a normal archer can nock a single arrow. The volley suppresses groups and forces spellcasters out of their casting rhythm. Accuracy per shot is lower than an aimed release, but the sheer volume finds gaps. Empties the quiver fast.
[Archery: 58]

Homing Shot.name: Homing Shot
Homing Shot.description:
An arrow released with such refined spatial sense that it curves in flight to track a moving or partially-covered target. The archer reads the target's momentum and bends the shot around intervening cover. Effective against evasive and fast targets who rely on breaking line of sight. Requires an unobstructed initial release and cannot correct around solid walls.
[Archery: 65]

Storm of Arrows.name: Storm of Arrows
Storm of Arrows.description:
The archer looses a single arrow enchanted with their own fighting spirit that splits mid-flight into a descending rain of spectral copies, blanketing an area in projectiles. All targets in the zone take piercing damage. The technique consumes only one physical arrow but drains stamina heavily, and the spectral copies dissipate on contact with anti-magic fields.
[Archery: 74]

Heartpiercer.name: Heartpiercer
Heartpiercer.description:
A single perfectly-aimed shot that reads the target's movement, breathing, and armor gaps to slip an arrow directly into a vital point. Deals catastrophic single-target damage and suppresses healing on the wound for several turns. The aim requires three seconds of stillness and a clear line; the archer is exposed during the draw and the shot can be interrupted.
[Archery: 82]

Skyfall Barrage.name: Skyfall Barrage
Skyfall Barrage.description:
The archer arcs dozens of shots high into the air to descend on a wide area like falling rain, striking targets who believe themselves safe behind cover or at extreme range. The barrage covers a large zone and ignores frontal shields. Requires open sky above and a moment to establish the firing arc; useless indoors or under heavy canopy.
[Archery: 91]

Arrow That Splits the Heavens.name: Arrow That Splits the Heavens
Arrow That Splits the Heavens.description:
The legendary shot. The archer pours everything into a single release that crosses any distance in an instant, unerring and unstoppable, punching through barriers, armor, and defensive magic as though they were mist. The arrow does not miss and cannot be blocked by conventional means. The draw disables the archer's arms for the rest of the engagement, and only a bow and archer of the highest caliber can survive the strain of loosing it.
[Archery: 100]

Rapid Fusillade.name: Rapid Fusillade
Rapid Fusillade.description:
A disciplined burst of rapid, accurate shots that keeps a target or group suppressed and off-balance. The shooter manages recoil and reload rhythm to maintain fire without sacrificing precision. Effective for pinning enemies and interrupting actions. Consumes ammunition quickly and requires a firearm in good condition; a fouled barrel jams under sustained fire.
[Firearms: 55]

Impossible Shot.name: Impossible Shot
Impossible Shot.description:
A precision shot that exploits ricochets, weak points, and improbable angles to hit targets behind cover or to disarm rather than kill. The shooter reads the environment for bounce surfaces and vulnerable spots. Enables non-lethal takedowns and shots that bypass shields. Requires a clear read of the geometry; open ground with no surfaces limits the trick options.
[Firearms: 63]

Deadeye Focus.name: Deadeye Focus
Deadeye Focus.description:
The shooter enters a state of perfect concentration where time seems to slow and every shot finds its mark. For several turns, accuracy is dramatically elevated and shots strike vital points automatically. The focus is mentally taxing and cannot be maintained indefinitely; when it breaks, the shooter suffers a wave of fatigue and reduced accuracy.
[Firearms: 72]

Armor-Piercing Round.name: Armor-Piercing Round
Armor-Piercing Round.description:
A specially-aimed shot channeling the shooter's skill into a single round that punches clean through armor, cover, and even multiple aligned targets. The shot ignores most physical defenses and deals heavy damage to everything in its path. Requires careful setup and a heavy-caliber firearm; light weapons cannot handle the technique and the recoil staggers the shooter.
[Firearms: 81]

Bullet Hell.name: Bullet Hell
Bullet Hell.description:
The shooter unleashes an overwhelming barrage that fills the air with lead, creating a lethal zone that shreds anything within it. The technique combines impossible fire rate with area coverage, leaving few safe angles. Devastating against groups and fast targets alike. Burns through an enormous quantity of ammunition and overheats all but the finest firearms.
[Firearms: 90]

The Final Shot.name: The Final Shot
The Final Shot.description:
The ultimate expression of gunmanship. The shooter takes a single breath, and in the stillness fires one round that carries their entire will. The shot crosses any distance instantly, ignores all conventional defense, and strikes with force enough to fell the mightiest foe. Time seems to stop for the pull of the trigger. The recoil and spiritual toll leave the shooter unable to fire again for the rest of the battle, and only a master with a peerless weapon can loose it without shattering their own hands.
[Firearms: 100]

Perfect Riposte.name: Perfect Riposte
Perfect Riposte.description:
The duelist reads an incoming attack and answers it with a counter so precise it turns the opponent's own force against them. A successful riposte deals bonus damage and briefly staggers the attacker. The technique requires the opponent to commit to an attack first; against a purely defensive foe it has nothing to counter.
[Dueling: 28]

Blade Bind.name: Blade Bind
Blade Bind.description:
The duelist traps the opponent's weapon with their own through precise leverage and pressure, locking it out of play for a critical moment. While bound, the opponent cannot attack or fully defend, and the duelist can strike or reposition. Strength and skill contest the bind; a much stronger opponent can force free. Only works blade-to-blade.
[Dueling: 40]

Duelist's Tempo.name: Duelist's Tempo
Duelist's Tempo.description:
The duelist seizes control of the exchange's rhythm, dictating the pace so completely that the opponent is always reacting, never initiating. For several turns the duelist gains initiative and a significant bonus to both offense and defense against a single chosen opponent. The control applies to one duel partner only; additional attackers break the tempo.
[Dueling: 53]

Killing Stroke.name: Killing Stroke
Killing Stroke.description:
A single decisive thrust delivered into an opening the duelist has patiently created through prior exchanges. Deals massive damage scaled to how many exchanges preceded it: a duelist who has read their opponent for several turns lands a near-fatal blow. Requires the setup; thrown out early, it is merely a strong attack.
[Dueling: 67]

Sword Saint's Presence.name: Sword Saint's Presence
Sword Saint's Presence.description:
The duelist projects such absolute mastery that opponents feel the futility of attacking before they commit. Lesser fighters hesitate, their strikes losing conviction. Against a single elite opponent it manifests as a battle of pure skill where the duelist reads every intention. Provides mastery-tier bonuses in single combat but does little against overwhelming numbers.
[Dueling: 83]

Unconquered.name: Unconquered
Unconquered.description:
The pinnacle of the duel. The duelist enters a state where, one-on-one, they simply cannot be defeated by any attack they can perceive: every strike is parried, every opening exploited, every feint seen through. For the duration of a single duel they are functionally untouchable by a foe of comparable or lesser mastery. The state demands total focus on one opponent; a second attacker, an area effect, or a broken concentration ends it, and the toll leaves the duelist drained for hours.
[Dueling: 100]

Bulwark Stance.name: Bulwark Stance
Bulwark Stance.description:
The shield-bearer roots into an immovable defensive posture, becoming a wall that protects both themselves and allies directly behind them. Incoming attacks are caught or deflected, and the bearer holds ground against forced movement, at the price of mobility: no pursuing, no repositioning. The stance protects on the turn you take it; holding it takes your action again each turn.
[Shield Combat: 39]

Shield Bash Combo.name: Shield Bash Combo
Shield Bash Combo.description:
A sequence of aggressive shield strikes that stagger and disorient the opponent, opening them for follow-up attacks. Each bash builds pressure, and a fully-connected combo leaves the target reeling. Effective for breaking an enemy's rhythm and creating openings for allies. Heavy shields deal more stagger; light shields are faster but gentler.
[Shield Combat: 49]

Aegis Ward.name: Aegis Ward
Aegis Ward.description:
The bearer raises their shield and channels their protective will into a barrier that extends beyond the shield's physical edge, guarding a wide arc against both physical and magical attacks. Allies within the arc share the protection. Holding it is exhausting work, and it drops if the bearer is knocked from their stance. It guards the arc on the turn you raise it; holding it takes your action again each turn.
[Shield Combat: 60]

Guardian's Retribution.name: Guardian's Retribution
Guardian's Retribution.description:
The bearer absorbs an incoming attack with their shield and instantly converts the blocked force into a devastating counterstrike. The more powerful the attack blocked, the harder the retribution hits. Requires precise timing to catch the attack cleanly; a mistimed block takes the hit without the counter. Turns an enemy's strongest blow into their undoing.
[Shield Combat: 73]

Immovable Fortress.name: Immovable Fortress
Immovable Fortress.description:
The bearer becomes an absolute anchor point on the battlefield, utterly unmovable and nearly impervious to frontal assault: attacks from the front are reduced to almost nothing, and the bearer can shield an entire cluster of allies. The fortress cannot advance; it holds a line, and attacks from the flanks or above bypass the frontal protection. It guards you and the allies behind you on the turn you take it; holding it takes your action again each turn.
[Shield Combat: 86]

Wall of the World.name: Wall of the World
Wall of the World.description:
The ultimate shield technique. The bearer plants themselves and raises a barrier of pure protective conviction that can hold back forces meant to level cities: a dragon's breath, a collapsing structure, an army's charge. While it stands, nothing passes the wall and the allies behind it are utterly safe. Holding it drains the bearer's very life force; sustaining it too long is fatal, and it can be raised only when everything is on the line. It guards everyone behind you on the turn you raise it; holding it takes your action again each turn.
[Shield Combat: 100]

Flowing Palm Style.name: Flowing Palm Style
Flowing Palm Style.description:
A martial form built on redirection, where the fighter uses circular motion to turn an opponent's force against them, deflecting attacks and unbalancing the attacker. Effective against stronger opponents whose own momentum becomes a liability. The style rewards patience and reading; a fighter who forces the tempo loses its advantages.
[Unarmed Combat: 25]

Pressure Point Strike.name: Pressure Point Strike
Pressure Point Strike.description:
A precise strike to a nerve cluster or vital point that produces effects far beyond the force applied: numbing a limb, disrupting balance, or briefly paralyzing. Requires intimate anatomical knowledge and a clean hit on an exposed point. Armored targets and non-humanoid creatures with unusual anatomy resist or negate the effect.
[Unarmed Combat: 35]

Iron Body.name: Iron Body
Iron Body.description:
The fighter conditions and channels their inner force to make their body as hard as steel, shrugging off blows that would break bone and striking with the force of a hammer. For several turns, physical damage taken is sharply reduced and unarmed strikes deal heavily increased damage. The technique drains stamina and cannot be held indefinitely.
[Unarmed Combat: 50]

Hundred Fist Rush.name: Hundred Fist Rush
Hundred Fist Rush.description:
A blindingly fast flurry of strikes delivered faster than the eye can follow, overwhelming an opponent's guard through sheer volume. Each impact is individually modest but the cumulative barrage is devastating. The rush burns stamina at a punishing rate and leaves the fighter briefly winded; against a patient defender who weathers it, the recovery window is dangerous.
[Unarmed Combat: 65]

Spirit Fist.name: Spirit Fist
Spirit Fist.description:
The fighter channels their inner energy through their strikes, projecting force beyond physical contact: a punch that lands as a concussive wave, a palm strike that ripples through armor to the body beneath. Ignores conventional armor and can strike at short range without contact. The energy expenditure is severe and each projection taxes the fighter's reserves.
[Unarmed Combat: 80]

Fist That Shatters Heaven.name: Fist That Shatters Heaven
Fist That Shatters Heaven.description:
The summit of the martial path. The fighter concentrates a lifetime of discipline into a single blow that carries force enough to crater the earth and stagger mythic beings. The strike ignores armor, barriers, and resistance, delivering pure annihilating impact. The recoil courses back through the fighter's own body, leaving them broken and spent; the technique can be attempted only once in a great while, and a lesser body cannot survive throwing it at all.
[Unarmed Combat: 100]

Umbral Approach.name: Umbral Approach
Umbral Approach.description:
The fighter closes distance in a blur, appearing at the target's blind spot to deliver a strike before they can react. Excellent for opening from stealth or punishing a distracted foe. The approach requires a moment of unobserved movement; a target with full awareness of the fighter's position can track and counter the step.
[Dagger Fighting: 38]

Twin Fang.name: Twin Fang
Twin Fang.description:
A rapid two-blade combination that strikes high and low simultaneously, forcing the opponent to defend two lines at once and usually failing to cover both. Deals combined damage and can inflict bleeding. Requires a blade in each hand; a single-dagger fighter cannot execute the dual-line attack.
[Dagger Fighting: 56]

Assassin's Flow.name: Assassin's Flow
Assassin's Flow.description:
The fighter enters a state of lethal fluidity, flowing between targets and strikes without pause, each kill or wound feeding into the next movement. For several turns, striking a target grants a burst of speed toward the next. Devastating against groups of weaker foes. The flow breaks if the fighter is forced to stop or is significantly wounded.
[Dagger Fighting: 66]

Vital Rupture.name: Vital Rupture
Vital Rupture.description:
A surgically precise strike into an organ or major vessel that inflicts a catastrophic, rapidly-worsening wound. The target hemorrhages and their combat ability degrades each turn until treated. Requires an opening at a vital point, easiest to find from a flank or against a distracted foe. Constructs and undead are immune.
[Dagger Fighting: 77]

Thousand Shadows.name: Thousand Shadows
Thousand Shadows.description:
The fighter moves so fast between strikes that they appear to occupy several positions at once, a swarm of afterimages closing on the target from every angle. Only one image is real, but the target cannot tell which until the blades land. Overwhelms defensive reactions. True-sight and spiritual perception can pick the real body from the shadows.
[Dagger Fighting: 88]

Death's Whisper.name: Death's Whisper
Death's Whisper.description:
The ultimate assassination art. The fighter erases their presence so completely, footstep, breath, heartbeat, even killing intent, that they become imperceptible for a single approach, materializing at the target's throat with a blade already moving. Against any target with a vital anatomy the strike is lethal. The technique demands perfect conditions and total spiritual silence; it can be attempted only once per engagement, and any prior detection of the fighter dispels the whisper before it begins.
[Dagger Fighting: 100]

Blazing Lance.name: Blazing Lance
Blazing Lance.description:
A concentrated spear of fire hurled with force enough to punch through light barriers and armor. More focused than a fireball, trading area for penetration and single-target damage. Effective against armored foes and shielded casters. Fire-resistant and aquatic targets shrug off much of the heat.
[Fire Magic: 63]

Rebirth Flame.name: Rebirth Flame
Rebirth Flame.description:
The caster wreathes themselves or an ally in restorative fire that burns away wounds and afflictions while searing anything that strikes them. The flame heals over several turns and punishes melee attackers. Its dual nature makes it costly; sustaining the phoenix flame drains mana rapidly, and water magic can quench it.
[Fire Magic: 77]

Hellfire Cascade.name: Hellfire Cascade
Hellfire Cascade.description:
The caster calls down a cascade of black flame that burns hotter than ordinary fire and resists being extinguished by mundane means. It sears through fire resistance that would blunt lesser flames and continues burning even underwater for a time. The forbidden intensity of the flame draws divine and infernal attention, and mishandling it can burn the caster.
[Fire Magic: 85]

Sunfire Incarnation.name: Sunfire Incarnation
Sunfire Incarnation.description:
The caster becomes a living conflagration, their body wreathed in solar flame that incinerates all who approach and lets them hurl bolts of star-hot fire. For the duration, the caster's fire magic is vastly amplified and their touch is lethal. The transformation consumes enormous mana and generates heat that endangers allies and flammable surroundings alike.
[Fire Magic: 92]

Ragnarok Ember.name: Ragnarok Ember
Ragnarok Ember.description:
The apocalypse of flame. The caster gathers the fury of a dying star into a single point and releases it as a cataclysm that can reduce an army, a fortress, or a monster of legend to ash. Nothing short of divine protection or absolute fire immunity survives the epicenter. Casting it empties the mage's reserves utterly and scorches the land for a long time after; it can be unleashed only when the world itself is at stake.
[Fire Magic: 100]

Radiant Lance.name: Radiant Lance
Radiant Lance.description:
A focused beam of holy light that pierces through darkness and undead flesh alike. Deals heavy damage to shadow-aligned and undead targets and can dispel minor darkness effects. Living, light-aligned targets take reduced damage. The beam requires a clear line to the target and is dimmed by heavy magical darkness.
[Light Magic: 72]

Sanctuary.name: Sanctuary
Sanctuary.description:
The caster raises a dome of protective light that shields allies within from harm and mends their wounds. Hostile creatures find it difficult to enter, and undead are actively repelled. The sanctuary is stationary and drains mana; the caster must remain to sustain it. It guards everyone inside on the turn you raise it; sustaining it takes your action again each turn.
[Light Magic: 78]

Judgment Ray.name: Judgment Ray
Judgment Ray.description:
A pillar of searing divine light called down upon a target, dealing massive damage that scales against the target's malevolence: devastating to the corrupt, the undead, and the demonic. Pure or innocent targets take little harm. The ray requires a moment to call down and open sky or ceiling; it cannot be summoned deep underground without a conduit.
[Divinity: 80]

Aegis of Dawn.name: Aegis of Dawn
Aegis of Dawn.description:
The caster clads an ally in radiant armor that turns aside blows and burns those who strike it. The armored ally gains significant defense and reflects a portion of melee damage back as holy fire. The blessing is potent but costly, and its light makes stealth impossible for the wearer.
[Light Magic: 85]

Heaven's Descent.name: Heaven's Descent
Heaven's Descent.description:
The caster opens a channel to the divine, calling down a wave of overwhelming light that heals and empowers allies while scouring enemies from the field. Undead and demonic forces are annihilated; corrupted terrain is purified. The channel demands immense mana and pure intent; a caster with a stained heart cannot complete it.
[Light Magic: 93]

Genesis Light.name: Genesis Light
Genesis Light.description:
The first and final light. The caster becomes a vessel for creation's own radiance, unleashing a dawn that can banish the deepest curse, resurrect the freshly fallen, and unmake any creature of darkness in an instant. The light rewrites corruption back to purity across a vast area. Channeling it burns through the caster's life force and can be done only in a moment of absolute need; the divine attention it draws is not lightly courted.
[Light Magic: 100]

Umbral Blades.name: Umbral Blades
Umbral Blades.description:
The caster conjures blades of solid shadow that strike from the darkness at multiple targets. The blades ignore a portion of physical armor by slipping through shadow rather than cutting through matter. Effective in darkness and dim light; bright illumination weakens the blades and reveals their trajectory.
[Shadow Magic: 69]

Shadowmeld.name: Shadowmeld
Shadowmeld.description:
The caster sinks into the shadows, becoming nearly invisible and able to move through darkness undetected while striking from concealment. Grants powerful stealth and ambush bonuses in shadowed environments. Bright light forces the caster out of the meld, and creatures with darkvision or magical detection can perceive them.
[Shadow Magic: 76]

Nightmare Grasp.name: Nightmare Grasp
Nightmare Grasp.description:
Tendrils of living shadow erupt to seize and constrict targets, dealing damage and instilling supernatural dread that saps their courage and resolve. Bound targets struggle to act as fear grips them. Creatures immune to fear resist the psychological component but are still physically restrained. Bright light severs the tendrils.
[Shadow Magic: 84]

Total Eclipse.name: Total Eclipse
Total Eclipse.description:
The caster smothers an area in absolute darkness that even magical light struggles to pierce, blinding enemies while the caster and shadow-attuned allies see clearly within. Enemy accuracy plummets and spellcasting falters in the dark. The eclipse drains mana to maintain and can be dispelled by sufficiently powerful light magic.
[Shadow Magic: 92]

Void Shroud.name: Void Shroud
Void Shroud.description:
The caster wraps themselves in a mantle of primordial darkness that devours incoming attacks and magic, and lets them strike with shadow that erodes whatever it touches. For the duration, the caster is wreathed in a hungry dark that consumes light, energy, and lesser spells. The shroud feeds on the caster's own vitality to sustain its appetite.
[Void Magic: 81]

Umbral Oblivion.name: Umbral Oblivion
Umbral Oblivion.description:
The deepest dark. The caster tears open a rent to the primordial shadow that existed before the first light, drowning a vast area in a darkness that unmakes what it touches: matter, magic, even memory fading at its edges. Foes caught within are erased; barriers dissolve. The abyss it channels is not fully controllable, and calling it risks the caster being consumed by the very void they opened. A weapon of last resort.
[Shadow Magic: 100]

Curse Bolt.name: Curse Bolt
Curse Bolt.description:
A bolt of malevolent energy that damages the target and layers a weakening curse: reduced strength, slowed reflexes, or fading vitality. The curse lingers until dispelled or it runs its course. Targets with strong willpower or magical warding resist the curse's onset, taking only the direct damage.
[Dark Magic: 67]

Life Drain.name: Life Drain
Life Drain.description:
The caster siphons vitality from a target, damaging them while healing themselves. The transfer is efficient against living creatures and useless against constructs and undead, which have no life to take. Overuse leaves a corrupting residue on the caster that perceptive holy magic can detect.
[Dark Magic: 75]

Plague Cloud.name: Plague Cloud
Plague Cloud.description:
The caster releases a cloud of virulent dark energy that sickens and weakens all enemies within, spreading debilitating affliction that worsens each turn. The cloud lingers and drifts, endangering anyone who enters. The caster is not immune without separate protection, and holy or purifying magic disperses the plague.
[Dark Magic: 83]

Soul Chains.name: Soul Chains
Soul Chains.description:
The caster binds a target's soul with chains of dark power, immobilizing them and slowly crushing their will and vitality. Bound targets cannot flee and weaken each turn. Escaping requires overpowering the caster's will or severing the chains with holy magic. Extremely powerful souls can resist the binding entirely.
[Soul Magic: 65]

Deathly Dominion.name: Deathly Dominion
Deathly Dominion.description:
The caster establishes an area of morbid power where death magic is amplified, the wounded weaken faster, and the caster can raise the freshly fallen as temporary servants. Within the dominion the caster's dark magic reaches its peak. The forbidden nature of the domain draws the ire of the Church and the attention of things better left undisturbed.
[Dark Magic: 91]

Grave of All Things.name: Grave of All Things
Grave of All Things.description:
The ultimate dark art, a spell the academies refuse to teach. The caster speaks a word of ending that reaches into everything living within a vast radius and commands it toward death, withering flesh, halting hearts, and unmaking vitality itself. Only the strongest wills and the divinely protected endure it. The magic feeds on the caster's own soul to pay its price, and each casting carves away a piece of them that never returns.
[Dark Magic: 100]

Element Braiding.name: Element Braiding
Element Braiding.description:
The caster combines two elements into a hybrid effect greater than either alone: steam from fire and water, magnetized storm from earth and lightning, freezing mist from water and wind. The fusion exploits the target's resistances by attacking through an unexpected combination. Requires command of both component elements.
[Elemental Magic: 55]

Primal Surge.name: Primal Surge
Primal Surge.description:
The caster channels raw elemental force through their body, empowering all their elemental spells for several turns with increased damage and reduced cost. The surge is versatile, benefiting whatever element the caster wields. Holding the surge strains the caster's channels; when it ends, they suffer a period of magical fatigue.
[Elemental Magic: 63]

Elemental Avatar.name: Elemental Avatar
Elemental Avatar.description:
The caster partially transforms into an elemental being of their chosen element, gaining resistance to that element, enhanced elemental attacks, and elemental movement: flowing like water, drifting like wind, enduring like stone. The avatar form drains mana continuously and is vulnerable to its opposing element while active.
[Elemental Magic: 72]

Convergence of Elements.name: Convergence of Elements
Convergence of Elements.description:
The caster draws all elemental forces into perfect balance around themselves, becoming a nexus that can reshape the battlefield: raising walls of stone, flooding the field, calling storms, and igniting the air with a thought. For the duration, the caster commands the environment itself. The convergence is exhausting and cannot be sustained beyond a few decisive turns.
[Elemental Magic: 90]

Genesis of the Elements.name: Genesis of the Elements
Genesis of the Elements.description:
The primordial working. The caster reaches back to the source from which all elements sprang and briefly wields creation's raw material, able to remake a swath of the world: turning sea to land, calling mountains from plains, summoning an elemental cataclysm that reshapes the region. The power is barely containable in a mortal frame; channeling it burns the caster hollow and can be attempted only once in a very long while, when nothing less will suffice.
[Elemental Magic: 100]

Arcane Barrage.name: Arcane Barrage
Arcane Barrage.description:
The caster fires a rapid volley of pure arcane missiles that unerringly strike their targets, ignoring cover and minor evasion. The missiles split among multiple foes or concentrate on one. Reliable and hard to dodge, though each missile deals modest damage. Anti-magic fields dissipate them before impact.
[Arcane Magic: 62]

Interwoven Casting.name: Interwoven Casting
Interwoven Casting.description:
The caster combines two spells into a single interwoven casting, producing effects neither could achieve alone and confounding defenses tuned to a single spell type. The weave requires deep understanding of both spells' structures; a mismatched pairing fizzles or backfires. Master casters use it to bypass specific wards.
[Arcane Magic: 69]

Arcane Surge Overload.name: Arcane Surge Overload
Arcane Surge Overload.description:
The caster deliberately pushes a spell beyond its safe limits, amplifying its power dramatically at the cost of magical backlash. The overloaded spell hits far harder than normal, but the caster takes recoil damage and risks temporary channel burnout. A calculated gamble for a decisive moment.
[Arcane Magic: 76]

Dispel Mastery.name: Dispel Mastery
Dispel Mastery.description:
The caster unravels hostile magic with surgical precision, stripping enchantments, dismissing summons, and collapsing barriers that lesser dispelling cannot touch. Against a magical opponent, it can leave them defenseless. Extremely durable or divinely-anchored magic resists even this, requiring repeated efforts to break.
[Arcane Magic: 84]

Arcane Transcendence.name: Arcane Transcendence
Arcane Transcendence.description:
The caster elevates their command of magic to a transcendent level, casting spells faster, cheaper, and stronger while perceiving the flows of magic around them with perfect clarity. For the duration, the caster operates on a higher plane of spellcraft. The ascension burns mana at a tremendous rate and drops the caster into deep exhaustion when it ends.
[Arcane Magic: 92]

Rewrite.name: Rewrite
Rewrite.description:
The forbidden apex of arcane theory. For a few heartbeats the caster edits the local rules of magic themselves: negating an element, reversing a spell's target, unmaking an enchantment as though it had never been cast, or forcing an impossible working to succeed. Reality protests, and the strain of imposing the caster's will on the fabric of magic is ruinous. It can be done only rarely, and each use leaves the caster's channels scarred.
[Arcane Magic: 100]

Frost Lance.name: Frost Lance
Frost Lance.description:
A spear of magically-hardened ice hurled with piercing force, dealing cold damage and slowing the target as frost spreads from the wound. Effective against fast targets whose speed it blunts. Fire and heat weaken the lance in flight, and fire-aligned creatures resist the chill.
[Ice Magic: 39]

Zero Point.name: Zero Point
Zero Point.description:
The caster plunges a target or small area to impossible cold, threatening to freeze foes solid where they stand. Fully frozen targets are helpless until they thaw or the ice is shattered, which deals bonus damage. High-vitality and fire-aligned targets resist the freeze, taking heavy cold damage instead. Demands significant mana.
[Ice Magic: 60]

Glacial Prison.name: Glacial Prison
Glacial Prison.description:
The caster encases a target in a thick tomb of enchanted ice that immobilizes them completely and slowly saps their warmth and strength. Breaking free requires overwhelming force or fire magic. The prison holds even powerful foes for a time, buying the caster and allies a crucial reprieve. Fire attacks free the prisoner faster.
[Ice Magic: 73]

Permafrost Domain.name: Permafrost Domain
Permafrost Domain.description:
The caster transforms the battlefield into a frozen waste where cold seeps into everything, enemies are perpetually slowed and chilled, and the caster's ice magic reaches its peak. Within the domain, the caster commands the cold absolutely. The domain drains mana continuously and can be melted at its edges by concentrated heat.
[Ice Magic: 86]

Fimbulwinter.name: Fimbulwinter
Fimbulwinter.description:
The endless winter. The caster calls down a cataclysm of absolute cold that freezes a vast region into a lifeless glacier, halting rivers, stilling the air, and entombing all who cannot resist it. The cold is deep enough to threaten mythic beings and reshape the land for a long season. Channeling it freezes the caster's own life to its edge, and only in the gravest need can such a winter be summoned.
[Ice Magic: 100]

Arc Cascade.name: Arc Cascade
Arc Cascade.description:
A bolt of lightning that leaps from target to target, striking several foes in sequence with diminishing force. Excellent against clustered enemies and conductive targets in armor or water. Grounded and insulated targets take reduced damage, and the chain cannot leap to a target it cannot reach through the air.
[Lightning Magic: 47]

Lightning Dash.name: Lightning Dash
Lightning Dash.description:
The caster becomes a bolt of lightning, discharging their body across a short distance in an instant and striking whatever lies at the destination. Combines rapid repositioning with a damaging arrival. Requires a clear path with no insulating barrier; a grounded wall or water between origin and destination disrupts the step.
[Lightning Magic: 56]

Storm Herald.name: Storm Herald
Storm Herald.description:
The caster calls a localized thunderstorm that answers their command, striking targets with bolts from above throughout the battle. Each turn, lightning falls where the caster directs. The storm is powerful but demands an open sky or high ceiling; underground or beneath heavy cover, the herald cannot summon its bolts.
[Lightning Magic: 66]

Overcharge.name: Overcharge
Overcharge.description:
The caster floods their body with electrical power, moving and casting at blinding speed for several turns while their touch and spells crackle with amplified lightning. Reactions sharpen and attacks accelerate. The overcharge strains the caster's body; when it ends, they suffer muscle fatigue and a period of sluggishness.
[Lightning Magic: 77]

Ion Storm.name: Ion Storm
Ion Storm.description:
The caster saturates a wide area with charged particles, creating a field where lightning arcs continuously between everything conductive and the very air burns with static. Enemies within take repeated shocks and their metal gear turns against them. Allies in armor are endangered too; the caster must account for the field's indiscriminate reach.
[Lightning Magic: 88]

Wrath of the Thunder God.name: Wrath of the Thunder God
Wrath of the Thunder God.description:
The heavens' judgment. The caster raises their hand and calls down a single, world-splitting bolt carrying the fury of the storm itself: a strike that can vaporize a monster of legend, shatter a citadel, and leave the sky scarred. Nothing conductive survives the epicenter. The discharge courses back through the caster, and the toll is such that the bolt can be called only once when all else has failed.
[Lightning Magic: 100]

Torrent.name: Torrent
Torrent.description:
