Short and Balanced.description: A short frame with even proportions, moderately broad shoulders, a natural waist, and limbs that suit your height. An everyday build with neither pronounced bulk nor extreme slenderness.

Claw Gauntlets.name: Claw Gauntlets
Claw Gauntlets.description:
Gauntlets fitted with curved steel claws: three blades over each set of knuckles that slash on the swing and pierce on the thrust. Claw fighters close in fast, rake through guards and leather, and turn every clinch into a bleeding wound. It is unarmed fighting with teeth, the style of beastkin duelists, pit fighters, and anyone who wanted their punches to leave marks.

Primary Attribute: Strength
Claw Gauntlets.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist fights with claw gauntlets, curved steel blades over armored knuckles. Describe combat with raking slashes, piercing claw thrusts, hooking cuts, blades caught and turned on the claws, and fast close-range footwork; the claws leave slashing and piercing wounds rather than blunt bruises, and every Unarmed Combat technique thrown with them cuts or pierces instead of bruising. WEAPON SKILL: Supports progression through Unarmed Combat.

Deepwatch Lantern Company.name: Deepwatch Lantern Company
Deepwatch Lantern Company.description:
Start as a junior member of Deepwatch Lantern Company, the Gold-rank Company at the top of the Riftmaw Depth Board. Leader: Tetsu Tetsuō. Hall: Floor Zero Gatehouse. Specialty: Riftmaw dives, deep mapping, rescue. You begin with a Company Crest Pin.

Company Skill: Dungeon Surveying
Deepwatch Lantern Company.traitNarrativeEffects: COMPANY: The protagonist is a junior member of Deepwatch Lantern Company (Gold rank; hall at Floor Zero Gatehouse, Floor Zero Gatehouse: Canteen; leader Tetsu Tetsuō). Company-mates know the protagonist by name and treat them as a junior: welcome at the hall, expected to pull their weight, and owed help in a real emergency. Membership is not a party: members keep their own posts and travel with the protagonist only when they agree in the scene. The protagonist can rise in the Company, leave it, or found their own.

The Flagon Irregulars.name: The Flagon Irregulars
The Flagon Irregulars.description:
Start as a junior member of the Flagon Irregulars, Ironhold's rowdy Silver-rank bounty Company that never lets a rookie go out alone. Leader: Ran Kōga. Hall: Ironhold. Specialty: monster bounties, warren clearing, training rookies. You begin with a Company Crest Pin.

Company Skill: Monster Harvesting
The Flagon Irregulars.traitNarrativeEffects: COMPANY: The protagonist is a junior member of the Flagon Irregulars (Silver rank; hall at Ironhold, The Rusty Flagon; leader Ran Kōga). Company-mates know the protagonist by name and treat them as a junior: welcome at the hall, expected to pull their weight, and owed help in a real emergency. Membership is not a party: members keep their own posts and travel with the protagonist only when they agree in the scene. The protagonist can rise in the Company, leave it, or found their own.

Tidecrest Company.name: Tidecrest Company
Tidecrest Company.description:
Start as a junior member of Tidecrest Company, the dashing Silver-rank escort Company of the Cerulean Coast. Leader: Torao Arami. Hall: Portmaris. Specialty: sea-lane and caravan escorts, coastal dungeons. You begin with a Company Crest Pin.

Company Skill: Acrobatics
Tidecrest Company.traitNarrativeEffects: COMPANY: The protagonist is a junior member of Tidecrest Company (Silver rank; hall at Portmaris, Portside Tavern Row; leader Torao Arami). The Gilded Caravan Company.name: The Gilded Caravan Company
The Gilded Caravan Company.description:
Start as a junior member of the Gilded Caravan Company, the Gold-rank desert caravan Company of the Mirage Sea. Leader: Takuma Hidaka. Hall: Sunveil Caravanserai. Specialty: desert caravans, catacomb salvage. You begin with a Company Crest Pin.

Company Skill: Merchant Trade

The Frostfang Hunt.name: The Frostfang Hunt
The Frostfang Hunt.description:
Start as a junior member of the Frostfang Hunt, the Silver-rank mountain hunting pack of the Veilpeak. Leader: Gunther Hyōshun. Hall: Frostbell Onsen Town. Specialty: mountain hunts, monster migrations, pass escorts. You begin with a Company Crest Pin.

Company Skill: Survival
The Frostfang Hunt.traitNarrativeEffects: COMPANY: The protagonist is a junior member of the Frostfang Hunt (Silver rank; hall at Frostbell Onsen Town, Mountain Guild Lodge; leader Gunther Hyōshun). The Greenwake Company.name: The Greenwake Company
The Greenwake Company.description:
Start as a junior member of the Greenwake Company, the Gold-rank trail-keepers of the Verdania Wilds. Leader: Hayato Haibara. Hall: Lanternmoss Village. Specialty: forest trails, canopy scouting, abyss expeditions. You begin with a Company Crest Pin.

Company Skill: Foraging

The Vaunted Blade Company.name: The Vaunted Blade Company
The Vaunted Blade Company.description:
Start as a junior member of the Vaunted Blade Company, Crownveil's famous Gold-rank tournament Company. Leader: Raiga Kōtetsu. Hall: Knight's Tournament Grounds. Specialty: tournaments, duels, high-profile bounties. You begin with a Company Crest Pin.

Company Skill: Dueling

The Emberforge Company.description:
Start as a junior member of the Emberforge Company, the Silver-rank Company of fighting smiths in Emberglass. Leader: Ragna Kadan. Hall: Emberglass Forge City. Specialty: volcanic ore runs, weapon testing, forge commissions. You begin with a Company Crest Pin.

Company Skill: Blacksmithing
The Emberforge Company.traitNarrativeEffects: COMPANY: The protagonist is a junior member of the Emberforge Company (Silver rank; hall at Emberglass Forge City, Forge Guild Commission Office; leader Ragna Kadan). Blank Charter (Found Your Own).name: Blank Charter (Found Your Own)
Blank Charter (Found Your Own).description:
Start with a Blank Company Charter, its fee already stamped paid. Gather two willing partners, choose a name and a crest, and file it at any Adventurer's Guild hall to found your own Company at Iron rank.

Company Skill: Persuasion
Blank Charter (Found Your Own).traitNarrativeEffects: COMPANY: The protagonist carries a Blank Company Charter with the fee prepaid and means to found their own Adventurer Company. They belong to no Company yet. Founding needs two partners who agree on screen and registration at an Adventurer's Guild hall; the player chooses the name and crest, never the narrator.

Portrait Style - Mothlight Reverie.name: Portrait Style - Mothlight Reverie
Portrait Style - Mothlight Reverie.description: Visual result: fine detailed linework, long fine hair strands, a soft painted finish, muted matte colors against deep indigo shadow, cool bioluminescent glow, one warm golden key light, and a quiet, wistful mood. Pairs well with Portrait Frame - Mothlight Offering and a dark, glowing Scene Background such as Crystal Cavern Depths. This selection controls art style, linework, palette, shading, lighting treatment, and finish only. It does not override Portrait Framing, character identity, age, species, outfit, powers, equipment, scene background, or user-written appearance details.
Portrait Style - Mothlight Reverie.traitNarrativeEffects: STYLE LOCK: high-resolution Mothlight Reverie anime illustration, a quiet nocturne style. Draw graceful adult anime faces with soft half-lidded eyes, fine lashes and calm features in fine, detailed linework with delicate line-weight variation. Build hair from long fine strands and loose wisps over soft masses; give fabric quiet texture and layered folds. Render selected colors faithfully but muted, matte and slightly desaturated, against deep indigo and blue-black shadow with cool cyan bioluminescent accents. Light is low-key chiaroscuro: one small warm golden key light from the frame or scene (otherwise a soft warm rim from off-frame) touches the face edge, hands and front folds, with soft bloom on light sources only and gentle haze behind. The mood is quiet, intimate and wistful. Keep faces, eyes, hands, anatomy, hair silhouettes and garment edges readable; never let darkness swallow the face. Block dot noise, speckling, mottled skin and noisy dithering. Preserve the selected Portrait Frame, anatomy, colors, outfit, pose, and background. Do not invent weapons, props, symbols, readable text, aura, magic effects, or events.

Portrait Frame - Mothlight Offering.name: Portrait Frame - Mothlight Offering
Portrait Frame - Mothlight Offering.description: FRAME LOCK TEXT: Mothlight offering portrait of [character name], framed waist-up in a three-quarter view, head gently bowed and eyes lowered toward one upturned palm held out to the side, a single small glowing moth or light hovering above the fingertips. The face, hair shape, raised hand, upper outfit, and selected background remain readable.
Portrait Frame - Mothlight Offering.traitNarrativeEffects: FRAME LOCK: mothlight offering portrait. This is the final camera and composition authority. Use a waist-up three-quarter view, the character turned slightly aside and filling about two-thirds of the frame, with open space on the side of the raised hand. Head gently bowed, eyes lowered and half-lidded, gaze resting on one hand raised to the side at chest-to-shoulder height, palm up, fingers relaxed and softly curled; the other arm rests low or within the sleeve. A single small glowing light hovers just above the fingertips: a luminous moth by default, or a wisp, ember, petal or tiny spirit if selected traits support one. It is the warm key light on the hand, face edge and front folds. Keep the face, both eyes, five clear fingers, full hair silhouette, shoulders and upper outfit readable. Use a calm, quiet expression; do not add tears, a partner, weapons or other props. The selected Portrait Style and scene detail cannot override this frame, move the camera, or change its visible body range.

Keeper of the Hollow Name.name: Keeper of the Hollow Name
Keeper of the Hollow Name.description: You read a name in colored glass that its owner gave up forty years ago: Kōtarō Kasuga. Spoken to the Hollow King, it makes the vessel he wears his last.
Keeper of the Hollow Name.traitNarrativeEffects: This character knows the Hollow King's true name, Kōtarō Kasuga. Spoken to him, it binds him to his current vessel: if that vessel falls, he dies for good instead of waking in another. Faceless Ones can sense the name on this character and grow wary or desperate around them.

Limit Break.name: Limit Break
Limit Break.description:
Shout it and mean it. LIMIT BREAK tears the ceiling off your body for a few breathless turns: every attribute surges past the limit everyone else lives under, and the whole room feels it happen. Then the bill arrives, and your body runs weak until it can be called again.

How it works: say "Limit Break" in your action. Every attribute +10 for 5 turns, then -4 for 5 turns of recoil, then it recharges (30 turns from start to ready).

Attribute limits: points you spend stop at 60. Bonuses from traits, boons and Limit Break stack past it.
Limit Break.traitNarrativeEffects: When Limit Break is active, render it loudly: air pressure drops, hair lifts, the ground cracks under a planted foot, and every witness knows a limit just broke. During recoil the character is visibly spent. Never trigger it unless the player calls it.

Goddess's Errands.name: Goddess's Errands
Goddess's Errands.description:
The goddess who reincarnated you is bored, nosy, and very invested in you. Every so often a glowing note flutters down in her handwriting with a small errand for the day ("Make someone laugh out loud", "Defeat three monsters, be careful!!"), and she rewards you when you do it.

How it works: every so often a new errand note arrives. Do it and your health and mana are restored and her Favor rises. Favor ranks I to V arrive after 3, 7, 12, 18 and 25 errands, and every rank permanently raises all six attributes. Ignore a note and it quietly fades, with no penalty.
Goddess's Errands.traitNarrativeEffects: Errand notes are small, glowing and written in a goddess's cheerful handwriting with doodles; only the bearer can read them. Errands are personal favors, not quests, and never appear in the quest log. The goddess never reveals anything the character could not otherwise learn.

Gacha Blessing.name: Gacha Blessing
Gacha Blessing.description:
Somewhere above Luxcellia a god runs a gacha game, and you are its favorite player. Every so often a glowing capsule pops into being beside you, spinning with rainbow light, and cracks open on something you can actually use. Usually it is Common. Sometimes it is not.

How it works: a capsule appears about every 25 turns, and one the story misses is not lost: it waits and opens at the next chance. Rates: Common 45%, Uncommon 25%, Rare 18%, Epic 9%, Legendary 2.5%, Mythic 0.5%. Pity: after nine capsules in a row below Epic, the tenth is guaranteed Epic or better. Ask about your gacha or your capsules to hear when the next one is due.
Gacha Blessing.traitNarrativeEffects: Capsules glow by rarity (white, green, blue, purple, gold, prismatic), and the item inside fits the bearer's build and situation. A capsule item belongs to the bearer on the spot, like combat loot. Other people find the capsules baffling and slightly rude.

Desperation Engine.name: Desperation Engine
Desperation Engine.description:
Most people weaken as they bleed. You get dangerous. Desperation Engine wires your body to the edge of death: the closer you come to falling, the harder, faster and tougher you fight.

How it works: below half health you are Cornered (+6 strength, +6 dexterity, +4 constitution). Below a quarter you reach Last Light (+12 strength, +12 dexterity, +8 constitution, +6 wisdom). Heal back up and the engine cools.
Desperation Engine.traitNarrativeEffects: When the engine kicks in, show it: pupils narrowing, breath steadying, the wound forgotten. Enemies who thought they were winning feel the exact moment the fight turned.

Predator's Feast.name: Predator's Feast
Predator's Feast.description:
You are what you eat, and you eat monsters. Predator's Feast turns harvested monster flesh, blood and marrow into growth: every real monster meal settles into your body and, over time, rebuilds it into something apex.

How it works: eat a part harvested from a monster (cooked counts) to feed the Feast, at most once every few turns. Your Feast tier rises at 3, 8, 15, 25 and 40 meals (I to V), and each tier permanently strengthens your body.
Predator's Feast.traitNarrativeEffects: Monster meals taste incredible to the bearer and alarming to everyone watching. As tiers rise, small adaptations show: night-sharp eyes, scales under stress, a growl low in the chest. Ordinary food is just food.

Otherworld Online Shop.name: Otherworld Online Shop
Otherworld Online Shop.description:
Your old world's online shopping survived the trip, and it delivers. A shop window only you can see sells everyday goods from home (instant noodles, chocolate, mayonnaise, shampoo, cheap umbrellas, paperbacks) for Luxcellian coin, and a cardboard box appears beside you a moment later. Ordinary there. Absurdly powerful here.

How it works: buy everyday old-world goods with coin (no weapons, vehicles or electronics beyond batteries and flashlights). Old-world food grants strong restorative bonuses, and the right merchant pays silly prices for it. Every so often a Time Sale halves the price of one category.
Otherworld Online Shop.traitNarrativeEffects: The shop window is private: only the bearer sees or hears it, and nobody else knows what is browsed or bought until a box appears. Browsing shows three to six goods with their prices and stops there; nothing is bought until the player names an item and agrees to its price in their own words, and nothing is ever bought for them. Prices are in Luxcellian coin and cheap: a snack, a seasoning or a notebook costs Copper; toiletries, clothing or a camping set a few Silver; only a bulk order reaches Gold. When the player buys, the story says the coins handed over, so they leave the purse. Deliveries arrive in a plain taped cardboard box. Luxcellians are fascinated by bubble wrap.

Second Playthrough.name: Second Playthrough
Second Playthrough.description:
You have done all this before. Or you read it, or played it, or dreamed it: either way Luxcellia feels like a route you already cleared, and the memories come back as you grow. Flashes of deja vu warn you, and old instincts return in pieces.

How it works: every so often a flash of deja vu gives you one true, useful detail about where you are or who is in front of you. At levels 15, 30, 45, 60 and 75 a memory fragment returns, and each one permanently raises your attributes.
Second Playthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: Deja vu is a feeling plus one useful truth: a hidden room, a lie, a weak point, what someone really wants. It never reveals a villain's true name or secret identity or how a quest ends, and the memories are sometimes wrong about details that changed.

Limit Break: Unleashed.name: Limit Break: Unleashed
Limit Break: Unleashed.description: Limit Break is active: every attribute +10, past any ceiling. It fades after 5 turns.
Limit Break: Unleashed.traitNarrativeEffects: The bearer is visibly beyond their limit: pressure in the air, light in the eyes, a body moving faster and hitting harder than it should.

Limit Break: Recoil.name: Limit Break: Recoil
Limit Break: Recoil.description: Limit Break's recoil: every attribute -4 for 5 turns while the body recovers.
Limit Break: Recoil.traitNarrativeEffects: The bearer is visibly spent: shaking hands, slow focus, a body paying back what it borrowed.

Goddess's Favor I.name: Goddess's Favor I
Goddess's Favor I.description: The goddess's Favor has reached rank I: every attribute +1.
Goddess's Favor I.traitNarrativeEffects: Goddess's Favor I. Her notes have more doodles now.

Goddess's Favor II.name: Goddess's Favor II
Goddess's Favor II.description: The goddess's Favor has reached rank II: every attribute +2.
Goddess's Favor II.traitNarrativeEffects: Goddess's Favor II. Her notes have more doodles now.

Goddess's Favor III.name: Goddess's Favor III
Goddess's Favor III.description: The goddess's Favor has reached rank III: every attribute +3.
Goddess's Favor III.traitNarrativeEffects: Goddess's Favor III. Her notes have more doodles now.

Goddess's Favor IV.name: Goddess's Favor IV
Goddess's Favor IV.description: The goddess's Favor has reached rank IV: every attribute +4.
Goddess's Favor IV.traitNarrativeEffects: Goddess's Favor IV. Her notes have more doodles now.

Goddess's Favor V.name: Goddess's Favor V
Goddess's Favor V.description: The goddess's Favor has reached rank V: every attribute +6.
Goddess's Favor V.traitNarrativeEffects: Goddess's Favor V. Her notes have more doodles now.

Desperation: Cornered.name: Desperation: Cornered
Desperation: Cornered.description: Desperation Engine: below half health, +6 strength, +6 dexterity, +4 constitution.
Desperation: Cornered.traitNarrativeEffects: The bearer fights with a cornered animal's focus.

Desperation: Last Light.name: Desperation: Last Light
Desperation: Last Light.description: Desperation Engine: below a quarter of health, +12 strength, +12 dexterity, +8 constitution, +6 wisdom.
Desperation: Last Light.traitNarrativeEffects: The bearer burns at the edge of death, calm and terrifying.

Predator's Feast I.name: Predator's Feast I
Predator's Feast I.description: Predator's Feast tier I: the monsters you have eaten are rebuilding you.
Predator's Feast I.traitNarrativeEffects: Monster meals leave the bearer warm and restless.

Predator's Feast II.name: Predator's Feast II
Predator's Feast II.description: Predator's Feast tier II: the monsters you have eaten are rebuilding you.
Predator's Feast II.traitNarrativeEffects: The bearer's eyes catch light in the dark.

Predator's Feast III.name: Predator's Feast III
Predator's Feast III.description: Predator's Feast tier III: the monsters you have eaten are rebuilding you.
Predator's Feast III.traitNarrativeEffects: Faint scales rise on the bearer's skin under stress.

Predator's Feast IV.name: Predator's Feast IV
Predator's Feast IV.description: Predator's Feast tier IV: the monsters you have eaten are rebuilding you.
Predator's Feast IV.traitNarrativeEffects: A growl lives low in the bearer's chest; monsters hesitate.

Predator's Feast V.name: Predator's Feast V
Predator's Feast V.description: Predator's Feast tier V: the monsters you have eaten are rebuilding you.
Predator's Feast V.traitNarrativeEffects: The bearer is an apex predator now, and every monster can tell.

Second Playthrough: Fragment I.name: Second Playthrough: Fragment I
Second Playthrough: Fragment I.description: A memory from the first playthrough has returned: +2 intelligence, +2 wisdom.
Second Playthrough: Fragment I.traitNarrativeEffects: The bearer sometimes moves like they are remembering a fight they never had.

Second Playthrough: Fragment II.name: Second Playthrough: Fragment II
Second Playthrough: Fragment II.description: A memory from the first playthrough has returned: +2 dexterity, +2 charisma.
Second Playthrough: Fragment II.traitNarrativeEffects: The bearer sometimes moves like they are remembering a fight they never had.

Second Playthrough: Fragment III.name: Second Playthrough: Fragment III
Second Playthrough: Fragment III.description: A memory from the first playthrough has returned: +2 strength, +2 constitution.
Second Playthrough: Fragment III.traitNarrativeEffects: The bearer sometimes moves like they are remembering a fight they never had.

Second Playthrough: Fragment IV.name: Second Playthrough: Fragment IV
Second Playthrough: Fragment IV.description: A memory from the first playthrough has returned: +2 intelligence, +2 wisdom, +2 dexterity.
Second Playthrough: Fragment IV.traitNarrativeEffects: The bearer sometimes moves like they are remembering a fight they never had.

Second Playthrough: Fragment V.name: Second Playthrough: Fragment V
Second Playthrough: Fragment V.description: A memory from the first playthrough has returned: +2 to every attribute.
Second Playthrough: Fragment V.traitNarrativeEffects: The bearer sometimes moves like they are remembering a fight they never had.

True Dragon.name: True Dragon
True Dragon.description:
Not dragon-blooded. Not dragon-touched. A dragon. You came back as the thing every bestiary puts on its last page, only smaller than the paintings: a lesser dragon the size of a warhorse, with a long road of growth ahead and a world that will not wait to decide what you are.

BODY: Foreclaws can grip and carry but not write or work fine tools. No humanoid armor fits; barding, harness and jewelry do. Speech is a dragon's voice from a dragon's throat, and people hear every word.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Villages ring bells. Knights reach for lances. Scholars reach for notebooks. The Twilight Dominion sends a formal greeting, and the Church sends for instructions.

RACIAL TRAIT: A hard body turns part of every blow: 10% of the health you lose each turn is restored at the end of it.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Fang and Claw +2 and Wing and Dive +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

EVOLUTION: At level 15 you become a Drake and gain Skyshaking Roar. At level 35 you choose a path by typing it: "evolve flame" for Flame Dragon, or "evolve storm" for Storm Dragon. At level 60 that path reaches its final form: Elder Flame Dragon or Elder Storm Dragon.

IMAGE GENERATION RULE: TRUE FORM, NOT A HUMANOID VARIANT. A true four-legged dragon with a long neck, wedge-shaped reptilian head, horns, a pair of large membranous wings, a heavy tail, and armored scales; quadruped stance; no human face, torso, or hands. Draw this body exactly; never give it a human face, human skin or a human figure it does not have. Appearance picks made for humanoids apply only where this body has the matching part: hair picks color the mane, crest, fur, feathers or glow; skin tone picks color the hide, scales, shell or surface; outfit picks become harness, barding, collar, cloth or ornament this body can wear; picks with no matching part are left out. Always a fully grown adult of its kind.

RACE REFERENCE: True Dragon is a full dragon, horse-sized at first, scaled, winged and four-legged. Use hoard instinct, pride, old draconic law, and the weight of being a legend that is still small as background hooks.
True Dragon.traitNarrativeEffects: You count things when you are nervous, and you are never comfortable sleeping on a floor that has nothing shiny under it. BODY: Foreclaws can grip and carry but not write or work fine tools. No humanoid armor fits; barding, harness and jewelry do. Speech is a dragon's voice from a dragon's throat, and people hear every word. People know your kind talks. WORLD: Villages ring bells. Knights reach for lances. Scholars reach for notebooks. The Twilight Dominion sends a formal greeting, and the Church sends for instructions. IMAGE GENERATION RULE: TRUE FORM, NOT A HUMANOID VARIANT. A true four-legged dragon with a long neck, wedge-shaped reptilian head, horns, a pair of large membranous wings, a heavy tail, and armored scales; quadruped stance; no human face, torso, or hands. Never humanize it. Humanoid-only appearance picks adapt to this body or are left out. Always a fully grown adult of its kind.

Drake.name: Drake
Drake.description: Drake: wings grown strong enough for true flight, scales thick as plate. Evolved form of the True Dragon (stage II). Bonuses: +2 strength, +1 constitution, +20 health, and the ability Skyshaking Roar. At level 35 you choose between Flame Dragon (type: evolve flame) and Storm Dragon (type: evolve storm).
Drake.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a True Dragon: now a Drake, wings grown strong enough for true flight, scales thick as plate. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan. Never humanize it.

Flame Dragon.name: Flame Dragon
Flame Dragon.description: Flame Dragon: the furnace wakes: breath that melts stone and scales that glow at the edges. Evolved form of the True Dragon (stage III). Bonuses: +4 strength, +1 constitution, +1 intelligence, +3 Fire Magic, +40 health. At level 60 this becomes Elder Flame Dragon.
Flame Dragon.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a True Dragon: now a Flame Dragon, the furnace wakes: breath that melts stone and scales that glow at the edges. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan. Never humanize it.

Elder Flame Dragon.name: Elder Flame Dragon
Elder Flame Dragon.description: Elder Flame Dragon: a legend's size and a volcano's patience; your shadow changes the weather. Final form of the True Dragon (stage IV). Bonuses: +6 strength, +1 constitution, +3 intelligence, +5 Fire Magic, +70 health. This is the top of the line.
Elder Flame Dragon.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a True Dragon: now an Elder Flame Dragon, a legend's size and a volcano's patience; your shadow changes the weather. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan. Never humanize it.

Storm Dragon.name: Storm Dragon
Storm Dragon.description: Storm Dragon: the sky claims you: lightning in the wingbeats and a hunter's speed. Evolved form of the True Dragon (stage III). Bonuses: +2 strength, +1 constitution, +2 dexterity, +1 intelligence, +3 Lightning Magic, +20 health, +20 Mana. At level 60 this becomes Elder Storm Dragon.
Storm Dragon.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a True Dragon: now a Storm Dragon, the sky claims you: lightning in the wingbeats and a hunter's speed. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan. Never humanize it.

Elder Storm Dragon.name: Elder Storm Dragon
Elder Storm Dragon.description: Elder Storm Dragon: a legend's size and a thunderhead's temper; storms follow you like hounds. Final form of the True Dragon (stage IV). Bonuses: +2 strength, +1 constitution, +4 dexterity, +3 intelligence, +5 Lightning Magic, +20 health, +50 Mana. This is the top of the line.
Elder Storm Dragon.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a True Dragon: now an Elder Storm Dragon, a legend's size and a thunderhead's temper; storms follow you like hounds. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan. Never humanize it.

Wyvern.name: Wyvern
Wyvern.description:
A lean sky-hunter: two hind legs, two wings that are its arms, a barbed tail, and no interest in gold or speeches. You came back built for the dive. Wyverns are the reason caravans watch the sky, and you are the first one anybody has ever heard apologize.

BODY: Wing-claws can hook and hold, nothing finer. Carries a harness and saddlebags, not armor. Speaks in a rasping voice that startles everyone, the wyvern included.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Caravan guards nock arrows on sight. Griffin riders want a race. Beast tamers want a contract, and are surprised to be asked for terms.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Wing and Dive +2 and Fang and Claw +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

EVOLUTION: At level 15 you become a Greater Wyvern and gain Barbed Tail Lash. At level 35 you choose a path by typing it: "evolve sky" for Sky Tyrant, or "evolve venom" for Venom Wyvern. At level 60 that path reaches its final form: Tempest Wyvern or Plague Wyvern.

IMAGE GENERATION RULE: TRUE FORM, NOT A HUMANOID VARIANT. A wyvern: built like a giant bat with a reptile's head. Its two great wings are its arms, with a hooked claw at each wing-elbow, and it stands on two strong hind legs with the wing-elbows folded to the ground. Lean narrow head, long neck, barbed whip tail, leathery scales; no human features. Draw this body exactly; never give it a human face, human skin or a human figure it does not have. Appearance picks made for humanoids apply only where this body has the matching part: hair picks color the mane, crest, fur, feathers or glow; skin tone picks color the hide, scales, shell or surface; outfit picks become harness, barding, collar, cloth or ornament this body can wear; picks with no matching part are left out. Always a fully grown adult of its kind.

RACE REFERENCE: Wyvern is a two-legged winged predator, about the size of a large horse. Use speed, hunger for open sky, and being mistaken for a mindless beast as background hooks.
Wyvern.traitNarrativeEffects: You cannot walk past a high ledge without measuring the drop for a dive. BODY: Wing-claws can hook and hold, nothing finer. Carries a harness and saddlebags, not armor. Speaks in a rasping voice that startles everyone, the wyvern included. WORLD: Caravan guards nock arrows on sight. Griffin riders want a race. Beast tamers want a contract, and are surprised to be asked for terms. IMAGE GENERATION RULE: TRUE FORM, NOT A HUMANOID VARIANT. A wyvern: built like a giant bat with a reptile's head. Its two great wings are its arms, with a hooked claw at each wing-elbow, and it stands on two strong hind legs with the wing-elbows folded to the ground. Lean narrow head, long neck, barbed whip tail, leathery scales; no human features. Never humanize it. Humanoid-only appearance picks adapt to this body or are left out. Always a fully grown adult of its kind.

Greater Wyvern.name: Greater Wyvern
Greater Wyvern.description: Greater Wyvern: broader wings, a heavier barb, and the lungs for a day-long hunt. Evolved form of the Wyvern (stage II). Bonuses: +2 dexterity, +1 strength, +20 health, and the ability Barbed Tail Lash. At level 35 you choose between Sky Tyrant (type: evolve sky) and Venom Wyvern (type: evolve venom).
Greater Wyvern.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Wyvern: now a Greater Wyvern, broader wings, a heavier barb, and the lungs for a day-long hunt. Draw and describe this greater form: still two hind legs, wings for arms, a barbed tail. Never humanize it.

Sky Tyrant.name: Sky Tyrant
Sky Tyrant.description: Sky Tyrant: nothing with wings outflies you, and you know it. Evolved form of the Wyvern (stage III). Bonuses: +4 dexterity, +1 strength, +1 constitution, +3 acrobatics, +40 health. At level 60 this becomes Tempest Wyvern.
Sky Tyrant.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Wyvern: now a Sky Tyrant, nothing with wings outflies you, and you know it. Draw and describe this greater form: still two hind legs, wings for arms, a barbed tail. Never humanize it.

Tempest Wyvern.name: Tempest Wyvern
Tempest Wyvern.description: Tempest Wyvern: you ride storm fronts for fun, and you hit like one. Final form of the Wyvern (stage IV). Bonuses: +6 dexterity, +1 strength, +3 constitution, +5 acrobatics, +70 health. This is the top of the line.
Tempest Wyvern.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Wyvern: now a Tempest Wyvern, you ride storm fronts for fun, and you hit like one. Draw and describe this greater form: still two hind legs, wings for arms, a barbed tail. Never humanize it.

Venom Wyvern.name: Venom Wyvern
Venom Wyvern.description: Venom Wyvern: the barb fills with a venom alchemists would kill for. Evolved form of the Wyvern (stage III). Bonuses: +4 dexterity, +1 strength, +1 intelligence, +3 Poison Magic, +20 health, +20 Mana. At level 60 this becomes Plague Wyvern.
Venom Wyvern.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Wyvern: now a Venom Wyvern, the barb fills with a venom alchemists would kill for. Draw and describe this greater form: still two hind legs, wings for arms, a barbed tail. Never humanize it.

Plague Wyvern.name: Plague Wyvern
Plague Wyvern.description: Plague Wyvern: one scratch from the barb is a countdown, and you choose how long. Final form of the Wyvern (stage IV). Bonuses: +6 dexterity, +1 strength, +3 intelligence, +5 Poison Magic, +20 health, +50 Mana. This is the top of the line.
Plague Wyvern.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Wyvern: now a Plague Wyvern, one scratch from the barb is a countdown, and you choose how long. Draw and describe this greater form: still two hind legs, wings for arms, a barbed tail. Never humanize it.

Sea Serpent.name: Sea Serpent
Sea Serpent.description:
Sailors have a hundred names for you and a prayer for each. You came back in the deep: a serpent as long as a fishing boat, finned and coiled, at home in water and stubbornly capable on land. The Tidelace shrines leave offerings for your kind. You are welcome to them.

BODY: No hands at all: coils grip, jaws carry. On land you move like a very large snake and need water every so often. Speech carries oddly, like a voice heard through a hull.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Fishermen bow or flee. Tidebound Shrine Keepers greet you by an old title. Merchant Lords quietly ask what it would cost to have you escort a ship.

RACIAL TRAIT: Your body knits itself: you recover 1% of your health every turn while hurt.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Fang and Claw +2 and Charge and Crush +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

EVOLUTION: At level 15 you become a Great Serpent and gain Riptide Rush. At level 35 you choose a path by typing it: "evolve leviathan" for Leviathan-kin, or "evolve mist" for Mist Serpent. At level 60 that path reaches its final form: Leviathan or Dream Leviathan.

IMAGE GENERATION RULE: TRUE FORM, NOT A HUMANOID VARIANT. A sea serpent: a long finned serpentine dragon with a crested head, frilled gills, a sinuous scaled body with no legs or small swept-back fins, and a paddle tail; no limbs with hands, no human features. Draw this body exactly; never give it a human face, human skin or a human figure it does not have. Appearance picks made for humanoids apply only where this body has the matching part: hair picks color the mane, crest, fur, feathers or glow; skin tone picks color the hide, scales, shell or surface; outfit picks become harness, barding, collar, cloth or ornament this body can wear; picks with no matching part are left out. Always a fully grown adult of its kind.

RACE REFERENCE: Sea Serpent is a finned serpentine dragon of the deep, boat-length. Use tides, shrine offerings, sailor superstition, and the pull of deep water as background hooks.
Sea Serpent.traitNarrativeEffects: You circle anything you are thinking hard about. BODY: No hands at all: coils grip, jaws carry. On land you move like a very large snake and need water every so often. Speech carries oddly, like a voice heard through a hull. WORLD: Fishermen bow or flee. Tidebound Shrine Keepers greet you by an old title. Merchant Lords quietly ask what it would cost to have you escort a ship. IMAGE GENERATION RULE: TRUE FORM, NOT A HUMANOID VARIANT. Never humanize it. Humanoid-only appearance picks adapt to this body or are left out. Always a fully grown adult of its kind.

Great Serpent.name: Great Serpent
Great Serpent.description: Great Serpent: twice the length, a crest like a banner, and scales that turn harpoons. Evolved form of the Sea Serpent (stage II). Bonuses: +2 constitution, +1 wisdom, +20 health, and the ability Riptide Rush. At level 35 you choose between Leviathan-kin (type: evolve leviathan) and Mist Serpent (type: evolve mist).
Great Serpent.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Sea Serpent: now a Great Serpent, twice the length, a crest like a banner, and scales that turn harpoons. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan. Never humanize it.

Leviathan-kin.name: Leviathan-kin
Leviathan-kin.description: Leviathan-kin: you grow toward the size the old stories warn about. Evolved form of the Sea Serpent (stage III). Bonuses: +4 constitution, +1 wisdom, +1 strength, +3 Water Magic, +40 health. At level 60 this becomes Leviathan.
Leviathan-kin.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Sea Serpent: now a Leviathan-kin, you grow toward the size the old stories warn about. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan. Never humanize it.

Leviathan.name: Leviathan
Leviathan.description: Leviathan: harbors rearrange their schedules around you. Final form of the Sea Serpent (stage IV). Bonuses: +6 constitution, +1 wisdom, +3 strength, +5 Water Magic, +70 health. This is the top of the line.
Leviathan.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Sea Serpent: now a Leviathan, harbors rearrange their schedules around you. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan. Never humanize it.

Mist Serpent.name: Mist Serpent
Mist Serpent.description: Mist Serpent: you learn to move in fog, in dreams, and in rumor. Evolved form of the Sea Serpent (stage III). Bonuses: +2 constitution, +3 wisdom, +1 charisma, +3 Illusion Magic, +20 health, +20 Mana. At level 60 this becomes Dream Leviathan.
Mist Serpent.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Sea Serpent: now a Mist Serpent, you learn to move in fog, in dreams, and in rumor. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan. Never humanize it.

Dream Leviathan.name: Dream Leviathan
Dream Leviathan.description: Dream Leviathan: half of what sailors see of you is real; none of them can tell which half. Final form of the Sea Serpent (stage IV). Bonuses: +2 constitution, +5 wisdom, +3 charisma, +5 Illusion Magic, +20 health, +50 Mana. This is the top of the line.
Dream Leviathan.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Sea Serpent: now a Dream Leviathan, half of what sailors see of you is real; none of them can tell which half. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan. Never humanize it.

Hydra.name: Hydra
Hydra.description:
One body, several opinions. You came back as a hydra with two heads that share a stomach and argue about everything else. Wounds close while people are still congratulating themselves. Adventurer manuals have a whole chapter on you, and most of it is wrong.

BODY: No hands; the heads do the fine work and bicker over it. Wears harness and barding only. Every head can speak, and they do not always agree.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Guild manuals say to bring fire. Scholars want to interview the heads separately. The fireside stories about you are mostly true.

RACIAL TRAIT: Your body knits itself: you recover 2% of your health every turn while hurt.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Fang and Claw +3, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

You died once already, so the theme is at least consistent. You came back as a phoenix: a bird of living fire about the size of an eagle, warm to stand near and very difficult to keep dead. Temples argue about what you mean. You are mostly trying not to set the curtains alight.

Kirin.name: Kirin
Kirin.description:
The gentlest thing in the bestiary, and the one nobody dares to hunt. You came back as a kirin: a deer-bodied, dragon-scaled creature with a single branching horn, said to appear only in the reign of a good ruler. Courts are extremely interested in where you choose to stand.

RACIAL TRAIT: Mana gathers in you on its own: you recover 2% of your Mana every turn.

Nine-Tailed Fox.name: Nine-Tailed Fox
Nine-Tailed Fox.description:
Not fox-eared. Not fox-blessed. The fox. You came back as a spirit fox with three tails and six to earn: silver-gold fur, lantern eyes, and a talent for being exactly as much trouble as a situation can hold. Shrines know your kind. So do gambling houses.

BODY: Paws manage latches, dice and stolen fried tofu. Wears bells, ribbons and the occasional stolen scarf. A warm, amused voice.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Kitsune-Blessed and Foxkin treat you as an ancestor come visiting. Shrine keepers set out offerings. Merchants count their change twice.

RACIAL TRAIT: Hard to finish: when your health falls to 10% or lower, you recover 25% of it at once. This can happen once every 60 turns.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Fang and Claw +2 and Uncanny Body +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

At level 60 that path reaches its final form: Nine-Tailed Celestial Fox or Nine-Tailed Enchanter.

Cerberus.name: Cerberus
Cerberus.description:
Three heads, one tail, and a job nobody explained. You came back as a cerberus: a great black hound with three heads that take turns sleeping, born with the bone-deep sense that there is a door somewhere you are supposed to be guarding. Until you find it, everything is a door.

BODY: Paws only; three jaws carry three things. Wears a collar by choice. Three voices: one polite, one blunt, one that mostly growls.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: The Twilight Court asks which gate you belong to. Gravekeepers bow. Everyone else counts the heads again and steps back.

Slime.name: Slime
Slime.description:
Yes, that kind of rebirth. You came back as a slime: a waist-high blob of translucent gel with a core, no bones, no face, and a surprising amount of opinion. Rookies are told you are the easiest monster in the Shallow Rift. You intend to be a learning experience.

BODY: No hands: you engulf, extrude a pseudopod, or carry things inside yourself. Wears nothing; holds anything. Speaks by vibrating, a bubbling voice people find hard to place.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Rookies draw swords and grin. Alchemists want a sample. Slime-Born folk stop and stare like they have seen a grandparent.

RACIAL TRAIT: Your body knits itself: you recover 2% of your health every turn while hurt.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Uncanny Body +3, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

EVOLUTION: At level 15 you become a Great Slime and gain Dissolve. At level 35 you choose a path by typing it: "evolve predator" for Predator Slime, or "evolve arcane" for Arcane Slime. At level 60 that path reaches its final form: King Slime or Philosopher's Slime.

IMAGE GENERATION RULE: TRUE FORM, NOT A HUMANOID VARIANT. A true slime: a rounded, translucent gelatinous blob with a glossy surface and a visible glowing core inside, no limbs, no skeleton, with at most two simple eye-like spots or none; not a humanoid, no human face or body. Draw this body exactly; never give it a human face, human skin or a human figure it does not have. Appearance picks made for humanoids apply only where this body has the matching part: hair picks color the mane, crest, fur, feathers or glow; skin tone picks color the hide, scales, shell or surface; outfit picks become harness, barding, collar, cloth or ornament this body can wear; picks with no matching part are left out. Always a fully grown adult of its kind.

RACE REFERENCE: Slime is a living blob of gel with a core, waist-high. Use absorbing, adapting, being underestimated, and the slow climb from the bottom of every bestiary as background hooks.

Goblin.name: Goblin
Goblin.description:
Bottom of the dungeon, bottom of the bounty board, and exactly as short as the jokes say. You came back as a goblin: green, sharp-eared, wiry, quick with a knife and quicker with a plan. Everything bigger than you thinks you are a nuisance. Everything bigger than you is wrong about how this ends.

BODY: Good hands, short reach: tools and weapons sized for you, armor patched to fit. Speaks fine, with an accent people assume means stupid.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Guild boards list you at a few Copper a head. Guards block the gate. Other goblins watch to see if you are worth following.

RACIAL TRAIT: Cornered Fury: at 35% health or lower you gain +4 strength and +4 dexterity until you recover past half.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Fang and Claw +2 and Charge and Crush +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

EVOLUTION: At level 15 you become a Hobgoblin and gain Warren Ambush. At level 35 you choose a path by typing it: "evolve champion" for Goblin Champion, or "evolve shaman" for Goblin Shaman. At level 60 that path reaches its final form: Goblin King or Goblin Sage-King.

Draw this body exactly; never give it a human face, human skin or a human figure it does not have. Always a fully grown adult of its kind.

RACE REFERENCE: Goblin is a small green dungeon-dweller, adult and cunning. Use warren politics, scavenging, being hunted for copper bounties, and outthinking the big folk as background hooks.

Kobold.name: Kobold
Kobold.description:
Small, scaled, and convinced beyond argument that you are a dragon who has not finished yet. You came back as a kobold: a knee-high lizard-folk tunneler with a trap-maker's mind and a hoarder's eye. Dungeons are not dangerous to you. Dungeons are home improvement.

BODY: Nimble clawed hands are excellent with tools, traps and locks. Gear must be cut down to size. Speaks plainly, in a fast, yipping voice.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Miners curse you by habit. Dragons, and anything draconic, find you oddly easy to like. The Crystalvein Cartel would rather hire you than fight you underground.

RACIAL TRAIT: A nose for small fortunes: every so often you turn up a useful scrap, a bent coin, or a small rough gem from the rubble.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Fang and Claw +3, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

EVOLUTION: At level 15 you become a Kobold Trapmaster and gain Tunnel Sense. At level 35 you choose a path by typing it: "evolve dragon" for Dragon-Sworn Kobold, or "evolve tunnel" for Tunnel-Master. At level 60 that path reaches its final form: Kobold Dragon-Priest or Kobold Tunnel King.

SIDE EVOLUTION: From level 15 you may also type "evolve wings" to become a Winged Kobold: small dragon wings for gliding and short flights, kept beside whichever path you take.

A kobold: a small reptilian creature with a dog-like snout, small horns, scaled hide, a long tail, and clawed hands and feet, standing upright; a fully grown adult kobold; clearly reptilian, not human. Draw this body exactly; never give it a human face, human skin or a human figure it does not have. Appearance picks made for humanoids apply only where this body has the matching part: hair picks color the mane, crest, fur, feathers or glow; skin tone picks color the hide, scales, shell or surface; outfit picks become harness, barding, collar, cloth or ornament this body can wear; picks with no matching part are left out. Always a fully grown adult of its kind.

RACE REFERENCE: Kobold is a small scaled tunneler with a gift for traps and digging. Use dragon-worship, tunnel craft, strength in numbers, and stubborn pride as background hooks.

Great Spider.name: Great Spider
Great Spider.description:
Eight legs, eight eyes, and one very human sense of dread about it. You came back as a great spider the size of a hound, at the bottom of a dungeon with nothing but silk, venom and a brain that will not stop narrating. Start small. Web everything.

BODY: No hands, but silk and eight legs do precise work. Wears nothing; carries by webbing things to its back. Speech is a dry, clicking voice that takes people a moment to realize is words.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Almost everyone screams. Arachne-Kin hush them. Tailors, astonishingly, ask about the silk.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Fang and Claw +3, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

EVOLUTION: At level 15 you become a Great Weaver and gain Venom Bite. At level 35 you choose a path by typing it: "evolve venom" for Venom Stalker, or "evolve silk" for Silk Weaver. At level 60 that path reaches its final form: Abyssal Arachne or Grand Loomspinner.

Draw this body exactly; never give it a human face, human skin or a human figure it does not have. Appearance picks made for humanoids apply only where this body has the matching part: hair picks color the mane, crest, fur, feathers or glow; skin tone picks color the hide, scales, shell or surface; outfit picks become harness, barding, collar, cloth or ornament this body can wear; picks with no matching part are left out. RACE REFERENCE: Great Spider is a giant dungeon spider with a thinking mind. Use webs, patience, venom, molting, and the long climb from prey to apex as background hooks.

Mimic.name: Mimic
Mimic.description:
Somebody, somewhere, is about to have a very bad day opening a chest. You came back as a mimic: a creature that looks like whatever you decide to look like, with a hinge-lid mouth and a tongue and a hunger for things people keep in boxes. Your disguise is perfect. Your patience needs work.

BODY: A tongue and pseudopods serve as hands. Cannot wear gear, but can store a great deal inside. A muffled, echoing voice, as if from inside a box.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Adventurers poke you with a ten-foot pole on principle. Merchants check their own stock twice. The Phantom Merchant's people have asked, politely, whether you take contracts.

RACIAL TRAIT: A nose for small fortunes: every so often you turn up a coin, a ring, or an odd trinket that turns up inside you.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Fang and Claw +2 and Uncanny Body +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

EVOLUTION: At level 15 you become a Greater Mimic and gain Snapping Lid. At level 35 you choose a path by typing it: "evolve vault" for Vault Mimic, or "evolve shape" for Shapeshifter Mimic. At level 60 that path reaches its final form: Living Treasury or Doppel-Mimic.

RACE REFERENCE: Mimic is a shapeshifting ambush creature whose resting form is a chest. Use patience, hoarding, disguise, and loneliness inside a perfect disguise as background hooks.

Skeleton.name: Skeleton
Skeleton.description:
No flesh, no pulse, no problem. You came back as a skeleton: bones, old armor, and blue lights where eyes used to be. You do not eat, sleep or tire, and you rattle slightly when you laugh. The living find you unsettling. You find them damp.

BODY: Hands work perfectly well, bony as they are; armor and weapons fit, mostly. Speech comes from nowhere in particular, a dry and oddly cheerful voice.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: The Church reaches for holy water. Necromancers ask who raised you, and do not believe the answer. Gravekeepers offer you a seat.

RACIAL TRAIT: Hard to finish: when your health falls to 10% or lower, you recover 25% of it at once. This can happen once every 50 turns.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Uncanny Body +3, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

EVOLUTION: At level 15 you become a Skeleton Knight and gain Fearless March. At level 35 you choose a path by typing it: "evolve knight" for Grave Knight, or "evolve mage" for Bone Mage. At level 60 that path reaches its final form: Dread Knight or Lich.

Minotaur.name: Minotaur
Minotaur.description:
Head of a bull, shoulders of a siege engine, sense of direction of a saint. You came back as a minotaur, born in a maze and incapable of being lost in one. People assume you are the monster at the center. For now, they are being unkind.

Ogre.name: Ogre
Ogre.description:
Big. That is the first thing, the second thing, and most of the third. You came back as an ogre: twice a man's height, grey-green, tusked, and far brighter than anyone expects from something that can lift a cart. Being underestimated is the only thing about you that is small.

BODY: Hands like shovels: strong, clumsy with small things. Needs everything made large. A rumbling voice.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Villagers hide the livestock. Mercenary captains make offers. The Oni-Blooded treat you as a rough sort of cousin.

Gargoyle.name: Gargoyle
Gargoyle.description:
Stone that woke up. You came back as a gargoyle: winged, horned, grey as a cathedral roof, and able to hold still for a week without minding. You spent your first days being rained on. You have views about gutters.

BODY: Clawed hands work well; heavy, and hard on furniture. Armor is pointless; cloaks are for dignity. A grinding, gravelly voice.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Priests are unsure whether you are a blessing or a problem with the roof. Thieves avoid your street. Architects ask who carved you, and you do not know.

A cat that lived long enough to grow a second tail and stop pretending. You came back as a nekomata: a large fork-tailed cat with lantern eyes, old enough in spirit to remember grudges and new enough at it to knock things off shelves. Graveyards make you feel oddly at home.

Tengu.description:
Mountain goblin, crow spirit, the worst sword teacher in the world and the best. You came back as a tengu: black-winged, beak-faced, perched on a pine and judging everyone's footwork. Monasteries warn novices about your kind. The good ones come looking anyway.

Kappa.name: Kappa
Kappa.description:
River imp, wrestler, obsessive about manners. You came back as a kappa: green, shelled, beaked, with a dish of water on your head that you guard with your life. You will challenge strangers to sumo. You will also set their broken bones afterward, free of charge.

BODY: Webbed hands are strong and deft. The shell replaces armor. A croaking, formal voice.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Farmers leave cucumbers at the bank. Wrestlers accept the challenge and lose. Healers are startled to learn where half their bone-setting came from.

RACIAL TRAIT: A hard body turns part of every blow: 10% of the health you lose each turn is restored at the end of it.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Charge and Crush +2 and Fang and Claw +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

Jorōgumo.name: Jorōgumo
Jorōgumo.description:
The spider the waterfall stories warn about. You came back as a jorōgumo: a golden orb-weaver the size of a carriage wheel, striped black and yellow, whose silk shines like koto strings. Travelers hear music near your web. It is a very effective web.

BODY: No hands; legs and silk do exquisite work, including playing strings. Wears nothing; decorates everything. A low, musical voice.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Woodcutters avoid your falls. Musicians come anyway. Great Spiders and Arachne-Kin treat you as nobility.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Fang and Claw +2 and Uncanny Body +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

At level 35 you choose a path by typing it: "evolve golden" for Golden Web Jorōgumo, or "evolve falls" for Deep Falls Jorōgumo. At level 60 that path reaches its final form: Jorōgumo of the Golden Loom or Jorōgumo of the Deep Falls.

Nue.description:
Nobody agrees on what you are, which is the point. You came back as a nue: a monkey's face, a tiger's limbs, a tanuki's body, a snake for a tail, arriving in a black cloud with a cry like a thrush. Courts have fallen ill just from hearing your kind at night.

BODY: Forepaws grip clumsily; the snake tail has its own reach and temper. Wears nothing. A thin, eerie voice, and the tail hisses commentary.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Palace guards loose arrows at the sound of you. Onmyoji-style exorcists want you named and bound. Those already called ill omens feel oddly seen.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Fang and Claw +3, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

Elemental Spirit.name: Elemental Spirit
Elemental Spirit.description:
Not a body. A phenomenon with opinions. You came back as an elemental spirit: a living knot of flame, water, wind, stone, frost or lightning, shaped more or less like whatever you were thinking about. Name your element when you describe yourself. The world will work around it.

BODY: No true hands: you shape the element to push, lift or hold, and it shows. Cannot wear gear; objects you carry must survive your element. A voice like your element makes.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Mages want a contract. Shrine keepers offer a home. Ordinary people react mostly to whether you are the burning kind.

RACIAL TRAIT: What hurts you feeds you: 25% of the health you lose each turn returns as Mana.

Dryad.description:
A tree that decided to see the world. You came back as a dryad: bark for skin, leaves for hair, sap for blood, and roots that would really prefer you sat down. You bloom when you are happy, which makes poker difficult.

BODY: Twig-fingered hands are gentle and capable. Wears woven things and flowers, not metal. A rustling, unhurried voice.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: The Verdant Throne treats you as a relative. Woodcutters put down their axes, sheepishly. Herbalists follow you around with baskets.

RACIAL TRAIT: Your body knits itself: you recover 1% of your health every turn while hurt.

Will-o'-Wisp.name: Will-o'-Wisp
Will-o'-Wisp.description:
A light in the marsh that people are told never to follow. You came back as a will-o'-wisp: a floating flame the size of a lantern, with no body to speak of and nowhere you cannot go. You could lead travelers astray. You could also lead them home. The Spiritfen is waiting to see which.

BODY: No body at all: you nudge small things with warmth and will, and pass through gaps. Cannot wear or carry much. A faint chiming voice.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Lanternkeepers greet you as kin. Lost travelers follow you gratefully, which is a responsibility. Exorcists hesitate.

RACIAL TRAIT: What hurts you feeds you: 25% of the health you lose each turn returns as Mana.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Uncanny Body +2 and Wing and Dive +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

EVOLUTION: At level 15 you become a Lantern Wisp and gain Ghost Flicker. At level 35 you choose a path by typing it: "evolve guiding" for Guiding Light Wisp, or "evolve grave" for Grave Light Wisp. At level 60 that path reaches its final form: Star Lantern or Soul Lantern.

Draw this body exactly; never give it a human face, human skin or a human figure it does not have. Appearance picks made for humanoids apply only where this body has the matching part: hair picks color the mane, crest, fur, feathers or glow; skin tone picks color the hide, scales, shell or surface; outfit picks become harness, barding, collar, cloth or ornament this body can wear; picks with no matching part are left out. Always a fully grown adult of its kind.

RACE REFERENCE: Will-o'-Wisp is a floating spirit light of the marshes. Use lantern-lit paths, the lost and the dead, guidance or mischief, and being a light with no hands as background hooks.

Golem.name: Golem
Golem.description:
Someone carved a word into stone and the stone woke up. You came back as a golem: clay, rock or iron in a rough body-shape, with a glowing word-seal for a heart and no memory of who wrote it. You do not get tired. You are beginning to get curious.

BODY: Thick fingers: immense strength, little finesse. Needs no armor. A slow grinding voice that learned speech by listening.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Mages ask whose you are. Builders offer wages. The Church checks your seal for forbidden letters.

RACIAL TRAIT: A hard body turns part of every blow: 15% of the health you lose each turn is restored at the end of it.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Charge and Crush +2 and Uncanny Body +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

Living Armor.name: Living Armor
Living Armor.description:
A suit of plate with nobody home, except you. You came back as living armor: an empty helm with a light inside, gauntlets that close on a hilt, and a hollow ring when you knock on your own chest. Somebody once wore you into a battle. You would like to know how it ended.

BODY: Gauntlets work as hands. You are the armor; you can hold a shield and weapon but wear nothing more than a cloak or tabard. An echoing voice from inside the helm.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Knights salute before they notice. Smiths want to look at your joins. The Church sprinkles holy water and is annoyed when nothing happens.

Marionette.name: Marionette
Marionette.description:
A doll that cut its own strings. You came back as a marionette: jointed wood and porcelain, painted eyes that follow people, and a grace no living body could manage. Somebody made you to perform. The show is whatever you decide it is now.

BODY: Jointed hands are precise and tireless. Wears clothes like anyone, and cracks instead of bleeding. A clear, slightly hollow voice.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Theaters want to hire you. Superstitious folk cross the street. Collectors name prices, and the Porcelain Gallery's keepers go very quiet.

Tsukumogami.name: Tsukumogami
Tsukumogami.description:
A hundred years of being used, and then one morning you had opinions. You came back as a tsukumogami: an old object that woke up. A sword, a lantern, an umbrella, a tea kettle, a koto, a mirror. Say which when you describe yourself. You remember every hand that ever held you.

BODY: What you can do depends on what you are: a lantern lights, a sword cuts, a kettle pours. Most forms hop, float or are carried. A voice suited to the object.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: People are startled, then oddly polite. Antique dealers go pale. Shrines hold ceremonies for objects like you and will find you a seat.

Clockwork Beast.name: Clockwork Beast
Clockwork Beast.description:
Brass, springs, and a mainspring that started ticking in time with a soul. You came back as a clockwork beast: a mechanical hound, cat, hawk or stag built by a craftsman who never expected it to look back. Say which beast when you describe yourself. Please do not let anyone wind you too tight.

BODY: Whatever the beast shape allows: jaws, talons or paws, all exact. Carries tools in a chest compartment. A voice like a music box with words.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Artificers want to open you up, kindly or otherwise. The Cinderborn Compact offers you a workshop. Animals are deeply suspicious.

RACIAL TRAIT: A hard body turns part of every blow: 10% of the health you lose each turn is restored at the end of it.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Fang and Claw +2 and Charge and Crush +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

Rune Sentinel.name: Rune Sentinel
Rune Sentinel.description:
A guardian nobody remembered to relieve. You came back as a rune sentinel: a ring of floating carved stones around a core of light, built to watch a door that fell down centuries ago. Your orders are illegible. You have decided to write new ones.

BODY: No hands: you move things with short pulses of force and carve with light. Wears nothing. A calm, layered voice, as if several stones spoke at once.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Scholars follow you taking rubbings. The Depthwarden Circle recognizes the script and will not say from where. Thieves give you a wide berth.

RACIAL TRAIT: What hurts you feeds you: 25% of the health you lose each turn returns as Mana.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Charge and Crush +2 and Uncanny Body +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

EVOLUTION: At level 15 you become a Greater Sentinel and gain Rune Lance. At level 35 you choose a path by typing it: "evolve ward" for Ward Sentinel, or "evolve cannon" for Glyph Cannon. At level 60 that path reaches its final form: Bastion Glyph or Rune Annihilator.

Draw this body exactly; never give it a human face, human skin or a human figure it does not have. Appearance picks made for humanoids apply only where this body has the matching part: hair picks color the mane, crest, fur, feathers or glow; skin tone picks color the hide, scales, shell or surface; outfit picks become harness, barding, collar, cloth or ornament this body can wear; picks with no matching part are left out. Free Construct.description:
Somebody built you. What they built is up to you. Free Construct is the open frame: an artificial being whose shape, materials and purpose come from your own description. A walking suit of crystal, a swarm of brass insects, a paper crane the size of a horse, a clay figure with flowers growing out of it. Write it, and that is what you are.

BODY: Whatever your described body allows, no more and no less. If you did not describe hands, you do not have them. Voice as described.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: People react to what they see: a marvel, a weapon, a toy, or someone's missing property. Artificers always want to know who made you.

RACIAL TRAIT: A hard body turns part of every blow: 10% of the health you lose each turn is restored at the end of it.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Uncanny Body +2 and Charge and Crush +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

Talking Cat.description:
You died, there was a light, and now you are a cat. A normal-looking cat, with a normal cat's size and an entirely abnormal ability to say exactly what you think. Witches would sign a contract for you in a heartbeat. You would like to read the contract first.

BODY: Paws: you open doors, knock things over and steal fish. No gear beyond a collar or satchel. Speaks perfectly, usually at the worst moment.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Most people talk to you before realizing you will answer. Witches and mages make offers. Catkin are personally offended and cannot say why.

RACIAL TRAIT: Hard to finish: when your health falls to 10% or lower, you recover 20% of it at once. This can happen once every 60 turns.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Fang and Claw +3, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

A small white fox with a red bib and a job. You came back as a spirit fox, the kind that sits at shrine gates carrying messages between people and whatever answers prayers. You are not the nine-tailed legend. You are the one who actually delivers the mail.

RACIAL TRAIT: Mana gathers in you on its own: you recover 2% of your Mana every turn.

Storm Raven.name: Storm Raven
Storm Raven.description:
Black feathers, bright eyes, and a memory for faces that should worry people. You came back as a storm raven: a large raven that rides ahead of bad weather and knows more than it lets on. Battlefields, crossroads and gallows have always belonged to your kind. So have secrets.

BODY: Beak and talons: you carry small things, untie knots and pick locks badly. A leg-band at most. A croaking voice that mimics others unsettlingly well.
