Feature - Moss and Wildflowers.description: Moss, small ferns or flowers growing on you, well tended or otherwise.
Feature - Moss and Wildflowers.traitNarrativeEffects: CREATURE FEATURE (visual only, no stats): render moss, small ferns and wildflowers growing on the body, on the body this race actually has.

Feature - Jeweled Brow.name: Feature - Jeweled Brow
Feature - Jeweled Brow.description: A gemstone set in the forehead, grown rather than mounted.
Feature - Jeweled Brow.traitNarrativeEffects: CREATURE FEATURE (visual only, no stats): render a gemstone set naturally in the brow, on the body this race actually has.

Feature - Tattered Wings.name: Feature - Tattered Wings
Feature - Tattered Wings.description: Wings with ragged edges and old tears. They still work.
Feature - Tattered Wings.traitNarrativeEffects: CREATURE FEATURE (visual only, no stats): render wings with ragged edges and old healed tears, on the body this race actually has.

Size - Small Enough to Carry.name: Size - Small Enough to Carry
Size - Small Enough to Carry.description: About the size of a house cat. You fit in a satchel and you know it. Up side: you fit anywhere, hide easily and get overlooked. Down side: you cannot reach, lift or block anything, and nobody takes you seriously until you make them.
Size - Small Enough to Carry.traitNarrativeEffects: CREATURE FEATURE (visual only, no stats): render a small adult creature about the size of a house cat, on the body this race actually has. SIZE IN PLAY (no stat change): hiding, squeezing through gaps and going unnoticed are one tier easier; lifting, shoving, intimidating and anything that needs reach or weight are one tier harder. People overlook it, pick it up without asking, and are slow to believe it is dangerous.

Size - Wolf-Sized.name: Size - Wolf-Sized
Size - Wolf-Sized.description: About the size of a large wolf. The middle road: you fit through doors, ride in a cart and can drag a person, with no special advantage and no special trouble.
Size - Wolf-Sized.traitNarrativeEffects: CREATURE FEATURE (visual only, no stats): render an adult creature about the size of a large wolf, on the body this race actually has. SIZE IN PLAY (no stat change): no modifiers. It fits where a person fits.

Size - Horse-Sized.name: Size - Horse-Sized
Size - Horse-Sized.description: About the size of a warhorse. Up side: you can carry a rider, break a door and block a road. Down side: indoors is a negotiation, hiding in a street is not happening, and you eat like three people.
Size - Horse-Sized.traitNarrativeEffects: CREATURE FEATURE (visual only, no stats): render an adult creature about the size of a warhorse, on the body this race actually has. SIZE IN PLAY (no stat change): carrying riders, breaking barriers and intimidating are one tier easier; hiding, moving quietly indoors and delicate work are one tier harder. Most doors, stairs and boats are a problem to solve.

Size - Towering.name: Size - Towering
Size - Towering.description: Taller than a house door by a good margin. Ceilings are a consideration. Up side: you are seen and feared from a distance, you move what nothing else can, and walls are a step. Down side: you cannot enter most buildings or hide at all, and feeding you is a question of logistics.
Size - Towering.traitNarrativeEffects: CREATURE FEATURE (visual only, no stats): render a towering adult creature, far taller than a doorway, on the body this race actually has. SIZE IN PLAY (no stat change): feats of raw force, breaking structures and frightening crowds are two tiers easier; hiding in the open is impossible, fine work is two tiers harder, and buildings, tunnels, ships and bridges may simply not take it. Its arrival is news in every town within a day.

Portrait Frame - Creature Full Form.name: Portrait Frame - Creature Full Form
Portrait Frame - Creature Full Form.description: FRAME LOCK TEXT: Full-form creature portrait of [character name]: the entire body in three-quarter side view, every part of it inside the frame, on visible ground with clear space on every side.
Portrait Frame - Creature Full Form.traitNarrativeEffects: FRAME LOCK: mandatory whole-creature illustration in three-quarter side view. This is the final camera and composition authority. Show the complete body the creature actually has, from its head to its farthest end, with every part inside the canvas and no edge contact. Add no wings, tail, horns or limbs that its description does not give it. Keep the creature at roughly 60-70 percent of the canvas along its longest dimension, with visible ground or resting surface beneath it and clear space around it. Reject head-only, bust, cropped-body and extreme close-up framing. The selected Portrait Style and scene detail cannot override this frame.

Portrait Frame - Creature Close Study.name: Portrait Frame - Creature Close Study
Portrait Frame - Creature Close Study.description: FRAME LOCK TEXT: Close creature study of [character name]: head, neck and forequarters, with the eyes as the focal point and a readable piece of the selected background behind.
Portrait Frame - Creature Close Study.traitNarrativeEffects: FRAME LOCK: close creature study. This is the final camera and composition authority. Frame the complete head and the front or upper part of the body, with everything that rises from the head fully inside the frame. Keep the eyes and the texture of the surface sharp and dominant, with a small readable portion of the selected Scene Background. Do not pull back to the whole body and do not crop the top of the head. The selected Portrait Style and scene detail cannot override this frame.

Portrait Frame - Creature in Its Lair.name: Portrait Frame - Creature in Its Lair
Portrait Frame - Creature in Its Lair.description: FRAME LOCK TEXT: Wide lair shot of [character name]: the whole creature at home in the selected scene, small enough in frame that the place reads as theirs.
Portrait Frame - Creature in Its Lair.traitNarrativeEffects: FRAME LOCK: wide environmental creature shot. This is the final camera and composition authority. Show the complete creature at roughly 35-45 percent of canvas height, settled or standing inside the selected Scene Background, with the environment fully readable around it: floor, walls or horizon, light source. The whole body stays inside the canvas. Do not move the camera closer or crop the creature. The selected Portrait Style and scene detail cannot override this frame.

Portrait Frame - Creature Size Reference.name: Portrait Frame - Creature Size Reference
Portrait Frame - Creature Size Reference.description: FRAME LOCK TEXT: Scale portrait of [character name]: the whole creature beside an ordinary person-sized object, such as a doorway, a cart or a lantern post, so its true size is unmistakable.
Portrait Frame - Creature Size Reference.traitNarrativeEffects: FRAME LOCK: whole-creature scale illustration. This is the final camera and composition authority. Show the complete creature beside one clearly person-sized object from the selected scene (a doorway, cart, lantern post, bench or fence) so its true size reads at a glance. No people in the frame. The whole body and the reference object stay inside the canvas with ground visible beneath both. The selected Portrait Style and scene detail cannot override this frame.

Portrait Frame - Creature in Motion.name: Portrait Frame - Creature in Motion
Portrait Frame - Creature in Motion.description: FRAME LOCK TEXT: Motion portrait of [character name]: the whole creature caught mid-movement, the way its own body moves, with the entire body inside the frame.
Portrait Frame - Creature in Motion.traitNarrativeEffects: FRAME LOCK: whole-creature motion illustration. This is the final camera and composition authority. Show the complete creature mid-movement in the way its own body moves: running, leaping, coiling, flowing, rolling, or flying only if it has wings. Every part of the body stays inside the canvas with clear space in the direction of travel. Add no wings, tail or limbs that its description does not give it. Keep the head and eyes readable. Reject cropped-body and head-only framing. The selected Portrait Style and scene detail cannot override this frame.

Axe Reaver.name: Axe Reaver
Axe Reaver.description:
Where a swordsman fences, an Axe Reaver fells. Axe fighters treat a battle like a stand of timber: read the grain, pick the cut, and put the whole body through it. Timber Strike opens a guard the way a wedge opens a log, Hewing Sweep clears the space around you, and the hooked beard of the axe pulls shields, ankles and weapons out of where their owners wanted them. It is not an elegant style. It is the style still standing when the elegant ones have run out of room.

Primary Attribute: Strength
Secondary Attribute: Charisma
Axe Reaver.traitNarrativeEffects: You judge doors, shields and people by where they would split, you keep your edge sharper than your manners, and you have never once called an axe a tool in front of company.

Skirmisher.name: Skirmisher
Skirmisher.description:
You win fights from six paces back. A Skirmisher throws: knives, javelins, shuriken, axes, whatever balances, and never stands where the answer lands. Quick Toss punishes anyone who looks away, Scatter Throw makes a doorway a bad place to stand, and by the time a line closes the distance it is a shorter line. Other fighters carry a weapon. You carry twelve, and you expect to get most of them back.

Primary Attribute: Dexterity
Secondary Attribute: Strength
Skirmisher.traitNarrativeEffects: You judge every object by how it would fly, you never sit with your throwing arm against a wall, and you retrieve your knives from targets, doorframes and the occasional ceiling without comment.

Psion.name: Psion
Psion.description:
No chant, no circle, no element. A Psion's weapon is attention. You speak into minds across a crowded room, feel the word somebody is about to say, and move the world with the effort other people spend on lifting a cup. Mind Speech makes you the best coordinated person in any party; Force Push makes you the reason nobody stands near a ledge. The Academy calls it a minor school. The Academy has never been thrown across a lecture hall by a first-year.

Primary Attribute: Intelligence
Secondary Attribute: Wisdom
Psion.traitNarrativeEffects: You answer questions half a beat before they are asked, small objects drift toward your hand when you are distracted, and you have learned to knock on a mind before you speak into it.

Stalking Predator.name: Stalking Predator
Stalking Predator.description:
CREATURE CALLING. You hunt the way your body was built to: downwind, low, patient, and then very suddenly not patient at all. A Stalking Predator fights with claw, fang and timing, picks the weakest point in a line the way a wolf picks the slowest deer, and has never needed a blacksmith. Written for true monster, beast and familiar bodies; a beastkin who takes it fights like the animal in their blood.

Primary Attribute: Strength
Secondary Attribute: Dexterity
Stalking Predator.traitNarrativeEffects: You go still before you move, you notice who in a room is limping, and you eat like something that is not sure when the next meal is.

Siege Beast.name: Siege Beast
Siege Beast.description:
CREATURE CALLING. Some bodies are arguments that walls lose. A Siege Beast fights with weight: the tackle, the charge, the long run-up that ends with something large becoming several smaller things. You do not fence, feint or flank. You arrive. Written for anything with horns, hooves, bulk or a shell; the bigger you are, the more this calling forgives.

Primary Attribute: Constitution
Secondary Attribute: Strength
Siege Beast.traitNarrativeEffects: You test floors before you trust them, doorframes remember you, and you have learned to walk at the back of a crowd so nobody is behind you when you stop.

Skyhunter.name: Skyhunter
Skyhunter.description:
CREATURE CALLING. The ground is where your prey lives; you only visit. A Skyhunter fights from height with the buffet, the swoop and the long dive, strikes once in passing and is gone before the answer arrives. Open sky makes you terrifying and a low ceiling makes you thoughtful. Written for anything that flies, wings or no wings.

Primary Attribute: Dexterity
Secondary Attribute: Wisdom
Skyhunter.traitNarrativeEffects: You look up before you look around, you measure every room by its rafters, and you sleep best somewhere nothing can reach without climbing.

Aberrant.name: Aberrant
Aberrant.description:
CREATURE CALLING. Your body does not follow the rules, and you have stopped apologizing for it. An Aberrant fights with whatever its shape allows: hardening against a blow, flattening under a door, catching a sword in itself and keeping it. Slimes, golems, living armor, loose bones, spirits of flame and things made of string all find a home here. Written for bodies no fencing manual has a chapter on.

Primary Attribute: Constitution
Secondary Attribute: Intelligence
Aberrant.traitNarrativeEffects: You forget which of your habits unsettle people, you rest in shapes nobody else would call comfortable, and healers examining you tend to start with a long pause.

Wild Hunter.name: Wild Hunter
Wild Hunter.description:
CREATURE TRADE. You feed yourself. A Wild Hunter knows game trails, wind, water, the hour each animal drinks, and how to take prey without a guild contract or a kitchen. For a monster this is simply being alive; for the people who meet you it is the difference between a creature that raids henhouses and one that keeps the wolves off the road. Works for any body that eats.

Primary Attribute: Constitution
Wild Hunter.traitNarrativeEffects: You know where the nearest water is at all times, you read tracks the way other people read signs, and you find it strange that anyone pays for meat.

Hoard Keeper.name: Hoard Keeper
Hoard Keeper.description:
CREATURE TRADE. Dragons keep gold, magpies keep buttons, mimics keep whatever was in the last chest, and you keep a hoard. A Hoard Keeper can smell value, remembers every piece in the pile and who it came from, and tells a true relic from a gilded fake by weight and temperature. Merchants find you unnerving to haggle with. Adventurers find out that a creature with a hoard is a creature that will trade.

Primary Attribute: Wisdom
Hoard Keeper.traitNarrativeEffects: You count things when you are nervous, you notice jewelry before faces, and you have never once thrown anything away.

Territory Warden.name: Territory Warden
Territory Warden.description:
CREATURE TRADE. Somewhere there is a stretch of forest, a cave system, a bridge or a rooftop district that is yours, and things that live there live there on your terms. A Territory Warden knows every path in its range, notices anything out of place by morning, and has an understanding with the neighbors, the travelers and the local guard that everyone finds easier than the alternative. Villages have paid tribute for less protection.

Primary Attribute: Charisma
Territory Warden.traitNarrativeEffects: You patrol without meaning to, you mark what is yours in ways people mostly do not notice, and you take trespass personally.

Guitar.name: Guitar
Guitar.description:
Six strings and a hollow body that fills a room without help. The guitar is the instrument of porches, campfires and the second verse everyone joins in on, and it travels better than anything else that can hold a whole song by itself.

Primary Attribute: Charisma
Guitar.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist's selected signature instrument is a six-string wooden guitar. Keep its recognizable form when this signature choice is depicted; do not replace it with a sword, a staff or a different instrument. PERFORMANCE: Describe playing through strummed chords, picked runs and a hand drummed on the body between verses. WEAPON SKILL: Supports performance. It can focus bard abilities or Sound Magic the character actually knows; selection alone grants no spells, buffs, healing, damage or emotional control. This signature selection takes priority over any generic instrument implied by a class or profession.

Stormstring Guitar.name: Stormstring Guitar
Stormstring Guitar.description:
An Aetherglass invention that the conservatories are still pretending not to like: a solid guitar strung with lightning-treated wire and fed through a mana crystal the size of a palm. It is very loud. Crowds in three regions have decided that is a virtue.

Primary Attribute: Charisma
Stormstring Guitar.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist's selected signature instrument is a solid-bodied stormstring guitar wired to a palm-sized mana crystal amplifier. Keep its recognizable form when this signature choice is depicted; do not replace it with a sword, a staff or a different instrument. PERFORMANCE: Describe playing through ringing sustained notes, crunching chords, feedback hum and the crack of a lightning-treated string. WEAPON SKILL: Supports performance. It can focus bard abilities or Sound Magic the character actually knows; selection alone grants no spells, buffs, healing, damage or emotional control. This signature selection takes priority over any generic instrument implied by a class or profession.

Lyre.name: Lyre
Lyre.description:
The oldest instrument the shrines still tune by ear: a curved frame, a handful of strings, and a sound like light on water. Hymns, epics and lullabies were all written for it first.

Primary Attribute: Charisma
Lyre.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist's selected signature instrument is a small hand lyre. Keep its recognizable form when this signature choice is depicted; do not replace it with a sword, a staff or a different instrument. PERFORMANCE: Describe playing through plucked arpeggios, drone strings and slow shining chords. WEAPON SKILL: Supports performance. It can focus bard abilities or Sound Magic the character actually knows; selection alone grants no spells, buffs, healing, damage or emotional control. This signature selection takes priority over any generic instrument implied by a class or profession.

Zither.name: Zither
Zither.description:
A long board of silk strings and movable bridges, played kneeling, with picks on three fingers. The zither is the sound of tea houses, moon-viewing and court evenings, and it can be made to sound like rain on demand.

Primary Attribute: Charisma
Zither.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist's selected signature instrument is a long floor zither with movable bridges. Keep its recognizable form when this signature choice is depicted; do not replace it with a sword, a staff or a different instrument. PERFORMANCE: Describe playing through plucked glides, bent notes, sweeping runs across the strings. WEAPON SKILL: Supports performance. It can focus bard abilities or Sound Magic the character actually knows; selection alone grants no spells, buffs, healing, damage or emotional control. This signature selection takes priority over any generic instrument implied by a class or profession.

Tambourine.name: Tambourine
Tambourine.description:
A frame, a skin and a ring of brass jingles: the instrument that turns a song into a dance. Light, loud and impossible to play while standing still.

Primary Attribute: Charisma
Tambourine.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist's selected signature instrument is a hand tambourine with brass jingles. Keep its recognizable form when this signature choice is depicted; do not replace it with a sword, a staff or a different instrument. PERFORMANCE: Describe playing through shaken shimmer, thumb rolls and sharp struck accents. WEAPON SKILL: Supports performance. It can focus bard abilities or Sound Magic the character actually knows; selection alone grants no spells, buffs, healing, damage or emotional control. This signature selection takes priority over any generic instrument implied by a class or profession.

Maracas.name: Maracas
Maracas.description:
Two dried gourds full of seeds and a great deal of opinion about tempo. Maracas are the heartbeat of harbor dances along the Cerulean Coast, and the reason nobody there claps on the wrong beat twice.

Primary Attribute: Charisma
Maracas.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist's selected signature instrument is a pair of seed-filled maracas. Keep its recognizable form when this signature choice is depicted; do not replace it with a sword, a staff or a different instrument. PERFORMANCE: Describe playing through crisp shaken rhythms, rolls and offbeat accents. WEAPON SKILL: Supports performance. It can focus bard abilities or Sound Magic the character actually knows; selection alone grants no spells, buffs, healing, damage or emotional control. This signature selection takes priority over any generic instrument implied by a class or profession.

Suzu Bells.name: Suzu Bells
Suzu Bells.description:
A handle, three tiers of small bells and five long ribbons: the instrument of shrine dance. Each shake is a clean bright sheet of sound, and the pauses matter as much as the bells.

Primary Attribute: Charisma
Suzu Bells.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist's selected signature instrument is a handheld tree of suzu bells with long ribbons. Keep its recognizable form when this signature choice is depicted; do not replace it with a sword, a staff or a different instrument. PERFORMANCE: Describe playing through measured shakes, cascades of small bells and the stillness between them. WEAPON SKILL: Supports performance. It can focus bard abilities or Sound Magic the character actually knows; selection alone grants no spells, buffs, healing, damage or emotional control. This signature selection takes priority over any generic instrument implied by a class or profession.

Piano.name: Piano
Piano.description:
The Emberglass makers answered a dare and built a piano that folds: four octaves, trestle legs and a case one strong person can carry. Taverns with no instrument of their own book the player before they book the room.

Primary Attribute: Charisma
Piano.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist's selected signature instrument is a folding traveling piano on trestle legs. Keep its recognizable form when this signature choice is depicted; do not replace it with a sword, a staff or a different instrument. PERFORMANCE: Describe playing through running scales, block chords, a walking left hand and the thump of a pedal. WEAPON SKILL: Supports performance. It can focus bard abilities or Sound Magic the character actually knows; selection alone grants no spells, buffs, healing, damage or emotional control. This signature selection takes priority over any generic instrument implied by a class or profession.

Taiko Drum.name: Taiko Drum
Taiko Drum.description:
A barrel of a drum and two sticks as thick as a wrist. Taiko is played with the whole body, heard across a harbor, and felt in the chest of everyone standing closer than that.

Primary Attribute: Charisma
Taiko Drum.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist's selected signature instrument is a barrel-bodied taiko drum on a stand with two thick sticks. Keep its recognizable form when this signature choice is depicted; do not replace it with a sword, a staff or a different instrument. PERFORMANCE: Describe playing through rolling thunder, rim clicks, shouted counts and full-arm strikes. WEAPON SKILL: Supports performance. It can focus bard abilities or Sound Magic the character actually knows; selection alone grants no spells, buffs, healing, damage or emotional control. This signature selection takes priority over any generic instrument implied by a class or profession.

Natural Weapons: Fang and Claw.name: Natural Weapons: Fang and Claw
Natural Weapons: Fang and Claw.description:
No forge made your weapons. Claws, talons, fangs, beak, pincers or a barbed tail: whatever your body grew is what you fight with, and it has never once been left at home.

Primary Attribute: Strength
Natural Weapons: Fang and Claw.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist fights with the natural weapons of their own body: claws, talons, fangs, beak, pincers or a barbed tail. Describe combat through those, never through a held weapon they did not choose. WEAPON SKILL: Supports progression through Fang and Claw. Natural weapons cannot be disarmed, sold or enchanted like an item.

Natural Weapons: Horn and Hoof.name: Natural Weapons: Horn and Hoof
Natural Weapons: Horn and Hoof.description:
Your weapon is the run-up. Horns, hooves, a thick skull, a heavy shell or simply a great deal of you, delivered at speed to one place.

Primary Attribute: Constitution
Natural Weapons: Horn and Hoof.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist fights with the natural weapons of their own body: horns, hooves, shoulders, shell and sheer weight. Describe combat through those, never through a held weapon they did not choose. WEAPON SKILL: Supports progression through Charge and Crush. Natural weapons cannot be disarmed, sold or enchanted like an item.

Natural Weapons: Wing and Talon.name: Natural Weapons: Wing and Talon
Natural Weapons: Wing and Talon.description:
Your weapon is the sky and whatever you bring down out of it: the wing that staggers, the talon that takes, the dive nobody hears until it is over.

Primary Attribute: Dexterity
Natural Weapons: Wing and Talon.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist fights with the natural weapons of their own body: wings, talons and the height to use them. Describe combat through those, never through a held weapon they did not choose. WEAPON SKILL: Supports progression through Wing and Dive. Natural weapons cannot be disarmed, sold or enchanted like an item.

Natural Weapons: Living Body.name: Natural Weapons: Living Body
Natural Weapons: Living Body.description:
You are the weapon, all the way through. Slime that engulfs, stone that falls, armor with nobody inside it, flame that leans: a body that was never built like a body.

Primary Attribute: Constitution
Natural Weapons: Living Body.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist fights with the natural weapons of their own body: a body of slime, stone, wood, bone, metal, flame or light used as its own weapon. Describe combat through those, never through a held weapon they did not choose. WEAPON SKILL: Supports progression through Uncanny Body. Natural weapons cannot be disarmed, sold or enchanted like an item.

Psionic Affinity.name: Psionic Affinity
Psionic Affinity.description:
The mind itself answers you. Its territory is thought sent without sound, the surface of other minds, and matter moved by will: quiet, precise, and unsettling to people who assumed their thoughts were private. No element, no chant, no circle.

Primary Attribute: Intelligence
Psionic Affinity.traitNarrativeEffects: MAGIC AFFINITY REFERENCE: Use psionics for telepathy, surface thought sensing, telekinesis and psychic force. It reads and speaks; it does not charm, command or rewrite a mind. Keep it distinct from Charm, Illusion, Dream and Soul.

No Human Voice.name: No Human Voice
No Human Voice.description: Your body was not built for speech and nothing has fixed that yet. You understand every word. What comes out of you is a growl, a chirp, a hiss, a chime or silence, and the world has to be taught to read it. Made for true monster bodies; anyone else who takes it has lost their voice to a curse.
No Human Voice.traitNarrativeEffects: NARRATIVE FLAW: The protagonist understands speech but cannot produce it. Their intended words reach others only as animal sound, gesture, writing scratched in the dirt, or a telepathic ability they actually hold. Render what the player says as what the listener actually hears and sees, then let the listener interpret it, sometimes wrongly. Strangers never guess a mind is behind it without proof. Companions who learn to read them are a real bond. Play the gap for comedy and for loneliness, never as a reason to ignore what the player meant to do.

No Outfit: Bare Hide.name: No Outfit: Bare Hide
No Outfit: Bare Hide.description: Nothing worn at all: fur, scale, shell, stone or slime exactly as it is. For true monster bodies. A humanoid who picks this is given plain everyday clothes instead.
No Outfit: Bare Hide.traitNarrativeEffects: OUTFIT STYLE LOCK: appearance only, no item. Render a true-form creature with no clothing, armor, harness or accessories of any kind. For a humanoid body, render plain modest everyday clothes instead.

Harness and Satchel.name: Harness and Satchel
Harness and Satchel.description: A fitted leather harness with a satchel or saddlebags, sized for a body that walks on four legs, flies or coils. The working kit of a creature with errands.
Harness and Satchel.traitNarrativeEffects: OUTFIT STYLE LOCK: look as described. Its garment is the starting item Creature Harness; in play, describe what is worn now. Render a practical leather harness with a satchel or saddlebags fitted to the body this character actually has, and no clothing beyond it.

Collar and Name Tag.name: Collar and Name Tag
Collar and Name Tag.description: A good collar, a small bell or tag, and nothing else. It says somebody would notice if you went missing, whether or not that is true.
Collar and Name Tag.traitNarrativeEffects: OUTFIT STYLE LOCK: look as described. Its garment is the starting item Collar and Name Tag; in play, describe what is worn now. Render a single well-made collar with a small tag or bell on the body this character actually has, and no clothing beyond it.

Werewolf.name: Werewolf
Werewolf.description:
You are not a wolfkin. Wolfkin are born with the ears and keep them; you were born, or bitten, with a second shape folded inside the first. Most days you pass for human with eyes a shade too bright, a temper a shade too short, and a nose that knows who was in a room an hour ago. The war form is what the stories are about: taller, furred, clawed, and very hard to argue with. Old packs teach the change as a discipline. People who learned it alone tend to be found by a pack sooner or later, and not always a friendly one.

THE WAR FORM: You can take it by choice, and strong anger, fear or a full moon can pull it out of you. It lasts a scene, it is not subtle, and anyone who sees it sees a monster first. Clothes and armor not made for it do not survive it. It grants no extra stats; it changes what you are fighting with (Fang and Claw) and how the room reacts.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Beastkin clans can smell what you are and have opinions. The Church keeps a list. Hunters keep silver, which stings and scars but is not the instant death the ballads claim.

IMAGE GENERATION RULE: DEMI-HUMAN HUMANOID. Werewolves in everyday form look human with sharp canines, bright predatory eyes and a rangy athletic build; draw the everyday human form unless the scene is the war form. No wolf ears or tail in everyday form.

RACE REFERENCE: Werewolf is a human-shaped shapechanger with a hidden wolf war form. Use pack politics, the pull of the moon, scent, temper and the cost of being seen changed as background hooks.
Werewolf.traitNarrativeEffects: You sort a room by smell before you look at it, and you get restless when the moon is fat. WAR FORM: narrative only, no stat change; taken by choice or pulled out by strong emotion or a full moon, it lasts a scene and witnesses react to a monster. IMAGE GENERATION RULE: DEMI-HUMAN HUMANOID. Everyday form is human with sharp canines and bright eyes; no ears or tail unless the war form is the scene. RACE REFERENCE: Werewolf is a human-shaped shapechanger with a hidden wolf war form.

Bloodmoon Hybrid.name: Bloodmoon Hybrid
Bloodmoon Hybrid.description:
It is not supposed to happen. Vampire blood and wolf blood have been at war longer than most kingdoms have had names, and each side has a rule about the other that is older than its laws. You are what happens when the rule is broken: a vampire's thirst and stillness, a wolf's nose and temper, and a body that has never fully decided which it is. There may be a dozen of you alive. Both courts and every old pack would like to know where.

HIDDEN FORM: Fangs and claws come out together when you let go: a lean, pale, furred thing with too many teeth, neither one nor the other. By choice, under strong emotion, or when you have gone too long without feeding. It lasts a scene, grants no extra stats, and ends any hope of passing unnoticed.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: Covens call you an abomination and offer you a place at the table in the same breath. Packs smell the grave on you. Hunters are not sure which kit to bring, which is the only advantage you get.

IMAGE GENERATION RULE: DEMI-HUMAN HUMANOID. A Bloodmoon Hybrid in everyday form looks human: pale, sharp-featured, with fangs and bright ringed eyes; no bat body, no wolf head, and no fur unless the hidden form is the scene.

RACE REFERENCE: Bloodmoon Hybrid is a human-shaped crossblood of vampire and werewolf. Use divided loyalties, thirst against temper, being hunted by both sides, and the rarity of their kind as background hooks.
Bloodmoon Hybrid.traitNarrativeEffects: You hold very still when you are angry, which unsettles people more than shouting would, and you know by scent who in a room is bleeding. HIDDEN FORM: narrative only, no stat change; a pale furred fanged shape shown by choice, strong emotion or hunger for one scene. IMAGE GENERATION RULE: DEMI-HUMAN HUMANOID. Everyday form is human, pale and sharp-featured with fangs; no fur, wolf head or bat body unless the hidden form is the scene. RACE REFERENCE: Bloodmoon Hybrid is a human-shaped crossblood of vampire and werewolf.

Human Form.name: Human Form
Human Form.description: You have learned to fold your true body into a human-shaped one. It is still you: the marks of what you are always show, and the story names them the first time you change. In human form you are person-sized with working hands. You fit through doors, sit in chairs, and can wear and use gear made for people. What only your true body can do (flight, breath, sheer size) waits until you change back. Changing either way takes your full attention for a moment, and armor made for people does not follow you into your true form. From level 60 you can hide every mark but one. To change, say that you take your human form, or that you return to your true form. In a party, only the one who says it changes.
Human Form.traitNarrativeEffects: HUMAN FORM: the bearer can shift between their true body and a human-shaped one whenever they say so; in a fight it is their action for the turn. Never change their shape for them. The trait In Human Form is the record of their shape: while they hold it they are in human form, and without it they are in their true form. If they change shape in other words and the trait has not followed, narrate the change anyway and remind them of the two phrases: take my human form, return to my true form. IN HUMAN FORM: an adult human-shaped person who keeps the marks listed for their race on their Human Form Marks trait; below level 60 every mark shows, from level 60 they may hide all but one. Strangers see an unusual person, not a monster, and react to the marks. Gear made for people fits and works. Natural weapons are only what the form still carries; flight, breath, great size and other true-body features wait for the true form. No attribute, skill, health or Mana changes in either shape. CHANGING BACK: armor and clothing made for people come off or tear, and protect nothing until worn again in human form. At 0 health or in great pain the true form returns unasked.

Human Form Marks: Dragon Kind.name: Human Form Marks: Dragon Kind
Human Form Marks: Dragon Kind.description: The marks your human form keeps. The story named yours when you learned the change.
Human Form Marks: Dragon Kind.traitNarrativeEffects: MARKS THE HUMAN FORM KEEPS. Use the line for the bearer's own race and no other. True Dragon: swept-back horns, slit pupils, scales along the forearms and throat, and a tail you are still learning to sit down with. Wyvern: long arms with a leathery web from wrist to ribs, slit pupils, a barbed tail, and a rasp in the voice. Sea Serpent: sea-colored hair that never quite dries, scale-patterned skin at the neck, gill lines, and cold hands. Hydra: two-toned hair, mismatched eyes, scales at the collarbone, and a second voice that sometimes answers first. Sky Serpent: long trailing locks at the temples like whiskers, small antlers, pearl-bright eyes, and a breeze that follows you indoors. Fairy Dragon: a slight figure with wing-patterned eyes, a dusting of bright scales across the nose, and wings that show as a shimmer behind you.

Human Form Marks: Mythic Beast.name: Human Form Marks: Mythic Beast
Human Form Marks: Mythic Beast.description: The marks your human form keeps. The story named yours when you learned the change.
Human Form Marks: Mythic Beast.traitNarrativeEffects: MARKS THE HUMAN FORM KEEPS. Use the line for the bearer's own race and no other. Phoenix: hair like banked embers that brightens with your mood, warm skin, and feather-marks at the temples and wrists. Fenrir: wolf ears and tail, pale eyes, canines a touch too long, and frost on your breath. Griffin: feathered hair, golden raptor eyes, taloned fingertips, and a lion's tail. Kirin: a single small horn, pearl-scaled cheekbones, cloven prints wherever you walk barefoot, and flowers where you stood too long. Nine-Tailed Fox: fox ears, as many tails as you have earned, and eyes that laugh before you do. Thunderbird: storm-dark feathered hair, static in your touch, and eyes that flash a moment before thunder. Cerberus: three-colored hair, a collar-mark at the throat, heavy canines, and two extra shadows that do not always match. Behemoth: great height and breadth, curling horns, a voice felt in the chest, and floors that creak.

Human Form Marks: Dungeon-Born.name: Human Form Marks: Dungeon-Born
Human Form Marks: Dungeon-Born.description: The marks your human form keeps. The story named yours when you learned the change.
Human Form Marks: Dungeon-Born.traitNarrativeEffects: MARKS THE HUMAN FORM KEEPS. Use the line for the bearer's own race and no other. Slime: translucent blue-tinted hair, and skin that is cool, too smooth, and slow to hold its shape when you laugh. Goblin: a short wiry build, green-tinged skin at the ears and knuckles, pointed ears, and very sharp teeth. Kobold: a small quick build, scaled forearms, a short tail, slit eyes, and horn nubs you insist are still growing. Great Spider: six small extra eyes like beauty marks across the brow, long fingers, and silk at your fingertips. Mimic: a shape that is almost perfect, which is the unsettling part: a seam at the nape, too many teeth when you yawn, and pockets that are not pockets. Skeleton: a gaunt pale figure with dark-ringed eyes, cold hands, bone-white knuckles, and a faint rattle when you laugh. Minotaur: a tall broad-shouldered build, horns, a tufted tail, and a nose ring you could take out and do not. Ogre: head and shoulders over any crowd, tusks at the lower lip, hands like shovels, and a voice that carries through walls. Gargoyle: stone-grey skin with a fine grain, small horns, folded wings that pass for a heavy cloak, and perfect stillness.

Human Form Marks: Yokai and Spirit.name: Human Form Marks: Yokai and Spirit
Human Form Marks: Yokai and Spirit.description: The marks your human form keeps. The story named yours when you learned the change.
Human Form Marks: Yokai and Spirit.traitNarrativeEffects: MARKS THE HUMAN FORM KEEPS. Use the line for the bearer's own race and no other. Nekomata: cat ears, two tails, slit pupils, and a habit of sitting on things instead of at them. Tengu: black-feathered hair, a sharp profile, a red tint to the eyes, and wings folded small against the back. Kappa: green-tinged skin, webbed fingers, a shell-patterned back, and a dish-shaped cap you never take off. Jorōgumo: a striking figure in gold and black, extra eyes hidden under the fringe, and threads that follow your hands. Nue: features that do not quite agree with each other, tiger-striped forearms, and a braid that moves like a snake because it is one. Elemental Spirit: a body with your element still in it: hair of flame, water, wind or frost, skin like stone or cloud, eyes like lightning. Dryad: bark-brown or leaf-green skin, flowers and leaves in the hair that turn with the season, and rootlike veins at the wrists. Will-o'-Wisp: a pale, faintly luminous figure with hair that drifts as if underwater and a light behind the eyes that shows in the dark. Fairy: pointed ears, eyes that catch the light like dew, a dusting of glitter on the skin, and the ghost of your wings, a shimmer behind you.

Human Form Marks: Construct.name: Human Form Marks: Construct
Human Form Marks: Construct.description: The marks your human form keeps. The story named yours when you learned the change.
Human Form Marks: Construct.traitNarrativeEffects: MARKS THE HUMAN FORM KEEPS. Use the line for the bearer's own race and no other. Golem: stone- or clay-toned skin with seams at the joints, a rune at the brow, and a weight no chair expects. Living Armor: the figure your armor remembers: a face behind the visor at last, eyes like forge-light, and a plate-mail gait. Marionette: doll-smooth skin, ball-jointed fingers and wrists, glass-bright eyes, and movements a little too exact. Tsukumogami: a person shaped like your object's spirit: a lantern glows through the skin, a sword keeps its edge in the eyes, a kettle steams when angry. Clockwork Beast: brass-bright eyes, plates at the joints, the ears or tail of your beast shape, and a ticking heard in a quiet room. Rune Sentinel: carved lines of light under the skin, eyes that glow when you concentrate, and small stones that orbit when you forget yourself. Free Construct: your materials worn as a person: whatever you were built from shows at the hands, the eyes and the seams.

Human Form Marks: Familiar.name: Human Form Marks: Familiar
Human Form Marks: Familiar.description: The marks your human form keeps. The story named yours when you learned the change.
Human Form Marks: Familiar.traitNarrativeEffects: MARKS THE HUMAN FORM KEEPS. Use the line for the bearer's own race and no other. Talking Cat: cat ears, a tail with opinions, slit pupils, and exactly the same voice. Spirit Fox: fox ears, one tail, a bell at the throat, and blue fire at the fingertips when you are amused. Storm Raven: glossy black feathered hair, dark clever eyes, a cloak that is not a cloak, and a head-tilt you cannot stop. Carbuncle: soft features, long ears, the ruby still set in your forehead, and luck that visibly follows you. Academy Owl: large round amber eyes behind spectacles, feathered hair in tufts, and a head that turns further than it should.

In Human Form.name: In Human Form
In Human Form.description: You are in your human form right now. Say that you return to your true form to change back.
In Human Form.traitNarrativeEffects: CURRENT SHAPE: HUMAN FORM. The bearer is in their human form now: an adult human-shaped person carrying the marks listed for their race on their Human Form Marks trait. Gear made for people fits; true-body features are unavailable until they change back.

Shifted Shape.name: Shifted Shape
Shifted Shape.description: You are wearing a shape other than your own right now. Say that you change back, or return to your own form, to end it.
Shifted Shape.traitNarrativeEffects: CURRENT SHAPE: CHANGED. The bearer is transformed right now by their own ability or item; the summary and recent story name the shape. Write that body and only that body until they change back, and never change their shape for them. If the story plainly shows them in their own body, this mark is stale: write what the story shows.

Halfling.name: Halfling
Halfling.description:
Waist-high to a human and entirely grown. Halflings are a small, sturdy, barefoot people of Crownveil's farm roads, river barges and well-kept kitchens: quick hands, quiet feet, a second helping, and a streak of luck that taller folk find statistically offensive. They prize comfort, hospitality and a good story, and they are far braver than their size suggests. The ones who leave home tend to walk straight into trouble and come back with the best version of what happened. People underestimate you. You have learned to let them, right up until it stops being useful.

IMAGE GENERATION RULE: DEMI-HUMAN HUMANOID. A Halfling is a small adult, about waist-high to a human, and always drawn as a grown adult: adult face, adult proportions, only smaller. Sturdy build, curly hair, slightly pointed ears, often barefoot with hardy feet.

RACE REFERENCE: Halfling is a small-statured adult humanoid with a grown adult's face, a sturdy frame, deft hands and an easy smile. Use luck, hospitality, appetite, quiet courage and being underestimated as background hooks.
Halfling.traitNarrativeEffects: You know where the nearest kitchen is in any building, you are rarely the first one noticed in a room, and dropped bread lands butter side up for you. IMAGE GENERATION RULE: DEMI-HUMAN HUMANOID. A Halfling is a small adult, about waist-high to a human, and always drawn as a grown adult: adult face, adult proportions, only smaller. Sturdy build, curly hair, slightly pointed ears, often barefoot with hardy feet. RACE REFERENCE: Halfling is a small-statured adult humanoid with a grown adult's face, a sturdy frame, deft hands and an easy smile.

Giant-Blooded.name: Giant-Blooded
Giant-Blooded.description:
Head and shoulders above the tallest human, and built to the scale of the mountains your ancestors came down from. Giant blood means long bones, a reach that changes every fight, and a body that treats cold, altitude and heavy loads as ordinary weather. The high clans of the Yukishiro peaks keep their histories in carved stone and long memory: every deed is weighed, and a name is earned twice, once from your clan and once from yourself. Doorways are a negotiation. So are chairs, boats and other people's armor. You are slower to anger than anyone expects, and much harder to stop once you have decided.

IMAGE GENERATION RULE: DEMI-HUMAN HUMANOID. Giant-Blooded remain humanlike and well proportioned at seven to eight feet tall: broad shoulders, long limbs, strong hands, weathered skin, sometimes stone-grey markings along the arms or brow. No monster body, no ogre features, no horns.

RACE REFERENCE: Giant-Blooded is a very tall, powerfully built adult humanoid with a calm bearing and a long reach. Use scale, endurance, a mountain upbringing, carved clan histories and deliberate patience as background hooks.
Giant-Blooded.traitNarrativeEffects: You duck through doorways without noticing any more, you carry what two others cannot, and people step aside before they have decided to. IMAGE GENERATION RULE: DEMI-HUMAN HUMANOID. Giant-Blooded remain humanlike and well proportioned at seven to eight feet tall: broad shoulders, long limbs, strong hands, weathered skin, sometimes stone-grey markings along the arms or brow. No monster body, no ogre features, no horns. RACE REFERENCE: Giant-Blooded is a very tall, powerfully built adult humanoid with a calm bearing and a long reach.

Winged Kobold.name: Winged Kobold
Winged Kobold.description: Winged Kobold: the wings came in. A pair of leathery dragon wings, small for the body and entirely real. An optional evolution a Kobold can take from level 15 by typing "evolve wings". It is permanent and sits beside the main evolution line, so no later path takes it away. Bonuses: +3 Wing and Dive, the skill line for fighting from the air. You glide well and fly in short bursts; on the dragon path the wings grow strong enough for real flight.
Winged Kobold.traitNarrativeEffects: WINGED KOBOLD: this kobold has a pair of small leathery dragon wings. HARD LIMITS: it glides down from any height and flies in short hops only (a rooftop, a chasm, about a hundred paces). A longer flight gives out partway and ends in a forced landing, and it cannot lift or carry another person in the air: narrate both as failing, whatever the player declares. Only as a Dragon-Sworn Kobold or Kobold Dragon-Priest do the wings carry it in sustained flight. Draw and describe the wings, folded at the back or spread, on the same kobold body. Never humanize it.

Guild Rank: F.name: Guild Rank: F
Guild Rank: F.description: An old record of your Guild rank. Your rank now lives on the Guild card in your pack.
Guild Rank: F.traitNarrativeEffects: An F-Rank adventurer: rookie boards, rookie pay, and patient advice from the clerks. Assessments and deeds are how anyone proves more.

Guild Rank: E.name: Guild Rank: E
Guild Rank: E.description: An old record of your Guild rank. Your rank now lives on the Guild card in your pack.
Guild Rank: E.traitNarrativeEffects: An E-Rank adventurer: past the rookie filter. The clerks know the face, and the boards open onto real but controlled danger.

Guild Rank: D.name: Guild Rank: D
Guild Rank: D.description: An old record of your Guild rank. Your rank now lives on the Guild card in your pack.
Guild Rank: D.traitNarrativeEffects: A D-Rank adventurer: trusted with overnight work and real threats, and veterans have started remembering the name.

Guild Rank: C.name: Guild Rank: C
Guild Rank: C.description: An old record of your Guild rank. Your rank now lives on the Guild card in your pack.
Guild Rank: C.traitNarrativeEffects: A C-Rank professional: no rookie speeches, full Guild support, and the work careers are built on. Other parties ask to join.

Guild Rank: B.name: Guild Rank: B
Guild Rank: B.description: An old record of your Guild rank. Your rank now lives on the Guild card in your pack.
Guild Rank: B.traitNarrativeEffects: A B-Rank elite: staff know the name, hard contracts are offered here first, and younger adventurers watch how this one moves.

Guild Rank: A.name: Guild Rank: A
Guild Rank: A.description: An old record of your Guild rank. Your rank now lives on the Guild card in your pack.
Guild Rank: A.traitNarrativeEffects: An A-Rank adventurer, a strategic asset: the hall goes quiet, the branch master makes time at once, and headquarters tracks where they go.

Guild Rank: S.name: Guild Rank: S
Guild Rank: S.description: An old record of your Guild rank. Your rank now lives on the Guild card in your pack.
Guild Rank: S.traitNarrativeEffects: An S-Rank adventurer, a living legend: rooms part, the guild master comes down in person, and towns plan around the visit. Crown and Church court them, and watch.

Gnome.name: Gnome
Gnome.description:
Hip-high to a human and entirely grown. Gnomes are a small, quick-witted people of the Kurogane Deephollow, where Crystalvein City's workshops and the Deepmarket run on their gears, lenses and mana-coils. They take things apart to see why they work, put them back together better, and keep a pocket of spare screws for emergencies that have not happened yet. They are curious, stubborn and cheerfully unafraid of explosions that are only probably going to happen. Everyone assumes the gnome in the room is the apprentice. You have built half of what they are using.

IMAGE GENERATION RULE: DEMI-HUMAN HUMANOID. A Gnome is a small adult, about hip-high to a human, and always drawn as a grown adult: adult face, adult proportions, only smaller. Large bright eyes, a strong nose, rounded ears with a slight point, nimble hands, often goggles or a tool belt.

RACE REFERENCE: Gnome is a small-statured adult humanoid with a grown adult's face, bright eyes, clever hands and ink-stained fingers. Use invention, curiosity, tinkering, mana-tech and being mistaken for the apprentice as background hooks.
Gnome.traitNarrativeEffects: Any mechanism left alone near you is a mechanism you have already opened, and something in your pockets is always ticking. IMAGE GENERATION RULE: DEMI-HUMAN HUMANOID. A Gnome is a small adult, about hip-high to a human, and always drawn as a grown adult: adult face, adult proportions, only smaller. Large bright eyes, a strong nose, rounded ears with a slight point, nimble hands, often goggles or a tool belt. RACE REFERENCE: Gnome is a small-statured adult humanoid with a grown adult's face, bright eyes, clever hands and ink-stained fingers.

Druid.name: Druid
Druid.description:
The wild was never scenery to you. Druids keep the old bargain between people and the green: Thornbind to hold whatever threatens it, Wild Shape to run, fly or fight as the beasts do. You start small, a hound, a hawk, a wildcat, and grow into the bear and the stag, then into a swarm, then into shapes the forests only whisper about. Every shape is honest flesh with its own appetites. The trick is coming back as yourself.

Primary Attribute: Wisdom
Druid.traitNarrativeEffects: Birds land near you without being asked, you greet old trees by name, and now and then you forget which way your ears are supposed to point.

Draconic Awakening (active).name: Draconic Awakening (active)
Draconic Awakening (active).description: Draconic Awakening is active: Mana +150, Fire Magic +10, intimidation +10. It fades after 5 turns.
Draconic Awakening (active).traitNarrativeEffects: The dragon blood is awake: slit golden eyes, scales along the skin, heat coming off the body. Lesser creatures falter before it, and witnesses remember what they saw.

Blessing of the Mind's Eye.name: Blessing of the Mind's Eye
Blessing of the Mind's Eye.description: Your consciousness reaches past the bone of your skull. The Blessing of the Mind's Eye opens the silent third sight of psionics: you hear the surface cadence of nearby intentions, slip wordless commands beneath a guard's attention, and focus pure mental force into invisible blows or telekinetic wedges. As your mastery deepens, you link allies in silent tactical communion and shatter hostile focus from across a room. When you press deep, a pale silver ring blooms around your pupils and the air hums like struck glass.
Blessing of the Mind's Eye.traitNarrativeEffects: Small unsecured objects drift a finger's breadth toward your open hand when you are deep in thought, and liars avoid your eyes.

◈◈ Notable Boon: Awakened Synapse.name: ◈◈ Notable Boon: Awakened Synapse
◈◈ Notable Boon: Awakened Synapse.description: The static behind your eyes has cleared into a clean wire. Thought reaches outward with effortless precision.

◈◈ Notable Boon: Sanguine Conduit.name: ◈◈ Notable Boon: Sanguine Conduit
◈◈ Notable Boon: Sanguine Conduit.description: Your pulse answers the call before the cut is made. Every drop spent carries sharper weight and obedience.

Loot Goblin.name: Loot Goblin
Loot Goblin.description: If it gleams, rattles, or sits behind a lock, your fingers are already halfway to your pack before wisdom gets a vote.
Loot Goblin.traitNarrativeEffects: NARRATIVE FLAW: Unattended chests, bulging coin pouches, and glinting relics exert a physical pull on your attention. Walking past unsearched wreckage or leaving salvage behind takes visible effort, and companions and guards quickly notice your eyes weighing every pocket and display case.

Fairy.name: Fairy
Fairy.description:
Small enough to sleep in a teacup, proud enough to correct a dragon. You came back as a fairy: a hand-tall fae with insect wings and a trail of glittering dust, and a world built for giants is about to learn what it overlooked.

BODY: About a hand tall, with the proportions of a grown adult. Wings of your own kind carry you anywhere a bird can go: name them (butterfly, moth, dragonfly, beetle or something stranger) and they stay that way. Small hands handle small things well and large things not at all. You wear fairy-made clothes and thimble-sized gear; human gear does not fit. A clear, bell-bright voice much bigger than the body.

FAIRY DUST: Your wings shed a glittering dust, and you glow softly when you feel strongly. Use both for show whenever you like: a sparkle, a trail of light, a glow to read by. The ability Glamour Dust turns the dust into a trick that dazzles, distracts and makes one small lie look true.

HOW THE WORLD SEES YOU: People lower their voices so they will not blow you away, then tell you secrets they should not. Fairy-Blooded folk bow. The Verdant Throne remembers the old treaties with your kind. Cats are a problem.

RACIAL TRAIT: Your dust renews itself: you recover 2% of your Mana every turn.

NATURAL WEAPONS: You start trained in Wing and Dive +2 and Uncanny Body +1, the skill lines for attacking with the body you have. Their abilities unlock by themselves as the skills rise.

EVOLUTION: At level 15 you become a Glimmer Fairy and gain Guiding Light. At level 35 you choose a path by typing it: "evolve court" for Court Fairy, or "evolve wild" for Wildwing Fairy. At level 60 that path reaches its final form: Fae Sovereign or Storm Sprite.

IMAGE GENERATION RULE: TRUE FORM, NOT A HUMAN-SIZED PERSON. A fairy: a tiny fully grown adult humanoid about the height of a hand, with adult proportions and an adult face, delicate translucent insect wings of the kind the player named (iridescent butterfly-like wings if none was named), and a faint glow of fairy dust; drawn at true scale beside a flower, a leaf or a cupped hand. Appearance picks apply as for any person, at this size. Never childlike. Always a fully grown adult of its kind.

RACE REFERENCE: Fairy is a hand-sized adult fae with insect wings, fairy dust and a soft glow. Use the fae courts, old bargains, flowers and moonlight, being underestimated, and a world built for giants as background hooks.
Fairy.traitNarrativeEffects: You cannot pass a flower without checking who lives in it. BODY: A hand tall with a grown adult's proportions; wings of the kind the player named; small hands; fairy-sized gear, and human gear does not fit; a bell-bright voice. People know your kind talks. FAIRY DUST: the wings shed glittering dust and the body glows with strong feeling, usable for show at any time. WORLD: People lower their voices around you, then overshare. Fairy-Blooded folk bow. The Verdant Throne remembers the old treaties. Cats are a problem. IMAGE GENERATION RULE: TRUE FORM, NOT A HUMAN-SIZED PERSON. A fairy: a tiny fully grown adult humanoid about a hand tall, adult proportions and face, translucent insect wings of the named kind, a faint glow of fairy dust, drawn at true scale. Never childlike. Always a fully grown adult of its kind.

Glimmer Fairy.name: Glimmer Fairy
Glimmer Fairy.description: Glimmer Fairy: a glow that lights the way, and dust that hangs in the air like starlight. Evolved form of the Fairy (stage II). Bonuses: +2 charisma, +1 dexterity, +20 health, and the ability Guiding Light. At level 35 you choose between Court Fairy (type: evolve court) and Wildwing Fairy (type: evolve wild).
Glimmer Fairy.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Fairy: now a Glimmer Fairy, a glow that lights the way, and dust that hangs in the air like starlight. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan: still a hand tall and a fully grown adult. Never childlike.

Court Fairy.name: Court Fairy
Court Fairy.description: Court Fairy: you learn the old courtesies, and a bow from you can bind a promise. Evolved form of the Fairy (stage III). Bonuses: +4 charisma, +1 dexterity, +1 wisdom, +3 Charm, +20 health, +20 Mana. At level 60 this becomes Fae Sovereign.
Court Fairy.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Fairy: now a Court Fairy, you learn the old courtesies, and a bow from you can bind a promise. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan: still a hand tall and a fully grown adult. Never childlike.

Wildwing Fairy.name: Wildwing Fairy
Wildwing Fairy.description: Wildwing Fairy: you go fast and fierce, with a sting in your dust and a gale in your wings. Evolved form of the Fairy (stage III). Bonuses: +4 dexterity, +2 charisma, +3 Wing and Dive, +40 health. At level 60 this becomes Storm Sprite.
Wildwing Fairy.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Fairy: now a Wildwing Fairy, you go fast and fierce, with a sting in your dust and a gale in your wings. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan: still a hand tall and a fully grown adult. Never childlike.

Fae Sovereign.name: Fae Sovereign
Fae Sovereign.description: Fae Sovereign: flowers turn to face you, and a court gathers wherever you land. Final form of the Fairy (stage IV). Bonuses: +6 charisma, +1 dexterity, +3 wisdom, +5 Charm, +20 health, +50 Mana. This is the top of the line.
Fae Sovereign.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Fairy: now a Fae Sovereign, flowers turn to face you, and a court gathers wherever you land. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan: still a hand tall and a fully grown adult. Never childlike.

Storm Sprite.name: Storm Sprite
Storm Sprite.description: Storm Sprite: your wingbeats call up gales and your dust cuts like hail. Final form of the Fairy (stage IV). Bonuses: +6 dexterity, +4 charisma, +5 Wing and Dive, +70 health. This is the top of the line.
Storm Sprite.traitNarrativeEffects: EVOLVED FORM of a Fairy: now a Storm Sprite, your wingbeats call up gales and your dust cuts like hail. Draw and describe this greater form, same body plan: still a hand tall and a fully grown adult. Never childlike.

The Wise Fool.name: The Wise Fool
The Wise Fool.description: You play the fool on purpose. People speak freely around someone harmless, and you hear all of it. Your jokes carry the truths nobody else will say, and the people laughing hardest rarely notice they have been read.
The Wise Fool.traitNarrativeEffects: PERSONALITY REFERENCE: Write a sharp mind behind a harmless act: daft questions, bad jokes, and now and then a truth slipped in that lands a beat later. People underestimate them and talk freely nearby. The act drops only when the player drops it.

Reaper's Scythe.name: Reaper's Scythe
Reaper's Scythe.description:
A long-handled blade curved like a crescent moon, favored by reapers, death-themed warriors, and anyone who picked intimidation first and figured out the practicality later. The angles are awkward and the reach is strange, but the sweeping attacks are brutal and the silhouette against a night sky is, frankly, worth the learning curve.

Primary Attribute: Strength
Reaper's Scythe.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist's iconic weapon is a reaper's scythe. Describe combat with wide sweeping arcs, spinning attacks, the dramatic visual of a crescent blade, and the reaper aesthetic. WEAPON SKILL: Supports progression through Scythe Combat.

Arcane Affinity.name: Arcane Affinity
Arcane Affinity.description:
Arcane magic answers you as structure rather than element: pure mana shaped into wards, constructs, counterspells and the patient theory every other school stands on. Where others feel heat or tide, you feel the lattice underneath, and it bends for you first.

Primary Attribute: Intelligence
Arcane Affinity.traitNarrativeEffects: MAGIC AFFINITY REFERENCE: Use arcane magic for raw mana, wards, constructs, dispelling and counterspells. Keep it distinct from the elements and from divine or spirit power.

Divine Affinity.name: Divine Affinity
Divine Affinity.description:
Divine power comes to you easily: healing that closes what it touches, purification, protection, and the bright judgment of the First Light. You do not need a temple to be heard, though temples tend to notice you.

Primary Attribute: Wisdom
Divine Affinity.traitNarrativeEffects: MAGIC AFFINITY REFERENCE: Use divine magic for healing, purification, warding and holy force drawn from the First Light. Keep it distinct from Light magic's radiance and from spirit work.

Spirit Affinity.name: Spirit Affinity
Spirit Affinity.description:
The dead and the unseen find you easy to talk to: ghosts, ancestors, shrine spirits and the echoes old places keep. You hear them before others feel the chill, and they tend to answer when you ask.

Primary Attribute: Wisdom
Spirit Affinity.traitNarrativeEffects: MAGIC AFFINITY REFERENCE: Use spirit channeling for speaking with ghosts and spirits, calming hauntings, and calling or binding spirits. Keep it distinct from Soul magic and from divine power.

Blessing of the Many Roads.name: Blessing of the Many Roads
Blessing of the Many Roads.description: Some gods hand out a sword. Yours handed you the map. The Blessing of the Many Roads makes no single thing extraordinary and everything a little easier: body, mind and nerve all start a step above where they would, your reserves of health and mana run deeper, and a dozen everyday arts come to your hands as if you had practiced them for years. It suits someone who wants to try every road and be caught flat-footed by none. The catch is the one every generalist knows: a specialist at their best still beats you at their one thing, so you win by choosing the ground.
Blessing of the Many Roads.traitNarrativeEffects: You are rarely the best in the room at anything and almost never the worst, and you have a quiet habit of already knowing a little about whatever the moment needs.

Transformation Sequence.name: Transformation Sequence
Transformation Sequence.description:
Light, ribbons, armor plates, a roar and a pose: your transformation looks however you make it the first time you call it, a magical-girl outfit, a masked rider's armor, a beast's hide or a stage costume, and it stays yours. The world waits for the sequence to finish, and nobody who does not already know can tell your two selves apart.

How it works: say you transform (or henshin, or suit up) in your action. Every attribute +4, health +150 and Mana +100 for 5 turns, ready again 10 turns after you started. From level 50 it becomes your Final Form: every attribute +8, health +300 and Mana +200.
Transformation Sequence.traitNarrativeEffects: The player transforms only when they call it. Keep the look they gave the first time; if they gave none, choose one that fits and keep it. Transformed, they cannot be linked to their everyday self by anyone who does not already know, unless they reveal it or were seen changing.

Transformation Sequence: Transformed.name: Transformation Sequence: Transformed
Transformation Sequence: Transformed.description: Transformed: every attribute +4, health +150 and Mana +100. It ends after 5 turns.
Transformation Sequence: Transformed.traitNarrativeEffects: In transformed form: the same look every time.

Transformation Sequence: Final Form.name: Transformation Sequence: Final Form
Transformation Sequence: Final Form.description: Final Form: every attribute +8, health +300 and Mana +200. It ends after 5 turns.
Transformation Sequence: Final Form.traitNarrativeEffects: In Final Form: the transformed look, grown greater.

Odd-Job Brawler.name: Odd-Job Brawler
Odd-Job Brawler.description:
A master swordsman needs a sword. You just need a room with furniture in it. Chair legs, soup ladles, orchard ladders, a tavern bench, a walking cane, or the cast-iron skillet still warm from breakfast: every object in reach has its own weight, swing, and comic timing. An Adaptive Grip turns whatever you snatch up into a balanced weapon on the first beat, while an Unorthodox Strike arrives from an angle no fencing manual ever warned about. It looks like a frantic scramble right until everyone else is on the floor and the crockery is somehow intact.

Primary Attribute: Dexterity
Odd-Job Brawler.traitNarrativeEffects: You instinctively test the balance and heft of every household object you pick up, mentally choreographing three ways to disarm a room with a coat rack, a broom, or a teapot before sitting down.

Pillow Knight.name: Pillow Knight
Pillow Knight.description:
Mockery lasts right up until six feet of high-density goose down takes a bandit captain off his boots. To the uninitiated, it is a full-length combat body pillow printed with an idealized heroine. To you, it is banner, buckler, and sacred trust. Pure, unironic devotion turns plush fabric and reinforced seams into a legitimate martial art: you weather heavy blows behind a Comfort Shield that absorbs steel and spite alike, then answer with a sweeping Pillow Bash driven by absolute conviction. Your morale is unbreakable. Your form is immaculate.

Primary Attribute: Charisma
Pillow Knight.traitNarrativeEffects: You treat your companion pillow with courtly etiquette, fluffing and brushing the cover after every skirmish, and you take immediate, polite offense when anyone calls it mere bedding.

Chaos Knight.name: Chaos Knight
Chaos Knight.description:
Other dark knights brood in tavern corners about their tragic past. You brought a sermon and a greatsword. As a sworn champion of the Dark Gods, you are the evil paladin in full blackened plate: loud, devout, and terrifyingly cheerful about the old powers that ruled before the First Light. Your Corrupting Strike plants festering rot in the wound that muffles healing magic, and when a fight calls for a miracle, you offer your own silhouette on the altar of a Shadow Bargain so your next spells land like a falling cathedral.

Primary Attribute: Strength
Chaos Knight.traitNarrativeEffects: Candle flames lean away from your pauldrons when you invoke your gods, temple bells hum a half-step flat as you pass, and your shadow occasionally lags a beat behind your boots.

Blessing of the Dark Gods.name: Blessing of the Dark Gods
Blessing of the Dark Gods.description: Before the First Light rose, older powers held the dark, and they still answer anyone bold enough to pray at full volume. The Blessing of the Dark Gods wraps any class in the heavy, theatrical favor of the pre-dawn pantheon. You can hurl a withering Curse Bolt that saps a foe's strength, call down a dark Divine Favor whose weight scales with your devotion, and walk into battle with the constitution and presence of a chosen herald.
Blessing of the Dark Gods.traitNarrativeEffects: When you call on your blessing, the light around your shoulders dims to a theatrical eclipse-violet and a low, satisfied hum answers from the nearest shadow.

Improvised Arms.name: Improvised Arms
Improvised Arms.description:
Whatever is in reach is your weapon: a length of pipe, a fence post, a walking cane, the chair leg that was holding up a table a moment ago. You never carry the same thing twice and never feel unarmed, because every room is an armory once you stop being picky.

Primary Attribute: Dexterity
Improvised Arms.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist fights with whatever is in reach: pipes, logs, canes, chair legs, ladders, shovels. Describe each fight through the object at hand, its weight and its comic timing; when one breaks, they grab the next. WEAPON SKILL: Supports progression through Exotic Weapons. Improvised arms start with no item and are never disarmed for long.

War Scythe.name: War Scythe
War Scythe.description:
A farmer's scythe blade straightened and set in line on a long pole: the levy's answer to cavalry. It does not sweep like a reaper's crescent. It thrusts, hooks and chops from a reach that keeps riders and spears honest, and it looks plain right up until it is used.

Primary Attribute: Strength
War Scythe.traitNarrativeEffects: WEAPON IDENTITY: The protagonist's iconic weapon is a war scythe, a straight heavy blade set in line on a long pole. Describe combat with reaching thrusts, hooking pulls and heavy chops that hold a line, unseat riders and keep foes at the end of the pole. WEAPON SKILL: Supports progression through Polearm Combat.

Race.name: Race
Race.custom:
Route permanent identity to Background paragraph 4 and complete visible anatomy to Appearance → CHARACTER. Preserve the selected fantasy race, species, bloodline, body plan, limb count, ears, horns, tails, wings, scales, fur, fangs, tusks, fins, gills, crystal, slime, construct, celestial, demon, beastkin, or other selected structures exactly. Never humanize or substitute them. With two races, a true-form race sets the body and the other shows only as its marks; between two humanoid races, blend them evenly in one body.

TRUE MONSTER, CONSTRUCT AND FAMILIAR RACES: for a race whose IMAGE GENERATION RULE begins TRUE FORM, that rule is the body. Write Background paragraph 4 and Appearance → CHARACTER for that body: size and scale, head, limbs, surface, natural weapons, eyes and markings. Appearance Builder picks made for humanoids apply only where the body has the matching part: hair picks color the mane, crest, fur, feathers or glow; skin tone picks color the hide, scales, shell or surface; outfit picks become harness, barding, collar, cloth or ornament the body can wear; face, facial hair and body type picks are left out unless the body has that feature. Creature Features picks are exact. Frame the whole creature the way the selected frame frames a person. The character is a fully grown adult of its kind. In Background, the character thinks and speaks as a person and lives in this body; do not write them as a pet or a mount.
Race.description: Your bloodline, your silhouette, your starting rumors. Pick the ancestry that makes you want to see the portrait. Humans blend in. Elves turn heads. Demons make people nervous. Beastkin ears move before their owners do. This shapes your portrait, how strangers read you, and the specific flavor of trouble you attract. You may pick two to play a blend; with a true monster, its body wins and the other race shows in its marks. Sub-groups below sort the bloodlines. The True Monsters, Constructs and Familiars groups are real non-human bodies: a dragon is a dragon, a slime is a slime. Each of those races has an evolution line that grows with your level. At level 30 each of them also learns a human form that keeps the marks of its true body.

Personality.name: Personality
Personality.custom: Route to Background paragraphs 2-3 only. Use it to shape temperament, habits, choices, dialogue tendencies, social behavior, and conflict; for one who has only just arrived, as temperament alone, with no local habits and nobody here yet reacting to it. It cannot create visible costume, expression, aura, props, powers, or scenery without a separate selected visual trait.
traits: The Noble Brat With a Heart
Personality.description: The archetype that runs the show. This is how you react, flirt, escalate, and cause scenes. The Dense Protagonist misses every hint. The Scheming Puppeteer catches all of them. The Battle Junkie starts fights for fun. The Villainess Enjoyer starts them for style. Pick the one that sounds like the most entertaining version of you.

Relationship Style.custom: Route to Background paragraphs 2-3 only. Use it to shape affection, trust, teasing, boundaries, commitment, and confession behavior without creating an existing partner, admirer, party, or harem. It does not add romance symbols, props, blush, or scenery.
