The descent from the dockside quarter into the bazaar proper is the beat's spine: passwords that are really introductions, doors that are really assessments, and a market that is orderly, well-lit and worse for both. The player goes in for something specific and the transaction is the objective. What they see along the way is the actual content: debt servitude operating openly, unregistered stalls, and a service for making inconvenient people stop being a problem. Ibuki is pragmatic rather than cruel and has made her peace with things the player may not be able to. End with the transaction completed, which implicates the player, and a Crownveil noble's involvement visible in outline. Sets up The Price of Freedom.

Shipwrecked: A Signal From the Water.name: Shipwrecked: A Signal From the Water
Shipwrecked: A Signal From the Water.mainObjective: Locate the source of the island's changed magical signal.
Shipwrecked: A Signal From the Water.questStatement: Something under the Cerulean shelf has been pulsing a signal for as long as anyone has bothered to measure it, and a stranger on the beach has just told you it changed when you arrived.
Shipwrecked: A Signal From the Water.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the Shipwrecked chain. Something under the Cerulean shelf has pulsed a signal for as long as anyone has bothered to measure it, and the measuring has always been a curiosity rather than a concern. A stranger on the beach tells the player it changed when they arrived. The beat is verification and recruitment: confirm the claim against independent records, establish that the change correlates with the player specifically, and work out what the stranger actually is, because their competence with dimensional navigation does not match the story they are telling about themselves. The Sirenblue Tidal Vault is a flooded sea dungeon where the tide controls the doors, the traps and which paths exist, so the dive being planned is genuinely beyond the player's equipment. Shizuku Shiosaki knows the tidal cave entrance. End with the claim confirmed and the player committed to a descent they are not ready for. Sets up The Sirenblue Depths.

Spare Reborn: There Is Another One.name: Spare Reborn: There Is Another One
Spare Reborn: There Is Another One.mainObjective: Read the full prophecy concerning the other Reborn for yourself.
Spare Reborn: There Is Another One.questStatement: You are not the only soul that came across, the other one arrived first, and everything the prophecy promised has already been assigned to them.
Spare Reborn: There Is Another One.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the Spare Reborn chain, built on the particular sting of being the redundant copy. The player is not the only soul that crossed, the other one arrived first, and every element of the prophecy everyone quotes has already been assigned to them. The beat is finding the other Reborn and reading the actual prophecy rather than the summary in circulation, which requires access to Aureliath's archives and somebody willing to grant it. Kosumi Hyosetsu is the contact and has her own reasons for helping. The other Reborn should not be written as arrogant; they are being carried by an institutional apparatus they did not ask for and are aware of how it looks. The prophecy's real text describes two complementary souls rather than one chosen and one spare, which nobody quoting it has bothered to read. End with the player having read it themselves and understanding the arrangement is not what the Crown has been telling people. Sets up The Prophecy's Shadow.

Spiritfen Convergence: The Veil Is Thinn.name: Spiritfen Convergence: The Veil Is Thinning Again
Spiritfen Convergence: The Veil Is Thinn.mainObjective: Secure Haku's agreement to share his memories of the previous veil crisis.
Spiritfen Convergence: The Veil Is Thinn.questStatement: The Spiritfen's boundary thins on a cycle everyone in the fen can predict, and this year it is thinning early, unevenly, and in the wrong places.
Spiritfen Convergence: The Veil Is Thinn.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the Spiritfen Convergence chain. The boundary between worlds in Meikyo Spiritfen thins on a cycle everyone local can predict, and this year it is thinning early, unevenly and in places that have never thinned before. The work is mapping: moving between the Misthollow Night Market, where ghost vendors and living merchants trade on both sides of the veil, and Ghostlight Harbor, taking readings and comparing them against the traditional cycle. Severin Kuresa and Kohaku Yoimizuki can each contribute a piece. The irregularity should be established as a pattern rather than randomness, and the pattern should be unsettling in a way that the fen's residents recognize before the player does. Haku Mugai was present the last time this happened and has spent a very long time not talking about it. Persuading him is the beat's objective and should require the player to earn it. Sets up The Lantern's Memory.

Starfall's Pull: Something Under the Baz.name: Starfall's Pull: Something Under the Bazaar
Starfall's Pull: Something Under the Baz.mainObjective: Hear Zahra explain what lies beneath the Starfall Bazaar.
Starfall's Pull: Something Under the Baz.questStatement: Seeress Zahra Truemoon has stopped taking clients, which she has never done, and the reason is directly beneath the bazaar she works in.
Starfall's Pull: Something Under the Baz.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the Starfall's Pull chain. Seeress Zahra Truemoon has stopped taking clients, which she has never done in a career built entirely on taking clients, and the reason is directly beneath the bazaar she works in. The beat is getting her to say so. The Starfall Bazaar is a night market of contracts, smuggled artifacts and playful danger with catacombs beneath it that most traders treat as storage and mild adventure. Sahim Hoshikuzuya and Safiya Ryuusazanami provide the market's texture and its rumors. Zahra should be written as a professional who has encountered something outside her professional vocabulary and is handling it badly, which for a seeress means refusing to look. The player's route to her cooperation is either reading what she will not or demonstrating that they already have. End with Zahra escorting the player to the catacomb entrance and declining to go further. Sets up The Bazaar's Depths.

Villainess Reborn: You Know How This End.name: Villainess Reborn: You Know How This Ends
Villainess Reborn: You Know How This End.mainObjective: Avert the first remembered story beat through your intervention.
Villainess Reborn: You Know How This End.questStatement: You know this story because you read it, you know which noblewoman you have woken up as, and you know exactly how many chapters she has left.
Villainess Reborn: You Know How This End.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the Villainess Reborn chain, built on foreknowledge as a mechanic. The player knows this story because they read it, knows which noblewoman they have woken up as, and knows precisely how many chapters she has left. The beat is an attempt to avert the first remembered scene, which the player can see coming and can position for. It should be a small early beat rather than a climactic one, and averting it should require real effort and produce real success. Then the momentum reasserts itself: the story is a system rather than a script, and removing one cause produces the same effect through a different route, with a different person carrying it. Kanade Baragiri and the rival cast should be established as people rather than plot functions. Aureliath's noble quarter provides the setting. End with the flag averted, something worse in its place, and the player understanding that being nice will not be sufficient. Sets up The Roseveil Redemption.

Waltz of Rift and Ruin: The Ballroom and.name: Waltz of Rift and Ruin: The Ballroom and the Breach
Waltz of Rift and Ruin: The Ballroom and.mainObjective: Discover direct evidence in Roseblack Manor's ballroom that the breach was deliberately directed.
Waltz of Rift and Ruin: The Ballroom and.questStatement: A rift opened inside a noble ballroom during a waltz, which is not where rifts open, and Akira Zen'in was standing closest to it and has not stopped thinking about that.
Waltz of Rift and Ruin: The Ballroom and.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the Waltz of Rift and Ruin chain. A rift opened inside Roseblack Manor's moonlit ballroom during a waltz, which is not where rifts open, and Akira Zen'in was standing nearest to it and has not stopped thinking about that since. The investigation is conducted inside a gothic estate that would very much prefer the incident be treated as an accident: the Margrave's household is helpful in a way that closes doors, the ballroom has been cleaned, and the guests have been given a version. The player works the physical evidence, the timing and the seating, and what emerges is that the breach was directed rather than natural. Akira is the chain's most useful witness and its most compromised one; his fire Blessing responded to the rift in a way he does not want examined. Establish the ballroom incident, the direction of the breach and Akira's discomfort without explaining the blood contract. Sets up The Noble's Confession.

Whispers in the Capital: An Invitation Y.name: Whispers in the Capital: An Invitation You Did Not Earn
Whispers in the Capital: An Invitation Y.mainObjective: Identify the sponsor who put your name on the gala invitation.
Whispers in the Capital: An Invitation Y.questStatement: An invitation to a Crownveil gala has arrived for you, and invitations to Crownveil galas do not arrive for people like you without somebody deciding they should.
Whispers in the Capital: An Invitation Y.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the Whispers in the Capital chain. An invitation to a Crownveil gala arrives for somebody with no standing to receive one, which means a person with standing chose to spend some. The beat happens before the party: working out who sponsored the invitation, what they expect in return, and whether attending is agreement. Aureliath's council wing, noble quarter and guild quarter are the investigative ground, and the answer should require the player to trade something for it. Sayaka Kujo, Shinji Souen and Suzuha Sumeragi can each be approached and each has a different read. The Sovereignty itself is the nominal source and the actual patron is somebody within it. The player should attend knowing they are being positioned, which is a stronger opening than attending in ignorance and makes the gala's social manoeuvring readable. Establish the patron system and the player's usefulness to somebody. Sets up Whispers at the Gala.

Wrong Skill's Right Purpose: The Blessin.name: Wrong Skill's Right Purpose: The Blessing Nobody Wanted
Wrong Skill's Right Purpose: The Blessin.mainObjective: Solve a concrete problem using your dismissed Blessing.
Wrong Skill's Right Purpose: The Blessin.questStatement: Your Blessing came through as a culinary talent, the appraiser laughed, and you have been living with that reaction ever since.
Wrong Skill's Right Purpose: The Blessin.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the Wrong Skill's Right Purpose chain, an underestimated-power fantasy played warm rather than bitter. The player's Blessing came through as a culinary talent, the appraiser laughed, and they have been managing that reaction ever since. Goldlotus Oasis is silk tents, blue pools, perfume shops and moonlit garden courtyards, the most romantic city in the Mirage Sea, and a place where food matters enormously. The beat is a problem that nobody else can solve and that the player's dismissed Blessing solves precisely: a spoiled supply, a diplomatic dinner, a sick caravan, resolved publicly in front of people who arrived expecting nothing. Momo Ibarajo narrates her own probability of embarrassment throughout and is the chain's warmest presence. The first hint that the Blessing interacts unusually with Rift-Touched ingredients should appear here without being explained. End with the room's opinion changed. Sets up The Chef's Challenge.

The Sky That Fell: The Rotating Approach.name: The Sky That Fell: The Rotating Approach
The Sky That Fell: The Rotating Approach.mainObjective: Read the anomalous logbook entry Stella shows you inside the observatory.
The Sky That Fell: The Rotating Approach.questStatement: The Fallen Star Observatory faces its bridge for two hours in every eight, and the last astronomer living there has not had a visitor in five years.
The Sky That Fell: The Rotating Approach.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of The Sky That Fell chain, and the player's introduction to the Fallen Star Observatory. The approach formation rotates on an eight hour cycle and its entrance faces the arrival bridge for roughly two of those hours. Time it wrong and the bridge ends at a sheer crystal face with a very long drop beneath it, and the wait is spent exposed on a platform where gravity behaves inconsistently and star constructs drift past without acknowledging anyone. The Guild's posted timings are two years out of date, which the player discovers by arriving on them. Inside, the observatory is colder than the outside air and the great dome is cracked open to the sky, so the whole main chamber is lit by starlight coming through a lens that shattered long before anyone alive was born. Stella Hoshifuru has been the only person living here for five years and reacts to a visitor with delight rather than suspicion, talks quickly, offers food she cannot really spare, and gets to the point faster than the player expects. She shows them the logbook: the same anomalous reading, taken on the same instrument, recorded every month for five years, dismissed by the Silver Crescent Academy as instrument error each time she submitted it. She has never stopped submitting it. Sets up Five Years of Bad Data.

The Sky That Fell: Five Years of Bad Dat.name: The Sky That Fell: Five Years of Bad Data
The Sky That Fell: Five Years of Bad Dat.mainObjective: Identify the deliberately removed window in the Academy's raw astronomical records.
The Sky That Fell: Five Years of Bad Dat.questStatement: Stella's logs were dismissed by the Silver Crescent Academy as instrument error, and the Academy's own comparison data has a gap exactly where hers does not.
The Sky That Fell: Five Years of Bad Dat.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of The Sky That Fell chain. The work here is archival rather than physical and should feel like real research: two sets of records, one kept obsessively by a woman alone in a ruin, one kept institutionally by the continent's premier academy, and a discrepancy sitting between them. Stella's logs are meticulous, cross-referenced and dated. The Academy's comparison data is cleaner, better presented and missing a window that corresponds exactly to the period her readings are strongest. Nagi Amanohara can obtain the Academy's raw submissions rather than its published summaries, and the raw set still contains what the published set does not. The finding is not that the Academy made an error. It is that somebody removed a window and signed off on the removal, which reframes five years of polite dismissal as five years of suppression and makes Stella's persistence look very different in hindsight. Stella takes this badly and quietly rather than dramatically; her assumption has always been that she was wrong and being humored, and learning she was right and being managed is worse. Do not resolve who ordered the edit here. Follows The Rotating Approach and sets up What the Broken Lens Shows.

The Sky That Fell: What the Broken Lens.name: The Sky That Fell: What the Broken Lens Shows
The Sky That Fell: What the Broken Lens.mainObjective: Secure Nagi's agreement to testify to the repeatable lens effect.
The Sky That Fell: What the Broken Lens.questStatement: The shattered telescope resolves more detail when you are the one standing at it, which Stella noticed immediately and has been afraid to write down.
The Sky That Fell: What the Broken Lens.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of The Sky That Fell chain and the point where the chain turns from institutional to uncanny. The great telescope's lens shattered generations ago and resolves almost nothing for almost everyone, which is why the observatory was abandoned. It resolves considerably more when the player is the one at the eyepiece. Stella noticed this within an hour of their arrival and has been afraid to write it down, because writing it down is what got her dismissed for five years. The quest is a controlled demonstration: repeat the observation, vary the conditions, rule out the obvious, and do it in front of Nagi Amanohara, who is a genuine skeptic and should be difficult to convince. Nagi's value to the chain is precisely that he does not want this to be true and cannot make it go away. Run it at different hours, with different observers, with the player absent and present. The effect holds. The chamber itself contributes: the instrument ring is unheated, breath fogs the surviving glass, and the gravity anomalies in the dome make loose objects drift upward during the strongest readings. By the end Nagi will testify to it, which is the thing the player actually needed. Follows Five Years of Bad Data and sets up The Piece That Fell.

The Sky That Fell: The Piece That Fell.name: The Sky That Fell: The Piece That Fell
The Sky That Fell: The Piece That Fell.mainObjective: Make direct contact with what lies at the impact formation.
The Sky That Fell: The Piece That Fell.questStatement: The telescope has always pointed at the impact site, and the impact site has never been surveyed because everyone assumed there was nothing left of it.
The Sky That Fell: The Piece That Fell.questDesignBrief: Part 4 of The Sky That Fell chain, and the chain's expedition beat. The telescope has always pointed at the same place: the impact formation where a piece of sky came down, which nobody has surveyed because everyone assumed there was nothing left to survey. Getting there is the hard part. The route crosses unstable formation edges, gravity wraiths patrol the approach, and the meteorite vault under the central crater is a genuine dungeon rather than a walk. What the player finds is not debris. It is intact, it is not inert, and it responds to their presence the way the broken lens did, which is the moment the chain's two mysteries become one mystery. Stella should be present if the player allows it; she has wanted to come here for five years and has never had a reason anyone would fund. Her reaction on arrival is the emotional center of the beat. Keep the discovery physically specific rather than abstract: something the player can touch, that changes when touched, and that neither of them can explain. Do not answer what it is. Follows What the Broken Lens Shows and sets up The Second Sky.

The Sky That Fell: The Second Sky.name: The Sky That Fell: The Second Sky
The Sky That Fell: The Second Sky.mainObjective: Carry out your chosen disposition of the observatory's report: publish, deliver or seal it.
The Sky That Fell: The Second Sky.questStatement: Stella has waited five years to be believed, and what the observatory reports now is entirely in your hands.
The Sky That Fell: The Second Sky.questDesignBrief: Part 5 and conclusion of The Sky That Fell chain. Everything now rests on what the observatory formally reports and who receives it. Three routes should be equally available and equally costly. Publishing openly vindicates Stella completely, ends five years of humiliation, and hands the Reaches a discovery that every faction will immediately fight over. Handing it to the Silver Crescent Academy gets it studied properly by the only institution equipped to do so, and that institution is the one that buried her data, so it also means her name will appear nowhere. Sealing it protects the site and asks Stella to stay silent for the rest of her life about the thing she was right about. Nagi argues for the Academy on the honest grounds that nobody else can handle it. Stella will accept whatever the player decides and should not be written as pleading; her dignity is the point. Whatever is chosen changes who controls the observatory and whether Stella remains its keeper. This concludes the chain and should land as a real ending rather than a handoff.

Cargo That Was Never Loaded: The Extra C.name: Cargo That Was Never Loaded: The Extra Crate
Cargo That Was Never Loaded: The Extra C.mainObjective: Locate the unmanifested crate in Bay Four.
Cargo That Was Never Loaded: The Extra C.questStatement: A freighter came in three crates heavier than its manifest, nobody has claimed the extra one, and the port has quietly stopped asking about it.
Cargo That Was Never Loaded: The Extra C.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the Cargo That Was Never Loaded chain, opening on ordinary dockside work at Windreach. The freighter came in three crates heavier than its manifest, which is common enough to be boring, except that two of the three have been claimed and the port has stopped asking about the third. The hangar bays smell of hot brass and cold altitude wind, the landing mesa is busy enough that nobody watches a person walking a cargo line, and the port's own staff answer questions with a practiced incuriosity that is itself information. The player works the paperwork trail: bills of lading, the crew's account of loading, the weight logs at two prior stops. Everyone is helpful and nobody is useful. The crate sits in Bay Four under a tarp with no consignee mark, and the longer the player looks at it the more obvious it is that several people already know exactly what it is and have agreed not to say. Establish the crate, the port's silence, and that the discrepancy started before Windreach. Sets up Bay Four's Governor.

Cargo That Was Never Loaded: Bay Four's.name: Cargo That Was Never Loaded: Bay Four's Governor
Cargo That Was Never Loaded: Bay Four's.mainObjective: Stop Bay Four's lift interference by opening or removing the crate.
Cargo That Was Never Loaded: Bay Four's.questStatement: Bay Four's lift machinery has been running flat since the freighter docked, and Fuuka Sorakumi has traced the interference to the crate nobody will open.
Cargo That Was Never Loaded: Bay Four's.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of the Cargo That Was Never Loaded chain, and the chain's pressure beat. Bay Four's lift machinery has been running flat since the freighter docked: the governor will not hold a setting, loads drift, and a bay that cannot be trusted with weight is a bay that kills somebody eventually. Fuuka Sorakumi has traced the interference to the unclaimed crate and wants it opened on straightforward engineering grounds. Tori Harihane wants it opened out of undisguised curiosity and talks fast enough to make that sound like the same argument. The port authority wants it removed unopened and off their books by nightfall. All three positions are reasonable and the player has to pick one. Opening it resolves the interference immediately and puts the player's name on a decision that other people were carefully avoiding. Removing it unopened protects them and leaves the machinery problem to reassert itself somewhere else. Fuuka's prototypes are half-finished and mostly work, which should be visible in how she approaches the problem. Follows The Extra Crate and sets up Whose Handwriting.

Cargo That Was Never Loaded: Whose Handw.name: Cargo That Was Never Loaded: Whose Handwriting
Cargo That Was Never Loaded: Whose Handw.mainObjective: Present the second forger's route through the ports.
Cargo That Was Never Loaded: Whose Handw.questStatement: The manifest was forged well, but it was forged twice, and the second hand is sloppier than the first.
Cargo That Was Never Loaded: Whose Handw.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of the Cargo That Was Never Loaded chain, relocating to Cloudfallen Market. The manifest was forged competently, and then forged again by somebody less careful, and the second hand is the thread. Cloudfallen sets up on whatever floating platform suits it that cycle, which makes tracing anything through it a matter of asking the right people before the market moves. Souta Amatsuki is that access: nineteen, wiry, a climber who sells what he hauls down off the formations himself, and connected to exactly the sort of people who handle paperwork nobody should be handling. The investigation should move physically as well as socially, across the central bridge with its glass floor panels and four hundred feet of open sky underneath. What emerges is not one falsified shipment but a route: the same second hand appears on documents at three ports over eight months, which means a standing arrangement rather than an opportunist. Souta's grin thins as he realizes how close some of this runs to people he trades with. Follows Bay Four's Governor and sets up The Consignee.

Cargo That Was Never Loaded: The Consign.name: Cargo That Was Never Loaded: The Consignee
Cargo That Was Never Loaded: The Consign.mainObjective: Settle the cargo claim through an actual handover or seizure.
Cargo That Was Never Loaded: The Consign.questStatement: Somebody has arrived to collect, they are polite, and they are extremely clear that the crate was always theirs.
Cargo That Was Never Loaded: The Consign.questDesignBrief: Part 4 and conclusion of the Cargo That Was Never Loaded chain. Somebody has arrived to collect, they are courteous, their documentation is better than the port's, and they are entirely clear that the crate has always been theirs. The complication is that they are not lying, or not simply lying, and the chain should not resolve into a villain. Souma Amagi's escort competence is decisive here whether the beat becomes a negotiation, a handover or a chase across the market ring, and his careful, quiet manner contrasts usefully with Souta's noise. The player's earlier choices set the terrain: if the crate was opened they know what is being claimed and can price it, and if it was not they are negotiating blind. Resolution can be sale, surrender, seizure or exposure, and each leaves the smuggling route in a different state. What matters is that the player ends up on the record with somebody, and Cloudfallen remembers who. This concludes the chain.

The Mounds Are Moving: Survey the Field.name: The Mounds Are Moving: Survey the Field
The Mounds Are Moving: Survey the Field.mainObjective: Finish documenting your resurvey of the mound field.
The Mounds Are Moving: Survey the Field.questStatement: The Duskfields bury their dead in mounds laid out to a pattern, and the survey taken ten years ago no longer matches the ground.
The Mounds Are Moving: Survey the Field.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of The Mounds Are Moving chain, opening on methodical fieldwork under an enormous perpetual sunset. The Tombherd is where the Duskfield clans interred their greatest riders alongside their bonded spirit-beasts, and the mounds are laid out to a pattern the clans have kept without ever writing down why. The player's job is unglamorous: walk the mound field with the ten year old survey, take bearings, record positions. The wrongness accumulates rather than announcing itself. A mound is forty paces from where the survey puts it. Then another. Then one is missing from the record entirely and the grass over it is undisturbed, which is impossible in both directions. Sougen Hakamori, the mound warden, follows at a distance and volunteers nothing, because he has offered this information before and been humored. The wind never stops on the Duskfields and the sound of it through the grave-grass is the whole ambience of the beat. End with a completed survey that demonstrably contradicts the record, in the player's own handwriting, which is the credibility the rest of the chain runs on. Sets up The Warden's Count.

The Mounds Are Moving: The Warden's Coun.name: The Mounds Are Moving: The Warden's Count
The Mounds Are Moving: The Warden's Coun.mainObjective: Get a Confederacy representative's formal acceptance of the mound survey evidence.
The Mounds Are Moving: The Warden's Coun.questStatement: Sougen Hakamori has counted the mounds every morning for decades, his numbers have been right the whole time, and everyone has assumed he is simply old.
The Mounds Are Moving: The Warden's Coun.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of The Mounds Are Moving chain, and its first real character beat. Sougen Hakamori has walked the mound field every morning for decades and counted, and his count has been correct the entire time, and the Confederacy has quietly filed him under old and devoted rather than listen. The quest is validation: get his tallies, check them against the player's own survey, and then get somebody with standing to accept both. That second half is the difficulty. The Windrunner Confederacy governs by parliament during the Great Gathering and is not in session, so the player is chasing clan representatives across a scattered region to make an unwelcome argument. Sougen himself should be written without bitterness. He is not vindicated so much as relieved, and he says less about it than the player expects. His camp sits at the field's edge with the tools of a man who has maintained something alone for a very long time. Asuka Kagehibari attaches herself to the investigation here, because a verified anomaly is the first thing that has genuinely frightened her. Follows Survey the Field and sets up What the Arrangement Spells.

The Mounds Are Moving: What the Arrangem.name: The Mounds Are Moving: What the Arrangement Spells
The Mounds Are Moving: What the Arrangem.mainObjective: Identify the completed shape of the converging mound pattern.
The Mounds Are Moving: What the Arrangem.questStatement: The mounds are not moving randomly. They are moving toward a shape, and Asuka Kagehibari has worked out enough of it to stop sleeping.
The Mounds Are Moving: What the Arrangem.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of The Mounds Are Moving chain, where the chain turns from strange to alarming. The mounds are not drifting randomly. Plotted across the ten year interval they are converging on a shape, and Asuka Kagehibari has worked out enough of it to have stopped sleeping. The work is pattern analysis done on the ground and on paper: overlay the surveys, project the movement, and see what the arrangement will be when it finishes. The shape is old, deliberate and recognizable to nobody currently alive, which means the answer has to come out of the Wind Shrine's records and the clan songs rather than any archive. Asuka should be the one who cracks it and should hate having done so. The reveal is what the shape is, not what it does, and the beat should resist explaining the mechanism; the horror is that something is arranging graves with intent and taking decades to do it. Sougen's reaction is quieter and worse: he recognizes it from a song his grandmother sang. Follows The Warden's Count and sets up The One That Has Not Moved.

The Mounds Are Moving: The One That Has.name: The Mounds Are Moving: The One That Has Not Moved
The Mounds Are Moving: The One That Has.mainObjective: Discover what the unmoved Ancestor Mound contains.
The Mounds Are Moving: The One That Has.questStatement: A single mound has stayed exactly where it was, it is older than the register, and nobody knows who is in it.
The Mounds Are Moving: The One That Has.questDesignBrief: Part 4 of The Mounds Are Moving chain and its escalation. Every mound in the field has shifted except one. It is older than the register, it appears on no survey, and the Ancestor Mound sits at what the projected pattern makes the center. Opening a mound is a serious cultural act in the Duskfields and the beat should make the player pay for it rather than waving it through: Sougen will not assist, the clans must be petitioned or circumvented, and the spirit-beast tunnels that connect the mounds underground offer a way in that avoids the ceremony and carries its own cost. Those tunnels were carved by dying bonded beasts and are a labyrinth of bone and compressed earth that is genuinely dangerous. What is inside the unmoved mound reframes everything the chain has established about who is buried here and who has been doing the arranging. Whether the player takes the honest route or the quiet one should change how the clans treat them for the rest of the chain. Follows What the Arrangement Spells and sets up Finish It or Stop It.

The Mounds Are Moving: Finish It or Stop.name: The Mounds Are Moving: Finish It or Stop It
The Mounds Are Moving: Finish It or Stop.mainObjective: Enact your choice to complete or permanently stop the mound arrangement.
The Mounds Are Moving: Finish It or Stop.questStatement: The pattern needs one more move to complete, and you are now the only person in a position to make it or prevent it.
The Mounds Are Moving: Finish It or Stop.questDesignBrief: Part 5 and conclusion of The Mounds Are Moving chain. The pattern requires one more movement and the player is now the only person positioned to cause it or prevent it. Neither option is safe and neither is obviously wrong. Completing the arrangement finishes something the Duskfields began generations ago for reasons that have been lost, and honors an intention nobody now understands. Breaking it protects the present at the cost of destroying the last surviving instance of something ancient and possibly load-bearing. Sougen Hakamori and Asuka Kagehibari fall on opposite sides and both arguments should be genuinely persuasive: he has tended this for a lifetime and trusts what his ancestors built, she has seen the shape and does not trust it at all. Stage the finale at the Ancestor Mound with the whole field visible and the wind doing what it always does. The Duskfields should feel changed afterward either way, and the clans should have an opinion about the player for a long time. This concludes the chain.

The Great Race: Unregistered Entry.name: The Great Race: Unregistered Entry
The Great Race: Unregistered Entry.mainObjective: Get your mounted entry accepted onto the Great Race card.
The Great Race: Unregistered Entry.questStatement: The Great Race takes Confederacy-sponsored riders, and you have no sponsor, no mount and no standing with anybody who could give you one.
The Great Race: Unregistered Entry.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of The Great Race chain, opening at the Beast-Run Fairgrounds during the Great Gathering. The Great Race takes Confederacy-sponsored riders and the player has no sponsor, no mount and no standing, which is the entire problem. The Fairgrounds are the most energetic place on the continent right now: paddock row full of storm-beasts being walked and argued over, trade row doing brisk business, the parliamentary sessions running alongside the racing, and courtship competitions happening in the middle of all of it. Getting in means finding a clan willing to bend, a mount nobody else wants, or a technicality. Every route should require the player to demonstrate something in front of people who will remember it. Fuyu Kazahaya is the pragmatic one worth cultivating; Sora Kazekami notices the player without being introduced to them, which is the chain's first spark. Keep the tone loud, warm and competitive rather than hostile. End with a mount the player has some relationship with and a name on the card that several people think is a mistake. Sets up The Herd Path.

The Great Race: The Herd Path.name: The Great Race: The Herd Path
The Great Race: The Herd Path.mainObjective: Complete the herd-path training with Sora.
The Great Race: The Herd Path.questStatement: Sora Kazekami has not lost a race since she was fourteen, and she has offered to train you, which is not the kindness it sounds like.
The Great Race: The Herd Path.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of The Great Race chain, relocating to Thundermane Valley for training. Thousands of lightning-crowned storm-beasts fill the valley during breeding season and the air smells permanently of ozone, which is the backdrop for the chain's central relationship. Sora Kazekami has been undefeated since she was fourteen, courts through challenge and physical proximity, and teaches by racing you rather than instructing you. She does not go easy and would consider going easy an insult. The training should produce genuine improvement and genuine bruises, run along the herd path where a mistake means being caught between moving animals the size of houses, and let the two of them talk between runs in the way people do when they are both too winded to be careful. Ash Hageshikiba runs the post here and provides the practical grounding: what the herds are doing this season, which lines are safe, what Sora is not saying about her own record. End with Sora rating the player as real competition, which she says plainly, once, and does not repeat. Follows Unregistered Entry and sets up The Fixed Heat.

The Great Race: The Fixed Heat.name: The Great Race: The Fixed Heat
The Great Race: The Fixed Heat.mainObjective: Secure evidence of the race-fixing arrangement during the fixed heat.
The Great Race: The Fixed Heat.questStatement: You have been entered in a heat you are meant to lose, the arrangement was made before you arrived, and Fuyu Kazahaya can prove it if you can survive the ride.
The Great Race: The Fixed Heat.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of The Great Race chain and its turn. The player has been entered into a heat they are intended to lose, and the arrangement predates their entry, which means somebody adjusted a fix to accommodate a rider who was not supposed to matter. The heat itself is genuinely dangerous: the course has been altered, one of the other riders knows and the rest do not, and the danger is real for everyone on the field rather than aimed at the player alone. Fuyu Kazahaya has suspected the fixing for a season and can prove the mechanism if the player survives the ride and brings back what she needs. Run the race as a real sequence with the storm-beasts, the crowd, the Champion's Stand and the smell of ozone, and let the player choose between riding to win, riding to gather evidence, and riding to protect the field. Sora is watching and will draw her own conclusions from which one they pick. Establish the mechanism of the fix without naming who paid for it. Follows The Herd Path and sets up Crown or Truth.

The Great Race: Crown or Truth.name: The Great Race: Crown or Truth
The Great Race: Crown or Truth.mainObjective: Resolve the Great Race finale by taking the crown or publicly exposing the fixing.
The Great Race: Crown or Truth.questStatement: You can win the Great Race, or you can throw it in a way that makes the fix undeniable, and the timing means you cannot do both.
The Great Race: Crown or Truth.questDesignBrief: Part 4 and conclusion of The Great Race chain. The Great Race runs on the final day of the Gathering with the whole Confederacy watching, and the player can win it or use it to make the fixing undeniable, and the timing of the exposure means they cannot do both. Winning delivers standing, a mount, clan recognition and Sora Kazekami's undivided respect as the person who finally beat her or nearly did, and leaves the corruption intact to poison the next three seasons. Throwing the race in the specific way that exposes the fix burns the crown, humiliates the player publicly in the moment, and cleans the sport in front of a parliament that is already assembled and cannot ignore it. Fuyu argues for the truth. Sora, interestingly, argues for the win, because racing is the only thing she has ever fully trusted and she does not want it to be the thing that gets broken open. Both endings should leave the relationship intact but differently shaped. This concludes the chain.

Memories That Are Not Yours: The Submerg.name: Memories That Are Not Yours: The Submerged Entry
Memories That Are Not Yours: The Submerg.mainObjective: Hear an archivist explain the judgment behind your admission.
Memories That Are Not Yours: The Submerg.questStatement: The Drowned Memory Archive admits people it finds interesting, which is not a metaphor and not a courtesy, and the door has opened for you.
Memories That Are Not Yours: The Submerg.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the Memories That Are Not Yours chain and the player's introduction to the Drowned Memory Archive. The archive sank into the Spiritfen marshwater centuries ago and now exists in the material and spirit worlds at once, which means the water is waist deep in rooms that are also completely dry depending on how you look at them. It collected crystallized recollections rather than books. The submerged entry does not open for everyone and the beat should make that explicit and uncomfortable: the player is assessed, by something, and admitted, and nobody can tell them what the criterion was. Shion Mizugaki meets them inside and is professionally welcoming and personally wary, because admissions have been irregular lately and she does not believe in coincidence. Asagi Minakami is delighted by the player for exactly the same reason. Establish the archive's nature, the two archivists, the flooded record halls with their crystallized memory shelving, and the fact that being let in was a judgment rather than a courtesy. Sets up Borrowed Recollection.

Memories That Are Not Yours: Borrowed Re.name: Memories That Are Not Yours: Borrowed Recollection
Memories That Are Not Yours: Borrowed Re.mainObjective: Identify whose life you experienced in the borrowed memory.
Memories That Are Not Yours: Borrowed Re.questStatement: Memory is stored in water here, and the stack you were sent to has just given you an afternoon that belonged to somebody else.
Memories That Are Not Yours: Borrowed Re.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of the Memories That Are Not Yours chain, and the beat that hooks the whole thing. The archive stores memory in water and in crystal, and reading is done by immersion rather than by looking. The player is sent to an ordinary shelf on ordinary business and takes a memory that is not theirs and not the one they reached for. Write the borrowed memory as a complete, specific, ordinary afternoon belonging to somebody else: a kitchen, a disagreement, a decision that seemed small. It should be emotionally particular rather than expository, and the player should surface knowing things about a stranger's life that they have no right to know. Shion's reaction is immediate alarm because misfiling is not a thing this archive does. Asagi's is fascination. The identification of whose memory it was should require work in the librarian's gallery and the central index, and the name that comes back matters later in the chain. Follows The Submerged Entry and sets up The Archivists Disagree.

Memories That Are Not Yours: The Archivi.name: Memories That Are Not Yours: The Archivists Disagree
Memories That Are Not Yours: The Archivi.mainObjective: Put your chosen quarantine or reading policy into effect in the Archive.
Memories That Are Not Yours: The Archivi.questStatement: Shion Mizugaki wants the affected stack quarantined immediately, Asagi Minakami wants it read to the bottom first, and they have stopped speaking to each other about it.
Memories That Are Not Yours: The Archivi.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of the Memories That Are Not Yours chain, and its faction beat. Shion Mizugaki wants the affected stack quarantined and the preservation wing sealed before contamination spreads further. Asagi Minakami wants it read to the bottom first on the grounds that quarantining an archive destroys the only thing an archive is for. Both are right and both are frightened, and they have stopped speaking to each other directly, which means the player is carrying messages between two people standing forty feet apart in a flooded hall. The player has to commit, and the commitment should hold for the rest of the chain: backing Shion means restricted access and a safer, slower investigation, backing Asagi means the run of the stacks and no protection at all. Write the disagreement as professional rather than petty, with each of them making the other's argument better than the other does. Whichever way it falls, the archivist who lost should stay involved and stay civil. Follows Borrowed Recollection and sets up The Leak.

Memories That Are Not Yours: The Leak.name: Memories That Are Not Yours: The Leak
Memories That Are Not Yours: The Leak.mainObjective: Reach the unindexed source shelf of the memory contamination.
Memories That Are Not Yours: The Leak.questStatement: The contamination is spreading between stacks, which the Archive has never done, and it is spreading along a path rather than outward.
Memories That Are Not Yours: The Leak.questDesignBrief: Part 4 of the Memories That Are Not Yours chain. Contamination is moving between stacks, which the archive has never done in its recorded history, and it is not spreading outward the way a spill would. It is following a path. The work is tracing that path through the record halls and the communication array, wading between shelves where the water is chest high in the material world and ankle deep in the spirit one, and the route the contamination takes implies somebody chose it. Depending on which archivist the player backed, they are doing this with institutional support and restricted hours or alone with unlimited access and no backup. Spirit-realm hazards should be present without becoming the point. The trail terminates at a source shelf that appears on no index, in a section of the preservation wing that both archivists will confirm does not exist. Follows The Archivists Disagree and sets up Your Own File.

Memories That Are Not Yours: Your Own Fi.name: Memories That Are Not Yours: Your Own File
Memories That Are Not Yours: Your Own Fi.mainObjective: Answer the Archive's offer of your own file by reading it or explicitly refusing.
Memories That Are Not Yours: Your Own Fi.questStatement: There is a memory of you on the source shelf, filed and dated, from before you arrived in this world.
Memories That Are Not Yours: Your Own Fi.questDesignBrief: Part 5 of the Memories That Are Not Yours chain and its centerpiece. On the source shelf, filed and dated in the archive's own hand, is a memory of the player. The date is before their arrival in this world. This should be staged quietly, with no monster and no interruption, in a small dry room inside a flooded building. The player can read it or refuse to. Reading it costs something specific and permanent and gives them something equally specific. Refusing it leaves the file intact and knowable, which is its own weight to carry, and the archive will not offer twice. Whichever archivist the player backed is present and reacts in character: Shion urges refusal and containment, Asagi cannot conceal that she wants it read and is ashamed of wanting that. Do not resolve what the file means or who filed it. The beat is the decision and the moment of standing in front of it. Follows The Leak and sets up Drain It or Drink It.

Memories That Are Not Yours: Drain It or.name: Memories That Are Not Yours: Drain It or Drink It
Memories That Are Not Yours: Drain It or.mainObjective: Drain or absorb the contaminated memory stack.
Memories That Are Not Yours: Drain It or.questStatement: The stack can be drained, which destroys everything in it including whatever was kept about you, or it can be taken in, which does not.
Memories That Are Not Yours: Drain It or.questDesignBrief: Part 6 and conclusion of the Memories That Are Not Yours chain. The affected stack can be drained, which destroys every memory in it including whatever the archive kept about the player, or it can be taken in, which preserves all of it inside a person instead of a building. Draining is the responsible choice and erases a truth about the player permanently, and Shion Mizugaki will help without hesitation. Absorbing grants knowledge that nobody else in Luxcellia has and changes the player measurably and visibly, and Asagi Minakami will help with an eagerness that should worry them. Stage it at the preservation wing with the water going down or coming up depending on the choice. The archive itself should feel like a participant rather than scenery; it admitted the player for a reason and this is the reason. Both endings are survivable and neither is clean. The archivist who was overruled stays and keeps working, which is the most human note available. This concludes the chain.

The Gate That Opens Both Ways: The Warde.name: The Gate That Opens Both Ways: The Warden's Lodge
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: The Warde.mainObjective: Hear Jinrei explain why he stopped logging crossings.
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: The Warde.questStatement: Jinrei Sumizu has logged every crossing at the Spiritgate for nineteen years and stopped writing six weeks ago without telling anyone why.
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: The Warde.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of The Gate That Opens Both Ways chain. The Spiritgate is a torii standing alone on a fog-shrouded island where looking through the arch shows the spirit realm laid over the physical one, and Jinrei Sumizu has logged every crossing there for nineteen years. Six weeks ago he stopped writing. The lodge is small, orderly, and full of nineteen years of identical ledgers, and the gap at the end of the current one is the loudest thing in the room. Jinrei is not evasive so much as carefully literal: he answers exactly what is asked and nothing adjacent. Getting the real answer requires either patience or the offering platforms, where what has been left recently does not match what the log says has crossed. The Spiritgate has always been understood as a one-way courtesy, the dead going through and the living not, and the beat's job is to establish that rule clearly before breaking it. Yuri Kagerou can confirm the protocol and is the one who says out loud what Jinrei will not. Sets up Nine Hundred Lanterns.

The Gate That Opens Both Ways: Nine Hund.name: The Gate That Opens Both Ways: Nine Hundred Lanterns
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: Nine Hund.mainObjective: Present the identities of the two living people with lit memorial lanterns.
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: Nine Hund.questStatement: Ancestor's Rest lights one lantern for each of the district's dead, and two of the lanterns burning tonight belong to people who are still alive.
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: Nine Hund.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of The Gate That Opens Both Ways chain, moving to Ancestor's Rest. The island graveyard lights one lantern for each of the district's dead, and the dead here are not gone; they sit among their own tombstones and receive visitors with the hospitality of people who have all the time in the world, which makes the investigation unusually cooperative and unusually strange. Two of tonight's lanterns belong to people who are still alive. The work is a census done gently: cross the lantern bridge, walk the memorial islands, ask the residents, and let them answer at their own unhurried pace. Tamao Usuzumi assists and is the emotional counterweight to the whole chain, eighteen and unhurried and better at sitting with grief than anyone the player has met. One of the two living names should land close to the player or to someone they have already met in this chain. The dead themselves find the situation improper rather than frightening, which is worse. Follows The Warden's Lodge and sets up The Returned.

The Gate That Opens Both Ways: The Retur.name: The Gate That Opens Both Ways: The Returned
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: The Retur.mainObjective: Hear the returned person's account of what crossing back cost them.
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: The Retur.questStatement: Somebody in Ghostlight Harbor appears on the register of the dead and on the harbor's tax rolls, and they are going about their week either way.
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: The Retur.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of The Gate That Opens Both Ways chain, relocating to Ghostlight Harbor where the mortal docks and the spirit quarter overlap. Somebody here appears on the register of the dead and on the harbor's tax rolls and is going about their week either way. The search runs through the canal district and the lantern workshop with Sayo Hotarubi's help, and the harbor's dual nature means the player is asking questions on both sides of the veil at once. The returned individual is the beat's whole point and must not be written as a monster: they are lucid, polite, working, and entirely unable to explain themselves. They remember dying. They remember coming back. They do not remember agreeing to it and they are frightened in a contained, ordinary way that is far more affecting than horror. What crossing back cost them should be specific and visible once the player knows to look. Do not resolve how it happened. Follows Nine Hundred Lanterns and sets up What They Brought.

The Gate That Opens Both Ways: What They.name: The Gate That Opens Both Ways: What They Brought
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: What They.mainObjective: Resolve the stowaway's presence through removal, return or a negotiated arrangement.
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: What They.questStatement: Whatever came back through the Spiritgate did not come alone, and the second thing has not introduced itself.
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: What They.questDesignBrief: Part 4 of The Gate That Opens Both Ways chain and its escalation. Whatever came back through the Spiritgate did not come alone, and the second passenger has been in Ghostlight Harbor for six weeks without introducing itself. The hunt runs through the canal district, the shipwright's yard and the lantern workshop at night, with Suzune Kawaragi providing local knowledge and a great deal of nerve. The passenger is genuinely dangerous and genuinely afraid, which should make the confrontation more than a fight: it did not choose to cross either, it does not belong on this side, and what it has been doing to stay is the thing that has been thinning the boundary. Give the player room to resolve it by force, by negotiation, or by returning it, and make each cost something different. Ghostlight's lanterns and canal water should carry the scene visually. Follows The Returned and sets up Close It or Widen It.

The Gate That Opens Both Ways: Close It.name: The Gate That Opens Both Ways: Close It or Widen It
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: Close It.mainObjective: Enact your decision to seal or open the Spiritgate.
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: Close It.questStatement: The Spiritgate can be sealed properly for the first time in its history, or it can be opened honestly in both directions, and the fen will be a different place either way.
The Gate That Opens Both Ways: Close It.questDesignBrief: Part 5 and conclusion of The Gate That Opens Both Ways chain. Back at the Spiritgate, with everything the player has learned, the arch can be sealed properly for the first time in its history or opened honestly in both directions. Sealing protects the living, ends the crossings, and abandons every one of the dead who has ever wanted to come back, including the ones the player has now met and liked. Opening dignifies both sides and makes the Spiritfen permanently unpredictable, with consequences the region will absorb for generations. Jinrei Sumizu wants it sealed because nineteen years of logs have taught him what the rule is for. Yuri Kagerou wants it opened because she has spent her life at a boundary she thinks is a lie. Tamao Usuzumi, if the player brought her, says almost nothing and is the person whose face they will remember. Stage it at the gate plaza in fog with both worlds visible through the arch. This concludes the chain.

The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: Ambass.name: The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: Ambassador's Introduction
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: Ambass.mainObjective: Secure Wakaba's arrangement of an audience at the Coiled Temple.
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: Ambass.questStatement: Wakaba Hiorigami is the only member of the Verdant Throne who deals with outsiders, she can get you an audience at the Coiled Temple, and she would very much rather you did not ask her to.
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: Ambass.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of The Serpent That Is Still Coiled chain, opening at Verdanthrone, the living temple city where every structure is a shaped tree and every wall is growing wood. Wakaba Hiorigami is the Verdant Throne's only outward-facing member and the sole route to an audience at the Coiled Temple, and she does not want to arrange it. The beat is a conversation rather than a trial, held in the throne grove and the rootsinger's garden, and her reluctance is the information the player is actually gathering. She is warm, botanically expressive, and evasive in a way that is clearly costing her something. The Throne's official position is that the temple houses a statue and the offerings are tradition. Wakaba does not contradict this and does not defend it either. Getting the introduction requires the player to give her a reason she can put in front of the Throne without it looking like doubt. Establish the temple, the nine centuries of offerings, and the political cost of asking the question at all. Sets up The Inner Sanctum.

The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The In.name: The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Inner Sanctum
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The In.mainObjective: Compare the inner sanctum's rib count with the temple register.
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The In.questStatement: Jasar Hebimichi has kept the temple for thirty years and will show you the coil itself, on the condition that you count the ribs.
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The In.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of The Serpent That Is Still Coiled chain. The temple is a pre-Luxcellian structure built in the shape of a coiled serpent, descending into the earth in concentric rings with round corridors that never quite let you walk straight. Jasar Hebimichi has kept it for thirty years and takes the player down through the outer and middle coils to the inner sanctum with the manner of a man conducting a tour he has given before and never enjoyed. At the bottom is the coil itself. He asks the player to count the ribs. The instruction sounds absurd until they do it, because the number does not match the number recorded in the temple's own register, and the register has been kept continuously for nine hundred years by people who had no reason to lie about ribs. Jasar is precise, sane and long disbelieved, and his relief at having a witness should be understated. The venom library and specimen gallery en route establish how much the builders knew. Follows Ambassador's Introduction and sets up The Offering Cycle.

The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Of.name: The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Offering Cycle
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Of.mainObjective: Identify the offerings' purpose as a regimen keeping the serpent asleep.
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Of.questStatement: The temple has fed the coil on a fixed cycle for nine centuries, and nobody currently living knows what the cycle is preventing.
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Of.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of The Serpent That Is Still Coiled chain, and its research beat. The temple has fed the coil on a fixed schedule for nine centuries and nobody currently alive can say what the schedule is for. The work is done in the venom library and the ritual basin among records in a script that predates the Evergrove's current language, cross-referenced against Jasar's own thirty years of logs. What emerges is that the composition of the offerings matters more than the quantity, that the recipe is pharmacological rather than devotional, and that the cycle is a dosing regimen. The temple has not been worshipping the serpent. It has been keeping it under. Jasar has suspected this for a decade and has never had the linguistic support to prove it, and the moment the player confirms it he goes very quiet. The implication that lands hardest is that somebody nine hundred years ago decided this was better than the alternative and did not write down why. Follows The Inner Sanctum and sets up The Ribbing Moves.

The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Ri.name: The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Ribbing Moves
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Ri.mainObjective: Submit recorded proof of the serpent's movement to the Verdant Throne.
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Ri.questStatement: You have seen it move and Jasar has seen it move, and the Verdant Throne will dismiss both of you unless the evidence is undeniable.
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Ri.questDesignBrief: Part 4 of The Serpent That Is Still Coiled chain. Both the player and Jasar have now seen movement, and the Verdant Throne will dismiss two witnesses as easily as one unless the evidence is impossible to argue with. The beat is careful, methodical verification inside a dangerous structure: fixed reference marks, timed observations across the incubation chambers and the inner sanctum, measurements taken the same way twice. The temple is A to S rank and the player should be at genuine risk while doing patient work, which is the tension of the beat. How Jasar has been treated so far pays off here; if the player has taken him seriously he gives them the thirty years of context that makes the evidence conclusive, and if not he gives them only what was asked. What they leave with must be something the Throne is constitutionally required to respond to rather than something it can refer to committee. Follows The Offering Cycle and sets up The Throne's Position.

The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Th.name: The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Throne's Position
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Th.mainObjective: Get the Verdant Throne's formal acknowledgment that the serpent is alive.
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Th.questStatement: Verdanthrone must now take a position on a nine-century arrangement, in public, and it will take the wrong one unless somebody has laid the ground.
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: The Th.questDesignBrief: Part 5 of The Serpent That Is Still Coiled chain, returning to Verdanthrone for a political beat in the throne grove. The Verdant Throne must now take a public position on a nine hundred year arrangement it has never examined, and it will take the wrong one out of institutional reflex unless the player has prepared the ground. Preparation is the gameplay: who has been spoken to beforehand, what Mei-Lin Rootsinger and Tsumugi Hanamori have been shown, whether Jasar attends in person and whether that helps or hurts. Wakaba Hiorigami is exposed by association here, having arranged the introduction that started all this, and the player can protect her or spend her for a better outcome. The session should be conducted with the courtesy of a place that settles things slowly, in a chamber grown rather than built, and the outcome is an acknowledgment rather than a decision: the serpent is alive, the Throne says so aloud, and the question of what to do about it becomes formally open. Follows The Ribbing Moves and sets up Wake It or Keep the Vigil.

The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: Wake I.name: The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: Wake It or Keep the Vigil
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: Wake I.mainObjective: Perform the ritual that wakes the serpent or renews the vigil.
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: Wake I.questStatement: The serpent can be woken, which nobody has attempted in nine centuries, or the vigil can be renewed, which commits the Evergrove for nine more.
The Serpent That Is Still Coiled: Wake I.questDesignBrief: Part 6 and conclusion of The Serpent That Is Still Coiled chain. Two futures, both nine centuries long. Waking the serpent is irreversible, unprecedented, and might be exactly right; the builders sedated something they did not destroy, and nobody has ever asked it anything. Renewing the vigil is safe, sustainable and commits another nine generations of the Evergrove to feeding something in the dark on a schedule they still will not understand. Jasar Hebimichi, who has given thirty years to the vigil, argues for waking it, and that reversal should carry real weight. Wakaba Hiorigami argues for the vigil and is arguing for her whole civilization's stability rather than for tradition. Stage the finale at the ritual basin in the inner sanctum with the coil filling the chamber. Whichever is chosen, the Evergrove is committed and the player is the reason. Give the ending room to be quiet rather than explosive. This concludes the chain.

Spores in the Nave: The Nave Bloom.name: Spores in the Nave: The Nave Bloom
Spores in the Nave: The Nave Bloom.mainObjective: Complete a direct safety assessment of the nave bloom.
Spores in the Nave: The Nave Bloom.questStatement: The Spore Cathedral grew rather than being built, it has been dormant for four hundred years, and something in the nave has flowered.
Spores in the Nave: The Nave Bloom.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the Spores in the Nave chain. The Spore Cathedral is not a ruin; it is a living fungal megastructure with its own ecosystem and its own awareness of everything inside it, and it has been dormant for four hundred years. Something in the spore nave has flowered. The approach through the mycelium bridge and into the nave should be beautiful and biologically wrong in equal measure: corridors that are fungal tubes, walls that respond to breath, light coming from the growth itself. Fantina Houshiko is the resident researcher and is both the player's guide and, subtly, someone whose account does not quite line up. The task is assessment rather than combat: establish what the bloom is, how fast it is growing, and whether it threatens anyone, because the Evergrove will act on whatever information reaches it first and currently has none. The cathedral's awareness should be felt rather than demonstrated. End with the player able to speak about the bloom with authority. Sets up What Fantina Is Not Saying.

Spores in the Nave: What Fantina Is Not.name: Spores in the Nave: What Fantina Is Not Saying
Spores in the Nave: What Fantina Is Not.mainObjective: Hear Fantina explain why she stayed beyond her posting.
Spores in the Nave: What Fantina Is Not.questStatement: Fantina Houshiko's posting to the cathedral ran out two years ago and she is still here, which Suiren Mochibana has only just noticed.
Spores in the Nave: What Fantina Is Not.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of the Spores in the Nave chain and its character beat. Fantina Houshiko's research posting expired two years ago and she is still living in the cathedral, which Suiren Mochibana has only just noticed while filing paperwork. The reason is sympathetic and compromising: she has formed a relationship with the organism that is closer than the Evergrove's rules permit, and the symbiont garden shows exactly how far it has gone. She is not a villain and is not concealing malice; she is concealing something she knows will end her career and separate her from the only thing she has ever fully understood. How the player handles this decides whether she becomes the chain's most valuable asset or a liability who is removed at the worst moment. Suiren is genuinely fond of her and genuinely obligated to report, which is the pressure. The growth chambers and the neural core should feature, and the organism's regard for Fantina should be visible to anyone paying attention. Follows The Nave Bloom and sets up The Second Nave.

Spores in the Nave: The Second Nave.name: Spores in the Nave: The Second Nave
Spores in the Nave: The Second Nave.questStatement: There is a chamber the surveys do not have, Fantina has been in it, and the bloom started directly above it.
Spores in the Nave: The Second Nave.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of the Spores in the Nave chain. There is a chamber below the archive bloom that appears on no survey, Fantina has been in it, and the flowering began directly above it. Reaching it is physically demanding and requires passing through the neural core, which is the closest thing the cathedral has to a mind and which notices the player individually. What is down there explains the four hundred year dormancy and, more importantly, what ended it. The chamber should be older than the cathedral around it, which raises the possibility that the fungus grew here because of what was already present rather than the other way round. Fantina's willingness to guide depends entirely on part two. The beat's atmosphere is pressure, spore-thick air, and the growing sense that the structure is aware of being investigated and has not decided how it feels about that. Follows What Fantina Is Not Saying and sets up Harvest or Burn.

Spores in the Nave: Harvest or Burn.name: Spores in the Nave: Harvest or Burn
Spores in the Nave: Harvest or Burn.mainObjective: Stop the bloom's spread by harvesting or destroying it.
Spores in the Nave: Harvest or Burn.questStatement: The bloom is worth a fortune to the right buyer and it is spreading toward inhabited canopy at a rate somebody has already calculated.
Spores in the Nave: Harvest or Burn.questDesignBrief: Part 4 and conclusion of the Spores in the Nave chain. The bloom is worth a great deal to the right buyer and it is expanding toward inhabited canopy on a timetable the player can now calculate. Harvesting is defensible if the spread can be controlled and enriches whoever the player chooses to enrich. Burning is safe, immediate, and destroys something that took four hundred years to become possible and cannot be recreated. The complication is Fantina Houshiko, who will not survive the second option intact in any sense that matters, and Suiren Mochibana, who has to file whatever happens. The Evergrove's canopy settlements are real people with a real deadline, so the safety argument should not be abstract. Stage the finale in the spore nave with the bloom at full extent and the cathedral aware of the decision being made inside it. Both endings should feel like a loss of something. This concludes the chain.

The Mines Answer Back: The Active Face.name: The Mines Answer Back: The Active Face
The Mines Answer Back: The Active Face.mainObjective: Elicit a direct response from the song at the active mine face.
The Mines Answer Back: The Active Face.questStatement: The Resonance Mines have sung at the working face for as long as anyone has cut stone there, and this season the song started answering questions.
The Mines Answer Back: The Active Face.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of The Mines Answer Back chain. The Resonance Mines are a working crystal mine and a hazard zone at once: the vein amplifies any energy it contacts, so every spell cast underground comes out unpredictably larger, and the crews have adapted by working almost entirely without magic. The mines have sung at the active face for as long as anyone has cut there and everyone treats it as ordinary. The player takes a shift, which should be physical, loud, dusty and genuinely companionable, with Doumen Kanenari and Tsurara Suishouden working alongside. The turn is quiet: the player says something, and the song changes, and it changes in a way that corresponds. Everyone else is too far up the tunnel or too used to the noise to notice, and the crew's easy acceptance of the singing makes the moment worse rather than better. Establish the mines, the amplification hazard, the crew's rhythm, and the single instance of response. Do not let anyone else confirm it yet. Sets up Doumen's Recording.

The Mines Answer Back: Doumen's Recordin.name: The Mines Answer Back: Doumen's Recording
The Mines Answer Back: Doumen's Recordin.mainObjective: Produce a translation of part of the mine's song with Doumen.
The Mines Answer Back: Doumen's Recordin.questStatement: Doumen Kanenari has transcribed the mine song for eleven years, filling nine notebooks, and the transcription has structure.
The Mines Answer Back: Doumen's Recordin.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of The Mines Answer Back chain, and its best character beat. Doumen Kanenari has transcribed the mine song for eleven years across nine notebooks, working in the frequency lab on his own time, and has been regarded by the cartel as a harmless eccentric for all eleven of them. He is not eccentric and the transcription is not noise. The work is analytical: help him sort the notebooks, identify recurring structures, and establish that the song has grammar. It is a language, it is not any language anyone has heard, and the partial translation the two of them produce contains something that reads unmistakably as a warning. Doumen's response to being right after eleven years should be careful rather than triumphant; he has been humored so long that he checks his own findings twice before saying them aloud. Tsurara is the one who takes it to the crew and gets nowhere. The harmonic corridor and deep resonance chamber can be used to test the translation acoustically. Follows The Active Face and sets up The Collapsed Entrance.

The Mines Answer Back: The Collapsed Ent.name: The Mines Answer Back: The Collapsed Entrance
The Mines Answer Back: The Collapsed Ent.mainObjective: Reach the concealed working inside Ironvein Drift.
The Mines Answer Back: The Collapsed Ent.questStatement: Ironvein Drift came down the same week the song changed, the cartel called it subsidence, and Tetsu Tetsuō was on shift and does not agree.
The Mines Answer Back: The Collapsed Ent.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of The Mines Answer Back chain, relocating to Ironvein Drift. The drift's entrance came down in the same week the song changed. The Crystalvein Cartel recorded it as subsidence and closed the file. Tetsu Tetsuo was on shift that day, has said otherwise to everyone who would listen, and has been moved to a worse rotation for it. Getting in means excavating a collapse that the cartel has no interest in reopening, through fungal galleries and ore chambers, with headlamp enchantments that are unreliable this close to the resonance vein. The physical work should be dangerous and slow. What the player finds past the collapse is a working that was cut and then concealed: a section opened, emptied and deliberately brought down behind whoever left. Tetsu's vindication should be brief and unsatisfying, because being right about a collapse that nearly killed him is not much of a prize. Follows Doumen's Recording and sets up What Was Cut Into.

The Mines Answer Back: What Was Cut Into.name: The Mines Answer Back: What Was Cut Into
The Mines Answer Back: What Was Cut Into.mainObjective: Identify the current holder of the material extracted from the concealed working.
The Mines Answer Back: What Was Cut Into.questStatement: Something was mined out of the deep rock and taken, and the mine has been asking about it ever since.
The Mines Answer Back: What Was Cut Into.questDesignBrief: Part 4 of The Mines Answer Back chain and its reveal. Something was mined out of the deep rock, removed, and the collapse was arranged to hide the fact rather than the hole. The investigation runs between the concealed working and the cartel's own processing records in Crystalvein, and Tsurara Suishouden is the one with the access to match extraction volumes against declared output. What was taken should be specific, physically describable, and clearly not an ore. Connecting it to the song is the moment the chain's threads join: the mine has been asking about it since the week it went, and Doumen's translated warning is about the removal rather than about the miners. End with a name and a buyer, both of them real people with reasons, and neither of them cartoonishly villainous. The amplification hazard should complicate at least one confrontation here. Follows The Collapsed Entrance and sets up Put It Back or Sell It.

The Mines Answer Back: Put It Back or Se.name: The Mines Answer Back: Put It Back or Sell It
The Mines Answer Back: Put It Back or Se.mainObjective: Physically return the extraction to the rock or deliver it to the buyer.
The Mines Answer Back: Put It Back or Se.questStatement: The cartel has a buyer arranged, the mine wants what was taken from it returned, and both of those things cannot happen.
The Mines Answer Back: Put It Back or Se.questDesignBrief: Part 5 and conclusion of The Mines Answer Back chain. The cartel has a buyer arranged and a sum attached that would fund the Deephollow for a generation. The mines want what was taken from them returned. Both cannot happen. Returning it quiets the song, closes the anomaly, and costs Crystalvein an amount of money the city will feel for years, with real consequences for miners who have nothing to do with any of this. Completing the sale makes the region genuinely rich and leaves the mines asking a question forever, which Doumen Kanenari understands better than anyone and will say so once, without pleading. The cartel's argument should be economically serious rather than greedy. Stage the finale at the deep resonance chamber with the song audible throughout. Doumen, Tsurara and Tetsu land on different sides for reasons consistent with what the chain has shown of each of them. This concludes the chain.

The Springs Remember: The Crystal Pools.name: The Springs Remember: The Crystal Pools
The Springs Remember: The Crystal Pools.mainObjective: Experience the pools' shared vision by drinking from them.
The Springs Remember: The Crystal Pools.questStatement: Geode Springs shows every drinker something true about themselves, and for the last month it has been showing everybody the same thing instead.
The Springs Remember: The Crystal Pools.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of The Springs Remember chain. Geode Springs sits inside a crystal formation so large the walls form a natural dome, with mineral water heated by deep volcanic vents and steam refracted into rainbow mist overhead. The springs have always shown a drinker something true about themselves, which is the entire basis of the region's affection for the place. For the last month they have been showing everybody the same thing instead, and the shared vision is specific enough to be investigated rather than dismissed. The player drinks and sees it. Write the vision concretely: a place, a direction, an act, rendered clearly enough that it can be pursued. Kirara Suishouin runs the pools and is worried in the practical way of somebody whose livelihood depends on the springs being trustworthy. The atmosphere should be warm, communal and slightly wrong, with other bathers comparing notes in low voices. Sets up The Same Vision, Fourteen People.

The Springs Remember: The Same Vision, F.name: The Springs Remember: The Same Vision, Fourteen People
The Springs Remember: The Same Vision, F.mainObjective: Assemble the bathers' differing visions into one coherent instruction.
The Springs Remember: The Same Vision, F.questStatement: Fourteen people have described the same vision and every account differs in exactly one detail, which is not how shared hallucinations work.
The Springs Remember: The Same Vision, F.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of The Springs Remember chain, and its satisfying investigative beat. Fourteen people have now described the shared vision and every account differs in exactly one detail, which is not how shared hallucination works and is not how memory works either. The gameplay is interviews conducted across Geode Springs and up into Crystalvein: a miner, a courting couple, a Depthwarden, a cartel clerk, each remembering the same thing with one element uniquely theirs. Akari Suitama has been keeping notes without knowing why and is the player's collaborator.
