The payoff is that the differing details are not errors; assembled in the right order they form a coherent instruction. Getting that order should require thought rather than luck. Write the fourteen as distinct people with distinct reasons for being at the springs, because the humanity of the sample is what makes the pattern land. Follows The Crystal Pools and sets up The Heart Well.

The Springs Remember: The Heart Well.name: The Springs Remember: The Heart Well
The Springs Remember: The Heart Well.mainObjective: Identify the source of the shared vision at the heart well.
The Springs Remember: The Heart Well.questStatement: The Luminous Grotto's heart well feeds every spring in the region, and Nozomi Kagebotan has been keeping people away from it for three weeks.
The Springs Remember: The Heart Well.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of The Springs Remember chain, moving to the Luminous Grotto. The heart well feeds every spring in the region, the grotto is the Deephollow's most famous romantic destination, and Nozomi Kagebotan has been quietly turning couples away from the deep end of it for three weeks with increasingly thin excuses. Her obstruction is protective rather than sinister and she should be relieved to stop lying. The grotto itself is the visual high point of the chain: bioluminescent crystals coating every surface in shifting blues and violets, a ceiling so densely clustered with glowing growth that it reads as a night sky. What is at the heart well is the source of the shared vision, and it is not healthy. Whether it is a thing, a person or a process is for the beat to reveal; what matters is that the springs have been transmitting rather than inventing, and something upstream is the one doing the transmitting. Follows The Same Vision, Fourteen People and sets up Tell the City or Keep It.

The Springs Remember: Tell the City or K.name: The Springs Remember: Tell the City or Keep It
The Springs Remember: Tell the City or K.mainObjective: Carry out your decision to disclose or contain the heart-well finding.
The Springs Remember: Tell the City or K.questStatement: Crystalvein runs on the springs being trustworthy, and you now know something about them that would end that.
The Springs Remember: Tell the City or K.questDesignBrief: Part 4 and conclusion of The Springs Remember chain. Crystalvein City runs on the springs being trustworthy: the tourism, the courtship customs, the mineral trade and a fair amount of the Deephollow's sense of itself. The player now knows something that would end that. Disclosure protects everyone who drinks from the springs and collapses an economy and a set of traditions built on them, and Kirara Suishouin will back it and lose her livelihood doing so. Containment preserves the city and leaves a falsehood running under it that the player will have to keep maintaining, and Nozomi Kagebotan will help and never quite forgive it. Neither is cowardice and neither is heroism. Stage the decision back at the crystal pools with the rainbow mist and the ordinary bathers who have no idea. Whatever is chosen should have a visible immediate consequence rather than a deferred one. This concludes the chain.

The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Piers at.name: The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Piers at First Light
The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Piers at.mainObjective: Place the envoy's seal in the keeping of a willing representative, yourself or another.
The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Piers at.questStatement: Nine came up out of the water at dawn for the first time in three generations, their envoy made eleven steps and sat down, and the seal needs hands.
The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Piers at.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of The Tide-Courts Send Word chain, opening on the working piers of Tsukihana Harbor at dawn. Nine figures come up out of the water for the first time in three generations, which stops the harbor completely: pearl boats hold position, the ferry landing empties, and the morning market simply forgets to open. Their envoy makes eleven steps up the boards and sits down carefully, and does not get up. It is not violence or poison; it is the crossing itself, which some of them cannot survive and there is no way to know which until it is happening. The tide-courts do not postpone, they substitute, and substitution requires only that the seal be held by somebody standing. Amaya Tamau, who dived for a living before she built a fortune, is the one person on the pier who understands what is being asked and says so plainly. The seal is heavier than it looks. Establish the delegation, the crossing sickness, the reception at dusk, and the fact that nobody consulted the player. Sets up The Causeway Hours.

The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Causeway.name: The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Causeway Hours
The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Causeway.mainObjective: Finish translating the message before the causeway floods.
The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Causeway.questStatement: The tide-courts' message is written in a script the surface has not needed for three generations, and Pearlwake Shrine keeps its hours by the flood rather than the bell.
The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Causeway.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of The Tide-Courts Send Word chain, relocating to Pearlwake Shrine across a tidal causeway that closes with the flood. The tide-courts' message is written in a script the surface has not needed for three generations and the only people who can still read it keep their hours by the water rather than the bell. High Tide Priestess Tsukiyomi will help, on her own terms, and her terms involve the player understanding what they are carrying before she translates it. The clock is real: the causeway floods, the sanctuary is cut off until the next low, and the reception is at dusk. The shrine's sacred pools glow at high tide and the incense smells of salt and starlight, which should carry the scene. Tsukimi Ayase assists with the older script. What the message actually says is worse than the harbor assumed, and the translation should land as a complication rather than a solution. Follows The Piers at First Light and sets up The Coast's Answer.

The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Coast's A.name: The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Coast's Answer
The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Coast's A.mainObjective: Present your account of the coastal houses' positions at the reception.
The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Coast's A.questStatement: Every house on the coast has spent three generations building around the assumption that the sea does not send anybody, and at dusk they will all be in one room with you.
The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Coast's A.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of The Tide-Courts Send Word chain, back at Tsukihana Harbor for the dusk reception. Every house on the coast has spent three generations arranging its affairs around the assumption that the sea does not send anybody, and at dusk they are all in one room with the player and a seal they cannot ignore. The beat is social navigation under pressure: pearl merchants, shipping interests, shrine authority and a Sovereignty observer, all being extremely polite. The player's objective is not to win the room but to map it, because knowing which houses are merely inconvenienced and which are genuinely afraid determines everything later. Tsukimi Ayase attends from the shrine and is the most useful read in the room. The waterfront at night with lanterns on the bridges and moon-viewing boats offshore is the setting. Nobody threatens anybody. Somebody should nonetheless leave the player in no doubt that a threat was made. Follows The Causeway Hours and sets up Down the Stair.

The Tide-Courts Send Word: Down the Stai.name: The Tide-Courts Send Word: Down the Stair
The Tide-Courts Send Word: Down the Stai.mainObjective: Arrive inside the Moon-Tide Palace Below.
The Tide-Courts Send Word: Down the Stai.questStatement: The tide-courts have invited you down, the stair is real, and nobody from the surface has walked it in living memory.
The Tide-Courts Send Word: Down the Stai.questDesignBrief: Part 4 of The Tide-Courts Send Word chain and its threshold beat. The tide-courts have invited the player down, the descent pool is real, and nobody from the surface has made the journey in living memory. The Moon-Tide Palace Below only fully manifests during certain tides, so the window matters and missing it means waiting a month the situation does not have. The descent should be physically demanding and genuinely awe-inducing: silver water, pearl doors, halls of impossible beauty patrolled by pearl sentries and drowned court dancers who are not hostile and not entirely present. The player passes out of surface law entirely here, which the beat should make felt rather than stated. Whoever the player has brought from the surface reacts to the scale of it. The upper halls and the tidal approach carry the sequence. End at the throne gallery with the player admitted and out of their depth in both senses. Follows The Coast's Answer and sets up The Matriarch's Terms.

The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Matriarch.name: The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Matriarch's Terms
The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Matriarch.mainObjective: Identify the succession cost hidden in the accord's terms.
The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Matriarch.questStatement: Pearl Matriarch Kashimi will deal, her terms are more generous than the surface deserves, and generosity from the deep is never free.
The Tide-Courts Send Word: The Matriarch.questDesignBrief: Part 5 of The Tide-Courts Send Word chain. Pearl Matriarch Kashimi will deal, and her terms are more generous than the surface has any right to expect, which is the problem. She is ancient, courteous, entirely reasonable and playing a game measured in generations rather than seasons. The gameplay is reading a document properly: the accord's headline terms are open-handed and its cost is buried in a clause about succession that only makes sense if you know how the coastal houses inherit. Tamaki Shinjutani can be persuaded to explain the deep courts' customs; Umi Kase can be persuaded to explain what the last accord did. Kashimi does not conceal the clause and will confirm it if asked directly, which makes her honest and does not make her safe. Stage it in the throne gallery with silver water underfoot. End with the player understanding exactly what signing would commit the surface to. Follows Down the Stair and sets up Sign or Refuse.

The Tide-Courts Send Word: Sign or Refus.name: The Tide-Courts Send Word: Sign or Refuse
The Tide-Courts Send Word: Sign or Refus.mainObjective: Give Pearl Matriarch Kashimi your answer by signing or explicitly refusing the accord.
The Tide-Courts Send Word: Sign or Refus.questStatement: Three generations of arrangement between the sea and the shore now rest on whether you put the seal to the page.
The Tide-Courts Send Word: Sign or Refus.questDesignBrief: Part 6 and conclusion of The Tide-Courts Send Word chain. Three generations of arrangement between the sea and the shore come down to whether the player puts the seal to the page. Signing reopens the water to the coast, restores the pearl trade and the old shrine calendars, and binds the surface to a succession clause it does not fully understand and will be living with long after everyone in the room is dead. Refusing preserves the coast's independence, honors nobody, and closes the sea for another lifetime, which the delegation will accept with a grace that is worse than anger. Amaya Tamau argues for signing on commercial and human grounds. Tsukimi Ayase argues for refusal on the grounds that the shrine has read the last accord and knows how the last one ended. Kashimi accepts either outcome without changing expression. Stage it in the throne gallery as the tide turns and the palace begins to withdraw. This concludes the chain.

The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Ninety-Six Con.name: The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Ninety-Six Confirmed
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Ninety-Six Con.mainObjective: Have the Guild record your arrival at the ninety-seventh floor door.
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Ninety-Six Con.questStatement: Ninety-six floors of the Riftmaw lie above you, every one of them walked, and everything below the door is simply the price of standing in front of it.
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Ninety-Six Con.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of The Ninety-Seventh Floor chain and the world's deepest endgame content, picks up after all ninety-six upper floors have been crossed. The final descent is the heart of the chapter: past floor fifty the architecture stops following normal physics, and the approach corridor to the door contains architecture from another world entirely, appearing beneath Luxcellia without explanation. Dungeon-born abominations and artificial guardians patrol it. The Guild will log the descent and its interest in doing so is unusually intense for a routine registration, which is the first thread. Beside the antechamber the player finds the Dream Camp, Monaka's research camp, where previous expeditions stopped and did not go further, and the state of it says a great deal. Monaka Kugirime is waiting at the door itself and has been for eleven months. Establish the door, the keeper and the Guild's attention. Sets up The Keeper's Question.

The Ninety-Seventh Floor: The Keeper's Q.name: The Ninety-Seventh Floor: The Keeper's Question
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: The Keeper's Q.questStatement: Monaka Kugirime has kept watch on this door for eleven months, and she asks everyone who arrives the same single question before she considers opening anything.
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: The Keeper's Q.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of The Ninety-Seventh Floor chain and its character centerpiece. Monaka Kugirime has kept watch on this door for eleven months and asks everyone who reaches it the same single question before she will consider opening anything. The question is short, personal, and has nothing to do with strength or clearance. She records the answer. She has recorded every answer anyone has ever given her and the record is in the antechamber where the player can read it if they think to look, which is a far better use of the beat than combat. There is no correct answer, only an honest one and a dishonest one, and she can tell the difference immediately and without drama. Write her as neither cryptic nor forbidding; she is patient, direct, faintly amused, and has had eleven months to get comfortable. What the player says here should be referenced by the chain's ending. Follows Ninety-Six Confirmed and sets up What the Guild Filed.

The Ninety-Seventh Floor: What the Guild.name: The Ninety-Seventh Floor: What the Guild Filed
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: What the Guild.mainObjective: Identify who authorized the amendment cutting the Riftmaw records off at floor ninety-four.
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: What the Guild.questStatement: The Guild's official floor records stop at ninety-four, two floors short of the foot of the Last Stair, and somebody signed off on that.
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: What the Guild.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of The Ninety-Seventh Floor chain, surfacing from the deepest place in the world to a filing office. The Guild's official Riftmaw records stop at floor ninety-four, which is two floors short of what every experienced delver has walked, and somebody signed the amendment. The investigation runs through Guild archives and the Frontier's expedition rosters, and the further it goes the clearer it becomes that this was not clerical caution but a decision taken at a level that had reasons. Whoever signed it is still alive and still employed. The tonal contrast between the antechamber and a records room should be used deliberately: the player has walked ninety-six floors and is now being obstructed by a clerk and a retention policy. What emerges reframes the Guild's eagerness to log the descent in part one. Do not resolve the motive fully; establish that the suppression was deliberate and recent enough to matter. Follows The Keeper's Question and sets up Through.

The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Through.name: The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Through
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Through.mainObjective: Return to the antechamber from beyond the ninety-seventh floor threshold.
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Through.questStatement: The door opens, and what is on the other side is not a floor.
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Through.questDesignBrief: Part 4 of The Ninety-Seventh Floor chain and its payoff. The door opens and what is on the other side is not a floor. Keep the sequence short, strange and physically disorienting rather than combat-heavy; the ninety-seventh is not a dungeon level and treating it like one wastes it. Whatever the player finds should reframe the entire Riftmaw retroactively: experienced first, then understood. Beyond the door is where the Builders went when they sealed it (lore: The Answer of the Reborn), and something there notices the player and is glad; the player comes back knowing what the door is and why Reborn are called. Monaka Kugirime does not come. She has never been through and says so without embarrassment, which tells the player something about what keeping the door has meant. The actual objective is returning, and returning should be in genuine doubt: the way back is not guaranteed to be where the way in was, and the player's answer to the keeper's question in part two should have some bearing on how the space treats them. Come out changed in a way that is specific and describable. Follows What the Guild Filed and sets up Report or Seal.

The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Report or Seal.name: The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Report or Seal
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Report or Seal.mainObjective: Deliver your report to the Guild or physically seal the floor.
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Report or Seal.questStatement: What you tell the Guild about the ninety-seventh floor changes the Ashenmere Frontier permanently, and so does saying nothing.
The Ninety-Seventh Floor: Report or Seal.questDesignBrief: Part 5 and conclusion of The Ninety-Seventh Floor chain. What the player tells the Adventurer's Guild changes the Ashenmere Frontier permanently, and so does telling them nothing. Reporting opens the deepest floor in the world to every faction that can field an expedition, transforms the Frontier's economy within a season, and hands the thing beyond the door to institutions that have already demonstrated they will edit inconvenient records. Sealing protects it, makes a liar of the player in front of the Guild, and effectively makes them Monaka Kugirime's successor whether or not either of them says so. Monaka will accept either and should not lobby; her only contribution is to point out, mildly, that she was asked the same question once. Stage it at the door, with the record of answers brought from the antechamber. Whatever is chosen should close the chain with weight rather than fanfare. This concludes the chain.

The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Ward Thres.name: The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Ward Threshold
The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Ward Thres.mainObjective: Gain Noctis's admission past the sanctum's ward threshold.
The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Ward Thres.questStatement: The Dominion's deepest ward has held one continuous note for centuries, Noctis Kagehira keeps it alone, and he does not admit visitors.
The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Ward Thres.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of The Sanctum Holds a Note chain, at the top of the world's power band. The Umbral Resonance Sanctum is an abandoned demon research facility where shadow magic resonance experiments went catastrophically wrong, and it exists in dimensional overlap: rooms flicker between the material and shadow planes at irregular intervals, with different architecture and different things in them on each side. Noctis Kagehira has kept the ward alone for a very long time and does not admit visitors, which is policy rather than temperament. Getting past the ward threshold is earned through competence: surviving the flickering halls, demonstrating that the player will not make the situation worse, and understanding enough of what the ward does to be worth talking to. The single continuous note that fills the sanctum should be present in every scene, felt in the teeth as much as heard. Establish the sanctum, its keeper, the note and the fact that Noctis has noticed something is wrong and has told nobody. Sets up The Note's Shape.

The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Note's Sha.name: The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Note's Shape
The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Note's Sha.mainObjective: Hear Noctis identify what the sanctum's note is sealing away.
The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Note's Sha.questStatement: The note is not decoration and not devotion. It is a seal held by sound, and Noctis will tell you what is behind it if you can stand to hear it.
The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Note's Sha.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of The Sanctum Holds a Note chain, and its reveal. The note is not devotion and not decoration. It is a seal maintained by sound, held continuously for centuries, and Noctis Kagehira will explain what it is holding closed if the player can stand to hear it. The beat runs through the dual laboratory and the resonance core, where the original experiments are still legible in the equipment and the notes, and where the player can work out most of the answer themselves before he confirms it. What is behind the seal should have implications reaching well past the Twilight Dominion and into the rest of the continent, and it should be described precisely enough to be frightening rather than vaguely enough to be safe. Noctis is not dramatic about any of this; he has lived with it for so long that he delivers it as maintenance information. The entity chamber can be glimpsed and not entered. Follows The Ward Threshold and sets up The Waver.

The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Waver.name: The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Waver
The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Waver.mainObjective: Trace the ward's interference to its source below the sanctum.
The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Waver.questStatement: The note has begun to waver, which centuries of maintenance say should be impossible, and it is not decay.
The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Waver.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of The Sanctum Holds a Note chain. The note has begun to waver, which centuries of maintenance records say should be impossible, and Noctis Kagehira has already ruled out everything he can rule out alone. The work is systematic elimination conducted inside a facility that is actively hostile: check the resonance core, check the shadow archive, verify the material and shadow plane readings separately because the flicker means half of any measurement is taken somewhere else. Decay would look different. Sabotage from inside would look different. What remains is external interference arriving from below, which the sanctum's own architecture insists is solid rock. Doing careful scientific work in a place where the room you are standing in changes every few minutes is the tension of the beat. Noctis's growing alarm should be visible only to someone who has spent the last two quests learning to read him. Follows The Note's Shape and sets up The Catacomb Below.

The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Catacomb B.name: The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Catacomb Below
The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Catacomb B.mainObjective: Hear Damian explain the catacomb work's effect on the ward.
The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Catacomb B.questStatement: Obsidian Heart Catacomb connects to the sanctum, Damian Kokushinden has always known that, and he has never mentioned it to the ward keeper.
The Sanctum Holds a Note: The Catacomb B.questDesignBrief: Part 4 of The Sanctum Holds a Note chain, descending into Obsidian Heart Catacomb, a dark crystal dungeon formed around the fossilized remains of an ancient dimensional rift where reality is unstable and demon ancestor echoes patrol the passages. Damian Kokushinden has always known the catacomb connects to the sanctum above and has never mentioned it to the ward keeper, which is the confrontation. He should not be a simple antagonist: his reasoning is coherent, his goal is defensible from where he stands, and what he is doing in the inscription chamber has a purpose that would be sympathetic if it were not destabilizing a seal he does not fully understand. The player can ally with him, oppose him, or take what they know back up to Noctis and let the two of them meet, which is the most interesting option and the most dangerous. Follows The Waver and sets up Rebuild or Release.

The Sanctum Holds a Note: Rebuild or Rel.name: The Sanctum Holds a Note: Rebuild or Release
The Sanctum Holds a Note: Rebuild or Rel.mainObjective: Perform the working that rebuilds or deliberately releases the ward.
The Sanctum Holds a Note: Rebuild or Rel.questStatement: The ward can be rebuilt on a new footing, which costs the Dominion something it cannot easily give, or it can be let go on purpose rather than by accident.
The Sanctum Holds a Note: Rebuild or Rel.questDesignBrief: Part 5 and conclusion of The Sanctum Holds a Note chain. The ward can be rebuilt on a new footing, which requires resources and commitments the Twilight Dominion cannot easily give and will remember giving, or it can be released deliberately rather than allowed to fail on its own schedule. Rebuilding preserves the seal, indebts the Dominion permanently to whoever arranged it, and commits somebody to keeping the note for the next several centuries. Releasing on the player's terms is genuinely safer than releasing by accident and still ends the arrangement that has held since the facility was abandoned. Noctis Kagehira has given his life to the note and will accept either, and the beat should make clear which one costs him more without letting him say it. Damian Kokushinden's fate is bound up in the choice. Stage the finale at the resonance core with the note audible and unstable, flickering between planes. This concludes the chain.

What the Sovereign Wants: Titan's Approa.name: What the Sovereign Wants: Titan's Approach
What the Sovereign Wants: Titan's Approa.mainObjective: Receive Elder Sylnara's grant of an audience at the heartwood sanctum.
What the Sovereign Wants: Titan's Approa.questStatement: The Verdant Sovereign receives almost no one, the approach alone is a test of standing, and Elder Sylnara decides who reaches the heart.
What the Sovereign Wants: Titan's Approa.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the What the Sovereign Wants chain, opening at the Elder Tree Heart where petals fall upward, the light is permanently golden, and the ground carries a heartbeat that is not the player's. The Elder Tree is a living titan whose roots span miles, and the Verdant Sovereign at its center receives almost nobody. Elder Sylnara decides who reaches the heartwood sanctum and has been doing so for centuries. The approach itself is the test: Titan's Approach is elite-danger terrain and the standing required to be received cannot be faked, argued for, or purchased. Sakuya Yozakuraryu can advise on what Sylnara actually weighs. The scale should be overwhelming and the pace slow, and the beat should resist combat in favor of awe and protocol. Shinra Kouyaryu is present and visibly carrying something. Establish the Sovereign's scale, Sylnara's gatekeeping, and the fact that audiences have become more frequent this year rather than less. Sets up Sylnara's Warning.

What the Sovereign Wants: Sylnara's Warn.name: What the Sovereign Wants: Sylnara's Warning
What the Sovereign Wants: Sylnara's Warn.mainObjective: Hear Sylnara describe the Sovereign's request that frightened her.
What the Sovereign Wants: Sylnara's Warn.questStatement: Sylnara has served the Sovereign for centuries without fear, and the requests it has begun making in the last year frighten her.
What the Sovereign Wants: Sylnara's Warn.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of the What the Sovereign Wants chain and its first hard turn. Elder Sylnara has served the Verdant Sovereign for centuries without fear and is frightened now, and getting her to say so plainly is the whole beat. The requests coming out of the heartwood sanctum in the past year have changed in kind rather than degree: they are more specific, more frequent, and they are asking for things rather than accepting them. Sylnara's loyalty makes this almost impossible for her to articulate, and the player should have to earn it through patience rather than pressure. Her account should be concrete: three requests, what each one asked for, and why the third one made her stop sleeping. Sakuya Yozakuraryu confirms the pattern from a different angle. The crown veil and the heartwood sanctum carry the scene, with the Sovereign present and enormous and not participating. Follows Titan's Approach and sets up The First Request.

What the Sovereign Wants: The First Requ.name: What the Sovereign Wants: The First Request
What the Sovereign Wants: The First Requ.mainObjective: Give effect to your answer to the Sovereign's first request through fulfillment, refusal or an alternative.
What the Sovereign Wants: The First Requ.questStatement: The Sovereign asks something of you directly. It is small, it is reasonable, and it is wrong.
What the Sovereign Wants: The First Requ.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of the What the Sovereign Wants chain. The Verdant Sovereign addresses the player directly for the first time and asks for something small. It is genuinely small, entirely reasonable, easily done, and wrong in a way the player can detect if they are paying attention to what it implies rather than what it requires. This is the chain's hook and it should be constructed carefully: the task itself should be almost trivial, and the implication should be visible only on reflection. Carrying it out, refusing it, or finding a third path all remain open, and the Sovereign's response to each sets its attitude toward the player for the rest of the chain. Elder Sylnara watches and does not intervene. The Sovereign's manner of speech should be unhurried to the point of being difficult, communicating across a timescale where the player's whole life is a short interval. Follows Sylnara's Warning and sets up The Last Reborn's Expedition.

What the Sovereign Wants: The Last Rebor.name: What the Sovereign Wants: The Last Reborn's Expedition
What the Sovereign Wants: The Last Rebor.mainObjective: Hear Shinra disclose where the previous Reborn expedition ended.
What the Sovereign Wants: The Last Rebor.questStatement: Shinra Kouyaryu knows where the previous Reborn's final expedition went, and that knowledge will either heal him or unmake him.
What the Sovereign Wants: The Last Rebor.questDesignBrief: Part 4 of the What the Sovereign Wants chain and its emotional centerpiece. Shinra Kouyaryu knows where the previous Reborn's final expedition went and has carried that knowledge alone because saying it aloud will either heal him or unmake him. Handling him badly loses the player an ally and the chain's key fact. Handling him well requires actual patience: he deflects, he changes subject, he offers smaller truths first, and the real account only comes when he decides it will. What he says should connect the previous Reborn's disappearance directly to what is happening beneath the Elder Tree, which is the moment the chain's two halves lock together. Stage it away from the sanctum, somewhere quieter in the crown veil, with the two of them alone. Shinra's state afterward should be visibly different regardless of how it goes. Follows The First Request and sets up What Grows Underneath.

What the Sovereign Wants: What Grows Und.name: What the Sovereign Wants: What Grows Underneath
What the Sovereign Wants: What Grows Und.mainObjective: Discover what is growing in the Root Abyss.
What the Sovereign Wants: What Grows Und.questStatement: The heart is not the whole tree, the root system runs further than any map, and something down there has been growing on its own schedule.
What the Sovereign Wants: What Grows Und.questDesignBrief: Part 5 of the What the Sovereign Wants chain, descending into the Root Abyss. The heart is not the whole tree; the root system runs further than any map and something down there has been growing on a schedule of its own. The descent is elite-danger and should be physically oppressive, with the golden light failing, the heartbeat in the ground getting louder and less reassuring, and the roots forming spaces that were clearly not shaped for anybody to walk. Sakuya Yozakuraryu accompanies if the relationship supports it and is out of her depth for the first time in the chain. What the player finds explains the Sovereign's new requests entirely and recontextualizes the first request in part three as considerably less small. Do not let the discovery be a monster; let it be a condition. Follows The Last Reborn's Expedition and sets up Consent or Refuse.

What the Sovereign Wants: Consent or Ref.name: What the Sovereign Wants: Consent or Refuse
What the Sovereign Wants: Consent or Ref.mainObjective: Tell the Sovereign your final consent or refusal directly.
What the Sovereign Wants: Consent or Ref.questStatement: The Sovereign asks for the thing it has been building toward all year, and nobody in the history of the Wilds has told it no.
What the Sovereign Wants: Consent or Ref.questDesignBrief: Part 6 and conclusion of the What the Sovereign Wants chain. The Verdant Sovereign asks for the thing the whole year has been building toward, and nobody in the recorded history of the Wilds has ever told it no. Consenting reshapes Verdania and possibly a good deal more, on the authority of something older and wiser than any institution the player has dealt with, which is exactly what makes it frightening. Refusing is unprecedented, and the Wilds will feel it immediately in ways that fall on people who had no part in the decision. Elder Sylnara, Shinra Kouyaryu and Sakuya Yozakuraryu split three ways, each consistent with what the chain has established about them, and each argument should be the best version of itself. Stage the finale in the heartwood sanctum with the Sovereign fully present. The ending should be quiet, enormous, and slow, and the region should be visibly different afterward. This concludes the chain.

The Crownless Throne: The Rumor at Court.name: The Crownless Throne: The Rumor at Court
The Crownless Throne: The Rumor at Court.mainObjective: Identify who is paying to circulate the crownless-throne claim.
The Crownless Throne: The Rumor at Court.questStatement: A claim to a throne nobody has sat on in three hundred years has started circulating in Aureliath, and it is circulating too well to be idle talk.
The Crownless Throne: The Rumor at Court.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of The Crownless Throne chain, opening in Aureliath at street level rather than in the palace. A claim to a throne nobody has sat on in three hundred years has begun circulating, and it is circulating too well and too consistently to be idle talk: the same details, the same phrasing, in the guild quarter and the noble quarter and along academy road within the same week. Somebody is spending money. The work is tracing rumor to source through the market district and the guild quarter, and the player should have to distinguish between people repeating it, people seeding it, and people who have been paid to seem like the first while being the second. Establish the crownless throne itself, the sealed vault beneath the capital, and the fact that the Sovereignty's official position is that the whole subject is a historical curiosity. End with a name or a paymaster, and with the player's own inquiries having been noticed. Sets up The Proving Labyrinth.

The Crownless Throne: The Proving Labyri.name: The Crownless Throne: The Proving Labyrinth
The Crownless Throne: The Proving Labyri.mainObjective: Finish a full run of the Proving Labyrinth.
The Crownless Throne: The Proving Labyri.questStatement: The old test of legitimacy still runs beneath the capital, Shougo Meikyuuin still administers it, and it has not been walked in a very long time.
The Crownless Throne: The Proving Labyri.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of The Crownless Throne chain. The Royal Proving Labyrinth was built centuries ago beneath the palace to test heirs, and it has been sealed for three generations because the current dynasty has not needed testing. Shougo Meikyuuin still administers it and has been waiting a very long time for somebody to require his services. The labyrinth is a real dungeon with combat, puzzle and moral wings, and its moral challenges are the point: it was designed to test whether a potential ruler possesses the qualities the dynasty valued, and it is entirely indifferent to whether the person walking it wants to rule. The judgment chamber and the reflection room should be genuinely uncomfortable. Shougo is precise, formal, and privately delighted, and he narrates the trial with the pride of a man dusting off something beautiful. What the labyrinth concludes about the player is recorded and matters later. Follows The Rumor at Court and sets up The Deep Vault.

The Crownless Throne: The Deep Vault.name: The Crownless Throne: The Deep Vault
The Crownless Throne: The Deep Vault.mainObjective: Hear Reizen explain the crown's true nature in the deep vault.
The Crownless Throne: The Deep Vault.questStatement: Reizen Oukanashi has guarded a crown nobody wears, alone, for longer than the current dynasty has existed.
The Crownless Throne: The Deep Vault.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of The Crownless Throne chain, descending to the Crownless Throne Vault beneath Aureliath: failed summoning circles, hero relics that did not work, broken crowns, and prophecy-corrupted guardians patrolling chambers the Crown sealed and stopped discussing. Reizen Oukanashi has guarded it alone for longer than the current dynasty has existed. He is formidable and should not be fought if there is any alternative, and the alternative is that he has been alone with this for a very long time and would like to talk to somebody who has walked the Proving Labyrinth. What he says about the crown reframes the entire claim: the throne is crownless for a reason, the reason is documented in the constitutional chamber, and the documentation is not what the Sovereignty's histories say. Reizen is tired rather than hostile, and his exhaustion is the most persuasive thing about him. Follows The Proving Labyrinth and sets up What Legitimacy Costs.

The Crownless Throne: What Legitimacy Co.name: The Crownless Throne: What Legitimacy Costs
The Crownless Throne: What Legitimacy Co.mainObjective: Communicate your decision about who may receive verification of the claim.
The Crownless Throne: What Legitimacy Co.questStatement: The claim is real. That is the inconvenient part, and it is now your problem as much as the Crown's.
The Crownless Throne: What Legitimacy Co.questDesignBrief: Part 4 of The Crownless Throne chain and its turn. The claim is genuine. Verifying it beyond dispute is the straightforward half, done between the vault's constitutional chamber and the Sovereignty's own archives in Aureliath, and the documents hold up. The hard half is that a verified truth is a weapon, and the player now controls who is holding it. The beat should force decisions about disclosure: showing it to the claimant's backers, to the Crown, to the Church, or to nobody, each of which starts a different clock. Somebody should attempt to buy it and somebody should attempt to bury it, both politely. The three endings available in part six should become visible here as real options rather than abstractions. Aureliath's council wing and noble quarter carry the political texture. End with the player certain of the truth and uncertain what to do with it, which is the correct place to be. Follows The Deep Vault and sets up The Queen's Position.

The Crownless Throne: The Queen's Positi.name: The Crownless Throne: The Queen's Position
The Crownless Throne: The Queen's Positi.mainObjective: Hear the Queen disclose her reason for not acting on the claim.
The Crownless Throne: The Queen's Positi.questStatement: Queen Celestine has known about the claim for years, and the reason she has done nothing is not cowardice.
The Crownless Throne: The Queen's Positi.questDesignBrief: Part 5 of The Crownless Throne chain. Queen Celestine Luxcrown has known about the claim for years and has done nothing, and the reason is neither cowardice nor conspiracy. The beat is a single long conversation, granted rather than demanded, in which she gives a full and candid account of a decision the player may still disagree with: what she inherited, what she verified, what she calculated the Sovereignty could survive, and what she decided to carry personally rather than put in front of a council. She should be tired, precise and entirely unapologetic without being cold. The player can challenge her and should find that she has already made every argument against herself. Nothing is resolved here and no permission is granted; what the player leaves with is the understanding that the crown has been governed by somebody thinking carefully, which makes the final choice harder rather than easier. Follows What Legitimacy Costs and sets up Crown, Bury, or Take.

The Crownless Throne: Crown, Bury, or Ta.name: The Crownless Throne: Crown, Bury, or Take
The Crownless Throne: Crown, Bury, or Ta.mainObjective: Carry out your chosen fate for the crownless throne: crown the claimant, bury the claim or take it up yourself.
The Crownless Throne: Crown, Bury, or Ta.questStatement: The claim can be crowned, buried, or taken up by you, and the Sovereignty survives all three as a different country.
The Crownless Throne: Crown, Bury, or Ta.questDesignBrief: Part 6 and conclusion of The Crownless Throne chain, with three genuine endings. Crowning the legitimate claimant installs a rival with a real right and puts the Sovereignty through a succession it has not prepared for, which is honest and destabilizing. Burying the claim preserves three hundred years of stability on a documented falsehood and makes the player complicit in maintaining it alongside Celestine. Taking it up personally makes the player a claimant with the Proving Labyrinth's recorded judgment behind them, which is the most dangerous option and the one Reizen Oukanashi least expects. Reizen accepts any of the three and says so, having guarded the vault long enough to have stopped believing any of them is clean. Shougo Meikyuuin's labyrinth record becomes relevant. Stage the finale in the seal chamber with the broken crowns present. Crownveil should be visibly a different country afterward whichever path is taken. This concludes the chain.

The Confession Maze: The Welcoming Arch.name: The Confession Maze: The Welcoming Arch
The Confession Maze: The Welcoming Arch.questStatement: The Church's maze takes a truth from everyone who walks it, the arch is the only entrance, and there is no version where you come out having given nothing.
The Confession Maze: The Welcoming Arch.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of The Confession Maze chain. The Gilded Confession Maze is a beautiful and unnerving structure of stained glass corridors where spoken lies become monsters and hidden desires take form, and the deeper anyone goes the more honesty the place demands. The welcoming arch is the only entrance and there is no version of walking it in which the player gives nothing. The beat should be personal and exposing: confession shades and guilt wraiths materialize from dishonesty rather than patrolling, so the danger scales with what the player is concealing. Tsubasa Myojo administers the arch with genuine kindness, which makes it worse. What the maze takes from the player is recorded by the Church, and the recording should be shown happening. Establish the mechanism, its keepers, and the fact that the extraction is not optional and never has been. The confessional alcove and resonance chamber carry the sequence. Sets up The One Who Did Not.

The Confession Maze: The One Who Did Not.name: The Confession Maze: The One Who Did Not
The Confession Maze: The One Who Did Not.mainObjective: Locate the Church record of the visitor who gave the maze nothing.
The Confession Maze: The One Who Did Not.questStatement: Somebody walked the maze and gave it nothing, which the Church's records treat as an administrative error rather than an impossibility.
The Confession Maze: The One Who Did Not.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of The Confession Maze chain. Somebody walked the maze and gave it nothing, and the Church's records treat this as an administrative error rather than the impossibility it is. The work is archival, conducted in Church holdings with Tsubasa Myojo's cooperation, and the interesting texture is how thoroughly the anomaly was processed rather than investigated: reclassified, appended, filed, and never revisited by anyone with the authority to be curious. The record exists and is complete, which means somebody chose not to look rather than failed to notice. Tsubasa's reaction on seeing it should be professional distress; the maze is her life's work and its authority rests entirely on it being unbeatable. The date on the record matters and should point somewhere uncomfortable. Follows The Welcoming Arch and sets up What Ryou Withheld.

The Confession Maze: What Ryou Withheld.name: The Confession Maze: What Ryou Withheld
The Confession Maze: What Ryou Withheld.mainObjective: Hear Ryou explain how he withheld his confession from the maze.
The Confession Maze: What Ryou Withheld.questStatement: The maze's own keeper is the anomaly, and Ryou Seikagami has been administering a truth-extraction rite while withholding his own.
The Confession Maze: What Ryou Withheld.questDesignBrief: Part 3 of The Confession Maze chain and its confrontation. The maze's own keeper is the anomaly: Ryou Seikagami has been administering a truth-extraction rite for years while withholding his own, and he knows exactly how he did it. His reason is human, sympathetic and does not excuse him, and the beat works best if the player wants to forgive him and can see precisely why they should not. The confrontation should happen inside the maze, in the shade gallery or at the threshold, where the structure itself is reacting to a conversation in which one party is lying by long practice. What he withheld should be specific and small enough to be recognizable rather than melodramatic. Tsubasa Myojo's presence or absence changes the scene considerably and the player can choose whether to bring her. The player decides what the Church learns and when. Follows The One Who Did Not and sets up Fix It or Learn From It.

The Confession Maze: Fix It or Learn Fro.name: The Confession Maze: Fix It or Learn From It
The Confession Maze: Fix It or Learn Fro.mainObjective: Repair the confession maze or publicly demonstrate its flaw.
The Confession Maze: Fix It or Learn Fro.questStatement: A maze that can be beaten is either repaired quietly or studied openly, and the Church will do whichever you make easiest.
The Confession Maze: Fix It or Learn Fro.questDesignBrief: Part 4 and conclusion of The Confession Maze chain. A maze that can be beaten is either repaired quietly or studied openly, and the Church of the First Light will do whichever the player makes easiest. Repairing it restores the instrument's reliability, preserves its authority over everyone who walks it in future, and requires burying Ryou Seikagami along with the flaw. Exposing the flaw ends the maze's authority, protects every person who would otherwise be judged by an instrument that can be gamed, and hands the Church a humiliation it will remember. Tsubasa Myojo argues for repair because she believes in the instrument. Ryou argues for exposure because he has spent years knowing it does not work and being the only one who does. Stage the finale at the glass confessor's chamber. Neither ending should feel like a victory over a villain; the flaw was always in the design. This concludes the chain.

Summoned and Discarded: Severance and a.name: Summoned and Discarded: Severance and a Side Door
Summoned and Discarded: Severance and a.mainObjective: Accept your first work contract from the Adventurer's Guild in Aureliath.
Summoned and Discarded: Severance and a.questStatement: The Crown dismissed you, but the Adventurer's Guild offers a way forward. This opening quest ends when you accept your first Guild work contract in Aureliath. Registration alone is not enough; finishing the contract or attracting the Court's attention is not required. Your opening inventory already contains the severance purse; this quest does not grant another twenty-five gold.
Summoned and Discarded: Severance and a.questDesignBrief:
Part 1 of the Summoned and Discarded chain. Play the Guild registration scene in Aureliath: the queue, the form, the rank assignment, and choosing work that will have the discarded summon. The single finishing event is the player accepting their first Guild work contract. End this chapter at that acceptance. Do not require completion of the job, an unusual feat, an observer's reaction or the Court Mage's attention. Those can develop later through the chosen job and the optional next chapter, The Power They Couldn't Measure. Keep the player free to choose the contract.

ORIGIN AND PAYMENT: Available through the selected Summoned and Discarded story start only. A later visit to Aureliath, the palace, or the Guild is not that origin. Preserve the player's existing history. The opening inventory already includes the Crown's 25 gold: never add that purse again on discovery, acceptance, progress, or completion.

Border Corruption: The Wagons That Weigh.name: Border Corruption: The Wagons That Weigh Wrong
Border Corruption: The Wagons That Weigh.mainObjective: Trace the missing requisitioned supplies to Fort Dawnsward's requisition yard.
Border Corruption: The Wagons That Weigh.questStatement: Greyhaven’s militia captain has counted the requisition wagons for a season, and the fort logs more taken than the village ever handed over. He mentioned it once to the wrong clerk, and the escorts stopped coming. He needs someone unattached to follow the wagons and find out who is eating the difference.
Border Corruption: The Wagons That Weigh.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the Border Corruption arc. The hook is a small, concrete accounting discrepancy that the player can verify themselves: count a requisition, compare it to the receipt, follow a wagon north from Greyhaven toward Fort Dawnsward. Genta Aramaki (militia captain) is the source; Otoha Suzukake (innkeeper) independently holds the honest numbers and can corroborate. Establish the human cost, the Broken Row, the stripped market, so the corruption is felt, not just tallied. The beat ends with the trail pointing unmistakably at the fort’s requisition yard and a merchant house the player cannot yet name. Do not reveal Baron Thorne yet. Sets up The Fort’s Crooked Supply.

Border Corruption: The Fort’s Crooked Su.name: Border Corruption: The Fort’s Crooked Supply
Border Corruption: The Fort’s Crooked Su.mainObjective: Obtain the ledger or contracts identifying the Crownveil baron behind the requisition laundering.
Border Corruption: The Fort’s Crooked Su.questStatement: The missing supplies pass through Dawnsward’s requisition yard and out again through a merchant house whose contracts no one at the fort will audit. Commander Tategami knows the numbers don’t add up and has told herself a crooked supply line beats no supply line while the fort must not fall. The proof is a ledger in her tower drawer she has refused to open.
Border Corruption: The Fort’s Crooked Su.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of the Border Corruption arc. The player works inside a fort under real siege pressure, where “the fort must not fall” genuinely justifies a great deal, which is exactly what makes the corruption hard to expose without endangering the line. Commander Tategami is the loyal-and-blind fulcrum: she can be pushed to open the ledger, or protected from having to. The shell house is Baron Thorne’s, though his name should surface only at the edge here, a seal, a signature, a magistrate’s stamp the player recognizes from Crownveil law. End with the player holding proof that the laundering runs to a Crown baron, and a choice about Tategami’s complicity. Sets up The Baron’s Necessary War.

Border Corruption: The Baron’s Necessary.name: Border Corruption: The Baron’s Necessary War
Border Corruption: The Baron’s Necessary.mainObjective: Act on the proof of Baron Thorne's profiteering through exposure, a negotiated deal or deliberate suppression.
Border Corruption: The Baron’s Necessary.questStatement: The border war’s misery has been feeding Baron Thorne, whose shell house logs civilian grain, livestock, and lumber as fort supply and resells the difference, the quotas inflated to cover the skim, every objection buried under the fort must not fall. The proof is in the player’s hands. What is not decided is what exposing a Crown baron does to the fort that depends on his crooked supply, and to the officer who let it happen.
Border Corruption: The Baron’s Necessary.questDesignBrief: Part 3 and conclusion of the Border Corruption arc. Baron Thorne is the authored villain (a Crownveil baron who weaponizes the legal system); this arc gives the war a schemer without inventing one. The climax is a decision, not a fight: Thorne’s corruption is procedurally spotless on paper, and destroying him may sever Dawnsward’s only supply line at the worst moment. Let the player choose the shape of the ending, public exposure, a quiet leveraged deal, protecting or burning Commander Tategami, forcing the Crown to actually supply its own fort, and let each choice carry a real cost to the front. Thorne should be dangerous precisely because everything he did was legal and framed as necessity. Conclusive: the arc resolves here, however the player resolves it.

Raise Your Banner.name: Raise Your Banner
Raise Your Banner.mainObjective: Register your Company at an Adventurer's Guild hall.
Raise Your Banner.questStatement: Any Adventurer's Guild hall will charter a new Company: a name, a crest, a fee, and two partners willing to stand under your banner.
Raise Your Banner.questDesignBrief: The player founds their own Adventurer Company. The player names it and chooses its crest; never invent either. At least two willing partners must agree on screen to stand under the banner: companions, other players, or recruits won over in play. Registration happens at any Adventurer's Guild hall desk: the clerk takes the charter fee (one Gold Coin, or a Blank Company Charter with the fee prepaid), records an address (an inn room is fine), and paints the crest on the Company Board at Iron rank. A clerk may ask awkward questions, and a rival Company may be watching the board. Partners who agree are Company members, not automatically party members.

Trial Contract: Earn a Banner.name: Trial Contract: Earn a Banner
Trial Contract: Earn a Banner.mainObjective: Be accepted into a Company by its leader after your trial contract.
Trial Contract: Earn a Banner.questStatement: Every Company recruits by trial. Ask, prove yourself on one contract alongside its members, and let the leader decide whether you fly its banner.
Trial Contract: Earn a Banner.questDesignBrief: The player asks to join an existing Adventurer Company. Its leader, or a member speaking for the leader, sets one trial contract that fits the Company's specialty: a Riftmaw dive for Deepwatch Lantern Company, a warren bounty for The Flagon Irregulars, an escort for Tidecrest Company or The Gilded Caravan Company, a hunt for The Frostfang Hunt, a trail job for The Greenwake Company, a public bout for The Vaunted Blade Company, an ore run for The Emberforge Company. Stormblood Vanguard offers no trials; it invites, and only after deeds the whole continent has heard of. At least one member works the trial with the player. Afterward the leader gives a verdict in person; the quest completes only on acceptance, and a failed trial can be asked for again later. Acceptance brings a crest pin and a standing welcome at the hall, not a party: members keep their own posts.

Company Contract: The Depth Board.name: Company Contract: The Depth Board
Company Contract: The Depth Board.mainObjective: Have your Company's new deepest floor painted on the Riftmaw Depth Board.
Company Contract: The Depth Board.questStatement: The Riftmaw Depth Board at the Floor Zero Gatehouse lists the deepest floor each Company has reached and come back from. Your Company's line is waiting to be written, or beaten.
Company Contract: The Depth Board.questDesignBrief: A Company Contract for a player who belongs to an Adventurer Company. The player's Company dives the Riftmaw together and must come back alive from a floor deeper than its current line on the Depth Board; a first dive sets the line. Floor danger follows the Riftmaw's depth bands, and the Company chooses how far to push. Deepwatch Lantern Company members may offer advice or a lantern, and a rival Company may be on the same stairs. The Guild paints the new line only for a return its clerk can confirm. Pay follows the normal bands for the deepest floor reached.

Company Contract: Pearl Road Escort.name: Company Contract: Pearl Road Escort
Company Contract: Pearl Road Escort.mainObjective: Deliver the pearl convoy safely to the Sapphire Sail Market.
Company Contract: Pearl Road Escort.questStatement: A pearl merchant wants a Company, not a lone sword, to bring a convoy of sea pearls along the coast from Portmaris to the Sapphire Sail Market, and Tidecrest and the Gilded Caravan are both bidding.
Company Contract: Pearl Road Escort.questDesignBrief: A Company Contract for a player who belongs to an Adventurer Company. A pearl convoy runs from Portmaris along the coast road to the Sapphire Sail Market. The player's Company wins the bid, or shares it with Tidecrest Company or The Gilded Caravan Company, whose rivalry makes the road tense. Threats: coastal raiders, a sea-cave monster, a bribed drover, and a rival bidder who would like the convoy to arrive late. Pay is C-rank, a few Gold, on delivery.

Company Contract: The Quarry Warrens.name: Company Contract: The Quarry Warrens
Company Contract: The Quarry Warrens.mainObjective: Clear the Monster Warrens of The Howling Quarry.
Company Contract: The Quarry Warrens.questStatement: The Flagon Irregulars posted a Company Contract they cannot finish alone: the Monster Warrens under The Howling Quarry are breeding faster than one Company can clear them.
Company Contract: The Quarry Warrens.questDesignBrief: A Company Contract for a player who belongs to an Adventurer Company. The Monster Warrens of The Howling Quarry in the Ashenmere Frontier have grown into a nest system. Ran Kōga's Flagon Irregulars posted the contract on Ironhold's Bounty Board Plaza for any Company willing to share the work and the pay. The player's Company clears the warrens chamber by chamber, possibly alongside Irregulars rookies who need keeping alive. A brood-mother is the final fight. Pay is C-rank to B-rank depending on what is found, split by agreement.

Company Contract: Banner Challenge.name: Company Contract: Banner Challenge
Company Contract: Banner Challenge.mainObjective: Win the banner challenge against the Vaunted Blade Company.
Company Contract: Banner Challenge.questStatement: The Vaunted Blade Company has posted a banner challenge in Aureliath's Guild Quarter: any rising Company may face them in public bouts at the Knight's Tournament Grounds, banner against banner.
Company Contract: Banner Challenge.questDesignBrief: A Company Contract for a player who belongs to an Adventurer Company. Raiga Kōtetsu's Vaunted Blade Company challenges rising Companies to a banner challenge at the Knight's Tournament Grounds: three public bouts, Company against Company, before a paying crowd. The player's Company picks its fighters, and members must agree to fight. Winning puts the player's crest on the Champion's Pavilion board and earns real renown; losing well earns respect. If the player flies the Vaunted Blade banner, the challenger is a rival Gold Company instead. Tournament rules apply: yielding ends a bout, killing ends a career.

The Porcelain Token: A Face for Later.name: The Porcelain Token: A Face for Later
The Porcelain Token: A Face for Later.mainObjective: Shatter the Porcelain Envoy's mask in The Porcelain Gallery.
The Porcelain Token: A Face for Later.questStatement: A polite stranger in a porcelain mask knew a secret you never told anyone, and left a warm porcelain token behind. The token is how they find you again. Turn it around.
The Porcelain Token: A Face for Later.questDesignBrief: Opposing the Porcelain Envoy. The token they left is warm and faintly pulls west; it can be followed to The Porcelain Gallery in the Rosethorn Nocturne, where the Envoy keeps rooms in the Private Collection and the animated dolls leave them alone. Along the way the player can meet the Envoy's buyers, people paying porcelain for confessions in baths and taprooms. Fire burns the stolen faces off a Faceless One. Beating the Envoy shatters the mask over an empty coat; the Envoy is not destroyed, only set back, and a new mask will turn up later. Elite fight at level 48 in a 44-60 dungeon.

The Porcelain Token: A Secret for a Secr.name: The Porcelain Token: A Secret for a Secret
The Porcelain Token: A Secret for a Secr.mainObjective: Bring the Porcelain Envoy three true secrets that were not yours to give.
The Porcelain Token: A Secret for a Secr.questStatement: The Envoy offered a trade: secrets for secrets, kept exactly. They know something about you. You could learn what they know about everyone else.
The Porcelain Token: A Secret for a Secr.questDesignBrief: Working with the Porcelain Envoy. The player gathers three real secrets from other people (through trust, theft, or eavesdropping) and delivers them to the Envoy in The Porcelain Gallery's Private Collection. The Envoy pays in kind, one true secret about someone powerful per secret delivered, and keeps the bargain to the letter. Every secret the player sells is fed to what sleeps beneath the Gilded Confession Maze, though the player only learns that later. The people whose secrets were sold can find out.

Continue?: The Save Point.name: Continue?: The Save Point
Continue?: The Save Point.mainObjective: Stop Hotori Arashiro's run through the Royal Proving Labyrinth and make her remember one person she has lost.
Continue?: The Save Point.questStatement: Another Reborn took your bounty a minute before you, called everyone NPCs, and laughed about her eleven deaths. She is running the Royal Proving Labyrinth for a 'secret ending.' Something about her save file is wrong.
Continue?: The Save Point.questDesignBrief: Opposing Hotori Arashiro. She is speedrunning the Royal Proving Labyrinth's heir trials, believing its last chamber is a way home, and leaving people behind in the trials as she goes. Killing her only sends her to her last shrine, angrier and missing another memory. The real win is to reach her in the Trial Nexus and make her remember one person she has forgotten (her brother's face, her best friend's name, her mother's song), which makes her hesitate. Clues that her Continue eats memories can come from her own jokes. A second remembered person may end her run for good: she can be redeemed.

Continue?: Any Percent.name: Continue?: Any Percent
Continue?: Any Percent.mainObjective: Clear the Royal Proving Labyrinth with Hotori Arashiro on her terms: fast, and leaving its people behind.
Continue?: Any Percent.questStatement: Hotori offered to team up: two Reborn, one route, the best clear time the Guild has ever recorded. All you have to do is stop caring about the people in the way.
Continue?: Any Percent.questDesignBrief: Working with Hotori Arashiro. A fast, fun, morally ugly run through the Royal Proving Labyrinth: skip the trials meant to test character, abandon a stranded trial candidate, take the reward. Hotori is great company and a real ally in a fight. The run ends at the Labyrinth's last chamber with no way home in it, and her reaction is the quest's emotional payoff: she laughs, too loud.

The File With Your Name: The Sealed Regi.name: The File With Your Name: The Sealed Registry
The File With Your Name: The Sealed Regi.mainObjective: Recover the false-charge network's sealed registry from the Cistern Hall of The Forgotten Aqueducts.
The File With Your Name: The Sealed Regi.questStatement: Chief Magistrate Shirasu has opened a file in your name. Everyone in Aureliath is guilty of something, he says; he only decides when. Somewhere there is a record of every case he decided in advance.
The File With Your Name: The Sealed Regi.questDesignBrief: Opposing Chief Magistrate Masanori Shirasu, part 1. His network's sealed registry, every fabricated case cross-indexed, lies under a writ ward in the Cistern Hall of The Forgotten Aqueducts beneath Aureliath. Baron Thorne knows where and fears it; Shinji Souen's money trail points the same way. The Aqueducts are a 32-48 dungeon with criminal tenants the network pays. Meanwhile the file in the player's name moves: a small warrant, a frozen account, a friend questioned. Opening the registry without Shirasu's seal burns it, so the player needs the seal, a forged one, or a way around the ward.

The File With Your Name: The Queen's Ver.name: The File With Your Name: The Queen's Verdict
The File With Your Name: The Queen's Ver.mainObjective: Lay the registry before Queen Celestine and bring Chief Magistrate Shirasu down in open court.
The File With Your Name: The Queen's Ver.questStatement: You have the registry. Queen Celestine has waited three years for an outsider to bring her exactly this. Shirasu has had forty years to prepare for the day someone does.
The File With Your Name: The Queen's Ver.questDesignBrief: Opposing Chief Magistrate Masanori Shirasu, part 2. The player brings the registry (and ideally Thorne's insurance archive and Shinji's money trail) to Queen Celestine in Aureliath. The Queen cannot move openly against her own judiciary without the constitutional crisis House Souen wants, so the case must be made in open court, where Shirasu is at his best: procedure, counter-charges, witnesses who suddenly forget. Attacking him with steel makes him the victim. Winning with evidence strips his office and exposes House Souen's coup and the Faceless funding behind it.

The File With Your Name: Independent Ass.name: The File With Your Name: Independent Assessor
The File With Your Name: Independent Ass.mainObjective: Take Chief Magistrate Shirasu's post as independent assessor and condemn the person he names.
The File With Your Name: Independent Ass.questStatement: Shirasu does not threaten people he can use. He offered you a post: independent assessor, a voice the court will trust. All it costs is a verdict you already know is false.
The File With Your Name: Independent Ass.questDesignBrief: Working with Chief Magistrate Masanori Shirasu. He names a target (a merchant, a witness, an honest clerk) and the player's testimony condemns them in Aureliath. Shirasu pays well and protects his people: warrants against the player vanish. The target is real, has a family, and is innocent. It makes the player part of the network Queen Celestine is trying to expose.

Decisive Resolution: The Sealed Files.name: Decisive Resolution: The Sealed Files
Decisive Resolution: The Sealed Files.mainObjective: Recover the two sealed null-reading case files from the Reliquary of First Light.
Decisive Resolution: The Sealed Files.questStatement: The Archbishop blessed you in front of a crowd and told you, quietly, that there were two before you, and the Church was merciful with the first. Someone kept the files.
Decisive Resolution: The Sealed Files.questDesignBrief: Opposing Archbishop Shizue Mihashira, part 1. Genma the Stern has been requesting archived files in violation of four canons; Kotone Myōjō has been reconstructing which parishioners vanished into the Conclave's Reborn program. Neither knows the other is working on the same rot. The two sealed null-reading files (the first executed under 'decisive resolution,' the second 'recalibrated') are in the Reliquary of First Light's Sealed Vault. Introducing Genma and Kotone, or getting either to trust the player, is the way in. The files name Mihashira.

Decisive Resolution: The Conclave Hears.name: Decisive Resolution: The Conclave Hears It
Decisive Resolution: The Conclave Hears.mainObjective: Expose Archbishop Shizue Mihashira before the Luminous Conclave in Solhaven.
Decisive Resolution: The Conclave Hears.questStatement: You have the files. Genma has his doubts and Kotone has her names. The Archbishop has the Conclave's love and fifty years of sincerity.
Decisive Resolution: The Conclave Hears.questDesignBrief: Opposing Archbishop Shizue Mihashira, part 2. The case is made in Solhaven's Cathedral Square before the Luminous Conclave: the two files, Kotone's reconstructed names, Genma's testimony against his own hierarchy, and ideally a prophecy fragment from the Saint's Buried Reliquary showing the Reborn are the cure, not the threat. Mihashira never denies anything; she explains, warmly, why it was necessary. Winning removes her from the Conclave and ends the program's quiet arm; she may then offer the player what she knows about the Hollow King, out of spite or out of faith.

Decisive Resolution: The Merciful Office.name: Decisive Resolution: The Merciful Office
Decisive Resolution: The Merciful Office.mainObjective: Hand a hidden Reborn over to Archbishop Mihashira's program in the Gilded Confession Maze.
Decisive Resolution: The Merciful Office.questStatement: The Archbishop offered you protection, purpose, and the Church's full weight against the Faceless. The price is help with her pastoral care: there is another Reborn hiding nearby who has not been read.
Decisive Resolution: The Merciful Office.questDesignBrief: Working with Archbishop Shizue Mihashira. She gives the player a name: a frightened Reborn hiding under a false identity. The player finds them and delivers them to the Glass Confessor's Chamber. Mihashira keeps her word: the Church's protection is real, and she shares what she knows about the Faceless. The delivered Reborn's fate is left for the player to discover.

The Last Seal: What the Archduke Holds.name: The Last Seal: What the Archduke Holds
The Last Seal: What the Archduke Holds.mainObjective: Learn from Yami Kurofuchi what Archduke Sōgetsu Yomisaka holds and why he is stronger than the Demon Lord.
The Last Seal: What the Archduke Holds.questStatement: Archduke Yomisaka toasted you by your true nature and told you the Dominion will have a new Lord. You may kneel beside her, or beneath her. Someone in Obsidian Spire has been sending black lilies to people who ask the wrong questions about him.
The Last Seal: What the Archduke Holds.questDesignBrief: Opposing Archduke Sōgetsu Yomisaka, part 1. Yami Kurofuchi, the Demon Lord's general, has been investigating the succession faction off the books, using duel invitations as cover. Earning his trust (a duel, a favor, a shared suspicion) gets the truth: Yomisaka holds the Last Seal of Succession, the final piece of Kuroyuki's old ritual, and has been drawing on its stored power for decades. That is why he stands above the Demon Lord and why she cannot act openly. Make the gap felt: anyone who tests Yomisaka now loses.

The Last Seal: A Sanction in Shadow.name: The Last Seal: A Sanction in Shadow
The Last Seal: A Sanction in Shadow.mainObjective: Win Demon Lord Kuroyuki Ōma's private sanction, or Sumire Tasogaretoge's own consent, to break the Last Seal.
The Last Seal: A Sanction in Shadow.questStatement: The Last Seal can be broken, but not by a stranger acting alone. The Demon Lord cannot be seen to move against her own court. Her daughter is the vessel nobody asked.
The Last Seal: A Sanction in Shadow.questDesignBrief: Opposing Archduke Sōgetsu Yomisaka, part 2. Either path works. Kuroyuki can sanction it privately, at the Palace of Eternal Twilight, only if the player proves they will keep the ritual secret; she has been waiting fifty years for a Reborn to do what she cannot. Or Sumire Tasogaretoge, the intended vessel, can choose to break it herself, which costs her the power she wanted to protect her people with. Yomisaka watches the whole court and will try to recruit the player first, generously.

The Last Seal: Break the Last Seal.name: The Last Seal: Break the Last Seal
The Last Seal: Break the Last Seal.mainObjective: Break the Last Seal of Succession in the Matriarch's Hall of the Obsidian Heart Catacomb.
The Last Seal: Break the Last Seal.questStatement: The Last Seal rests in the Matriarch's Hall, under the Archduke's private wards, beneath a city that would call breaking it treason. With it intact he cannot truly be beaten.
The Last Seal: Break the Last Seal.questDesignBrief: Opposing Archduke Sōgetsu Yomisaka, part 3. A deep descent through a 72-92 mythic dungeon to the Matriarch's Hall, where the Last Seal sits under Yomisaka's wards and demon ancestor echoes. Breaking it strips his borrowed reserve: he can no longer rise whole from near death. He will know the moment it breaks.

The Last Seal: The Archduke's Duel.name: The Last Seal: The Archduke's Duel
The Last Seal: The Archduke's Duel.mainObjective: Defeat Archduke Sōgetsu Yomisaka in a sanctioned duel under Twilight law in the Demon Court.
The Last Seal: The Archduke's Duel.questStatement: The Seal is broken and he is mortal. He is also still the finest duelist in the Dominion, three centuries deep in its court, and he has accepted your challenge with delight.
The Last Seal: The Archduke's Duel.questDesignBrief: Opposing Archduke Sōgetsu Yomisaka, finale. A formal duel in the Demon Court of Obsidian Spire, witnessed by Kuroyuki and Yami. Without the Seal he is still mythic level 97, immune to fire, dark, poison and mind magic, resistant to nearly everything else; only frost truly hurts him. This should be the hardest fight in the Dominion. If he loses, the succession faction collapses, the treaty with the Hollow King is exposed, and Sumire is free.

The Last Seal: Kneel Beside Her.name: The Last Seal: Kneel Beside Her
The Last Seal: Kneel Beside Her.mainObjective: Steal Demon Lord Kuroyuki Ōma's ritual notes from the Duchess's Archive for Archduke Yomisaka.
The Last Seal: Kneel Beside Her.questStatement: The Archduke offered you a seat at the right hand of the next Demon Lord. All he needs is a copy of notes the current one has spent fifty years trying to destroy.
The Last Seal: Kneel Beside Her.questDesignBrief: Working with Archduke Sōgetsu Yomisaka. A heist in Obsidian Spire: Duchess Kyouka's archive holds Kuroyuki's original ritual notes, which Yomisaka needs to fire the rite into Sumire. Kyouka is no fool and the archive is warded by five centuries of paranoia. Success earns the Archduke's lavish patronage and makes the player complicit in crowning a puppet.

The Name Under the Glass: The Second Nul.name: The Name Under the Glass: The Second Null Reading
The Name Under the Glass: The Second Nul.mainObjective: Learn from Court Mage Serika Amamiya's sealed research who the second null-reading summon was.
The Name Under the Glass: The Second Nul.questStatement: Every face in the room went blank and one voice said: you are the cure, and he is what you were sent to cure. Then everyone forgot. You did not. Court Mage Serika has records of two summons that read like you did.
The Name Under the Glass: The Second Nul.questDesignBrief: Opposing the Hollow King, part 1. Serika's private research into null readings found two prior cases, both sealed by the Church, both 'recalibrated.' She will share it only for something she wants (proof about the fifth summon, protection, or a promise). The second file, forty years old, is signed by then-Bishop Shizue Mihashira, and its subject vanished into the Gilded Confession Maze. Its pages show a name inked out. The player learns that the Hollow King was a summoned Reborn, unmade by the Church, and that his name was taken, not lost.

The Name Under the Glass: The Stolen Cip.name: The Name Under the Glass: The Stolen Cipher
The Name Under the Glass: The Stolen Cip.mainObjective: Find the Veilwalker who stole the Gilded Confession Maze's cipher and win it from them.
The Name Under the Glass: The Stolen Cip.questStatement: The Maze's stained glass records every confession it ever took, his name included. Only two living people can read it: the High Priestess, and a Veilwalker who stole the cipher and has been hiding ever since.
The Name Under the Glass: The Stolen Cip.questDesignBrief: Opposing the Hollow King, part 2. The thief hides in plain sight on Shadowglass Embassy Row, in the Intelligence Salon or the Hidden Office, wearing a borrowed identity because the Faceless are hunting them too. Finding them is a spy game; winning the cipher is a negotiation, a rescue, or a theft. The Faceless arrive before the player leaves. (The High Priestess also knows the cipher; asking her means asking the Church.)

The Name Under the Glass: Read the Glass.name: The Name Under the Glass: Read the Glass
The Name Under the Glass: Read the Glass.mainObjective: Read the Hollow King's true name from the stained glass of the Glass Confessor's Chamber.
The Name Under the Glass: Read the Glass.questStatement: The name is written in colored light in the Gilded Confession Maze, in the chamber where it was taken. The Archbishop keeps that chamber, and the Maze makes monsters out of lies.
The Name Under the Glass: Read the Glass.questDesignBrief: Opposing the Hollow King, part 3. A 46-62 dungeon where spoken lies become shades; honesty is the key. The Glass Confessor's Chamber is Archbishop Mihashira's seat (she may be gone if the player already exposed her). With the cipher, one panel reads: Kōtarō Kasuga, summoned forty years ago, recalibrated here. Whoever reads it gains the trait Keeper of the Hollow Name. The Hollow King feels it happen.

The Name Under the Glass: Speak His Name.name: The Name Under the Glass: Speak His Name
The Name Under the Glass: Speak His Name.mainObjective: Face the Hollow King in the Entity Chamber of The Umbral Resonance Sanctum and speak his true name.
The Name Under the Glass: Speak His Name.questStatement: Every vessel he wears can be broken, and he simply wakes in another. Only his name ends him, spoken to him by someone who read it. He holds court in the Entity Chamber, and he is waiting for you.
The Name Under the Glass: Speak His Name.questDesignBrief: Opposing the Hollow King, finale. A mythic 75-95 dungeon of dimensional overlap to the Entity Chamber. He is level 100, immune to dark, fire, poison and mind magic, resistant to everything else, vulnerable only to light, and he unmakes memories mid-fight. Speaking his name (Kōtarō Kasuga) to him makes the current vessel his last: if it falls, he dies. He will ask the player what their mother called them. This should be the hardest fight in Luxcellia.

The Name Under the Glass: Give Him Your.name: The Name Under the Glass: Give Him Your Name
The Name Under the Glass: Give Him Your.mainObjective: Speak your name into the stained glass of the Gilded Confession Maze and let the Hollow King keep it.
The Name Under the Glass: Give Him Your.questStatement: He offered you what he offers every Reborn: an end to being hunted, a place in his court, and a face that is anyone's. All you have to give him is your name.
