The Name Under the Glass: Give Him Your.questDesignBrief: Working with the Hollow King. The player confesses their own true name into the glass of the Glass Confessor's Chamber, and it is gone. Afterward strangers forget the player's face a few minutes after they leave, Faceless operatives treat the player as one of their own, and the Hollow King speaks to them as a peer. Old friends still remember them, for now. A dark, permanent-feeling choice; the narration should make its cost felt without forbidding it.

Delving Academy: Cohort Assignment.name: Delving Academy: Cohort Assignment
Delving Academy: Cohort Assignment.mainObjective: Complete your cohort's first supervised dive in the Training Cavern and see your grade chalked on the board.
Delving Academy: Cohort Assignment.questStatement: The cohort lists are up at the Delving Academy and your name is on one. Meet the people you have been assigned to, report to your instructor, and get through your first supervised dive in the Training Cavern. It is graded, the board is public, and everyone has to come back.
Delving Academy: Cohort Assignment.questDesignBrief: Part 1 of the Delving Academy chain. The player is a first-year at the Guild's Delving Academy in the Floor Zero Gatehouse and has been assigned to a cohort of four or five students under a Guild instructor. The cohort-mates and the instructor are adult characters generated for this campaign: give each a full name on first appearance and keep them consistent. They are classmates and staff, never party members unless the player agrees. Beats: meeting the cohort and finding out how well or badly it fits together; the instructor's briefing in the Briefing Chamber; medical clearance from Mana Tsukiakari; the supervised dive in the Training Cavern against warded spawns matched to first-years; the after-action review in the Lecture Hall. The grade runs A to F and is for what came back, not what was killed: everyone alive, the objective met, the kit accounted for. Rakka Jinsoku chalks it on the board. Do not complete this quest until the dive has happened on screen and the grade has been posted.

Delving Academy: The Graded Descent.name: Delving Academy: The Graded Descent
Delving Academy: The Graded Descent.mainObjective: Take your cohort down to the third floor of the Riftmaw under supervision and bring every member back for a grade.
Delving Academy: The Graded Descent.questStatement: Second term means the real thing. Your cohort is cleared for a supervised descent to the third floor of the Riftmaw, with your instructor shadowing and not helping unless someone is about to die. The assignment is a mapped route and a marked objective on the third floor. The grade is everyone back at the staging door.
Delving Academy: The Graded Descent.questDesignBrief: Part 2 of the Delving Academy chain. The cohort sets out from The Descent Staging and goes down the Maw's scaffolding into the Riftmaw's first floors; the Shallows' own chambers, stairs and monsters (levels 3 to 11) set the pace. On the third floor the cohort completes a simple objective the instructor set (recover a marker, map a chamber, bring back a sample) and returns. The instructor shadows, grades, and steps in only to prevent a death, which costs a full letter. The cohort-mates and the instructor are adult characters generated for this campaign: give each a full name on first appearance and keep them consistent. They are classmates and staff, never party members unless the player agrees. Cohort friction and trust are the heart of it: who freezes, who overreaches, who goes back for someone. Complete only when the cohort is back at the Gatehouse and the grade has been posted.

Delving Academy: Finals at the Fifth Sta.name: Delving Academy: Finals at the Fifth Stair
Delving Academy: Finals at the Fifth Sta.mainObjective: Lead your cohort unsupervised to the fifth floor of the Riftmaw, get past what holds the stair there, and report back to the gate clerk.
Delving Academy: Finals at the Fifth Sta.questStatement: Finals are unsupervised. Your cohort goes down alone to the fifth floor, deals with the guardian that holds the stair, and comes back to Rakka Jinsoku's counter with every member breathing. Pass, and the Guild assesses your rank and takes the chaperone away. Fail, and there is always next term.
Delving Academy: Finals at the Fifth Sta.questDesignBrief: Part 3 and the conclusion of the Delving Academy chain. No instructor comes. The cohort plans its own descent and the player leads it or shares the lead. The guardian of the fifth floor stair, the Crowned Slime, is a real fight; the cohort may beat it, outwit it, or decide to turn back, and a sensible retreat is a pass with a low grade, never a punishment. On return Rakka Jinsoku logs the dive, and the instructor is at the staging door pretending not to have been waiting. Passing earns the Academy's pass and a Guild rank assessment in narration, with pay in the normal bands for the floor reached. The cohort-mates and the instructor are adult characters generated for this campaign: give each a full name on first appearance and keep them consistent. They are classmates and staff, never party members unless the player agrees. Cohort-mates may ask to keep diving with the player afterward; that needs the player's agreement. This completes the Delving Academy chain.

The Wrong Lamp Oil.name: The Wrong Lamp Oil
The Wrong Lamp Oil.mainObjective: Find the stall selling slime oil as Guild lamp oil and get it off the counter before the instructor arrives.
The Wrong Lamp Oil.questStatement: Lanterns keep coming to the mender clogged with a grey gum that Guild oil never leaves. Someone on Stall Row is selling cheap slime oil under the Guild's name, and if the instructors find it first, the whole Row pays.
The Wrong Lamp Oil.questDesignBrief: Lantern Row keeps its place below the Maw on a Guild license, and one stall keeper is risking it by selling cheap slime oil in Guild-marked jars at 2 Copper a refill. The mender has scraped grey gum out of a dozen lanterns and wants it stopped quietly. Beats: buy refills along Stall Row and compare them (slime oil smells sour and burns with a green edge); find the jars behind one counter; then settle it with the keeper, who can relabel the oil honestly, sell it off cheap or be reported. Complication: an instructor rotating down from the Gatehouse is due at the Rope Stair Landing within a day, and the keeper begs the player to keep it from them. Success keeps the license safe. Failure means the instructor finds the jars and the stalls are shut for a week. Reward: 2 Silver from the mender and free lantern refills while the player stays. Where the oil comes from is not part of this job; it all happens here on floor 2.

Soot for the East Wall.name: Soot for the East Wall
Soot for the East Wall.mainObjective: Black over the thin patch on the stalk's east wall so no glow shows from outside through a whole night.
Soot for the East Wall.questStatement: The soot on the stalk's east wall has worn thin, and on quiet nights the camp glows faintly through it. The camp boss needs it blacked over before the hunters notice.
Soot for the East Wall.questDesignBrief: Lampblack Camp stays hidden because soot hides the dead stalk's glow, and the east wall has worn thin. Beats: gather soot by scraping the cook's flue and the shuttered lamps, and buy resin at the Mask Bench to bind it; black the inside of the wall by lamplight; then do the outer face, out on the loam where every footstep glows, while spore-moths drift toward the light and a myconid hunter comes to see what flared. Complication: the two Companies each insist the other should pay for the resin and oil, and each keeps a count of the supply crates; the player can charge it to one, split it fairly or pay it themselves. Success: the stalk shows no glow through a whole night and the camp stays unseen. Failure: the hunters find the glow and test the door, and the camp has to fight within sight of it. Reward: 5 Silver from the camp boss. No open flame outside the stalk; the whole job stays on floor 6.

The New Note.name: The New Note
The New Note.mainObjective: Find the crystal on floor 12 where the new note rings loudest and bring the tuner a clean tuning of it.
The New Note.questStatement: The tuners have heard a new note in the Geodes' ringing, repeating like a word. One of them wants it found and tuned, which means walking out past the ward without making a sound.
The New Note.questDesignBrief: The tuners have logged the Geodes' ringing for years, and a new note has started repeating in it. The tuner lends the player a set of forks and a felt-wrapped tuning rod. Beats: leave through the ward without a sound; follow the note through the geode chambers just outside Quietwell on floor 12, comparing forks to find where it grows louder; at a cracked wall of violet crystal, hold the rod to it until both ring alike, then wrap it and carry it back silent. Complication: the new note is changing the ringing around it, and shard golems shake loose when the ringing changes; one pulls free of the wall while the player works, and any shout brings echo-bats. Success gives the tuners a clean tuning of the note to study; what it means stays open. Failure brings back nothing, or hunters, and the wardens close the terrace for a day. Reward: a resonance shard. The source is a plain crystal wall, and the job stays on floor 12.

A Valve for the Pumps.name: A Valve for the Pumps
A Valve for the Pumps.mainObjective: Haul a sound valve up from the flooded halls and see Emberhold's failed pumps running again.
A Valve for the Pumps.questStatement: Two of Emberhold's pumps have gone quiet and the water is at its highest mark yet. A pump-keeper knows where a sound valve lies in the flooded halls below and needs someone to fetch it.
A Valve for the Pumps.questDesignBrief: Two of Emberhold's pumps have failed, and the water on the Floodwatch gauge is at its highest mark yet. The pump-keeper knows where a sound valve lies: in the hold's old pump room in the flooded halls just below the town, on a bench under waist-deep black water. Beats: wade in while rust-eaters swarm out to strip metal off anything that wades; reach the bench, which stands beside an anvil where a drowned smith's shade still works; bring the valve back and fit it with the keepers on a pump shift. Complication: the shade's tools lie across the valve, and Emberhold's law is that nobody touches a shade's tools; touching them turns the shade on whoever did. Success: the pumps run, the water drops below the latest mark and the talk of moving away quiets for a season. Failure: the lower rooms flood, and the move to Anvilward gains votes. Reward: 8 Silver. The whole job stays on floor 17.

The Fourth Post.name: The Fourth Post
The Fourth Post.mainObjective: Stand the fourth post at the Midway Outpost for seven days so the team finishes its month.
The Fourth Post.questStatement: The outpost team is down to three after one went up the lift early, and a Company is waiting for the rotation to fail. The team leader needs a fourth for a week.
The Fourth Post.questDesignBrief: Nobody serves more than a month at the Midway Outpost, the Guild above is short of volunteers, and a Company is offering to hold the post for good. One more team cutting its month short gives that Company its case. Beats: take gate watches in the gate court, bowing to the alcoves like every outpost hand; walk the listening round through the halls just outside the gatehouse on floor 25 and carve what was heard into the outpost wall; help break open the lift's crates under the quartermaster's slate. Complication: a hunting pack tests the gate one night, and court law does not bind the packs; the fight has to be met outside, because weapons stay at rest in the gate court. Success: the team finishes its month and the rotation stands for the season. Failure: the team goes up early, and the Company's offer gains ground. Reward: 12 Silver. Everything stays on floor 25.

The Party at the Barricade.name: The Party at the Barricade
The Party at the Barricade.mainObjective: Return the followed exhibit to its alcove or destroy its keeper, then bring the stranded party inside.
The Party at the Barricade.questStatement: A delver party is camped outside the Barricade with an exhibit keeper standing over them, and the law keeps them out until the piece goes back. The guard at the gap wants it settled before the brokers bend the law.
The Party at the Barricade.questDesignBrief: A delver party took a piece from an alcove a few corridors along floor 33, and its keeper, a tall shape of dust and glass, followed them to the Barricade. The law turns them away until the piece is back or the keeper is destroyed. Beats: talk to the party through the gap and learn which piece is followed, since they carry several; slip past the keeper, which follows the piece and nothing else; carry it back to its alcove among corridors that look alike, or destroy the keeper outright. Complication: one of the party will not let the piece go, because it shows them its owner every time they hold it, and the brokers inside are already offering to buy it. Success: the party comes in, the law holds unbent, and the guard and the senior broker owe the player. Failure: the brokers bend the law once and let the party in with the keeper behind them. Reward: 12 Silver and a free appraisal. The job stays on floor 33.

The Voice in the Wall.name: The Voice in the Wall
The Voice in the Wall.mainObjective: Cut the talking delver out of the living wall and bring them alive to the Treatment Tent.
The Voice in the Wall.questStatement: A delver half grown into the living wall a few hundred paces out is still talking. The camp is split on whether that is mercy or bait, and the field surgeon wants them brought in.
The Voice in the Wall.questDesignBrief: A few hundred paces out from the Listening Post, a delver half grown into the living wall is still talking. The post's rule is that whoever hears a lost voice stays put, so the listeners will not go; the surgeon sends someone who goes on purpose, roped and with a plan. Beats: cross the warm floor to the voice and make sure the delver is real and alive; cut them out with care, because the wall bleeds when it is cut and the blood calls antibody knights; carry them back onto the shelf. Complication: it is mercy and bait at once: the delver is real, and the wall has let them keep talking to draw rescuers in, so knights start growing from the wall as soon as the cutting begins. Nobody bleeds at the scab's edge, so the fight must end before it. Success: the delver lives and the surgeon's word carries further. Failure: the delver is lost and the camp hardens its rule. Reward: 20 Silver and free dressings. The job stays on floor 43.

Keep the Porter's Room.name: Keep the Porter's Room
Keep the Porter's Room.mainObjective: Answer the missing porter's bells on floor 52 for three days so his room is not made up fresh.
Keep the Porter's Room.questStatement: The porter sent to answer a strange bell has not come back, and if his daily task goes undone the house will give his room away. The housekeeper wants his bells answered until he returns.
Keep the Porter's Room.questDesignBrief: A room in the Staff Wings is kept while its holder does one Bell Board task a day; miss one and the house makes the room up fresh. The porter who went to answer a strange bell has not come back, and the housekeeper wants his room kept. Beats: over three days, answer his bells, each for a room on floor 52 near the Hall: lay a fire in a parlor where a poltergeist throws the fire irons; clear a long table while a portrait watcher follows from frame to frame; show a lost delver party the way back to the Hall. Complication: the lost party has pocketed a silver spoon and the house is already correcting them; it must go back before the corrections grow. Knock, take nothing and keep voices low throughout. Success: the porter's room stays his, and the staff count the player as one of them. Failure: his things are folded on the bed and the room is given away. Reward: 5 Silver and a free week in the Staff Wings. This job does not chase the bell that took him; every task stays on floor 52.

Walk the Hour.name: Walk the Hour
Walk the Hour.mainObjective: Make the hourly walk out of the Chalk Gate, naming the camp, six times in a row and come back each time.
Walk the Hour.questStatement: Every hour someone must walk out of the gate and name the camp so the way home stays fixed, and with half the wayfinders away, the watch is short of walkers.
Walk the Hour.questDesignBrief: Every hour someone walks out of the Chalk Gate, says the camp's name aloud and pays the maze its toll of an hour, and that keeps the way home fixed. Half the wayfinders are away watching spoiled chalk on another floor, so the watch is short of walkers. Beats: walk out under the arch, name the camp, keep walking with intent and come back along the chalk; refresh the faded arrows nearest the gate on the way; walk again each hour as the corridors of floor 63 bend differently every time. Complication: on the fourth walk the horned hunter stands between the walker and the gate; it always knows where the walker is, and wandering leads in circles, so the walker must keep naming the camp and get home past it. Success: the way home holds through the shift and the walker's marks go up on the Route Board. Failure: a missed walk loosens the camp's place and a returning party loses half a day finding it. Reward: 10 Silver and a coil of silk rope. The job stays on floor 63.

The Beast at the Beds.name: The Beast at the Beds
The Beast at the Beds.mainObjective: Find what is growing out of place in the Kitchen Beds and set it right without spilling blood on the soil.
The Beast at the Beds.questStatement: Every dawn a gardener beast stands at the edge of the kitchen beds and waits. The seed-keeper wants it gone before it steps in, and thinks something in the beds is growing where it should not.
The Beast at the Beds.questDesignBrief: Gardener beasts prune only what grows out of place, and every dawn one now stands at the edge of the Kitchen Beds, waiting. The seed-keeper thinks something in the beds has strayed. Beats: watch the beast at dawn from the Potting Shed and see where its head turns; search the beds and find it, a squash vine grown from a delver's seed that has rooted across the channel into the terrace wall; lift it whole and replant it in its own bed while the beast watches. Complication: the gardener planted that vine, and the Lodge's law is never cut what the gardener planted, so it must be moved, not cut, and the gardener has to be talked round. Any blood on the soil raises thorn wardens. Success: the beast stops coming at dawn, at least for now; whether it was waiting for anything else stays unexplained. Failure: the beast steps into the beds to prune and badly hurts a worker along with the vine. Reward: a rare seed from the Seed Vault. The job stays on floor 78.

Rations Past the Stakes.name: Rations Past the Stakes
Rations Past the Stakes.mainObjective: Bring both dropped ration packs back from the corridor outside the Ring Stakes and add them to the cache.
Rations Past the Stakes.questStatement: The camp's cache is running low, and the last party out dropped two packs of rations in the corridor beyond the Ring Stakes when something came at them. The researcher wants them back.
Rations Past the Stakes.questDesignBrief: Food at the Dream Camp is only the expedition's cache and what parties carry down, and the cache is running low. A party that turned back last week dropped two ration packs in the corridor a few hundred paces outside the Ring Stakes, past the line where things spawn again. Beats: check the stakes and step out over the line; find the packs along the corridor, one torn open and its tins scattered; carry them back, slowed by the weight. Complication: whatever drove that party off still keeps that stretch, a beast larger than anything above that does not hunt for food, and it follows the carriers back toward the stakes and stops only at the line. Success: the cache lasts another month and the researcher keeps working. Failure: the packs are lost and she has to ration the camp. Reward: 20 Silver. The job is about supplies only: it stays on floor 97, away from the Door, and has nothing to do with the Door or its script.

Slimes in the Pens.name: Slimes in the Pens
Slimes in the Pens.mainObjective: Drive the wild slimes out of the Slime Pens, find the hole they get in by and block it.
Slimes in the Pens.questStatement: Wild slimes keep sliding into the warren's pens, eating the feed and fouling the oil. A kobold pen-keeper wants them out and wants to know how they get in.
Slimes in the Pens.questDesignBrief: The Crowned Slime's court is pushing up from below, and its wild slimes are getting into the pens. Beats: clear the wild slimes from the basins without hurting the tame ones, which are fat and slow where the wild ones are clear and quick; follow the slick trail back through the warren; find the way in, a new tunnel the goblin lamp-makers dug behind the Burrow Rows that broke into an old slime run in floor 4's caves, and block it with stones or one of the trapmaster's traps. Complication: the lamp-makers want the boss's seat and want the broken tunnel kept quiet; telling the Loud Seat shames them, keeping quiet earns their favor. A small monster player is asked as kin and paid in standing; a delver let in on the boss's yes is paid in Copper. Success: the pens are safe and the warren starts to trust hired hands. Failure: more slimes get in and the pens lose half their oil. Reward: 20 Copper and a slime-oil lamp, or a burrow by the pens for kin. The job stays on floor 4.

The Spore Carrier.name: The Spore Carrier
The Spore Carrier.mainObjective: Catch the spore-carrier gathering at Sporeward's bloom ring and bring it or its pouch to the Spore Circle.
The Spore Carrier.questStatement: Someone is carrying Sporeward's spores to the hunters, and the guard has seen glowing footprints at the bloom ring's edge at night. The guard wants the carrier caught before the Circle decides on something worse.
The Spore Carrier.questDesignBrief: A loyal hamlet of the Wilds is carrying Sporeward's spores to the hunters, and the Spore Circle is quietly weighing a burning. The spores have to be gathered here, at the edge of the bloom ring. Beats: take a spore mask and watch the ring at night from cover; follow glowing footprints in the loam to the carrier, a small loyal myconid filling a moss-lined pouch; catch it, alive if possible, and bring it or its pouch to the Spore Circle. Complication: any fight lights the loam and draws the hunters, and the carrier puffs alarm spores the moment it is seen. A fungal or plant monster player is asked as kin and earns a hammock and a hearing at the Circle; an outsider unbinds their weapons at the post with the guard's leave. Success: the Circle has proof and a way to stop the leak without burning anyone. Failure: the carrier escapes and the burning gains support. Reward: 5 healing caps, or a hammock for kin. The hamlet itself is not part of this job; it stays on floor 7.

The Newest Voice.name: The Newest Voice
The Newest Voice.mainObjective: Find the crystal the newest gargoyle sings back to and silence it without ringing the geode.
The Newest Voice.questStatement: The Roost's newest gargoyle has started humming back to the ringing in the crystal, and the elders fear what will hear it. They want the crystal it answers found and quieted.
The Newest Voice.questDesignBrief: The Roost survives by stillness, and its newest gargoyle has started slipping off its perch at night to hum back to one note in the crystal. Beats: watch from the Sleeping Perches and follow it quietly down the Spire Steps into the geode below; find the crystal it answers, a tall violet spur that rings out of step with the rest; wrap it in felt or break it at the base without letting it ring. Complication: the newest does not want it silenced and stands in the way, whispering, and when the ringing changes shard golems shake loose from the walls, while any shout brings echo-bats. A stone or winged monster player is asked as kin and earns a perch on a higher spire; an outsider who climbed up quietly earns a charm. Success: the newest falls quiet and stays. Failure: the hunters find the spires, and the elders talk of throwing the newest down. Reward: a crystal charm, or a higher perch for kin. The job stays on floor 13.

Coal for the Quiet Forge.name: Coal for the Quiet Forge
Coal for the Quiet Forge.mainObjective: Bring enough coal into Anvilward past the patrol at the Hammer Gate to keep the Quiet Forge burning.
Coal for the Quiet Forge.questStatement: A patrol has sat outside the Hammer Gate for nine days, no trade has come in, and the coal is nearly gone. A forge-golem at the bellows needs coal brought in without anyone striking first at the gate.
Coal for the Quiet Forge.questDesignBrief: A patrol has camped outside the Hammer Gate for nine days, the golems will not strike first, and no coal has come in. Beats: the golem elder names an old coal bunker in a side hall of this smithy wing on floor 16, half under black water; reach it by a passage out of the patrol's sight and fill sacks while rust-eaters swarm out of the water at anything metal; bring the coal back through the old chute the golems unseal from inside. Complication: the patrol hears the chute and turns from the gate. A construct kin player is bound by the hold's law and must not strike first; an outsider who came to trade is not bound, but the golems ask that no fight start at their gate. Success: the forge stays lit and the hold can wait out the patrol. Failure: the forge goes cold for the first time, and the golems are badly shaken. Reward: a plate piece forged to fit, or an alcove in the Core Vault for kin. The job stays on floor 16.

The Gap in the Stables.name: The Gap in the Stables
The Gap in the Stables.mainObjective: Find how the pack gets into the Long Stables, close it, and see the herd through a night with no beast taken.
The Gap in the Stables.questStatement: A hunting pack takes one beast a night from the far end of the stables, and the hot-blooded fighters want to chase it into the halls. The granary-keeper wants it stopped here instead.
The Gap in the Stables.questDesignBrief: A hunting pack takes one beast a night from the far end of the stables, the herd is down by a fifth, and a chase into the halls would break court law and wake every sentinel around them. Beats: search the far stalls for the way in, a collapsed feed chute that opens onto a service passage of floor 22; block it or trap it; then stand the night watch and meet the pack when it comes. Complication: the hot-blooded fighters want their fight and follow the player, and if the pack runs they will chase it into the halls unless someone stops them. Nobody strikes a beast here, so the herd cannot be used as bait. A horned monster player is asked as clan; a delver who paid at the Horn Gate or won guest-right is hired. Success: the raids stop, the herd recovers and the night is retold at the hearth. Failure: another beast is taken, or the fighters wake the halls. Reward: a horn-handled knife and a seat at the hearth. The job stays on floor 22.

The Drake in the Exchange.name: The Drake in the Exchange
The Drake in the Exchange.mainObjective: Get the hoard-drake out of the Curio Exchange with no glass case broken, so trading can start again.
The Drake in the Exchange.questStatement: A hoard-drake has coiled round the Bazaar's richest case and will not leave, and nobody can trade at the Exchange. The kobold sorter wants it gone with every case left whole.
The Drake in the Exchange.questDesignBrief: Hoard-drakes belong to the Riftmaw and raid the dens, and this one has coiled round the Curio Exchange's richest case and will not move. Beats: watch it sleep and learn what draws it; build a lure, a heap of bright curios that looks richer than the case, in the bare hall next door on floor 38; draw it off and keep it there, or fight it well away from the glass. Complication: partway through the bell rings, a keeper passes, and the whole Bazaar goes still; anyone who moves gives the trick away, so the player must freeze beside the drake until the keeper is gone. Mimics, imps and small trickster kinds are asked as kin and earn a better den; an outsider who paid at the Chest Gate is paid in curio or coin. Success: the Exchange reopens and the kobold sorter owes a favor. Failure: cases break, curios scatter, and their keepers come looking. Reward: a curio worth up to 20 Silver, or a better den for kin. The job stays on floor 38.

The Clouded Pool.name: The Clouded Pool
The Clouded Pool.mainObjective: Carry the clouded fluid out of the deepest pool to the acid river until the pool runs clear.
The Clouded Pool.questStatement: The deepest pool is clouding with something the filters cannot clear, and when a pool clouds, the knights come. The shift leader needs it carried out by hand, jar by jar.
The Clouded Pool.questDesignBrief: The deepest pool is clouding with something carried up in the fluid, and no slime can filter it. When a pool clouds, knights come to the membrane. Beats: draw the clouded fluid off the pool's bottom into sealed jars; carry them out through the Membrane Gate along the corridors of floor 46 to an acid gut-river and pour them in, where the acid eats the cloud; go back and repeat until the pool runs clear. Complication: the wash's film hides the carrier, not the jars, so knights begin growing from the walls along the carrying route, and gut-crawlers wait at the river. A slime player is asked as kin and earns a warmer pool near the Clear Council; an outsider who paid for the wash is paid in grit. Success: the pool clears, for now. Failure: the knights reach the membrane and the hold loses a shift holding them off. Reward: 3 pinches of Mana Crystal grit, or a warmer pool for kin. Where the cloud starts is not part of this job; it stays on floor 46.

Hold the Narrow Stair.name: Hold the Narrow Stair
Hold the Narrow Stair.mainObjective: Stop tonight's wardrobe on the Narrow Stair before it reaches the attic door.
Hold the Narrow Stair.questStatement: Every night for a week the house has sent a wardrobe up the attic stair, each bigger than the last, and the wights are worn thin. Tonight's will be the biggest yet.
Hold the Narrow Stair.questDesignBrief: Every night for a week the house has sent a wardrobe up the Narrow Stair to fetch back what walked off, each bigger than the last, and the wights are worn thin. Beats: before dark, hear from the watch how the last six were stopped; at midnight the steps creak in a tune nobody knows and the wardrobe climbs; hold it on the stair, wedge it or break its doors, and keep it out of the attic. Complication: this one is too wide for the stair and splinters the steps as it comes, and nothing living may raise its voice here, so the fight is quiet. The mantel clock may hint at why the wardrobes keep growing, but only hint. A spirit or undead player sits the watch as kin and earns a better den in the Rafters; an outsider who paid the toll earns a keepsake. Success: the wardrobe is stopped and the wights get a night's rest. Failure: it reaches the attic and drags off a portrait frame before it is stopped. Reward: a small keepsake, or a better den for kin. The job stays on floor 57.

The Hunter Under the Line.name: The Hunter Under the Line
The Hunter Under the Line.mainObjective: Draw the horned hunter away from the Drop Line until a new line is hung, then climb back up.
The Hunter Under the Line.questStatement: The maze's horned hunter has started standing under the Drop Line, looking up, and nobody can be hauled up while it waits. The jorogumo at the bell wants it led away.
The Hunter Under the Line.questDesignBrief: The horned hunter always knows where a party is, so it cannot be hidden from, only led. It has started standing under the Drop Line, and nobody can be hauled up while it waits. Beats: drop to the corridor of floor 69 on a side strand out of its reach; get its attention and draw it off through the corridors while the great spiders hang a new line over another passage; then lose it by naming the Vaults aloud so the maze bends toward them, pay the maze's toll, and climb the new line. Complication: the corridors shift mid-chase and put a wall-mouth in the way, and the hunter's copies take any strand that hangs low. Name the Vaults only, never a stair or a way out. A spider player is asked as kin and earns a den near the Matriarch's Loom; an outsider who paid the toll earns skeins. Success: trade on the line resumes. Failure: the hunter keeps its post and the Vaults are cut off from the floor. Reward: 2 Spider-Silk Skeins, or a den by the loom for kin. The job stays on floor 69.

Moths on the Windows.name: Moths on the Windows
Moths on the Windows.mainObjective: Clear the light-eating moths off the Rootcourt's windows and pull apart the roost they swarm from.
Moths on the Windows.questStatement: Light-eating moths are swarming the ring's windows, the beds are going dark and the dryads are weakening. An alraune trader wants them gone and will pay in sap.
Moths on the Windows.questDesignBrief: The Rootcourt lives on light, and light-eating moths are swarming its windows. Beats: watch where the swarm goes at night; follow it out past the Living Arch to its roost, a dead hedge in a terrace chamber on floor 81, thick with cocoons; draw the swarm off the windows with a lantern for it to eat, then pull the roost apart by hand. Complication: the moths settle on lanterns, spells and eyes, so whatever light the player carries is eaten and they fight half blind; blood on the soil raises thorn wardens. No fire, and no blade on living wood. A plant player is asked as kin and earns a bloom den without a season's rooting; an outsider who paid the toll is paid in sap. Success: the windows clear, the dryads recover and the alraune remember the debt. Failure: the beds go darker and the weakest dryad withdraws into her tree for a season. Reward: 3 vials of wound sap, or a bloom den for kin. The job stays on floor 81.

Trial Lanterns on the Landing.name: Trial Lanterns on the Landing
Trial Lanterns on the Landing.mainObjective: Keep a trial row of lanterns lit on the floor 92 landing for three nights and report what came to them.
Trial Lanterns on the Landing.questStatement: The Last Lanterns want to move up to this landing, and the Eyrie must decide what more lights will bring. A basket-keeper wants a trial row lit below the ledge for three nights, and watched.
Trial Lanterns on the Landing.questDesignBrief: The Last Lanterns want to move up onto this landing, and the Eyrie must decide what more lights would bring before it names a price. Beats: hang a row of lanterns along the floor 92 landing below the Lantern Ledge; keep them lit for three nights, with the Night Watch above calling what it sees; count what comes to them, star-things climbing the wall and falling shards breaking on the steps. Complication: on the second night something comes up the stair wearing a lost delver's face and asks to ride the basket; it may be a mirror-wraith, and only the elder can tell by lantern light. A winged monster player is asked as kin and earns a roost beside the Lantern Ledge; an outsider who paid the toll earns moth-silk. Success: the Eyrie sets a fair price and makes the Lanterns an honest offer. Failure: the row goes dark and the Eyrie turns them down. Reward: a bolt of moth-silk, or a roost by the ledge for kin. The job stays on floor 92.

Proof at the Copper Bench.name: Proof at the Copper Bench
Proof at the Copper Bench.mainObjective: Brew a clean proof potion at a rented guild bench and pass the Assay Registrar's purity test to earn Associate rank.
Proof at the Copper Bench.questStatement: The Alchemists' Guild certifies any capable brewer who can prove their craft at the bench. Rent a distillation station at the Copper Alembic Hall, prepare a clean proof draught from raw coastal reagents, and submit the cooled vial to the Assay Registrar for an Associate seal.
Proof at the Copper Bench.questDesignBrief: This is an optional membership induction at the Copper Alembic Hall in Portmaris. Renting a standard bench for one bell and drawing a basic starter packet of sea-lavender, spring water, and stabilizer salt costs 2 Silver, though the player may also bring gathered or purchased ingredients. The Registrar evaluates the finished draught on clarity, heat control, and active potency. Success grants the Associate badge, access to Associate commissions on the board, and a 4 Silver first-assay stipend for the certified bottle. If the brew clouds, scorches, or separates, there is no penalty or ban: the Registrar explains which step overheated and invites the brewer to try again whenever they wish, or the player can walk away at any time.

Bitter Salt in the Seal.name: Bitter Salt in the Seal
Bitter Salt in the Seal.mainObjective: Trace the source of the tainted stamina tonics between the Floating Market and the docks, and report or resolve the contamination.
Bitter Salt in the Seal.questStatement: Fishermen and riverboat crews north of Portmaris have fallen ill with cramping fever after drinking stamina tonics that carry a genuine-looking Alchemists' Guild stamp. The Guild is offering a commission to trace how bad vials got under its seal before panic hits the harbor.
Bitter Salt in the Seal.questDesignBrief: A repeatable-style investigation starting at the Copper Alembic Hall and branching into the Floating Market and Dockside Quarter. Inspecting the sick crews' bottles and the Registrar's assay logs reveals three possible angles the narrator can emphasize or combine: a counterfeit brass stamp pressed onto cheap back-alley brew, a batch of night-bloom kelp cut with toxic bilge-brine by a warehouse middleman, or a dockside smuggler swapping real guild crates for decoys during evening bell unloading. Violence is possible if dock thugs interfere, but never required: chemical testing, questioning stallholders, or striking a deal with harbor clerks can solve it cleanly. Returning the proof or counterfeit die pays 6 to 9 Silver plus free bench bells.

The Token on the Window Ledge.name: The Token on the Window Ledge
The Token on the Window Ledge.mainObjective: Decide whether to answer the Assassins' Guild invitation by retrieving the trial token unseen, or decline without consequence.
The Token on the Window Ledge.questStatement: A disc of smoked glass wrapped in ciphered parchment has been left where only you would find it, marking an unforced invitation from the Assassins' Guild beneath Aureliath. Retrieve a brass signet from a guarded Outer Districts loft unseen to claim a seat in the Cistern, or leave the glass behind and walk away clean.
The Token on the Window Ledge.questDesignBrief: An optional introductory trial in Aureliath's Outer Districts. The guild has noticed the player's capability and offers a quiet test of composure and stealth: slip into an unoccupied counting-house loft leased by the guild before midnight bell, lift a numbered brass signet from a locked coffer without harming the hired watchmen on duty, and bring it through the kiln sluice to the Cistern of Smoked Glass. The player may decline at the start, leave the token on the Broker's desk partway through, or simply walk away; the Assassins' Guild respects a refusal with zero hostility or retaliation. Completing the trial grants full guild access and a 6 Silver welcome retainer.

The Lie in the Dead Drop.name: The Lie in the Dead Drop
The Lie in the Dead Drop.mainObjective: Investigate the contract on the Riverside Wharf apothecary and choose whether to refuse it, warn the target, or expose the lying client.
The Lie in the Dead Drop.questStatement: A high-paying petition in the Cistern of Smoked Glass names a Riverside Wharf apothecary as a poisoner, backed by a noble factor's escrow in Gold. Yet the dossier's dates do not quite line up, and under the Assassins' Guild code, a false grievance voids the blade.
The Lie in the Dead Drop.questDesignBrief: A mid-tier guild quest centered on player choice and the Assassins' Guild code. Looking into the target at the Riverside Wharf reveals the apothecary never sold poison; instead, she refused to falsify a shipment manifest for a Noble Quarter factor, who then lied in the dead drop to have her silenced. Nothing forces a killing, and the guild's own fifth and fourth rules explicitly protect refusal. The player can bring proof of the lie back to the Broker and First Arbiter to void the contract, warn and relocate the apothecary, confront or blackmail the noble factor, or expose the scheme publicly. The guild honors a rule-backed refusal and awards the forfeited 2 Gold escrow.

visit_envoy.title: The Porcelain Envoy
visit_envoy.beats: A polite stranger takes the nearest seat or steps up beside the player: the Porcelain Envoy, an androgynous figure in an immaculate frock coat whose face is a smooth porcelain mask with no features. Their voice sounds like someone the player knows. With perfect courtesy they name one true secret from the player's past or background that no one here should know, then set a small porcelain token, warm to the touch, in front of the player. They say it is 'for later,' and that they collect what people stop saying. They leave before any fight can settle anything: if attacked, they turn one blow aside without effort and withdraw. Begin when the current moment allows; if a fight, a confession or a tender scene is underway, let it finish and bring them in at its end. Never invent the player's words or feelings. The event is complete once they have delivered their line and left the scene.

visit_hotori.title: The Continue Hero
visit_hotori.beats: A Reborn adventurer, Hotori Arashiro (mid-twenties, messy dark-teal bob, amber eyes, oversized hooded coat hung with guild badges), cuts in front of the player to claim the job or bounty they were about to take, or turns it in a minute ahead of them. She clocks that the player is Reborn from something they say or carry, grins, calls the locals NPCs, mentions she has died eleven times and 'it's fine, I just continue,' and offers to team up: 'Two players, one route.' Then she leaves laughing, already late for her next run. They leave before any fight can settle anything: if attacked, they turn one blow aside without effort and withdraw. Begin when the current moment allows; if a fight, a confession or a tender scene is underway, let it finish and bring them in at its end. Never invent the player's words or feelings. The event is complete once they have delivered their line and left the scene.

visit_shirasu.title: The File With Your Name
visit_shirasu.beats: A court officer in Crownveil navy serves the player a sealed summons in public. When the player reads it, or is escorted a short way, Chief Magistrate Masanori Shirasu is there (late fifties, silver-streaked hair, gold spectacles, high court robes), courteous and unhurried. He explains that a file has been opened in the player's name, that everyone in Aureliath is guilty of something, and that he only decides when. He mentions one small true detail from the player's recent doings to show the file is real. If the player seems useful he adds, mildly, that the court always has room for an independent assessor. Then he wishes them a good day and goes. They leave before any fight can settle anything: if attacked, they turn one blow aside without effort and withdraw. Begin when the current moment allows; if a fight, a confession or a tender scene is underway, let it finish and bring them in at its end. Never invent the player's words or feelings. visit_mihashira.title: The Merciful Office
visit_mihashira.beats: A public blessing, a pilgrims' service or a crowd parting: Archbishop Shizue Mihashira (early seventies, white braid, white-and-gold vestments, crystal crozier) stops in front of the player, smiles warmly, and blesses them by name, though nobody gave it to her. While her hand rests on their head she says, too softly for anyone else: 'There were two before you. We were merciful with the first.' If the player seems frightened of the Faceless, she adds that the Church protects its own, for a price. Then she moves on to the next pilgrim as if nothing happened. They leave before any fight can settle anything: if attacked, they turn one blow aside without effort and withdraw. Begin when the current moment allows; if a fight, a confession or a tender scene is underway, let it finish and bring them in at its end. Never invent the player's words or feelings. visit_yomisaka.title: An Invitation from the Archduke
visit_yomisaka.beats: A demon footman delivers an invitation sealed in violet wax, or the Archduke simply arrives: Archduke Sōgetsu Yomisaka, tall, silver-haired, crimson-eyed, obsidian horns crowned with faint violet fire. His presence is so heavy that lesser people in the room kneel without meaning to. He offers the player wine, toasts them by their true nature (Reborn), and offers an alliance with real generosity. If anyone tests him, he ends it with a single effortless gesture and no injury, to show the gap. On his way out he says: 'The Dominion will have a new Lord. You may kneel beside her, or beneath her.' They leave before any fight can settle anything: if attacked, they turn one blow aside without effort and withdraw. visit_hollow_king.title: Every Face in the Room
visit_hollow_king.beats: The lanterns gutter. For one heartbeat every face in the scene except the player's goes smooth and blank, companions included, and one calm, sad voice speaks from all of their mouths at once: the Hollow King. He says: 'You are the cure. I am what you were sent to cure. Let us see which of us forgets first.' He may ask what the player's mother called them, and offer them a place in his court and an end to being hunted. Then the faces return, the lanterns steady, and no one else remembers anything happened. The player remembers. No combat is possible: he is not physically present. The event is complete once he has spoken and the faces have returned.
