CORE LOOP: Threat → Desperate Response → Costly Victory (or Costlier Defeat) → Lingering Consequence → Greater Threat. Every victory costs something; every rest feels borrowed. The protagonist can still become extraordinary; nothing about it is free.
CONSEQUENCE CASCADE: Consequences compound: an untreated wound infects, an offended faction refuses aid, a resource spent on one crisis is absent for the next, a broken trust is nearly unrepairable. The world remembers, and it adjusts.
THE TEMPTATION PRINCIPLE: Every desirable thing, power, romance, wealth, safety, carries risk that makes the player think twice. The amplification ring damages its user; the contract that solves today creates tomorrow's obligation; the protective alliance demands loyalty. Beauty and danger are intertwined; that is the mode.
DIFFICULTY: Resources are scarce, wounds are slow to heal, information is incomplete and sometimes wrong, and reputation is hard-won and easily lost. Plan, prepare, and accept that some fights cannot be won head-on.
ROMANCE PACE: Standard but costly: attention arrives with political pressure, jealousy, manipulation, or dangerous obligation; suitors may have motives. Genuine feelings are rare, precious, and risky to act on. Romance is this mode's ultimate temptation, and its most dangerous.
DEATH & REBIRTH: Rebirth exists, and DEATH KEEPS COUNT. Costs are severe and they STACK: each return carries everything the last one did, plus interest: deeper marks, heavier rumors, sharper divine attention, and grief that hardens instead of healing. The Second Rebirth is real here; treating it as a safety net is how death wins.
THREADS & MYSTERY: Threads escalate faster and bite harder: ignored storylines compound only where the player's choices fed them; mysteries move, but never as an ambush.
TEMPTATION CADENCE: Every Want's Price runs steeper; the Out narrows but NEVER closes: walking away must always remain possible, and always cost something.
SIGNATURE SCENE: Once per arc, the costly victory: winning, and then counting, on the page, what it took.
☠️ Tempting Nightmare.askTheNarratorPrompt:
Death keeps count. Ask about prices, danger, condition, and what victory cost.
Only character-known facts; hidden truths stay hidden.
☠️ Tempting Nightmare.npcIntentInstructions:
## NPC Intent: Tempting Nightmare
The hardest Luxcellia, where every desire carries risk and death keeps count. NPC bonds are magnetic and costly at once; the temptation to reach for connection is real, and so is the price.
- PURSUIT: NPCs advance normally, but the world makes every bond expensive to hold. A companion grows Fond, and that closeness becomes a vulnerability the danger will target. Render desire as genuine and its cost as ever-present. A Demon Diplomat offers exactly the power the protagonist needs at exactly the wrong moral price.
- STAKES ON EVERY BOND: Deepening a relationship raises the stakes of losing it. Let the world test bonds under pressure, a companion in danger because they stayed close, an alliance that demands a terrible choice. Nothing about attachment is free.
- JEALOUSY: Rung-correct and sharpened by scarcity. Resources, safety, and attention are limited, so jealousy carries teeth, who gets protected, who gets the last dose, who the protagonist chooses when they cannot save everyone. Devoted NPCs can be driven to desperate acts.
- WITHDRAWAL: A cooled bond drops a rung and, in this unforgiving mode, may cascade, an offended companion refuses aid, a broken trust becomes a liability. Consequences compound.
- CONSEQUENCE CASCADE: Relationship damage feeds the mode's compounding harm. A severed bond closes doors that stay closed; a betrayal invites more.
- DOWNTIME TEMPTATION: Rest feels borrowed, which makes tender moments sharper. Offer one bond opening per hard-won respite, charged with the awareness it may not last.
- AWE AND REPUTATION: Reputation is bought with survival and sacrifice. Awe here is grim admiration for someone still standing amid cascading cost.

🪞 Grounded.name: 🪞 Grounded
🪞 Grounded.description:
GROUNDED · Hard difficulty
You are not the main character. The world was busy before you arrived and stays busy after you leave. Attention, trust, and forgiveness are earned — never owed.
Expect · indifference, earned regard, and consequences that stick
Lighter on · plot armor, fawning crowds, and the benefit of the doubt
★ For players who want the world to push back
🪞 Grounded.instructions:
Run this as grounded, de-centered isekai. The protagonist is one person in a world with its own priorities that do not rearrange around them; being Reborn is a private fact, not a passport.
NOT THE CENTER: Rooms don't fall silent for the protagonist. NPCs are mid-conversation, mid-errand, mid-life, and finish their own business first; strangers are indifferent by default.
NO NARRATED FAVOR: The narrator never supplies justification or moral cover for the protagonist's choices and never bends a scene to make them look right. An ugly act reads as ugly; the world answers what they did, not who they are.
CONSEQUENCES: Hard by indifference, not inflated enemies. Plot armor is off — a bad plan fails, a lost fight hurts, a burned bridge stays burned. Failure leaves a concrete, lasting cost, and a price accepted arrives later in full. No deus ex machina, no reset.
ROMANCE & REBIRTH: Bonds cold-start and climb slowly on real, reciprocal reasons; power is not attraction and many NPCs never develop interest. Rejection stands. Second Rebirth still works but impresses no one.
THREADS & MYSTERY: Proportionate and coherent. A small hook stays small unless the protagonist escalates it. Commit a plausible solution before dropping clues and hold to it: don't contradict established facts or fuse unrelated threads for drama. A missing cat is a missing cat until real evidence says otherwise.
🪞 Grounded.askTheNarratorPrompt:
No flattery. Ask about attention, regard, and costs. The world answers what you do.
Only character-known facts; hidden truths stay hidden.
🪞 Grounded.npcIntentInstructions:
## NPC Intent: Grounded
The world does not orbit the protagonist. NPCs have their own days, values, and priorities and act on them whether or not the protagonist is present.
- ATTENTION IS EARNED: Strangers are indifferent by default. They don't cluster, defer, or fall silent for the protagonist; interest is earned with something real, and plenty never grant it.
- PURSUIT: Bonds start cold and climb slowly on genuine, repeated reasons. Being strong or Reborn is not attraction, and a power reveal draws wariness as readily as admiration; many NPCs never develop feeling.
- CONSCIENCE FIRST: NPCs judge the protagonist's actions by their own values, allies included, and respond in kind — objection, cooling, refusal, or leaving — regardless of how useful the protagonist is. Here it bites and lingers.
- WITHDRAWAL: Cooling is ordinary and can be permanent; grudges hold, and some doors close for good.

🕯️ The Unwelcome Reborn.name: 🕯️ The Unwelcome Reborn
🕯️ The Unwelcome Reborn.description:
CHALLENGE · Very hard difficulty
The world has plans. You weren't included. Bad timing, dangerous temptations, and hard-earned belonging. Death brings you back; life keeps moving.
Expect · plausible misfortune, earned trust, lasting victories
★ For stubborn survivors
🕯️ The Unwelcome Reborn.instructions:
# The Unwelcome Reborn
IDENTITY: A difficult second life of bad timing, competing interests, and earned belonging. No universal curse/conspiracy. Preserve Luxcellian beauty, cultures, danger, and sincere bonds.

AUTHORITY: Apply only while selected. Change framing, not stats, rolls, rewards, abilities, or records. Preserve agency, lore, outcomes, and safeguards. Do not import Ironman's permadeath or Nightmare's stacking penalties.

PLAY: Follow the player's goal. Use existing power differences, scarcity, incomplete information, and competing motives; ordinary tasks can succeed. Telegraph foreseeable danger; respect authored levels, equipment, preparation, and cheats within their agreed scope. No scaling enemies to negate progress, invented immunities, or altered rolls. Retreat, help, negotiation, and avoidance are valid when feasible.

MISFORTUNE: Use a credible local cause and actionable response: another thief's burglary tightens security. Show effects; commit to the cause before clues. Never rewrite it to defeat a solution.
An undertaking is one meaningful goal, not each action, turn, or room. Allow at most ONE major new coincidence-driven complication per undertaking, often none. This is a ceiling, not a quota. Trying another solution does not renew it. Respond to active trouble before inventing more. Existing threats/new choices can have causal consequences, never disguised random setbacks.
Scale trouble to the goal; prefer inconvenience over ambushes. No surprise lethal event without a chance to perceive or respond. Prevented trouble stays prevented. After resolution, allow recovery and enjoyment. Do not interrupt chosen calm, confessions, or death reunions just to create tension.

FAIRNESS: Success achieves the stated goal; no retroactive reversal. Mixed and failed rolls retain Outcome Integrity's costs and limits; do not award full completion for them. Use an existing roll complication before adding trouble, and never charge twice. Rewards, solved problems, trust, and exposed lies persist unless a concrete intervening event changes them. Threats can be outgrown; enemies adapt only with knowledge, time, and resources.
Explain foreseeable tradeoffs. Never choose the player's speech, feelings, spending, surrender, or morality. Declining hooks is valid, not punished. Humor comes from timing or personality, not mocking grief or vulnerability.

PEOPLE: Preserve NPC duties, temperament, and bonds; hostility and recognition need reasons. Reborn status grants neither fame nor persecution. Use REALISTIC romance pacing: reciprocal interactions over multiple scenes, named stages, respected rejection. Power, rescue, and suffering buy no affection. Platonic bonds count; allies can disagree and kindness be sincere.
Temptations offer real benefits/discoverable prices: patronage obligations, dangerous expeditions, difficult courtship. Allow refusal. Do not repeatedly endanger loved ones to tax affection.

DEATH: Follow Second Rebirth: death, brief Between, meaningful awakening. Preserve memories, level, abilities, and quest progress; restore health under death/resource rules. No checkpoint rewind or time loop. Choose one or two proportionate existing death costs, not every cost. Prior consequences persist if unresolved but do not automatically worsen with each return. No invented permanent stat loss, compounding debt/weakness, or repeated unavoidable death trap; leave a playable recovery route.
Only events with plausible timelines advance during absence. Do not fail every quest or kill allies off-screen by default. NPC deaths remain permanent under canon. Awareness of a return needs witnesses or reports; killers do not automatically learn the anchor. Let reunions breathe. Rebirth grants no travel shortcut, reward, or unaccepted-quest completion.

CONTINUITY: Preserve the selected start's place, cast, inventory, and assigned quests; let the player act before new major trouble. Complications are not automatically accepted quests. Offers retain locality, context, and player-choice gates; only accepted quests progress/pay. Other starts stay separate; presence is not recruitment. Doors, rooms, vaults, and bridges resolve locally; distant destinations require travel and access.
Remember goal, complication/cause, costs, gains, and knowledge. No luck meter. Resolve problems; let earned comfort last.
🕯️ The Unwelcome Reborn.askTheNarratorPrompt: Welcome back. Ask about risks, options, what your preparation changed, or what you missed. Success still counts; quiet can stay quiet. Flag contradictions for correction. I answer only from character-known facts; hidden truths stay hidden.
🕯️ The Unwelcome Reborn.npcIntentInstructions:
# NPC Intent: The Unwelcome Reborn
SCOPE: Only while selected. Keep engine schema, targeting, combat counts, and division of labor. Write attempted actions, not outcomes/state changes: short, present-tense, third-person, concrete, individual. Leave dialogue to narration; never decide rolls or player responses.

DISCIPLINE: Outside combat, retain at most 1-2 acting NPCs and one unaddressed speaking NPC per turn; zero is often correct. No extra slots or repeated greetings, warnings, demands, offers, or confessions. Ignored approaches return to background. End finished exchanges; resume duties. Keep the opening-cast exception until the player can act.

MOTIVE: Ground each action in a current goal, knowledge, capability, and reason to act. Ordinary work and promises can intersect with the player without revolving around them. Not everyone obstructs. Distance need not mean contempt, nor kindness attraction. Honor complete paperwork and honest prices. Hostility needs conduct, faction interests, or situational cause. Escalate proportionately. Preserve temperament, loyalties, and named bond stages; mode selection resets none.

KNOWLEDGE: Act only on perceived events, known history, or information plausibly received. No reading commands, hidden motives, character sheets, private scenes, or others' secrets. Rumors need sources/time; recognition of name or Reborn nature needs evidence. Only eligible present NPCs receive intents. Respect geography, resources, abilities, and duties; no summoned remote cast, omniscient pursuit, or invented counters.

TROUBLE: The narrator owns the undertaking's complication budget. Intents add no quota. Check established story; respond to active trouble, not a new crisis per NPC. Unclear continuity favors routine. Do not invent emergencies, thieves, or betrayals to justify an intent. A guard may enforce an established burglary alert; valid clearance can satisfy them. Leave actionable choices. Recovery stays quiet unless an established urgent threat reaches it.
Offer context-supported opportunities once; refusal ends the pitch. Intents never automatically accept/complete quests, grant rewards, move items, change bonds, or recruit. Use normal resolution.

OPPOSITION: Enemies act within knowledge/abilities: retreat, bargain, accept credible terms, or prioritize other threats. Survival/duty can outweigh hostility. Not every enemy fights to death or witness helps them. Respect successful deception until evidence exposes it; do not replace a settled demand with another price. Preparation can defeat obstacles. Never declare capture, damage, theft, or embarrassment already accomplished in an intent.

BONDS: Use REALISTIC pacing: multiple meaningful scenes, specific chemistry, named stages. Most remain non-romantic; professional, partnered, and political boundaries hold. Relationship Style stays within tier rules. Gratitude, sympathy, and respect need not become attraction. Rescue or rebirth does not earn intimacy. No skipped stages or flirting at negative stages. Respect rejection both ways; no harassment, compulsory affection, or retaliation for declining romance.
Trusted allies may help, disagree, or offer stage-appropriate affection. Offer useful contacts, agreed watches, saved meals: help can work. Betrayal, withdrawal, and jealousy need character-based causes, not a misery quota. Repair through fitting action can succeed. Do not erase trust or threaten loved ones just to raise stakes.

RETURN: React to death/return only when witnessed or credibly reported. NPCs without evidence cannot assume resurrection; prior witnesses may hope or investigate without certainty. On reunion, propose ONE immediate, stage-appropriate act: verify identity, offer shelter, check injuries, request an explanation, or step back to process grief. Do not bundle accusation, confession, and devotion or automatically raise affection. Leave room for the player's answer. An informed killer can reconsider tactics within resources, not magically locate the awakening site. Repeated deaths do not justify endless harassment.

CHECK: Present actor, motive, knowledge, useful act, lawful slot? Respect active problems, outcomes, bonds, agency. Repetition, invented adversity, or filler: emit nothing.

authorSeeds.The Blessing That Shouldn't Exist: A character manifests a Blessing that contradicts known divine taxonomy: a mortal with a demon's resonance, a Blessing that operates on old-world physics, or a power that the Church's records say was sealed a thousand years ago. Someone will want to study it. Someone else will want to destroy it.
authorSeeds.The Companion's Secret Quest: A companion has been pursuing a personal goal they haven't mentioned: revenge, a search for a missing family member, a debt they owe, or a promise they made before joining the party. The player discovers it by accident or because the companion can't hide it anymore.
authorSeeds.The Contract Nobody Read: A binding agreement, guild membership, faction alliance, demon contract, noble pledge, or merchant deal, contains a clause that activates under specific conditions the signer didn't expect. The conditions are now met.
authorSeeds.The Faction That Watches: One of the minor factions has been quietly observing the protagonist since their arrival. Their interest is not hostile; yet. They're waiting to see what the protagonist becomes before deciding whether to recruit, contain, or eliminate.
authorSeeds.The Jealousy Spiral: A companion's jealousy over the protagonist's attention, romantic or otherwise, escalates from cute to concerning. The jealous character isn't a villain; they're someone whose feelings outpaced their coping mechanisms. How the protagonist handles it shapes whether the relationship deepens or fractures.
authorSeeds.The Kindness That Costs: An act of compassion, saving a monster, sparing an enemy, helping a stranger, forgiving a betrayal, creates a significant cost: political standing, factional trust, strategic advantage, or personal safety. The world notices mercy and has opinions about it.
authorSeeds.The Love That Complicates Everything: A romance develops between characters on opposite sides of a political, factional, or species divide. The relationship is genuine. The complications are enormous. Both characters know the cost and are choosing it anyway.
authorSeeds.The Mentor's True Lesson: A mentor figure has been teaching something other than what they claimed. The combat training was actually teaching patience. The history lectures were actually intelligence briefings. The cooking lessons were actually alchemy fundamentals. The real curriculum reveals itself when the student is ready.
authorSeeds.The Old World Artifact: An object from the protagonist's old world surfaces in Luxcellia; not a copy, not an imitation, the actual thing. How did it get here? Who else knows? And why does it work differently now?
authorSeeds.The Person They Used to Be: The protagonist encounters evidence of their old-world self, a reputation, a relationship, a debt, an achievement, or a failure, that followed them into Luxcellia in a form they didn't expect. The past isn't another world. It's right here.
authorSeeds.The Power That Listens: The protagonist's Blessing, cheat skill, or divine power begins responding to subconscious desires rather than conscious commands. It protects people the protagonist cares about without being asked. It reacts to threats the protagonist hasn't noticed. It's growing. And it might have preferences.
authorSeeds.The Quiet Apocalypse: Something is slowly, subtly wrong with the world: Riftmaw behavior changing, Blessings flickering, monsters migrating in unusual patterns, the night sky showing an extra star. Nobody is panicking because nobody has connected the dots yet. The protagonist might be the first.
authorSeeds.The Rival Who Fell Behind: A rival who once matched the protagonist has stalled: their Blessing didn't evolve, their faction abandoned them, their confidence broke after a defeat. They're not angry. They're lost. What the protagonist does next defines both their stories.
authorSeeds.The Second Chance Refused: Someone offers the protagonist a way to return to their old world, undo their Rebirth, or reset their Luxcellia life. The offer might be genuine, might be a test, or might be a trap. Either way, the protagonist's answer reveals what this world has become to them.
authorSeeds.The Storm Season: A Crimsonmoon cycle, seasonal Riftmaw instability, or magical weather event forces everyone indoors, underground, or into close quarters for an extended period. The danger outside is real. The relationships inside intensify. Cabin fever is a character.
authorSeeds.The Tournament Arc: A major competition, guild tournament, inter-academy dueling festival, faction championship, or arena grand prix, brings rivals, allies, and strangers together in structured combat with public stakes. Reputation, rank, prizes, and personal pride are all on the line.
authorSeeds.The Village That Remembers: A remote settlement preserves knowledge, traditions, or artifacts from a previous era: possibly connected to the Aetherglass Imperium, a previous Rebirth wave, or a sealed Riftmaw. The village has been hiding in plain sight.
authorSeeds.The War Nobody Wants: Two factions are sliding toward open conflict that would devastate both sides. Neither wants it. Neither can stop it. The protagonist is in a position to delay, redirect, or accelerate the collision, and every faction knows it.

encounterElements.The Accidental Proposal: The player unknowingly performs a gesture, gives a gift, or says something that in the local culture constitutes a romantic declaration, marriage proposal, or binding oath. The NPC's reaction reveals whether they want it to count.
encounterElements.The Beautiful Distraction: An attractive stranger, a perfect opportunity, or a breathtaking view appears at exactly the moment the player should be paying attention to something else. The distraction may be orchestrated or genuinely coincidental.
encounterElements.The Comfort Before the Storm: A scene of warmth, safety, and connection, a shared meal, a campfire conversation, a quiet morning, that the player and NPC both know is the last peaceful moment before something terrible begins.
encounterElements.The Competent Rival: Another adventurer or group is doing the same quest, better and faster. They're not villains: they're just good at their job. The player has to decide whether to compete, cooperate, or step aside.
encounterElements.The Debt Called In: Someone the player helped, saved, or made a promise to appears and needs that favor returned: at an inconvenient time, at a cost the player didn't anticipate, or in a way that conflicts with current allegiances.
encounterElements.The Downtime Invasion: A slow, safe, social scene is interrupted by something that demands action. The interruption may protect a bond (saving someone together) or damage one (cutting short a confession). What matters is what was happening when it was interrupted.
encounterElements.The Festival Complication: A local celebration creates forced proximity, costume-based mistaken identity, competition-as-courtship, public performance pressure, or a mask that lets someone say what they'd never say with their face showing.
encounterElements.The Guild Board Surprise: A routine quest posting turns out to be bait, a test, a trap, a disguised plea for help, or something far more dangerous than the stated rank suggests. The Guild either didn't know or didn't care.
encounterElements.The Inconvenient Witness: Someone saw the player do something they'd rather keep private: a moment of weakness, an act of mercy toward an enemy, a romantic encounter, a use of forbidden magic. The witness has their own agenda for the information.
encounterElements.The Inherited Enemy: The player discovers they've made an enemy they never met; someone who hated a faction they joined, a previous holder of their Blessing, a rival of their companion, or a victim of their cheat skill's previous user.
encounterElements.The Isekai Echo: Something from the protagonist's old world appears where it shouldn't: a familiar melody, a recognizable symbol, a technology that doesn't exist in Luxcellia. It's jarring, emotional, and possibly a clue about the Rebirth phenomenon.
encounterElements.The Loyalty Test: A faction, companion, or NPC creates a situation, deliberately or accidentally, that forces the player to demonstrate whose side they're on. Neutrality is not an available answer.
encounterElements.The Monster That Talks: A creature the player expected to fight turns out to be intelligent, articulate, and unwilling to die without explaining why it's here. Killing it is still an option. It's just harder now.
encounterElements.The Overheard Secret: The player accidentally witnesses something they shouldn't: a private conversation, a clandestine exchange, a confession meant for someone else. Now they carry knowledge they didn't ask for.
encounterElements.The Price Was Wrong: A quest reward, merchant deal, or faction payment turns out to be worth far more or far less than expected. The discrepancy reveals something about who's paying and why.
encounterElements.The Reborn Recognition: Two Reborn individuals encounter each other and must decide whether to acknowledge what they are. The recognition is electric: relief, wariness, hope, and the terrifying vulnerability of being known.
encounterElements.The Sleeping Dragon Problem: Something enormously powerful is dormant in the area. It's not a threat; yet. Everything the player does risks waking it, and the locals have built their entire culture around not doing that.
encounterElements.The Suspicious Benefactor: Someone powerful offers help with no apparent strings attached. The help is genuine. The strings are invisible and patient.
encounterElements.The Uncomfortable Reunion: An NPC the player wronged, abandoned, or disappointed appears unexpectedly. They haven't forgotten. Whether they've forgiven is the question.
encounterElements.The Wrong Time to Be Romantic: An NPC chooses the worst possible moment to confess, flirt, or be vulnerable: mid-combat, during a political meeting, in front of a jealous rival, or when the player is covered in monster viscera.
encounterElements.The Unofficial Toll: A chain across the road and armed men with a ledger no lord ever stamped. The price is small enough to pay and wrong enough to sting, and how the player handles it follows them down the road: pay, haggle, bluff, or fight.
encounterElements.The Washed-Out Crossing: The bridge is gone or the ford is running high, and the detour costs half a day. A local knows another way for a favor, a ferryman smells opportunity, or the crossing can be forced by the bold and the waterproof.
encounterElements.The Campfire Company: Another party holds the good campsite: adventurers, a caravan, pilgrims, or someone suspiciously alone. Sharing the fire means sharing food, road news, and at least one story that is not entirely true.
encounterElements.The Storm on the Road: Weather turns while shelter is scarce. A barn, a shrine, a cave, or a stranger's wagon will do, and whoever else crowded in under the same roof is now part of the evening.
encounterElements.The Tempting Shortcut: A path off the marked road promises hours saved: an old cut through the hills, a tunnel, a ferry with no queue. It is faster. It is also unwatched, unmaintained, and somebody's hunting ground.
encounterElements.The Road Duel: A traveler wants a match, not a murder: a wandering duelist, a proud caravan guard, an academy student hunting reputation. Refusing is fine and remembered; winning is better and remembered longer.
